mu_0+mu_1+mu_2=2r(a d+1)=2, so node0 also has the required zero flow.

Before checking signs, verify the complete algebraic identity

    q||x_0||^2-2f_2+sum lambda_ij Q_ij
                      =||r x_0-s d g_0-d g_1-g_2||^2. (7)

Its x_0 coefficients are immediate from mu. The terminal cross entries
are s d and d: in the terminal-square parameterization of the predecessor,
alpha_star=r, alpha_0=d-a t, alpha_1=b-d, which sum to one, and

    V_alpha=r x_0-s d g_0-d g_1.

The g_1 diagonal is lambda_01+lambda_21=d^2. The g_0 diagonal is
mu_0+(1-a)lambda_01, which equals s^2d^2 by(5). The coefficient of
<g_0,g_1> is

    a mu_1+(a-1)lambda_10-lambda_01
      =-2(1-r)d+(s-1)d^2+2b
      =2s d^2,

again by(5). The g_2 diagonal is one by terminal flow. These account for
every quadratic coefficient, proving(7) even before any multiplier signs
are assumed.

### All multiplier signs, analytically

First t>=1/2. The left side of(1), at t=1/2, equals

    (a-1)^2(a+2)/2=(a^3-3a+2)/2<=1

for a<=sqrt(3); use its strict increase in t. Also 0<r<1/2 follows from
r^2=1/(2a+2b+1) and a>1,b>=3/2.

Next d>=1. Put t_0=1/(a^2-1). At that argument the left side of(1)
minus one is

    a^2(3-a^2)/[(a^2-1)(a+1)^2]>=0.

Thus t<=t_0 and r<=1/(a+1), which is equivalent to d>=1.
It follows that lambda_10=d(d-2r)>0. From(5),
d^2<2b/a<b^2, because a b>=(3/2)sqrt(2)>2.
Hence lambda_21>0. All mu_i are positive.

For lambda_01, all quantities are continuous in a on this interval; this
follows directly from strict monotonicity of the left side of(1) in t,
or from taking limits of its unique bounded positive roots.
If lambda_01=0, its two expressions in(6) give d=2t and

    0=d^2+2d-2b=2(2t-1)(t+1).

Therefore t=1/2,d=1. Equation a r d=1-r and r=(a-1)/2 then force
a^2=3. There is no zero in [sqrt(2),sqrt(3)). At a=sqrt(2),
t(2t+1)=a+1, r=1/(2t+1), d=a t, and lambda_01=2r^2>0.
Consequently lambda_01>=0 throughout, vanishing only at sqrt(3).

For lambda_20 put alpha_0=d-a t. It is also continuous. To locate its
possible zeros using fully explicit algebra, set c=1/(a+1) and take the
legal capped quadratic with derivative min(c,x), starting at1. Its trajectory
for (a,b) has gradients (c,c,-ct), terminal normalized value c^2t^2,
and every Q occurring in(6) is zero EXCEPT

    Q_20=-a b/(a+1)^2.

The square vector in(7) evaluated there equals -a alpha_0/(a+1): this
follows from(5), or from
a alpha_0=r(a+2b)-b. Thus the algebraic identity(7) gives

    a^2 alpha_0^2+2ab alpha_0
                         =a^2(a^2-2)t^2.              (8)

In particular alpha_0=0 is possible only at a=sqrt(2), because t>0.
At a=sqrt(3), the values t=1/2,d=1 give alpha_0=1-sqrt(3)/2>0.
By continuity and absence of another zero, alpha_0>0 for sqrt(2)<a<=sqrt(3)
and it is zero at sqrt(2). This proves the remaining multiplier sign.
The capped quadratic is used only to check the displayed polynomial identity,
without assuming a bound from a certificate before its signs are established.

All multipliers in(6) are now nonnegative, so the full square(7) proves
the middle-range upper value. Combined with(3), this proves that range.

## 5. Range three below2: the active star-outgoing edge changes

Let sqrt(3)<=a<=2, s=a-1, b=3/2, q=s^2/4. In addition to mu_i, now use
nu_0=lambda_(star,0). Set all unlisted multipliers zero and take

    mu_0=s^2,    mu_1=mu_2=s,
    nu_0=a^2-3=s^2+2s-2,
    lambda_10=lambda_20=2-a=1-s,
    lambda_21=1.

Every coefficient is nonnegative in this interval. At node0,
mu_0=nu_0+lambda_10+lambda_20; at node1,
mu_1+lambda_10=lambda_21; and at node2,
mu_2+lambda_20+lambda_21=2. The FULL identity is

    q||x_0||^2-2f_2+sum lambda_ij Q_ij
                 =||(s/2)x_0-s g_0-g_1-g_2||^2.       (9)

To check its coefficients, the g_0 diagonal is
(mu_0+nu_0+lambda_10+lambda_20)/2=s^2; the g_1 diagonal is
(mu_1+lambda_10+lambda_21)/2=1; and the g_2 diagonal is one.
The <g_0,g_1> and <g_0,g_2> coefficients both equal
a s+s(1-s)=2s. The <g_1,g_2> coefficient is
(3/2)s+(3/2)(1-s)+1/2=2. The x_0 cross coefficients are
-mu_0,-mu_1,-mu_2, exactly as on the RHS. The flow cancels all values.

This proves the third-range upper bound through a=2. Notice that nu_0
is strictly positive for sqrt(3)<a<=2. These are optimal certificates for
a fixed earlier step; no claim of global schedule optimality is made.

## 6. Range three above2, and all zero boundaries

For a>=2, interpolation with the minimizer gives <x_0,g_0>>=||g_0||^2,
and smoothness gives ||g_0||<=||x_0||. Thus

    ||x_1||^2<=||x_0||^2+a(a-2)||g_0||^2
                                      <=(a-1)^2||x_0||^2.

At the last step b=3/2, direct expansion of the one-step identity gives

    (1/4)||x_1||^2-2f_2+Q_(1,star)+Q_(2,star)+Q_(2,1)
                       =||(1/2)x_1-g_1-g_2||^2.

Consequently W_2(a,3/2)<=(a-1)^2/4, completing the third range.
The lower arguments in Section2 include arbitrary b=0 and arbitrary large b.
At a=0 the original-coordinate certificate(4) is already PSD. Any other
zero insertions leave the actual iterates unchanged, as also proved in the
accepted zero-compression fact. Multiplying normalized functions by L restores
every original L>0 without changing either step or normalized error.

## 7. Optimizing the last step does NOT restore convexity in the earlier step

Put

    a_left=3/2,   a_right=sqrt(3),
    q_local=(2-sqrt(3))/2=1/(4+2sqrt(3)).

The middle-range formula gives t=sqrt(3)-1 at a_left and therefore final
b=sqrt(3). At a_right the final b=3/2. In both cases

    rho_two(a_left)=rho_two(a_right)=q_local.           (10)

For EVERY a strictly between these two endpoints one has

    rho_two(a)>q_local.                               (11)

To prove this directly, suppose some b had W_2(a,b)<=q_local. The Huber
bound in(3) forces a+b>=T_0=3/2+sqrt(3), so b>1. The quadratic bound forces
(a-1)(b-1)<=r_0=(sqrt(3)-1)/2. But

    (a-1)(b-1)>=(a-1)(T_0-a-1)>r_0,

because the last quadratic is strictly concave in a and takes exactly r_0
at both a_left and a_right. This is a contradiction. The already established
attainment of rho_two makes the inequality in(11) strict for its infimum.

Thus even AFTER eliminating the final step exactly, the remaining value is
not quasiconvex (and hence not convex) in the earlier step. In particular,
the midpoint of the two endpoints in(10) violates the convex-value inequality.
This is a sharper closure obstruction than nonconvexity of the unoptimized
whole-schedule value.

## 8. A strict suboptimal local minimum and a coordinatewise trap

The schedule

    (a,b)=(sqrt(3),3/2)

is the UNIQUE minimizer of W_2 on the entire region a>3/2,b>=0, with value
q_local. Indeed (11) excludes 3/2<a<sqrt(3). For a>sqrt(3), the third/fourth
bounds in(3) have minimal maximum (a-1)^2/4>q_local. At a=sqrt(3), their
unique minimizer is b=3/2. Hence this point is a strict local minimum in the
full nonnegative two-step domain.

It is also globally optimal in EACH coordinate separately. The fixed-prefix
assertion was proved above. With b=3/2 fixed, the Huber bound is strictly
larger than q_local when a<sqrt(3), and the quadratic bound is strictly
larger when a>sqrt(3). Thus a=sqrt(3) is the unique best first step for that b.

Nevertheless it is not a global schedule minimum. The range-one certificate
at a=sqrt(2), b=(3+sqrt(8sqrt(2)+9))/4 has q<2/15<q_local. To check these
strict comparisons without decimals, sqrt(2)>7/5 implies b>37/20, so
a+b>13/4 and q=1/(1+2a+2b)<2/15. Also sqrt(3)<26/15, which follows by
squaring, gives q_local>2/15.

This supplies a concrete full-class obstruction to concluding global optimality
from exact successive one-coordinate minimizations, even when each subproblem
is solved globally and the full interpolation/PSD certificates are retained.
It does not contradict the uniqueness of the separate globally optimal
two-step calibration, and it makes no asymptotic claim.

claim: Candidate uniform closure of the ENTIRE retuned two-bridge family with block capacities (4,4,27/7): primitive validity forces T_tot<81/5<9^rho, rho=log_2(1+sqrt2). This excludes the needed primitive amplification threshold for every positive pair of bridge excesses, not only seed29a1f4a5269032b1. No quadratic-balance assumption or cut-saturation assumption is used. evidence:
# A two-dimensional obstruction at a saturated primitive cut

Status: complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. No solver or verifier
call. The only existing fact used is 1252b8823bb5a290, for its explicit finite
smooth-convex interpolation construction. Every other identity is proved here.

## 1. Definitions and an energy identity

For a nonnegative physical schedule h of length n let T_tot=1+sum_i h_i.
For normalized smoothness 1 and an optimum jet (0,0,0), put

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V_h=2 sum_(i<n) h_i(f_i-f_n)
          +sum_(i<n) h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
          -T_tot(T_tot-1)||g_n||^2.

Here primitive validity means V_h>=0 on every legal convex 1-smooth GD
trajectory. Suppose the sampled data additionally satisfy

    f_i=<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2 for every i,
    x_n=g_n.

The first condition is exactly Q_(i,star)=0; the second gives
f_n=||g_n||^2/2. Expanding

    ||x_0||^2-||x_n||^2
       =2 sum h_i<g_i,x_i>-sum h_i^2||g_i||^2

therefore gives the exact identity

    V_h=||x_0||^2-T_tot^2||g_n||^2.                 (1)

For any such data, whether or not yet jointly interpolable, write y_i=x_i-g_i.
Direct substitution also gives

    Q_ij=<g_i-g_j,y_j>.                             (2)

## 2. General two-bridge construction

Let a,b,c be arbitrary finite nonnegative blocks, with capacities

    A=1+sum a_i, B=1+sum b_i, C=1+sum c_i.

Take r_L,r_R>0 and h=(a,1+r_L,b,1+r_R,c). Define

    D_tail=B+C+r_R, T_tot=A+D_tail+r_L,
    eta_cut=r_L/D_tail, beta_inner=r_R/C,
    p_aux=-B/r_L.

The first scalar array is a legal Huber trajectory: start at A and use
derivative clip(x,-eta_cut,1). During a and at its endpoint the gradient is
1. Its endpoint is 1. The first bridge lands at -r_L=-eta_cut D_tail.
Every remaining query has gradient -eta_cut, and the final point is
-eta_cut. All the data satisfy the hypotheses of (1), so

    V_base=A^2-T_tot^2 eta_cut^2.                   (3)

The second scalar array is defined as follows. During a use constant
gradient p_aux, start at A p_aux, and end at p_aux. The first bridge lands
at -r_L p_aux=B. On the remaining schedule (b,1+r_R,c) use the ACTUAL
Huber trajectory with derivative clip(x,-beta_inner,1), starting at B.
The b block ends at 1, the second bridge lands at -r_R=-C beta_inner,
and c ends at -beta_inner. Assign every value by
f_i=g_i x_i-g_i^2/2. Thus (1) yields

    V_aux=A^2 B^2/r_L^2-T_tot^2 beta_inner^2.        (4)

The second array is generally NOT interpolable across the first bridge.
It is only auxiliary data; its possible violations are accounted for below.

For epsilon_mix>0, combine both arrays into two-dimensional data

    X_i=(x_i^base,sqrt(epsilon_mix) x_i^aux),
    G_i=(g_i^base,sqrt(epsilon_mix) g_i^aux),
    F_i=f_i^base+epsilon_mix f_i^aux.

The GD equations hold coordinate by coordinate, all Q_(i,star) remain zero,
and X_n=G_n. Consequently

    V_mix=V_base+epsilon_mix V_aux.                 (5)

Here is a complete interpolation audit. Partition the samples into L (a
and its endpoint), M (b and its endpoint after the first bridge), and R (c
and its final endpoint after the second bridge). Overlaps are assigned to
the group whose gradient is used at the relevant bridge. The groups are
disjoint in original time: L includes the first bridge query, M includes
the second bridge query, and R includes the terminal sample.

* Within L all gradients in each scalar array agree, so Q=0.
* Within M union R the auxiliary data are one legal Huber trajectory;
  the base gradients agree, so all Q<=0 there.
* From L to M, the auxiliary target has y_j>=0 and the source gradient
  p_aux<1, so Q_aux<=0. From M to L, the auxiliary target y_i is a
  nonnegative multiple of p_aux<0 and 1-p_aux>0, so Q_aux<=0.
* From L to R, if R_j is the remaining sum of physical c steps after its
  target sample j, the two residuals are

      Q_base=-(1+eta_cut)eta_cut R_j,
      Q_aux=beta_inner(-p_aux-beta_inner)R_j.

* From R to L, if H_i is the remaining sum of physical a steps after its
  target sample i, then

      Q_base=-(1+eta_cut)H_i,
      Q_aux=(-beta_inner-p_aux)p_aux H_i.

Zero remaining sums give zero in both arrays. Thus duplicate positions
caused by zero steps do not require a separate limiting argument.

The optimum-outgoing inequalities hold too: Q_(star,i)=-<G_i,Y_i>,
and the inner product is nonnegative separately in each scalar array.
For the auxiliary L data this is H_i p_aux^2>=0, and in the other groups
it follows directly from their plateau coordinates. Q_(i,star)=0 already.

When r_L r_R<BC, one has -p_aux>beta_inner. The ONLY potentially positive
auxiliary residuals are L-to-R, and all interpolation inequalities hold for

    0<epsilon_mix<=epsilon_max,
    epsilon_max=eta_cut(1+eta_cut)
                    /[beta_inner(-p_aux-beta_inner)].             (6)

When r_L r_R>BC the ONLY potentially positive auxiliary residuals are
R-to-L, and all inequalities hold for

    0<epsilon_mix<=epsilon_max,
    epsilon_max=(1+eta_cut)
                    /[(-p_aux)(beta_inner+p_aux)].                 (7)

When r_L r_R=BC both cross families are nonpositive for any epsilon_mix.

All these are complete original-index interpolation checks, including both
cross directions and both optimum directions.

## 3. One fixed globally legal function

Include the zero optimum sample and define, on R^2,

    H_mix(v)=max_i { c_i+<X_i,v-G_i>+||v-G_i||^2/2 },
    c_i=<G_i,X_i>-F_i=||G_i||^2/2,
    f_mix(x)=sup_v { <x,v>-H_mix(v) }.

The maximum includes i=star. This is the explicit finite interpolation
construction of accepted fact 1252b8823bb5a290, proof section 2, applied to
the entire finite data set. The checked Q inequalities imply that f_mix
interpolates every (X_i,G_i,F_i), is convex differentiable and 1-smooth,
and has f_mix(0)=0=min f_mix. Thus the mixed data are one actual GD
trajectory of one fixed function; they are not an adaptive oracle or a
reset of the function at a bridge.

## 4. A universal quantitative two-cut necessary condition

Any primitive h as above necessarily satisfies

    r_L r_R [A^2+r_L(T_tot+A)] <= A^2 BC.           (8)

First assume r_L r_R<BC and choose epsilon_mix=epsilon_max in (6).
Using D_tail=B+C+r_R, substitution into (3)-(5) gives

    V_mix = (BC+r_R D_tail)(D_tail+r_L)
              /[D_tail^2 r_R(BC-r_L r_R)]
             * {A^2 BC-r_L r_R[A^2+r_L(T_tot+A)]}.

The prefactor is positive, proving necessity of (8) in this case. For an
algebra check, before the final factorization the numerator is

    (BC+r_R D_tail)
       {A^2[BC(D_tail+r_L)-r_L r_R D_tail]
                                     -T_tot^2 r_L^2 r_R}.

Use A^2 D_tail+T_tot^2 r_L
=(D_tail+r_L)[A^2+r_L(T_tot+A)] to obtain the displayed factorization.

If r_L r_R>BC, set z_aux=-p_aux=B/r_L and beta_inner>z_aux, and use (7).
Equation (5) becomes

    V_mix=(beta_inner+eta_cut z_aux)/(beta_inner-z_aux)
             * {A^2-T_tot^2[(1+eta_cut)beta_inner/z_aux-eta_cut]}.

The bracket is strictly smaller than A^2-T_tot^2<0. Hence no such schedule
is primitive. If r_L r_R=BC, V_aux=z_aux^2(A^2-T_tot^2)<0, so sufficiently
large epsilon_mix in the fully legal mixed data again gives V_mix<0.
This excludes the two remaining cases and completes (8).

No quadratic-balance assumption about a,b,c appears in this argument.

## 5. Saturated first cut forces its inner tail cut

Suppose in addition r_L T_tot=A D_tail. Then eta_cut=A/T_tot, V_base=0,
and A^2+r_L(T_tot+A)=A T_tot. Condition (8) reduces to

    T_tot r_L r_R<=ABC,
    equivalently r_R D_tail<=BC.                   (9)

Therefore a positive defect r_R D_tail>BC in the inner tail cannot be
repaired by any signed storage or full collection of interpolation edges
while keeping this outer cut exactly saturated. This statement concerns
primitive validity of this actual schedule, not all objective certificates.

The geometry also explains the conclusion without (8): at outer saturation
(4) becomes (T_tot/D_tail)^2[B^2-D_tail^2 beta_inner^2], which is strictly
negative exactly when the tail cut fails. Any sufficiently small positive
mixture allowed above then has V_mix<0.

## 6. Explicit refutation candidate for the outstanding eight-step seed

Set u=10/7, C=27/7, A=B=4, and

    D_tail=(165+sqrt(65641))/42,
    r_R=D_tail-55/7,
    T_tot=(4+D_tail+sqrt((4+D_tail)^2+16D_tail))/2,
    r_L=T_tot-4-D_tail.

The schedule is

    (3/2,3/2,1+r_L,3/2,3/2,1+r_R,10/7,10/7).

Directly from these root equations,

    r_R D_tail=196/9, r_L T_tot=4D_tail,
    BC=108/7<196/9.

Thus (9) fails. Here is a concrete mixing scale without an unspecified
smallness parameter. Define eta_cut=r_L/D_tail, beta_inner=r_R/C,
p_aux=-4/r_L, and

    epsilon_mix=eta_cut(1+eta_cut)
                      /[2 beta_inner(-p_aux-beta_inner)].          (10)

It is positive: the first defining polynomial has its positive root in
(10,101/10), and substituting 5/2 into
r_L^2+(4+D_tail)r_L-4D_tail shows r_L<5/2. Hence
r_L r_R<(5/2)(157/70)=157/28<108/7=BC. Formula (10) is half of (6).

For reference the two position arrays are

    base: (4,5/2,1,-r_L,-r_L+(3/2)eta_cut,
           -r_L+3eta_cut,-C eta_cut,-(1+u)eta_cut,-eta_cut),
    aux:  (4p_aux,(5/2)p_aux,p_aux,4,5/2,1,
           -r_R,-(1+u)beta_inner,-beta_inner).

The gradient arrays are

    base: (1,1,1,-eta_cut,-eta_cut,-eta_cut,
                           -eta_cut,-eta_cut,-eta_cut),
    aux:  (p_aux,p_aux,p_aux,1,1,1,
                           -beta_inner,-beta_inner,-beta_inner).

Values are g_i x_i-g_i^2/2 in each coordinate. Sections 2-3 show that
their mixed two-dimensional jets come from the explicit fixed f_mix.
Finally beta_inner D_tail=1372/243=4(343/243), so

    V_mix = epsilon_mix(T_tot/D_tail)^2
                  [16-(1372/243)^2]
          = -epsilon_mix(T_tot/D_tail)^2 * 937600/59049 < 0.        (11)

This gives an exact concrete primitive counterexample for the proposed
eight-step seed. It closes that seed's proposed primitive amplification.
It makes no claim that a different direct objective certificate is
impossible, and does not settle the unrestricted asymptotic target.

## Literature and verification status

Targeted Matlas and web retrieval supplied no theorem used in this proof.
The primitive/Huber regime had already been audited in previous rounds;
this continuation uses the accepted finite interpolation construction
rather than an external black box. All new results above remain candidates
pending a selected verifier allocation. No fact was submitted or written.

## 7. Retuning both bridges does not repair the fixed shortened-tail family

The obstruction is wider than the exact radical seed. For ANY nonnegative
blocks of capacities A=B=4 and C=27/7, every primitive schedule
(a,1+r_L,b,1+r_R,c) with r_L,r_R>0 has

    T_tot<81/5<9^rho, rho=log_2(1+sqrt(2)).         (12)

This rules out the required primitive amplification seed throughout the
two-parameter bridge family with these three physical blocks, without a
quadratic-product assumption and without requiring either cut to saturate.

Here is the entire scalar deduction. The first-cut Huber array from section2
gives T_tot r_L<=A(B+C+r_R). The same construction at the second bridge
(start on its positive plateau at A+B+r_L, negative slope r_R/C) gives
T_tot r_R<=C(A+B+r_L). For a fixed T=T_tot set

    R=T-A-B-C,
    U(T)=A(T-A)/(T+A), S(T)=C(T-C)/(T+C),
    L(T)=R-S(T).

Both cuts force L(T)<=r_L<=U(T), with r_R=R-r_L. At
T0=81/5 these endpoints and their complementary r_R values are

    r_L=L(T0)=128/65,  r_R=S(T0)=216/91,
    r_L=U(T0)=244/101, r_R=R-U(T0)=6812/3535.

Let Phi_T(z)=z(R-z)[A^2+z(T+A)]. Its derivative is

    Phi_T'(z)=A^2 R+2[(T+A)R-A^2]z-3(T+A)z^2.

Since R>0, this quadratic has one negative and one positive root. Thus
Phi_T increases and then decreases on (0,R); its minimum on any closed
subinterval is attained at an endpoint. The two exact endpoint excesses
over the necessary bound A^2 BC in (8), at T0, are

    Phi_T0(L(T0))-A^2 BC=26650944/1922375>0,
    Phi_T0(U(T0))-A^2 BC=97846272/1785175>0.

For T>=T0, U and S increase, while their derivatives
2A^2/(T+A)^2 and 2C^2/(T+C)^2 lie in (0,1). Hence L=R-S and R-U
also increase. Each endpoint product z(R-z)[A^2+z(T+A)] strictly increases,
because all its positive factors increase. If the cut interval is empty,
the cuts already fail; otherwise both endpoint excesses stay positive and
Phi_T(z)>A^2 BC throughout the interval. This contradicts (8) and proves
T<T0.

For the last inequality in (12), let lambda=1+sqrt(2), so 2^rho=lambda.
One has 9^6-2^19=7153>0 and

    lambda^19=9369319+6625109 sqrt(2)
       >9369319+(7/5)6625109
       =(81/5)^6+8890332269/15625.

Therefore 9^(6rho)>lambda^19>(81/5)^6 and (12) follows.

All endpoint arithmetic here is exact rational arithmetic for two displayed
values. It is not a reopened schedule search or numerical PEP screen.

evidence:
# Exact one-bridge defect lifting and the retained slack penalty

Status: complete candidate interface, NOT verified. No fact_submit or numerical
search. The proof uses only accepted interpolation fact1252b8823bb5a290 and
the direct calculations below, not earlier unverified findings as premises.

## Definitions

Let h have capacity K=1+sum h_i. On a legal normalized GD trajectory with
minimizer0 define

    I_i_star=-Q_(i,star)=<g_i,x_i>-f_i-||g_i||^2/2>=0,
    delta_end=f_n-||g_n||^2/2>=0,
    y_end=x_n-g_n,
    V_h=2sum h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                           -K(K-1)||g_n||^2.

The squared-distance telescope gives

    V_h=||x0||^2-||xn||^2-2sum h_i I_i_star
                         -2(K-1)f_n-K(K-1)||g_n||^2.             (1)

Call the endpoint core when x_n=g_n. In that case interpolation to/from0
forces f_n=||g_n||^2/2, and (1) reduces to

    V_h=||x0||^2-K^2||g_n||^2-2sum h_i I_i_star.                (2)

All sample data and the initial-distance term are retained.

## A. Appending at a saturated outer cut preserves a core-ended defect

Let b be any nonnegative schedule of capacity D with an actual legal
trajectory having endpoint x_m=g_m. Its dimension and all earlier values,
points, gradients and optimum interpolation slacks are arbitrary.
Let c be any nonnegative block of capacity C, and r_ext>0 satisfy

    T_tot=D+C+r_ext, r_ext T_tot=DC.                            (3)

If V_b<0 on that trajectory, then (b,1+r_ext,c) is not primitive.

Proof. Use a scalar base trajectory whose derivative is clip(x,-r_ext/C,1),
starting at D. The entire b block stays on its positive plateau and ends
at1; the bridge lands at-r_ext; c remains on its negative plateau and
ends at-r_ext/C. The base energy is D^2-T_tot^2(r_ext/C)^2=0 by(3).

For the auxiliary vector array retain EVERY supplied b sample. Write
e=g_m=x_m and append the bridge, which lands at-r_ext e. On c set the
constant gradient v_end=-(r_ext/C)e, so its initial point is C v_end
and its final point v_end. Assign each appended value
f_i=<v_end,x_i>-||v_end||^2/2. This auxiliary array may violate old/new
cross interpolation and is not claimed to be legal by itself.

Combine the base and auxiliary arrays in orthogonal coordinates with a
positive multiplier epsilon_mix on every auxiliary squared norm and value.
All base-zero constraints remain valid under this mixture:

* Within the old b samples, the auxiliary data are the original legal data.
* Within the new c samples, the auxiliary gradient is constant.
* A new-to-old base constraint can be zero only at an old query with
  zero remaining b steps, hence at its endpoint x_m=e. The auxiliary
  Q_(new,m) is zero by direct expansion using x_m=g_m=e and f_m=||e||^2/2.
* An old-to-new base constraint can be zero only at a new query with zero
  remaining c steps, hence at x=v_end=g. Direct expansion gives
  Q_(old,new)=Q_(old,star)<=0.
* Every auxiliary optimum constraint is valid: old ones by hypothesis;
  appended incoming ones are zero and outgoing ones are
  -R_i||v_end||^2<=0, where R_i is the remaining c stepsize sum.

Zero steps create only the endpoint duplicates already covered above.
All other base cross constraints are strictly negative. If E_bad is the
finite set of pairs with Q_aux>0, choose

    epsilon_mix=min(1, min_(ij in E_bad) [-Q_base,ij/(2Q_aux,ij)]),

interpreting the inner minimum as1 for an empty set. Every pair in E_bad
has Q_base<0 by the preceding audit, so epsilon_mix>0. The combined data
obey all original-index interpolation inequalities. The explicit conjugate
construction in fact1252b8823bb5a290 interpolates them by one fixed legal
convex differentiable 1-smooth function with minimizer0.

The auxiliary core endpoint permits (2). No new I_i_star is added, and
T_tot^2||v_end||^2=D^2||e||^2 by(3). Therefore

    V_aux=V_b, V_mix=epsilon_mix V_b<0.                         (4)

This is a true defect inheritance rule for the displayed core-ended
witness class. It does not assert that every failure of primitive validity
admits such a witness.

## B. Prepending has an explicit nonnegative retained-slack penalty

Let b now be any nonnegative schedule of capacity D and any actual legal
trajectory (z_j,g_j,f_j) with minimizer0. Let a have capacity A and let
r_ext>0 satisfy

    T_tot=A+D+r_ext, r_ext T_tot=AD,
    kappa_lift=(T_tot/D)^2>1.

Put p_aux=-z_0/r_ext. Before the supplied b trajectory insert constant
gradient p_aux on a, starting at A p_aux and ending at p_aux, then the
bridge1+r_ext. Its next point is -r_ext p_aux=z_0, exactly the supplied
tail start. On the inserted points use f=<p_aux,x>-||p_aux||^2/2.

The scalar base is clip(x,-r_ext/D,1), starting at A; its primitive energy
is zero by the saturated-cut identity. The auxiliary old/new data can be
mixed with this base exactly as in partA, PROVIDED

    <p_aux,y_end><=delta_end.                                  (5)

For completeness, the active cross checks differ from partA as follows.
Tail-to-inserted-end constraints have Q_aux=Q_(tail,star)<=0 because the
inserted endpoint has x=g=p_aux and f=||p_aux||^2/2. Inserted-to-tail-end
constraints have the common value <p_aux,y_end>-delta_end, which is
nonpositive exactly by(5). Every other possibly positive cross constraint
has strictly negative base slack. The same finite positive minimum
therefore gives a legal mixture, including all zero-step duplicates and
all optimum constraints. This proves interpolation, not negativity yet.

Let Sigma_I=sum_(j<m) b_j I_j_star be the weighted ACTUAL tail optimum
interpolation slack. Applying (1) separately to the tail and auxiliary
full array, and using A^2/r_ext^2=kappa_lift, gives the exact identity

    V_aux=kappa_lift V_b+Penalty,

    Penalty=(kappa_lift-1)
                  [||y_end||^2+2 I_m_star+2 Sigma_I]
              +[2T_tot(T_tot-D)/D] delta_end.                  (6)

Every term of Penalty is nonnegative. Here
I_m_star=<g_m,y_end>-delta_end; substitution of
z_m=g_m+y_end into (1) verifies (6) term by term. In particular, a negative
tail V_b alone does NOT imply V_aux<0. A valid defect-lifting certificate
must keep this complete penalty and require kappa_lift V_b+Penalty<0.

At a core endpoint, (5) is automatic and delta_end=I_m_star=0, so

    V_aux=kappa_lift V_b+2(kappa_lift-1)Sigma_I.                (7)

When additionally every weighted incoming optimum slack vanishes,
Sigma_I=0, the negative energy scales exactly by kappa_lift. The new
two-cut Huber construction is in this special class. Discarding Sigma_I
outside it would repeat the same wrong-sign loss of value information
that obstructed the earlier mixed-moment state.

## C. The exact criterion for moving the minimum to the final proximal point

There is a precise normalization test; a reset cannot be presumed. For any
finite fully legal transcript without fixing a particular optimum, define
delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2 for every sample, including the terminal one. Add
the proposed optimum jet

    x_star_new=x_n-g_n, g_star_new=0, f_star_new=delta_n.

Keeping ALL original samples, a convex 1-smooth interpolant with this new
optimum exists if and only if

    delta_n<=delta_i for every i.                              (8)

Necessity and sufficiency are both explicit. The new interpolation edges
are Q_(i,star_new)=Q_(i,n)<=0 and
Q_(star_new,i)=delta_n-delta_i. The former already hold in the full
transcript; the latter are exactly(8). When they all hold, translate the
new optimum to(0,0,0) and use the finite interpolation construction of
fact1252b8823bb5a290. Translation changes no GD displacement or primitive
energy and makes x_n=g_n. This supplies a core-ended witness with exactly
the original V_h. When (8) fails, such a preserved-data normalization is
impossible.

For a concrete failure, f(x)=x^2/4, h=(5), x0=1 has
x1=-3/2, g0=1/2, g1=-3/4, f0=1/4, f1=9/16. Thus
delta0=1/8 and delta1=9/32. The proposed new optimum is at-3/4 with
value9/32, and its edge to sample0 violates interpolation by
delta1-delta0=5/32>0. The transcript has V_h=-25<0, so even a genuinely
negative primitive-energy example need not admit this particular
normalization. This does NOT exclude a different core-ended counterexample
for the same schedule; indeed this one-step schedule has others.

## Scope and useful next test

These interfaces give necessary inheritance rules at saturated primitive
cuts, and an exact penalty away from the special all-tight tail class.
They retain all actual prefix interpolation and an explicit fixed-function
realization. They neither provide an improved objective certificate nor
prove that arbitrary primitive failures have core-ended witnesses. The
preserved-data normalization is now exactly characterized by(8), and can
fail on a negative-energy instance. Existence of some OTHER core-ended
witness for every nonprimitive schedule is still a separate closure claim;
no all-schedule induction may assume it.

author: max2
claim: Terminal sharpness NECESSITY candidate: for every nonnegative prefix h of sum S, rho_last(h)=q_S iff W(h,psi(S,0))=q_S iff the FULL intrinsic primitive energy V_h is nonnegative on every legal trajectory iff V_h has a complete finite-pair nonnegative/PSD certificate. Equality forces unique final b, terminal support star/last, no star-outgoing prefix multipliers, and exact star-incoming weights.
evidence:
# Terminal sum-guard equality is equivalent to intrinsic primitivity

Status: complete UNVERIFIED candidate. No additional fact_submit is allocated.
The accepted predecessors are1252b8823bb5a290 and b98bb807d514e80d. The
known primitive-energy functional is already used in max4's shared research;
the new point here is NECESSITY from sharpness of the terminal sum guard.
No unverified terminal minimax or guard candidate is a proof premise.

## 1. Definitions and the equivalence

Fix k>=0 and a finite nonnegative prefix h_pre=(h_0,...,h_(k-1)). Put
S=sum h_pre and define

    t=(-1+sqrt(8S+9))/4,
    b_S=1+t,
    r=1/(2t+1),
    q_S=r^2=1/[1+2(S+b_S)].                            (1)

Thus t(2t+1)=S+1, t=r(S+1), and 1-r=2r^2(S+1).
Let rho_last=inf_(b>=0) W_(k+1)(h_pre,b), in the original project
normalization. It is always at least q_S.

For a smoothness-one trajectory of the prefix, with arbitrary initial
point and any minimizer, define the translation-invariant intrinsic energy

    V_prim(h_pre)=2sum_(i<k) h_i(f_i-f_k)
       +sum_(i<k)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
       -S(S+1)||g_k||^2.                              (2)

Here f_i are function values, g_i are gradients, and the GD recursion is
x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i. In arbitrary smoothness L, use f_i/L and g_i=grad f(x_i)/L.
The value in(2) is unchanged by a common additive shift of all function values.

The following four statements are equivalent:

(A) rho_last(h_pre)=q_S.

(B) W_(k+1)(h_pre,b_S)=q_S.

(C) V_prim(h_pre)>=0 on EVERY finite-dimensional legal convex 1-smooth
    trajectory with a minimizer.

(D) There are nonnegative coefficients eta_ij on distinct finite-prefix
    pairs i,j in {0,...,k} such that

      V_prim(h_pre)+sum_(i!=j)eta_ij Q_ij                (3)

    is PSD on the FULL formal space of (g_0,...,g_k), after substituting
    the prefix GD positions. All value coefficients cancel. Equivalently,
    the finite-node flow of eta is

      out_i-in_i=-2h_i,       i<k,
      out_k-in_k=2S.

When (A) holds, b_S is the unique optimal final step. Leading, interior,
trailing and all-zero prefixes are included in the equivalence.

## 2. The universal lower guard and its equality location

Accepted fact b98bb807d514e80d gives, for every b>=0,

    W_(k+1)(h_pre,b)
       >=max{1/[1+2(S+b)], (b-1)_+^2/(S+1)^2}.         (4)

The first term decreases strictly; the second increases strictly for b>1.
They meet at b=b_S and value q_S, by(1). Thus rho_last>=q_S, and (B)
implies (A) with the asserted unique step.

To justify (A) implies (B) without using the unverified minimax result,
take a sequence b_j with W(h_pre,b_j)->q_S. The continuous lower envelope
in(4) has unique minimizer b_S and tends to infinity as b tends to infinity,
so b_j->b_S. The function W(h_pre,b) is lower semicontinuous: for every
fixed actual prefix instance its last objective is a continuous function
of b, and W is the supremum of these functions in the same normalization.
Therefore W(h_pre,b_S)<=liminf_j W(h_pre,b_j)=q_S. The reverse follows
from(4), proving (B). This argument needs no prior existence theorem for
an optimal final step.

## 3. Sufficiency of the intrinsic energy: an explicit identity

Normalize the minimizer to zero. Append b_S, write n=k+1, and put

    V=r[x_k-(S+2)g_k].

The following algebraic identity holds on every formal trajectory:

    q_S||x_0||^2-2f_n
      +2q_S sum_(i<k)h_i Q_(i,star)
      +2q_S(S+2) Q_(k,star)
      +2r Q_(n,star)+2(1-r)Q_(n,k)
          =||g_n-V||^2+q_S V_prim(h_pre).             (5)

One derivation is to apply the terminal-square expansion in accepted
fact1252b8823bb5a290 with alpha_star=r, alpha_k=1-r and every other
terminal weight zero. It gives V=x_n-(1-r)(x_k-g_k), which equals the
displayed V because b_S-1+r=t+r=r(S+2). After expanding its remaining
prefix terms and using

    ||x_0||^2-||x_k||^2
       =sum_(i<k)[2h_i<x_i,g_i>-h_i^2||g_i||^2],

the star terms cancel every <x_i,g_i>, and the remaining expression is
exactly q_S times(2). This checks (5) without any assumption that its
prefix remainder is PSD on unrestricted data.

If (C) holds, the RHS of(5) is nonnegative on every actual trajectory.
All Q terms on the LHS are nonpositive with nonnegative coefficients.
Thus 2f_n<=q_S||x_0||^2 and W(h_pre,b_S)<=q_S. Equation(4) gives equality.
This proves (C)=>(B) directly, without needing a finite multiplier
representation in advance. The implication (D)=>(C) follows from(3)
because all finite Q are nonpositive on actual trajectories.

## 4. Necessity: two explicit equality instances force the terminal support

First assume all k prefix steps are positive, allowing k=0, and assume (B).
By accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290, select a tight full nonnegative-flow PSD
certificate at level q_S with no incoming terminal multipliers. Write its
outgoing probabilities as alpha_j=lambda_(n,j)/2 for j in {star,0,...,k}.

Consider the scalar Huber function with derivative clamp(x,[-q_S,q_S]),
started at x_0=1. If P_i=sum_(u<i)h_u, its prefix points and gradients are

    x_i=1-q_S P_i,    g_i=q_S.

The final point is 1-q_S(S+b_S), still strictly in its positive linear
region, and its normalized error is q_S. Moreover, at EVERY prefix sample,

    delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2
            =q_S[1-q_S(P_i+1)]>0.                    (6)

The inequality uses P_i<=S and q_S(S+1)=r t=(1-r)/2<1.
Every star-outgoing prefix residual Q_(star,i)=-delta_i is strictly negative.
Complementarity in the accepted full certificate therefore forces

    lambda_(star,i)=0,       0<=i<=k.                  (7)

Next use the scalar capped quadratic with derivative min(c,x), c=1/(S+1),
also started at1. Its whole prefix remains on the right affine branch:

    x_i=1-cP_i,   g_i=c,   x_k=c.

The appended step sends it to x_n=-ct and gradient g_n=-ct. Its normalized
error is c^2t^2=q_S. For i<k the outgoing terminal residual is exactly

    Q_(n,i)=-b_S c^2(S-P_i)<0,                        (8)

while Q_(n,k)=Q_(n,star)=0. To check(8), start from Q_(n,k)=0, then increase
the old point from c to x_i=c+c(S-P_i). Its old value increases by c times
that displacement while its pairing with g_n changes by -ct times that
displacement. The resulting difference is -(1+t)c^2(S-P_i).
Strict positivity of the prefix steps makes S-P_i>0 for every i<k.
Complementarity now forces alpha_i=0 for every i<k.

Thus only alpha_star and alpha_k=1-alpha_star remain. Evaluate the terminal
square on the Huber equality trajectory. The accepted fact gives g_n=V_alpha,
so

    q_S=alpha_star(1-Sq_S)-(t+alpha_star)q_S.

Equivalently,

    alpha_star[1-(S+1)q_S]=(t+1)q_S.

The bracket is positive, and(1) gives its unique solution

    alpha_star=r,   alpha_k=1-r.                      (9)

All these restrictions hold for every selected optimal certificate of
the stated no-incoming-terminal type. They were deduced from actual scalar
equality functions, not from a rank guess or an assumed sparse prefix.

## 5. Full PSD forces the remaining optimum multipliers

The accepted terminal remainder is

    R_alpha=q_S||x_0||^2-2(1-r)delta_k
             -r^2||x_k-(S+2)g_k||^2
             +sum_(i!=j in {star,0,...,k})lambda_ij Q_ij.

It is PSD on the FULL original prefix formal space. By(7), no multiplier
points out of star. Let mu_i=lambda_(i,star). Its x_0-square coefficient
is q_S-r^2=0. A PSD matrix with a zero diagonal entry has a zero row:
on any two-coordinate restriction, a nonzero off-diagonal entry would make
the quadratic negative for one sufficiently small signed second coordinate.
Therefore every x_0--gradient cross coefficient in R_alpha vanishes.

Finite-pair Q_ij have no x_0 cross term after the GD substitution, because
x_j-x_i does not contain x_0. The star terms contribute -mu_i<x_0,g_i>.
Expansion of the negative square then forces

    mu_i=2q_S h_i,       i<k,
    mu_k=2q_S(S+2).                                  (10)

No interpolation multiplier on a finite queried-prefix pair is discarded.
Substitute(10), divide by q_S, and use the telescoping calculation in(5).
The result is exactly

    R_alpha/q_S=V_prim(h_pre)
           +sum_(i!=j in {0,...,k})(lambda_ij/q_S)Q_ij.

This is PSD on the full gradient formal space, and each eta_ij=lambda_ij/q_S
is nonnegative. All value coefficients cancel because they already cancel
in R_alpha. Their coefficients give precisely the finite flows in(D).
Thus (B)=>(D), completing the equivalence for positive prefixes.

## 6. Zero-step lifting and the empty prefix

Delete zero prefix steps and select as representatives each original
positive-step query index, with original index k representing the last
prefix query. Actual coincident queries have identical gradients and values:
adding their two Q inequalities gives ||g_i-g_j||^2<=0, and their values
then agree. The original and compressed schedules therefore have identical
S, b_S, q_S, W and rho_last.

The energy(2) is also unchanged by this compression. Terms at zero steps
have coefficient zero, while the final gradient is the selected original
g_k. Hence condition(C) is equivalent on the two schedules.

If (B) holds, apply the positive-prefix proof to the compressed schedule
and lift its finite eta multipliers by the representative-index map.
All other eta vanish. Every mapped finite Q is the corresponding compressed
Q as an identity in independent original formal vectors, because the
omitted h coefficients are zero. The lifted quadratic(3) is the congruence
of the compressed PSD matrix with the coordinate-selection map. Unused
gradient columns are zero; no equality between duplicated formal gradients
is needed for PSD. This proves(D) in the full ORIGINAL formal space.

For an empty or all-zero prefix, S=0, V_prim=0, b_S=3/2, q_S=1/4, and
eta=0 is a certificate in(D). The sufficiency identity(5) proves the upper
value, and(4) proves the lower value and uniqueness. These cases therefore
require no strictness or Slater assumption.

## 7. What this does and does not close

The result characterizes exactly WHEN the sum-based terminal lower guard
is sharp: the complete prefix must satisfy the full intrinsic primitive
energy inequality, equivalently its full finite-pair PSD certificate.
It supplies a necessity statement for the single terminal ConPD bridge
psi(S,0), not merely the familiar sufficiency of composing a primitive
prefix with an empty terminal block.

The primitive energy itself is not new; it is already present in shared
findings504a69a1e000d6aa and2973c2322cdee545. Their numerical probes and
unverified composition statements are not premises here. The accepted
terminal reduction is what forces(7)-(10) and the complete finite certificate.

An arbitrary globally optimal longer schedule need not attain this particular
sum-only guard. A dominant terminal block can have several steps, and its
earlier prefix is not thereby primitive. Nor does this equivalence bound
the largest sum of a primitive prefix of a fixed length. Those are distinct
unresolved bridges to the original asymptotic target.

    t=(-1+sqrt(8S+9))/4,  b_0=1+t,
    r=1/(2t+1),  q=r^2,  c=1/(S+1).

    V_prim=2sum_(i<k)h_i(f_i-f_k)

finite construction gives a normalized legal prefix and one fixed convex
1-smooth function F whose trajectory under h_pre satisfies, for EVERY b>=0,

    2F(x_k-b g_k) >= q+epsilon Delta/2 > q.             (2)

Gram/jet operations below. Therefore

    inf_(b>=0) W_(k+1)(h_pre,b) >= q+epsilon Delta/2.    (3)

negative-energy witness, its normalization, and the prefix geometry; no
horizon-uniform comparison with the exact Zhang--Jiang profile is claimed.

First compress zero steps. Energy(1) is unchanged, since a zero step's
coefficient vanishes and the final query can be retained as representative.
The all-zero case has V_prim=0, so a negative witness leaves a nonempty
positive prefix. Work with that prefix until restoring duplicates at the end.

We may first arrange that the k+1 prefix gradients are linearly independent,
while retaining a negative energy. If they are not, take a direct sum with a
small positively weighted actual quadratic prefix whose gradients are independent.
Such an auxiliary prefix is obtained from k+1 distinct eigenvalues in(0,1):
the gradients evaluate z P_i(z), where P_i(z)=product_(u<i)(1-h_u z), and
the P_i have distinct degrees0,...,k with nonzero leading coefficients.
After division of each row by its nonzero eigenvalue this is an invertible
polynomial evaluation matrix. Choose all initial coordinates nonzero.

Energy(1) is linear in the Gram/value data of a direct sum. If the original
energy is -D_0<0 and the auxiliary energy is E_aux, a weight
0<zeta<=D_0/[2(D_0+|E_aux|)] keeps the combined energy at most -D_0/2.
Its gradient Gram matrix is positive definite. This direct sum is an actual
smooth convex function and supplies every finite-prefix Q inequality.

For this independent-gradient prefix choose

    f_*<min_(0<=i<=k)(f_i-||g_i||^2/2).

Solve the finite linear system for z_*:

    <g_i,z_*>=f_*-f_i+<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2,
                         0<=i<=k.                    (4)

Independence guarantees a solution, for example in the span of the gradients
using their positive definite Gram matrix. Append the jet(z_*,0,f_*).
Then EVERY outgoing optimum residual Q_(i,*) is zero, while EVERY incoming
one is strictly negative:

    Q_(*,i)=f_*-f_i+||g_i||^2/2<0.

All finite-prefix inequalities are unchanged. Translate z_* to zero and
subtract f_* from all values. The interpolation construction in the accepted
fact gives a globally convex 1-smooth function with exactly those jets and
minimum zero. Its initial distance R=||x_0-z_*|| is positive; if it were zero,
the nonzero independent g_0 would be the gradient at a minimizer.

It now satisfies

The chosen minimizer is allowed to differ from the original witness's
minimizer. Every interpolation direction has been checked before making
that change; no function value or normalization is independently reset.

and let C have derivative min(c,x) and value C(0)=0. Use the fixed product

    F_A(z_1,z_2)=omega A(z_1/sqrt(omega))
                 +(1-omega)C(z_2/sqrt(1-omega)),
    x_0^A=(sqrt(omega),sqrt(1-omega)).

Both coordinate functions are convex differentiable and 1-smooth; hence
so is F_A, with minimum zero. For P_i=sum_(u<i)h_u its full prefix is

    x_i^A=x_0^A-P_i g_A,
    g_A=(sqrt(omega)q,sqrt(1-omega)c).

The first scalar coordinate stays above q because q(S+1)<1; the second
stays at least c because c(S+1)=1. Thus these gradients and positions are
the actual full trajectory for the prescribed order of h_pre.
Define its prefix proximal data y_i^A=x_i^A-g_A and
delta_i^A=F_A(x_i^A)-||g_A||^2/2. At its terminal point for b_0, put

    w_A=(sqrt(omega)q,-sqrt(1-omega)c t).

Direct scalar evaluation gives the following identities:

    <g_A,w_A>=0,
    2<x_k^A,w_A>-||w_A||^2=q,

For the last identity, the second coordinate is immediate and the first
reduces to r[1-q(S+1)]=(1+t)q. The remaining identities follow by evaluating

zero outgoing interpolation residual to the optimum.

The two vectors g_A and y_k^A are independent: y_k^A has positive first
coordinate and zero second coordinate, while g_A has positive second
coordinate. For each earlier i<k the exact inactive-plane margin is

    margin_i:=delta_i^A-<y_i^A,w_A>
          =(1-omega)b_0 c^2(S-P_i)>0.                 (7)

This follows by evaluating the capped-coordinate terminal-to-i residual;
the Huber coordinate's corresponding residual is zero. Positive compressed
steps guarantee S-P_i>0.

## 4. The negative energy provides a positive perturbation slope

For prefix B set

    y_i^B=x_i^B-g_i^B,  delta_i^B=f_i^B-||g_i^B||^2/2,
    V_B=x_k^B-b_0 g_k^B-(1-r)y_k^B,
    Phi_B=2(1-r)delta_k^B+||V_B||^2,
    Delta=-q E_B>0.

||x_0^B||^2-||x_k^B||^2 along GD:

      +2q sum_(i<k)h_i Q_(i,star)^B
      +2q(S+2)Q_(k,star)^B=q E_B.

Indeed V_B=r[x_k^B-(S+2)g_k^B], because t+r=r(S+2). Expansion cancels
all x_i--g_i pairings against the star terms and leaves precisely(1).
Using the normalization and saturation in(5), it follows that

    Phi_B=q+Delta.                                    (8)

Let u_1 be the unique vector in span(g_A,y_k^A) solving

    <g_A,u_1>=-<g_k^B,V_B>,
    <y_k^A,u_1>=delta_k^B-<y_k^B,V_B>.                 (9)

Its existence follows from the positive definite two-vector Gram matrix
identified after(6). Put D=||u_1||^2>=0 and for i<k put

    remote_i=delta_i^B-<y_i^B,V_B>-<y_i^A,u_1>.

Choose explicitly

    epsilon=min{1/2, Delta/[2(D+Delta)],
                    min_(i<k) margin_i/[2(margin_i+|remote_i|)]}. (10)

Every entry is positive, so 0<epsilon<=1/2. Computing u_1 requires only
a two-by-two linear system; no optimization or numerical sweep is involved.

    x_i^C=(sqrt(1-epsilon)x_i^A,sqrt(epsilon)x_i^B),
    g_i^C=(sqrt(1-epsilon)g_A,sqrt(epsilon)g_i^B),
    f_i^C=(1-epsilon)f_i^A+epsilon f_i^B.

It is realized by the corresponding scaled product of the two legal
functions. Its initial squared norm is one, its minimum value is zero,
and every ordered prefix Q is the same convex combination of the two
valid Q values. Thus it retains the complete prefix, not just selected edges.
Define one FIXED terminal test vector

    w_C=(sqrt(1-epsilon)[w_A+epsilon u_1/(1-epsilon)],
                                          sqrt(epsilon)V_B).

Equation(9) gives <g_k^C,w_C>=0. For the last prefix plane its other
equation gives delta_k^C-<y_k^C,w_C>=0. For EVERY earlier plane,

    delta_i^C-<y_i^C,w_C>
        =(1-epsilon)margin_i+epsilon remote_i
                                      >=margin_i/2>0, (11)

where the last inequality follows from(10). The optimum plane has value zero.
Consequently the maximum of the prefix conjugate affine planes at w_C is
EXACTLY zero. No earlier plane can defeat the displayed terminal lower bound.

## 6. An exact gain expression for one globally legal function

By accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 the maximal prefix interpolant

    F=[v -> ||v||^2/2+max_j(<y_j^C,v>-delta_j^C)]^*

is a globally convex differentiable 1-smooth function with minimum zero,
interpolating EVERY prefix jet C. Its trajectory under h_pre is therefore
exactly C. The test-vector orthogonality and(11) imply, for EVERY b>=0,

    2F(x_k^C-b g_k^C)
       >=2<x_k^C,w_C>-||w_C||^2=Gamma_epsilon.

Expanding this final expression, then using(6) and(9), gives

    Gamma_epsilon
       =(1-epsilon)q+epsilon Phi_B
                             -epsilon^2 D/(1-epsilon)
       =q+epsilon Delta-epsilon^2 D/(1-epsilon).        (12)

For clarity, the cross term from the A block is
2epsilon<b_0 g_A+(1-r)y_k^A,u_1>. Combined with the B block this equals

    epsilon[2<x_k^B,V_B>-||V_B||^2
       -2b_0<g_k^B,V_B>
       +2(1-r)(delta_k^B-<y_k^B,V_B>)]=epsilon Phi_B,

by the definition of V_B. This checks every term in(12).

The second bound in(10) gives

    epsilon D/(1-epsilon)<=Delta D/(2D+Delta)<=Delta/2.

Substituting in(12) proves(2)-(3). F is fixed before the final step is chosen;
the same single test vector proves its bound on the entire nonnegative ray.

Restore zero steps by repeating their actual query jets. The duplicate
conjugate planes add nothing to the finite maximum, and every trajectory
identity is unchanged. The actual normalized initial distance remains one.
For any prescribed L>0, replace F with L F and divide its objective by L.

The construction turns ANY concrete failure of intrinsic primitivity into
an explicit strictly stronger final-stage lower bound. Its gain can be small
because the saturation radius, independent-gradient perturbation, and remote
anchor margins can deteriorate. Controlling those constants along a whole

evidence:
# Exact positive-level terminal policy for a retained Markov prefix

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof candidate. No verifier or numerical solver call.
This is a conditional constructive theorem for every prefix in the stated
class, not an assertion that every prescribed schedule has a prefix in this
class with the required benchmark payoff. All new algebra is proved here.

## 1. The retained prefix and its full data

Work with smoothness one in a Euclidean space. Let a prescribed prefix be
partitioned into nonnegative ordinary blocks of sums s_0,...,s_m, separated
by checkpoints b_0,...,b_(m-1). Put C_i=s_i+1. Choose

    a_i=b_i-1>0,  0<beta_i<=a_i/C_(i+1),
    alpha_0=1/C_0,
    alpha_(i+1)^2=(a_i beta_i/C_(i+1)) alpha_i^2,
    g_0=alpha_0 e_0,
    g_(i+1)=-beta_i g_i+v_(i+1),

where v_(i+1) is orthogonal to the entire previously used space and has
squared norm alpha_i^2 beta_i(a_i/C_(i+1)-beta_i). The e_0 vector is unit.
Set X_0=e_0, X_(i+1)=X_i-(s_i+b_i)g_i, and

    Z_i=X_i-C_i g_i.

For j<i define

    P_(j,i)=product_(j<=l<i) beta_l,
    Q_(j,i)=product_(j<=l<i) a_l/C_(l+1),
    R_l=a_l-C_(l+1)beta_l,
    H_(j,i)=sum_(l=j)^(i-1) (-1)^(l-j) R_l P_(j,l),

where empty products equal one. Direct induction gives

    ||g_i||^2=alpha_i^2,
    <g_j,g_i>=(-1)^(i-j) alpha_j^2 P_(j,i),
    alpha_i^2=alpha_j^2 P_(j,i)Q_(j,i),
    <g_j,Z_i>=-alpha_j^2 H_(j,i)  (j<i),
    <g_j,Z_i>=0                   (j>=i).           (1)

For the last equality, Z_0=0 and
Z_(i+1)-Z_i=-a_i g_i-C_(i+1)g_(i+1). Its inner product
with g_(i+1) is zero by the displayed gradient recurrence. Every later
gradient is a scalar multiple of g_(i+1) plus a vector orthogonal to this
increment. The formula for an earlier gradient follows by substituting
its signed product correlation and summing these increments. This also
proves all identities in (1), without citing an unverified finding.

Assume the following explicitly checkable prefix inequalities hold:

    H_(j,i)>=s_i P_(j,i)[(-1)^(i-j)-Q_(j,i)]_+
                                                   for j<i,           (2)
    P_(j,i)<=1             for j<i, i-j even, s_j>0.                  (3)

Here [t]_+=max(t,0). In particular every H_(j,i) is nonnegative.
Define J_old(z)=max(0,<g_0,z>,...,<g_m,z>). The actual queries in
block i, after an ordinary partial sum u in [0,s_i], have position
Z_i+(C_i-u)g_i and proposed proximal point Z_i+(s_i-u)g_i.
Its selected plane g_i has value (s_i-u)alpha_i^2. Equations (1)-(2)
compare every old plane with it; (1) and (3) compare every future plane.
The zero plane is dominated too. Thus g_i is a subgradient of J_old at
this proximal point and the complete prescribed prefix is realized by
f_old=env_1 J_old. Every endpoint Z_i has value zero. The intermediate
partial sums require no extra condition because each comparison is
affine in u and its endpoints are included.

For completeness, for any finite maximum J of linear functions including
zero, its proximal minimizer z(x) is unique. If g=x-z(x), the subgradient
optimality condition is g in partial J(z(x)). Monotonicity of partial J
gives ||g(x)-g(y)||^2<=<g(x)-g(y),x-y>. Comparing the two minimizing
expressions in the envelope and using this Lipschitz bound shows
env_1 J is differentiable with gradient g and is convex and 1-smooth.
This supplies the fixed smooth function used below.

## 2. Append one whole terminal block, preserving every old query

Append a checkpoint of size b=1+A with A>0, followed by an arbitrary
nonnegative block of sum C-1, where C>=1. The bridge uses the existing
endpoint gradient g_m, so the next start is X_new=Z_m-A g_m.
Choose a level parameter T>=C and beta with 0<beta<=A/T. In one new
orthogonal direction set

    g_new=-beta g_m+v_new,
    ||v_new||^2=alpha_m^2 beta(A/T-beta),
    Z_new=X_new-T g_new.

Set J=max(J_old,<g_new,z>) and f=env_1 J. In the new ordinary block
the proposed proximal points have form Z_new+d g_new with
T-C<=d<=T-1. The final proximal height is
(T-C)||g_new||^2, and the squared gradient is

    ||g_new||^2=(A beta/T)alpha_m^2.                 (4)

Only old indices j<m with m-j odd can obstruct the extension. For each
such j retain

    p_j=P_(j,m), q_j=Q_(j,m), c_j=H_(j,m)/p_j>=0,
    D_j=A q_j, E_j=A-c_j.

Define the future-plane cap

    U=min_{j<m, m-j odd, s_j>0} 1/p_j,             (5)

with empty minimum +infinity. At old positive-height queries the new
plane is dominated exactly when beta<=U. Indeed (1) makes its intercept
zero there and its relative positive slope is beta p_j. At old zero
height queries all new-plane values are zero. Old indices of the other
parity give negative slopes and no additional condition.

For an index j of the obstructing parity, subtracting the selected new
plane at Z_new+d g_new and dividing by alpha_j^2 p_j gives exactly

    -c_j+A-T beta+d beta(1-D_j/T).                 (6)

Consequently define, for T>=C,

    F_j(T)=C+D_j-C D_j/T,             if T<=D_j,
           1+D_j-D_j/T,               if T>=D_j.  (7)

The formulas agree at T=D_j whenever this point belongs to the domain.
The maximum of (6) over d in [T-C,T-1] is nonpositive exactly when

    beta F_j(T)>=E_j.                             (8)

For all other old indices, the new signed residual is the old
nonnegative residual plus p_j(A-T beta), and the new correlation has
negative sign. Their comparisons therefore hold automatically. This
includes g_m. The zero plane is dominated because T-C>=0.

Thus (5), (8), and 0<beta<=A/T are NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT for the
specified new samples to come from the same fixed J while retaining all
prefix samples. There is no removal of a queried interpolation condition.

Origin remains a closest minimizer to e_0. In fact J>=0, J(0)=0, and
the retained g_0=e_0/C_0 plane forces <e_0,z><=0 at every zero of J.
The envelope has the same zero set: a zero minimum in its defining
nonnegative sum requires z=x and J(z)=0. Hence every minimizer is at
distance at least one from e_0, with equality attained at origin. The
EXACT normalized final objective is

    V(T,beta)=alpha_m^2 A beta(2T-2C+1)/T.         (9)

## 3. Eliminate all continuous feasibility choices explicitly

Indices with E_j<=0 give no constraint in (8), since F_j is positive.
For each remaining index, 0<E_j<=A. Its square-root endpoint is

    T_j^+ = [A(1+D_j)
                +sqrt(A^2(1+D_j)^2-4 A D_j E_j)]/(2E_j).             (10)

The radicand is at least A^2(D_j-1)^2. The PSD upper choice beta<=A/T
can satisfy (8) exactly when T<=T_j^+, for T>=C. To prove this, if
C<=T<=D_j, then

    F_j(T)-T=-(T-C)(T-D_j)/T>=0,

so A F_j(T)>=E_j T holds. For T>=max(C,D_j), the same inequality is

    E_j T^2-A(1+D_j)T+A D_j<=0.

This convex quadratic is nonpositive at both 1 and D_j, since E_j<=A.
Thus its smaller root is no greater than min(1,D_j), and on the stated
domain the condition is precisely T<=T_j^+. Also T_j^+>=max(1,D_j),
so the first range creates no missing case.

The future cap can satisfy (8) exactly when F_j(T)>=z_j:=E_j/U, where
z_j=0 if U=+infinity. F_j is continuous and strictly increasing, with
limit 1+D_j. If z_j>=1+D_j, no finite T is feasible. Otherwise its
exact lower endpoint is

    T_j^- = C,                         if z_j<=F_j(C),
            C D_j/(C+D_j-z_j),         if F_j(C)<z_j<=D_j,
            D_j/(1+D_j-z_j),           otherwise.                  (11)

The middle case automatically implies C<D_j. The last case has a
positive denominator by the previously checked strict inequality.

Set

    T_min=max(C, max_j T_j^-),
    T_max=min_j T_j^+,                                      (12)

over indices with E_j>0. Empty maxima contribute no bound and an empty
minimum is +infinity. There is an extension exactly when no index has
z_j>=1+D_j and T_min<=T_max. Its ENTIRE set of possible T is the closed
interval [T_min,T_max]. At each T in this interval the allowed beta is

    max(0,max_j E_j/F_j(T)) <= beta <= min(A/T,U),  beta>0.             (13)

This is an explicit policy from the actual retained history, rather than
an assertion that feasible scales exist. Positive finite T_min is always
attained. If T_max is infinite, the optimum below is still finite.

## 4. Closed-form best payoff for this frozen prefix

At fixed T, (9) increases in beta, so choose beta_max=min(A/T,U).
Put d=2C-1, and interpret A/U=0 when U=+infinity. Before imposing the
interval (12), the payoff is increasing up to

    T_peak=max(d,A/U)

and decreasing thereafter. Indeed for T<=A/U it is
alpha_m^2 A U(2-d/T), a strictly increasing function. For T>=A/U it
is alpha_m^2 A^2(2T-d)/T^2, whose derivative has the sign of d-T.
Since C>=1, d>=C, so T_peak lies in the original domain. The exact
constrained optimizer is therefore

    T_opt=min(T_max,max(T_min,T_peak)),
    beta_opt=min(A/T_opt,U),
    V_opt=alpha_m^2 A beta_opt(2T_opt-2C+1)/T_opt.       (14)

All quantities in (10)-(14) are obtained by finitely many scalar
operations on already retained data. No optimization oracle, parameter
limit, dimension-dependent normalization, or hidden vanishing scale is
used. The prefix may have any finite number of checkpoints and arbitrary
nonnegative ordinary blocks. Its physical boundary magnitude alpha_m is
retained in (14), rather than silently normalized away.

## 5. Positive levels can repair a genuinely impossible zero-level join

For any M>1 take three arbitrary ordinary blocks each of sum M-1, and
the two checkpoints 4M+1 and 2M+1. On the first two blocks choose
beta_0=2, alpha_0=1/M. Then

    ||g_1||^2=8/M^2, R_0=2M,
    p_0=2, q_0=4, c_0=M,
    A=2M, C=M, D_0=8M, E_0=M, U=1/2.

The old prefix is legal: its only earlier-plane residual is 2M>=0 and
the future correlation is negative. At T=C=M, inequality (8) requires
beta>=1, while the old-query future bound requires beta<=1/2. Thus NO
zero-level new block is legal for this exact frozen prefix.

Equations (10)-(14) instead give

    T_min=8M/7,
    T_max=1+8M+sqrt(64M^2+1),
    T_opt=4M, beta_opt=1/2,
    V_opt=12/M+2/M^2.                                  (15)

At the optimum the terminal gradient is g_new=-g_1/2. In particular the
old frozen prefix needs no change and no new dimension at this optimal
final join. There is also a legal endpoint choice T=T_min=8M/7 and
beta=1/2. There the unqueried residual is H_(0,2)=-6M/7<0, while
P_(0,2)=1, Q_(0,2)=7 and w_2=M/7. Its exact comparison is
H_(0,2)=w_2(1-7); the positive-part term is zero. Its normalized payoff
is 2/M+7/M^2. Thus enforcing that every unqueried Z_i remain a
minimizer would incorrectly reject this legal positive-level continuation.

This example is an arbitrary-block parametric family, not a new uniform
benchmark comparison. The earlier nonperiodic comparison in shared
finding b0bf06c26eb801e6 is a separate complete joint candidate. The
present result supplies an exact arbitrary-prefix terminal policy that
can replace an existential endpoint choice in future work.

## 6. A separate algebraic invariant for internal positive margins

The preceding interval theorem assumes all retained blocks have zero
proximal endpoint value. For further iteration, internal positive
margins cannot be erased. The following exact cancellation describes
their location in the full state.

For a chain with margins w_i>=0, define T_i=s_i+1+w_i and
A_i=b_i-1-w_i>0, and keep the gradient recurrence with these parameters.
For fixed beta_i put

    R_l^w=b_l-1-w_l-(s_(l+1)+1+w_(l+1))beta_l,
    R_l^0=b_l-1-(s_(l+1)+1)beta_l.

Let H^w and H^0 be the corresponding signed residual sums. Every
interior w_l contribution cancels between the two adjacent summands, so

    H^w_(j,i)=H^0_(j,i)-w_j+(-1)^(i-j)P_(j,i)w_i.      (16)

Let Q^w_(j,i)=product_(j<=l<i) A_l/T_(l+1). At the actual proximal
segment d in [w_i,s_i+w_i], the exact old-plane comparison is

    H^w_(j,i)>=w_i P_(j,i)[(-1)^(i-j)-Q^w_(j,i)]
           +s_i P_(j,i)[(-1)^(i-j)-Q^w_(j,i)]_+.

Substituting (16) cancels the parity-dependent endpoint term and gives

    H^0_(j,i)-w_j+w_i P_(j,i)Q^w_(j,i)
          >=s_i P_(j,i)[(-1)^(i-j)-Q^w_(j,i)]_+.        (17)

The nonnegative margin itself is not disposable: it remains at both
endpoints of (17), and every intermediate margin remains in Q^w through
the true squared-gradient ratios. The example in (15) illustrates a
negative H^w at an unqueried residual point with valid positive-height
samples. The interval theorem does not assert a greedy optimum over
future internal cells or an arbitrary-schedule lower bound.

## Retrieval and status

The fact graph was searched before this subgoal. No accepted fact there
provides this positive-level policy. A targeted Matlas query about
Moreau support functions and polygon projections returned projection and
Frank-Wolfe results that are not used. The derivation above is elementary
and does not rely on any new external black box. No fact has been
submitted because the current TASK allocates no additional verifier call.

evidence:
# Exact Huber padding gives a core-ended realization of every primitive defect

Status: complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. No numerical PEP or
fact_submit call. The only fact used is 1252b8823bb5a290, specifically its
finite smooth-convex interpolation construction. This file includes every
new deduction; earlier shared findings are context, not premises.

## 1. Statement and definitions

Fix a finite nonnegative stepsize schedule h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)). Put
s=sum_i h_i, T=1+s, and R_i=sum_(t=i)^(n-1) h_t for 0<=i<=n.
Thus R_n=0. Consider any actual finite convex differentiable 1-smooth
trajectory x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i, with g_i=grad f(x_i), f_i=f(x_i).
Let

  delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2,
  Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
  V_h=2 sum_(i<n) h_i(f_i-f_n)
       +sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-T(T-1)||g_n||^2.

Then there exists another actual trajectory for the SAME h, in at most
one additional dimension, on an everywhere finite convex differentiable
1-smooth function with minimizer0, such that

  x_n_new=g_n_new, f_n_new=||g_n_new||^2/2,
  V_h_new=V_h.

In particular, h has a negative primitive-energy witness if and only if it
has a witness whose endpoint equals its terminal gradient relative to a
minimizer. No preservation of the normalized objective error is asserted.

Here and below a core endpoint means precisely x_n=g_n with optimum0.

## 2. Choose one finite Huber companion

If R_i=0, nonnegativity of h forces every later step to be zero.
Consequently x_i=x_n, g_i=g_n, f_i=f_n and delta_i=delta_n.
Choose any c>0 such that

  c^2 >= max_(i:R_i>0) (delta_n-delta_i)_+/R_i,                 (1)

with empty maximum0 and (a)_+=max(a,0). This is a finite maximum.

Define the fixed scalar Huber function

  H_c(z)=z^2/2                         if |z|<=c,
         c|z|-c^2/2                   if |z|>=c.

Start its GD run at z_0=T c. Every step of the given schedule stays on
its positive affine ray:

  z_i=(1+R_i)c, H_c'(z_i)=c,
  H_c(z_i)=(R_i+1/2)c^2.                                    (2)

These formulas include its final point z_n=c. The derivative is
continuous, nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz, so H_c is a fixed legal
convex differentiable 1-smooth function.

Run the direct sum f(x)+H_c(z). Its exact sampled data are

  X_i=(x_i,(1+R_i)c),
  G_i=(g_i,c),
  F_i=f_i+(R_i+1/2)c^2.                                    (3)

The original-index GD equations hold, including zero steps.

The companion's finite interpolation residual is zero for every ordered
pair: its two gradients are equal and its sampled values are affine.
Therefore

  Q_ij_new=Q_ij_original<=0.                                (4)

Its adjusted values obey

  Delta_i=F_i-||G_i||^2/2=delta_i+R_i c^2>=delta_n=Delta_n.    (5)

For R_i>0 this follows from(1); for R_i=0 it follows from the duplicate
sample observation above. No strictness or limiting argument is needed.

## 3. Add the new optimum, retaining every query jet

Replace the old optimum by the new jet

  X_star_new=X_n-G_n=(x_n-g_n,0),
  G_star_new=0,
  F_star_new=Delta_n=delta_n.                               (6)

The previous optimum, if one was specified, is not retained. All query
jets(3) are retained exactly.

For every query i, direct expansion gives

  Q_(i,star_new)=Q_(i,n)_new=Q_(i,n)_original<=0,
  Q_(star_new,i)=Delta_n-Delta_i<=0.                         (7)

At i=n both quantities are zero. Equations(4),(7) check every ordered
interpolation pair in the enlarged finite data set.

By the finite interpolation construction in fact1252b8823bb5a290, these
data are interpolated by one everywhere finite convex differentiable
1-smooth function with the new optimum jet. Concretely, after translating
the new optimum to0 and its value to0, form

  H(v)=max_(j in {star,0,...,n})
       {<G_j,X_j>-F_j+<X_j,v-G_j>+||v-G_j||^2/2},
  F_new(x)=sup_v {<x,v>-H(v)}.

Here X_j,F_j in the displayed formula denote the translated data.
This is the accepted fact's explicit construction, with the whole
finite set treated as interpolation input. It interpolates every
original-index query and the zero optimum. Translation preserves all
GD differences. At the last query,

  x_n_new=G_n=(g_n,c),
  f_n_new=F_n-delta_n=||G_n||^2/2.                           (8)

The initial displacement is explicitly

  x_0_new=(x_0-x_n+g_n,Tc),

so it is nonzero since c>0.

## 4. Exact preservation of primitive energy

The energy is unchanged by a common translation of positions and a
common subtraction from all function values. It is additive under the
orthogonal direct sum(3). The Huber companion has exactly zero energy:
from(2),

  V_companion/c^2
    =2 sum_i h_i R_i+sum_i h_i(1-h_i)-s(s+1)=0,

because

  2 sum_i h_i R_i=s^2+sum_i h_i^2.

Thus V_h_new=V_h, without an approximation or an unproved inequality.

This supplies a core-ended realization of every negative witness.
The converse follows because a core-ended witness is itself legal.
For n=0 or an all-zero schedule the construction still works, and V_h=0.

## 5. What happens to the retained optimum slacks

After the normalization, the incoming optimum slack is exactly

  I_i_star_new=-Q_(i,n)_original>=0.                         (9)

Thus the construction DOES NOT remove queried-to-terminal interpolation
slack. Define d=x_0-x_n and Sigma_n=-sum_(i<n)h_i Q_(i,n).
Expansion of the definitions gives

  V_h+2 Sigma_n=||d+g_n||^2-T^2||g_n||^2.                    (10)

Equivalently, the core realization has

  ||x_0_new||^2-T^2||g_n_new||^2
     =||d+g_n||^2-T^2||g_n||^2,

independent of c. Padding removes the terminal-adjusted-value obstruction
but leaves exactly the old query-to-terminal slack ledger. This is why
the result does not, by itself, prove tail heredity at a prepended
saturated bridge.

## 6. Exact hostile check: the old direct-reset counterexample

Take f(x)=x^2/4, h=(5), x_0=1. The original data are

  (x_0,x_1)=(1,-3/2),
  (g_0,g_1)=(1/2,-3/4),
  (f_0,f_1)=(1/4,9/16),
  (delta_0,delta_1)=(1/8,9/32),
  V_h=-25.

A direct preserved-data core reset fails because delta_1>delta_0.
Choose c=1/4. Then c^2=1/16>=(delta_1-delta_0)/5=1/32.
After padding and normalizing, the data are

  x_0_new=(7/4,3/2),  g_0_new=(1/2,1/4), f_0_new=5/16,
  x_1_new=(-3/4,1/4), g_1_new=(-3/4,1/4), f_1_new=5/16.

They satisfy x_1_new=x_0_new-5g_0_new and
x_1_new=g_1_new. Their finite Q residuals are unchanged from the legal
original pair; their optimum residuals follow(7). Direct substitution
in the energy gives

  V_h_new=5(1-5)(5/16)-30(5/8)=-25.

Thus the very example that defeats an unpadded reset is repaired
exactly by one extra equality-mode coordinate.

## 7. Saturated append heredity, with the entire proof included

Let b and c_block be any nonnegative physical blocks, with capacities
D=1+sum b_i and C=1+sum(c_block)_i. Let r>0 solve

  T_join=D+C+r, r T_join=DC.                               (11)

If the joined schedule (b,1+r,c_block) is primitive, then b is primitive.
This is a necessary prefix heredity theorem at an exactly saturated
primitive bridge. No primitive assumption about c_block is needed.

Proof by contrapositive. If b is not primitive, sections1-4 turn an
actual negative witness into a legal core-ended witness for b, with
endpoint e=x_m=g_m and value||e||^2/2. Denote its energy V_b<0.

Construct a scalar base Huber run with gradient clip(z,-r/C,1), initial
point D. During b it has gradient1 and ends at1; the bridge lands at-r;
during c_block its gradient is v_base=-r/C and it ends atv_base.
All incoming optimum slacks are zero and the final point equals its
gradient. Squared-distance telescoping therefore gives

  V_base=D^2-T_join^2(r/C)^2=0                             (12)

by(11).

For an auxiliary vector array, retain ALL supplied core-ended b samples.
The new bridge lands at-r e. During c_block use constant gradient

  v_aux=-(r/C)e.

Its starting point is C v_aux, and its terminal point is v_aux.
Assign each new value <v_aux,x>-||v_aux||^2/2. This array is not presumed
legal across the join; the following audit supplies that legality after
mixing.

For epsilon>0, combine base and auxiliary points and gradients in
orthogonal coordinates with auxiliary scale sqrt(epsilon), and combine
their values with scale epsilon. All GD equations are exact.

Every active base interpolation constraint has nonpositive auxiliary
residual:

* Old-old constraints: the auxiliary data are the original legal b run.
* New-new constraints: constant auxiliary gradient makes them zero.
* New-to-old constraints: the base residual can be zero only at an old
  target whose remaining b sum is0. That target is the old core endpoint,
  including any zero-step duplicates. At this target, direct expansion
  gives Q_aux(new,m)=0.
* Old-to-new constraints: the base residual can be zero only at a new
  target whose remaining c_block sum is0. That target has x=g=v_aux,
  so Q_aux(old,new)=Q_aux(old,star)<=0.
* Incoming optimum constraints: old ones are legal; new ones are0.
  Outgoing optimum constraints: old ones are legal; new ones are
  minus the remaining c_block sum times||v_aux||^2, hence nonpositive.

For every auxiliary pair with Q_aux>0 the corresponding base residual
is therefore strictly negative. The finite choice

  epsilon=min(1, min_(Q_aux>0) [-Q_base/(2Q_aux)])

is positive, interpreting the inner minimum as1 when there are no such
pairs. The combined data obey all interpolation constraints, including
both optimum directions and every original zero-step index. The
construction in fact1252b8823bb5a290 realizes one fixed legal function.

For any core-ended legal trajectory of capacityK, distance telescoping
gives

  V=||x_0||^2-K^2||g_end||^2-2sum h_i I_i_star.              (13)

The auxiliary full trajectory is core-ended, adds no new incoming
optimum slack, and its bridge query was already a core endpoint.
Equation(11) gives T_join^2||v_aux||^2=D^2||e||^2.
Using(13) for the old b run and the full auxiliary array yields

  V_aux=V_b.

Together with(12), the fully legal combined trajectory has energy
epsilon V_b<0. This proves the stated contrapositive.

## 8. Scope and the next unmatched condition

The missing existence of SOME core-ended negative witness is settled
by this candidate construction; the old preserved-data reset criterion
remains correct but was not a universal obstruction after dimensional
padding. The saturated-append converse now covers arbitrary primitive
failures in its prefix.

This does not establish a corresponding arbitrary-tail converse for a
prepended saturated bridge. Its complete value/optimum-slack penalty
remains, and(9) identifies the retained quantity exactly. Neither the
original normalized objective ratio nor the unrestricted asymptotic
Zhang-Jiang target follows from this primitive-energy reduction.

No new statement here is in the fact graph. All claims await a selected
verification allocation; they may not be cited downstream as facts.
