evidence:
# All relative phases of two scalar secant bands

Status: complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. No verifier request
is allocated by the current TASK or master guidance. Every new estimate used
in this document is proved here. Earlier C18/C19 findings are motivation,
not premises. The only accepted fact cited is b98bb807d514e80d for the exact
benchmark definitions. No external theorem or numerical search is used.

## 1. Statement

Set c_sc=13/5 and a_sc=c_sc^(-17). Define

    Hsc_0=(), Hsc_(j+1)=(Hsc_j,bsc_j,Hsc_j),
    bsc_j=a_sc c_sc^j, Nsc_j=2^j-1,
    ssc_j=sum Hsc_j=a_sc(c_sc^j-2^j)/(c_sc-2).

Let f be a fixed differentiable convex function on the real line with
1-Lipschitz derivative g, f(0)=0=min f. On the two rays choose arbitrary
constants M_slow,M_fast with 0<M_slow<=M_fast<=1. Either physical ray can
be called slow. Suppose each nonzero queried point on ray sigma satisfies

    M_sigma/c_sc <= |g(x_t)|/|x_t| <= M_sigma.             (1)

The constants, derivative, and initial point can depend on the horizon m.
No relation between the two scales is imposed. The derivative may be
nonperiodic and asymmetric, with any number of knots or repeated visits.
Only the finitely many queried secants are constrained by (1).

Put K_sc=192*27^4 and C_sc=200000*c_sc^3*K_sc^2/a_sc. Then GD under the
complete word Hsc_m, starting from any x_0!=0, satisfies

    2 f(x_(Nsc_m))/x_0^2 <= C_sc c_sc^(-m).              (2)

In particular the supremum over this entire class, divided by the exact
U_(Nsc_m)^ZJ, tends to zero. Each ray's secants must fit in its own band of
width factor13/5, but the two bands can have arbitrary relative scale and
phase. This closes the phase restriction in C19. It is still a restricted
scalar class, not all scalar functions and not unrestricted W.

Within the proof abbreviate c_sc,a_sc,bsc_j,ssc_j by c,a,b_j,S_j. These
are local aliases, unrelated to the Huber slopes c,a in the project glossary.
All matrix products below use maximum and multiplication, not addition.

## 2. Exact two-state upper envelope

For ray sigma put

    d_sigma(j)=(1-b_j M_sigma/c)_+,
    u_sigma(j)=(b_j M_sigma-1)_+,
    B_j=[[d_slow(j),u_fast(j)],[u_slow(j),d_fast(j)]].

Rows denote the output ray, columns the input ray. A scalar step with
queried secant lambda on ray sigma has multiplier1-b_j lambda. Its
same-ray magnitude is at most d_sigma(j), and its opposite-ray magnitude
at most u_sigma(j). A zero coefficient excludes that nonzero transition.

Define (A odot B)_(i,j)=max_k A_(i,k)B_(k,j), and let E_0 be the identity
matrix. The exact recurrence for the relaxed sign-path envelope is

    E_(j+1)=E_j odot B_j odot E_j.                       (3)

Induction by the two intermediate signs in the word decomposition shows
that E_j(output,input) bounds every actual radius ratio. This proves an
upper bound even though independently maximizing its entries need not
produce one legal function. No such realization is asserted.

Let I be the first integer with b_I M_fast>1. Write

    t=b_I M_fast, s=b_I M_slow.

Then I>=18, 1<t<=c, and 0<s<=t. Every checkpoint before I has upper
secant product at most1, so E_I is diagonal. Its entries are

    p_s=p(s), p_f=p(t),
    p(z)=product_(h in Hsc_I)(1-h z/(c b_I)).             (4)

All these factors are positive. With eta=13/8, the sum formula gives
S_I/b_I>=eta: (2/c)^3<1/2 and (2/c)^2<4/5 imply (2/c)^17<1/40.
Consequently

    p(t)/p(s) <= exp[-5(t-s)/8].                         (5)

This follows termwise from log(1-u)-log(1-v)<=-(u-v) for 0<=v<=u<1.
We shall also use, for 0<z<=c,

    p(z) <= exp[-5z/8-z^2/70],  p(z)>1/27.             (6)

For the first inequality, log(1-v)<=-v-v^2/2 and the level counts give

    sum_(h in Hsc_I) h^2/b_I^2
       =[1-(2/c^2)^I]/(c^2-2).

Since 2/c^2<1/3 and I>=18, the coefficient of z^2 in the logarithm is
larger than (26/27)/(2c^2(c^2-2))>1/70. For the lower bound, every
v=h z/(c b_I) is at most1/c, and their sum is at most5/3. Integration
gives log(1-v)>=-v/(1-1/c), so log p(z)>=-65/24>-3. The elementary
factorial-series bound e<3 gives p(z)>1/27.

## 3. A common-band product estimate proved from scratch

For M in (0,1] set

    q_sec(z)=max(1-z/c,z-1),
    P_sec(m,M)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)
                     q_sec(a M c^j)^(2^(m-j-1)).

The empty product is1. We prove

    M P_sec(m,M)^2 <=(60000/a)c^(-m).                    (7)

Let k be the largest integer with y=a M c^k<=13/9. Then k>=17 and
5/9<y<=13/9. The first branch of q_sec holds through k; its second
branch holds afterwards. For m>=k+1, log(1-v)<=-v on levels below k
gives

    log P_sec(m,M)/2^(m-k-1)
      <=-5y/4+log(1-y/c)
          +sum_(ell=1)^(m-k-1)2^(-ell)log(c^ell y-1).    (8)

For m=k+1 this is at most-25/36. Otherwise keep ell=1 exactly, extend
the positive terms ell>=2 to infinity, and replace their logarithms by
ell log c+log y. The result is

    E(y)=-5y/4+(1/2)log[c y(c-y)^2(cy-1)].               (9)

On the indicated interval E''(y)<-1/2. Indeed its three negative terms
are -1/(c-y)^2, -1/(2y^2), and -c^2/(2(cy-1)^2); the last two alone
have total magnitude greater than2/9+c^2/18>1/2. At y=4/5,
E'=5/216 and c y(c-y)^2(cy-1)=113724/15625<(27/10)^2. Since
e>163/60, E(4/5)<log(162/163)<=-1/163. The tangent parabola therefore
gives E(y)<=-1/163+25/46656<-1/200. Thus

    P_sec(m,M)<=exp[-2^(m-k-1)/200]  for m>=k+1.         (10)

For m<=k every factor is at most1 and M<=(13/(9a))c^(-m). For
m=k+J, J>=1, equation(10) bounds M P_sec^2 by
(13/(9a))c^(-m)c^J exp(-2^J/200). As c<4 and z^2 exp(-z)<=1 for
z>=0, this is at most (520000/(9a))c^(-m), proving(7).

## 4. Separated activation: s<=1/c

This case is included to keep the statement independent of unverified C19.
At level I write

    A=p_s^2(1-s/c), D=p_s p_f(t-1), F=p_f^2(1-t/c).

Then E_(I+1)=[[A,D],[0,F]]. At I+1 a fast input must cross and a slow
input cannot cross. Hence

    E_(I+2)=[[A^2(1-s), A max(D(1-s),F(ct-1))],[0,0]].

Its right/left nonzero-entry ratio is at most max(R_1,R_2), where

    R_1=(t-1)/(1-s/c) *exp[-5(t-s)/8],
    R_2=(1-t/c)(ct-1)/[(1-s/c)(1-s)] *exp[-5(t-s)/4].

Both increase with s. R_1 increases with t up to c; R_2 decreases with
t from1, since its logarithmic derivative is
-1/(c-t)+c/(ct-1)-5/4, is decreasing, and equals-1/4 at t=1.
Thus R_1<=(169/90)exp(-18/13)<1 and
R_2<=(169/90)exp(-10/13)<1. The latter inequalities follow respectively
from exp(18/13)>31/13>169/90 and
exp(10/13)>349/169>169/90.

If E_j=[[A_j,R A_j],[0,0]] with R<=1, recurrence(3) preserves R and

    A_(j+1)=A_j^2 max(d_slow(j),R u_slow(j))
           <=A_j^2 q_sec(b_j M_slow).

Its initial A_(I+2) is P_sec(I+2,M_slow). Every later nonzero endpoint
is therefore on the slow ray, with radius at most P_sec(m,M_slow)|x_0|.
Equation(7) supplies the required bound in this case.

## 5. Overlapping activation: one off-diagonal entry controls all levels

Now assume 1/c<s<=t<=c. At level I use all four entries

    E_(I+1)=[[A,D],[C,F]],
    A=p_s^2(1-s/c), D=p_s p_f(t-1),
    C=p_s p_f(s-1)_+, F=p_f^2(1-t/c).

At I+1 put d=(1-s)_+, u_s=cs-1>0, u_f=ct-1>0. Thus
B_(I+1)=[[d,u_f],[u_s,0]]. The two relations

    C d=0,  C u_f<=D u_s                              (11)

hold: for s<=1 the first entry C vanishes, while for s>1 the second
inequality reduces to (t-1)/(s-1)>=(ct-1)/(cs-1).

Set L=max(A d,D u_s). Direct multiplication in(3) gives new entries

    A_0=A L,                F_0=F D u_s,
    D_0=max(A D d,D^2 u_s,A F u_f),
    C_0=max(A F u_s,C^2 u_f),
    E_(I+2)=[[A_0,D_0],[C_0,F_0]].                     (12)

These entries satisfy, without any division by a potentially zero entry,

    A_0 F_0<=C_0 D_0,  C_0 u_f<=D_0 u_s.             (13)

For the first inequality use D_0>=D L and C_0>=A F u_s. For the
second, the two possibilities in C_0 are bounded by D_0 u_s/u_f:
D_0>=A F u_f treats the first, and D_0>=D^2 u_s together with(11)
treats the second.

For every j>=I+2 both rays must cross at checkpoint j, even at the
smallest permitted secants. Write u_s(j)=b_j M_slow-1 and
u_f(j)=b_j M_fast-1. Their ratio u_f(j)/u_s(j) decreases with j.
Suppose E_j=[[A_j,D_j],[C_j,F_j]] satisfies

    A_j F_j<=C_j D_j, C_j u_f(j)<=D_j u_s(j), D_j>0.

Multiplication by the pure crossing B_j yields exactly

    D_(j+1)=D_j^2 u_s(j),
    A_(j+1)=A_j D_j u_s(j),
    F_(j+1)=F_j D_j u_s(j),
    C_(j+1)=max(A_j F_j u_s(j),C_j^2 u_f(j)).           (14)

The first product inequality persists because the term A_j F_j u_s(j)
occurs in C_(j+1). The ratios A_j/D_j and F_j/D_j are constant, while
C_(j+1)/D_(j+1)<=C_j/D_j. Together with decreasing u_f/u_s, this proves
the second product inequality at the next level. Equation(13) starts
the induction. The full two-state envelope is therefore controlled by
the scalar recurrence for D_j in(14).

For clarity its starting value in(12) is the maximum of three terms:

    T_1=p_s^2 p_f^2 (t-1)^2(cs-1),
    T_2=p_s^3 p_f (1-s/c)(t-1)(1-s)_+,
    T_3=p_s^2 p_f^2 (1-s/c)(1-t/c)(ct-1).              (15)

The positivity D_0>0 and a uniform ratio bound follow as follows. Every
entry in(12) is less than16. If t<=2, T_3>=(1/27^4)(72/845)>
1/(12*27^4). If t>=2 and s<=3/4, T_2>=(1/27^4)(37/208) exceeds that
same bound. If t>=2 and s>=3/4, T_1>=(1/27^4)(19/20) does so. Thus

    max(A_0,D_0,C_0,F_0)/D_0 <= K_sc=192*27^4.         (16)

By(14) this ratio bound holds at every later level.

## 6. The off-diagonal recurrence decays uniformly

We prove, writing J=m-I-2>=0,

    D_m <= exp[-2^J/400].                             (17)

Here D_(I+2)=D_0 in the notation of(12). To avoid ambiguity, recurrence(14)
propagates each of the three starting terms in(15) independently; their
maximum is the propagated D_0 because positive powers commute with max.

The future factors are c^ell s-1 with ell=2,3,..., and are all greater
than1. For any starting term T, their complete infinite logarithmic
budget, divided by 2^J, is bounded above by

    log T + log(c^2)+(1/2)log[s(c^2 s-1)].              (18)

To derive(18), index future factors by k=1,2,..., so they equal
c^(k+1)s-1. Keep the first correction log(1-1/(c^2 s)) exactly with
weight1/2 and drop the later negative corrections. The sums of 2^(-k)
and k2^(-k) are1 and2, giving(18). Extending a finite tail is valid
because all added original logarithms are positive.

### Case 1/c<s<=1

In this range p_s contains exactly the low factors of P_sec(I+2,M_slow),
whose base value is

    p_s^4 (1-s/c)^2 q_sec(cs).

From(5),

    p_f(t-1)/[p_s(1-s/c)] <= c/e<1.                    (19)

Indeed the logarithmic expression increases with s and t on s<=1,
t<=c and equals c/e at s=1,t=c. Thus T_1 and T_2 are at most this
base value. At all future levels q_sec(c^ell s)=c^ell s-1. The index k
in(10) is either I or I+1, so their propagated values are at most
exp[-2^J/400].

For T_3 use p_s^2 p_f^2<=exp[-5(s+t)/4]. For fixed s the logarithm
of exp(-5t/4)(1-t/c)(ct-1) decreases for t>=1. Replacing t by1 in
(18) therefore gives the upper bound

    F_low(s)=-5(s+1)/4+log[(c-s)(c-1)^2]
                         +(1/2)log[s(c^2 s-1)].        (20)

On [1/c,1], F_low''<-1: the last two negative curvature terms alone
have magnitudes greater than1/2+1/2. At s=2/3,

    F_low'(2/3)=-407/7627,
    (c-s)^2(c-1)^4 s(c^2s-1)
       <(163/60)^4(13/12)<exp(49/12).

The last upper comparison uses e>163/60 and exp(1/12)>13/12. Thus
F_low(2/3)<-1/24. Since (407/7627)^2/2<1/600, its tangent parabola
proves F_low(s)<-1/25 throughout the interval. This is stronger than
the exponent required by(17).

### Case 1<=s<=t<=c

T_2=0. First, the function p(t)^2(1-t/c)(ct-1) is decreasing for
t>=1. The derivative of 2log p is at most-5/4, and the remaining
logarithmic derivative is -1/(c-t)+c/(ct-1). Therefore

    T_3<=p_s^4(1-s/c)^2(cs-1)
         <=P_sec(I+2,M_slow).

The index k in(10) is I-1 or I, so the same propagation proves(17)
for this term.

For T_1 use the quadratic improvement in(6). Its bound in(18) is

    F_high(s,t)=-5(s+t)/4-(s^2+t^2)/35+2log(t-1)
                  +log(cs-1)+log(c^2)
                  +(1/2)log[s(c^2s-1)].               (21)

The part depending on t has second derivative at most-25/32. Its
derivative at t=c is-26/175. Completing the tangent parabola gives

    F_high(s,t)<=F_high(s,c)+1/60.                     (22)

The function s->F_high(s,c) has second derivative less than-2/5.
For example the four positive magnitudes have sum bounded below by

    2/35+c^2/(c^2-1)^2+1/(2c^2)
                              +c^4/(2(c^3-1)^2)>2/5.

At s=7/4 its derivative is -213097/10765020, with magnitude less
than1/40. The argument of its combined logarithm is

    (c-1)^2 c^2 (cs-1)*sqrt[s(c^2s-1)] <268<exp(28/5).

The first inequality follows on squaring rational quantities. The
second follows from
(163/60)^5[1+3/5+(3/5)^2/2+(3/5)^3/6]>268.
Its tangent-parabola correction is less than1/1000. Hence(22) is
strictly less than

    28/5-87/16-3929/14000+1/60+1/1000
       =-211/2100<-1/10.

This proves(17) for T_1 and completes all cases. Every displayed
rational comparison is a finite arithmetic inequality; none asserts
a numerical scan or an optimized trajectory.

## 7. Radius, complete objective area, and early horizons

In the overlapping case equations(16)--(17) give

    |x_(Nsc_m)|<=K_sc exp[-2^(m-I-2)/400]|x_0|,
                                                    m>=I+2. (23)

First suppose the bands hold everywhere on their rays. Then integration
from the minimizer gives f(x)<=M_sigma x^2/2. In(23) use M_sigma<=M_fast
and M_fast=t/(a c^I)<=c/(a c^I). With J=m-I-2, the normalized error is
at most

    (c^3 K_sc^2/a)c^(-m)c^J exp(-2^J/200)
       <=(40000 c^3 K_sc^2/a)c^(-m).                   (24)

For m<=I the signs cannot change, all envelope factors are at most1,
and M_fast<=(c/a)c^(-m). For m=I+1 every entry of E_(I+1) is at most
c-1, giving the bound c^2(c-1)^2 c^(-m)/a. These are smaller than(24).
The separated case was bounded in section4 by(7), including its own
two early ranges by the same estimates. Thus the global-band assertion
holds at every horizon.

For the stated queried-only hypotheses take m>=1. The final step of
Hsc_m is a<1/2. Smoothness and g(0)=0 ensure it preserves any nonzero
ray. Write x_pre for the last query and x_end for the terminal point.
If a query or iterate already has zero gradient, the remaining objective
is zero. Otherwise monotonicity and(1) give, on its ray sigma,

    |g(x_end)|<=|g(x_pre)|<=M_sigma |x_pre|
                    <=M_sigma |x_end|/(1-a).

The entire area between0 and x_end obeys

    f(x_end)=integral_0^|x_end| |g(sigma r)| dr
                <=|x_end| |g(x_end)|.

Thus the preceding endpoint estimate with M_sigma x_end^2 is enlarged
by at most2/(1-a)<4. Formula(2), with the chosen C_sc, follows. This
retains all function-value area, even if the derivative is arbitrary
between or outside the queries. At m=0, 1-smoothness directly gives
2f(x_0)<=x_0^2, also smaller than(2).

## 8. Exact benchmark comparison and scope

The accepted fact b98bb807d514e80d defines the exact benchmark. Write
C_n=S_circle(n)+1 and B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1. Its shifted recursions are

    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(0<=j<n) Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=j<n) Gamma(C_j,B_(n-j-1)),
    Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,
    Gamma(A,B)=2A+B/2+sqrt(B^2+8AB)/2.

Here is an elementary stronger growth estimate, proved rather than
imported from an unverified finding. Homogeneity and the defining
quadratic of Omega show that
Omega(A,B)<=(A^(3/4)+B^(3/4))^(4/3) is equivalent to
t^(4/3)+(1-t)^(4/3)+[t(1-t)]^(4/3)<=1 on[0,1]. Put u=t^(1/3),
v=(1-t)^(1/3). The difference from1 equals

    u^3 v^3[1/(1+u+u^2)+1/(1+v+v^2)-uv]>=0,

because each reciprocal is at least1/3 and uv<=2^(-2/3)<2/3.
Induction gives C_n<=(n+1)^(4/3). Also Gamma(A,B)<=B+4A by squaring
the square-root comparison, and induction using
u^(4/3)+v^(4/3)<=(u+v)^(4/3) gives B_n<=1+4n^(4/3).

Consequently(2), divided by U_(Nsc_m)^ZJ=1/B_(Nsc_m), is at most

    C_sc c_sc^(-m)[1+4(2^m-1)^(4/3)] ->0,

since c_sc^3=2197/125>16. All constants are uniform over the function,
the two secant scales, their relative phase, and horizon-dependent knots.

The newly closed gap is arbitrary relative phase of two bounded secant
bands. The proof makes no claim when a single ray's queried secants
span more than13/5. The independent factor-four relaxation already
has divergent illegal trajectories; dropping (1) requires new fixed-profile
information, not merely rerunning the matrix recursion. No fact graph
node has been created by this document.

claim: Exact one-cell closure for arbitrary POSITIVE-VALUE affine-envelope prefixes: projecting a final constant gradient into the old geometric span preserves every queried jet and improves normalized payoff by exactly (2S+1)||v_perp||^2/R^2. On the reversed boundary ray, including ALL affine offsets and orthogonal innovations, the global optimum reduces to an explicit intersection of quadratic-root intervals plus finitely many concave-quadratic vertices. This retains actual G and closest-minimizer distance R. Consequently greedy immediate-cell maximization never creates fresh dimensions; their benefit must repay the displayed cost in later cells.
evidence:
# Exact terminal affine-cell policy and the cost of a new direction

Status: self-contained UNVERIFIED candidate. No fact submission or numerical
solver. This concerns an explicitly described one-cell continuation of a
fixed prefix, not all smooth-convex extensions or the uniform ZJ target.

## 1. General positive-value prefix

Let

    J_old(z)=max_{j in P} (eta_j+<a_j,z>),

where P is a finite index set containing the zero plane (eta_*=0,a_*=0).
Suppose J_old(0)=0 and 0 is a closest zero to the initial point x_init.
Write R=||x_init||>0. Thus every eta_j<=0. Let f_old=env_1 J_old.
For a prescribed finite GD prefix retain EVERY queried jet (x_k,g_k,f_k),
its proximal point z_k=x_k-g_k, and height H_k=J_old(z_k).
The prefix may have arbitrary positive heights, arbitrary affine offsets,
non-Markov gradients, and arbitrary prescribed nonnegative steps.

After a chosen checkpoint applied to the last retained query, let X be
the resulting next position. Append any nonnegative ordinary list of sum
S, and put C=S+1>=1 and d=2C-1. We seek a single new affine plane

    ell(z)=a+<p,z>, a<=0,
    J=max(J_old,ell), f=env_1 J,

whose gradient p is used throughout the whole new ordinary block,
including its final sample. The data before X are kept exactly.

The prefix is preserved exactly when

    a+<p,z_k><=H_k                              for every old query k. (1)

The proposed new queries after partial mass u in [0,S] have position
X-u p and proximal point X-(u+1)p. The new plane dominates old plane j
at such a point exactly when

    (u+1)||p||^2-<p,X+(u+1)a_j>
                    +eta_j+<a_j,X>-a <=0.                          (2)

This expression is affine in u. Hence it suffices, and is necessary,
to check (2) at u=0 and u=S; both are actual endpoint samples. This
also checks the zero plane because it is included in P. An active new
plane supplies the required subgradient, so the proximal optimality
condition gives the same p at every supplied intermediate query. All
steps of the given ordinary list therefore occur in their actual order.

The envelope is convex, differentiable and 1-smooth: its proximal point
is the unique minimizer of J(z)+||x-z||^2/2; the subgradient monotonicity
inequality gives ||p(x)-p(y)||^2<=<p(x)-p(y),x-y>, where p(x)=x-z(x).
Comparing the two minimizing expressions yields derivative p(x).
Thus this construction is one fixed smooth-convex function.

The minimum and normalization remain exact. J>=0 and J(0)=0 since
a<=0. Its zero set is a subset of the old zero set and still contains
0, so 0 remains closest to x_init at distance R. The envelope has the
same zero set as J, since both nonnegative terms in its minimizing
expression must vanish at a zero. At the final query, the exact score is

    2 f_end/R^2 = [2a+2<p,X>-d||p||^2]/R^2.                         (3)

## 2. Orthogonal innovations have an exact immediate price

Let V be the linear span of X, all z_k, all old normals a_j, and x_init.
Decompose p=p_parallel+p_perp orthogonally with p_parallel in V.
Replace the new plane by a+<p_parallel,z>.

Every old-query test (1) is unchanged. In each new-query test (2), the
linear terms are unchanged while the squared norm decreases by
||p_perp||^2. Thus every test remains valid. The same a<=0 still retains
the closest minimizer. Equation (3) shows the EXACT increase in score:

    score_projected-score_original=d||p_perp||^2/R^2.                (4)

This is strict when p_perp is nonzero. It is valid for the whole new
constant-gradient block, not just an unqueried terminal sample. No old
position, gradient, value, or affine plane has been discarded.

Consequently no maximizer of this immediate one-cell objective has a
component in a fresh direction orthogonal to the complete old geometry.
For example, when old data are Markov and p=-beta g+v_perp with
||v_perp||^2=||g||^2 beta(A/T-beta), the immediate penalty is exactly

    d||g||^2 beta(A/T-beta)/R^2.                                    (5)

Creating new directions may still be useful for later blocks. Formula
(4) says that an immediate-cell maximization policy never chooses them;
it does not say that their globally optimal use is impossible. Starting
from a one-dimensional prefix and repeatedly maximizing only this
immediate objective therefore cannot create a new dimension.

## 3. Explicit exact optimization on the reversed boundary ray

Let g be the nonzero gradient at the retained checkpoint query, set
G2=||g||^2, and suppose

    A=-<g,X>/G2>0.

Allow all new planes of the form

    ell(z)=G2 theta+<-beta g+v_perp,z>,
    beta>=0, theta<=0,

where v_perp is orthogonal to V. By (4), optimizing this entire family
reduces exactly to v_perp=0. No Markov or zero-height prefix assumption
is made. Define the retained dimensionless numbers

    u_k=H_k/G2, v_k=<g,z_k>/G2                    for old queries k,
    u_*=v_*=0                                  for an extra index *,
    r_j=(eta_j+<a_j,X>)/G2,
    c_j=<a_j,g>/G2                              for old planes j.

The extra * among the query bounds imposes theta<=0; it is separate
from the zero plane already included among the old planes. Conditions
(1)-(2) become exactly

    theta<=u_k+v_k beta                           for every k,*;
    theta>=t beta^2+(t c_j-A)beta+r_j              for every j,
                                                     t in {1,C}.  (6)

Set U_aff(beta)=min_k(u_k+v_k beta). Feasibility is equivalent to all
the explicit convex quadratic inequalities

    t beta^2+(t c_j-A-v_k)beta+(r_j-u_k)<=0,
                            j in P, t in {1,C}, k in queries union{*}. (7)

Each has a positive leading coefficient. If its discriminant is
negative the family is infeasible. Otherwise it gives the closed
interval between its two real roots. Intersect those finitely many
root intervals with beta>=0. This is the exact feasible interval I,
possibly empty. The pair zero-plane/* with t=C also gives

    0<=beta<=A/C,                                                   (8)

so every nonempty I is compact. These formulas include equality and
zero-step degeneracies. If beta=0 is feasible, (6) forces theta=0
through the zero plane and theta<=0, and the terminal block is already
at a minimizer. Positive score requires beta>0.

For beta in I, the largest allowed theta is U_aff(beta), and the exact
best score at that beta is

    V(beta)=(G2/R^2)[2U_aff(beta)+2A beta-d beta^2].                  (9)

This is a strictly concave piecewise quadratic function on I. It has an
explicit finite maximization rule. For each query bound k, let

    I_k=I intersect {beta: u_k+v_k beta<=u_l+v_l beta for every l}.

The set I_k is a closed interval, possibly empty, determined by affine
half-line intersections. On a nonempty I_k, clamp (A+v_k)/d to I_k and
call the result beta_k. Compare the finitely many values V(beta_k).
Any largest one is the global optimum; set theta_opt=U_aff(beta_opt).
Every optimizing parameter, scale, intercept, and normalized value is
therefore explicitly determined by retained finite data and quadratic
roots. No continuous optimizer or presumed feasible parameter appears.

The frozen prefix can have positive internal values and nonzero offsets.
In particular this rule does not replace them by zero, and it retains
both the true boundary magnitude G2 and the actual distance R.

## 4. A nonzero affine offset improves a frozen multidimensional prefix

This quantitative example distinguishes the affine rule from merely
choosing a positive homogeneous terminal level. For any M>1 prescribe
three arbitrary nonnegative ordinary blocks, each of sum M-1, with
checkpoints 4M+1 and 2M+1. Work in R^2 with x_init=(1,0), and set

    p=(1/M,0), q=(-2/M,2/M), J_old(z)=max(0,<p,z>,<q,z>).

On the first block use gradient p. Its positions run from (1,0) to p;
all its proximal points are d p, 0<=d<=M-1. The q plane is negative
there. The checkpoint 4M+1 leads to X_1=(-4,0). Put

    Z_1=X_1-Mq=(-2,-2).

On the second block use gradient q. Its proximal points are Z_1+d q,
0<=d<=M-1. The q plane has value d||q||^2, while the p plane has
value -2/M-2d/M^2<=0. Thus both supplied prefix blocks and their
checkpoint queries are legal. The second checkpoint 2M+1 leads to

    X=X_1-3Mq=(2,-6), G2=8/M^2, A=2M, C=M.

Origin is closest because the retained p plane forces the first
coordinate of every old zero to be nonpositive. Thus R=1.

For the new plane G2 theta+<-beta q,z>, its exact old-query upper
bound is

    theta<=min(0, k(1-2beta)), k=(M-1)/8.                           (10)

Indeed on the first block the normalized inequality is
theta<=(1-2beta)d/8 for 0<=d<=M-1. On the second it is
theta<=d(1+beta), whose minimum is zero. The zero endpoints are
actual retained queries.

For beta>=1/2 the unconstrained optimizer of (9) with (10) is

    beta_aff=(7M+1)/[4(2M-1)],
    theta_aff=(M-1)(1-2beta_aff)/8<0.                               (11)

Here is the complete new-plane feasibility check, not just an objective
stationarity calculation. Put d=2M-1>1, so

    beta_aff=(7d+9)/(8d),
    theta_aff=-3(d-1)(d+3)/(64d),
    7/8<beta_aff<2.

Among the terminal checks for the zero plane, the larger t=C is the
only stronger one. Its lower bound for theta is

    L_0=C beta_aff(beta_aff-2).

The exact slack is

    theta_aff-L_0
       =(d-1)(57d^2+126d+81)/(128d^2)>0.                            (12)

For old plane q, the strongest lower bound is
L_q=C(beta_aff+1)(beta_aff-2)<=L_0. For old plane p it is

    L_p=C(beta_aff^2-9beta_aff/4+1/4),

because beta_aff>1/4 makes the t=C bound stronger than t=1. Its slack
is

    theta_aff-L_p=(55d^3+85d^2-27d-81)/(128d^2)>0.                  (13)

The numerator is at least 28d+4 for d>=1, using d^3>=d and d^2>=1.
Thus every old plane, the zero plane, and all past queries are checked.
The chosen beta maximizes the full piecewise quadratic upper bound:
below 1/2 that bound is increasing, and above 1/2 its vertex is (11).
Its feasibility proves global optimality within this affine ray family.

The exact normalized score is

    V_aff=(57M^2+2M+5)/[2M^2(2M-1)].                              (14)

For a homogeneous new plane theta=0, (10) forces beta<=1/2. The
objective 2A beta-(2C-1)beta^2 increases on that interval. Beta=1/2
is feasible by the same checks, so the homogeneous optimum is

    V_hom=12/M+2/M^2.

The exact gain from retaining the affine-value freedom is

    V_aff-V_hom=9(M+1)^2/[2M^2(2M-1)]>0.                           (15)

No new direction is used at the terminal cell; the earlier two-
dimensional prefix is preserved. This example illustrates the general
optimizer and does not supply a new all-schedule or asymptotic result.

## 5. What remains for iteration

Equations (1)-(3) apply to any proposed internal affine cell too, but
maximizing its endpoint objective is not a proved optimal policy for the
remaining schedule. Equation (4) makes the lost mechanism quantitative:
every immediate optimum removes fresh orthogonal information, while a
later-block policy may need that information. A constructive uniform
comparison must therefore control the later return on the exact cost
(4), or use a different family. The present interval and affine formulas
solve the terminal one-cell choice; they do not assume the needed
continuation value or hide it inside a feasibility claim.

## Sources and verification status

# Projection realization and a constructive terminal objective gap

Status: complete candidate, NOT verifier-accepted. No numerical solver or
fact_submit call. The only accepted predecessor used is1252b8823bb5a290,
for the explicit finite smooth-convex interpolation construction. All new
lemmas and calculations are proved within this file. This is a constructive,
quantitative companion to max2's unverified terminal-sharpness equivalence
cd21b59c480a46f9; that candidate is NOT a premise.

## 1. Definitions and result

Fix a finite nonnegative prefix schedule h=(h_0,...,h_(k-1)), put
s=sum h_i and D=s+1, and define its intrinsic primitive energy by

  V_h=2sum_(i<k)h_i(f_i-f_k)
       +sum_(i<k)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-sD||g_k||^2.             (1)

All functions below have smoothness1, and an optimum at0 of value0
unless a translation is explicitly mentioned. Write

  Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
  y_i=x_i-g_i, delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2,
  I_i_star=<g_i,x_i>-f_i-||g_i||^2/2=-Q_(i,star).

A projection function is

  F_K(X)=max_(G in K){<X,G>-||G||^2/2}
        =(||X||^2-dist(X,K)^2)/2,                           (2)

where K is a nonempty closed convex set containing0. Its gradient is the
nearest-point projection P_K. Such a function is convex differentiable
1-smooth, minimized at0, and EVERY incoming optimum slack is zero.

We prove two statements.

(P) If h has any legal witness with V_h<0, it has one on a projection
function F_K; K may be chosen as the convex hull of0 and its k+1 sampled
gradients. One extra ambient coordinate suffices before taking that hull.
Thus projection functions universally test primitive validity.

(T) Define

  t=(-1+sqrt(8D+1))/4, b=1+t,
  r=1/(2t+1), q=r^2=1/[1+2(s+b)].                          (3)

Every V_h<0 witness can be converted to a fixed legal projection-function
instance for the schedule(h,b) whose normalized objective error is

  q + [-q epsilon V_aux]/[D^2+epsilon||X_0_aux||^2] > q.     (4)

Here the finite auxiliary prefix, its negative V_aux, and epsilon>0 are
constructed explicitly below. At most three extra ambient coordinates
beyond the supplied witness suffice. The final K has at most k+3 listed
vertices, including0.

This is a strict excess over the sum-based terminal guard at its prescribed
bridge. No uniform positive excess over the exact asymptotic benchmark is
claimed.

## 2. Elementary properties of projection functions

The maximum(2) has a unique maximizer because the objective equals
||X||^2/2-||X-G||^2/2 and K is closed convex and nonempty. Existence follows
by restricting a minimizing sequence for distance to a bounded ball.

The projection normal inequality is

  <X-P_K(X),G-P_K(X)><=0 for every G in K.

Using it at X and X' gives

  <X-X',P_K(X)-P_K(X')>>=||P_K(X)-P_K(X')||^2.

Hence P_K is1-Lipschitz. The two maximizing inequalities yield

  0<=F_K(X+U)-F_K(X)-<P_K(X),U>
    <=<P_K(X+U)-P_K(X),U><=||U||^2.

This proves differentiability and gradient P_K; the Lipschitz property
then proves1-smoothness. Convexity follows from the supremum of affine
functions of X. Since0 belongs to K, F_K>=0 and F_K(0)=0.

At any query with G=P_K(X), the maximizing value is
F_K(X)=<G,X>-||G||^2/2. Thus I_i_star=0, and substitution gives

  Q_ij=<G_i-G_j,Y_j>, Y_j=X_j-G_j.                          (5)

Conversely, if finite data satisfy all Q<=0, all I_i_star=0, and both
optimum directions, let K_fin=conv{0,G_0,...,G_m}. Equation(5) and the
outgoing optimum inequalities say

  <Y_j,G-G_j><=0 for every vertex G of K_fin.

They say the same for every G in K_fin by convexity. Therefore G_j is
the projection of X_j onto K_fin. Formula(2) realizes ALL those finite
values and gradients, with one fixed compact polytope.

## 3. Replace the supplied function by its finite maximal interpolant

Start from the given negative witness and retain all its queried jets,
including the terminal one and the zero optimum. Put

  Phi(v)=max_(j in {star,0,...,k}){<y_j,v>-delta_j}.          (6)

Here the star plane is0. Optimum interpolation gives delta_j>=0, so
Phi>=0 and Phi(0)=0. Phi is finite, convex and globally Lipschitz with
constant M=max_j||y_j||. In particular,

  0<=Phi(v)<=M||v||.

The interpolant supplied in fact1252b8823bb5a290 is exactly

  F(x)=max_v {<x,v>-||v||^2/2-Phi(v)}.                     (7)

Indeed, its conjugate lower quadratics expand as
||v||^2/2+<y_j,v>-delta_j. The fact therefore shows that F is convex
differentiable1-smooth with minimizer0 and interpolates every retained
query. Running h on F from x_0 reproduces the supplied finite trajectory
and its negative energy exactly. No full original function is discarded
without preserving the required finite data.

## 4. A scaled epigraph turns the whole primitive defect into projection data

For a positive parameter Lambda define the closed convex polyhedron

  K_Lambda={(v,z): Lambda z>=Phi(v)}.                      (8)

It contains0. Run h on F_(K_Lambda) from

  X_0^Lambda=(x_0,-Lambda).

Write its query points as (u_i,w_i) and projected gradients as (v_i,z_i).
Inductively w_i=-Lambda-a_i/Lambda with a_i>=0. Since w_i<0 and
Phi(v)>=0, for fixed v the maximizing vertical coordinate in(2) is its
smallest feasible one. Consequently

  z_i=Phi(v_i)/Lambda,
  a_0=0, a_(i+1)=a_i+h_i Phi(v_i),                         (9)
  F_(K_Lambda)(u_i,w_i)
   =max_v {<u_i,v>-||v||^2/2-Phi(v)
             -[a_i Phi(v)+Phi(v)^2/2]/Lambda^2}.           (10)

These are exact formulas for one fixed function, not time-dependent
oracle choices.

Here is a uniform finite-horizon error estimate. Let

  B=max(1,||x_0||) product_(i<k)(1+2h_i),
  P=2MB, C=(s+1/2)P^2,
  U=sqrt(2C) product_(i<k)(1+h_i).

The objective in(10) at v=0 equals0, so its maximizing v_i satisfies
<u_i,v_i>-||v_i||^2/2>=0 and hence ||v_i||<=2||u_i||.
The GD recursion proves ||u_i||<=B. Thus Phi(v_i)<=P and
0<=a_i<=sP for every query, including the terminal one.

The maximizer g_F(u) in(7) has norm at most||u|| because grad F is
1-Lipschitz and grad F(0)=0. Evaluating(10) at g_F(u_i) and using
Phi(g_F(u_i))<=P gives

  0<=F(u_i)-F_(K_Lambda)(u_i,w_i)<=C/Lambda^2.

The objective in(7) is1-strongly concave in v. To spell out the needed
bound, its negative is ||v||^2/2+Phi(v)-<u_i,v>; subtract its value at
its minimizer g_F(u_i), and use convexity of Phi and the minimizer
subgradient to obtain at least||v-g_F(u_i)||^2/2.
The preceding value comparison therefore yields

  ||v_i-g_F(u_i)||<=sqrt(2C)/Lambda.

Let the original interpolated run of F have points x_i and gradients g_i.
Using the1-Lipschitz property of grad F in the GD recursions gives

  ||u_i-x_i||<=sqrt(2C)[product_(j<i)(1+h_j)-1]/Lambda,
  ||v_i-g_i||<=U/Lambda.                                 (11)

The original points also lie in the ball of radiusB. On this ball
||grad F||<=B, so

  |F_(K_Lambda)(u_i,w_i)-f_i|<=BU/Lambda+C/Lambda^2,
  |(||v_i||^2+z_i^2)-||g_i||^2|
      <=3BU/Lambda+P^2/Lambda^2.                          (12)

These bounds include C=0, when all displayed errors are zero.

Define

  H_abs=sum_(i<k)h_i|1-h_i|+sD,
  C_1=BU(4s+3H_abs), C_2=4sC+H_abs P^2.

Substituting(12) into(1) gives the explicit bound

  |V_h^Lambda-V_h|<=C_1/Lambda+C_2/Lambda^2.                (13)

For V_h=-v_def<0, choose any finite

  Lambda>max{1,2(C_1+C_2)/v_def}.

Then V_h^Lambda<-v_def/2<0. This proves the existence of a negative
projection-function witness. No numerical optimization or limit verdict
is used: the bound supplies a finite admissible parameter.

Finally, let K_fin be the convex hull of0 and the k+1 gradients actually
encountered in this run. It is a subset of K_Lambda containing all these
gradients. The projection normal inequalities remain true on K_fin,
so(2) with K_fin realizes exactly the same finite run. This proves(P).

The large coordinate changes the initial-distance normalization. The
argument transfers intrinsic primitive energy, not the original
normalized objective ratio.

## 5. One zero-energy companion enforces the precise terminal balance

We now start with the legal negative projection prefix just constructed,
so I_i_star=0 for every prefix query. Let its terminal data be(x,g,f),
put y=x-g, and note delta=f-||g||^2/2=<g,y>>=0.

The identities following from(3) are

  t(2t+1)=D, rD=t, 1-r=2r^2D.                             (14)

Define the signed terminal balance

  J=r||y||^2-(t+1)<g,y>.                                 (15)

If J=0 no additional coordinate is needed. If J is nonzero, add one
scalar Huber trajectory with constant positive gradient c, starting at
(D+a)c and ending at(1+a)c, for parameters a>0,c>0 specified below.
At prefix query i its point is (1+a+R_i)c, where R_i is the remaining
stepsize sum. All its incoming optimum slacks and finite Q residuals
are zero. Its intrinsic primitive energy is exactly zero, because

  2sum h_i R_i+sum h_i(1-h_i)-sD=0.

Its contribution to J is

  a[ra-(t+1)]c^2.

Choose:

* If J>0: a=(t+1)/(2r), c^2=J/{a[(t+1)-ra]}.
* If J<0: a=2(t+1)/r, c^2=(-J)/{a[ra-(t+1)]}.

Every displayed denominator is strictly positive. The direct sum now
has J=0, every incoming optimum slack still0, and the same negative
primitive energy. Denote this complete auxiliary prefix by
(X_i,G_i,F_i), its initial point X_0_aux, and its energy V_aux<0.
For its last prefix sample write X,G,Y=X-G,delta=<G,Y>.

Thus the exact inherited boundary condition is

  r||Y||^2=(t+1)<G,Y>.                                   (16)

The function-value moment delta was retained and balanced; it was not
replaced by a bound of the wrong sign.

## 6. Append the prescribed bridge and specify every new terminal datum

Append b=1+t and define

  Z=X-bG=Y-tG,
  P_term=r[Y-DG],
  Y_term=Z-P_term=(1-r)Y,
  F_term=<P_term,Z>-||P_term||^2/2.                       (17)

By(16),

  <P_term-G,Y>=r||Y||^2-(rD+1)<G,Y>=0.                  (18)

Here rD=t. In particular

  F_term-||P_term||^2/2
      =<P_term,Y_term>=(1-r)delta>=0.

The terminal incoming optimum residual is0 and its outgoing optimum
residual is nonpositive.

Because all incoming optimum residuals in the prefix are0, equation(5)
gives for every old query i

  Q_(i,term)=<G_i-P_term,Y_term>
     =(1-r)<G_i-G,Y>=(1-r)Q_(i,k)<=0.                    (19)

The other cross direction is

  Q_(term,i)=<P_term-G_i,Y_i>.                           (20)

At i=k this is0 by(18). It is also0 at any old query with R_i=0,
because those queries coincide with the last prefix sample. Other
residuals(20) may be positive; we keep them instead of assuming legality.

## 7. Exact finite slack mixing supplies the remaining inequalities

Use the scalar base function with derivative min(1,z), with value0 at0.
Explicitly, it is z^2/2 for z<=1 and z-1/2 for z>=1. It is convex
differentiable1-smooth and minimized at0.

Start it atD. During the entire prefix it has gradient1 and point1+R_i,
so its final prefix point is1. The appended bridge reaches-t, with
gradient-t and value t^2/2. Every incoming optimum residual is0.
Its finite prefix residuals and old-to-terminal residuals are0, while

  Q_base(term,i)=-(1+t)R_i.                              (21)

Thus whenever an auxiliary residual(20) is positive, its base residual
is strictly negative. Define the finite positive coefficient

  epsilon=min(1,
      min_(i:Q_aux(term,i)>0) [(1+t)R_i/(2Q_aux(term,i))]), (22)

with an empty inner minimum interpreted as1.

Combine base and auxiliary points and gradients in orthogonal
coordinates, scaling the auxiliary coordinates by sqrt(epsilon) and
its values by epsilon. The GD equations remain exact. All prefix
constraints are legal; all old-to-terminal constraints are nonpositive
by(19); new-to-old constraints are nonpositive by(21),(22).
Both optimum directions are nonpositive. Zero-step duplicates have
already been treated explicitly.

Every combined incoming optimum residual is0. By section2, one compact
polytope K=conv{0, all combined sampled gradients} realizes the entire
supplied schedule through the fixed function F_K in(2).
This K has at most k+3 listed vertices. Thus no terminal feasibility
condition is hidden in the construction.

## 8. The exact normalized objective surplus

For any prefix whose incoming optimum slacks are all0, distance
telescoping gives

  V_h=||X_0||^2-||X+sG||^2
     =||X_0||^2-||Y+DG||^2.                             (23)

For completeness, insert F_i=<G_i,X_i>-||G_i||^2/2 into(1).
The sum 2sum h_i<G_i,X_i>-sum h_i^2||G_i||^2 equals
||X_0||^2-||X||^2, and the remaining terms combine to
-2s<X,G>-s^2||G||^2. This proves(23).

Equations(14),(17),(18) give

  2F_term=||P_term||^2+2(1-r)delta
         =r^2||Y-DG||^2+4r^2D<G,Y>
         =q||Y+DG||^2.

Therefore the exact auxiliary terminal objective deficit is

  q||X_0_aux||^2-2F_term=q V_aux<0.                       (24)

The base has initial norm squaredD^2 and final twice-value t^2=qD^2.
After the fully legal mixture,

  ||X_0_mix||^2=D^2+epsilon||X_0_aux||^2,
  2F_mix(term)-q||X_0_mix||^2=-q epsilon V_aux>0.

Dividing proves(4). This is an actual positive, finite, algebraically
specified objective surplus for a fixed legal function.

## 9. A finite exact check

For h=(3/2), take the scalar quadratic f(x)=x^2/2 from x_0=1.
Its prefix endpoint and gradient are both-1/2, every incoming optimum
slack is0, and

  D=5/2, V_h=1-D^2/4=-9/16.

Here Y=0, so J=0. With t=(sqrt(21)-1)/4, the terminal point and gradient
are t/2. No auxiliary new-to-old violation occurs, so epsilon=1 is
permitted in(22). Mixing with the stated scalar base gives precisely

  2F_mix(term)/||X_0_mix||^2=(125/116)q>q.

The surplus9q/116 agrees exactly with(4):
(-q V_h)/(D^2+1)=9q/116.

## 10. Scope, related work, and remaining gap

This construction realizes, rather than merely infers, a strict failure
of the terminal sum guard whenever the prefix is not primitive. It
complements max2's dual certificate characterization rather than
claiming that equivalence as a new independent target solution.

All signed function-value information in the original witness is stored
in Phi and then in the geometry of K_Lambda. The subsequent Huber
companion balances the exact mixed terminal moment(16), and the finite
epsilon retains every queried-prefix and new/old interpolation edge.

The surplus(4) can be small: Lambda, the moment-balancing coordinate and
the active-constraint mixing scale all affect its denominator and
epsilon. No bound uniform over arbitrary schedules, horizons, or defects
has been obtained. An improved asymptotic schedule or the exact-profile
lower theorem therefore does not follow.

The original target remains open. No claim in this file has entered the
fact graph, and no new verifier or numerical allocation was consumed.

# Exact terminal affine-cell policy and the cost of a new direction

Status: self-contained UNVERIFIED candidate. No fact submission or numerical
solver. This concerns an explicitly described one-cell continuation of a
fixed prefix, not all smooth-convex extensions or the uniform ZJ target.

## 1. General positive-value prefix

Let

    J_old(z)=max_{j in P} (eta_j+<a_j,z>),

where P is a finite index set containing the zero plane (eta_*=0,a_*=0).
Suppose J_old(0)=0 and 0 is a closest zero to the initial point x_init.
Write R=||x_init||>0. Thus every eta_j<=0. Let f_old=env_1 J_old.
For a prescribed finite GD prefix retain EVERY queried jet (x_k,g_k,f_k),
its proximal point z_k=x_k-g_k, and height H_k=J_old(z_k).
The prefix may have arbitrary positive heights, arbitrary affine offsets,
non-Markov gradients, and arbitrary prescribed nonnegative steps.

After a chosen checkpoint applied to the last retained query, let X be
the resulting next position. Append any nonnegative ordinary list of sum
S, and put C=S+1>=1 and d=2C-1. We seek a single new affine plane

    ell(z)=a+<p,z>, a<=0,
    J=max(J_old,ell), f=env_1 J,

whose gradient p is used throughout the whole new ordinary block,
including its final sample. The data before X are kept exactly.

The prefix is preserved exactly when

    a+<p,z_k><=H_k                              for every old query k. (1)

The proposed new queries after partial mass u in [0,S] have position
X-u p and proximal point X-(u+1)p. The new plane dominates old plane j
at such a point exactly when

    (u+1)||p||^2-<p,X+(u+1)a_j>
                    +eta_j+<a_j,X>-a <=0.                          (2)

This expression is affine in u. Hence it suffices, and is necessary,
to check (2) at u=0 and u=S; both are actual endpoint samples. This
also checks the zero plane because it is included in P. An active new
plane supplies the required subgradient, so the proximal optimality
condition gives the same p at every supplied intermediate query. All
steps of the given ordinary list therefore occur in their actual order.

The envelope is convex, differentiable and 1-smooth: its proximal point
is the unique minimizer of J(z)+||x-z||^2/2; the subgradient monotonicity
inequality gives ||p(x)-p(y)||^2<=<p(x)-p(y),x-y>, where p(x)=x-z(x).
Comparing the two minimizing expressions yields derivative p(x).
Thus this construction is one fixed smooth-convex function.

The minimum and normalization remain exact. J>=0 and J(0)=0 since
a<=0. Its zero set is a subset of the old zero set and still contains
0, so 0 remains closest to x_init at distance R. The envelope has the
same zero set as J, since both nonnegative terms in its minimizing
expression must vanish at a zero. At the final query, the exact score is

    2 f_end/R^2 = [2a+2<p,X>-d||p||^2]/R^2.                         (3)

## 2. Orthogonal innovations have an exact immediate price

Let V be the linear span of X, all z_k, all old normals a_j, and x_init.
Decompose p=p_parallel+p_perp orthogonally with p_parallel in V.
Replace the new plane by a+<p_parallel,z>.

Every old-query test (1) is unchanged. In each new-query test (2), the
linear terms are unchanged while the squared norm decreases by
||p_perp||^2. Thus every test remains valid. The same a<=0 still retains
the closest minimizer. Equation (3) shows the EXACT increase in score:

    score_projected-score_original=d||p_perp||^2/R^2.                (4)

This is strict when p_perp is nonzero. It is valid for the whole new
constant-gradient block, not just an unqueried terminal sample. No old
position, gradient, value, or affine plane has been discarded.

Consequently no maximizer of this immediate one-cell objective has a
component in a fresh direction orthogonal to the complete old geometry.
For example, when old data are Markov and p=-beta g+v_perp with
||v_perp||^2=||g||^2 beta(A/T-beta), the immediate penalty is exactly

    d||g||^2 beta(A/T-beta)/R^2.                                    (5)

Creating new directions may still be useful for later blocks. Formula
(4) says that an immediate-cell maximization policy never chooses them;
it does not say that their globally optimal use is impossible. Starting
from a one-dimensional prefix and repeatedly maximizing only this
immediate objective therefore cannot create a new dimension.

## 3. Explicit exact optimization on the reversed boundary ray

Let g be the nonzero gradient at the retained checkpoint query, set
G2=||g||^2, and suppose

    A=-<g,X>/G2>0.

Allow all new planes of the form

    ell(z)=G2 theta+<-beta g+v_perp,z>,
    beta>=0, theta<=0,

where v_perp is orthogonal to V. By (4), optimizing this entire family
reduces exactly to v_perp=0. No Markov or zero-height prefix assumption
is made. Define the retained dimensionless numbers

    u_k=H_k/G2, v_k=<g,z_k>/G2                    for old queries k,
    u_*=v_*=0                                  for an extra index *,
    r_j=(eta_j+<a_j,X>)/G2,
    c_j=<a_j,g>/G2                              for old planes j.

The extra * among the query bounds imposes theta<=0; it is separate
from the zero plane already included among the old planes. Conditions
(1)-(2) become exactly

    theta<=u_k+v_k beta                           for every k,*;
    theta>=t beta^2+(t c_j-A)beta+r_j              for every j,
                                                     t in {1,C}.  (6)

Set U_aff(beta)=min_k(u_k+v_k beta). Feasibility is equivalent to all
the explicit convex quadratic inequalities

    t beta^2+(t c_j-A-v_k)beta+(r_j-u_k)<=0,
                            j in P, t in {1,C}, k in queries union{*}. (7)

Each has a positive leading coefficient. If its discriminant is
negative the family is infeasible. Otherwise it gives the closed
interval between its two real roots. Intersect those finitely many
root intervals with beta>=0. This is the exact feasible interval I,
possibly empty. The pair zero-plane/* with t=C also gives

    0<=beta<=A/C,                                                   (8)

so every nonempty I is compact. These formulas include equality and
zero-step degeneracies. If beta=0 is feasible, (6) forces theta=0
through the zero plane and theta<=0, and the terminal block is already
at a minimizer. Positive score requires beta>0.

For beta in I, the largest allowed theta is U_aff(beta), and the exact
best score at that beta is

    V(beta)=(G2/R^2)[2U_aff(beta)+2A beta-d beta^2].                  (9)

This is a strictly concave piecewise quadratic function on I. It has an
explicit finite maximization rule. For each query bound k, let

    I_k=I intersect {beta: u_k+v_k beta<=u_l+v_l beta for every l}.

The set I_k is a closed interval, possibly empty, determined by affine
half-line intersections. On a nonempty I_k, clamp (A+v_k)/d to I_k and
call the result beta_k. Compare the finitely many values V(beta_k).
Any largest one is the global optimum; set theta_opt=U_aff(beta_opt).
Every optimizing parameter, scale, intercept, and normalized value is
therefore explicitly determined by retained finite data and quadratic
roots. No continuous optimizer or presumed feasible parameter appears.

The frozen prefix can have positive internal values and nonzero offsets.
In particular this rule does not replace them by zero, and it retains
both the true boundary magnitude G2 and the actual distance R.

## 4. A nonzero affine offset improves a frozen multidimensional prefix

This quantitative example distinguishes the affine rule from merely
choosing a positive homogeneous terminal level. For any M>1 prescribe
three arbitrary nonnegative ordinary blocks, each of sum M-1, with
checkpoints 4M+1 and 2M+1. Work in R^2 with x_init=(1,0), and set

    p=(1/M,0), q=(-2/M,2/M), J_old(z)=max(0,<p,z>,<q,z>).

On the first block use gradient p. Its positions run from (1,0) to p;
all its proximal points are d p, 0<=d<=M-1. The q plane is negative
there. The checkpoint 4M+1 leads to X_1=(-4,0). Put

    Z_1=X_1-Mq=(-2,-2).

On the second block use gradient q. Its proximal points are Z_1+d q,
0<=d<=M-1. The q plane has value d||q||^2, while the p plane has
value -2/M-2d/M^2<=0. Thus both supplied prefix blocks and their
checkpoint queries are legal. The second checkpoint 2M+1 leads to

    X=X_1-3Mq=(2,-6), G2=8/M^2, A=2M, C=M.

Origin is closest because the retained p plane forces the first
coordinate of every old zero to be nonpositive. Thus R=1.

For the new plane G2 theta+<-beta q,z>, its exact old-query upper
bound is

    theta<=min(0, k(1-2beta)), k=(M-1)/8.                           (10)

Indeed on the first block the normalized inequality is
theta<=(1-2beta)d/8 for 0<=d<=M-1. On the second it is
theta<=d(1+beta), whose minimum is zero. The zero endpoints are
actual retained queries.

For beta>=1/2 the unconstrained optimizer of (9) with (10) is

    beta_aff=(7M+1)/[4(2M-1)],
    theta_aff=(M-1)(1-2beta_aff)/8<0.                               (11)

Here is the complete new-plane feasibility check, not just an objective
stationarity calculation. Put d=2M-1>1, so

    beta_aff=(7d+9)/(8d),
    theta_aff=-3(d-1)(d+3)/(64d),
    7/8<beta_aff<2.

Among the terminal checks for the zero plane, the larger t=C is the
only stronger one. Its lower bound for theta is

    L_0=C beta_aff(beta_aff-2).

The exact slack is

    theta_aff-L_0
       =(d-1)(57d^2+126d+81)/(128d^2)>0.                            (12)

For old plane q, the strongest lower bound is
L_q=C(beta_aff+1)(beta_aff-2)<=L_0. For old plane p it is

    L_p=C(beta_aff^2-9beta_aff/4+1/4),

because beta_aff>1/4 makes the t=C bound stronger than t=1. Its slack
is

    theta_aff-L_p=(55d^3+85d^2-27d-81)/(128d^2)>0.                  (13)

The numerator is at least 28d+4 for d>=1, using d^3>=d and d^2>=1.
Thus every old plane, the zero plane, and all past queries are checked.
The chosen beta maximizes the full piecewise quadratic upper bound:
below 1/2 that bound is increasing, and above 1/2 its vertex is (11).
Its feasibility proves global optimality within this affine ray family.

The exact normalized score is

    V_aff=(57M^2+2M+5)/[2M^2(2M-1)].                              (14)

For a homogeneous new plane theta=0, (10) forces beta<=1/2. The
objective 2A beta-(2C-1)beta^2 increases on that interval. Beta=1/2
is feasible by the same checks, so the homogeneous optimum is

    V_hom=12/M+2/M^2.

The exact gain from retaining the affine-value freedom is

    V_aff-V_hom=9(M+1)^2/[2M^2(2M-1)]>0.                           (15)

No new direction is used at the terminal cell; the earlier two-
dimensional prefix is preserved. This example illustrates the general
optimizer and does not supply a new all-schedule or asymptotic result.

## 5. What remains for iteration

Equations (1)-(3) apply to any proposed internal affine cell too, but
maximizing its endpoint objective is not a proved optimal policy for the
remaining schedule. Equation (4) makes the lost mechanism quantitative:
every immediate optimum removes fresh orthogonal information, while a
later-block policy may need that information. A constructive uniform
comparison must therefore control the later return on the exact cost
(4), or use a different family. The present interval and affine formulas
solve the terminal one-cell choice; they do not assume the needed
continuation value or hide it inside a feasibility claim.

## 6. Completeness for a fixed smooth-convex prefix and constant-gradient tail

There is also a precise completeness statement for the finite program
(1)-(3). It needs a minimal old envelope, rather than arbitrary additional
old planes. Let the old jets and the optimum jet (0,0,0) be any legal
smooth-convex data at smoothness one. For every old query define

    z_k=x_k-g_k,
    H_k=f_k-||g_k||^2/2,
    eta_k=H_k-<g_k,z_k>,
    J_min(z)=max(0, eta_k+<g_k,z>: old queries k).                  (16)

The smooth-convex interpolation inequality in accepted fact
1252b8823bb5a290 gives, for every ordered pair of old queries,

    H_i>=H_j+<g_j,z_i-z_j>.

The optimum inequalities give H_i>=0 and eta_i<=0. Hence J_min(z_i)=H_i,
g_i is a subgradient there, and env_1 J_min realizes every old jet and
the optimum at origin. This uses the accepted necessary interpolation
inequality; the actual realizing envelope has just been constructed.

Among ALL convex 1-smooth functions preserving these jets and minimum
zero at origin, impose the additional restriction that every sample in
the appended ordinary block, including its terminal sample, has the
same gradient p. Then (1)-(2), with the old planes from (16), are an
exact finite characterization of the possible tails. For the reverse
direction, equal gradients at two samples force

    f_i-f_j=<p,x_i-x_j>

by applying the accepted interpolation inequality in both directions.
Thus if f_start is the value at X, the tail value after partial mass u
is f_start-u||p||^2. Every tail supporting affine plane in its
nonsmooth interpolation data has the SAME intercept

    a=f_start-<p,X>+||p||^2/2.

The optimum inequality gives a<=0. Applying the interpolation
inequality between each old sample and each tail sample gives (1)-(2).
Their necessity has therefore been proved directly from arbitrary
smooth-convex data, without presuming a particular old global function.
Their sufficiency is the envelope construction of Section 1. In
particular the old function outside the queried samples may change;
the complete queried jets and optimum remain fixed.

The finite maximization of 2a+2<p,X>-d||p||^2 is attained whenever this
constant-tail family is nonempty. It is a closed feasible problem. Its
zero-plane t=C inequality and a<=0 imply

    C||p||^2<=<p,X>, ||p||<=||X||/C,
    -||X||^2/(4C)<=a<=0.

Thus its parameter set is compact. Every optimizer lies in the span of
the old geometric data by the strict improvement (4). The extra
restriction p=-beta g reduces it to the explicit ray optimizer of
Section 3; that restriction is not claimed to contain the unrestricted
vector optimizer.

For true closest-minimizer normalization one must additionally establish
that origin is closest to x_init among the zeros of J_min. This is
already an assumption in Section 1 and holds in Section 4. A concrete
sufficient certificate is

    x_init=sum_k lambda_k g_k,
    lambda_k>=0, lambda_k eta_k=0.                                (17)

For any zero z of J_min this gives <x_init,z><=0, hence
||x_init-z||^2>=||x_init||^2, with equality at z=0. Any minimizer of
ANY other interpolating smooth-convex function must also satisfy all
eta_k+<g_k,z><=0, by applying interpolation to that minimizer. Thus
(17), or a separately computed genuine distance profile, supplies the
same true normalization throughout the exact constant-tail class.

The case C=1 is a terminal-sample specialization. For C>1 this is an
exact reduction only for tails whose gradient stays constant at all
their samples. The program can be empty for an incompatible long block;
no arbitrary-schedule feasibility or benchmark bound is inferred.

Exact energy identity V_new=V_original+[K_rep V_ball-(s I_n-J_n)^2]/Lambda^2 supplies a finite negative choice. evidence:
# A finite exact projection lift of arbitrary primitive defects

Status: complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. No solver or
fact_submit. The argument below is elementary and self-contained. It does
not use another unverified finding as a premise. It gives an alternative
finite-data implementation of the projection reduction in1afc93b8e38d3cfc.

## 1. Input, notation and conclusion

Let h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) be any finite nonnegative schedule. Put
s=sum h_i and D=1+s. Take any actual convex differentiable1-smooth
GD data(x_i,g_i,f_i), 0<=i<=n, with a minimizer normalized to0 of value0.
Write

  Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
  I_i=<g_i,x_i>-f_i-||g_i||^2/2>=0,
  delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2>=0,
  J_i=sum_(t<i)h_t I_t,
  V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)
       +sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-sD||g_n||^2.

Assume V_h=-v_def<0. We construct explicit finite data in dimension d+3,
on a fixed projection function associated with a compact polytope K
containing0, such that its primitive energy is still negative and all its
incoming optimum slacks are exactly0.

The constructed K has at most n+2 listed vertices:0 and the n+1 sampled
gradients. After an optional orthogonal compression, its ambient dimension
is at most n+1. Every quantity is obtained by finite arithmetic, square roots,
a fixed two-dimensional recurrence, and finite maxima. No limiting
interpolant or numerical PEP evaluation is required.

As a consequence, primitive validity of h is equivalent to

  ||X_n+s P_K(X_n)||<=||X_0||                             (1)

for every finite-dimensional compact polytope K containing0 and every
GD run X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i P_K(X_i). It suffices in testing failure to use
polytopes with at most n+2 listed vertices.

## 2. One slack coordinate, with its interpolation errors retained exactly

For Lambda>0 define auxiliary finite data

  X_i^a=(x_i,-Lambda-J_i/Lambda),
  G_i^a=(g_i,I_i/Lambda),
  F_i^a=<G_i^a,X_i^a>-||G_i^a||^2/2
       =f_i-[I_i J_i+I_i^2/2]/Lambda^2.                  (2)

The GD equations hold exactly because J_(i+1)-J_i=h_i I_i.
Every incoming optimum residual of this auxiliary array is0 by its
assigned value. We do NOT assume its other interpolation constraints
are legal. They are exactly

  Q_ij^a=Q_ij+A_ij/Lambda^2,
  A_ij=-(I_i-I_j)(J_j+I_j),                              (3)
  Q_(star,i)^a=-delta_i+B_i/Lambda^2,
  B_i=I_i(J_i+I_i)>=0.                                  (4)

To verify(3), when incoming slacks are0 the finite residual equals
<G_i^a-G_j^a,X_j^a-G_j^a>. Its original-coordinate part is
Q_ij+I_i-I_j. The added-coordinate part is
-(I_i-I_j)-(I_i-I_j)(J_j+I_j)/Lambda^2.
The constant terms cancel, leaving(3). Equation(4) follows directly
from(2).

If the sum of h between indices i and j is0, every step between them
is zero. The original queries, gradients and values are identical;
also I_i=I_j and J_i=J_j. Thus A_ij=0 for those duplicate queries.

## 3. One explicit strict projection trajectory repairs every other edge

Let e=(1,0) in R^2 and take the closed Euclidean ball

  K_ball={z:||z-e||<=2}.

It contains0 in its interior. Define the fixed projection function

  F_ball(x)=max_(g in K_ball){<x,g>-||g||^2/2}.

Run the SAME schedule h from x_0^ball=e+(0,L), where L=6s+4.
Its gradients always have norm at most3. Hence

  ||x_i^ball-e||>=L-3s=3s+4>2.

Every query stays strictly outside the ball, so, setting
z_i=x_i^ball-e, u_i=z_i/||z_i||,

  g_i^ball=e+2u_i,
  y_i^ball=x_i^ball-g_i^ball=(||z_i||-2)u_i.              (5)

This is an exact finite recurrence of arithmetic and square roots.
All incoming optimum slacks are0. The outgoing optimum slack is

  delta_i^ball=<g_i^ball,y_i^ball>
       =(||z_i||-2)(2+<e,u_i>)>0.                       (6)

Different positive cumulative times have different unit directions u_i.
Here is an explicit proof, including arbitrary large finite steps.
The recursion for z_i is

  z_(i+1)=mu_i z_i-h_i e,
  mu_i=1-2h_i/||z_i||>0,

because h_i<=s and ||z_i||>=3s+4>2s.
The second coordinate z_(i,2) stays strictly positive.
For the ratio of first to second coordinates,

  z_(i+1,1)/z_(i+1,2)
    =z_(i,1)/z_(i,2)-h_i/(mu_i z_(i,2)).

It decreases strictly at every positive step and is unchanged at a
zero step. Thus u_i!=u_j whenever the cumulative step between i and j
is positive.

The finite projection residuals are therefore

  Q_ij^ball=2(||z_j||-2)(<u_i,u_j>-1)<0                 (7)

for every such pair, and they are0 at zero-step duplicates. This
checks BOTH ordered directions of every pair.

For completeness, projection functions are legal without invoking a
new external theorem. The nearest-point normal inequalities imply
<P_K(x)-P_K(x'),x-x'>>=||P_K(x)-P_K(x')||^2, hence
P_K is1-Lipschitz. The maximizing expression for F_K implies

  0<=F_K(x+d)-F_K(x)-<P_K(x),d>
     <=<P_K(x+d)-P_K(x),d><=||d||^2.

Thus grad F_K=P_K, so F_K is convex differentiable1-smooth. Since0
belongs to K, its minimum is F_K(0)=0. At every query
F_K(x)=<P_K(x),x>-||P_K(x)||^2/2, giving the asserted zero incoming
slack and the formula for finite Q.

## 4. A finite repair coefficient gives exact full interpolation

Let the finite coefficient K_rep be

  max{0,
      max_(0<=i<=n) B_i/delta_i^ball,
      max_(i!=j, positive cumulative step)
                  (A_ij)_+/(-Q_ij^ball)}.               (8)

Every denominator is strictly positive by(6),(7). The last maximum is
omitted if its index set is empty. All quantities are explicitly
determined by the original finite data and the fixed ball run.

For any Lambda>0 combine the auxiliary array(2) and the ball array in
orthogonal coordinates with ball-coordinate scale sqrt(K_rep)/Lambda:

  X_i=(X_i^a,(sqrt(K_rep)/Lambda)x_i^ball),
  G_i=(G_i^a,(sqrt(K_rep)/Lambda)g_i^ball),
  F_i=F_i^a+(K_rep/Lambda^2)f_i^ball.                     (9)

When K_rep=0 these extra coordinates are simply zero. Every GD
equation remains exact, and all incoming optimum residuals remain0.
For distinct finite samples,

  Q_ij_new=Q_ij+[A_ij+K_rep Q_ij^ball]/Lambda^2<=0,

using(8); the duplicate-query case follows from A_ij=Q_ij^ball=0.
For outgoing optimum residuals,

  Q_(star,i)_new=-delta_i+
              [B_i-K_rep delta_i^ball]/Lambda^2<=0.

These checks account for EVERY original-index interpolation constraint.
No positivity has been assumed merely from a small-parameter argument.

Define the compact polytope

  K=conv{0,G_0,...,G_n}.

Because all incoming optimum residuals are0, the checked finite
inequalities state

  <X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j><=0,

and the outgoing optimum inequalities give the same condition at vertex0.
Convex combinations give the condition for every point of K. It is
precisely the nearest-point normal condition, so P_K(X_j)=G_j.
Consequently the fixed function

  F_K(X)=max_(G in K){<X,G>-||G||^2/2}

interpolates all the constructed points, gradients and values. It is
a fixed globally legal function, with no adaptive resetting.

## 5. Exact primitive energy and a finite negative choice

For arbitrary original legal data, telescoping the GD squared distances
and using the definitions of I_i gives

  V_h=||x_0||^2-||x_n+s g_n||^2+2(sI_n-J_n).             (10)

For the auxiliary array all incoming slacks are0, so the same algebra,
which does not require prior legality, gives

  V_aux=||X_0^a||^2-||X_n^a+s G_n^a||^2
       =V_h-(sI_n-J_n)^2/Lambda^2.                      (11)

Indeed X_0^a has added coordinate-Lambda, while X_n^a+sG_n^a has added
coordinate-Lambda+(sI_n-J_n)/Lambda. Expanding these squares and then
using(10) proves(11).

Let V_ball be the intrinsic primitive energy of the fixed ball
trajectory, calculated by(1)'s energy definition, or equivalently by

  V_ball=||x_0^ball||^2
                  -||x_n^ball+s g_n^ball||^2.

Energy is additive in orthogonal coordinates. Therefore the fully legal
data(9) have EXACTLY

  V_new=V_h+
        [K_rep V_ball-(sI_n-J_n)^2]/Lambda^2.             (12)

Choose, for example,

  Lambda^2=1+2K_rep max(V_ball,0)/v_def.                 (13)

This is positive and finite. If K_rep max(V_ball,0)=0, (12) is at most
-v_def. Otherwise the positive contribution in(12) is strictly below
v_def/2. In all cases

  V_new<-v_def/2<0.

The output is thus a concrete negative witness on a compact projection
function, produced by finite exact operations.

The final dimension can be reduced to at most n+1. Let W be the linear
span of the n+1 output gradients, hence of K. Project every query onto W.
The GD equations, gradient pairings and function values are unchanged;
projection onto K ignores the component orthogonal to W. The orthogonal
component of every query is the same, so it also cancels from the two
squared norms in the energy identity. This preserves V_new exactly.

## 6. The lossless primitive operator criterion and its limitation

For a projection function, every I_i is0, so(10) is exactly

  V_h=||X_0||^2-||X_n+s P_K(X_n)||^2.

If h is primitive, it is nonnegative on every such trajectory, proving(1).
Conversely, if h is not primitive, sections2-5 produce a compact polytope
with at most n+2 listed vertices and a negative energy, so(1) fails.
This proves the asserted equivalence with the original intrinsic
primitive inequality.

All old function values remain encoded: they determine I_i and hence
the additional coordinates, the repair coefficient and the final
polytope. The reduction is not a permission to delete queried-history
constraints or optimum terms from an arbitrary full certificate.

The initial norm is changed by the added -Lambda coordinate and the
ball coordinates. The construction does NOT preserve normalized
objective error and does not by itself settle the asymptotic
Zhang-Jiang target. It supplies an exact finite projection realization
for intrinsic primitive defects and a precise geometry in which to
pursue that target's remaining primitive-capacity questions.

No new result in this file has been verified or written as a fact.

# Exact two-cell budget for a fresh orthogonal direction

Status: UNVERIFIED self-contained proof candidate. No solver or verifier
call. This gives an exact conditional choice of innovation energy for two
specified cells, not a uniform comparison for arbitrary complete schedules.

## 1. Fixed old geometry and the two future cells

Let J_old(z)=max_j(eta_j+<a_j,z>) be a finite maximum including zero,
with minimum zero at origin. Assume origin is a true closest minimizer
to the initial point, at distance R>0. Retain all old queried proximal
points z_k and their values H_k=J_old(z_k). These determine the old
smooth-envelope jets. Let X be the fixed next starting position after
the prescribed checkpoint from this retained prefix.

Prescribe a first nonnegative ordinary list of sum S_1, then a checkpoint
b>=0, then a second nonnegative ordinary list of sum S_2. Define

    C_1=S_1+1, C_2=S_2+1, L=S_1+b.

Take q_0 in the old geometric span, offsets a_1,a_2<=0, and beta>0.
All these are fixed parameters in the result below. In a new orthogonal
direction e define

    q=q_0+sqrt(r-||q_0||^2)e,  r>=||q_0||^2,
    ell_1(z)=a_1+<q,z>,
    ell_2(z)=a_2-<beta q,z>,
    J_r=max(J_old,ell_1,ell_2), f_r=env_1 J_r,
    h=<q_0,X>.

The old span contains X, all old normals, all old proximal points and
the initial point. Thus every inner product of q with old data equals
the corresponding product with q_0, while ||q||^2=r. We intend to use
gradient q on the first ordinary block and gradient -beta q on the
second. The new direction is chosen before the actual run. No adaptive
change of the global function occurs.

## 2. All legality conditions are affine in r

At old queried proximal points, preserving both new planes requires

    a_1+<q_0,z_k><=H_k,
    a_2-beta<q_0,z_k><=H_k.                                      (1)

These conditions do not involve r. At a first-block proximal point
X-tq, t in [1,C_1], comparing ell_1 with old plane j gives

    a_1+h-eta_j-<a_j,X>+t<a_j,q_0>-t r>=0.                       (2)

Comparing it with the future plane ell_2 gives

    a_1-a_2+(1+beta)h-(1+beta)t r>=0.                            (3)

The first-block query using the checkpoint is included at t=C_1.
After that checkpoint the second block starts at X-Lq. Its proximal
points are X-(L-t beta)q, t in [1,C_2]. Comparing ell_2 with old
plane j gives

    a_2-beta h-eta_j-<a_j,X>
       +(L-t beta)<a_j,q_0>+beta(L-t beta)r>=0.                   (4)

Comparing it with ell_1 gives

    a_2-a_1-(1+beta)h+(1+beta)(L-t beta)r>=0.                     (5)

The zero plane is already one of the old planes in (2) and (4).
Every expression is affine in t, so (2)-(3) need be checked only at
t=1,C_1 and (4)-(5) only at t=1,C_2. These are exactly the actual
endpoint samples of the ordinary blocks. Intermediates are convex
combinations of endpoint inequalities even if a block contains very
unequal nonnegative steps or zero steps.

Consequently, after (1), the EXACT allowed set for r is the intersection
of r>=||q_0||^2 with the finitely many affine half-line conditions
(2)-(5) at these endpoints. It is a closed interval [r_min,r_max],
possibly empty. A zero coefficient in any inequality requires checking
its constant term; it must not be divided away. Its endpoints are
explicit maxima and minima of the corresponding scalar ratios.

If it is nonempty, it is bounded: the zero-plane condition (2) at
t=C_1 gives r<=(a_1+h)/C_1. Thus no unbounded variance or limiting
parameter is being used. Every allowed r is realized by the displayed
single new coordinate, and all samples belong to one fixed J_r.

Here is the smooth-function justification. When the selected affine
plane is maximal at a proposed proximal point z, its normal is a
subgradient of J_r at z. Since x-z is that normal, z uniquely minimizes
J_r(z)+||x-z||^2/2. This produces precisely the claimed gradient of
the envelope at the queried x. Subgradient monotonicity proves the
envelope gradient is 1-Lipschitz, and the envelope is convex and
differentiable. The position recursions therefore follow the complete
prescribed schedule. Adding the two nonpositive-intercept planes keeps
origin a minimizer and shrinks the old zero set. Since origin was
already closest, the actual distance remains exactly R.

## 3. The exact lookahead policy and its immediate cost

At the first block endpoint, the normalized objective is

    V_1(r)=[2a_1+2h-(2C_1-1)r]/R^2.                            (6)

At the second block endpoint, it is

    V_2(r)=[2a_2-2beta h+K r]/R^2,
    K=2beta L-(2C_2-1)beta^2.                                  (7)

Thus the exact optimal innovation energy over this entire family is

    r_opt=r_max if K>0,
          r_min if K<0,
          any point of the interval if K=0.                     (8)

This is a concrete choice from retained geometry and the supplied
future schedule. It does not assume that the feasible interval exists;
the interval test gives the exact answer. All gradient magnitudes and
the true distance R appear in the formulas.

For r_2>=r_1 in the feasible interval, the immediate price and subsequent
gain are exactly

    V_1(r_1)-V_1(r_2)=(2C_1-1)(r_2-r_1)/R^2,
    V_2(r_2)-V_2(r_1)=K(r_2-r_1)/R^2.                            (9)

If 0<beta<=L/C_2, all the second-block coefficients of r in (4)-(5)
are nonnegative, and K>=beta L/C_2>0 when L>0. Thus first-block
legality puts upper bounds on the fresh energy, the second block puts
lower bounds (with zero-coefficient exceptions checked), and lookahead
chooses the largest allowed amount. This contrasts with (6), which
strictly prefers the smallest amount whenever both are feasible. The
ratio of future gain to immediate cost is exactly K/(2C_1-1).

For larger beta no monotonicity shortcut is made: the signed half-line
intersection and the sign of K in (8) still give the exact solution.

## 4. A full arbitrary-block family that repays the cost

Choose M>1 and tau>=2. Start at x_init=(1,0), put p=(1/M,0), and
take J_old(z)=max(0,<p,z>). First apply ANY nonnegative block of sum
M-1 with gradient p, followed by checkpoint 4M+1. Its endpoint is
X=(-4,0), and all of its proximal samples are d p, 0<=d<=M-1.
Its minimum zero is closest at origin, since every zero has first
coordinate nonpositive; R=1.

In Sections 1-3 take

    q_0=(-2/M,0), a_1=a_2=0, beta=1/2,
    S_1=S_2=M-1, b=tau M+1, L=(tau+1)M, h=8/M.

The new planes at every old positive proximal point are respectively
negative and identical to its existing p-plane, so (1) holds.
The exact feasible innovation interval is

    4/M^2<=r<=8/M^2.                                             (10)

The lower endpoint is the PSD condition r>=||q_0||^2. The zero-plane
first-block endpoint gives the upper endpoint r<=h/M=8/M^2. The
old p-plane bound in (2) is

    r<=-2/M^2+12/(Mt), t=1,M,

which is at least 10/M^2 at its more restrictive endpoint. Condition
(3) gives exactly the same bound as the zero plane. Thus every r in
(10) passes all first-block and future-plane tests.

For the second block, beta<=L/C_2=tau+1, so every test improves as r
increases. It remains to check the lower endpoint. There q=q_0 is
scalar, the second block starts at (2tau-2,0), and its gradient
-q/2=p is exactly the retained old positive normal. Its proximal
points have first coordinates between 2tau-3 and 2tau-2-1/M, all
positive for tau>=2. The p plane is maximal, and the q plane is
negative. This checks every second-block test at the lower endpoint;
their affine monotonicity proves them for the whole interval. Hence
(10) is exact, and every internal and terminal query is legal.

At the two ends of (10), the first-block scores are

    V_1(4/M^2)=8/M+4/M^2,
    V_1(8/M^2)=8/M^2.

The second-block scores are

    V_2(4/M^2)=(4tau-6)/M+1/M^2,
    V_2(8/M^2)=(8tau-4)/M+2/M^2.                               (11)

Thus spending a fresh squared component 4/M^2 costs
8/M-4/M^2 immediately and earns

    (4tau+2)/M+1/M^2

at the next block endpoint. The exact ratio is

    [(4tau+2)M+1]/(8M-4),                                      (12)

which is greater than one for tau>=2 and is unbounded as tau grows.
All three ordinary blocks may have completely different nonperiodic
step patterns; only their prescribed equal total masses are used.
There is no dimension or closest-minimizer loss in (11)-(12).

This example is a test of the general innovation budget, not a new
uniform B_n theorem. Its main point is that the direction discarded
by a greedy immediate-cell optimizer has an exact, demonstrably useful
future value. The arbitrary-prefix interval in Sections 1-3 supplies
the actual legality budget for such decisions.

## Status and next interface

The fact graph and shared findings were searched first. Targeted Matlas
retrieval gave no useful external theorem, and none is used. All new
formulas, old/future-plane checks, and normalization arguments are in
this joint proof. No unverified predecessor is invoked as a fact.

The remaining issue is choosing the old parallel vector q_0, offsets,
and reversal beta over many cells so that the complete exact B_n bound
holds for every prescribed schedule. The innovation amount is now an
explicit endpoint choice conditional on those parameters; their global
choice is not replaced by an existence assertion here.
