# Exact last-crossing capture for nonperiodic scalar profiles

Status: complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. No fact_submit is
allocated. All new ingredients are proved in this document; earlier scalar
findings are not premises. This is a scoped obstruction with an exact
worst-case value, not an all-scalar upper bound.

## 1. A class with unbounded secant variation

Set c_sc=13/5, a_sc=c_sc^(-17), bsc_j=a_sc c_sc^j, and

    Hsc_0=(), Hsc_(j+1)=(Hsc_j,bsc_j,Hsc_j),
    Nsc_j=2^j-1,
    ssc_j=sum Hsc_j=a_sc(c_sc^j-2^j)/(c_sc-2).

Choose any integer ell>=17 and put mu_core=1/bsc_ell<=1. Choose a radius
R_core>0. On each of the positive and negative rays choose a locally
absolutely continuous function G_sigma:[0,infinity)->[0,infinity) such that

    G_sigma(R)=R                         for 0<=R<=1,
    0<=R G_sigma'(R)<=G_sigma(R)/2       for almost every R>1. (1)

The two ray profiles can differ and need not be periodic. Require only

    8/13 <= G_+(R)/G_-(R) <= 13/8        for R>=1.          (2)

Define one fixed physical derivative, before running the algorithm, by

    g(x)= mu_core R_core G_+(x/R_core)   for x>=0,
    g(x)=-mu_core R_core G_-(-x/R_core)  for x<=0,
    f(x)=integral_0^x g(u)du.

These are globally convex differentiable1-smooth functions with unique
minimizer0. In fact their derivatives are mu_core-Lipschitz. To see this,
integrating(1) gives 1<=G_sigma(R)<=sqrt(R) for R>=1 and
0<=G_sigma'(R)<=1/(2sqrt(R))<=1/2 there. On the core the derivative is1;
across0 use G_+(R)+G_-(T)<=R+T. Thus the normalized radial functions
are monotone and1-Lipschitz on their whole domains.

For each fixed mu_core and every horizon m, the exact supremum over this
class, over R_core and all nonzero initial points, is

    sup 2f(x_(Nsc_m))/x_0^2
         = mu_core/(1+2 mu_core ssc_m).                 (3)

More specifically, every trajectory with a strict sign crossing ends
exactly at the minimizer. The remaining trajectories never change sign
and obey the upper bound in(3). Both statements use all actual GD steps.

The class permits arbitrarily many horizon-dependent knots and secants
tending to zero at infinity. For example any measurable elasticity
w(R) in[0,1/2] specifies an even member by
G(R)=exp(integral_1^R w(t)dt/t) outside its core. In particular constant
w=1/4 gives secants G(R)/R=R^(-3/4), with unbounded variation.

A nonperiodic asymmetric example is obtained by defining, for z>=0,

    eta(z)=(1/8)sin(log(1+z)),
    G_+(R)=R^(1/4)exp( eta(log R)/2),
    G_-(R)=R^(1/4)exp(-eta(log R)/2),       R>=1.

Here |eta|<=1/8, |eta'|<=1/8, so the two elasticities lie in[3/16,5/16]
and their ratio lies in[exp(-1/8),exp(1/8)] inside[8/13,13/8]. The latter
follows, for example, from exp(1/8)<=1/(1-1/8)=8/7<13/8. Arbitrary
piecewise absolutely continuous eta with the same bounds is also allowed,
with any finite number of breakpoints chosen as a function of m.

The complete function values in normalized coordinates are

    F(sigma R)=R^2/2                         for R<=1,
    F(sigma R)=1/2+integral_1^R G_sigma(u)du  for R>=1,
    f(x)=mu_core R_core^2 F(x/R_core).                    (4)

No function-value area is omitted in(3) or(4).

## 2. An exact bound for the crossing cost

Fix either one of the radial functions G in(1). Define its increasing
flow clock on positive radii by

    Clock_G(R)=integral_1^R du/G(u).

This equals log R on the core. For R>=1 put q(R)=R/G(R). By(1),

    q'(R)=[1-RG'(R)/G(R)]/G(R)>=1/[2G(R)],

and q(1)=1. Consequently

    Clock_G(R)<=2(q(R)-1),             R>=1.            (5)

We claim that for every h>=2, every r>0, and every positive overshoot
z=hG(r)-r, one has

    Clock_G(z)<=h-2.                                    (6)

If z<1, its clock is negative and(6) holds. Suppose z>=1. If r<=1,
then z=(h-1)r<=h-1. Since G>=1 beyond1, its clock is at most z-1<=h-2.

Now let r>=1 and write u=G(r), q=r/u. If z>=r, monotonicity and(5)
give

    Clock_G(z)<=2(q-1)+(z-r)/u
                  =2(q-1)+h-2q=h-2.

If 1<=z<=r, integration of the elasticity bound in(1) gives
G(z)>=G(r)sqrt(z/r). Therefore(5) gives

    Clock_G(z)<=2(z/G(z)-1)
       <=2(sqrt(rz)/u-1)
       =2sqrt(q(h-q))-2<=h-2.

The last inequality is q(h-q)<=h^2/4. This proves(6) for all cases,
with no homogeneity, curvature constancy, or choice of knots at runtime.

For a crossing from source ray sigma to target ray tau, the landing
radius is still z=hG_sigma(r)-r. If z>=1, condition(2) implies

    Clock_(G_tau)(z)
       <=(13/8) Clock_(G_sigma)(z)
       <=(13/8)(h-2).                                 (7)

If z<1 its target clock is negative, so(7) remains valid for h>=2.

For a noncrossing step r'=r-hG_sigma(r)>0 on the same ray,

    Clock_(G_sigma)(r)-Clock_(G_sigma)(r')
      =integral_(r')^r du/G_sigma(u)
      >=(r-r')/G_sigma(r)=h.                           (8)

These are bounds on the actual fixed derivative, not independent-secant
choices. Equations(7)--(8) are the needed asymmetric flow-state law.

## 3. The actual suffix forces capture after the last crossing

Normalize positions by R_core and the objective by mu_core R_core^2.
The GD steps become h'=mu_core h. Write

    b'_j=mu_core bsc_j=c_sc^(j-ell),
    S'_j=mu_core ssc_j.

In particular b'_ell=1, and the normalized gradient is exactly x on the
unit core. A step of size b'_ell therefore sends every core point to0.

For all j>=17,

    S'_j/b'_j=[1-(2/c_sc)^j]/(c_sc-2)>=13/8.            (9)

Indeed (2/c_sc)^3<1/2 and (2/c_sc)^2<4/5 imply its seventeenth power
is less than1/40. Also

    S'_ell=[1-(2/c_sc)^ell]/(c_sc-2)<5/3.              (10)

Since G_sigma(r)<=r everywhere, a strict crossing can occur only at a
step h'>1. Thus it has some level j>=ell+1>=18 and h'=b'_j>=c_sc>2.
If the trajectory reaches0 anywhere it remains there. In the other case,
choose its last strict crossing and call its level j and target ray tau.
By(7) its landing clock is at most(13/8)(b'_j-2).

Every occurrence of level j in the ruler word is immediately followed
by the complete word Hsc_j. Since j>=ell+1, that suffix contains a
step of level ell. The steps after the last such step in Hsc_j form
exactly Hsc_ell. Therefore the physical normalized step sum after the
chosen crossing and before that cancelling step is at least

    S'_j-1-S'_ell.                                     (11)

There are no subsequent strict crossings by choice of the last crossing.
If no iterate has yet reached0, all these steps move inward on ray tau,
so(8) adds their exact time lengths. At the input to the cancelling step,
its clock is at most

    (13/8)(b'_j-2)-(S'_j-1-S'_ell)
      <= S'_ell-9/4 < -7/12 <0.                      (12)

Negative clock means radius less than1. The next actual step has size1
and gradient equal to its position, so it sends this iterate exactly to0.
All remaining steps keep it there. This proves the last-crossing assertion.
It also covers a landing in the core directly. If m<=ell+1, all steps
are at most1 in normalized units and no strict crossing is possible.

## 4. Exact objective on the surviving paths

Consider a trajectory that never crosses, has nonzero endpoint of radius
R_end, and normalized endpoint gradient magnitude u. All queried radii
are at least R_end, so all queried gradient magnitudes are at least u.
Writing S'=mu_core ssc_m and R_init=|x_0|/R_core, the exact position
telescope gives

    R_init>=R_end+S' u.                               (13)

Every G_sigma is monotone1-Lipschitz and vanishes at0. Its complete
area up to R_end is at most the area under min(r,u):

    F(sigma R_end)<=u R_end-u^2/2.                     (14)

Use(13) in(14) and complete the scalar square:

    2F(sigma R_end)
       <=2u R_init-(2S'+1)u^2
       <=R_init^2/(2S'+1).                            (15)

Multiplying the normalized ratio by mu_core proves the upper bound(3).
Crossing trajectories have value0 by section3 and satisfy it too.

For equality take both profiles G_sigma(R)=min(R,1), which satisfy(1)
and(2), and take normalized initial radius R_init=2S'+1. Every iterate
then remains on the positive plateau and the endpoint is R_end=S'+1.
Its exact area is F(R_end)=S'+1/2, yielding equality in(15). This proves
the asserted supremum is attained, including m=0. The core scale and
physical normalization in(4) give precisely(3), not a gradient-norm proxy.

## 5. Exact benchmark comparison and limits of the result

Uniformly in ell and R_core,

    mu_core/(1+2 mu_core ssc_m)<=1/(1+2ssc_m),          (16)

because mu_core<=1. Equality in this further supremum is attained at
ell=17, where mu_core=1. For m>=3 the sum formula and
(2/c_sc)^m<1/2 give

    1/(1+2ssc_m) <= (c_sc-2)c_sc^(-m)/a_sc.

For completeness, the comparison uses the exact recursions in accepted
fact b98bb807d514e80d, not a numerical asymptotic constant. In shifted
variables C_n=S_circle(n)+1 and B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 they are
C_0=B_0=1,

    C_n=max_j Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_j Gamma(C_j,B_(n-j-1)),
    Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,
    Gamma(A,B)=2A+B/2+sqrt(B^2+8AB)/2.

The needed bound B_n<=1+4n^(4/3) has a short independent proof.
The positive-root formula gives
Omega(A,B)<=(A^(3/4)+B^(3/4))^(4/3) once
t^(4/3)+(1-t)^(4/3)+[t(1-t)]^(4/3)<=1 on[0,1]. With
u=t^(1/3), v=(1-t)^(1/3), the difference is
u^3v^3[1/(1+u+u^2)+1/(1+v+v^2)-uv]>=0, because both reciprocals
are at least1/3 and uv<=2^(-2/3)<2/3. Induction yields
C_n<=(n+1)^(4/3). Then Gamma(A,B)<=B+4A and the power-sum inequality
give B_n<=1+4n^(4/3) by induction. Consequently the ratio of(16) to
U_(Nsc_m)^ZJ is at most

    ((c_sc-2)/a_sc)c_sc^(-m)[1+4(2^m-1)^(4/3)] ->0,

since c_sc^3>16. This comparison is uniform over all admitted profiles,
core levels, radii, knots, initial points, and horizon-dependent choices.

The exact quadratic core is load-bearing: its reciprocal curvature must
occur as a physical ruler step. The argument does not replace that step
by an approximate cancellation. It also uses outer elasticity at most1/2
and the factor13/8 comparison of the two radial derivatives. The result is
therefore not an all-scalar obstruction. Removing core resonance, allowing
faster outer growth, or allowing much larger changing ray asymmetry are
separate unresolved mechanisms.

The local paper2103.01338 was checked for the motivation that nonlinear
scalar profiles can behave differently from quadratics. Its log-cosh
example concerns fractal Chebyshev steps and is described there as a
simulation; it supplies no theorem for this ruler word. Matlas returned
no applicable theorem for(6). No external result is used in the proof.

# The core-resonance boundary and a larger capture class

The counterexample concerns exact annihilation, not the objective upper
bound. The second result extends the capture class without using C23 as
an unverified premise.

## 1. Removing exact resonance breaks annihilation on the actual ruler word

Let c_sc=13/5, a_sc=c_sc^(-17), bsc_j=a_sc c_sc^j and
Hsc_(j+1)=(Hsc_j,bsc_j,Hsc_j), with Hsc_0 empty and Nsc_j=2^j-1 its
length. Take the single fixed
function

    f(x)=x^2/4                 for |x|<=1,
    f(x)=|x|/2-1/4            for |x|>=1.

Its derivative is g(x)=(1/2)max(-1,min(x,1)), globally monotone and
1/2-Lipschitz, and its unique minimizer is0. Its two outer radial
profiles are constant, so every outer growth and symmetry requirement
from the capture proposal holds. Its core curvature is mu=1/2.

Start at x_0=1 and use the complete actual word Hsc_19. Each step in
Hsc_18 is at most bsc_17=1. Thus while in the core it has multiplier
1-h/2 in[1/2,1), preserving sign and decreasing radius. Define the exact
positive product

    P18=product_(j=0)^17
             (1-bsc_j/2)^(2^(17-j)).

The first Hsc_18 sends x_0 to P18. The next actual checkpoint is
bsc_18=13/5, with core multiplier1-13/10=-3/10. The final Hsc_18
again remains in the core and multiplies by P18. Hence

    x_(Nsc_19)=-(3/10)P18^2 !=0,
    2f(x_(Nsc_19))/x_0^2=(9/200)P18^4>0.

All intermediate points are in the core, and the central step is a
strict crossing. This is a fully legal counterexample to the extension
"every crossing trajectory ends exactly at0" after dropping the
resonance assumption. No physical ruler step equals2: for j>=17 it is
(13/5)^(j-17), and prime factorization excludes equality with2; steps
before17 are less than1. Thus no core multiplier is zero.

The example supplies no benchmark-scale lower bound: its exact payoff
is small and no asymptotic separation is asserted. It identifies a
specific invalid extension of the capture argument, not instability
of the actual scalar problem. Nonresonance is necessary to escape this
annihilation mechanism, but this example does not establish that it is
sufficient to construct a hard profile.

## 2. A continuous tradeoff between outer growth and ray asymmetry

Fix any p_grow in[1/2,2/3], put beta_grow=1-p_grow and

    K_grow=(p_grow/beta_grow)^(p_grow),
    1<=kappa_ray<=13/(8 K_grow).

Choose an integer ell>=17 and mu_core=1/bsc_ell<=1, a core radius
R_core>0, and two locally absolutely continuous radial functions with

    G_sigma(R)=R                           on[0,1],
    0<=R G_sigma'(R)<=p_grow G_sigma(R)     almost everywhere beyond1,
    1/kappa_ray<=G_+(R)/G_-(R)<=kappa_ray   for R>=1.

Set g(sigma R_core R)=sigma mu_core R_core G_sigma(R) and integrate
from0 to define f. These are legal fixed convex differentiable
mu_core-smooth functions: 1<=G_sigma(R)<=R^(p_grow)<=R beyond1,
and G_sigma'<=p_grow R^(p_grow-1)<=1. Across the origin the same
Lipschitz bound follows from G_sigma(R)<=R. All complete values are

    f(sigma R_core R)/(mu_core R_core^2)
       =R^2/2                         for R<=1,
       =1/2+integral_1^R G_sigma(u)du  for R>=1.

For this entire class, for every m,

    sup 2f(x_(Nsc_m))/x_0^2
       =mu_core/(1+2 mu_core ssc_m),                    (1)

where ssc_m=a_sc(c_sc^m-2^m)/(c_sc-2). Again every path with a strict
crossing ends exactly at0. The class allows arbitrary nonperiodic
elasticities in the specified range and horizon-dependent knot counts.

### Standalone crossing estimate

For one radial profile write Clock(R)=integral_1^R du/G(u) and
q(R)=R/G(R). For R>=1,

    q'(R)>=beta_grow/G(R),
    Clock(R)<=(q(R)-1)/beta_grow.                      (2)

For a crossing z=hG(r)-r>0 at h>=2 we claim

    Clock(z)<=K_grow h-1/beta_grow.                    (3)

First, beta_grow K_grow=p_grow^(p_grow) beta_grow^(beta_grow)
is at least1/2 on the stated range. The logarithm of twice this
quantity is0 at p_grow=1/2 and has derivative
log(p_grow/beta_grow)>=0. Consequently K_grow>=1/(2 beta_grow).
The right side of(3) is nonnegative for h>=2. If z<1 this proves(3).
If r<=1<=z, monotonicity gives Clock(z)<=z-1<=h-2, which is at most
the right side because beta_grow<=1/2.

Now suppose r,z>=1 and put u=G(r), q=r/u. When z>=r we have q<=h/2;
using(2) and monotonicity,

    Clock(z)<=(q-1)/beta_grow+(z-r)/u
      =h+(1/beta_grow-2)q-1/beta_grow
      <=h/(2 beta_grow)-1/beta_grow
      <=K_grow h-1/beta_grow.

When z<=r, integration of the growth bound gives
G(z)>=u(z/r)^(p_grow). Hence

    z/G(z)<=q^(p_grow)(h-q)^(beta_grow)
       <=p_grow^(p_grow) beta_grow^(beta_grow) h.

The last maximum occurs at q=p_grow h; differentiating its logarithm
establishes it on0<q<h. Substitution into(2) proves(3).

For a crossing to the other ray with z>=1, the target clock is at most
kappa_ray times its source clock. For z<1 the target clock is negative.
Thus the target cost is bounded by

    kappa_ray(K_grow h-1/beta_grow).                   (4)

Any noncrossing step decreases its own ray clock by at least h, since
the integral of1/G between its new and old radii is at least its
displacement divided by the old gradient.

### The actual last crossing and the cancelling step

Normalize the physical GD steps by mu_core. Put b'_j=c_sc^(j-ell)
and S'_j=mu_core ssc_j. The level-ell step has size1 and cancels every
unit-core point. Since G_sigma(R)<=R, any strict crossing has level
j>=ell+1 and size b'_j>=c_sc>2. Its immediately following Hsc_j
contains a final level-ell step, with trailing suffix Hsc_ell.

For j>=17,

    S'_j/b'_j=[1-(2/c_sc)^j]/(c_sc-2)>=13/8,
    S'_ell<5/3.                                       (5)

The first inequality follows from (2/c_sc)^17<1/40, itself implied by
(2/c_sc)^3<1/2 and (2/c_sc)^2<4/5.

After the last strict crossing, if no point has yet reached0, all
subsequent steps move inward on the same ray. The time before the
specified cancelling step is S'_j-1-S'_ell. Its input clock is therefore
less than or equal to

    (kappa_ray K_grow-13/8)b'_j
                         +1+S'_ell-kappa_ray/beta_grow. (6)

Because the coefficient of b'_j is nonpositive, use b'_j>=c_sc and
S'_ell<5/3. The resulting upper bound increases with kappa_ray, since
K_grow c_sc-1/beta_grow>=0. At its allowed maximum it becomes

    8/3-13/(8 beta_grow K_grow)<0.                    (7)

To check the strict sign without a decimal estimate, the quantity
beta_grow K_grow increases with p_grow and at2/3 equals4^(1/3)/3.
Since4^(1/3)<8/5, it is less than8/15. The bound in(7) is therefore
less than8/3-195/64=-73/192. Negative clock places the iterate inside
the quadratic core, and the next actual size1 step sends it to0.
This proves the annihilation assertion for every crossing path.

### Complete value bound and sharpness

For a surviving noncrossing path let u be its terminal normalized
gradient magnitude and R_end its radius. With S'=mu_core ssc_m,
its exact position telescope yields R_init>=R_end+S'u. Monotonicity
and1-smoothness bound the full function area by uR_end-u^2/2. Hence

    2F_end<=2uR_init-(2S'+1)u^2<=R_init^2/(2S'+1).

Rescaling proves the upper bound(1). It is attained by the symmetric
Huber choice G_sigma(R)=min(R,1), starting at R_init=2S'+1; its entire
trajectory stays on the plateau and has R_end=S'+1 and
F_end=S'+1/2. Empty horizons are included.

This proves the continuous tradeoff independently of C23. In particular,
even outer profiles can have arbitrary elasticity up to2/3, with no
periodicity, while the p_grow=1/2 endpoint allows ray ratio13/8. A
matching core checkpoint remains indispensable to this exact capture
argument, as the legal Hsc_19 example in section1 demonstrates.

# Every ruler prefix preserves a quadratic neighborhood

Status: complete unverified candidate, no verifier allocation. This result
does not assume a core curvature reciprocal to a schedule step. It excludes
initial points already inside a quadratic core; it does not exclude an
outside initial point entering a core during a partial block.

## Statement

Put c_sc=13/5, a_sc=c_sc^(-17), bsc_j=a_sc c_sc^j,
Hsc_0=(), Hsc_(j+1)=(Hsc_j,bsc_j,Hsc_j), and Nsc_m=2^m-1. For every
lambda in[0,1], every m>=0, and EVERY chronological prefix h_0,...,h_(t-1)
of Hsc_m, including the empty prefix,

    |product_(i=0)^(t-1)(1-lambda h_i)|<=1.             (1)

Writing Q_m(lambda)=|product_(h in Hsc_m)(1-lambda h)|, also

    lambda Q_m(lambda)^2 <= (c_sc/a_sc)c_sc^(-m).      (2)

Consequently let f be any globally convex differentiable1-smooth function
on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space with minimizer0 and f(0)=0.
Suppose that on the closed ball of radius R_core it is exactly
f(x)=<x,A_core x>/2, where A_core is a real symmetric matrix satisfying
0<=A_core<=I. For every nonzero initial point in that ball, the entire
GD trajectory on Hsc_m stays in the same ball and sees only that
quadratic. Thus

    2f(x_(Nsc_m))/||x_0||^2
         <=(c_sc/a_sc)c_sc^(-m).                       (3)

The nonlinear continuation outside the ball is arbitrary and can depend
on the horizon. It never influences the trajectory. Scalar cores of
every curvature lambda in(0,1], including nonresonant ones, are included.

## 1. Scalar proof, including every intermediate prefix

Abbreviate c=c_sc, a=a_sc, b_j=bsc_j and eta=13/8. The case lambda=0
has every product equal to1 and zero objective. Assume lambda>0 and let
I be the first level with t=lambda b_I>1. Then I>=18 and 1<t<=c.
Every step of Hsc_I has lambda h<=1, so every one of its prefix products
has magnitude at most1. Its complete product is a number P in[0,1].

The physical sum is

    ssc_I=a(c^I-2^I)/(c-2),
    ssc_I/b_I=[1-(2/c)^I]/(c-2)>=eta.

For the last inequality, (2/c)^3<1/2 and (2/c)^2<4/5 imply
(2/c)^17<1/40. The bound1-z<=exp(-z) on[0,1] therefore gives

    P<=exp(-lambda ssc_I)<=exp(-eta t).                (4)

The word Hsc_(I+1) is (Hsc_I,b_I,Hsc_I). Before its middle step the
amplitude is at most P. At and after that step it is at most
(t-1)P<1, since (t-1)P<=(c-1)exp(-eta)<1. The last strict inequality
follows from exp(eta)>1+eta>c-1. Thus every prefix of Hsc_(I+1) also
has amplification at most1.

Its complete multiplier magnitude is Q_(I+1)=P^2(t-1). We need the
stronger bound

    Q_(I+1)<=1/[c lambda b_(I+1)].                     (5)

Since b_(I+1)=c b_I, multiplying(5) by its denominator and using(4)
reduces it to c^2 t(t-1)exp(-2eta t)<=1. The elementary exponential
series gives exp(2eta t)> (2eta t)^3/6, so the left side is at most

    [3c^2/(4eta^3)](t-1)/t^2
       <=3c^2/(16eta^3)<1.                            (6)

Here (t-1)/t^2<=1/4 follows from (t-2)^2>=0, and the last inequality
is a strict rational comparison at c=13/5 and eta=13/8. Zero factors
in P cause no difficulty and only strengthen these inequalities.

Now induct on j>=I+1. Suppose every prefix of Hsc_j has amplification
at most1 and its complete multiplier satisfies Q_j<=1/(c lambda b_j).
Put z=lambda b_j>1. In Hsc_(j+1) the first complete block has output
amplitude at most Q_j relative to its input. Its central checkpoint
therefore produces amplitude at most

    (z-1)Q_j <=(z-1)/(c z)<1/c.

Every prefix of the following Hsc_j multiplies this by at most1. This
proves(1) at the next level. Moreover the exact recursion gives

    Q_(j+1)=Q_j^2(z-1)
       <=(z-1)/(c^2 z^2)<1/(c^2 z)
       =1/[c lambda b_(j+1)].                         (7)

Equations(5)--(7) prove the induction. Earlier horizons m<=I already
have every lambda h<=1, completing the proof of(1) for all horizons.

## 2. Uniform complete-block objective

For m<=I, equation(1) gives lambda Q_m^2<=lambda, while
lambda=t/b_I<=c/b_I<=c/b_m. For m>=I+1, equation(7) gives

    lambda Q_m^2<=1/[c^2 lambda b_m^2]
       <1/(c^3 b_m)<=c/b_m,

because lambda b_m=c^(m-I)t>c. As c/b_m=(c/a)c^(-m), this proves(2).
The bound is uniform over lambda, including horizon-dependent choices.

## 3. Arbitrary nonlinear continuation is invisible from inside the core

Diagonalize the real symmetric matrix A_core orthogonally. In each
eigendirection of eigenvalue lambda, quadratic GD multiplies by exactly
the scalar prefix product in(1). Hence every quadratic prefix map has
Euclidean operator norm at most1, and its iterates stay within the
initial radius. At each such point the actual gradient of f is A_core x,
including the boundary by differentiability and continuity. Induction
on the actual GD steps therefore identifies the actual iterates with
the quadratic iterates throughout the entire word.

In that orthonormal eigenbasis the exact final objective is the sum of
lambda Q_m(lambda)^2 times the corresponding squared initial coordinate.
Using(2) termwise proves(3). This is full objective area and the original
squared-distance normalization. A semidefinite zero eigenspace is harmless.

## 4. Exact-profile comparison

Use the benchmark definitions from accepted fact b98bb807d514e80d:
C_n=S_circle(n)+1 and B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 obey the positive-root joins

    C_n=max_j Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_j Gamma(C_j,B_(n-j-1)), C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,
    Gamma(A,B)=2A+B/2+sqrt(B^2+8AB)/2.

To make the comparison independent of earlier unverified findings,
Omega(A,B)<=(A^(3/4)+B^(3/4))^(4/3) follows from
t^(4/3)+(1-t)^(4/3)+[t(1-t)]^(4/3)<=1. For u=t^(1/3) and
v=(1-t)^(1/3), the difference is
u^3v^3[1/(1+u+u^2)+1/(1+v+v^2)-uv]>=0: both reciprocals are at
least1/3 and uv<=2^(-2/3)<2/3. Induction gives C_n<=(n+1)^(4/3).
The bound Gamma(A,B)<=B+4A and the power-sum inequality then give
B_n<=1+4n^(4/3). Thus the ratio of(3) to U_(Nsc_m)^ZJ is at most

    (c_sc/a_sc)c_sc^(-m)[1+4(2^m-1)^(4/3)] ->0,

because c_sc^3>16.

## Scope

Changing an arbitrary outside profile cannot create a hard instance
from an initial point inside its exact quadratic neighborhood, even
when the core curvature is off the checkpoint grid. To exploit nonlinear
geometry one must start outside that neighborhood, or use a function
with no exact quadratic neighborhood. Entrance during a partial block
is different: this proof bounds prefixes of complete Hsc_j words, not
every suffix from every possible entrance time. No all-scalar claim is
made, and no new fact-graph node has been created.

fact_submit. All calculations and interpolation checks are included here;
no unverified result is used as a premise.

## 1. Supplied data and the exact extension functional

Let b be any nonnegative tail schedule of capacity D=1+sum b_i, with
actual legal convex1-smooth sampled data(x_j,g_j,f_j), minimizer0 and

  f_j=<g_j,x_j>-||g_j||^2/2                              (1)

at every sample. Thus every incoming optimum slack is0. Define

  K=conv{0,g_0,...,g_m}, sigma_K(v)=max_(g in K)<g,v>,
  x=x_0, g=g_m, y=x_m-g_m, delta=<g,y>>=0.

Let a be any nonnegative prefix block of capacity A. Choose r>0 with

  T=A+D+r, rT=AD,
  beta=T/D=A/r>1, ell=A+r=(beta-1)D.                    (2)

For v in the closed halfspace

  <v,y><=delta+<x,y>/r,                                (3)

put

  C_ext(v)=max{
    ||ell v-beta x||^2,
    beta^2||x||^2+ell^2[sigma_K(v)-<x/D,v>]
  }.                                                   (4)

This is a finite continuous convex coercive function. The halfspace is
nonempty: in the equivalent variable p=v-x/r, p=0 is feasible because
delta>=0. Hence its minimum C_min is attained.

We prove the concrete implication

  C_min<||y+Tg||^2  ==>  (a,1+r,b) is not primitive.     (5)

The construction retains the full tail gradient hull in sigma_K and
the actual terminal value delta in(3). No condition saying that missing
interpolation constraints are feasible is assumed: they are checked
below. Formula(4) is the exact smallest auxiliary starting norm in the
constant-prefix-gradient extension family described next.

## 2. The new prefix gradient and its supporting condition

Fix any v satisfying(3), put p=v-x/r, and define

    [sigma_K(x+rp)-<p,x>-r||p||^2]/r}.                   (6)

Take the nonnegative square root z. Embed the whole supplied tail with
one additional zero coordinate. Give every new prefix query the same
gradient P=(p,z). The last prefix query has point

  X_L=(x,0)+(1+r)P,

and the first query has point

  X_start=(x,0)+(A+r)P.

The bridge step1+r lands exactly at the supplied tail initial point(x,0).
All individual steps of a are realized by this constant gradient,
including zero steps. Assign every new value

Let Y_L=(x,0)+rP. Equation(6) says exactly

  <(g_j,0)-P,Y_L><=0 for every tail gradient and for0.    (7)

The gradient0 condition gives <P,Y_L>>=0. Earlier prefix queries have
proximal points Y_L+HP, with H their remaining prefix step sum, and
outgoing optimum slacks <P,Y_L>+H||P||^2>=0.

The new-prefix-to-final-tail residual is

  <P-(g,0),(y,0)>=<p,y>-delta<=0                       (8)

by(3). Every tail query with zero remaining steps is identical to the
final one, so(8) also handles all terminal zero-step duplicates.

At this stage the auxiliary array is not assumed legal at all other
cross edges.

## 3. Why the starting norm is exactly(4)

For fixed p, condition(7) is equivalent to the lower bound on z^2 in(6).
The squared starting norm is

  ||x+ell p||^2+ell^2 z^2.

It increases with z^2, so(6) is its minimum. Expanding the maximum gives

beta^2||x||^2+ell^2[sigma_K(v)-<x/D,v>], proving(4).

The halfspace(3) is precisely the remaining active condition(8).

minimum starting norm over the single-extra-coordinate extensions of
this specified kind. Any number of added orthogonal coordinates has
the same best value, since only their total squared gradient norm enters.

Its prefix gradient is1 and the prefix ends at1; the bridge lands at-r.

last tail query or its zero-step duplicates; the auxiliary constraint

Combine the scalar base and the auxiliary data in orthogonal coordinates,

All incoming optimum slacks still vanish.

This identity is algebraic and does not require prior cross feasibility.
The auxiliary endpoint has zero added coordinate, so its energy is

If this is negative, equations(9),(11) produce a legal mixture of energy
epsilon V_aux<0. Taking a minimizer of(4) proves(5).

At v=0 this recovers the old forced-core-prefix choice p=-x/r,z=0,
when that choice satisfies(3), and its starting cost is beta^2||x||^2.

## 6. Sharp calibration on a retained affine tail

Let every tail gradient equal1 on the scalar projection function for
K=[0,1]. Start at x=D+w with any w>0, so the endpoint is1+w,
y=w and delta=w. The admissibility condition in p is p<=1.

For p<=-x/r, the support is0 and the cost is at least beta^2 x^2.
For -x/r<=p<=1, formula(6) is

  z^2=(1-p)(x+rp)/r,

and the squared starting cost is affine in p with slope

  ell^2(1-x/D)=-ell^2 w/D<0.

It is therefore minimized at p=1,z=0, with

  C_min=(T+w)^2=||y+Tg||^2.

The forced-core-prefix choice instead has the strictly larger cost

  beta^2(D+w)^2-(T+w)^2
    =(beta-1)w[2T+(beta+1)w]>0.

This recovers the exact zero-energy affine trajectory without losing
its nonzero terminal value. It shows that the earlier penalty was a
penalty of a specified extension, not an optimal-extension obstruction.

## 7. A negative witness hidden by that forced-prefix penalty

Take the tail h=(3/2), D=5/2, and the fixed two-dimensional function

  f(u,v)=u^2/2+H_1(v),

where H_1 is the ordinary Huber function of threshold1. Start at
x=(1,D+1). Its endpoint and gradient are

  x_m=(-1/2,2), g=(-1/2,1), y=(0,1), delta=1.

Every incoming optimum slack is0 and V_tail=-9/16. Use an empty prefix
A=1 and the saturated bridge

  r=(sqrt(89)-7)/4, T=(7+sqrt(89))/4,
  beta=T/D=(7+sqrt(89))/10>8/5.

The forced-core-prefix choice has energy

this supplied tail witness from refuting the joined schedule.

The new choice p=(-1/r,1),z=0 is admissible:
Y_L=(0,D+1+r), so every supplied tail gradient has the same inner
product with Y_L as p, and the terminal constraint is equality.
Its starting point is(-beta,T+1), with energy exactly

In fact here the original fixed function u^2/2+H_1(v) already realizes

It does not give a new asymptotic schedule or prove arbitrary-tail
heredity. Such a theorem would still need to show the strict criterion(5)

evidence:
# A quantitative exact terminal completion on nonperiodic schedules

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof candidate. No verifier or numerical-solver
request. This is an explicit family at every sufficiently large horizon,
not the unrestricted all-schedule comparison. Every new calculation used
below is included here; no unverified finding is a premise.

Verified predecessors used:

- `1252b8823bb5a290`: the complete smooth-convex interpolation inequality
  and the pointwise maximal completion at a genuinely unqueried terminal.
- `dfde2fa326c908bf`: the exact Chebyshev steps, their sum and polynomial,
  and the universal complex-lens construction and polynomial estimate.
- `b98bb807d514e80d`: the single-cut functional K_n, the exact benchmark
  recursions, and B_n <= 1+4 n^p for p=log_2(3).

We use smoothness one and initial distance one throughout. Thus the
normalized objective is 2f(x_n). General smoothness follows by scaling.

## 1. An arbitrary-block prefix with a completely specified fresh direction

Let M>=2 and A>=4. Prescribe ANY two nonnegative ordinary lists of sum
M-1 each, separated by the checkpoint AM+1. A final step b will be added
after the second list. Work in R^2 and put

    nu=sqrt(2A-4),
    p=(1,0)/M,                  q=(-2,nu)/M,
    J(z)=max(0,<p,z>,<q,z>),
    f_old=env_1 J,              x_init=(1,0).

The squared boundary gradient is exactly ||q||^2=2A/M^2. The fresh
component of q has squared norm (2A-4)/M^2; it is not dropped from the
state or normalization.

In the first block every gradient is p. To check this, a query after
ordinary partial mass u has proposed proximal point

    z=(1-(u+1)/M,0),       0<=u<=M-1.

Here <p,z>>=0 and <q,z>=-2<p,z>. Thus p is an active subgradient of J.
At the checkpoint query the position is p and its proximal point is 0.
The checkpoint AM+1 sends the trajectory to X=(-A,0).

In the second block every gradient is q. Write t=u+1 in [1,M]. Its
proposed proximal point is X-tq. The current height is

    <q,X-tq>=(2A/M)(1-t/M)>=0.

Its excess over the p-plane is

    <q-p,X-tq>=3A/M-(2A+2)t/M^2 >= (A-2)/M >0.

This checks both other planes at every actual query, even if an
individual ordinary step is very large. The comparisons are affine in
t, and the displayed bounds hold on the whole interval. The old q-plane
was already checked at every first-block query, so both cross directions
and every queried sample belong to the same fixed J.

The envelope justification is elementary: if g is an active-plane
subgradient at z and x=z+g, its subgradient inequality makes z the unique
minimizer of J(w)+||x-w||^2/2. Adding the inequalities for two such
proximal pairs proves

    ||g(x)-g(x')||^2 <= <g(x)-g(x'),x-x'>.

The minimizing inequalities identify g as the derivative of the convex
envelope, which is consequently 1-smooth. All claimed GD updates and
sample values follow from this fixed envelope.

At the last query, just before the final step b, the proximal point and
position are respectively

    y=X-Mq=(2-A,-nu),         x_last=y+q.

One has <q,y>=0, <p,y><0, f_old(x_last)=||q||^2/2. At ALL old
queries the value and gradient are retained in the completion below.

## 2. The exact four-anchor maximal interpolant

Set

    a=1-1/M,       z_A=(a,0),       delta_A=a/M,
    z_B=X-q,
    delta_B=(M-1)||q||^2.

For a retained jet (x,g,f), its proximal point z=x-g and height
delta=f-||g||^2/2 give the conjugate quadratic

    ||v||^2/2 + <z,v> - delta.

This is exactly the quadratic H_j in fact 1252b8823bb5a290 after
expansion. In the first block (z,delta) traces the line segment from
(z_A,delta_A) to (0,0). Both endpoints are actual queried samples. In
the second block it traces the segment from (z_B,delta_B) to (y,0),
again with both endpoints queried. Therefore the maximum of ALL retained
quadratics, including the optimum jet, is exactly

    H(v)=||v||^2/2 + max(0,
                        <z_A,v>-delta_A,
                        <y,v>,
                        <y,v>+(M-1)(<q,v>-||q||^2)).             (1)

No constraint is deleted: intermediate quadratics are convex
combinations of these endpoint quadratics. By the accepted fact,

    F(x)=sup_v [<x,v>-H(v)]                                    (2)

is one fixed finite convex 1-smooth function, preserves every old query,
has F(0)=0=min F, and is the pointwise maximal such interpolant.
It is selected before running the complete prescribed schedule.

The actual closest-minimizer distance stays ONE. The initial jet is

    x_init=(1,0),  g_init=p,  F(x_init)=1/M-1/(2M^2).

For any minimizer z of F, the accepted interpolation inequality between
this jet and (z,0,0) gives

    0 >= F(x_init)+<p,z-x_init>+||p||^2/2 = <p,z>.

Hence z has first coordinate <=0 and ||x_init-z||>=1. Origin attains
distance one. This proves the genuine normalization for F, not merely
for the old envelope.

## 3. Closed formula at the genuinely unqueried terminal

Let

    b=1+M epsilon,    0<=epsilon<=1,
    d=(2,-nu)=-Mq,
    e=z_A-y=(A-2+a,nu),
    D=||e||^2=(A-2+a)^2+2A-4.

The actual terminal point is

    x_n=x_last-bq = y+epsilon d.

Define

    tau=a(2epsilon-1/M)_+/D,
    v=epsilon d-tau e.                                       (3)

Here 0<=tau<=2epsilon/D<=1/2 because D>=(A-2)^2>=4.
The elementary products that will be used are

    ||d||^2=2A,   <d,e>=2a,   <y,d>=0,
    <y,e>=-(A-2)(A+a)<0.                                    (4)

We now check ALL four affine terms in (1) at v.

If tau=0, the y-term and zero term both equal zero, and the z_A-term
is a(2epsilon-1/M)<=0. If tau>0, then

    <e,v>=2a epsilon-tau D=a/M,

so the y-term and z_A-term tie. The y-term is nonnegative because
<y,v>=-tau<y,e>>=0. Finally

    <q,v>=-[2A epsilon-2a tau]/M <=0,

since tau<=2epsilon/D and 2A-4/D>0. Consequently the z_B-term is
strictly below the y-term, its difference being
(M-1)(<q,v>-||q||^2)<0. This also handles epsilon=0.

For tau=0, y is an active subgradient of the max-affine part of H.
For tau>0, y+tau e is the convex combination (1-tau)y+tau z_A
of its active slopes. In both cases

    x_n=v+y+tau e

is a subgradient of H at v. Strong convexity of H therefore makes v
the unique maximizer in (2), and it is the ACTUAL terminal gradient.
Substituting (3)-(4) gives the exact normalized value

    V(M,A,epsilon) := 2F(x_n)
       = 2A epsilon^2
         - a^2(2epsilon-1/M)_+^2/D.                         (5)

Every parameter and endpoint is finite, and epsilon=0 is included.
In particular, since a<=1 and D>=4,

    A epsilon^2 <= V(M,A,epsilon) <= 2A epsilon^2.           (6)

The precise relative loss from the upper bound is at most
2/(A D)<=2/[A(A-2)^2], which tends to zero as A grows.
Equation (5), rather than that limit, is used in the comparisons below.

There is a substantial completion effect here. For A>=4 and epsilon<=1,
both <p,x_n> and <q,x_n> are nonpositive. Thus J(x_n)=0 and
f_old(x_n)=0, whereas (5) is positive for epsilon>0. No queried value
has changed: only the behavior away from the retained samples differs.
The original old function's unqueried zero set does not constrain the
maximal interpolant. Its actual closest minimizer remains at distance one.

The upper bound in (6) also has an intrinsic interpretation. Every
interpolant of the last query and optimum has F(y)=0 by the unit-step
descent inequality, because F(y+q)=||q||^2/2. Smoothness then gives
2F(x_n)<=||x_n-y||^2=2A epsilon^2. The exact completion loses only
the displayed finite old-query correction from this upper bound.

## 4. A fixed horizon-dependent choice

For each integer N>=4096 let Chi_N be the increasing list

    c_j=sec^2((2j-1)pi/[2(2N+1)]),       1<=j<=N.

Write L_N for THREE successive copies of this list, and define

    M=2N(N+1)+1,       A=M^(1/12),       epsilon=M^(-1/3),
    h^(N)=(L_N, AM+1, L_N, 1+M^(2/3)),
    n_N=6N+2.                                                 (7)

The exact sum formula in dfde2fa326c908bf makes each L_N have mass
M-1. Also M>=4^12, so A>=4 and the preceding construction applies
without a limiting argument. It gives the explicit value (5), and

    W_(n_N)(h^(N)) >= V(M,A,epsilon) >= M^(-7/12).             (8)

To obtain a family at EVERY integer horizon n>=24578, take
N=floor((n-2)/6), and insert n-(6N+2) zero steps at the very beginning
of (7). These duplicate a retained query, change no trajectory or
value, and preserve the same formula. No new terminal jet is queried
before the final nonzero step. Denote this length-n schedule by h^[n].

The first bridge is of order M^(13/12), the final bridge is of order
M^(2/3), and the ordinary lists depend on the horizon. This is not a
fixed periodic schedule or a bounded-length legality example.

## 5. Every quadratic and every specified single-cut Huber test is smaller

Let Q_n(h) denote the maximum normalized terminal error of all convex
quadratics with curvature in [0,1], over every dimension. By orthogonal
diagonalization this is

    Q_n(h)=max_(0<=lambda<=1) lambda product_j(1-h_j lambda)^2.

Set T=(2N+1)^2=2M-1, and let P_N be the polynomial of Chi_N. The
verified Chebyshev identity implies

    |P_N(lambda)|^2 <= min(1,1/(T lambda)),   0<lambda<=1.      (9)

For the first bound, put sqrt(lambda)=sin(theta): the numerator of
P_N is, up to sign, sin((2N+1)theta), and
|sin(k theta)|<=k|sin(theta)| follows by telescoping k unit complex
numbers. The second bound follows from |Cheb_(2N+1)(sqrt(lambda))|<=1.

There are six complete copies of Chi_N in (7). For z=T lambda, its
quadratic error is at most

    T^(-1) z (1+A z)^2(1+z)^2 min(1,z^(-6)).                 (10)

Indeed (AM+1)/T<=A and (1+M^(2/3))/T<=1 for M>=2. If z<=1,
the expression following T^(-1) is <=16A^2. If z>=1, it is
<=16A^2/z<=16A^2. Therefore

    Q_(n_N)(h^(N)) <=16 A^2/T <=16 M^(-5/6).                 (11)

Now consider the exact K_n in fact b98bb807d514e80d. We check every
index, not merely the two selected bridges. In the increasing Chi_N,
the first entry is <=4/3, and the ratio of successive entries is <=9.
For the latter write c_j=csc^2(theta_j), where
theta_j=(N-j+1)pi/(2N+1). Consecutive positive angles have ratio <=2,
and concavity of sin on [0,pi/2] gives c_(j+1)/c_j<=4<=9.
The weaker constant 9 is retained in the bounds below. Thus every
ordinary entry satisfies h_j<=9(1+P_j), with P_j the full preceding
mass. This remains true at the beginning of each repeated copy.
Also max c_j=csc^2(pi/(2N+1))<=T/4<M, by sin(t)>=2t/pi.

- A cut in the first L_N has tail mass at least AM. Its single-cut
  term is at most 81/(2AM) <=41 M^(-5/6).
- At the bridge AM+1 the prefix mass is M-1 and the tail mass is
  M-1+b. Its term is A^2/[1+2(M-1+b)]<=A^2/M=M^(-5/6).
- A cut in the second L_N has prefix mass at least (A+1)M and tail
  mass at least b>=M^(2/3). Its term is at most
  1/[2A^2 M^(2/3)] = M^(-5/6)/2.
- At the final bridge b=1+M^(2/3), one plus the prefix mass is
  (A+2)M. Its term is M^(-2/3)/(A+2)^2<=M^(-5/6).
- The global Huber term is <=1/M<=M^(-5/6).

Consequently

    K_(n_N)(h^(N)) <=41 M^(-5/6).                              (12)

Inserted zero steps contribute zero cut terms and change no mass, so
(11)-(12) hold for h^[n] as well. The second-block estimate only needs
the maximum individual step, and hence survives arbitrary permutations
there. The first-block ordering assumption is used explicitly above.

## 6. The universal complex lens also misses this family

Let Lens_n and Gap_h be exactly those in accepted fact dfde2fa326c908bf.
Since n>=N, Lens_n is contained in Lens_N. The Chebyshev ellipse
calculation in that fact gives

    |z||P_N(z)|^2 <= cosh^2(2)/T,       z in Lens_n.

For T|z|<=1, the product formula instead gives

    |P_N(z)| <= exp(s(Chi_N)|z|) <= exp(1/6) <= cosh(2).

The last inequality follows, for example, from exp(1/6)<=6/5 and
cosh(2)>=3. Thus, with C=cosh(2),

    |P_N(z)|^2 <= C^2 min(1,1/(T|z|)).                         (13)

The accepted upper bound on a legal polynomial transcript is
Gap_h(z)<=(2Re z-|z|^2)|Poly_n(z)|^2<=2|z||Poly_n(z)|^2.
Using (13) and the same two ranges as in (10), now with T|z| as the
nonnegative scalar variable, proves

    sup_(z in Lens_n) Gap_(h^[n])(z)
        <=32 cosh^12(2) M^(-5/6).                            (14)

This bounds ONLY the universal-lens channel; it makes no assertion
about the full schedule-dependent legal complex region.

## 7. Comparison with the actual full B_n sequence

No asymptotic profile constant or limit is assumed. First, the verified
upper bound B_n<=1+4n^p, p=log_2(3), yields the explicit estimates

    K_n(h^[n])/U_n^ZJ <=41(1+4n^p)/M^(5/6),
    Q_n(h^[n])/U_n^ZJ <=16(1+4n^p)/M^(5/6),
    [sup_(z in Lens_n) Gap_(h^[n])(z)]/U_n^ZJ
        <=32 cosh^12(2)(1+4n^p)/M^(5/6).                      (15)

Here M>=2N^2, n<=6N+7<=8N, and p<5/3 because 27<32. Every
right-hand side tends to zero. Thus these three established channels
all miss the exact benchmark on the very same family.

For a pointwise lower comparison, set s=1+sqrt(2) and
d_N=floor(log_2 N). In the verified primitive mass recurrence,

    C_j=S_circle(j)+1,
    C_j=max_(k<j) Omega(C_k,C_(j-k-1)),
    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt((u+v)^2+4uv))/2,

one has C_j>=C_(j-1), and the balanced choice gives
C_(2^r-1)>=s^r. The dominant recurrence with its final empty block
gives B_n>=2C_(n-1)-1. Since n-1>=2^(d_N+2)-1,

    B_n>=2s^(d_N+2)-1>=s^(d_N+2).                            (16)

On the other hand N<2^(d_N+1) and M<=5N^2, so

    B_n V(M,A,epsilon)
      >= [s^2/20^(7/12)] [s/2^(7/6)]^d_N
      > (18/25)(16/15)^d_N >1,                               (17)

for d_N>=12. For the elementary constants: s>12/5,
2^(7/6)<9/4 since 2^7<(9/4)^6, and 20^(7/12)<8.
Finally (16/15)^d_N >=1+d_N/15>=9/5 for d_N>=12, so the
last product is at least 162/125>1.

Equations (5), (15), and (17) concern the actual B_n at EVERY integer
n>=24578, not just a dyadic comparison constant. They prove for this
explicit family

    W_n(h^[n]) >= V(M,A,epsilon) > U_n^ZJ,
    max(K_n(h^[n]),Q_n(h^[n]),sup_Lens_n Gap_(h^[n]))
        = o(U_n^ZJ).                                         (18)

The ratio supplied by (17) in fact diverges. This is a concrete gain
from retaining the two-dimensional geometry and completing the free
terminal. It is not a lower bound of this strength for all schedules.

## 8. A scalar comparison with the same retained first block

There is a useful further explanation of the dimensional mechanism.
Keep the first block and all of its scalar jets fixed, including
x_init=1, gradient 1/M, and optimum 0. After the bridge AM+1 the
scalar position is -A. Consider ANY legal scalar continuation whose
gradient is a constant -v throughout the second ordinary block,
including its last query. Convexity gives v>=0. Its last queried
position is x_E=-A+(M-1)v. Smoothness and the optimum force
x_E<=-v if v>0, hence 0<=v<=A/M (the v=0 case has value zero).

Interpolation against the optimum bounds the last queried value by

    f(x_E)<=Av-(M-1/2)v^2 <= A^2/[4(M-1/2)].

After the final step b>=1 the position is x_T=-A+(M-1+b)v.
If x_T<=0, monotonicity on the negative ray gives f(x_T)<=f(x_E).
If x_T>=0, then x_T<=A epsilon. When A epsilon<=1, the retained
initial derivative and convexity imply 0<=f'(x)<=1/M on [0,x_T],
so f(x_T)<=A epsilon/M. Therefore EVERY such scalar continuation has

    2f(x_T)<=max(A^2/(2M-1), 2A epsilon/M).                     (19)

For (7), A epsilon=M^(-1/4)<=1, and (19) is <=2M^(-5/6).
The two-dimensional construction gives >=M^(-7/12), larger by at
least M^(1/4)/2. The second scalar block's values and gradient may be
chosen freely subject to legality; this is more than a comparison with
one specific scalar example. It is still a constant-gradient block
restriction, and does not upper-bound every one-dimensional trajectory
on the full schedule.

## Scope and remaining task

This joint proof supplies an exact arbitrary-block terminal policy, a
four-anchor active-set formula, all old/new comparisons, the actual
boundary gradient, true distance normalization, and a quantitative
family at every large horizon that defeats several baseline channels.
It does not assert that every schedule has an advantageous two-block
partition, that the completed function remains adverse after an
arbitrary further suffix, or that a greedy intermediate completion is
globally optimal. The all-schedule exact-profile comparison remains open.

Targeted Matlas searches returned no external theorem used in the proof.
The exact accepted predecessors above were read. A search hit for an
older lower-bound paper returned HTTP 503 and was not relied on. All
new results remain candidates because the current assignment allocates
no additional verifier requests.

glossary.L_N: Three consecutive copies of Chi_N, with total mass M-1.
glossary.h^[n]: For N=floor((n-2)/6), the schedule h^(N) padded at its beginning with n-(6N+2) zeros.
glossary.Q_n: Worst normalized objective among all convex quadratic functions, equal to the scalar spectral maximum in Section5.
glossary.T: The scalar (2N+1)^2=2M-1 in the polynomial estimates.
glossary.P_N: The terminal polynomial of Chi_N from accepted fact dfde2fa326c908bf.
glossary.d_N: floor(log_2 N), used only in the pointwise lower estimate on the exact B_n.
glossary.C: The scalar cosh(2) in the universal-lens estimate.
glossary.x_E: Last scalar queried point in the comparison of Section8.
glossary.x_T: Scalar point after the final step in Section8.

One has <q,y>=0, <p,y><0, f_old(x_last)=||q||^2/2. At ALL old
queries the value and gradient are retained in the completion below.

## 2. The exact four-anchor maximal interpolant

Set

    a=1-1/M,       z_A=(a,0),       delta_A=a/M,
    z_B=X-q,
    delta_B=(M-1)||q||^2.

For a retained jet (x,g,f), its proximal point z=x-g and height
delta=f-||g||^2/2 give the conjugate quadratic

    ||v||^2/2 + <z,v> - delta.

This is exactly the quadratic H_j in fact 1252b8823bb5a290 after
expansion. In the first block (z,delta) traces the line segment from
(z_A,delta_A) to (0,0). Both endpoints are actual queried samples. In
the second block it traces the segment from (z_B,delta_B) to (y,0),
again with both endpoints queried. Therefore the maximum of ALL retained
quadratics, including the optimum jet, is exactly

    H(v)=||v||^2/2 + max(0,
                        <z_A,v>-delta_A,
                        <y,v>,
                        <y,v>+(M-1)(<q,v>-||q||^2)).             (1)

No constraint is deleted: intermediate quadratics are convex
combinations of these endpoint quadratics. By the accepted fact,

    F(x)=sup_v [<x,v>-H(v)]                                    (2)

is one fixed finite convex 1-smooth function, preserves every old query,
has F(0)=0=min F, and is the pointwise maximal such interpolant.
It is selected before running the complete prescribed schedule.

The actual closest-minimizer distance stays ONE. The initial jet is

    x_init=(1,0),  g_init=p,  F(x_init)=1/M-1/(2M^2).

For any minimizer z of F, the accepted interpolation inequality between
this jet and (z,0,0) gives

    0 >= F(x_init)+<p,z-x_init>+||p||^2/2 = <p,z>.

Hence z has first coordinate <=0 and ||x_init-z||>=1. Origin attains
distance one. This proves the genuine normalization for F, not merely
for the old envelope.

## 3. Closed formula at the genuinely unqueried terminal

Let

    b=1+M epsilon,    0<=epsilon<=1,
    d=(2,-nu)=-Mq,
    e=z_A-y=(A-2+a,nu),
    D=||e||^2=(A-2+a)^2+2A-4.

The actual terminal point is

    x_n=x_last-bq = y+epsilon d.

Define

    tau=a(2epsilon-1/M)_+/D,
    v=epsilon d-tau e.                                       (3)

Here 0<=tau<=2epsilon/D<=1/2 because D>=(A-2)^2>=4.
The elementary products that will be used are

    ||d||^2=2A,   <d,e>=2a,   <y,d>=0,
    <y,e>=-(A-2)(A+a)<0.                                    (4)

We now check ALL four affine terms in (1) at v.

If tau=0, the y-term and zero term both equal zero, and the z_A-term
is a(2epsilon-1/M)<=0. If tau>0, then

    <e,v>=2a epsilon-tau D=a/M,

so the y-term and z_A-term tie. The y-term is nonnegative because
<y,v>=-tau<y,e>>=0. Finally

    <q,v>=-[2A epsilon-2a tau]/M <=0,

since tau<=2epsilon/D and 2A-4/D>0. Consequently the z_B-term is
strictly below the y-term, its difference being
(M-1)(<q,v>-||q||^2)<0. This also handles epsilon=0.

For tau=0, y is an active subgradient of the max-affine part of H.
For tau>0, y+tau e is the convex combination (1-tau)y+tau z_A
of its active slopes. In both cases

    x_n=v+y+tau e

is a subgradient of H at v. Strong convexity of H therefore makes v
the unique maximizer in (2), and it is the ACTUAL terminal gradient.
Substituting (3)-(4) gives the exact normalized value

    V(M,A,epsilon) := 2F(x_n)
       = 2A epsilon^2
         - a^2(2epsilon-1/M)_+^2/D.                         (5)

Every parameter and endpoint is finite, and epsilon=0 is included.
In particular, since a<=1 and D>=4,

    A epsilon^2 <= V(M,A,epsilon) <= 2A epsilon^2.           (6)

The precise relative loss from the upper bound is at most
2/(A D)<=2/[A(A-2)^2], which tends to zero as A grows.
Equation (5), rather than that limit, is used in the comparisons below.

There is a substantial completion effect here. For A>=4 and epsilon<=1,
both <p,x_n> and <q,x_n> are nonpositive. Thus J(x_n)=0 and
f_old(x_n)=0, whereas (5) is positive for epsilon>0. No queried value
has changed: only the behavior away from the retained samples differs.
The original old function's unqueried zero set does not constrain the
maximal interpolant. Its actual closest minimizer remains at distance one.

The upper bound in (6) also has an intrinsic interpretation. Every
interpolant of the last query and optimum has F(y)=0 by the unit-step
descent inequality, because F(y+q)=||q||^2/2. Smoothness then gives
2F(x_n)<=||x_n-y||^2=2A epsilon^2. The exact completion loses only
the displayed finite old-query correction from this upper bound.

For the first bound, put sqrt(lambda)=sin(theta): the numerator of

## 9. Exact optimization of the whole homogeneous second-gradient class

The parallel component need not be fixed at -2/M. There is an explicit
optimal choice, and it applies to TWO UNEQUAL prescribed block masses.
This section includes its own prefix, active-set, and optimization proof.

Let the two ordinary sums be M_0-1 and M_1-1, with M_0>1, M_1>=1.
Let the first bridge be A M_0+1 for ANY A>0, and let the final step be
b>=0. Start from (1,0), use p=(1,0)/M_0 in the first block, and for
0<=kappa<=A put

    q_kappa=(-kappa,sqrt(kappa(A-kappa)))/M_1,
    X=(-A,0),
    y=X-M_1 q_kappa.

Then ||q_kappa||^2=A kappa/M_1^2 and <q_kappa,y>=0. This parameter
covers, up to an orthogonal rotation fixing the first coordinate, EVERY
possible q in any finite dimension that satisfies

    <q,X-M_1 q>=0.

Indeed that equation forces q_1=-M_1||q||^2/A<=0. Setting
kappa=-M_1 q_1 gives the displayed norm and fresh squared component
kappa(A-kappa)/M_1^2, which is nonnegative exactly for kappa in [0,A].
Thus the class being optimized is precisely the homogeneous new-plane
class whose second block ends at proximal value zero, with this first
block fixed. It does not include arbitrary affine intercepts or positive
endpoint levels.

All prefixes are legal for J=max(0,<p,z>,<q_kappa,z>). At an old
first-block proximal point the q-plane is a nonpositive multiple of
the p-plane. At a second-block proximal point X-tq_kappa, 1<=t<=M_1,
the q-plane has value

    A kappa/M_1 * (1-t/M_1)>=0,

while its first coordinate -A+t kappa/M_1 is nonpositive. Hence the
p-plane is <=0. These verify every actual old/new comparison. For
kappa=0 the second block is already at a minimizer and has gradient
zero; no strict positivity is presumed at that endpoint.

Let

    c=1/M_0,  a=1-c,  L=A+2a,
    epsilon=(b-1)/M_1,
    d=(kappa,-sqrt(kappa(A-kappa))),
    z_A=(a,0),  e=z_A-y,
    D=(A-kappa)L+a^2.

For epsilon>=0 the terminal point is y+epsilon d. The complete retained
conjugate maximum is again exactly four terms:

    H_kappa(v)=||v||^2/2+max(0,
                   <z_A,v>-ac,
                   <y,v>,
                   <y,v>+(M_1-1)(<q_kappa,v>-||q_kappa||^2)). (20)

For M_1=1 the last term duplicates the preceding term. The endpoint
data produce (20) directly: first-block proximal heights are <p,z>,
and second-block proximal heights are <q_kappa,z>. All intermediate
quadratics are convex combinations of the two endpoints of their own
block. Accepted fact 1252b8823bb5a290 gives the fixed maximal interpolant
F_kappa=H_kappa^*. The initial-jet inequality <p,z><=0 at every
minimizer proves the actual closest distance is one, for every kappa.

Define clip_[0,1](u)=max(0,min(1,u)), and put

    tau=clip_[0,1](a(kappa epsilon-c)/D),
    v=epsilon d-tau e.                                      (21)

Here D>=a^2>0. The useful identities are

    ||d||^2=A kappa,    <d,e>=a kappa,
    <y,d>=0,           <y,e>=-(A-kappa)(A+a)<=0.              (22)

If tau=0, then kappa epsilon<=c, the y-term and zero term tie,
and the z_A-term is <=0. If 0<tau<1, the y-term and z_A-term tie,
since <e,v>=ac, and the y-term is >=0. If tau=1, then
<e,v>>=ac, so the z_A-term dominates the y-term. It is also >=0:
the inequality a(kappa epsilon-c)>=D implies

    v_1=-(A-kappa)+kappa epsilon-a
        >= (A-kappa)(A/a+1)+c >= c.

For 0<kappa<=A, the fourth term never exceeds the y-term. In the
interior case,

    <q_kappa,v>=-kappa(A epsilon-a tau)/M_1<=0,

because a tau<=a^2 kappa epsilon/D<=A epsilon; the last inequality
uses a^2 kappa<=A D. For tau=0 it is immediate. For tau=1, the
condition above gives kappa epsilon>=D/a+c>=a+c=1, hence
A epsilon>=1>a. At kappa=0 this fourth term simply equals the y-term.

For 0<tau<1, y+tau e is an active convex combination of slopes;
at tau=0 or1 the appropriate endpoint is active. Since
x_n=v+y+tau e, this proves the exact terminal gradient and value for
EVERY kappa and EVERY epsilon>=0. The value is

    V_kappa = min_(0<=t<=1) J_kappa(t),
    J_kappa(t)=A kappa epsilon^2
               -2t a(kappa epsilon-c)
               +t^2[(A-kappa)L+a^2].                        (23)

This also proves that V_kappa is concave in kappa: it is a minimum of
affine functions of kappa. There is no numerical or existence step in
the following optimization.

### Exact global optimizer in kappa

Set

    epsilon_low=L/[A M_0(A+a)],
    epsilon_high=L/A.

When epsilon_low<epsilon<epsilon_high, choose

    kappa_opt=A(A+a)/L + a/[M_0 epsilon(A+a)],
    tau_opt=epsilon A/L.                                    (24)

These inequalities ensure 0<kappa_opt<A and 0<tau_opt<1. This is the

    A epsilon^2-2a epsilon t-L t^2=0.

Consequently (23) bounds every V_kappa by the SAME number

    V_opt=epsilon^2 [A(A+a)/L]^2 + 2epsilon Aac/L.             (25)

Substitution of (24) in the unconstrained minimizer of (23) gives
exactly tau_opt, so this bound is attained. The argument is an explicit
upper certificate on this parameter class, paired with its displayed
realizing direction; it assumes no minimax interchange.

Outside that open epsilon interval, kappa_opt=A is a global optimizer.
Here is a direct proof including cases when the interval is empty.
At kappa=A let

    t_A=clip_[0,1]((A epsilon-c)/a).

If epsilon<=epsilon_low, then t_A<=epsilon A/L. If
epsilon>=epsilon_high, then t_A<=1<=epsilon A/L. In either case the

Thus the endpoint A attains the global maximum, and both transition

For this scalar endpoint write x=A epsilon. Its exact value is

    V_A=x^2,                   0<=x<=c,
        2cx-c^2,               c<=x<=1,
        (x-a)^2+2ac,           x>=1.                          (26)

This follows either from (23) or directly from the three possible

If 0<=b<=1, the final point lies on the segment from y+q_kappa to y.
Every retained interpolant has F(y)=0 and gradient zero there, and has

    (1-b)^2 A kappa/M_1^2.

It is maximized by kappa=A. This handles zero final steps and b=1.

For the remaining degenerate first mass M_0=1, its sole nonzero

In (7) take M_0=M_1=M, A=M^(1/12), epsilon=M^(-1/3). The strict

## 10. The unit-final-step obstruction survives positive levels and offsets

The zero value at b=1 in Section9 is not repaired at the benchmark scale

Let an arbitrary convex 1-smooth f have minimum zero at the origin. Let
the start of its last ordinary block be X, let that block have sum M_1-1,
and suppose its gradient is the same vector q at every actual sample in
that block, including its last query. Append a unit final step. Its last
queried position is x_E=X-(M_1-1)q. Interpolation with the optimum and
the unit-step descent inequality give, respectively,

    f(x_E)<=<q,x_E>-||q||^2/2,
    f(x_E-q)<=f(x_E)-||q||^2/2.

Consequently

    2f(x_E-q) <=2<q,X>-2M_1||q||^2
       = ||X||^2/(2M_1)-2M_1||q-X/(2M_1)||^2
       <= ||X||^2/(2M_1).                                   (28)

This holds in every dimension, with arbitrary positive values, arbitrary
affine intercepts in any realizing envelope, and arbitrary behavior
away from the retained samples. The constant-gradient hypothesis is
the only special restriction on the final ordinary block.

For the first-block geometry of Section9, X=(-A,0), and all retained
first jets ensure the true closest initial distance is one. The single
cut at the preceding checkpoint AM_0+1, on the same schedule ending in
a unit step, already gives exactly

    K_cut=A^2/(2M_1+1).

Equation (28) is only a factor 1+1/(2M_1) larger. Thus this whole class,
even after freeing every second-block level, direction, intercept and
the maximal terminal completion, cannot beat that baseline by a growing
factor when the final step is one. On the modified schedules (7) with
the last step replaced by one, its bound is M^(-5/6)/2=o(1/B_n), using
the same exact benchmark upper estimate as in (15).

This closes only the proposed extension by positive levels INSIDE a
constant-gradient last block. It leaves varying gradients inside that
block, more chronological cells, and the unrestricted worst case open.
It identifies a precise missing mechanism for extending the new
terminal gain to arbitrary schedules.

## Scope and remaining task

This joint proof supplies an exact arbitrary-block terminal policy, a
four-anchor active-set formula, all old/new comparisons, the actual
boundary gradient, true distance normalization, and a quantitative
family at every large horizon that defeats several baseline channels.
It does not assert that every schedule has an advantageous two-block
partition, that the completed function remains adverse after an
arbitrary further suffix, or that a greedy intermediate completion is
globally optimal. The all-schedule exact-profile comparison remains open.

Targeted Matlas searches returned no external theorem used in the proof.
The exact accepted predecessors above were read. A search hit for an
older lower-bound paper returned HTTP 503 and was not relied on. All
new results remain candidates because the current assignment allocates
no additional verifier requests.

claim: Exact saturated-cut intrinsic certificate interface: all cross-block multipliers are forced, the full PSD matrix splits into prefix and tail blocks, and the tail retains the signed credit E_theta=V_tail-theta sum b_i Q_(i,terminal), theta=1-(D/T)^2. evidence:
# Saturated-cut certificates retain a signed terminal-interpolation credit

Status: self-contained candidate, NOT verifier-accepted. No solver or
fact_submit was used. The full initial-distance objective theorem is not
being restricted here: the statement concerns the explicitly specified
intrinsic primitive energy. The only accepted background used is the
necessity of the interpolation inequalities in fact 1252b8823bb5a290.

## 1. Definitions and an exact identity

Work at smoothness one. On a GD trajectory for a list h of sum s and
capacity C=1+s, write g_i=grad f(x_i), f_i=f(x_i), and

  Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <= 0,
  V_h=2 sum_(i<n) h_i(f_i-f_n)
          +sum_(i<n) h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-sC||g_n||^2.

Take two lists a,b of capacities A,D, respectively, and set

  T=A+D+r,  r>0,  rT=AD,
  kappa=(T/D)^2=(A/r)^2,
  theta=1-1/kappa.

In particular 0<r<min(A,D), kappa>1 and 0<theta<1. The joined
schedule is h=(a,1+r,b). Denote its bridge query by L and the tail
queries by j=0,...,m; z=m is the final query. Tail indices in Q always
mean the corresponding original joined indices. Define

  J_b=sum_(j<m) b_j Q_(j,z),
  E_theta(b)=V_b-theta J_b,
  C_cross=sum_(j<m) b_j Q_(j,L)+Q_(z,L)+r Q_(L,z).

The exact identity, including every value term, is

  V_h = V_a + kappa E_theta(b) - (kappa-1) C_cross.       (1)

All coefficients in -C_cross are nonnegative on actual inequalities
-Q. Thus universal nonnegativity of V_a and E_theta(b) is a sufficient
condition for universal nonnegativity of V_h. It is not necessary here
to assume V_b>=0. Whether this genuinely enlarges the allowable tail
class is a separate question.

Here is a direct audit of (1). Put p=g_L, q=g_z, and
H=sum_(j<m)b_j g_j. Then x_tail,0=x_L-(1+r)p and x_z=x_tail,0-H.
For C=C_cross+J_b the value part is

  C_f=2sum_(j<m)b_j f_j+(r-D)f_L+(2-D-r)f_z.

Expand each Q and use
2sum_j b_j<g_j,sum_(i<j)b_i g_i>=||H||^2-sum_j b_j^2||g_j||^2.
The gradient part reduces exactly to

  C_g=sum_(j<m)b_j(1-b_j)||g_j||^2
            +[(D-r)/2-r^2]||p||^2+(D+r)||q||^2/2.

All mixed p,H,q products cancel. The identities

  (kappa-1)(D-r)=2(A+r),
  kappa r^2=A^2,  kappa D^2=T^2

then show V_h=V_a+kappa V_b-(kappa-1)C coefficient by coefficient:
the f_L coefficient is 2(1+r), the f_z coefficient is -2(T-1),
the p-square coefficient is -r(1+r), and the q-square coefficient
is -T(T-1). Substituting kappa theta=kappa-1 proves (1).

## 2. Full intrinsic certificates force the bridge coefficients

For this part assume the entries of a and b are strictly positive;
either list may be empty. Suppose an explicit intrinsic certificate is
given:

  M_h=V_h+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij,
  lambda_ij>=0,

where values cancel and M_h is PSD in the full independent formal
gradient vector. Allowing the optimum index and x_0 initially does not
enlarge this class. Indeed V_h has no x_0-square coefficient, so PSD
forces the x_0 row to vanish. Its cross coefficients are -lambda_i,star,
which forces every lambda_i,star=0. Summing the value-flow equalities
then gives sum_i lambda_star,i=0, so these multipliers also vanish.
This argument relies on the absence of an initial-distance term and
does NOT apply to a full objective certificate.

There are two explicit equality trajectories for V_h. A scalar Huber
trajectory staying on one affine ray has every gradient equal to 1,
all finite Q zero, and V_h=0. A second trajectory uses the derivative

  f'(x)=min(1,max(x,-eta)),  eta=r/D,

starting at A. The prefix gradient is 1, its last query is 1, the
bridge lands at -r, and the tail gradient is -eta until its endpoint
-eta. Every incoming optimum residual is zero. Distance telescoping
gives V_h=A^2-T^2 eta^2=0.

For completeness, if R_i is a prefix query's remaining prefix sum
and R_j is a tail query's remaining tail sum, this second trajectory
has

  Q_(prefix i,tail j)=-(1+eta)eta R_j,
  Q_(tail j,prefix i)=-(1+eta)R_i.                       (2)

Every within-block Q is zero. Since M_h>=0 and all lambda Q<=0,
equality of V_h forces multiplier complementarity and M_h to vanish
on each equality gradient vector. Those vectors span the two block
indicators e_A,e_B, so both indicators lie in the kernel of M_h.

By (2), the only potentially nonzero cross multipliers are

  nu_i=lambda_(prefix i,z),  mu_j=lambda_(tail j,L).

For a prefix index i<L, the corresponding row of M_h e_B is
-D nu_i/2. Thus nu_i=0 for every i<L. Write nu=nu_L.
For a nonterminal tail index j, the corresponding row of M_h e_A
is [r mu_j-nu b_j]/2; at z it is [r mu_z-nu]/2.
Consequently

  mu_j=(nu/r)b_j  (j<m),  mu_z=nu/r.

The sum of the prefix value-flow equations is
sum_j mu_j-nu=2(A+r). Therefore all cross multipliers are fixed:

  lambda_(j,L)=(kappa-1)b_j (j<m),
  lambda_(z,L)=kappa-1,
  lambda_(L,z)=r(kappa-1),                              (3)

and every other cross multiplier is zero. The mixed gradient block
of the full matrix vanishes, not merely its value on equality data.

## 3. Exact cone interface and the sign that cannot be discarded

Let lambda^A,lambda^B be the two within-block multiplier arrays of
the given full certificate. Define a signed tail array by

  lambda_hat_ij=lambda^B_ij/kappa
                 -theta b_i * 1_(i<m,j=z).             (4)

Combining (1) with (3) yields the full block-diagonal identity

  M_h = M_a + kappa M_b,
  M_a=V_a+sum lambda^A_ij Q_ij,
  M_b=V_b+sum lambda_hat_ij Q_ij.                       (5)

Each summand has its own value cancellation, since its values are in
a disjoint block. Full PSD is equivalent to PSD of both summands.
The prefix multipliers are nonnegative. The exact tail constraints are

  lambda_hat_ij>=0 except possibly i<m,j=z,
  lambda_hat_(i,z)>=-theta b_i.                        (6)

Conversely, any prefix intrinsic certificate and any PSD tail identity
with the value cancellation and bounds (6) give a nonnegative full
certificate by (3),(4). Equivalently, the tail has an ordinary
nonnegative certificate for E_theta(b), not necessarily for V_b.

Thus direct restriction to an ordinary primitive tail certificate would
require the stronger bounds

  lambda^B_(i,z)>=(kappa-1)b_i.                        (7)

They are not implied for each full certificate. The next exact example
proves this, including full nonnegativity and PSD.

## 4. Exact full certificate violating the proposed coefficient floor

Use the empty prefix A=1, tail b=(1,1) of capacity D=3, and

  r=sqrt(7)-2, T=sqrt(7)+2, kappa=(11+4sqrt(7))/9.

The full schedule is h=(sqrt(7)-1,1,1). Use original indices 0,1,2,3,
where 0 is the bridge query and 1,2,3 are the tail queries. Set

  lambda_10=lambda_20=lambda_30=kappa-1,
  lambda_03=r(kappa-1),
  lambda_12=5kappa/2, lambda_21=17kappa/4,
  lambda_23=37kappa/4-1, lambda_32=12kappa,
  lambda_13=3kappa/4-1,

with every unlisted multiplier zero. All are nonnegative, since
kappa>4/3. Direct substitution, or (1) and the audited tail identity
below, gives

  V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij
   =kappa { ||(g_1-g_2)-(g_2-g_3)/8||^2
                         +(255/64)||g_2-g_3||^2 } >=0. (8)

For the tail alone, write u=g_0-g_1 and v=g_1-g_2 using local indices.
Its signed multiplier list is

  lambda_hat_01=5/2, lambda_hat_10=17/4,
  lambda_hat_12=33/4, lambda_hat_21=12,
  lambda_hat_02=-1/4, lambda_hat_20=0.

The value coefficients cancel, and expansion gives

  V_(1,1)+sum lambda_hat_ij Q_ij
      =||u||^2-<u,v>/4+4||v||^2
      =||u-v/8||^2+(255/64)||v||^2.

Nevertheless lambda_13=(kappa-1)-kappa/4 is strictly below the
proposed floor kappa-1. The restricted terminal coefficient is -1/4.
This refutes the inference of (7) from full nonnegativity and PSD.

There IS another ordinary primitive certificate for this tail:
lambda_01=2,lambda_10=4,lambda_12=8,lambda_21=12, all other
multipliers zero, gives ||u||^2+4||v||^2. Accordingly this example
does not disprove existence of a suitable re-selection, arbitrary-tail
heredity, or the original asymptotic minimax problem. It identifies
the exact missing sign assertion rather than replacing it with PSD.

## 5. A particular nonprimitive tail cannot exploit this credit

The previously considered b=(17/10,2,6/5) fails even E_theta for
every 0<=theta<=1. Here is a self-contained witness.
Put m=7/34, ell=21/85. Define the continuous derivative

  f'(x)=x                  for x<=m,
         m                 for m<=x<=m+ell,
         x-ell             for x>=m+ell,

and integrate with f(0)=0. Its derivative is nondecreasing and
1-Lipschitz, so f is convex differentiable 1-smooth with minimizer 0.
Starting at x_0=106/85 gives

  (x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3)=(106/85,-77/170,77/170,7/34),
  (g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3)=(1,-77/170,7/34,7/34).

The endpoint is core: x_3=g_3=m, f_3=m^2/2. Define
I_i=<g_i,x_i>-f_i-||g_i||^2/2. Direct scalar evaluation gives

  I_0=ell(1-m)=567/2890, I_1=I_2=I_3=0,
  sum_(i<3)b_i I_i=567/1700,
  V_b=-13581/23120.

At a core endpoint, expansion gives Q_(i,3)=-I_i. Thus

  E_theta(b)=-13581/23120+theta*567/1700
           <= -29349/115600 <0.                       (9)

The value of V_b can also be checked without integrating every term:
distance telescoping gives
V_b=x_0^2-D^2g_3^2-2sum b_i I_i, with D=59/10.
This proves (9) exactly.

Consequently this specific tail cannot acquire a valid E_theta
certificate at any saturated join parameter. A rank-one coefficient
matching attempt on this same fixed tail also failed, but (9) is the
stronger actual-function obstruction. Neither statement excludes other
nonprimitive tails. No numerical schedule screen was reopened.

evidence:
# A quantitative exact terminal completion on nonperiodic schedules

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof candidate. No verifier or numerical-solver
request. This is an explicit family at every sufficiently large horizon,
not the unrestricted all-schedule comparison. Every new calculation used
below is included here; no unverified finding is a premise.

Verified predecessors used:

- `1252b8823bb5a290`: the complete smooth-convex interpolation inequality
  and the pointwise maximal completion at a genuinely unqueried terminal.
- `dfde2fa326c908bf`: the exact Chebyshev steps, their sum and polynomial,
  and the universal complex-lens construction and polynomial estimate.
- `b98bb807d514e80d`: the single-cut functional K_n, the exact benchmark
  recursions, and B_n <= 1+4 n^p for p=log_2(3).

We use smoothness one and initial distance one throughout. Thus the
normalized objective is 2f(x_n). General smoothness follows by scaling.

## 1. An arbitrary-block prefix with a completely specified fresh direction

Let M>=2 and A>=4. Prescribe ANY two nonnegative ordinary lists of sum
M-1 each, separated by the checkpoint AM+1. A final step b will be added
after the second list. Work in R^2 and put

    nu=sqrt(2A-4),
    p=(1,0)/M,                  q=(-2,nu)/M,
    J(z)=max(0,<p,z>,<q,z>),
    f_old=env_1 J,              x_init=(1,0).

The squared boundary gradient is exactly ||q||^2=2A/M^2. The fresh
component of q has squared norm (2A-4)/M^2; it is not dropped from the
state or normalization.

In the first block every gradient is p. To check this, a query after
ordinary partial mass u has proposed proximal point

    z=(1-(u+1)/M,0),       0<=u<=M-1.

Here <p,z>>=0 and <q,z>=-2<p,z>. Thus p is an active subgradient of J.
At the checkpoint query the position is p and its proximal point is 0.
The checkpoint AM+1 sends the trajectory to X=(-A,0).

In the second block every gradient is q. Write t=u+1 in [1,M]. Its
proposed proximal point is X-tq. The current height is

    <q,X-tq>=(2A/M)(1-t/M)>=0.

Its excess over the p-plane is

    <q-p,X-tq>=3A/M-(2A+2)t/M^2 >= (A-2)/M >0.

This checks both other planes at every actual query, even if an
individual ordinary step is very large. The comparisons are affine in
t, and the displayed bounds hold on the whole interval. The old q-plane
was already checked at every first-block query, so both cross directions
and every queried sample belong to the same fixed J.

The envelope justification is elementary: if g is an active-plane
subgradient at z and x=z+g, its subgradient inequality makes z the unique
minimizer of J(w)+||x-w||^2/2. Adding the inequalities for two such
proximal pairs proves

    ||g(x)-g(x')||^2 <= <g(x)-g(x'),x-x'>.

The minimizing inequalities identify g as the derivative of the convex
envelope, which is consequently 1-smooth. All claimed GD updates and
sample values follow from this fixed envelope.

At the last query, just before the final step b, the proximal point and
position are respectively

    y=X-Mq=(2-A,-nu),         x_last=y+q.

One has <q,y>=0, <p,y><0, f_old(x_last)=||q||^2/2. At ALL old
queries the value and gradient are retained in the completion below.

## 2. The exact four-anchor maximal interpolant

Set

    a=1-1/M,       z_A=(a,0),       delta_A=a/M,
    z_B=X-q,
    delta_B=(M-1)||q||^2.

For a retained jet (x,g,f), its proximal point z=x-g and height
delta=f-||g||^2/2 give the conjugate quadratic

    ||v||^2/2 + <z,v> - delta.

This is exactly the quadratic H_j in fact 1252b8823bb5a290 after
expansion. In the first block (z,delta) traces the line segment from
(z_A,delta_A) to (0,0). Both endpoints are actual queried samples. In
the second block it traces the segment from (z_B,delta_B) to (y,0),
again with both endpoints queried. Therefore the maximum of ALL retained
quadratics, including the optimum jet, is exactly

    H(v)=||v||^2/2 + max(0,
                        <z_A,v>-delta_A,
                        <y,v>,
                        <y,v>+(M-1)(<q,v>-||q||^2)).             (1)

No constraint is deleted: intermediate quadratics are convex
combinations of these endpoint quadratics. By the accepted fact,

    F(x)=sup_v [<x,v>-H(v)]                                    (2)

is one fixed finite convex 1-smooth function, preserves every old query,
has F(0)=0=min F, and is the pointwise maximal such interpolant.
It is selected before running the complete prescribed schedule.

The actual closest-minimizer distance stays ONE. The initial jet is

    x_init=(1,0),  g_init=p,  F(x_init)=1/M-1/(2M^2).

For any minimizer z of F, the accepted interpolation inequality between
this jet and (z,0,0) gives

    0 >= F(x_init)+<p,z-x_init>+||p||^2/2 = <p,z>.

Hence z has first coordinate <=0 and ||x_init-z||>=1. Origin attains
distance one. This proves the genuine normalization for F, not merely
for the old envelope.

## 3. Closed formula at the genuinely unqueried terminal

Let

    b=1+M epsilon,    0<=epsilon<=1,
    d=(2,-nu)=-Mq,
    e=z_A-y=(A-2+a,nu),
    D=||e||^2=(A-2+a)^2+2A-4.

The actual terminal point is

    x_n=x_last-bq = y+epsilon d.

Define

    tau=a(2epsilon-1/M)_+/D,
    v=epsilon d-tau e.                                       (3)

Here 0<=tau<=2epsilon/D<=1/2 because D>=(A-2)^2>=4.
The elementary products that will be used are

    ||d||^2=2A,   <d,e>=2a,   <y,d>=0,
    <y,e>=-(A-2)(A+a)<0.                                    (4)

We now check ALL four affine terms in (1) at v.

If tau=0, the y-term and zero term both equal zero, and the z_A-term
is a(2epsilon-1/M)<=0. If tau>0, then

    <e,v>=2a epsilon-tau D=a/M,

so the y-term and z_A-term tie. The y-term is nonnegative because
<y,v>=-tau<y,e>>=0. Finally

    <q,v>=-[2A epsilon-2a tau]/M <=0,

since tau<=2epsilon/D and 2A-4/D>0. Consequently the z_B-term is
strictly below the y-term, its difference being
(M-1)(<q,v>-||q||^2)<0. This also handles epsilon=0.

For tau=0, y is an active subgradient of the max-affine part of H.
For tau>0, y+tau e is the convex combination (1-tau)y+tau z_A
of its active slopes. In both cases

    x_n=v+y+tau e

is a subgradient of H at v. Strong convexity of H therefore makes v
the unique maximizer in (2), and it is the ACTUAL terminal gradient.
Substituting (3)-(4) gives the exact normalized value

    V(M,A,epsilon) := 2F(x_n)
       = 2A epsilon^2
         - a^2(2epsilon-1/M)_+^2/D.                         (5)

Every parameter and endpoint is finite, and epsilon=0 is included.
In particular, since a<=1 and D>=4,

    A epsilon^2 <= V(M,A,epsilon) <= 2A epsilon^2.           (6)

The precise relative loss from the upper bound is at most
2/(A D)<=2/[A(A-2)^2], which tends to zero as A grows.
Equation (5), rather than that limit, is used in the comparisons below.

There is a substantial completion effect here. For A>=4 and epsilon<=1,
both <p,x_n> and <q,x_n> are nonpositive. Thus J(x_n)=0 and
f_old(x_n)=0, whereas (5) is positive for epsilon>0. No queried value
has changed: only the behavior away from the retained samples differs.
The original old function's unqueried zero set does not constrain the
maximal interpolant. Its actual closest minimizer remains at distance one.

The upper bound in (6) also has an intrinsic interpretation. Every
interpolant of the last query and optimum has F(y)=0 by the unit-step
descent inequality, because F(y+q)=||q||^2/2. Smoothness then gives
2F(x_n)<=||x_n-y||^2=2A epsilon^2. The exact completion loses only
the displayed finite old-query correction from this upper bound.

## 4. A fixed horizon-dependent choice

For each integer N>=4096 let Chi_N be the increasing list

    c_j=sec^2((2j-1)pi/[2(2N+1)]),       1<=j<=N.

Write L_N for THREE successive copies of this list, and define

    M=2N(N+1)+1,       A=M^(1/12),       epsilon=M^(-1/3),

## 5. Every quadratic and every specified single-cut Huber test is smaller

Let Q_n(h) denote the maximum normalized terminal error of all convex

Set T=(2N+1)^2=2M-1, and let P_N be the polynomial of Chi_N. The
verified Chebyshev identity implies

For the first bound, put sqrt(lambda)=sin(theta): the numerator of
P_N is, up to sign, sin((2N+1)theta), and

Now consider the exact K_n in fact b98bb807d514e80d. We check every

- A cut in the first L_N has tail mass at least AM. Its single-cut
