## 9. Exact optimization of the whole homogeneous second-gradient class

The parallel component need not be fixed at -2/M. There is an explicit
optimal choice, and it applies to TWO UNEQUAL prescribed block masses.
This section includes its own prefix, active-set, and optimization proof.

Let the two ordinary sums be M_0-1 and M_1-1, with M_0>1, M_1>=1.
Let the first bridge be A M_0+1 for ANY A>0, and let the final step be
b>=0. Start from (1,0), use p=(1,0)/M_0 in the first block, and for
0<=kappa<=A put

    q_kappa=(-kappa,sqrt(kappa(A-kappa)))/M_1,
    X=(-A,0),
    y=X-M_1 q_kappa.

Then ||q_kappa||^2=A kappa/M_1^2 and <q_kappa,y>=0. This parameter
covers, up to an orthogonal rotation fixing the first coordinate, EVERY
possible q in any finite dimension that satisfies

    <q,X-M_1 q>=0.

Indeed that equation forces q_1=-M_1||q||^2/A<=0. Setting
kappa=-M_1 q_1 gives the displayed norm and fresh squared component
kappa(A-kappa)/M_1^2, which is nonnegative exactly for kappa in [0,A].
Thus the class being optimized is precisely the homogeneous new-plane
class whose second block ends at proximal value zero, with this first
block fixed. It does not include arbitrary affine intercepts or positive
endpoint levels.

All prefixes are legal for J=max(0,<p,z>,<q_kappa,z>). At an old
first-block proximal point the q-plane is a nonpositive multiple of
the p-plane. At a second-block proximal point X-tq_kappa, 1<=t<=M_1,
the q-plane has value

    A kappa/M_1 * (1-t/M_1)>=0,

while its first coordinate -A+t kappa/M_1 is nonpositive. Hence the
p-plane is <=0. These verify every actual old/new comparison. For
kappa=0 the second block is already at a minimizer and has gradient
zero; no strict positivity is presumed at that endpoint.

Let

    c=1/M_0,  a=1-c,  L=A+2a,
    epsilon=(b-1)/M_1,
    d=(kappa,-sqrt(kappa(A-kappa))),
    z_A=(a,0),  e=z_A-y,
    D=(A-kappa)L+a^2.

For epsilon>=0 the terminal point is y+epsilon d. The complete retained
conjugate maximum is again exactly four terms:

    H_kappa(v)=||v||^2/2+max(0,
                   <z_A,v>-ac,
                   <y,v>,
                   <y,v>+(M_1-1)(<q_kappa,v>-||q_kappa||^2)). (20)

For M_1=1 the last term duplicates the preceding term. The endpoint
data produce (20) directly: first-block proximal heights are <p,z>,
and second-block proximal heights are <q_kappa,z>. All intermediate
quadratics are convex combinations of the two endpoints of their own
block. Accepted fact 1252b8823bb5a290 gives the fixed maximal interpolant
F_kappa=H_kappa^*. The initial-jet inequality <p,z><=0 at every
minimizer proves the actual closest distance is one, for every kappa.

Define clip_[0,1](u)=max(0,min(1,u)), and put

    tau=clip_[0,1](a(kappa epsilon-c)/D),
    v=epsilon d-tau e.                                      (21)

Here D>=a^2>0. The useful identities are

    ||d||^2=A kappa,    <d,e>=a kappa,
    <y,d>=0,           <y,e>=-(A-kappa)(A+a)<=0.              (22)

If tau=0, then kappa epsilon<=c, the y-term and zero term tie,
and the z_A-term is <=0. If 0<tau<1, the y-term and z_A-term tie,
since <e,v>=ac, and the y-term is >=0. If tau=1, then
<e,v>>=ac, so the z_A-term dominates the y-term. It is also >=0:
the inequality a(kappa epsilon-c)>=D implies

    v_1=-(A-kappa)+kappa epsilon-a
        >= (A-kappa)(A/a+1)+c >= c.

For 0<kappa<=A, the fourth term never exceeds the y-term. In the
interior case,

    <q_kappa,v>=-kappa(A epsilon-a tau)/M_1<=0,

because a tau<=a^2 kappa epsilon/D<=A epsilon; the last inequality
uses a^2 kappa<=A D. For tau=0 it is immediate. For tau=1, the
condition above gives kappa epsilon>=D/a+c>=a+c=1, hence
A epsilon>=1>a. At kappa=0 this fourth term simply equals the y-term.

For 0<tau<1, y+tau e is an active convex combination of slopes;
at tau=0 or1 the appropriate endpoint is active. Since
x_n=v+y+tau e, this proves the exact terminal gradient and value for
EVERY kappa and EVERY epsilon>=0. The value is

    V_kappa = min_(0<=t<=1) J_kappa(t),
    J_kappa(t)=A kappa epsilon^2
               -2t a(kappa epsilon-c)
               +t^2[(A-kappa)L+a^2].                        (23)

This also proves that V_kappa is concave in kappa: it is a minimum of
affine functions of kappa. There is no numerical or existence step in
the following optimization.

### Exact global optimizer in kappa

Set

    epsilon_low=L/[A M_0(A+a)],
    epsilon_high=L/A.

When epsilon_low<epsilon<epsilon_high, choose

    kappa_opt=A(A+a)/L + a/[M_0 epsilon(A+a)],
    tau_opt=epsilon A/L.                                    (24)

These inequalities ensure 0<kappa_opt<A and 0<tau_opt<1. This is the
global optimizer over the ENTIRE kappa interval. To prove it, fix
t=tau_opt in (23). The coefficient of kappa is

    A epsilon^2-2a epsilon t-L t^2=0.

Consequently (23) bounds every V_kappa by the SAME number

    V_opt=epsilon^2 [A(A+a)/L]^2 + 2epsilon Aac/L.             (25)

Substitution of (24) in the unconstrained minimizer of (23) gives
exactly tau_opt, so this bound is attained. The argument is an explicit
upper certificate on this parameter class, paired with its displayed
realizing direction; it assumes no minimax interchange.

Outside that open epsilon interval, kappa_opt=A is a global optimizer.
Here is a direct proof including cases when the interval is empty.
At kappa=A let

    t_A=clip_[0,1]((A epsilon-c)/a).

If epsilon<=epsilon_low, then t_A<=epsilon A/L. If
epsilon>=epsilon_high, then t_A<=1<=epsilon A/L. In either case the
coefficient A epsilon^2-2a epsilon t_A-L t_A^2 of kappa in
J_kappa(t_A) is nonnegative. For 0<=kappa<=A it follows that

    V_kappa<=J_kappa(t_A)<=J_A(t_A)=V_A.

Thus the endpoint A attains the global maximum, and both transition
equalities cause no loss. If epsilon_low>=epsilon_high, these two
outside ranges cover every epsilon>=0 and no interior case exists.

For this scalar endpoint write x=A epsilon. Its exact value is

    V_A=x^2,                   0<=x<=c,
        2cx-c^2,               c<=x<=1,
        (x-a)^2+2ac,           x>=1.                          (26)

This follows either from (23) or directly from the three possible
clipped values of t_A. Formulas (24)-(26) are a complete constructive
solution for every finite b>=1, unequal M_0,M_1, and A>0.

If 0<=b<=1, the final point lies on the segment from y+q_kappa to y.
Every retained interpolant has F(y)=0 and gradient zero there, and has
gradient q_kappa and value ||q_kappa||^2/2 at y+q_kappa. The unit

at y+t q_kappa for 0<=t<=1: the distances to gradients 0 and q_kappa
are at most t||q_kappa|| and (1-t)||q_kappa||, whose sum is their
mutual distance. Equality forces the collinear point. Integrating
gives the exact final value

    (1-b)^2 A kappa/M_1^2.

It is maximized by kappa=A. This handles zero final steps and b=1.

For the remaining degenerate first mass M_0=1, its sole nonzero
initial jet has gradient (1,0) and proximal point zero. Taking kappa=A
makes y=0 and reduces the maximal terminal function on the positive
axis to x^2/2, because every negative-side retained conjugate affine

For any kappa the forced minimizer y and smoothness bound give the
upper bound A kappa(b-1)^2/M_1^2, proving optimality. The b<=1
segment proof gives the same formula. Thus M_0=1 needs no division

### Quantitative improvement on the same full-horizon family

In (7) take M_0=M_1=M, A=M^(1/12), epsilon=M^(-1/3). The strict
interior regime applies: epsilon<1<epsilon_high, and

    epsilon_low <= (A+2)/(A^2 M) <= 2/(AM) < epsilon

for A>=4 and M>=4^12. Hence (24) is an explicit legal direction on

## 10. The unit-final-step obstruction survives positive levels and offsets

The zero value at b=1 in Section9 is not repaired at the benchmark scale
merely by allowing a positive second-block proximal level. A bound for
the ENTIRE constant-second-gradient class is available without choosing
an envelope representation.

Let an arbitrary convex 1-smooth f have minimum zero at the origin. Let
the start of its last ordinary block be X, let that block have sum M_1-1,
and suppose its gradient is the same vector q at every actual sample in
that block, including its last query. Append a unit final step. Its last
queried position is x_E=X-(M_1-1)q. Interpolation with the optimum and
the unit-step descent inequality give, respectively,

    f(x_E)<=<q,x_E>-||q||^2/2,
    f(x_E-q)<=f(x_E)-||q||^2/2.

Consequently

    2f(x_E-q) <=2<q,X>-2M_1||q||^2
       = ||X||^2/(2M_1)-2M_1||q-X/(2M_1)||^2
       <= ||X||^2/(2M_1).                                   (28)

This holds in every dimension, with arbitrary positive values, arbitrary
affine intercepts in any realizing envelope, and arbitrary behavior
away from the retained samples. The constant-gradient hypothesis is
the only special restriction on the final ordinary block.

For the first-block geometry of Section9, X=(-A,0), and all retained
first jets ensure the true closest initial distance is one. The single
cut at the preceding checkpoint AM_0+1, on the same schedule ending in
a unit step, already gives exactly

    K_cut=A^2/(2M_1+1).

Equation (28) is only a factor 1+1/(2M_1) larger. Thus this whole class,
even after freeing every second-block level, direction, intercept and
the maximal terminal completion, cannot beat that baseline by a growing
factor when the final step is one. On the modified schedules (7) with
the last step replaced by one, its bound is M^(-5/6)/2=o(1/B_n), using
the same exact benchmark upper estimate as in (15).

This closes only the proposed extension by positive levels INSIDE a
constant-gradient last block. It leaves varying gradients inside that
block, more chronological cells, and the unrestricted worst case open.
It identifies a precise missing mechanism for extending the new
terminal gain to arbitrary schedules.

## 11. A new universally valid terminal two-checkpoint functional

There is a simple schedule-level consequence, without any parameter
feasibility assumption. In Section9, for M_0>1, fix the direction

    kappa_0=A(A+a)/(A+2a),

independently of the final step. For every epsilon>=0, (23) and ac>=0
give

    V_(kappa_0)
       >= min_(t in R) [A kappa_0 epsilon^2
                        -2t a kappa_0 epsilon+t^2 D_0],
    D_0=a(A+a).

Completing this scalar square yields

    V_(kappa_0) >= kappa_0^2 epsilon^2.                       (29)

Specifically, A kappa_0-a^2 kappa_0^2/D_0=kappa_0^2. The relaxation
to real t and omission of the nonnegative term go in the lower-bound
direction. M_0=1 has the same conclusion with kappa_0=A by its explicit
scalar construction in Section9.

Now let h be ANY finite nonnegative schedule of length n>=2. For an
index j<n-1 with h_j>1 set

    P_j=sum_(t<j) h_t,
    S_j=sum_(j<t<n-1) h_t,
    gamma_j=(h_j-1+P_j)/(h_j-1+2P_j),
    D_j^two=gamma_j^2 *
       [(h_j-1)(h_(n-1)-1)_+/((1+P_j)(1+S_j))]^2.            (30)

Define D_n^two(h) as the maximum of these terms, or zero if there is
no such index (also set it to zero for n<2). Every denominator for an
included j is positive; no 0/0 convention is hidden.

For h_(n-1)>1 apply the actual two-block construction with
M_0=1+P_j, M_1=1+S_j, A=(h_j-1)/M_0 and
epsilon=(h_(n-1)-1)/M_1. All intervening ordinary entries are used
exactly in their prescribed order. Formula (29), with the genuine
normalization one, becomes (30). If h_(n-1)<=1 the displayed term is
zero and the bound holds directly. Thus

    W_n(h) >= max(K_n(h),D_n^two(h))                           (31)

for every nonnegative schedule. The finite maximization over j is part
of adversary selection; it changes no function during a trajectory.
Since 1/2<=gamma_j<=1, a weaker bound replaces gamma_j^2 by 1/4.
This is a new chronological product term, not a putative equality for W.

For the schedules (7), select the large bridge between the two L_N
blocks. Formula (30) gives

    D_n^two(h^[n]) >= (25/36) M^(-1/2),                       (32)

using A>=4 and gamma_j=(A+a)/(A+2a)>=5/6. Thus the improvement over
the previously available K, quadratic, and universal-lens channels is
already visible in an explicit universally valid scalar functional of
the schedule. No optimization oracle is needed to evaluate (30).

## 12. A counterexample to uniform comparison by the enlarged functional

The new functional (31) STILL does not solve the target. This can be
tested constructively without making any claim about small true W.

Keep N,M,A from (7). Let L_N^up be the three increasing copies of
Chi_N and L_N^down the three decreasing copies. Define

    h_bad^(N)=(L_N^up, AM+1, L_N^down, 1).                    (33)

Its length is still 6N+2; the same beginning-zero padding covers every
large integer horizon. All of its D_j^two terms are zero because its
last step is one. Quadratic polynomials are independent of the order
inside each ordinary block. The bound (10) still applies, with the
smaller final factor 1+lambda instead of 1+b lambda; the same is true
of (13)-(14). Thus the quadratic and universal-lens channels are again
O(M^(-5/6)).

Here every single-cut term is small as well. The first increasing block
has the same bound 81/(2AM) as before. At the bridge the exact term is
A^2/(2M+1). For a cut in the DECREASING block, denote by T_j its full
tail mass. Within a decreasing copy, each entry is at most four times
its successor, by the adjacent-ratio proof in Section5. A last entry
in a copy is <=4/3; it is either followed by another copy or by the
unit final step. Hence every entry in the second block obeys

    h_j <=4(1+T_j),       h_j<=M.

The full prefix mass there is at least (A+1)M. Its single-cut term is
therefore at most

    h_j^2/[A^2 M^2(1+2T_j)] <=4/(A^2 M).

The final unit-step cut contributes zero, and the global Huber term
is <=1/M. Consequently K_n(h_bad^[n])<=41M^(-5/6), and the same
exact-B_n estimate (15) proves

    max(K_n(h_bad^[n]),D_n^two(h_bad^[n]),Q_n(h_bad^[n]),
        sup_(z in Lens_n) Gap_(h_bad^[n])(z)) / U_n^ZJ ->0.    (34)

This is an explicit refutation of the proposed UNIFORM comparison by
that combined lower functional. It is not a counterexample to the
unrestricted target and not an upper bound on W_n(h_bad^[n]). The
unit-tail cap (28) additionally shows that allowing arbitrary positive
levels in one constant-gradient second block cannot repair this
failure. A repair must use internal gradient changes, more cells, or a
different source of retained terminal value.

## Scope and remaining task

This joint proof supplies an exact arbitrary-block terminal policy, a
four-anchor active-set formula, all old/new comparisons, the actual
boundary gradient, true distance normalization, and a quantitative
family at every large horizon that defeats several baseline channels.
It does not assert that every schedule has an advantageous two-block
partition, that the completed function remains adverse after an
arbitrary further suffix, or that a greedy intermediate completion is
globally optimal. The all-schedule exact-profile comparison remains open.

Targeted Matlas searches returned no external theorem used in the proof.
The exact accepted predecessors above were read. A search hit for an
older lower-bound paper returned HTTP 503 and was not relied on. All
new results remain candidates because the current assignment allocates
no additional verifier requests.

evidence:
# Nonresonant cores: a uniform attraction envelope

Status: complete candidate, NOT verifier-accepted. This was completed before
reading the new projection assignment at 15:06 UTC. It is preserved rather
than pursued further. No new verification is allocated. All new ingredients
are proved here; C23--C25 are not premises.

## Statement and exact class

Set c_sc=13/5, a_sc=c_sc^(-17), bsc_j=a_sc c_sc^j,
Hsc_0=(), Hsc_(j+1)=(Hsc_j,bsc_j,Hsc_j), and Nsc_m=2^m-1.
Let ssc_j=sum Hsc_j=a_sc(c_sc^j-2^j)/(c_sc-2).

Choose p_grow in[1/2,2/3], beta_grow=1-p_grow,
K_grow=(p_grow/beta_grow)^(p_grow), and
1<=kappa_ray<=13/(8 K_grow). Choose ANY mu_core in(0,1] and any
R_core>0. No reciprocal-checkpoint or other resonance condition is imposed.
For each sign sigma choose a locally absolutely continuous radial function
G_sigma such that

    G_sigma(R)=R                         for 0<=R<=1,
    0<=R G_sigma'(R)<=p_grow G_sigma(R)   almost everywhere for R>1,
    1/kappa_ray<=G_+(R)/G_-(R)<=kappa_ray for R>=1.

Define one fixed function by

    g(sigma R_core R)=sigma mu_core R_core G_sigma(R),
    f(x)=integral_0^x g(t)dt.

For every horizon m and every nonzero initial point, the actual GD run on
Hsc_m satisfies

    2f(x_(Nsc_m))/x_0^2 <= (c_sc/a_sc)c_sc^(-m).       (1)

The bound is uniform over all of these parameters and functions, which may
depend on m. Arbitrarily many nonperiodic knots and unbounded radial secant
variation are allowed. The class is NOT all scalar smooth convex functions.

The new ingredient is an attraction inequality for a growing interval. In
normalized coordinates write b_j=mu_core bsc_j, S_j=mu_core ssc_j,
eta=13/8, rho_core=1/8, k_env=1/8, and A_env=13/40. Let I be the first
level with t=b_I>1 and put J=I+1. For j>=J and 0<=q<=rho_core, every
initial point of radius at most q b_j obeys

    |T_j(x)| <= min(A_env q, k_env rho_core),          (2)

where T_j is the actual normalized GD map for the whole word Hsc_j.
Thus this whole interval ends inside the quadratic core. This statement
handles partial-block entry and subsequent exit; it does not presume that
first entry alone is permanent capture.

## Legality and complete areas

Integrating the elasticity bound gives 1<=G_sigma(R)<=R^(p_grow)<=R
for R>=1 and 0<=G_sigma'(R)<=p_grow R^(p_grow-1)<=1 there.
Together with the core formula, each ray is monotone and 1-Lipschitz.
Across zero, G_+(R)+G_-(T)<=R+T proves the same Lipschitz property.
Consequently g is monotone and mu_core-Lipschitz, and f is convex,
differentiable and 1-smooth with its unique minimizer at zero.

The complete normalized function values are

    F(sigma R)=R^2/2                         for R<=1,
    F(sigma R)=1/2+integral_1^R G_sigma(u)du  for R>=1,
    f(x)=mu_core R_core^2 F(x/R_core).

No plateau or previously traversed area is omitted.

## An absolute clock bound valid even at small crossing steps

In this section abbreviate p=p_grow, beta=beta_grow, K=K_grow.
For one ray define Clock(R)=integral_1^R du/G(u). It equals log R
on the core. Set q_R=R/G(R). Outside the core,

    q_R'>=beta/G(R),   Clock(R)<=(q_R-1)/beta.          (3)

For EVERY h>1 and every overshoot z=hG(r)-r>0, claim

    Clock(z)<=K h-1/beta.                             (4)

When z<=1, use the global bound G(r)<=r^p, valid also for r<=1.
Maximizing h r^p-r over r>0 gives

    z <= beta p^(p/beta) h^(1/beta)
       = (beta K h)^(1/beta).

Thus log z <= log(beta K h)/beta <= K h-1/beta, proving (4).
This logarithmic case removes the earlier restriction h>=2.

If z>=1 and r<=1, then h>=2 and Clock(z)<=z-1<=h-2.
The inequality h-2<=K h-1/beta follows from
K>=1/(2beta), which is equivalent to
p^p beta^beta>=1/2. This last expression equals 1/2 at p=1/2,
and its logarithm has derivative log(p/beta)>=0 thereafter.
If r,z>=1 and z>=r, monotonicity and (3) give

    Clock(z)<=h+(1/beta-2)q_R-1/beta
             <=h/(2beta)-1/beta<=K h-1/beta,

using q_R<=h/2. If 1<=z<=r, the growth assumption gives
G(z)>=G(r)(z/r)^p, and therefore

    z/G(z)<=q_R^p(h-q_R)^beta<=p^p beta^beta h.

The maximum occurs at q_R=p h, as differentiating the logarithm verifies.
Equation (3) again proves (4).

Write A=K h-1/beta. On a crossing to the other ray, if A>=0 then
the target clock is at most kappa_ray A: for z>=1 this follows by
integrating the ray comparison, and for z<1 the target clock is negative.
If A<0, (4) forces z<1, where BOTH ray clocks equal log z, so the
target clock is at most A, with no multiplicative loss. Finally every
noncrossing nonzero step decreases its own clock by at least h, because
the integral of 1/G over its inward displacement is at least h.

## Every crossing word ends in a fixed small core interval

For every j>=17,

    S_j/b_j=[1-(2/c_sc)^j]/(c_sc-2)>=eta.              (5)

For the elementary numerical bound, (2/c_sc)^3<1/2 and
(2/c_sc)^2<4/5 imply (2/c_sc)^17<1/40.
Any strict crossing needs h>1, hence has level at least18, since
mu_core<=1 and bsc_17=1.

Choose the last strict crossing of a run on any Hsc_m, and call its
level j and size h=b_j. Every occurrence of level j is immediately
followed by a complete Hsc_j. There are no subsequent strict crossings.
If the path reaches zero it stays there and the conclusion holds.
Otherwise all later steps are on the same ray and decrease its clock.
Using at least the following Hsc_j, the final clock is at most

    (kappa_ray K-eta)h-kappa_ray/beta  if A>=0,
    (K-eta)h-1/beta                   if A<0.          (6)

For A>=0 the first expression increases with kappa_ray, so its maximum
at kappa_ray=eta/K is -eta/(beta K). The function
beta K=p^p beta^beta increases on[1/2,2/3] and is at most
4^(1/3)/3<8/15. Thus this maximum is less than -195/64<-21/8.
For A<0, K<=eta and K=(p/beta)^p<=p/beta imply

    (K-eta)h-1/beta <= K-eta-1/beta <=-eta-1=-21/8.

Since exp(21/8)>1+21/8+(21/8)^2/2+(21/8)^3/6>8, every
crossing word ends with radius less than rho_core=1/8.              (7)
This conclusion holds for arbitrary input radii and all admitted
nonresonant curvatures. It says small core capture, not annihilation.

For later use, on either ray Clock(R)<=R-1 for ALL R>0: use
G>=1 beyond1 and log R<=R-1 below1. A word with no strict crossing
and no zero iterate consequently has

    Clock(R_end)<=R_init-1-S_j.                       (8)

## Exact attraction recurrence

Let I be the first level with t=b_I>1. Then I>=18 and 1<t<=c_sc.
All steps of Hsc_I are at most1. Its quadratic-core multiplier P
is nonnegative and satisfies P<=exp(-S_I)<=exp(-eta t).
Every core-started prefix of Hsc_I remains in the core. At the central
step of Hsc_(I+1), the largest possible radius factor is
(t-1)P<=(c_sc-1)exp(-eta)<1; the latter follows from
exp(eta)>1+eta>c_sc-1. The following Hsc_I again stays in the core.
Its complete absolute multiplier is Q=P^2(t-1).

With J=I+1 and b_J=c_sc t,

    b_J Q <= c_sc t(t-1)exp(-2eta t)
           <=3c_sc/(16eta^3)=1248/10985<1/8=k_env.   (9)

Indeed exp(2eta t)>(2eta t)^3/6 and (t-1)/t^2<=1/4.
Since rho_core b_J<=c_sc^2/8=169/200<1, every input of radius
q b_J, q<=rho_core, stays in the core throughout this base word.
Its endpoint is at most k_env q and hence satisfies (2).

Inductively assume (2) at level j-1, where j>J. Take an input
radius at most q b_j with q<=rho_core, and call r_1 its radius after
the first Hsc_(j-1). The exact word has the form
Hsc_(j-1), b_(j-1), Hsc_(j-1).

If c_sc q<=rho_core, the induction hypothesis on the first block gives

    r_1<=min(A_env c_sc q,k_env rho_core)<=q,

because A_env c_sc=169/200<1. Thus r_1<=rho_core and the middle
step uses the quadratic core. Its output radius is
(b_(j-1)-1)r_1<=b_(j-1)r_1; here b_(j-1)>2. Applying the induction
hypothesis to the second block with parameter r_1 gives both

    r_end<=A_env r_1<=A_env^2 c_sc q<=A_env q,
    r_end<=k_env rho_core.

If c_sc q>rho_core, the first block still has r_1<=rho_core.
When that block crosses this is (7). When it never crosses, (8) gives

    Clock(r_1)<=rho_core b_j-1-S_(j-1)
       <=-(eta/c_sc-rho_core)b_j-1=-b_j/2-1<-3,

because b_j>=c_sc^2 t>4. Since exp(3)>8, this also gives
r_1<rho_core. A zero output is harmless. The middle step again has
radius at most b_(j-1)rho_core. The second induction application,
now with parameter rho_core, gives r_end<=k_env rho_core.
Since q>rho_core/c_sc and A_env=c_sc k_env, this is at most A_env q.
Both parts of (2) follow. This completes the induction.

The recurrence is an inequality on actual fixed-function GD maps; it
does not choose a different derivative at different times. In the
asymmetric case it needs only the radius bounds for both initial signs,
not an assertion that the reachable image is a centered interval.

## Uniform full-objective bound

For any path with no crossing, write u for its terminal gradient
magnitude in normalized coordinates and r for its terminal radius.
Monotonicity yields R_init>=r+S_m u. The full terminal area satisfies
F_end<=u r-u^2/2 because G(t)<=min(t,u) for 0<=t<=r. Completing
the square therefore gives

    2F_end/R_init^2<=1/(1+2S_m).                      (10)

Suppose m>=J and the path crosses. If R_init<=rho_core b_m,
apply (2) with q=R_init/b_m. Its endpoint is in the core and

    2F_end/R_init^2<=A_env^2/b_m^2<=1/b_m^2.

If R_init>rho_core b_m, equation (7) instead gives
2F_end/R_init^2<=rho_core^2/R_init^2<1/b_m^2.
As b_m>c_sc and S_m>=eta b_m, both this bound and (10), after
multiplication by mu_core, are at most

    1/(c_sc bsc_m)                                   (11)

for m>=J; here 1/(2eta)<=1/c_sc.
For m<=I all steps are at most1 in normalized coordinates, so there
is no crossing. The bound (10) is at most1 and
mu_core<=c_sc/bsc_m, since b_m<=b_I=t<=c_sc.
Together these cases prove (1), including the empty word.

## Exact benchmark comparison and scope

Use the benchmark recursions in accepted fact b98bb807d514e80d:
C_n=S_circle(n)+1, B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1, C_0=B_0=1,

    C_n=max_j Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_j Gamma(C_j,B_(n-j-1)),
    Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,
    Gamma(A,B)=2A+B/2+sqrt(B^2+8AB)/2.

For completeness, Omega(A,B)<=(A^(3/4)+B^(3/4))^(4/3).
To prove it, put t=A^(3/4)/(A^(3/4)+B^(3/4)); the positive-root
formula reduces it to
t^(4/3)+(1-t)^(4/3)+[t(1-t)]^(4/3)<=1.
With u=t^(1/3), v=(1-t)^(1/3), the difference equals
u^3 v^3[1/(1+u+u^2)+1/(1+v+v^2)-uv]>=0:
both reciprocals are at least1/3 and uv<=2^(-2/3)<2/3.
Induction gives C_n<=(n+1)^(4/3). Since Gamma(A,B)<=B+4A,
another induction gives B_n<=1+4n^(4/3). Consequently (1) divided
by U_(Nsc_m)^ZJ is at most

    (c_sc/a_sc)c_sc^(-m)[1+4(2^m-1)^(4/3)] ->0,

because c_sc^3>16. No external theorem is used.

This removes the resonance assumption from the earlier nonperiodic
subpower class and handles all outside initial points using (2).
The common quadratic neighborhood, outer growth restriction and
bounded ray ratio remain load-bearing. No all-scalar or unrestricted
multidimensional upper bound, and no new accepted fact, is asserted.

claim: Constructive short-tail re-selection candidate: for any nonnegative tail with at most two positive steps, even arbitrary signed incoming-terminal multipliers cannot enlarge the intrinsic primitive certificate class. Any PSD signed identity with other multipliers nonnegative can be replaced by an ordinary nonnegative certificate, including a valid lift to the original zero-step formal space. evidence:
# Saturated-cut certificates retain a signed terminal-interpolation credit

Status: self-contained candidate, NOT verifier-accepted. No solver or
fact_submit was used. The full initial-distance objective theorem is not
being restricted here: the statement concerns the explicitly specified
intrinsic primitive energy. The only accepted background used is the
necessity of the interpolation inequalities in fact 1252b8823bb5a290.

## 1. Definitions and an exact identity

Work at smoothness one. On a GD trajectory for a list h of sum s and
capacity C=1+s, write g_i=grad f(x_i), f_i=f(x_i), and

  Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <= 0,
  V_h=2 sum_(i<n) h_i(f_i-f_n)
          +sum_(i<n) h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-sC||g_n||^2.

Take two lists a,b of capacities A,D, respectively, and set

  T=A+D+r,  r>0,  rT=AD,
  kappa=(T/D)^2=(A/r)^2,
  theta=1-1/kappa.

In particular 0<r<min(A,D), kappa>1 and 0<theta<1. The joined
schedule is h=(a,1+r,b). Denote its bridge query by L and the tail
queries by j=0,...,m; z=m is the final query. Tail indices in Q always
mean the corresponding original joined indices. Define

  J_b=sum_(j<m) b_j Q_(j,z),
  E_theta(b)=V_b-theta J_b,
  C_cross=sum_(j<m) b_j Q_(j,L)+Q_(z,L)+r Q_(L,z).

The exact identity, including every value term, is

  V_h = V_a + kappa E_theta(b) - (kappa-1) C_cross.       (1)

All coefficients in -C_cross are nonnegative on actual inequalities
-Q. Thus universal nonnegativity of V_a and E_theta(b) is a sufficient
condition for universal nonnegativity of V_h. It is not necessary here
to assume V_b>=0. Whether this genuinely enlarges the allowable tail
class is a separate question.

Here is a direct audit of (1). Put p=g_L, q=g_z, and
H=sum_(j<m)b_j g_j. Then x_tail,0=x_L-(1+r)p and x_z=x_tail,0-H.
For C=C_cross+J_b the value part is

  C_f=2sum_(j<m)b_j f_j+(r-D)f_L+(2-D-r)f_z.

Expand each Q and use
2sum_j b_j<g_j,sum_(i<j)b_i g_i>=||H||^2-sum_j b_j^2||g_j||^2.
The gradient part reduces exactly to

  C_g=sum_(j<m)b_j(1-b_j)||g_j||^2
            +[(D-r)/2-r^2]||p||^2+(D+r)||q||^2/2.

All mixed p,H,q products cancel. The identities

  (kappa-1)(D-r)=2(A+r),
  kappa r^2=A^2,  kappa D^2=T^2

then show V_h=V_a+kappa V_b-(kappa-1)C coefficient by coefficient:
the f_L coefficient is 2(1+r), the f_z coefficient is -2(T-1),
the p-square coefficient is -r(1+r), and the q-square coefficient
is -T(T-1). Substituting kappa theta=kappa-1 proves (1).

## 2. Full intrinsic certificates force the bridge coefficients

For this part assume the entries of a and b are strictly positive;
either list may be empty. Suppose an explicit intrinsic certificate is
given:

  M_h=V_h+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij,
  lambda_ij>=0,

where values cancel and M_h is PSD in the full independent formal
gradient vector. Allowing the optimum index and x_0 initially does not
enlarge this class. Indeed V_h has no x_0-square coefficient, so PSD
forces the x_0 row to vanish. Its cross coefficients are -lambda_i,star,
which forces every lambda_i,star=0. Summing the value-flow equalities
then gives sum_i lambda_star,i=0, so these multipliers also vanish.
This argument relies on the absence of an initial-distance term and
does NOT apply to a full objective certificate.

There are two explicit equality trajectories for V_h. A scalar Huber
trajectory staying on one affine ray has every gradient equal to 1,
all finite Q zero, and V_h=0. A second trajectory uses the derivative

  f'(x)=min(1,max(x,-eta)),  eta=r/D,

starting at A. The prefix gradient is 1, its last query is 1, the
bridge lands at -r, and the tail gradient is -eta until its endpoint
-eta. Every incoming optimum residual is zero. Distance telescoping
gives V_h=A^2-T^2 eta^2=0.

For completeness, if R_i is a prefix query's remaining prefix sum
and R_j is a tail query's remaining tail sum, this second trajectory
has

  Q_(prefix i,tail j)=-(1+eta)eta R_j,
  Q_(tail j,prefix i)=-(1+eta)R_i.                       (2)

Every within-block Q is zero. Since M_h>=0 and all lambda Q<=0,
equality of V_h forces multiplier complementarity and M_h to vanish
on each equality gradient vector. Those vectors span the two block
indicators e_A,e_B, so both indicators lie in the kernel of M_h.

By (2), the only potentially nonzero cross multipliers are

  nu_i=lambda_(prefix i,z),  mu_j=lambda_(tail j,L).

For a prefix index i<L, the corresponding row of M_h e_B is
-D nu_i/2. Thus nu_i=0 for every i<L. Write nu=nu_L.
For a nonterminal tail index j, the corresponding row of M_h e_A
is [r mu_j-nu b_j]/2; at z it is [r mu_z-nu]/2.
Consequently

  mu_j=(nu/r)b_j  (j<m),  mu_z=nu/r.

The sum of the prefix value-flow equations is
sum_j mu_j-nu=2(A+r). Therefore all cross multipliers are fixed:

  lambda_(j,L)=(kappa-1)b_j (j<m),
  lambda_(z,L)=kappa-1,
  lambda_(L,z)=r(kappa-1),                              (3)

and every other cross multiplier is zero. The mixed gradient block
of the full matrix vanishes, not merely its value on equality data.

## 3. Exact cone interface and the sign that cannot be discarded

Let lambda^A,lambda^B be the two within-block multiplier arrays of
the given full certificate. Define a signed tail array by

  lambda_hat_ij=lambda^B_ij/kappa
                 -theta b_i * 1_(i<m,j=z).             (4)

Combining (1) with (3) yields the full block-diagonal identity

  M_h = M_a + kappa M_b,
  M_a=V_a+sum lambda^A_ij Q_ij,
  M_b=V_b+sum lambda_hat_ij Q_ij.                       (5)

Each summand has its own value cancellation, since its values are in
a disjoint block. Full PSD is equivalent to PSD of both summands.
The prefix multipliers are nonnegative. The exact tail constraints are

  lambda_hat_ij>=0 except possibly i<m,j=z,
  lambda_hat_(i,z)>=-theta b_i.                        (6)

Conversely, any prefix intrinsic certificate and any PSD tail identity
with the value cancellation and bounds (6) give a nonnegative full
certificate by (3),(4). Equivalently, the tail has an ordinary
nonnegative certificate for E_theta(b), not necessarily for V_b.

Thus direct restriction to an ordinary primitive tail certificate would
require the stronger bounds

  lambda^B_(i,z)>=(kappa-1)b_i.                        (7)

They are not implied for each full certificate. The next exact example
proves this, including full nonnegativity and PSD.

## 4. Exact full certificate violating the proposed coefficient floor

Use the empty prefix A=1, tail b=(1,1) of capacity D=3, and

  r=sqrt(7)-2, T=sqrt(7)+2, kappa=(11+4sqrt(7))/9.

The full schedule is h=(sqrt(7)-1,1,1). Use original indices 0,1,2,3,
where 0 is the bridge query and 1,2,3 are the tail queries. Set

  lambda_10=lambda_20=lambda_30=kappa-1,
  lambda_03=r(kappa-1),
  lambda_12=5kappa/2, lambda_21=17kappa/4,
  lambda_23=37kappa/4-1, lambda_32=12kappa,
  lambda_13=3kappa/4-1,

with every unlisted multiplier zero. All are nonnegative, since
kappa>4/3. Direct substitution, or (1) and the audited tail identity
below, gives

  V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij
   =kappa { ||(g_1-g_2)-(g_2-g_3)/8||^2
                         +(255/64)||g_2-g_3||^2 } >=0. (8)

For the tail alone, write u=g_0-g_1 and v=g_1-g_2 using local indices.
Its signed multiplier list is

  lambda_hat_01=5/2, lambda_hat_10=17/4,
  lambda_hat_12=33/4, lambda_hat_21=12,
  lambda_hat_02=-1/4, lambda_hat_20=0.

The value coefficients cancel, and expansion gives

  V_(1,1)+sum lambda_hat_ij Q_ij
      =||u||^2-<u,v>/4+4||v||^2
      =||u-v/8||^2+(255/64)||v||^2.

Nevertheless lambda_13=(kappa-1)-kappa/4 is strictly below the
proposed floor kappa-1. The restricted terminal coefficient is -1/4.
This refutes the inference of (7) from full nonnegativity and PSD.

There IS another ordinary primitive certificate for this tail:
lambda_01=2,lambda_10=4,lambda_12=8,lambda_21=12, all other
multipliers zero, gives ||u||^2+4||v||^2. Accordingly this example
does not disprove existence of a suitable re-selection, arbitrary-tail
heredity, or the original asymptotic minimax problem. It identifies
the exact missing sign assertion rather than replacing it with PSD.

## 5. A particular nonprimitive tail cannot exploit this credit

The previously considered b=(17/10,2,6/5) fails even E_theta for
every 0<=theta<=1. Here is a self-contained witness.
Put m=7/34, ell=21/85. Define the continuous derivative

  f'(x)=x                  for x<=m,
         m                 for m<=x<=m+ell,
         x-ell             for x>=m+ell,

and integrate with f(0)=0. Its derivative is nondecreasing and
1-Lipschitz, so f is convex differentiable 1-smooth with minimizer 0.
Starting at x_0=106/85 gives

  (x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3)=(106/85,-77/170,77/170,7/34),
  (g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3)=(1,-77/170,7/34,7/34).

The endpoint is core: x_3=g_3=m, f_3=m^2/2. Define
I_i=<g_i,x_i>-f_i-||g_i||^2/2. Direct scalar evaluation gives

  I_0=ell(1-m)=567/2890, I_1=I_2=I_3=0,
  sum_(i<3)b_i I_i=567/1700,
  V_b=-13581/23120.

At a core endpoint, expansion gives Q_(i,3)=-I_i. Thus

  E_theta(b)=-13581/23120+theta*567/1700
           <= -29349/115600 <0.                       (9)

The value of V_b can also be checked without integrating every term:
distance telescoping gives
V_b=x_0^2-D^2g_3^2-2sum b_i I_i, with D=59/10.
This proves (9) exactly.

Consequently this specific tail cannot acquire a valid E_theta
certificate at any saturated join parameter. A rank-one coefficient
matching attempt on this same fixed tail also failed, but (9) is the
stronger actual-function obstruction. Neither statement excludes other
nonprimitive tails. No numerical schedule screen was reopened.

## 6. Complete two-bridge identity with retained earlier anchors

The identity also provides a closed, explicitly signed value state
through two bridges. Let a_1,a_2 be any nonnegative physical prefix
lists of capacities A_1,A_2. Starting with the physical tail b of
capacity D_0, define

  H_1=(a_1,1+r_1,b), D_1=A_1+D_0+r_1, r_1 D_1=A_1 D_0,
  H_2=(a_2,1+r_2,H_1), D_2=A_2+D_1+r_2, r_2 D_2=A_2 D_1,
  kappa_1=(D_1/D_0)^2, kappa_2=(D_2/D_1)^2,
  K=kappa_1 kappa_2=(D_2/D_0)^2, theta_2=1-1/K.

Let L_1,L_2 be the respective bridge query indices in the final
original indexing and z the final query. For each physical step in
a_1 or a_2, its gradient/value index is also its original index in H_2.
Define the following sums of actual inequalities, without collapsing
any old query or replacing it by a new anchor:

  C_1=sum_(j in b steps)b_j Q_(j,L_1)+Q_(z,L_1)+r_1 Q_(L_1,z),
  C_2=sum_(i in H_1 steps)(H_1)_i Q_(i,L_2)
                                      +Q_(z,L_2)+r_2 Q_(L_2,z),
  J_left1=sum_(i in a_1 steps)(a_1)_i Q_(i,z)
                                      +(1+r_1)Q_(L_1,z).

Then the complete identity is

  V_(H_2)=V_(a_2)+kappa_2 V_(a_1)+K E_theta2(b)
       -kappa_2(kappa_1-1)C_1-(kappa_2-1)C_2
       -(kappa_2-1)J_left1.                            (10)

Every coefficient displayed on -Q is nonnegative. In particular the
earlier a_1 queries still have their actual outgoing edges to z, and
every query inside H_1 has its actual edge to L_2. These are not removed
by the unqueried-terminal theorem.

To verify (10) algebraically, apply the audited expansion in Section 1
at each cut. The weighted incoming-terminal sum for H_1 is exactly
J_b+J_left1. Substitution gives a J_b coefficient
kappa_2(kappa_1-1)+(kappa_2-1)=K-1=K theta_2; all other terms are
those displayed in (10). This derivation is part of this same candidate
proof, not an invocation of an unverified finding as a theorem.

Consequently, if explicit nonnegative intrinsic certificates are given
for a_1 and a_2, and an explicit nonnegative certificate is given for
E_theta2(b), (10) assembles an intrinsic certificate for H_2. Its PSD
remainder is the sum of the three input PSD remainders with scales
1,kappa_2,K. All original actual multipliers are sums of nonnegative
numbers. No positive remainder is presumed for a benchmark block.

## 7. Final objective certificate, including initial distance

Here is the exact final conversion for any intrinsic certificate
produced by (10), and in particular for the example below. Write H=H_2,
let its terminal query be n, its capacity be D=1+sum_(i<n)H_i, and let

  M_H=V_H+sum_(i!=j<=n)lambda_ij Q_ij >=0

be the assembled PSD identity, with all lambda_ij>=0. Define

  t=(-1+sqrt(8D+1))/4, beta=1+t,
  gamma=1/(2t+1), q=gamma^2,
  x_(n+1)=x_n-beta g_n.

The arithmetic identities are t=gamma D, 1-gamma=2qD, and
q=1/[1+2(sum H_i+beta)]. The accepted terminal-square parameterization
in fact 1252b8823bb5a290(c) applies with terminal probabilities
alpha_star=gamma, alpha_n=1-gamma, and all other alpha_i=0.
Give the queried prefix the following additional optimum multipliers:

  lambda_pre_(i,star)=2q H_i  (i<n),
  lambda_pre_(n,star)=2q(D+1),

and multiply every intrinsic lambda_ij by q. All these coefficients
are nonnegative and their flows are exactly the required 2alpha_i.
There are no optimum-outgoing multipliers in this particular
constructed certificate; none is dropped from an arbitrary certificate.
The full identity supplied by the accepted parameterization is

  q||x_0||^2-2f_(n+1)
    +q sum_(i!=j<=n)lambda_ij Q_ij
    +2q sum_(i<n)H_i Q_(i,star)+2q(D+1)Q_(n,star)
    +2(1-gamma)Q_(n+1,n)+2gamma Q_(n+1,star)
  =||g_(n+1)-[gamma x_n-(t+gamma)g_n]||^2+q M_H.       (11)

The optimum is translated to x_star=0,f_star=0 in this display.
It follows that W_(n+1)(H,beta)<=q. The factor on ||x_0||^2 is retained,
so this is a certificate in the original objective normalization.

To audit its application rather than re-prove the accepted component,
the prefix remainder of that component is

  R=q||x_0||^2-2(1-gamma)(f_n-||g_n||^2/2)
       -||gamma x_n-(t+gamma)g_n||^2
       +2q sum_(i<n)H_i Q_(i,star)+2q(D+1)Q_(n,star)
       +q sum lambda_ij Q_ij.

Using t=gamma D and 1-gamma=2qD, its mixed <x_n,g_n> coefficient
cancels. Its f_n and ||g_n||^2 coefficients are respectively
-2q(D-1) and -qD(D-1). Distance telescoping then gives R=q M_H,
which is exactly (11). Every queried-prefix inequality is retained.

## 8. A full two-bridge calibration and its exact scope

Take b=(1,1), and take both a_1,a_2 empty. Then

  D_0=3, D_1=2+sqrt(7), r_1=sqrt(7)-2,
  D_2=[1+D_1+sqrt((1+D_1)^2+4D_1)]/2, r_2=D_2-1-D_1.

Thus H_2=(1+r_2,sqrt(7)-1,1,1). For E_theta2(b), use the signed
tail coefficients in Section 4 and add theta_2 b_i to each incoming
terminal coefficient. The only initially negative coefficient becomes
theta_2-1/4>0: already kappa_1>4/3 and K>kappa_1. All other
coefficients are nonnegative. The PSD remainder is
||u-v/8||^2+(255/64)||v||^2, because the added interpolation terms
exactly cancel the -theta_2 J_b term in E_theta2.

Equations (10),(11) therefore give a completely explicit certificate
for this five-step objective schedule after appending beta. This is a
calibration of signed coordinates with nonnegative actual multipliers,
not an improved asymptotic schedule. In particular, the physical tail
capacity 3 is already smaller than that of the legal two-step primitive
schedule (3/2,3/2), whose capacity is 4. The old tail also has an ordinary
primitive certificate, so this example does not establish strict
enlargement by the E_theta state.

The comparator's primitive property has a direct identity, so no
unverified external premise is needed: at h=(3/2,3/2), take
lambda_01=1,lambda_10=7/2,lambda_12=17/2,lambda_21=14,
lambda_02=1/2,lambda_20=1. Expanding gives V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij=0.
All six multipliers are positive. Replacing the capacity-3 tail by this
capacity-4 tail in the same two saturated joins strictly increases both
successive capacities, since the positive root
Omega(A,D)=[A+D+sqrt((A+D)^2+4AD)]/2 is increasing in D for A,D>0.
The terminal q in (11) strictly decreases. The displayed calibration
is therefore strictly dominated already at its own finite horizon.

The unresolved bridge toward an improvement is concrete: find an actual
tail with a nonnegative certificate for E_theta at some theta<1 and with
a capacity gain large enough to pay for the physical prefix lengths.
Neither the existence of that tail nor the required infinite-horizon
comparison with U_n^ZJ is asserted here.

## 9. Exact re-selection for tails with at most two positive steps

The new state cannot give a genuinely larger primitive certificate
class on tails with at most two positive steps. More strongly, suppose
an identity V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij has value cancellation and is PSD,
with every multiplier nonnegative EXCEPT that incoming-terminal
lambda_(i,n) may have arbitrary real signs, without any lower bound.
For at most two positive steps, an ordinary nonnegative intrinsic
certificate can always be constructed. This is a certificate statement;
no unproved dual-attainment equivalence is used.

For one positive step u, value cancellation gives
lambda_10=lambda_01+2u. An affine Huber trajectory has equal gradients
and all Q=V=0. Thus PSD forces the all-one vector into the kernel.
The second row of the matrix times that vector is
u(lambda_01-2)/2, so lambda_01=2, lambda_10=2+2u.
The remainder is (2-u^2)||g_0-g_1||^2; PSD requires u<=sqrt(2).
Both multipliers are already nonnegative.

Now take two positive steps h=(u,v), with s=u+v. Put

  c=lambda_02, d=lambda_20, a=lambda_01, b=lambda_12.

Only c,b can be signed; a,d,lambda_10,lambda_21 are nonnegative.
The value equations give

  lambda_10=a+c-d+2u,
  lambda_21=b+c-d+2s.

The same affine equality argument puts the all-one gradient vector in
the PSD kernel. Direct expansion of its first and last rows gives

  u a+s c=2u,
  v(b+c)+u d=2s(u+1).

Therefore

  a=2-(s/u)c,
  b=2s(u+1)/v-c-(u/v)d,
  lambda_10=2(u+1)-(v/u)c-d,
  b=2(u+1)+(u/v)lambda_10>0.                           (12)

So b is actually positive. In gradient differences U=g_0-g_1 and
V=g_1-g_2, the complete quadratic is

  [2-u^2+v(u-1)c/u]||U||^2
    +[c-(u-1)d]<U,V>+[C_0-(u/v)d]||V||^2,             (13)
  C_0=s[2(u+1)/v-s].

These formulas can be checked from the six explicit pair residuals;
no inequality replacement occurs. If c>=0, all the supplied
multipliers are nonnegative already, by (12).

If c<0, PSD implies both diagonal coefficients in (13) are
nonnegative. Since d>=0, the last coefficient implies C_0>=0.
If u<1 then u<sqrt(2). If u>=1, the c contribution in the first
coefficient is nonpositive, so its nonnegativity implies u<=sqrt(2).
Now replace the supplied multipliers by the explicit adjacent-only list

  lambda'_01=2, lambda'_10=2+2u,
  lambda'_12=2s(u+1)/v,
  lambda'_21=2s(u+1)/v+2s,
  lambda'_02=lambda'_20=0.

All are nonnegative. Substitution is (13) with c=d=0 and gives

  V_h+sum lambda'_ij Q_ij
       =(2-u^2)||U||^2+C_0||V||^2 >=0.                (14)

This constructs the re-selection, rather than inferring a false
coefficient bound for the original certificate.

For nonnegative lists with zero entries and at most two positive
entries, first restrict the given signed certificate to the subspace
where all jets in a zero-step run agree. Congruence preserves PSD;
terms between coincident jets vanish; remaining coefficients aggregate
by query class. Only coefficients entering the final class can remain
signed. The intrinsic energy becomes the positive-compressed energy.
Apply the result above (or V_empty=0). Lift the newly constructed
ordinary certificate to the original formal space by selecting each
positive-step query as its representative and selecting the original
terminal n as the terminal representative. Positions agree as formal
identities because every omitted step coefficient is zero. The lifted
quadratic is a congruence of the compressed PSD matrix; all unused
formal-gradient columns vanish. No equality between duplicate formal
gradients is imposed in the final certificate.

Accordingly, a strict advantage from the terminal-credit state, if one
exists, requires at least three positive physical tail steps. The
specific three-step rational tail in Section 5 is already excluded by
an actual-function witness. General three-step and longer re-selection
is not proved by this calculation.

claim: C27 complete strict-SIMPLEX reduction candidate: any intrinsic primitive failure for the SAME schedule with m positive steps has a negative projection-function witness in dimension m+1 on a simplex with exactly m+2 vertices, every nonduplicate sample projecting strictly onto its own distinct vertex. Gives full normal/Gram game and exact physical norm identity V_h=||x0||^2-||xn+S P_C(xn)||^2. Explicit triangle at h=3/2 has V=-3/80; a translation family on that SAME triangle preserves V while normalized objective with the CLOSEST minimizer tends to0. No capacity/profile theorem is inferred.
evidence:
# Strict simplex witnesses for primitive failure

Status: complete candidate, NOT verifier-accepted. No new fact_submit or
numerical search is allocated. The proof uses the interpolation necessity
in accepted fact 1252b8823bb5a290. The public projection/saturation findings
20c6d21ee60a4cb0 and 4ad60ca9f3ec3e2e were leads, not premises.
All new steps, including the independent-gradient perturbation, are below.

## 1. Exact statement

For a finite nonnegative physical schedule h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), put
S=sum h_i and define, on any actual convex differentiable 1-smooth GD run,

    V_h=2 sum_(i<n) h_i(f_i-f_n)
        +sum_(i<n) h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
        -S(S+1)||g_n||^2.                            (1)

Call h primitive when V_h>=0 for every such finite-dimensional run with
a minimizer. Let m be the number of strictly positive steps of h.

The following conditions are equivalent:

* h is primitive;
* for every finite-dimensional compact convex polytope C containing0,
  the function F_C(x)=(||x||^2-dist(x,C)^2)/2 and its GD run satisfy
  ||x_n+S P_C(x_n)||<=||x_0||;
* the same inequality holds for every full-dimensional simplex in
  R^(m+1) with vertices 0,v_0,...,v_m.

More strongly, if h fails primitivity, a negative witness can be chosen
on a simplex of the last form with its m+1 distinct compressed query
gradients exactly v_0,...,v_m. Every projection normal inequality at
one of these query vertices is STRICT against each different vertex,
including zero. Duplicates introduced by zero steps are simply restored.
Thus there are exactly m+2 vertices, dimension m+1, and no limiting
interpolant. The original step values and order are unchanged.

The construction preserves a strictly negative intrinsic energy. It
does NOT preserve the normalized objective error, or the initial distance.
Section7 gives a fixed triangle where the absolute negative energy stays
constant while even the objective normalized by the closest-minimizer
distance tends to zero.

## 2. Projection functions and every normal inequality

Let C be a nonempty compact convex set containing0. The unique maximizer
of <x,v>-||v||^2/2 over v in C is its nearest point p=P_C(x), by completing
the square. Therefore

    F_C(x)=max_(v in C)(<x,v>-||v||^2/2)
          =(||x||^2-dist(x,C)^2)/2.                   (2)

The nearest-point condition is

    <x-p,v-p><=0 for EVERY v in C.                   (3)

Necessity follows by differentiating squared distance along the segment
from p to v; sufficiency follows by expanding ||x-v||^2. Applied twice,
(3) gives ||P_C(x)-P_C(y)||^2<=<P_C(x)-P_C(y),x-y>, so P_C is
1-Lipschitz. Comparing the maxima in (2) gives

    0<=F_C(x+d)-F_C(x)-<P_C(x),d>
      <=<P_C(x+d)-P_C(x),d><=||d||^2.

Consequently F_C is convex, differentiable, and 1-smooth, with gradient
P_C. It is nonnegative and F_C(0)=0. Its minimizer set is precisely the
polar cone C^polar={z:<z,v><=0 for every v in C}: use (3) with p=0.

For proposed query data X_i,G_i, define

    Y_i=X_i-G_i,  F_i=<G_i,X_i>-||G_i||^2/2.

On C=conv{0,G_0,...,G_m}, the COMPLETE projection conditions are

    <Y_i,G_j-G_i><=0 for ALL i,j,
    <Y_i,-G_i><=0 for ALL i.                         (4)

Convex combinations then give (3) for every retained point. No adjacent
or chronological subset replaces (4).

## 3. A finite strict perturbation with independent gradients

Compress zero steps from the supplied negative witness. A zero step repeats
the point, gradient, and function value. Its coefficients in (1) vanish,
and S and the final jet are unchanged, so V_h is unchanged. If m=0 then
V_h=0, and there was no negative witness. Hence assume m>=1 and the
compressed steps are all positive; write their actual energy as -v_def<0.

Construct an auxiliary quadratic on R^(m+1): let

    theta_l=(l+1)/(2(m+2)), 0<=l<=m,
    A_aux=diag(theta_0,...,theta_m),
    psi(z)=<z,A_aux z>/2,  z_0=(1,...,1).

Run the same compressed schedule and denote its jets by z_i,w_i,psi_i.
If P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z), its coordinate gradients are
w_(i,l)=theta_l P_i(theta_l). These m+1 gradients are linearly independent.
Indeed the P_i have distinct degrees 0,...,m and nonzero leading
coefficients. A linear combination vanishing at the m+1 distinct theta_l
is a polynomial of degree at most m with m+1 roots, hence is zero; the
distinct-degree basis then makes every coefficient zero.

Every two sample positions z_i,z_j are distinct, since P_i-P_j is a
nonzero polynomial of degree at most m and cannot vanish at all theta_l.
For the signed residual convention from accepted fact 1252b8823bb5a290,

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,

direct substitution for this auxiliary quadratic gives

    Q_ij^aux=-<z_i-z_j,A_aux(I-A_aux)(z_i-z_j)>/2<0    (i!=j). (5)

All theta_l lie strictly between0 and1. Let E_aux be the finite energy
of this explicitly given quadratic run. Choose

    epsilon=v_def/[2(v_def+|E_aux|)] in(0,1/2].       (6)

Take the fixed product function

    f_mix(x,z)=f_original(x)+epsilon psi(z/sqrt(epsilon)).

Start it at (x_0,sqrt(epsilon)z_0). Its sampled points and gradients are
(x_i,sqrt(epsilon)z_i) and (g_i,sqrt(epsilon)w_i), with values
f_i+epsilon psi_i. It is convex differentiable 1-smooth, and all GD
equations are exact. Energy and every Q are additive across these
coordinates. Hence its energy is

    V_mix=-v_def+epsilon E_aux<=-v_def/2<0,           (7)

its gradients are independent, and all finite distinct-sample Q_ij
are strictly negative by (5). Rename these mixed data x_i,g_i,f_i.

## 4. One origin/value shift makes an actual simplex trajectory

Set

    f_* = min_i(f_i-||g_i||^2/2)-1,
    r_i = f_*-f_i+<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2.

Let A_gram=(<g_i,g_j>)_(0<=i,j<=m), which is positive definite.
Define z_*=sum_j (A_gram^(-1)r)_j g_j. Then <g_i,z_*>=r_i.
Set X_i=x_i-z_* and F_i=f_i-f_*. The GD equations are unchanged,
and the defining equalities give

    F_i=<g_i,X_i>-||g_i||^2/2.                        (8)

For all finite ordered pairs, the Q residual is unchanged and is
strictly negative. Substituting (8) into it gives

    Q_ij=<X_j-g_j,g_i-g_j><0 for i!=j.               (9)

Moreover <X_i-g_i,g_i>=F_i-||g_i||^2/2>=1. These are ALL the
normal inequalities (4), including strict inequalities against zero.
Consequently the fixed polytope C=conv{0,g_0,...,g_m} satisfies
P_C(X_i)=g_i and F_C(X_i)=F_i at every compressed query.
Thus it is an actual globally legal projection-function realization;
we did not just assign independent values and gradients.

The g_i are linearly independent, so these m+2 points are all vertices
of a simplex of dimension m+1. Orthogonally project all X_i onto
W=span{g_0,...,g_m}. Gradients, values, GD equations, and all inequalities
(9) are unchanged. The removed component is constant along the run.
This puts the entire realization in dimension m+1. All initial points
are nonzero, since <g_0,X_0>=F_0+||g_0||^2/2>0.

Translation of the points and a common shift of the values leave (1)
unchanged; orthogonal compression does too. Therefore its final energy
is exactly V_mix<0. Restoring the original zero steps repeats the
corresponding actual jets and keeps the same polytope, all physical
steps, and the energy. This proves the claimed finite sign reduction.

## 5. The norm identity, including the discarded-slack term

For arbitrary original legal data with minimizer0 and value0 define

    I_i=<g_i,x_i>-f_i-||g_i||^2/2>=0,
    J=sum_(i<n)h_i I_i.

The GD squared-distance telescope gives

    V_h=||x_0||^2-||x_n+Sg_n||^2+2(S I_n-J).         (10)

Indeed ||x_0||^2-||x_n||^2
=2sum h_i<g_i,x_i>-sum h_i^2||g_i||^2; substitute
<g_i,x_i>=f_i+||g_i||^2/2+I_i and expand the final square.

For projection functions, (2) makes every I_i exactly zero. Therefore
the proposed physical-step formula is exactly

    V_h=||x_0||^2-||x_n+S P_C(x_n)||^2.             (11)

It is generally false without the extra slack in (10). Combining (11)
with sections2--4 proves all equivalences in section1. No missing
function values were dropped: they determine r, z_*, and the resulting
positions relative to the simplex.

## 6. A precise full Gram game and its scope

For the compressed length m define the lower-triangular matrix T_h by
(T_h)_ii=1, (T_h)_ij=h_j for j<i, and zero for j>i. Let A_gram be
the positive definite gradient Gram matrix and b_i=<g_i,X_0>.
The complete normal inequalities are precisely

    b_j-b_i <= (T_h A_gram)_ij-(T_h A_gram)_ii   for all i,j,
    b_i >= (T_h A_gram)_ii                      for all i. (12)

The strict simplex construction makes all nontrivial inequalities strict.
Conversely any positive definite A_gram and b satisfying (12) have a
realization: choose independent vectors with this Gram matrix, and set
X_0=sum_j(A_gram^(-1)b)_j g_j. Equations (12) then prove all projection
conditions for the specified simplex and prescribed GD trajectory.

Put d_i=h_i for i<m, d_m=-S. Then sum_i d_i=0 and

    V_h=2 b^T d-d^T A_gram d,
    ||X_0||^2=b^T A_gram^(-1)b.                       (13)

These formulas retain every queried vertex. They are a lossless
finite-dimensional game for primitive validity, not yet a capacity bound.
In particular, no conclusion S+1<=(m+1)^(log_2(1+sqrt(2))) is inferred.

Adding a common constant to every b_i preserves the finite differences
and the primitive energy, and can enforce the origin inequalities. It
changes the initial norm in (13); it therefore cannot be used freely in
an objective-normalized lower bound.

## 7. An exact triangle, and a quantitative normalization failure

Take the one-step schedule h=(3/2), the triangle

    v_0=(1,0),  v_1=(-2/5,1/10), C=conv{0,v_0,v_1},
    X_0=(2,267/20), X_1=(1/2,267/20).

The two query normals are Y_0=(1,267/20) and Y_1=(9/10,53/4).
ALL nontrivial projection comparisons are

    <Y_0,v_1-v_0>=<Y_1,v_0-v_1>=-13/200,
    <Y_0,-v_0>=-1,  <Y_1,-v_1>=-193/200.

Thus these are strict vertex projections, and their complete values are
F_C(X_0)=3/2, F_C(X_1)=21/20. The norm game gives

    V_h=72889/400-72904/400=-3/80<0.                  (14)

For every T>=0 put u=(1,14), X_i(T)=X_i+T u. Since
<u,v_0>=<u,v_1>=1, every finite normal difference above is unchanged,
and the origin comparisons only become more negative. Hence the SAME
fixed triangle realizes the same gradient trajectory for every T,

    F_C(X_i(T))=F_C(X_i)+T,
    V_h(T)=-3/80.

Its minimizer cone is {z:z_1<=0, z_2<=4z_1}. Both coordinates of
X_0(T) are positive, while both coordinates of a cone point are
nonpositive. Expanding squared distances proves that zero is the
closest minimizer to X_0(T). Therefore the genuine normalized terminal
objective is

    [21/10+2T]/[(2+T)^2+(267/20+14T)^2] ->0.          (15)

This is not merely an arbitrary poor choice of minimizer. It proves that
an absolute negative primitive margin alone cannot lower-bound the
normalized objective even on one fixed simplex and one fixed schedule.
It does not upper-bound the worst case for that schedule: other instances
may give a much larger value.

The mechanism holds on every independent-gradient simplex. Let u be
the unique vector in the gradient span with <u,g_i>=1 for all i.
Translation by T u preserves all finite normal inequalities and shifts
all sample values by T, while improving the origin comparisons.
Since sum d_i=0, it leaves V_h unchanged. The closest-minimizer distance
is Theta(T): for each cone point z, <g_i,z><=0, so
||X_0+Tu-z||>=(T+<g_i,X_0>)/||g_i|| for sufficiently large T;
the upper bound O(T) follows by choosing z=0. Thus (15)'s dilution
is a general geometric feature, not a special coordinate artifact.

## 8. A failed capacity-witness simplification

A natural attempt to make the simplex game tractable is to require all
nonzero visited vertices to have one common radius. This is NOT a
universal class of primitive counterexamples, even at length1.

Suppose 0<=h_i<2 and every nonzero sampled projection gradient has norm R.
If both consecutive gradients are nonzero, projection cocoercivity gives

    ||g_i-g_(i+1)||^2
      <=h_i<g_i,g_i-g_(i+1)>
      =(h_i/2)||g_i-g_(i+1)||^2.

They must therefore be equal. If a zero gradient is ever reached, that
point is a minimizer and all later gradients are zero. Before that time
the gradient is constant. If no zero is reached, x_n+Sg_n=x_0 and V_h=0.
If a zero is reached, each h_i<2 step decreases squared distance to zero:
the vertex0 inequality gives <x_i,g_i>>=||g_i||^2, hence

    ||x_(i+1)||^2<=||x_i||^2-h_i(2-h_i)||g_i||^2.

Thus (11) is nonnegative again. In particular equal-radius vertex walks,
including regular-simplex vertex walks, cannot reject h=(3/2), although
the explicit strict triangle (14) does reject it. Allowing projections
onto nonvertex faces is outside this failed simplification.

The exact general simplex reduction succeeds. The equal-radius capacity
ansatz fails, and the unrestricted capacity inequality remains open.

evidence:
# Audit: the earlier Chebyshev families already have large ray witnesses

Status: UNVERIFIED exact comparison using accepted facts. This corrects the
strategic interpretation of earlier findings, not their displayed interpolation
formulas. No verifier call or numerical computation was used.

The all-large-horizon families in findings `e2dad1cf3b95b8d7` and
`54a304d61fe223b4` were compared with K, quadratics and the universal complex
lens, but not with the stronger VERIFIED functional F_ray from fact
`1fca3e5dd555cb4a`. They are already very bad schedules for F_ray.

Let N>=4096, M=2N(N+1)+1, A=M^(1/12). The first ordinary list in either
family begins with an increasing Chebyshev copy Chi_N. Its last two adjacent
steps are

    b_0=csc^2(2theta), b_1=csc^2(theta), theta=pi/(2N+1).

Their exact identification follows from accepted fact `dfde2fa326c908bf`.
Select JUST these two steps as ray checkpoints. Let P be the total preceding
mass and T the total following mass, so the middle ordinary block is empty.
Beginning-zero padding changes neither P nor T. Both families satisfy

    P+1<=M,
    T<=total mass<=(A+3)M,
    A>=4,
    M>=2304A and M>=1152.                               (1)

The mass bound follows from the two lists of mass M-1, bridge AM+1 and
last step either 1 or 1+M^(2/3). For the numerical-free large-M checks,
M>=2^25 and M/A=M^(11/12)>=2^22>2304, while A>=4 because
M>=2^25>4^12.

Since sin(t)<=t and pi^2<10,

    b_1-1>=(2M-1)/10-1>=M/12,
    b_0-1>=(2M-1)/40-1>=M/48.                           (2)

The last inequalities hold for M>=48. Set L_pair=(b_0-1)(b_1-1), so

    L_pair>=M^2/576>=4AM.                               (3)

The exact accepted ray parameters are

    m_0=1/(P+1), m_1=(b_0-1)/(P+1), O_1=P/(P+1),
    z_term=(L_pair-P)/(P+1), m_old=m_0,
    e_term=P/(P+1)^2.

There is no same-ray monotonicity condition on the two nonterminal slopes
m_0,m_1, because each ray has been visited only once. Both are positive.
Moreover

    P+2T+1<=(2A+7)M+1<=4AM<=L_pair.

Consequently q=z_term/(2T+1)>=m_old. Also q<=z_term/(T+1), so it is an
admissible terminal slope. In particular the full old-slope condition
z_term>=(1+T)m_old holds. This checks every feasibility hypothesis of
the accepted ray fact, including its retained remote offset.

Its exact normalized payoff is

    2e_term+z_term^2/(2T+1).

Using (1)--(3),

    z_term >= (M^2/576-M)/M >= M/1152,
    2T+1<=4AM,

so the complete ray functional satisfies

    F_ray_n(h)>=M/(5308416 A)=M^(11/12)/5308416.           (4)

This tends to infinity on BOTH earlier families, including the family
ending with a unit step. It also gives a bound at every padded horizon.
The actual benchmark obeys B_n>=2n+1 by accepted fact `0be8b54e0a33381c`.
For a pointwise check already at N>=4096, n>=6N+2, M>=2N^2 and A<=N^(1/4)
(since M<=5N^2 and N>=5). Thus

    B_n F_ray_n(h)
       >=24N^(11/4)/5308416>1.

For the last inequality N>=2^12 gives its numerator at least24*2^33,
larger than5308416. The ratio diverges with N.

Therefore these examples do NOT demonstrate a geometric witness regime
uncovered by all the project's accepted baseline witnesses. They remain
valid separations from the explicitly listed weaker channels K, Q and
the universal lens, and their exact terminal formulas remain separately
useful. The omission of F_ray must not be used to motivate more work
merely improving the payoff on these same schedules.

The last-unit obstruction for a constant-gradient final block is still a
correctly scoped candidate; it is an obstruction to that selected prefix
and continuation class, not to the full ray adversary on the schedule.

This audit neither refutes the all-schedule target nor supplies an upper
bound on W_n. It identifies a previously unmade comparison against a
verified predecessor and rules out a misleading claim of target-level
novelty for these families.
