author: max
claim: Exact candidate invariant for ONE fixed maximal finite-prefix interpolant: its proximal value F(x)-||grad F(x)||²/2 is an active convex combination of the seed proximal values, at EVERY x. Hence every later unit step caps F by the largest seed height even after arbitrarily many internal gradient changes. Exact convex-roof formula identifies the true minimizer set and gives a quantitative arbitrary-suffix recurrence. Greedy maximal extensions leave the whole function unchanged and cannot create height. A Huber counterexample proves this is not an upper bound for other prefix interpolants or unrestricted W.
evidence:
# Height budgets and a two-checkpoint construction with an arbitrary tail

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof candidate. No new verifier allocation and no
solver call. All new ingredients are proved below in the same document;
unverified earlier findings are not premises. This does not establish the
uniform comparison with the complete sequence B_n.

Verified inputs: fact `1252b8823bb5a290` for smooth-convex interpolation and
the maximal finite-prefix interpolant; fact `1fca3e5dd555cb4a` for the ray
comparison in Section 5. The definitions of W_n, K_n and B_n are those in
fact `b98bb807d514e80d`. Work at smoothness one, minimum zero.

## 1. An invariant of one fixed maximal prefix interpolant

Take finitely many legal jets (x_j,g_j,f_j), including (0,0,0). Define

    y_j=x_j-g_j,       delta_j=f_j-||g_j||^2/2,
    M_seed=max_j delta_j,
    m_seed(v)=max_j(<y_j,v>-delta_j),
    H_seed(v)=||v||^2/2+m_seed(v),
    F_seed(x)=sup_v(<x,v>-H_seed(v)).                       (1)

The accepted fact proves that F_seed is the maximal convex 1-smooth
interpolant of these jets. Each delta_j is nonnegative by interpolation
with the optimum. For every x, put v=grad F_seed(x). Strong conjugate
optimality gives

    x-v=sum_j alpha_j y_j,
    alpha_j>=0, sum_j alpha_j=1,

where positive alpha_j occur only among affine terms active in m_seed(v).
To justify the convex-hull subgradient assertion directly, the directional
derivative of a finite maximum of affine functions is the maximum of the
active slopes in that direction. A vector outside their convex hull can
be strictly separated from that hull and cannot satisfy the subgradient
inequality. Every convex combination of active slopes does satisfy it.
Using their common active value in (1) now gives the exact identity

    F_seed(x)-||grad F_seed(x)||^2/2
        =sum_j alpha_j delta_j in [0,M_seed].              (2)

Thus arbitrary later changes of gradient on this ONE fixed function do
not create a proximal value above the maximum seed value.

There is an equivalent finite convex-roof formula. Let K_seed be the
convex hull of all y_j, and define, for z in K_seed,

    J_roof(z)=min {sum_j alpha_j delta_j:
                  alpha>=0, sum alpha=1, sum alpha_j y_j=z},

and J_roof=+infinity outside K_seed. The coefficient simplex is compact,
so the minima exist; 0<=J_roof<=M_seed on K_seed. Then

    F_seed(x)=min_alpha [sum alpha_j delta_j
                         +||x-sum alpha_j y_j||^2/2].       (3)

For a direct proof, minimize the displayed continuous convex function
over the coefficient simplex and set v=x-sum alpha_j y_j. Its directional
optimality conditions on the simplex say that positive coordinates
minimize delta_j-<y_j,v>. These are exactly the active terms of m_seed(v),
giving equality with (1). This is an identity, not a numerical program.

In particular, with K_zero=conv{y_j:delta_j=0},

    argmin F_seed=K_zero,
    dist(x,K_seed)^2/2 <= F_seed(x)
                         <= dist(x,K_seed)^2/2+M_seed.      (4)

The minimizer identity follows from (3): its two nonnegative summands
vanish exactly when x=sum alpha_j y_j with support on zero-height jets.
It supplies the actual closest-minimizer distance, without substituting
distance to the generally larger set K_seed.

For any GD step t>=0 from x, let x_new=x-t grad F_seed(x). The elementary
smoothness inequality and (2), with delta=F_seed(x)-||grad F_seed(x)||^2/2,
give

    F_seed(x_new)<=delta+(1-t)^2||grad F_seed(x)||^2/2
                  =(1-t)^2 F_seed(x)+[1-(1-t)^2]delta
                  <=(1-t)^2 F_seed(x)
                      +[1-(1-t)^2]_+ M_seed.              (5)

This holds along any nonnegative schedule, irrespective of the number
of gradient changes. A unit step gives F_seed(x_new)<=M_seed. Every
following step in [0,2] preserves that value cap. Iterating (5) gives,
for a suffix t_0,...,t_(r-1), the explicit bound

 F_seed(x_r) <= product_(i<r)(1-t_i)^2 F_seed(x_0)
   +M_seed sum_(j<r)[1-(1-t_j)^2]_+
                         product_(j<i<r)(1-t_i)^2.          (6)

Empty products and sums have their usual meanings.

Greedily adjoining jets of F_seed at new points and recomputing the
maximal interpolant leaves the entire function unchanged. Indeed the
new conjugate quadratic is <=H_seed everywhere, by interpolation of
F_seed with its actual new jet, whereas all old quadratics remain.
Their maximum is therefore still H_seed. In particular such greedy
extensions cannot increase M_seed, by (2).

The scope is essential. The bound does NOT hold for arbitrary other
interpolants of the seed. Seed jets (0,0,0) and (1,1,1/2) have M_seed=0
and maximal interpolant F_seed(x)=x^2/2. The symmetric Huber function

    f_H(x)=x^2/2 for |x|<=1, and |x|-1/2 for |x|>=1

has the same seed. Starting at1 with schedule (R+1,1), R>=2, the maximal
quadratic ends at0, whereas f_H visits -R and -(R-1), with normalized
terminal value 2R-3. Its new proximal height at -R is R-1>0. Hence
creating new height requires a nonmaximal choice of the future function;
the invariant is not an upper bound on the unrestricted W_n.

glossary.F_seed: Pointwise maximal 1-smooth convex interpolant of the fixed finite legal seed jets.
glossary.m_seed: Maximum affine function max_j(<y_j,v>-delta_j) built from seed proximal points and heights.
glossary.K_seed: Convex hull of the seed proximal points y_j.
glossary.K_zero: Convex hull of the seed proximal points with delta_j=0; the exact minimizer set of F_seed.
glossary.J_roof: Minimum convex-combination height above each point of K_seed, extended by infinity outside K_seed.

author: max
claim: New explicit arbitrary-schedule candidate lower bound survives an arbitrary final tail: for ANY i<j with h_i,h_j>1, put A=(h_i-1)/(1+P_i), epsilon=(h_j-1)/(1+S_ij), and T_j=sum after j. One fixed four-plane Moreau envelope in dimension2, with true initial distance1 and all old/new constraints checked, gives W_n(h)>=A² min(epsilon²,epsilon)/[4(1+2T_j)]. No feasibility oracle is used. Exact angle optimization within the cap family is also explicit. A horizon-dependent unit-step-block example separates this functional from the ENTIRE verified F_ray by a factor at least sqrt(M)/12; that example itself is already above the target scale by K, so it is not advertised as resolving the difficult benchmark regime.
evidence:
# Height budgets and a two-checkpoint construction with an arbitrary tail

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof candidate. No new verifier allocation and no
solver call. All new ingredients are proved below in the same document;
unverified earlier findings are not premises. This does not establish the
uniform comparison with the complete sequence B_n.

Verified inputs: fact `1252b8823bb5a290` for smooth-convex interpolation and
the maximal finite-prefix interpolant; fact `1fca3e5dd555cb4a` for the ray
comparison in Section 5. The definitions of W_n, K_n and B_n are those in
fact `b98bb807d514e80d`. Work at smoothness one, minimum zero.

## 2. Fully explicit three-cell construction

Prescribe arbitrary nonnegative lists B_0,B_1,B_2 of respective sums
M_0-1, M_1-1, T, where M_0,M_1>=1 and T>=0. Put two checkpoints between
them:

    h=(B_0, A M_0+1, B_1, 1+M_1 epsilon, B_2),
    A>0, epsilon>0.                                      (7)

Their entries can be arbitrarily large individually; only their actual
partial sums are used. Select any kappa satisfying

    0<kappa<A,             kappa(1+epsilon)<=A.             (8)

In R^2, write

    a=1-1/M_0,
    nu=sqrt(kappa(A-kappa)),
    p=(1,0)/M_0,              q=(-kappa,nu)/M_1,
    X=(-A,0),                y=X-M_1 q=(kappa-A,-nu),
    d=-M_1 q=(kappa,-nu),     e=(a,0)-y,
    D=||e||^2=(A-kappa)(A+2a)+a^2>0,
    w=d-(a kappa/D)e,
    W_sq=||w||^2=A kappa-a^2 kappa^2/D,
    lambda_cap=epsilon/(2T+1),
    r_cap=lambda_cap w.                                  (9)

The following products are exact:

    <d,y>=0, <d,e>=a kappa, <y,e>=-(A-kappa)(A+a),
    <e,w>=0, <d,w>=W_sq, <q,w>=-W_sq/M_1,
    w_1=kappa(A-kappa)(A+a)/D>0,
    <y,w>=a kappa(A-kappa)(A+a)/D>=0.                     (10)

Here w_1 denotes the first coordinate, not a time index. Define ONE
fixed nonsmooth convex function and its Moreau envelope by

    J_cap(z)=max(0,<p,z>,<q,z>,<r_cap,z-y>),
    f_cap(x)=min_z[J_cap(z)+||x-z||^2/2],   x_init=(1,0).   (11)

All four planes are chosen before running the entire supplied schedule.
The fourth plane has intercept -<r_cap,y><=0; this intercept is retained.

For completeness, this envelope is convex, differentiable and 1-smooth.
The strictly convex coercive minimization has a unique proximal point
z(x); optimality says g(x)=x-z(x) belongs to the subgradient of J_cap
there. Monotonicity of subgradients at two points gives
<g(x)-g(x'),x-x'> >= ||g(x)-g(x')||^2. Thus g is 1-Lipschitz. The
two minimizing inequalities show that it is the derivative of the
envelope, and joint convexity followed by minimization proves convexity.
An active affine-plane slope at z is a subgradient, so it suffices below
to check activation at x=z+that slope.

### First block and first checkpoint

For partial ordinary sum u in [0,M_0-1], propose gradient p and proximal
point z=(1-(u+1)/M_0,0). Its first coordinate lies in [0,a]. The p-plane
is nonnegative, and the q-plane is nonpositive. Since <e,w>=0,

    <r_cap,z-y>=lambda_cap (z_1-a)w_1<=0.

Thus p is active at every actual sample, including the first checkpoint
query at x=p. That checkpoint sends the iterate exactly to X=(-A,0).

### Second block and second checkpoint

For t=u+1 in [1,M_1], propose gradient q and proximal point X-tq.
It equals y+(M_1-t)q. The q-height is

    <q,X-tq>=(A kappa/M_1)(1-t/M_1)>=0.

The excess of q over p is affine in t, with endpoints controlled by
its value at t=M_1:

    <q-p,X-tq>=A kappa/M_1+A/M_0
                         -t(A kappa/M_1^2+kappa/(M_0 M_1))
                   >=(A-kappa)/M_0>0.

The fourth plane has value

    <r_cap,X-tq-y>
       =-lambda_cap(M_1-t)W_sq/M_1<=0.

All old and future plane comparisons therefore hold at every sample.
The position at the second checkpoint is y+q. Its step 1+M_1 epsilon
sends the trajectory to

    x_C=y+epsilon d.                                     (12)

### Arbitrary final list

For every partial tail sum u in [0,T], propose gradient r_cap. Its
proximal point is

    Z(u)=y+epsilon d-(u+1)lambda_cap w.

The fourth plane there has nonnegative value

    <r_cap,Z(u)-y>
       =lambda_cap[epsilon-(u+1)lambda_cap]W_sq>=0,         (13)

because (u+1)/(2T+1)<=1. The p-plane is nonpositive since

    M_0<p,Z(u)>
       =kappa-A+epsilon kappa-(u+1)lambda_cap w_1<=0

by (8) and w_1>0. The q-plane is also nonpositive:

    M_1<q,Z(u)>=-epsilon A kappa
                         +(u+1)lambda_cap W_sq<=0,

using W_sq<=A kappa and (u+1)lambda_cap<=epsilon. Thus the fourth
plane is active throughout the entire final list, including its endpoint.
This checks all directions of every old/new comparison using the same J_cap.

### Exact value, boundary gradients and true normalization

At the terminal point x_C-T r_cap, adding half the squared gradient to
(13) gives

    2 f_cap(x_n)=epsilon^2 W_sq/(2T+1).                   (14)

The actual squared gradients are

    ||p||^2=1/M_0^2,
    ||q||^2=A kappa/M_1^2,
    ||r_cap||^2=epsilon^2 W_sq/(2T+1)^2.                  (15)

The terminal proximal value is exactly

    delta_end=T epsilon^2 W_sq/(2T+1)^2.                 (16)

The fresh component of q has squared norm kappa(A-kappa)/M_1^2; it
has not been dropped from any norm or scale calculation. The construction
retains an explicitly positive value budget when T>0, in contrast to a
pure quadratic terminal completion followed by a unit-step reset.

The origin is a minimizer: its p- and q-planes are zero and its fourth
plane is <=0 by (10). The minimum of J_cap and its envelope is zero.
Every minimizer z of J_cap satisfies <p,z><=0, hence z_1<=0. A minimizer
of the envelope is exactly a minimizer of J_cap, since both terms in
its defining minimum are nonnegative. Therefore the closest minimizer
to x_init=(1,0) is genuinely the origin, at distance exactly one.
Equation (14) is consequently the required normalized objective, not
an evaluation using an arbitrarily distant optimum.

All endpoints M_0=1, M_1=1 and T=0 are included. In particular a=0
causes no singularity because 0<kappa<A makes D>0. Zero steps duplicate
queries and have no effect on the proof. No parameter limit is hidden.

## 3. A schedule functional with no feasibility oracle

For any nonnegative schedule h of length n and any i<j with h_i>1,
h_j>1, define

    P_i=sum_(t<i) h_t,
    S_ij=sum_(i<t<j) h_t,
    T_j=sum_(j<t<n) h_t,
    A_ij=(h_i-1)/(1+P_i),
    epsilon_ij=(h_j-1)/(1+S_ij).

Choose explicitly

    kappa=A_ij/[2 max(1,epsilon_ij)].                      (17)

It is positive, at most A_ij/2, and satisfies (8), because
1+epsilon<=2max(1,epsilon). From D>=a^2 one has

    W_sq>=A kappa-kappa^2>=A kappa/2.

Thus (14) yields, for EVERY eligible pair,

 W_n(h) >= A_ij^2 min(epsilon_ij^2,epsilon_ij)
                                      /[4(1+2T_j)].       (18)

Define C_n^tail(h) to be the maximum of the right side over all eligible
pairs, with zero when there are none. The construction proves the new
candidate universal lower bound

    W_n(h)>=max(K_n(h), C_n^tail(h)).                      (19)

The pair selection is adversary selection before the run; there are no
unproved existence parameters and no changes to the supplied schedule.
Unlike a product term tied to h_(n-1), C_n^tail need not vanish when the
last step is one. Arbitrarily long, nonperiodic final lists are covered
with their exact mass loss 1+2T_j. No assertion that (19) matches 1/B_n
uniformly is made.

## 4. Exact optimization within the displayed cap directions

For fixed A>0, a>=0, epsilon>0, T>=0, all directions satisfying (8)
are admissible in the preceding proof. The exact score is proportional
to

    W_sq(kappa)=A kappa-a^2 kappa^2/
                         [(A-kappa)(A+2a)+a^2].            (20)

If a=0, this is A kappa, so its maximum on the admissible interval is
at kappa=A/(1+epsilon). If a>0, differentiation with the positive
denominator gives

    W_sq'(kappa)=A-a^2 kappa[2D+(A+2a)kappa]/D^2.

Put b=A+2a and C=(A+a)^2, so D=C-b kappa. Expanding its numerator
factorizes as

    D^2 W_sq'(kappa)
        =(A+a)^2 [A(A+a)-b kappa]
                       [(A+a)-kappa].                    (21)

The second bracket is positive for kappa<A. Hence the unique unconstrained
maximizer in (0,A) is

    kappa_0=A(A+a)/(A+2a).

Its squared direction norm is W_sq(kappa_0)=kappa_0^2. The exact optimum
within the explicitly checked cap family is consequently

    kappa_opt=min(kappa_0,A/(1+epsilon)) for a>0,
    kappa_opt=A/(1+epsilon) for a=0.                       (22)

At the feasibility endpoint, kappa(1+epsilon)=A, the old p-plane is
still dominated, by the nonnegative subtraction in its comparison. The
optimization therefore has no open-boundary loss. This is an optimum
only within this displayed family of cap planes, not over all prefixes
or all legal interpolants.

## 5. A strict comparison with the entire verified ray functional

The following family establishes that (18) contains information absent
from F_ray, although the schedules are already above the target scale
by the single-cut witness and hence do not solve the hard regime.

Let an integer M>=16 be given, A=M^(1/8), epsilon=M^(-1/4), and choose

    h=(1 repeated M-1 times, A M+1,
       1 repeated M-1 times, 1+M epsilon, 1).              (23)

Only its two large checkpoints have entries >1, so the verified ray
construction can select at most those two: a selected first checkpoint
must exceed1, and every later selected checkpoint must also exceed1
because positive new gradient magnitude requires (b-1)m>O>=0.
If both are chosen, its exact z_term is

    z_term=A epsilon-(M-1)/M
          =M^(-1/8)-1+1/M<0.                             (24)

Indeed M^(-1/8)<=1/sqrt(2)<3/4 and 1/M<=1/16. Thus this pair is
infeasible even before its terminal old-slope constraint. Every feasible
ray witness has at most one cut, and fact 1fca3e5dd555cb4a gives exactly

    F_ray_n(h)=K_n(h).

The global Huber term is <=1/M. The first cut contributes
A^2/[1+2(M-1+1+M epsilon+1)]<=A^2/(2M). At the second cut,
one plus the prefix mass is (A+2)M and the tail has sum1, so its value is
epsilon^2/[3(A+2)^2]<=M^(-3/4)/3. Thus

    F_ray_n(h)=K_n(h)<=M^(-3/4).                          (25)

The new cap, with T=1, has from (18)

    2f_cap(x_n)>=A^2 epsilon^2/12=M^(-1/4)/12.             (26)

Its ratio to the complete ray functional is at least sqrt(M)/12 and
tends to infinity, with a genuinely unit final step and exact distance1.
This comparison is deliberately scoped: n=2M+1, so (25) itself does
not establish that F_ray is below the project benchmark. No such claim
is used to market this family as a new solution of the all-schedule gap.

## Remaining interface

The invariant (2) identifies a structural limitation of repeatedly using
one maximal interpolant. The new fourth plane explicitly creates the
proximal value needed to survive an arbitrary tail, and (18) gives its
quantitative schedule cost without unspecified feasible parameters.
The missing target-level step is still to compare a sufficiently rich
legal construction uniformly against the complete sequence B_n.

Remark2 and its preceding interpolation proof, was read for context;
all identities used above are proved from the accepted project fact and
the displayed elementary constructions, not from an external black box.

author: max4
claim: Strict local obstruction at the three-step silver tail, even with unbounded signed terminal credit: some neighborhood of h=(sqrt2,2,sqrt2) contains no distinct schedule of equal or larger capacity whose E_theta is universally nonnegative, for ANY theta. Four explicit legal core-ended witnesses have every Q_(i,terminal)=0; their exact first-order cone rules out every nonzero direction of nonnegative capacity change. evidence:
# Three-step silver is locally maximal even with arbitrary terminal credit

Status: complete self-contained candidate, NOT verifier-accepted. No numerical
PEP evaluation or fact_submit. The only accepted predecessor is
1252b8823bb5a290, used for finite smooth-convex interpolation of one explicitly
checked two-dimensional data array. This is a finite local obstruction, not
the unrestricted asymptotic minimax theorem.

## 1. Statement and definitions

For a positive three-step schedule h=(u,v,w), put s=u+v+w and T=1+s.
On any actual convex differentiable 1-smooth GD trajectory define

  Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
  V_h=2sum_(i<3)h_i(f_i-f_3)+sum_(i<3)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                               -sT||g_3||^2,
  E_theta(h)=V_h-theta sum_(i<3)h_i Q_(i,3).

Let t=sqrt(2), lambda=1+t, and h_S=(t,2,t), whose capacity is
T_S=3+2t=lambda^2.

There exists epsilon_0>0 such that, for every positive h satisfying

  0<||h-h_S||<epsilon_0,  T>=T_S,

one of four explicit legal witnesses below has V_h<0 and Q_(i,3)=0 for
all i<3. In particular E_theta(h)<0 on that same witness for EVERY real
theta. This excludes not only the bounded terminal-credit state but every
PSD intrinsic certificate with arbitrary signed incoming-terminal
multipliers and nonnegative multipliers on the other actual inequalities.

For each theta>=0 it follows that h_S is a strict local capacity
maximizer in the E_theta class, and also in the class of certificates
allowing arbitrary signed incoming-terminal multipliers. No claim of
global optimality among all three-step schedules or of the project's
all-horizon result is made.

## 2. Core-ended equality data and its energy

Suppose a finite legal GD transcript has optimum (0,0,0), and

  f_i=<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2 for all i,  x_3=g_3.

Put y_i=x_i-g_i. Direct expansion gives

  Q_ij=<g_i-g_j,y_j>,  Q_(i,3)=0,
  V_h=||x_0||^2-T^2||g_3||^2.                          (1)

The energy identity follows by telescoping squared distances and
substituting the displayed value formula. All four witnesses below have
these properties, so all their incoming-terminal interpolation slacks
vanish exactly.

For convenience put

  a=u-1, A=u+1, r=v-1, D=w+1, eta=r/D.

Restrict to a sufficiently small fixed open neighborhood of h_S in which
u,v,w>1, eta a<1, and 0<r(w-1)<1. These strict conditions hold at h_S.

## 3. Four actual witness inequalities

If V_h is nonnegative on every witness in this section, the following
four smooth scalar expressions must be nonnegative:

  F_Q=1-T^2(u-1)^2(v-1)^2(w-1)^2,
  F_B=A^2-T^2 eta^2,
  F_C=A^2-T^2 r^2(w-1)^2,
  F_N=a u F_B+(1+eta)u^2(2-u^2).                     (2)

Each vanishes at h_S.

Q witness. Use f(x)=x^2/2, x_0=1. Its final gradient is
-(u-1)(v-1)(w-1), and (1) gives V_h=F_Q.

B witness. Integrate f'(x)=min(1,max(x,-eta)) with f(0)=0, and start
at x_0=A. The points and gradients are

  x=(A,1,-r,-eta),  g=(1,1,-eta,-eta).

They obey the given three steps and the value/core conditions in (1),
so V_h=F_B. The derivative is continuous, monotone, and 1-Lipschitz.

C witness. Integrate f'(x)=min(x,1) with f(0)=0, and start at x_0=A.
The points and gradients are

  x=(A,1,-r,r(w-1)),  g=(1,1,-r,r(w-1)).

The last point lies in (0,1) by the neighborhood restriction. The
function is convex differentiable 1-smooth, minimized at 0, and obeys
(1), so V_h=F_C.

N witness. Start with the B data as a scalar base array. Define a second
scalar array, not assumed interpolable by itself, by

  x_aux=(1,-a,r a,eta a),  g_aux=(1,-a,eta a,eta a),
  f_aux,i=g_aux,i*x_aux,i-g_aux,i^2/2.

All three GD equations hold. The first two auxiliary proximal points
are zero, the third is w eta a, and the fourth is zero. Consequently
the only positive auxiliary finite residual is

  Q_aux,(0,2)=(1-eta a)w eta a.

Indeed all edges into queries 0,1,3 have zero target proximal point;
the edge 1->2 is negative and 3->2 is zero. Both optimum directions
are also valid, since every g_aux,i*y_aux,i is nonnegative.
For the base array, the same edge has
Q_base,(0,2)=-(1+eta)w eta.

Set the explicit positive coefficient

  epsilon_mix=(1+eta)/[a(1-eta a)]

and combine the arrays orthogonally:

  X_i=(x_base,i,sqrt(epsilon_mix)x_aux,i),
  G_i=(g_base,i,sqrt(epsilon_mix)g_aux,i),
  F_i=f_base,i+epsilon_mix f_aux,i.

Every residual is the corresponding base residual plus epsilon_mix
times the auxiliary one. The sole potentially positive edge is exactly
canceled; every other finite edge is nonpositive. The optimum jet is
zero, all incoming optimum residuals vanish, and all outgoing optimum
residuals are nonpositive by the preceding proximal-point check.

Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290, proof section2, supplies one fixed globally
convex differentiable 1-smooth interpolating function. More explicitly,
with indices including the zero optimum, let

  c_i=<G_i,X_i>-F_i,
  H(z)=max_i[c_i+<X_i,z-G_i>+||z-G_i||^2/2],
  F(X)=sup_z[<X,z>-H(z)].

The accepted interpolation construction gives F(X_i)=F_i,
grad F(X_i)=G_i and F(0)=0=min F. Thus this is a legal fixed function,
not merely an oracle data proposal. The combined array still obeys
X_3=G_3 and the value formula in (1). Its energy is

  V_mix=F_B+epsilon_mix(1-T^2 eta^2 a^2)
       =F_N/[a(1-eta a)].                             (3)

For the last equality, multiply by a(1-eta a) and use
A=a+2, u=a+1 and 1-A^2a^2=u^2(2-u^2). The resulting numerator is
a u(A^2-T^2 eta^2)+(1+eta)(1-A^2a^2), exactly F_N.
Its denominator is positive. Thus F_N<0 gives the claimed legal
negative-energy witness, with all incoming-terminal Q zero.

## 4. The first-order feasible cone has strictly negative capacity change

Let d=(d_u,d_v,d_w) be a direction at h_S. Put

  p=d_u+d_w, q=d_v, sigma=p+q.

If all four directional derivatives of the expressions in (2) are
nonnegative, the Q and B derivatives imply, respectively,

  q<=-(3+t)p/2,
  q<=(t-1)p/2.                                      (4)

Here is the calculation. Differentiating F_Q at its zero value gives

  dF_Q=-2[lambda p+q+(p+q)/lambda^2],

and (lambda+lambda^(-2))/(1+lambda^(-2))=(3+t)/2.
Differentiating F_B gives

  dF_B=2[t p-(1+lambda^2)q],

and t/(1+lambda^2)=(t-1)/2. These are precisely (4).

Suppose also sigma>=0. If p>0, the first bound in (4) implies
sigma<=-(1+t)p/2<0, a contradiction. If p<0, the second implies
sigma<=(1+t)p/2<0, also a contradiction. Thus p=0 and q=0.
Write d_u=e,d_w=-e.

The C derivative in this remaining direction is

  dF_C=2lambda(1+lambda^2)e,

so nonnegativity forces e>=0. Since dF_B=0 and both F_B and
u^2(2-u^2) vanish at h_S, differentiating F_N gives

  dF_N=(1+eta_S)[-4t e]=-8e,

where eta_S=1/lambda and 1+1/lambda=t. Hence e<=0 too. Consequently
d=0. The only direction with all four derivatives nonnegative and
nonnegative capacity change is the zero direction.

## 5. Turning the cone calculation into an actual local theorem

If the stated neighborhood did not exist, there would be a sequence
h_k!=h_S converging to h_S with capacity at least T_S and all four
F_Q,F_B,F_C,F_N nonnegative. Define

  d_k=(h_k-h_S)/||h_k-h_S||.

A subsequence converges to a unit vector d. Differentiability of each
F at h_S and F(h_S)=0 imply grad F(h_S) dot d>=0 after dividing by
||h_k-h_S||. The capacity condition similarly gives
d_u+d_v+d_w>=0. Section4 forces d=0, contradicting ||d||=1.

Therefore some epsilon_0 exists. For any h in the asserted punctured
neighborhood with capacity at least T_S, at least one of the four
expressions in (2) is negative. Select its corresponding witness in
Section3. It is legal, has V_h<0, and has Q_(i,3)=0 for all i<3.
This proves the statement for every theta simultaneously.

Finally, for a putative PSD intrinsic identity with arbitrary signed
coefficients only on incoming-terminal edges, evaluation on that
witness makes all signed terms zero. Every other coefficient is
nonnegative and multiplies Q<=0. The PSD expression would therefore
be at most V_h<0, impossible. This verifies the stronger certificate
scope directly, without a dual-attainment assertion.

To check that h_S itself belongs to the classes called locally maximal,
the following explicit nonnegative multipliers give a zero remainder:

  lambda_01=2, lambda_10=2lambda,
  lambda_21=2t lambda, lambda_31=lambda_13=2lambda,
  lambda_23=2lambda^2+2t lambda, lambda_32=2lambda^3,

and every unlisted multiplier is zero. Expansion using t^2=2 gives
V_(h_S)+sum lambda_ij Q_ij=0. Thus V_(h_S)>=0 on all legal trajectories;
for theta>=0, the nonpositive incoming-terminal sum gives
E_theta(h_S)>=V_(h_S)>=0. No such membership assertion is needed or
made for negative theta.

## Scope for the project

This blocks a local perturbation repair of the three-step silver tail
by the new signed terminal-interpolation state, even with unbounded
credit. It does not show that a distant three-step tail, a longer tail,
or another full value/moment state is impossible. It does not turn
intrinsic energy into the original objective ratio; the changed
normalizations in these hard functions are used only to test V_h.

evidence:
# Projection capacity calibration and an exponential false-positive family

Status: complete candidate calculations, NOT verifier-accepted. No solver or
fact_submit. All new ingredients are proved below. Accepted fact
1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the smooth-convex interpolation inequalities;
b98bb807d514e80d supplies only the named exact benchmark recursion.
This is a capacity test, not a proof of the all-length capacity conjecture.

For a nonnegative schedule h of length n, put S=sum h_i, D=1+S, and

    V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)
       +sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-SD||g_n||^2.

Primitive means V_h>=0 on every actual convex differentiable 1-smooth
GD run. All witnesses and certificates below use the physical steps.

## 1. Exact projection witnesses give two necessary tests

For any compact interval C containing zero, the function
F_C(x)=max_(v in C)(xv-v^2/2) is convex, differentiable and 1-smooth,
with derivative equal to the nearest-point projection onto C. This follows
by completing the square; the projection normal inequality gives its
1-Lipschitz property. At every actual sample, f_i=x_i g_i-g_i^2/2.
The squared-distance telescope therefore gives exactly

    V_h=x_0^2-(x_n+Sg_n)^2.                           (1)

Choose one checkpoint b=h_j>1. Put
A=1+sum_(i<j)h_i, B=1+sum_(i>j)h_i, so D=A+B+b-1.
Choose u>0, v=(b-1)u/B, C=[-v,u], and x_0=A u.
Every preceding ordinary step stays on the positive plateau, with
gradient u, and the checkpoint input is exactly u. Its output is
-(b-1)u=-Bv. Every following ordinary step stays on the negative plateau,
with gradient -v, and the final point is -v. All function values are
those of the ONE fixed projection function, so (1) gives

    V_h=A^2u^2-D^2(b-1)^2u^2/B^2.

Thus every primitive schedule satisfies the exact cut conditions

    D(h_j-1)_+ <= (1+sum_(i<j)h_i)(1+sum_(i>j)h_i).   (2)

There is a second projection witness: start the scalar unit quadratic
at1 and let x_i=product_(t<i)(1-h_t). A compact interval containing zero
and ALL these finitely many points has projection gradient g_i=x_i at
every sample and the same values x_i^2/2. Therefore every primitive h has

    D |product_(i<n)(1-h_i)| <=1.                    (3)

Condition (3) tests curvature1 only, not all curvatures.

## 2. Exact two-step capacity upper bound

For any primitive h=(h_0,h_1), (2) gives

    h_0,h_1 <= M_D:=2D/(D+1),  D=1+h_0+h_1.          (4)

If a step is at most1 this is automatic; otherwise rearrange its own
cut inequality D(h_i-1)<=D-h_i.
Let D_two be the unique root larger than4 of

    D_two^4-4D_two^3-1=0.                            (5)

We claim D<=D_two. There is nothing to prove if D<4. For D>=4,
(4) and h_0+h_1=D-1 imply both steps lie in
[L_D,M_D], where L_D=D-1-M_D>1. The function
(x-1)(D-2-x) is concave and has the same value at these two endpoints.
Consequently

    (h_0-1)(h_1-1)
      >= (M_D-1)(L_D-1)
      = (D-1)(D^2-3D-2)/(D+1)^2.

Multiplying by D and applying (3) yields

    D(D-1)(D^2-3D-2)<=(D+1)^2,

which is precisely D^4-4D^3-1<=0. The polynomial is strictly increasing
for D>3, negative at4 and positive at5, proving (5)'s uniqueness and
the claimed upper bound.

## 3. An explicit full certificate attains that bound

Put b=sqrt(2) and let a be the positive root of

    a^2+ba=2+2b,
    a=(-b+sqrt(10+8b))/2.

Then 1<a<2. Set S=a+b and L_cert=S(2-b)>0. On the two-step schedule
(a,b), use Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2. The following
is an identity on the FULL formal three-gradient space:

    V_(a,b) = sum_(i!=j) lambda_ij (-Q_ij),          (6)

where

    lambda_01=0,
    lambda_10=b L_cert,
    lambda_02=(a-1)L_cert,
    lambda_20=L_cert,
    lambda_21=S(S+b),
    lambda_12=(b-1)lambda_21+b L_cert.

All coefficients are nonnegative, so accepted interpolation necessity
Q_ij<=0 proves primitive validity in every finite dimension.

Here is a full coefficient check. Write u=g_0,v=g_1,w=g_2 and use
x_1=x_0-a u, x_2=x_0-a u-b v. The five residuals used in (6) are

    Q_10=f_1-f_0+(||u||^2+||v||^2)/2+(a-1)<u,v>,
    Q_02=f_0-f_2+(1/2-a)||u||^2+||w||^2/2
                                      -b<u,v>-<u,w>,
    Q_20=f_2-f_0+(||u||^2+||w||^2)/2
                                      +(a-1)<u,w>+b<v,w>,
    Q_12=f_1-f_2+(1/2-b)||v||^2+||w||^2/2-<v,w>,
    Q_21=f_2-f_1+(||v||^2+||w||^2)/2+(b-1)<v,w>.

The three mixed-gradient coefficients cancel directly from the displayed
lambdas. The function coefficients are 2a,2b,-2S: use
(b+2-a)L_cert=2a and (2-b)S(S-b)=2b, both consequences of
aS=2+2b and b^2=2. The squared-gradient coefficients are

    ||u||^2: (a-1)^2 L_cert-a=a(1-a),
    ||v||^2: (2-3b/2)S(S+b)+b(b-1)L_cert=b(1-b),
    ||w||^2: -[aL_cert+bS(S+b)+bL_cert]/2=-S(S+1).

For the first equality, expanding (a-1)^2 S(2-b) using aS=2+2b
gives 2a-a^2. For the second, divide by S; the constant terms cancel
and the result is a(2-3b/2), whose product with S is b-2=b(1-b).
The third uses b^2=2. This verifies every coefficient in (6).

Let D=1+a+b. Then D(a-1)=1+b and
D(a-1)(b-1)=b^2-1=1. Also a=2D/(D+1), so equality holds throughout
the bound in section2. Finally a>3-b because the defining polynomial
at 3-b equals 7-5sqrt(2)<0. Thus D>4 and D=D_two. Explicitly,

    D_two=[2+sqrt(2)+sqrt(10+8sqrt(2))]/2
         =Omega(1,1+sqrt(2)).                        (7)

The last expression uses the exact primitive join notation from
accepted fact b98bb807d514e80d. Equations (2)--(7) give an analytic
capacity bound and an attaining universal certificate, not an SDP result.
This is a two-step calibration, not a new all-length capacity claim.

## 4. Cut tests plus curvature1 admit exponentially large false positives

Fix r_geom=3/2. For each integer k>=1 put

    u_i=(r_geom-1)r_geom^i=(1/2)(3/2)^i, 0<=i<k,
    h^(k)=(u_0,u_1,...,u_(k-1),1,u_(k-1),...,u_1,u_0).

Its length is n=2k+1 and its exact physical capacity is

    D=1+sum h^(k)=2 r_geom^k.                         (8)

Every cut condition (2) holds STRICTLY. For a left-half step, put
A=r_geom^i, b=(r_geom-1)A. The other mass is B=D-r_geom A+1.
Since A<=r_geom^(k-1)=D/(2r_geom),

    AB-D(b-1)
      =D[(2-r_geom)A+1]-r_geom A^2+A
      >=D[(3/2-r_geom)A+1]+A=D+A>0.

The mirror cut has the same two masses interchanged. The center step1
has zero left side in (2); steps below1 also satisfy it trivially.
Condition (3) holds with product ZERO because of that center step.

Nevertheless these schedules are not primitive for every k>=15. This
can be shown on the ONE fixed scalar quadratic f(x)=x^2/4, starting at1.
Its curvature is lambda=1/2, and its final iterate is

    x_n=(1/2)[product_(i=0)^(k-1)(1-r_geom^i/4)]^2.    (9)

None of these factors is zero. For i=0,...,5 the product of their
absolute values is exactly

    C_6=(3/4)(5/8)(7/16)(5/32)(17/64)(115/128)
       =1026375/134217728 > 1/256.

For i>=6, r_geom^i/4>=729/256>2, so

    |1-r_geom^i/4|>=r_geom^i/8>=729/512>sqrt(2),

where the last strict comparison is 729^2>2*512^2. Hence for k>=6,

    x_n > (1/2)(1/256)^2 2^(k-6)=2^(k-23),
    D |g_n|=r_geom^k x_n > 3^k/2^23.                 (10)

For k>=15 this exceeds1, since 3^15=14348907>8388608=2^23.

To check that (10) really forces primitive failure, for any legal
smooth-convex data with minimizer0 put
I_i=<g_i,x_i>-f_i-||g_i||^2/2>=0. A direct telescope gives

    V_h=||x_0||^2-||x_n||^2-2sum h_i I_i
                         -2S f_n-S(S+1)||g_n||^2.

Smoothness and convexity give ||x_n||>=||g_n|| and
2f_n>=||g_n||^2. Thus

    V_h<=||x_0||^2-D^2||g_n||^2.                     (11)

Equation (10) makes (11) negative for the explicit quadratic run.
All steps and function values are actual; the failure is not a relaxed
gradient assignment. Capacity (8) grows exponentially with n, so (2)
and (3) alone cannot establish ANY polynomial capacity upper bound.

This refutes only the cut-plus-curvature1 filter. The curvature1/2 test
explicitly detects the family. It makes no insufficiency claim about
the entire quadratic class, and does not propose a primitive schedule
above the silver-power threshold.

## 5. These scalar defects also have finite simplex projection witnesses

For completeness, the negative energy just established can be placed
inside the requested projection class by finite operations, without
using the unverified C27 reduction as a premise. This also explains why
projection witnesses can detect a failure not detected by (2) or (3).

Given this length n schedule and its negative quadratic energy -v_def,
take an auxiliary diagonal quadratic with eigenvalues
theta_l=(l+1)/(2(n+2)), l=0,...,n, started with all coordinates1.
Its n+1 gradients are independent because the polynomials
P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z) have distinct degrees0,...,n; evaluation
at n+1 distinct theta_l, followed by nonzero row scaling theta_l, is
invertible. All distinct auxiliary Q_ij are strictly negative: they
equal minus one half the A_aux(I-A_aux) squared norm of the sample
position difference, and the relevant polynomial difference cannot
vanish at n+1 distinct nodes.

Let E_aux be its finite energy. Add it in orthogonal coordinates with
squared scale epsilon=v_def/[2(v_def+|E_aux|)]. The product function
is an actual 1-smooth convex function, its new energy is at most
-v_def/2, all new gradients are independent, and all finite Q_ij<0.
Rename these mixed jets x_i,g_i,f_i and their positive definite gradient
Gram matrix A_gram. Choose

    f_*=min_i(f_i-||g_i||^2/2)-1,
    r_i=f_*-f_i+<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2,
    z_*=sum_j(A_gram^(-1)r)_j g_j.

Then X_i=x_i-z_* and F_i=f_i-f_* satisfy
F_i=<g_i,X_i>-||g_i||^2/2. Every finite residual is unchanged and
equals <X_j-g_j,g_i-g_j><0. The comparison with vertex zero is
<X_i-g_i,-g_i>=-(F_i-||g_i||^2/2)<=-1. These are ALL normal
inequalities for C=conv{0,g_0,...,g_n}, proving P_C(X_i)=g_i and
F_C(X_i)=F_i. Translation and the common value shift leave energy
unchanged. Projection onto the gradient span places this simplex
and its trajectory in dimension n+1 with exactly n+2 vertices.

Thus every k>=15 in (8) has an explicit finite simplex projection
counterexample. This construction preserves the negative sign and
retains every queried vertex, but not normalized objective error.

## Scope and the next missing ingredient

The exact two-step optimum and the exponential false-positive family
are quantitative consequences of actual geometric tests. They identify
precisely why extrapolating the two-step cut/product proof cannot work
at arbitrary length. A general capacity argument must use additional
curvatures or additional coupled simplex normal inequalities. No
unproved inequality with silver exponent is used anywhere above.

claim: Complete global classification candidate for the entire fixed-middle-step family: for h=(u,2,w) with u,w>=0, universal nonnegativity of E_theta for ANY real theta forces u=w=sqrt(2). More generally every other member has an actual core-ended smooth-convex witness with all incoming-terminal Q zero and negative primitive energy, excluding even arbitrary signed terminal multipliers. evidence:
# Three-step silver is locally maximal even with arbitrary terminal credit

Status: complete self-contained candidate, NOT verifier-accepted. No numerical
PEP evaluation or fact_submit. The only accepted predecessor is
1252b8823bb5a290, used for finite smooth-convex interpolation of one explicitly
checked two-dimensional data array. This is a finite local obstruction, not
the unrestricted asymptotic minimax theorem.

## 1. Statement and definitions

For a positive three-step schedule h=(u,v,w), put s=u+v+w and T=1+s.
On any actual convex differentiable 1-smooth GD trajectory define

  Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
  V_h=2sum_(i<3)h_i(f_i-f_3)+sum_(i<3)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                               -sT||g_3||^2,
  E_theta(h)=V_h-theta sum_(i<3)h_i Q_(i,3).

Let t=sqrt(2), lambda=1+t, and h_S=(t,2,t), whose capacity is
T_S=3+2t=lambda^2.

There exists epsilon_0>0 such that, for every positive h satisfying

  0<||h-h_S||<epsilon_0,  T>=T_S,

one of four explicit legal witnesses below has V_h<0 and Q_(i,3)=0 for
all i<3. In particular E_theta(h)<0 on that same witness for EVERY real
theta. This excludes not only the bounded terminal-credit state but every
PSD intrinsic certificate with arbitrary signed incoming-terminal
multipliers and nonnegative multipliers on the other actual inequalities.

For each theta>=0 it follows that h_S is a strict local capacity
maximizer in the E_theta class, and also in the class of certificates
allowing arbitrary signed incoming-terminal multipliers. No claim of
global optimality among all three-step schedules or of the project's
all-horizon result is made.

## 2. Core-ended equality data and its energy

Suppose a finite legal GD transcript has optimum (0,0,0), and

  f_i=<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2 for all i,  x_3=g_3.

Put y_i=x_i-g_i. Direct expansion gives

  Q_ij=<g_i-g_j,y_j>,  Q_(i,3)=0,
  V_h=||x_0||^2-T^2||g_3||^2.                          (1)

The energy identity follows by telescoping squared distances and
substituting the displayed value formula. All four witnesses below have
these properties, so all their incoming-terminal interpolation slacks
vanish exactly.

For convenience put

  a=u-1, A=u+1, r=v-1, D=w+1, eta=r/D.

Restrict to a sufficiently small fixed open neighborhood of h_S in which
u,v,w>1, eta a<1, and 0<r(w-1)<1. These strict conditions hold at h_S.

## 3. Four actual witness inequalities

If V_h is nonnegative on every witness in this section, the following
four smooth scalar expressions must be nonnegative:

  F_Q=1-T^2(u-1)^2(v-1)^2(w-1)^2,
  F_B=A^2-T^2 eta^2,
  F_C=A^2-T^2 r^2(w-1)^2,
  F_N=a u F_B+(1+eta)u^2(2-u^2).                     (2)

Each vanishes at h_S.

Q witness. Use f(x)=x^2/2, x_0=1. Its final gradient is
-(u-1)(v-1)(w-1), and (1) gives V_h=F_Q.

B witness. Integrate f'(x)=min(1,max(x,-eta)) with f(0)=0, and start
at x_0=A. The points and gradients are

  x=(A,1,-r,-eta),  g=(1,1,-eta,-eta).

They obey the given three steps and the value/core conditions in (1),
so V_h=F_B. The derivative is continuous, monotone, and 1-Lipschitz.

C witness. Integrate f'(x)=min(x,1) with f(0)=0, and start at x_0=A.
The points and gradients are

  x=(A,1,-r,r(w-1)),  g=(1,1,-r,r(w-1)).

The last point lies in (0,1) by the neighborhood restriction. The
function is convex differentiable 1-smooth, minimized at 0, and obeys
(1), so V_h=F_C.

N witness. Start with the B data as a scalar base array. Define a second
scalar array, not assumed interpolable by itself, by

  x_aux=(1,-a,r a,eta a),  g_aux=(1,-a,eta a,eta a),
  f_aux,i=g_aux,i*x_aux,i-g_aux,i^2/2.

All three GD equations hold. The first two auxiliary proximal points
are zero, the third is w eta a, and the fourth is zero. Consequently
the only positive auxiliary finite residual is

  Q_aux,(0,2)=(1-eta a)w eta a.

Indeed all edges into queries 0,1,3 have zero target proximal point;
the edge 1->2 is negative and 3->2 is zero. Both optimum directions
are also valid, since every g_aux,i*y_aux,i is nonnegative.
For the base array, the same edge has
Q_base,(0,2)=-(1+eta)w eta.

Set the explicit positive coefficient

  epsilon_mix=(1+eta)/[a(1-eta a)]

and combine the arrays orthogonally:

  X_i=(x_base,i,sqrt(epsilon_mix)x_aux,i),
  G_i=(g_base,i,sqrt(epsilon_mix)g_aux,i),
  F_i=f_base,i+epsilon_mix f_aux,i.

Every residual is the corresponding base residual plus epsilon_mix
times the auxiliary one. The sole potentially positive edge is exactly
canceled; every other finite edge is nonpositive. The optimum jet is
zero, all incoming optimum residuals vanish, and all outgoing optimum
residuals are nonpositive by the preceding proximal-point check.

Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290, proof section2, supplies one fixed globally
convex differentiable 1-smooth interpolating function. More explicitly,
with indices including the zero optimum, let

  c_i=<G_i,X_i>-F_i,
  H(z)=max_i[c_i+<X_i,z-G_i>+||z-G_i||^2/2],
  F(X)=sup_z[<X,z>-H(z)].

The accepted interpolation construction gives F(X_i)=F_i,
grad F(X_i)=G_i and F(0)=0=min F. Thus this is a legal fixed function,
not merely an oracle data proposal. The combined array still obeys
X_3=G_3 and the value formula in (1). Its energy is

  V_mix=F_B+epsilon_mix(1-T^2 eta^2 a^2)
       =F_N/[a(1-eta a)].                             (3)

For the last equality, multiply by a(1-eta a) and use
A=a+2, u=a+1 and 1-A^2a^2=u^2(2-u^2). The resulting numerator is
a u(A^2-T^2 eta^2)+(1+eta)(1-A^2a^2), exactly F_N.
Its denominator is positive. Thus F_N<0 gives the claimed legal
negative-energy witness, with all incoming-terminal Q zero.

## 4. The first-order feasible cone has strictly negative capacity change

Let d=(d_u,d_v,d_w) be a direction at h_S. Put

  p=d_u+d_w, q=d_v, sigma=p+q.

If all four directional derivatives of the expressions in (2) are
nonnegative, the Q and B derivatives imply, respectively,

  q<=-(3+t)p/2,
  q<=(t-1)p/2.                                      (4)

Here is the calculation. Differentiating F_Q at its zero value gives

  dF_Q=-2[lambda p+q+(p+q)/lambda^2],

and (lambda+lambda^(-2))/(1+lambda^(-2))=(3+t)/2.
Differentiating F_B gives

  dF_B=2[t p-(1+lambda^2)q],

and t/(1+lambda^2)=(t-1)/2. These are precisely (4).

Suppose also sigma>=0. If p>0, the first bound in (4) implies
sigma<=-(1+t)p/2<0, a contradiction. If p<0, the second implies
sigma<=(1+t)p/2<0, also a contradiction. Thus p=0 and q=0.
Write d_u=e,d_w=-e.

The C derivative in this remaining direction is

  dF_C=2lambda(1+lambda^2)e,

so nonnegativity forces e>=0. Since dF_B=0 and both F_B and
u^2(2-u^2) vanish at h_S, differentiating F_N gives

  dF_N=(1+eta_S)[-4t e]=-8e,

where eta_S=1/lambda and 1+1/lambda=t. Hence e<=0 too. Consequently
d=0. The only direction with all four derivatives nonnegative and
nonnegative capacity change is the zero direction.

## 5. Turning the cone calculation into an actual local theorem

If the stated neighborhood did not exist, there would be a sequence
h_k!=h_S converging to h_S with capacity at least T_S and all four
F_Q,F_B,F_C,F_N nonnegative. Define

  d_k=(h_k-h_S)/||h_k-h_S||.

A subsequence converges to a unit vector d. Differentiability of each
F at h_S and F(h_S)=0 imply grad F(h_S) dot d>=0 after dividing by
||h_k-h_S||. The capacity condition similarly gives
d_u+d_v+d_w>=0. Section4 forces d=0, contradicting ||d||=1.

Therefore some epsilon_0 exists. For any h in the asserted punctured
neighborhood with capacity at least T_S, at least one of the four
expressions in (2) is negative. Select its corresponding witness in
Section3. It is legal, has V_h<0, and has Q_(i,3)=0 for all i<3.
This proves the statement for every theta simultaneously.

Finally, for a putative PSD intrinsic identity with arbitrary signed
coefficients only on incoming-terminal edges, evaluation on that
witness makes all signed terms zero. Every other coefficient is
nonnegative and multiplies Q<=0. The PSD expression would therefore
be at most V_h<0, impossible. This verifies the stronger certificate
scope directly, without a dual-attainment assertion.

To check that h_S itself belongs to the classes called locally maximal,
the following explicit nonnegative multipliers give a zero remainder:

  lambda_01=2, lambda_10=2lambda,
  lambda_21=2t lambda, lambda_31=lambda_13=2lambda,
  lambda_23=2lambda^2+2t lambda, lambda_32=2lambda^3,

and every unlisted multiplier is zero. Expansion using t^2=2 gives
V_(h_S)+sum lambda_ij Q_ij=0. Thus V_(h_S)>=0 on all legal trajectories;
for theta>=0, the nonpositive incoming-terminal sum gives
E_theta(h_S)>=V_(h_S)>=0. No such membership assertion is needed or
made for negative theta.

## 6. Global classification when the middle physical step equals 2

The same witnesses give a complete result on one entire three-step
family, not merely near h_S. Let u,w>=0 and h=(u,2,w). If E_theta(h)
is nonnegative on every legal trajectory for even one real theta, then

  u=w=sqrt(2).                                      (5)

The same necessary conclusion holds for an intrinsic PSD certificate
with arbitrary signed incoming-terminal coefficients and nonnegative
coefficients on every other inequality. Conversely, at u=w=sqrt(2)
the explicit certificate above establishes E_theta>=0 for every
theta>=0. No sufficiency for negative theta is asserted.

Here is a complete proof covering endpoints and all parameter ranges.
Put T=u+w+3. A first-cut core-ended Huber witness, when u>1, has initial
point 1, prefix gradient 1, and negative plateau slope
-(u-1)/(w+3) after the first step. Its two remaining physical steps
are 2,w; it ends at its negative Huber threshold. Its energy is

  1-T^2(u-1)^2/(w+3)^2.

Its incoming-terminal residuals vanish, so validity forces
T(u-1)<=w+3=T-u and hence u<=2T/(T+1)<2. If u<=1, u<2 holds already.

A last-cut Huber witness starts at u+3 with positive plateau gradient
1 through the first two steps, then the last step w>1 reaches its
negative threshold -(w-1). Its energy is

  (u+3)^2-T^2(w-1)^2.

The same reasoning forces w<2; this is already true when w<=1.
All these are actual clipped-derivative functions of the same form as
the B witness, and their endpoints are core.

The B witness from Section3 is legal for every u,w>=0 with middle
step 2. Its nonnegativity says

  (u+1)(w+1)>=u+w+3,  or uw>=2.                    (6)

Together with u,w<2 this forces 1<u,w<2. On this whole box the C and
N constructions in Section3 are legal: w-1 is in (0,1), and
eta a=(u-1)/(w+1)<1. Thus all four expressions (2) must be nonnegative.

We first rule out u>t. If also w>=t, then
T(u-1)(w-1)>T_S(t-1)^2=1, contradicting F_Q>=0.
If w<t, set D=1+w<lambda. Since r=1 and T=u+D+2, direct expansion gives

  (D^2/u)F_N
   =P_u(D):=u^2 D^2+(4-2u^2-u^3)D-(u-1)(u+2)^2.    (7)

Its leading coefficient is positive and its constant term is negative,
so P_u has one positive and one negative root and is negative between
zero and its positive root. Using lambda^2=2lambda+1,

  P_u(lambda)=-(lambda+1)u^3-2u^2+4(lambda+1).

This is zero at u=t and strictly decreasing for u>0. Therefore it is
negative for u>t. The positive root of P_u lies beyond lambda, and
P_u(D)<0 for 0<D<=lambda. Equation(7) contradicts F_N>=0. We have
proved u<=t.

If u<t, (6) gives w>=2/u>t. For 1<w<2, condition F_C>=0 is equivalent
to

  (u+w+3)(w-1)<=u+1.

The left side is strictly increasing in w. At the smallest allowed
w=2/u, its difference from u+1 is

  (u+2/u+3)(2/u-1)-(u+1)
       =2(u+1)(2/u^2-1)>0.

This is a contradiction. Hence u=t, and (6) then forces w>=t.
If w>t, the quadratic witness is strictly negative. Therefore w=t,
proving (5).

Every exclusion above uses a fixed legal witness with every Q_(i,3)=0.
It consequently works for arbitrary real theta, or for arbitrary
individual signed coefficients on the incoming-terminal edges. This
global classification is restricted to the exact middle step 2.

## Scope for the project

This blocks a local perturbation repair of the three-step silver tail
by the new signed terminal-interpolation state, even with unbounded
credit. Section6 additionally classifies the exact-middle-step-2 family.
It does not exclude a distant three-step tail with a different middle
step, a longer tail, or another full value/moment state. It does not turn
intrinsic energy into the original objective ratio; the changed
normalizations in these hard functions are used only to test V_h.

evidence:
# Height budgets and a two-checkpoint construction with an arbitrary tail

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof candidate. No new verifier allocation and no
solver call. All new ingredients are proved below in the same document;
unverified earlier findings are not premises. This does not establish the
uniform comparison with the complete sequence B_n.

Verified inputs: fact `1252b8823bb5a290` for smooth-convex interpolation and
the maximal finite-prefix interpolant; fact `1fca3e5dd555cb4a` for the ray
comparison in Section 5. The definitions of W_n, K_n and B_n are those in
fact `b98bb807d514e80d`. Work at smoothness one, minimum zero.

## 1. An invariant of one fixed maximal prefix interpolant

Take finitely many legal jets (x_j,g_j,f_j), including (0,0,0). Define

    y_j=x_j-g_j,       delta_j=f_j-||g_j||^2/2,
    M_seed=max_j delta_j,
    m_seed(v)=max_j(<y_j,v>-delta_j),
    H_seed(v)=||v||^2/2+m_seed(v),
    F_seed(x)=sup_v(<x,v>-H_seed(v)).                       (1)

The accepted fact proves that F_seed is the maximal convex 1-smooth
interpolant of these jets. Each delta_j is nonnegative by interpolation
with the optimum. For every x, put v=grad F_seed(x). Strong conjugate
optimality gives

    x-v=sum_j alpha_j y_j,
    alpha_j>=0, sum_j alpha_j=1,

where positive alpha_j occur only among affine terms active in m_seed(v).
To justify the convex-hull subgradient assertion directly, the directional
derivative of a finite maximum of affine functions is the maximum of the
active slopes in that direction. A vector outside their convex hull can
be strictly separated from that hull and cannot satisfy the subgradient
inequality. Every convex combination of active slopes does satisfy it.
Using their common active value in (1) now gives the exact identity

    F_seed(x)-||grad F_seed(x)||^2/2
        =sum_j alpha_j delta_j in [0,M_seed].              (2)

Thus arbitrary later changes of gradient on this ONE fixed function do
not create a proximal value above the maximum seed value.

There is an equivalent finite convex-roof formula. Let K_seed be the
convex hull of all y_j, and define, for z in K_seed,

    J_roof(z)=min {sum_j alpha_j delta_j:
                  alpha>=0, sum alpha=1, sum alpha_j y_j=z},

and J_roof=+infinity outside K_seed. The coefficient simplex is compact,
so the minima exist; 0<=J_roof<=M_seed on K_seed. Then

    F_seed(x)=min_alpha [sum alpha_j delta_j
                         +||x-sum alpha_j y_j||^2/2].       (3)

For a direct proof, minimize the displayed continuous convex function
over the coefficient simplex and set v=x-sum alpha_j y_j. Its directional
optimality conditions on the simplex say that positive coordinates
minimize delta_j-<y_j,v>. These are exactly the active terms of m_seed(v),
giving equality with (1). This is an identity, not a numerical program.

In particular, with K_zero=conv{y_j:delta_j=0},

    argmin F_seed=K_zero,
    dist(x,K_seed)^2/2 <= F_seed(x)
                         <= dist(x,K_seed)^2/2+M_seed.      (4)

The minimizer identity follows from (3): its two nonnegative summands
vanish exactly when x=sum alpha_j y_j with support on zero-height jets.
It supplies the actual closest-minimizer distance, without substituting
distance to the generally larger set K_seed.

For any GD step t>=0 from x, let x_new=x-t grad F_seed(x). The elementary
smoothness inequality and (2), with delta=F_seed(x)-||grad F_seed(x)||^2/2,
give

    F_seed(x_new)<=delta+(1-t)^2||grad F_seed(x)||^2/2
                  =(1-t)^2 F_seed(x)+[1-(1-t)^2]delta
                  <=(1-t)^2 F_seed(x)
                      +[1-(1-t)^2]_+ M_seed.              (5)

This holds along any nonnegative schedule, irrespective of the number
of gradient changes. A unit step gives F_seed(x_new)<=M_seed. Every
following step in [0,2] preserves that value cap. Iterating (5) gives,
for a suffix t_0,...,t_(r-1), the explicit bound

 F_seed(x_r) <= product_(i<r)(1-t_i)^2 F_seed(x_0)
   +M_seed sum_(j<r)[1-(1-t_j)^2]_+
                         product_(j<i<r)(1-t_i)^2.          (6)

Empty products and sums have their usual meanings.

Greedily adjoining jets of F_seed at new points and recomputing the
maximal interpolant leaves the entire function unchanged. Indeed the
new conjugate quadratic is <=H_seed everywhere, by interpolation of
F_seed with its actual new jet, whereas all old quadratics remain.
Their maximum is therefore still H_seed. In particular such greedy
extensions cannot increase M_seed, by (2).

The scope is essential. The bound does NOT hold for arbitrary other
interpolants of the seed. Seed jets (0,0,0) and (1,1,1/2) have M_seed=0
and maximal interpolant F_seed(x)=x^2/2. The symmetric Huber function

    f_H(x)=x^2/2 for |x|<=1, and |x|-1/2 for |x|>=1

has the same seed. Starting at1 with schedule (R+1,1), R>=2, the maximal
quadratic ends at0, whereas f_H visits -R and -(R-1), with normalized
terminal value 2R-3. Its new proximal height at -R is R-1>0. Hence
creating new height requires a nonmaximal choice of the future function;
the invariant is not an upper bound on the unrestricted W_n.

## 6. Sharp quantitative cost of creating a new height

Return to an ARBITRARY fixed legal finite seed from Section1. At any proposed
new point X put

    v=grad F_seed(X), delta=F_seed(X)-||v||^2/2.

Let f_new be ANY legal convex 1-smooth interpolant of the same seed, and
let g=grad f_new(X), d_new=f_new(X)-||g||^2/2. It need not be maximal.
The retained outgoing interpolation inequalities imply

    f_new(X)<=<X,g>-H_seed(g).

The quadratic strong-convexity bound on H_seed at v, whose subgradient
is X, yields

    F_seed(X)-f_new(X)>=||g-v||^2/2.                      (27)

Equivalently, use convexity of m_seed with subgradient X-v at v to
obtain the sharper useful arrangement

    d_new+||g-v/2||^2<=delta+||v||^2/4
                             <=M_seed+||v||^2/4.          (28)

For clarity, the expansion is

 d_new<=<X,g>-||g||^2-m_seed(g)
      <=<v,g>-||g||^2+<X-v,v>-m_seed(v)
       =delta+||v||^2/4-||g-v/2||^2.

Thus an increase b=d_new-delta>0 is impossible unless b<=||v||^2/4.
When v!=0, (27)--(28) further give the explicit necessary value loss

 F_seed(X)-f_new(X)
   >= ||v||^2/8 [1-sqrt(1-4b/||v||^2)]^2.               (29)

Indeed (28) puts g in the ball with center v/2 and radius
sqrt(||v||^2/4-b); its distance to v is at least ||v||/2 minus that
radius. If v=0, no positive b is possible. The same lower bound applies
when d_new>=M_seed+b, since delta<=M_seed. At b=||v||^2/4 the value
loss is at least ||v||^2/8, a nonvanishing cost that cannot be hidden
by dropping the boundary gradient from the state.

The inequalities are sharp for legal data, not merely abstract vectors.
Use the seed (0,0,0),(1,1,1/2), so F_seed=x^2/2. Choose R>=2,
X=-R, and the symmetric Huber function with threshold tR, 1/2<=t<=1.
It retains the seed because tR>=1. It has g=-tR,
d_new=t(1-t)R^2, and value loss (1-t)^2R^2/2. Thus it attains
(27)--(29), with t=(1+sqrt(1-4b/R^2))/2. The point X is reached from
the seed x_0=1 by the nonnegative step R+1; it is a valid next query.

There is also a general tail consequence. If one interpolant of the
seed has the SAME gradient g at every actual sample of a prescribed
tail starting at X, including its terminal sample, and its step sum
is T, interpolation in both directions between equal-gradient jets
forces f_end=f_new(X)-T||g||^2. Completing the square in (27) gives

    2f_end <=2delta+||v||^2/(2T+1)
                    -(2T+1)||g-v/(2T+1)||^2.             (30)

This is a necessary bound for every such constant-gradient continuation
in any dimension. It separates the retained height from the geometric
gradient budget, with an exact tail loss. It is not asserted for tails
whose gradients vary.

glossary.d_new: Proximal value f_new(X)-||grad f_new(X)||²/2 of any other legal prefix interpolant.
glossary.b: Positive increase d_new-delta in this height-budget statement.
glossary.v: Actual gradient grad F_seed(X) at the selected point X.
