evidence:
# Height budgets and a two-checkpoint construction with an arbitrary tail

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof candidate. No new verifier allocation and no
solver call. All new ingredients are proved below in the same document;
unverified earlier findings are not premises. This does not establish the
uniform comparison with the complete sequence B_n.

Verified inputs: fact `1252b8823bb5a290` for smooth-convex interpolation and
the maximal finite-prefix interpolant; fact `1fca3e5dd555cb4a` for the ray
comparison in Section 5. The definitions of W_n, K_n and B_n are those in
fact `b98bb807d514e80d`. Work at smoothness one, minimum zero.

## 2. Fully explicit three-cell construction

Prescribe arbitrary nonnegative lists B_0,B_1,B_2 of respective sums
M_0-1, M_1-1, T, where M_0,M_1>=1 and T>=0. Put two checkpoints between
them:

    h=(B_0, A M_0+1, B_1, 1+M_1 epsilon, B_2),
    A>0, epsilon>0.                                      (7)

Their entries can be arbitrarily large individually; only their actual
partial sums are used. Select any kappa satisfying

    0<kappa<A,             kappa(1+epsilon)<=A.             (8)

In R^2, write

    a=1-1/M_0,
    nu=sqrt(kappa(A-kappa)),
    p=(1,0)/M_0,              q=(-kappa,nu)/M_1,
    X=(-A,0),                y=X-M_1 q=(kappa-A,-nu),
    d=-M_1 q=(kappa,-nu),     e=(a,0)-y,
    D=||e||^2=(A-kappa)(A+2a)+a^2>0,
    w=d-(a kappa/D)e,
    W_sq=||w||^2=A kappa-a^2 kappa^2/D,
    lambda_cap=epsilon/(2T+1),
    r_cap=lambda_cap w.                                  (9)

The following products are exact:

    <d,y>=0, <d,e>=a kappa, <y,e>=-(A-kappa)(A+a),
    <e,w>=0, <d,w>=W_sq, <q,w>=-W_sq/M_1,
    w_1=kappa(A-kappa)(A+a)/D>0,
    <y,w>=a kappa(A-kappa)(A+a)/D>=0.                     (10)

Here w_1 denotes the first coordinate, not a time index. Define ONE
fixed nonsmooth convex function and its Moreau envelope by

    J_cap(z)=max(0,<p,z>,<q,z>,<r_cap,z-y>),
    f_cap(x)=min_z[J_cap(z)+||x-z||^2/2],   x_init=(1,0).   (11)

All four planes are chosen before running the entire supplied schedule.
The fourth plane has intercept -<r_cap,y><=0; this intercept is retained.

For completeness, this envelope is convex, differentiable and 1-smooth.
The strictly convex coercive minimization has a unique proximal point
z(x); optimality says g(x)=x-z(x) belongs to the subgradient of J_cap
there. Monotonicity of subgradients at two points gives
<g(x)-g(x'),x-x'> >= ||g(x)-g(x')||^2. Thus g is 1-Lipschitz. The
two minimizing inequalities show that it is the derivative of the
envelope, and joint convexity followed by minimization proves convexity.
An active affine-plane slope at z is a subgradient, so it suffices below
to check activation at x=z+that slope.

### First block and first checkpoint

For partial ordinary sum u in [0,M_0-1], propose gradient p and proximal
point z=(1-(u+1)/M_0,0). Its first coordinate lies in [0,a]. The p-plane
is nonnegative, and the q-plane is nonpositive. Since <e,w>=0,

    <r_cap,z-y>=lambda_cap (z_1-a)w_1<=0.

Thus p is active at every actual sample, including the first checkpoint
query at x=p. That checkpoint sends the iterate exactly to X=(-A,0).

### Second block and second checkpoint

For t=u+1 in [1,M_1], propose gradient q and proximal point X-tq.
It equals y+(M_1-t)q. The q-height is

    <q,X-tq>=(A kappa/M_1)(1-t/M_1)>=0.

The excess of q over p is affine in t, with endpoints controlled by
its value at t=M_1:

    <q-p,X-tq>=A kappa/M_1+A/M_0
                         -t(A kappa/M_1^2+kappa/(M_0 M_1))
                   >=(A-kappa)/M_0>0.

The fourth plane has value

    <r_cap,X-tq-y>
       =-lambda_cap(M_1-t)W_sq/M_1<=0.

All old and future plane comparisons therefore hold at every sample.
The position at the second checkpoint is y+q. Its step 1+M_1 epsilon
sends the trajectory to

    x_C=y+epsilon d.                                     (12)

### Arbitrary final list

For every partial tail sum u in [0,T], propose gradient r_cap. Its
proximal point is

    Z(u)=y+epsilon d-(u+1)lambda_cap w.

The fourth plane there has nonnegative value

    <r_cap,Z(u)-y>
       =lambda_cap[epsilon-(u+1)lambda_cap]W_sq>=0,         (13)

because (u+1)/(2T+1)<=1. The p-plane is nonpositive since

    M_0<p,Z(u)>
       =kappa-A+epsilon kappa-(u+1)lambda_cap w_1<=0

by (8) and w_1>0. The q-plane is also nonpositive:

    M_1<q,Z(u)>=-epsilon A kappa
                         +(u+1)lambda_cap W_sq<=0,

using W_sq<=A kappa and (u+1)lambda_cap<=epsilon. Thus the fourth
plane is active throughout the entire final list, including its endpoint.
This checks all directions of every old/new comparison using the same J_cap.

### Exact value, boundary gradients and true normalization

At the terminal point x_C-T r_cap, adding half the squared gradient to
(13) gives

    2 f_cap(x_n)=epsilon^2 W_sq/(2T+1).                   (14)

The actual squared gradients are

    ||p||^2=1/M_0^2,
    ||q||^2=A kappa/M_1^2,
    ||r_cap||^2=epsilon^2 W_sq/(2T+1)^2.                  (15)

The terminal proximal value is exactly

    delta_end=T epsilon^2 W_sq/(2T+1)^2.                 (16)

The fresh component of q has squared norm kappa(A-kappa)/M_1^2; it
has not been dropped from any norm or scale calculation. The construction
retains an explicitly positive value budget when T>0, in contrast to a
pure quadratic terminal completion followed by a unit-step reset.

The origin is a minimizer: its p- and q-planes are zero and its fourth
plane is <=0 by (10). The minimum of J_cap and its envelope is zero.
Every minimizer z of J_cap satisfies <p,z><=0, hence z_1<=0. A minimizer
of the envelope is exactly a minimizer of J_cap, since both terms in
its defining minimum are nonnegative. Therefore the closest minimizer
to x_init=(1,0) is genuinely the origin, at distance exactly one.
Equation (14) is consequently the required normalized objective, not
an evaluation using an arbitrarily distant optimum.

All endpoints M_0=1, M_1=1 and T=0 are included. In particular a=0
causes no singularity because 0<kappa<A makes D>0. Zero steps duplicate
queries and have no effect on the proof. No parameter limit is hidden.

## 3. A schedule functional with no feasibility oracle

For any nonnegative schedule h of length n and any i<j with h_i>1,
h_j>1, define

    P_i=sum_(t<i) h_t,
    S_ij=sum_(i<t<j) h_t,
    T_j=sum_(j<t<n) h_t,
    A_ij=(h_i-1)/(1+P_i),
    epsilon_ij=(h_j-1)/(1+S_ij).

Choose explicitly

    kappa=A_ij/[2 max(1,epsilon_ij)].                      (17)

It is positive, at most A_ij/2, and satisfies (8), because
1+epsilon<=2max(1,epsilon). From D>=a^2 one has

    W_sq>=A kappa-kappa^2>=A kappa/2.

Thus (14) yields, for EVERY eligible pair,

 W_n(h) >= A_ij^2 min(epsilon_ij^2,epsilon_ij)
                                      /[4(1+2T_j)].       (18)

Define C_n^tail(h) to be the maximum of the right side over all eligible
pairs, with zero when there are none. The construction proves the new
candidate universal lower bound

    W_n(h)>=max(K_n(h), C_n^tail(h)).                      (19)

The pair selection is adversary selection before the run; there are no
unproved existence parameters and no changes to the supplied schedule.
Unlike a product term tied to h_(n-1), C_n^tail need not vanish when the
last step is one. Arbitrarily long, nonperiodic final lists are covered
with their exact mass loss 1+2T_j. No assertion that (19) matches 1/B_n
uniformly is made.

## 4. Exact optimization within the displayed cap directions

For fixed A>0, a>=0, epsilon>0, T>=0, all directions satisfying (8)
are admissible in the preceding proof. The exact score is proportional
to

    W_sq(kappa)=A kappa-a^2 kappa^2/
                         [(A-kappa)(A+2a)+a^2].            (20)

If a=0, this is A kappa, so its maximum on the admissible interval is
at kappa=A/(1+epsilon). If a>0, differentiation with the positive
denominator gives

    W_sq'(kappa)=A-a^2 kappa[2D+(A+2a)kappa]/D^2.

Put b=A+2a and C=(A+a)^2, so D=C-b kappa. Expanding its numerator
factorizes as

    D^2 W_sq'(kappa)
        =(A+a)^2 [A(A+a)-b kappa]
                       [(A+a)-kappa].                    (21)

The second bracket is positive for kappa<A. Hence the unique unconstrained
maximizer in (0,A) is

    kappa_0=A(A+a)/(A+2a).

Its squared direction norm is W_sq(kappa_0)=kappa_0^2. The exact optimum
within the explicitly checked cap family is consequently

    kappa_opt=min(kappa_0,A/(1+epsilon)) for a>0,
    kappa_opt=A/(1+epsilon) for a=0.                       (22)

At the feasibility endpoint, kappa(1+epsilon)=A, the old p-plane is
still dominated, by the nonnegative subtraction in its comparison. The
optimization therefore has no open-boundary loss. This is an optimum
only within this displayed family of cap planes, not over all prefixes
or all legal interpolants.

## 5. A strict comparison with the entire verified ray functional

The following family establishes that (18) contains information absent
from F_ray, although the schedules are already above the target scale
by the single-cut witness and hence do not solve the hard regime.

Let an integer M>=16 be given, A=M^(1/8), epsilon=M^(-1/4), and choose

    h=(1 repeated M-1 times, A M+1,
       1 repeated M-1 times, 1+M epsilon, 1).              (23)

Only its two large checkpoints have entries >1, so the verified ray
construction can select at most those two: a selected first checkpoint
must exceed1, and every later selected checkpoint must also exceed1
because positive new gradient magnitude requires (b-1)m>O>=0.
If both are chosen, its exact z_term is

    z_term=A epsilon-(M-1)/M
          =M^(-1/8)-1+1/M<0.                             (24)

Indeed M^(-1/8)<=1/sqrt(2)<3/4 and 1/M<=1/16. Thus this pair is
infeasible even before its terminal old-slope constraint. Every feasible
ray witness has at most one cut, and fact 1fca3e5dd555cb4a gives exactly

    F_ray_n(h)=K_n(h).

The global Huber term is <=1/M. The first cut contributes
A^2/[1+2(M-1+1+M epsilon+1)]<=A^2/(2M). At the second cut,
one plus the prefix mass is (A+2)M and the tail has sum1, so its value is
epsilon^2/[3(A+2)^2]<=M^(-3/4)/3. Thus

    F_ray_n(h)=K_n(h)<=M^(-3/4).                          (25)

The new cap, with T=1, has from (18)

    2f_cap(x_n)>=A^2 epsilon^2/12=M^(-1/4)/12.             (26)

Its ratio to the complete ray functional is at least sqrt(M)/12 and
tends to infinity, with a genuinely unit final step and exact distance1.
This comparison is deliberately scoped: n=2M+1, so (25) itself does
not establish that F_ray is below the project benchmark. No such claim
is used to market this family as a new solution of the all-schedule gap.

## 6. Sharp quantitative cost of creating a new height

Return to an ARBITRARY fixed legal finite seed from Section1. At any proposed
new point X put

    v=grad F_seed(X), delta=F_seed(X)-||v||^2/2.

Let f_new be ANY legal convex 1-smooth interpolant of the same seed, and
let g=grad f_new(X), d_new=f_new(X)-||g||^2/2. It need not be maximal.
The retained outgoing interpolation inequalities imply

    f_new(X)<=<X,g>-H_seed(g).

The quadratic strong-convexity bound on H_seed at v, whose subgradient
is X, yields

    F_seed(X)-f_new(X)>=||g-v||^2/2.                      (27)

Equivalently, use convexity of m_seed with subgradient X-v at v to
obtain the sharper useful arrangement

    d_new+||g-v/2||^2<=delta+||v||^2/4
                             <=M_seed+||v||^2/4.          (28)

For clarity, the expansion is

 d_new<=<X,g>-||g||^2-m_seed(g)
      <=<v,g>-||g||^2+<X-v,v>-m_seed(v)
       =delta+||v||^2/4-||g-v/2||^2.

Thus an increase b=d_new-delta>0 is impossible unless b<=||v||^2/4.
When v!=0, (27)--(28) further give the explicit necessary value loss

 F_seed(X)-f_new(X)
   >= ||v||^2/8 [1-sqrt(1-4b/||v||^2)]^2.               (29)

Indeed (28) puts g in the ball with center v/2 and radius
sqrt(||v||^2/4-b); its distance to v is at least ||v||/2 minus that
radius. If v=0, no positive b is possible. The same lower bound applies
when d_new>=M_seed+b, since delta<=M_seed. At b=||v||^2/4 the value
loss is at least ||v||^2/8, a nonvanishing cost that cannot be hidden
by dropping the boundary gradient from the state.

The inequalities are sharp for legal data, not merely abstract vectors.
Use the seed (0,0,0),(1,1,1/2), so F_seed=x^2/2. Choose R>=2,
X=-R, and the symmetric Huber function with threshold tR, 1/2<=t<=1.
It retains the seed because tR>=1. It has g=-tR,
d_new=t(1-t)R^2, and value loss (1-t)^2R^2/2. Thus it attains
(27)--(29), with t=(1+sqrt(1-4b/R^2))/2. The point X is reached from
the seed x_0=1 by the nonnegative step R+1; it is a valid next query.

There is also a general tail consequence. If one interpolant of the
seed has the SAME gradient g at every actual sample of a prescribed
tail starting at X, including its terminal sample, and its step sum
is T, interpolation in both directions between equal-gradient jets
forces f_end=f_new(X)-T||g||^2. Completing the square in (27) gives

    2f_end <=2delta+||v||^2/(2T+1)
                    -(2T+1)||g-v/(2T+1)||^2.             (30)

This is a necessary bound for every such constant-gradient continuation
in any dimension. It separates the retained height from the geometric
gradient budget, with an exact tail loss. It is not asserted for tails
whose gradients vary.

## 7. Exact optimal constant-gradient tail for each displayed prefix

Section2's perpendicular direction gave a simple explicit guarantee. The
full outgoing optimum for the SAME retained first two blocks can in fact
be attained with a slightly different fourth plane. Keep all definitions
through e,D in (9), retain the feasibility range (8), and put

    sigma=2T+1,
    tau=a(kappa epsilon-sigma/M_0)_+/D,
    r_exact=(epsilon d-tau e)/sigma.                      (31)

If a=0 set tau=0, as the formula already does. In all cases
0<=tau<1: when a>0, (8) and D>=(A-kappa)(A+2a) imply
tau<=a/(A+2a)<1/2. Replace the fourth plane in (11) by

    <r_exact,z-y>.

The exact score is

 V_exact(kappa)= [A kappa epsilon^2
               -a^2(kappa epsilon-sigma/M_0)_+^2/D]/sigma. (32)

This score is the maximum over ALL legal constant-gradient tails with
the fixed first- and second-block jets at this kappa, including arbitrary
affine intercepts and extra dimensions. This assertion concerns the
given prefix, not every possible two-block prefix or varying-gradient
tail. The range (8) remains explicit.

### Full attainment checks

One has

    <y,r_exact>=-tau<y,e>/sigma>=0,
    0<=<e,r_exact><=a/M_0,
    <q,r_exact>=(-epsilon A kappa+tau a kappa)/(sigma M_1)<0.

The last sign follows from tau<=a kappa epsilon/D and
A kappa-a^2 kappa^2/D>0. Also the first coordinate of r_exact is positive:
it is at least epsilon w_1/sigma, since tau<=a kappa epsilon/D.

At every first-block proximal point z=(t,0), 0<=t<=a, the difference
between the fourth plane and the p-plane is affine in t. At t=0 it
is -<r_exact,y><=0. At t=a it is <r_exact,e>-a/M_0<=0. Hence the
fourth plane preserves every first jet. At every second-block proximal
point y+(M_1-u)q it has value (M_1-u)<r_exact,q><=0 and so preserves
every second jet. The origin is still a minimizer.

For partial tail mass u in [0,T], let Z=y+epsilon d-(u+1)r_exact.
The p-plane is <=0 because its first-coordinate numerator is bounded
by kappa(1+epsilon)-A<=0. The q-plane is <=0 because

 M_1<q,Z>=-epsilon A kappa
       +(u+1)(epsilon A kappa-tau a kappa)/sigma<=0.

The new plane is nonnegative: from epsilon d=sigma r_exact+tau e,

    <r_exact,Z-y>
       =(
          sigma-u-1
         )||r_exact||^2+tau<r_exact,e>
       >=T||r_exact||^2>=0.

Thus this one fixed four-plane envelope gives the entire desired tail
with actual gradient r_exact. Its terminal score is

    2epsilon<d,r_exact>-sigma||r_exact||^2
      =[epsilon^2||d||^2-tau^2 D]/sigma,

which is (32). The actual closest minimizer remains the origin by the
same p-plane argument as Section2. The terminal proximal value is

    T||r_exact||^2+tau<r_exact,e>,                         (33)

with <r_exact,e>=a/M_0 when tau>0. Both sources of retained value are
explicit; neither is discarded.

### Optimality for the entire fixed-prefix constant-tail class

The seed conjugate maximum, including the optimum and all first two
block queries, is exactly

 m_seed(r)=max(0, <(a,0),r>-a/M_0,
                 <y,r>,
                 <y,r>+(M_1-1)(<q,r>-||q||^2)).           (34)

All intermediate terms are convex combinations of the two endpoints
on each block; every endpoint is an actual retained query. The formula
also includes empty blocks, when the corresponding endpoints coincide.
For any legal tail with gradient r, its start value is bounded by the
outgoing seed inequalities, and the equal-gradient values decrease by
T||r||^2. Hence its terminal value is at most

    sup_r [<y+epsilon d,r>-sigma||r||^2/2-m_seed(r)].        (35)

At r_exact the y-term in (34) dominates zero, and it dominates the last
term because <q,r_exact><0. It also dominates the (a,0)-term since
<e,r_exact><=a/M_0. If tau>0 those two terms tie; if tau=0 the
y-term alone can be used. Thus y+tau e is a convex combination of
active slopes in (34). The exact identity

    y+epsilon d=sigma r_exact+y+tau e

is the global optimality condition for the strictly concave expression
in (35). This proves its maximum is V_exact(kappa)/2. The constructed
envelope attains it while satisfying ALL incoming inequalities too.
For extra orthogonal dimensions, the old slopes and the start position
have zero components, and the term -sigma||r||^2/2 strictly penalizes
each new orthogonal component. Thus they cannot improve (35).

## 8. Explicit optimum over the admissible angle and its finite budget

Set

    kappa_lim=A/(1+epsilon),
    kappa_0=A(A+a)/(A+2a),
    kappa_free=kappa_0+a sigma/[M_0 epsilon(A+a)].

The exact maximizer of (32) over 0<kappa<=kappa_lim is

    kappa_best=min(kappa_lim,kappa_free).                 (36)

This includes a=0, when kappa_free=A>kappa_lim and tau=0. To prove
the nonzero-a formula, (32) increases linearly while
kappa<=sigma/(M_0 epsilon). Above this threshold put

    c=sigma/M_0, b=A+2a, C=(A+a)^2,
    u=kappa-c/epsilon, C_t=C-bc/epsilon, D=C_t-bu.

When this active region meets (0,A), C_t>a^2>0. Apart from the positive
factor epsilon^2/(sigma D^2), the derivative is

    A C_t^2-2 C C_t u+b C u^2.

Its smaller root gives exactly kappa_free, and its larger root gives
A+a-a c/[epsilon(A+a)]>A. Hence the derivative changes from positive
to negative only at kappa_free in the admissible region. If the positive
part never activates before kappa_lim, the score is increasing and
kappa_free>=kappa_lim; indeed either c/epsilon<A and
kappa_free>c/epsilon, or c/epsilon>=A and kappa_free>=A.
This proves (36) in every case, including equality at a breakpoint.

When the optimum is interior, its parameters and score simplify to

    tau_best=epsilon A/(A+2a),
    V_best=epsilon^2 kappa_0^2/(2T+1)
                      +2epsilon A a/[M_0(A+2a)].          (37)

The second term is a retained old height, but it is NOT available for
arbitrarily long tails. Interiority requires kappa_free<kappa_lim,
which is equivalent, for a>0, to

    2T+1 < [M_0 epsilon(A+a)/a](kappa_lim-kappa_0).         (38)

In particular the right side must be positive. Once the threshold is
reached, (36) fixes kappa_best=kappa_lim and one must use the exact
boundary formula (32). If 2T+1>=M_0 epsilon kappa_lim, tau=0 there
and the score is precisely epsilon^2 A kappa_lim/(2T+1), which decays
with the tail mass. This identifies the finite scale budget behind the
seemingly tail-independent term in (37), without an o(1) shortcut.

## Remaining interface

The invariant (2) identifies a structural limitation of repeatedly using
one maximal interpolant. The new fourth plane explicitly creates the
proximal value needed to survive an arbitrary tail, and (18) gives its
quantitative schedule cost without unspecified feasible parameters.
The missing target-level step is still to compare a sufficiently rich
legal construction uniformly against the complete sequence B_n.

Matlas searches supplied no external theorem used here. The previously
downloaded exact text of Taylor--Hendrickx--Glineur, arXiv:1502.05666v6,
Remark2 and its preceding interpolation proof, was read for context;
all identities used above are proved from the accepted project fact and
the displayed elementary constructions, not from an external black box.

glossary.r_exact: Gradient (epsilon d-tau e)/sigma on every sample of the optimized constant-gradient tail.
glossary.tau: a(kappa epsilon-sigma/M_0)_+/D, the active mixture coefficient of the two prefix conjugate planes.
glossary.V_exact: Exact normalized optimum for this fixed-prefix constant-tail class, formula(32) in the evidence.
glossary.kappa_lim: A/(1+epsilon), the explicit sufficient range retaining old-plane domination.
glossary.kappa_free: A(A+a)/(A+2a)+a sigma/[M_0 epsilon(A+a)], the unrestricted critical angle of formula(32).
glossary.M_0: One plus ordinary prefix mass before the first checkpoint.
glossary.M_1: One plus mass between the two checkpoints.
glossary.D: Squared norm of e=(a,0)-y, equal to (A-kappa)(A+2a)+a².

claim: C31 complete energy-preserving affine-gradient reduction: every primitive witness with q distinct gradients has a realization in dimension<=q-1, including a minimizer, with EVERY finite Q and V unchanged. Any two-gradient witness is therefore scalar after this transformation. More sharply, for an arbitrary-dimensional trajectory with just one transition between two constant-gradient phases at step b, universal V>=0 is EQUIVALENT to the existing single-cut condition D(b-1)_+<=(1+P)(1+Q). evidence:
# Affine gradient dimension and the exact limit of two constant-gradient phases

Status: self-contained candidate, NOT verifier-accepted. No solver or
fact_submit. The only accepted input is finite smooth-convex interpolation
necessity from fact 1252b8823bb5a290; the realizing conjugate construction
is also proved below. Prior unverified projection findings are not used.

For a nonnegative schedule h of length n, let P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t and
S=P_n. On an actual 1-smooth convex GD trajectory define

    V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)
        +sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
        -S(S+1)||g_n||^2.

## 1. Exact removal of the common orthogonal gradient component

Let E=span{g_i-g_0:0<=i<=n}. There is a constant vector c in E^perp
such that every g_i=v_i+c, with v_i in E. Define

    y_i=projection_E x_i,   f'_i=f_i-<c,x_i>.

Then y_(i+1)=y_i-h_i v_i. Moreover, every finite interpolation residual
is unchanged:

    f'_i-f'_j+<v_i,y_j-y_i>+||v_i-v_j||^2/2
      =f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0.    (1)

Indeed the component of x_j-x_i in E^perp is -(P_j-P_i)c; the
corresponding inner product is exactly canceled by the value correction.
This proves (1) for EVERY ordered pair, not just consecutive queries.

These data are realizable in E by an everywhere finite differentiable
convex function with gradient Lipschitz constant one and a minimizer.
To see this directly, put

    a_i=<v_i,y_i>-f'_i,
    H(z)=max_i {a_i+<y_i,z-v_i>+||z-v_i||^2/2},
    F(y)=sup_z {<y,z>-H(z)}.

The inequalities (1) imply H(v_i)=a_i and y_i in partial H(v_i).
The function H is finite and 1-strongly convex, and grows quadratically.
Thus for each y its conjugate maximization has a unique point z(y).
Strong monotonicity of partial H gives
||z(y)-z(w)||<=||y-w||; comparison of the two maximizing expressions
shows that F is differentiable with gradient z(y). This proves all
claimed regularity and interpolation F(y_i)=f'_i, grad F(y_i)=v_i.
An active quadratic of H at zero has a gradient y_* in partial H(0).
Consequently grad F(y_*)=0 and F(y_*)=-H(0), so a minimizer exists.
No preassigned optimum or preservation of its location was assumed.

The primitive energy is EXACTLY unchanged. Write C=||c||^2. Then

    f'_i-f'_n=(f_i-f_n)-(S-P_i)C,
    ||v_i||^2=||g_i||^2-C.

Using 2sum_i h_i P_i=S^2-sum_i h_i^2, the change in V equals

    C[-2sum_i h_i(S-P_i)-sum_i h_i(1-h_i)+S(S+1)]=0. (2)

Therefore a trajectory with q distinct gradients has a realization with
the SAME primitive energy in dimension at most q-1. If all gradients
are equal, V=0 and the transformed function can be taken constant.
For a schedule with m positive steps, every negative-energy witness can
be realized in dimension at most m, since there are at most m+1 distinct
sampled gradients. Zero steps simply repeat points and gradients.

In particular ANY two-gradient witness, including one that revisits its
two gradients many times, has a scalar realization with identical V.
This does not assert that its scalar realization is a projection onto
an interval. The conjugate construction may add other gradients away
from the finite queried trajectory. Normalized objective error is not
asserted to survive the value correction or the new minimizer.

## 2. One change of gradient: the exact arbitrary-dimensional test

Fix one actual checkpoint index j and write

    P=sum_(i<j)h_i, b=h_j, Q=sum_(i>j)h_i,
    S=P+b+Q, D=1+S, A=P+b.

Consider EVERY legal trajectory, in any finite dimension, satisfying

    g_i=u for 0<=i<=j,
    g_i=v for j+1<=i<=n.                            (3)

All function values remain those of the same actual function. Then

    V_h>=0 for all trajectories (3)

holds if and only if

    D(b-1)_+ <= (P+1)(Q+1).                         (4)

Thus arbitrary dimension and arbitrary legal values within two constant-
gradient phases do not strengthen the usual single-cut test at all.
For (3) with u!=v, a quantitative version when b>1 is

    V_h >= [(P+b)t/(Q+1)]
                [(P+1)(Q+1)-D(b-1)],
    t=||u||^2-<u,v>>0.                             (5)

### Every cross-history constraint is retained

If u=v then V_h=0, as follows from affine values and the same summation
as (2). If u!=v then b>0, because a zero step repeats its point. Put

    Delta=f_j-f_(j+1), d=||u-v||^2.

Two queries with the same gradient must have exactly their affine value
difference: apply both interpolation inequalities and combine them.
For a query before j at remaining ordinary sum s in [0,P] and a query
after j at elapsed sum q in [0,Q], their point displacement is
(b+s)u+q v and their value difference is

    Delta+s||u||^2+q||v||^2.

Consequently their two ordered interpolation inequalities are exactly

    Delta >= b<u,v>+d/2-s t,
    Delta <= b||u||^2-d/2-q(d-t).                   (6)

The adjacent pair gives b t>=d>0, so t>0. The strongest lower bound in
(6) is at s=0. The strongest upper bound is at q=Q if d>=t, and at
q=0 otherwise. The queried history contains both those endpoints.
Hence ALL the finite interpolation constraints in (3) reduce exactly to

    b<u,v>+d/2 <= Delta
       <=b||u||^2-d/2-Q(d-t)_+ .                  (7)

Same-gradient pairs already have equality. The initial ordinary steps
do not disappear by assumption: their effect is the monotone term -s t
in (6). Equation (7) implies, for r=d/t,

    r+Q(r-1)_+ <= b,
    r <= b                          if 0<b<=1,
    r <= (b+Q)/(1+Q)                if b>1.         (8)

### The full primitive energy

Summing the actual affine values in the two phases gives

    V_h=A[2Delta+(P-b+1)||u||^2-(A+1)||v||^2].      (9)

For example, the prefix contribution uses
sum_(i<=j)h_i P_i=(A^2-sum_(i<=j)h_i^2)/2, and the suffix
contribution uses the identical formula for its elapsed sums. No
replacement step or surrogate endpoint value appears in (9).

Substitute the lower bound on Delta from (7), and use
||v||^2=||u||^2-2t+d. This yields

    V_h >= A[2(P+1)t-A d].                         (10)

If 0<b<=1 then (8) implies the bracket divided by t is at least
2(P+1)-(P+b)b>=P+1>0. If b>1, use the other bound in (8) and the
identity

    2(P+1)(Q+1)-(P+b)(Q+b)
       =(P+1)(Q+1)-D(b-1).

This proves (5) and the sufficient direction of (4), including b<=1.
The case b=0 has only u=v and was already treated.

### Necessity is attained by one fixed interval projection

When (4) fails, necessarily b>1. Set w=(b-1)/(Q+1)>0, and let
C=[-w,1]. The fixed function

    F_C(x)=max_(z in C)(xz-z^2/2)

is convex differentiable 1-smooth, has gradient clip(x,-w,1), and
minimum zero at zero. Start at x_0=P+1. Every prefix gradient up to
checkpoint j is 1, because x_j=1 and preceding radii are at least1.
The checkpoint lands at 1-b=-(Q+1)w. Every suffix gradient is -w,
and the terminal point is -w. Every query satisfies
F_C(x_i)=x_i g_i-g_i^2/2. A squared-distance telescope therefore gives

    V_h=(P+1)^2-D^2 w^2<0.                        (11)

This proves necessity with an actual scalar projection and all original
steps retained. It also shows that the sign threshold in (5) is sharp.

## 3. Consequence for the geometric program

Single-cut tests already cover the ENTIRE arbitrary-dimensional class
(3), not just a preselected pair of opposite scalar gradients. Enlarging
that class by changing angles, ambient dimension, values, or the common
orthogonal gradient component cannot supply a new primitive-capacity
inequality. A new geometric test must have at least two gradient changes.
Two gradient values with repeated changes still remain scalar by Section1;
to exploit higher-dimensional gradient geometry requires at least three
distinct gradient values and affine gradient rank at least two.

These are exact scope limits of witness classes. They do not bound all
primitive capacities or solve the unrestricted objective question.

claim: Assigned near-critical ruler is a genuine constant-level gap for the tested mechanisms. For every m>=128 at the original appended b=1+a_m, ALL quadratic curvatures and ALL single-cut witnesses are dominated by K=1/(2 sum H_m+1). Every retained two-block prefix in the explicit cap-angle range, followed by ANY legal constant-gradient tail (all dimensions, affine offsets and positive values), also has normalized objective <=K. The joint proof derives B_(2^m-1)<=1+4(2^m-1)^log_2(1+sqrt2), hence limsup K B<=2/e<1. It also gives exact full-spectrum and first/last-occurrence K formulas for EVERY b>=0, and the exact large-b threshold where the old last-cut witness already matches B. This is a mechanism obstruction on the assigned family, not an upper bound on unrestricted W and not primitive rejection.
evidence:
# Near-critical ruler: complete quadratic screen and a quantitative cap obstruction

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof candidate. No solver, numerical sweep, or
fact_submit was used. All new estimates are proved here; prior unverified
findings are not premises. Accepted fact `b98bb807d514e80d` supplies the
definitions and validity of K_n and the exact benchmark recursions; accepted
fact `1252b8823bb5a290` supplies smooth-convex interpolation. This does not
upper-bound the unrestricted W_n and does not settle the project target.

## 1. Exact schedule and all quadratic curvatures, including arbitrary b

Fix an integer m>=2. Within this document write

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j),
    n=2^m-1, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

The parameters c,a remain fixed for this entire horizon. They are not
recomputed when j changes. The symbol H_j here names a schedule, not the
conjugate jet quadratic from the project glossary. Put r=c-2 and A_mass=a/r.
Counting the occurrences of each level gives, for 0<=j<=m,

    S_j=2^j-1+a(c^j-2^j)/(c-2),
    M_j=A_mass c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j.                       (1)

There are 2^(m-j-1) occurrences of d_j in H_m. Its scalar multiplier at
curvature t in [0,1] is exactly

    P_m(t)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-d_j t)^(2^(m-j-1)).     (2)

Let p_m be H_m without its final d_0 and let h^(m,b)=(p_m,b), b>=0. Then

    sum h^(m,b)=S_m-d_0+b,
    R_(m,b)(t)=(1-bt) product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-d_j t)^N_j,
    N_0=2^(m-1)-1, N_j=2^(m-j-1) for 1<=j<m.           (3)

The exact worst normalized quadratic objective over ALL finite dimensions
is

    Q_m(b)=max_(0<=t<=1) t R_(m,b)(t)^2.                (4)

Indeed diagonalizing a positive semidefinite Hessian bounded by the identity
makes the normalized error a weighted average of the displayed scalar
quantities. A scalar quadratic attains the maximum. Zero eigenvalues have
zero objective contribution; affine translations to a minimizer change
neither calculation. Thus this is a full quadratic-class computation.

For an exact finite characterization of (4), subdivide [0,1] at all its
distinct interior roots 1/d_j and, when b>0, 1/b. On each root-free open
interval the logarithmic derivative of the nonzero objective is

    L(t)=1/t-2b/(1-bt)-2sum_j N_j d_j/(1-d_j t),
    L'(t)=-1/t^2-2b^2/(1-bt)^2
                    -2sum_j N_j d_j^2/(1-d_j t)^2<0.   (5)

Consequently there is exactly one interior maximizer between consecutive
roots, also between zero and the first root. On the last interval the
maximum is either its unique root of L or t=1. Values at roots are zero.
Coincident roots are combined, and b=0 simply removes its term. Equations
(3)--(5) specify the complete spectrum without a numerical sweep.

The unit-curvature values alone are

    P_m(1)=-(ac)^(2^m-1)c^(-m),
    R_(m,b)(1)=(1-b)(ac)^(2^m-2)c^(1-m).                (6)

They are not used as a replacement for (4).

## 2. Exact single-cut screen for every appended b

For a cut with step d, preceding mass P and following mass T, the accepted
cut value is (d-1)_+^2/[(1+P)^2(1+2T)]. For a fixed d and total schedule
mass S, its reciprocal denominator is

    D(P)=(1+P)^2[1+2(S-d-P)].

Its derivative has the sign of 2(S-d)-3P. Therefore its minimum on any
closed interval is attained at an endpoint. Among all occurrences of a
given level it suffices to check the first and last occurrence.

For h^(m,b), all levels 1<=j<m remain present. Their first and last
preceding masses are, respectively,

    P_j^first=S_j, P_j^last=S_m-d_j-S_j.                (7)

Their following masses are S_m-d_0+b-d_j-P. At level zero, after deleting
the original last occurrence, the endpoint preceding masses are

    P_0^first=0, P_0^last=S_m-2d_0-d_1,                 (8)

with following masses S_m-2d_0+b and d_1+b. For m=2 the two occurrences
in (8) refer to the same remaining index. The appended b contributes

    (b-1)_+^2/(1+S_m-d_0)^2.                           (9)

Taking the maximum of the cuts in (7)--(9) and
1/[1+2(S_m-d_0+b)] is EXACTLY K_n(h^(m,b)). No omitted internal cut can
be larger, by the denominator argument. In particular the accepted final
cut already proves W_n(h^(m,b))>=1/B_n whenever

    b>=1+(1+S_m-d_0)/sqrt(B_n).                        (10)

The global Huber term proves the same comparison whenever
b<=(B_n-1)/2-(S_m-d_0), if that right side is nonnegative. These tests use
the actual B_n, not a guessed dyadic constant.

## 3. An exact all-cut result at the original final step

For the remainder take m>=128 unless indicated, and first set b=d_0, so
the actual schedule is H_m. The following rational bounds will be used:

    12/5<lambda<c<49/20<5/2,
    3/8<a<lambda-2<1/2,
    ac>=127/128>7/8,
    0<a<c-2=r<=9/20.                                   (11)

For example lambda<17/7 gives
c<2193/896<49/20 for m>=128; a=(1-1/m)/c then exceeds3/8.
The upper bound a<lambda-2 follows from a=(m-1)/[(m+1)lambda].
Consequently 0<A_mass<1, and (1) gives

    M_j<=c^j, M_(j+1)<=c M_j,
    a c^j<=r M_j.                                      (12)

Let M=M_(m-1). For a first occurrence of any level j, P=S_j and its
following mass is at least S_(m-1). Its cut is at most
r^2/(2M-1). For a last occurrence, its preceding mass is at least
S_(m-1), and its following mass is S_j. Since x^2/(2x-1) is increasing
for x>=1 and M_j<=M, its cut is also at most

    r^2 M_j^2/[M^2(2M_j-1)]<=r^2/(2M-1).              (13)

These statements include the unique central occurrence, for which the
first and last positions coincide. Using c<=5/2, r<=1/2 and M>=1,

    r^2(2M_m-1)<= (5M-1)/4 <= 2M-1.

Thus every single-cut term is no larger than the global Huber term:

    K_n(H_m)=1/(2S_m+1).                               (14)

## 4. Full-spectrum quadratic bound at b=d_0

This argument controls every t in [0,1], not only t=1. Write
v_j=a c^j t and, for the partial ruler H_j,

    Y_j=c v_j |P_j(t)|.

If no level 0,...,m-1 satisfies d_j t>=1, all factors in (2) are
nonnegative, and 1-u<=exp(-u) gives

    t P_m(t)^2<=t exp(-2S_m t)<=1/(2e S_m).             (15)

The last maximum is over all nonnegative t, so it also bounds the actual
restricted interval. Suppose instead that j is the first level with
d_j t>=1. If j=0, Y_0=ac t<=1. If j>=1, all factors in P_j are
nonnegative and t<=1/(1+a)<=8/11. Equations (1), (11) give

    t S_j>=v_j/r-t,
    Y_j<=c v_j exp(-v_j/r+t)<=cr exp(t-1)<1.            (16)

Here the maximum of v exp(-v/r) is r/e, cr<5/4, and
exp(3/11)>1+3/11=14/11>5/4. For every subsequent level l>=j the
factor is on its nonpositive side, and the exact recursion is

    Y_(l+1)=[1-(1-t)/v_l]Y_l^2<=Y_l^2<=1.             (17)

The bracket lies in [0,1]. If an earlier factor is zero the conclusion
holds directly as well. Therefore

    t P_m(t)^2<=1/[c^2 a^2 c^(2m)t]
                      <=d_(m-1)/(c^2 a^2 c^(2m)),      (18)

using t>=1/d_(m-1). Equations (15),(18) prove the explicit full-spectrum
estimate

    Q_m(d_0)<=max{1/(2e S_m),
                 (1+a c^(m-1))/(c^2 a^2 c^(2m))}.      (19)

Both entries are strictly below (14). For the first, S_m>=1 gives
(2S_m+1)/(2e S_m)<=3/(2e)<3/4. For the second, using (12) and ac>7/8,

    (2S_m+1)(1+a c^(m-1))/(c^2 a^2 c^(2m))
       <=2/[(ac)^2 c^m]+2/[c^2 ac]
       <=16/49+25/63=2233/3087<3/4.                   (20)

For the first term of this last bound it already suffices that m>=3
and c>2. Thus, with considerable slack,

    Q_m(d_0)<(3/4)K_n(H_m).                            (21)

## 5. Exact benchmark comparison, with no fitted constant

Let rho=log_2(lambda). The accepted benchmark defines the primitive mass
C_n=S_circle(n)+1 with join

    Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,

and B_n with join G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2. We prove directly
from these recursions that

    C_n<=(n+1)^rho, B_n<=1+4n^rho.                     (22)

Put F(t)=(1+t)^rho-1, t>0. Direct differentiation, with t=exp(z), gives

    d^2/dz^2 log F(exp z)
      =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)[(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/F(t)^2>0.

The strict inequality follows by integrating the positive derivative of
(1+t)^rho-1-rho t for t>0. Convexity at z and -z gives
F(t)F(1/t)>=F(1)^2=(lambda-1)^2=2. If A=t^rho B and
D=(1+t)^rho B, this says (D-A)(D-B)>=2AB, or
D^2-(A+B)D-AB>=0. Hence

    Omega(A,B)<=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho.

Zero arguments follow by continuity. Induction in the primitive
recursion proves the first bound in (22). Since G(A,D)<=4A+D,
induction in the dominant recursion, with a split k and l=n-k-1,
gives B_n<=1+4[(k+1)^rho+l^rho]<=1+4n^rho. The last inequality follows
by integrating the increasing derivative of x^rho, including l=0.

In our family (1) implies

    M_m/lambda^m
       =(1+1/m)^m[A_mass+(1-A_mass)(2/c)^m] -> e,        (23)

since A_mass->1 and 2/c is bounded below1. Thus the EXACT finite bound

    K_n(H_m) B_n
      <=[1+4(2^m-1)^rho]/(2M_m-1)                     (24)

has limit 2/e<1. This uses an upper bound derived for the actual B_n
at every integer horizon; it assumes no asymptotic phase or decimal
value for B_n/lambda^m. In particular, the full quadratic and all-cut
baseline is strictly below U_n^ZJ for every sufficiently large m.

## 6. Retained two-block geometry and all constant tails in its cap range

Here is the precise mechanism tested next. For ANY two selected cuts i<j
of an arbitrary schedule, let P be the mass before i, S the mass strictly
between i and j, T the mass after j, and define

    M_0=1+P, M_1=1+S,
    A=(h_i-1)/M_0, epsilon=(h_j-1)/M_1, sigma=2T+1.

Assume h_i,h_j>1 and choose the cap-range angle

    0<kappa<=A/(1+epsilon).                            (25)

Use the retained prefix gradients and proximal point

    p=(1,0)/M_0,
    q=(-kappa,sqrt(kappa(A-kappa)))/M_1,
    X=(-A,0), y=X-M_1 q, d=-M_1 q.                    (26)

These prefix data are actual jets of the single Moreau envelope of
J(z)=max(0,<p,z>,<q,z>), starting at (1,0). Before the first checkpoint
the proximal points are (1-(u+1)/M_0,0), 0<=u<=P, so the p-plane is
active. That checkpoint, of size1+A M_0, sends its input p to X. In
the second block, the proposed proximal points X-tq, 1<=t<=M_1, have

    <q,X-tq>=(A kappa/M_1)(1-t/M_1)>=0,
    <q-p,X-tq>
      =A kappa/M_1+A/M_0
          -t[A kappa/M_1^2+kappa/(M_0 M_1)]
      >=(A-kappa)/M_0>0.

This verifies every actual old query, even if individual ordinary steps
are large. At the second checkpoint its jet is

    x_j=y+q, g_j=q, f_j=||q||^2/2.

For completeness, the envelope minimizes J(z)+||x-z||^2/2. This has a
unique minimizer, and an active-plane slope g at z proves optimality at
x=z+g. At two proximal points, monotonicity of the subgradients gives
||g-g'||^2<=<g-g',x-x'>, hence a 1-Lipschitz gradient. The two minimizing
inequalities identify the derivative as g; joint convexity proves
convexity of the envelope. Thus the claimed function has the required
global regularity, not only valid formal data.

The second checkpoint, of size1+M_1 epsilon, sends the iterate to
X_tail=y+epsilon d. The optimum jet is (0,0,0). Every interpolant of
this prefix has origin as an actual closest minimizer to (1,0): the
retained first checkpoint jet (p,p,||p||^2/2), interpolated with any
minimizer z, forces <p,z><=0. Its squared distance from (1,0) is
therefore at least1, attained at origin. This normalization persists
for all extensions below.

Allow ANY legal continuation with a single common gradient g at every
tail query, including the terminal sample; allow affine intercepts,
positive values and extra dimensions, and retain every prefix jet.
Its endpoint is y+epsilon d-Tg. The accepted interpolation inequality
from this endpoint to the old jet (y+q,q,||q||^2/2) gives

    2f_end<=2epsilon<d,g>-sigma||g||^2
                         <=epsilon^2||d||^2/sigma
                         =A kappa epsilon^2/sigma.

This uses a retained old query, not a reset to a new problem. From (25),
EVERY such constant-tail continuation obeys the exact universal cap

    2f_end<=U_ij:=A^2 epsilon^2/[(1+epsilon)(1+2T)].     (27)

In particular it covers all angles and all optimized tail planes of the
previous explicit two-checkpoint cap policy. It does not cover angles
kappa>A/(1+epsilon), different two-block prefixes, or variable-gradient
tails. No claim that (27) is attained for every pair is needed below.

## 7. The complete cap-range mechanism is dominated by K on H_m

Return to the full H_m, m>=128. For a selected pair i<j let their levels
be u,v; write d=a c^v=h_j-1, x=1+S, and epsilon=d/x. The individual
accepted cut terms at i and j are K_i,K_j. Direct cancellation gives

    U_ij/K_i=epsilon^2/(1+epsilon)
                          +2d epsilon/(1+2T),          (28)
    U_ij/K_j=(h_i-1)^2(1+P+h_i+S)^2
                          /[(1+P)^2 x(x+d)].           (29)

Every occurrence of level v has a full H_v immediately after it, so
T>=S_v. If v>=2 then M_v>=M_2=4+2a+ac>5, and by (11),(12),

    2d/(1+2T)<=2r M_v/(2M_v-1)<=10r/9<=1/2.

Consequently, for epsilon<=1, (28) is at most1.

If epsilon>1, then x<d. The first selected cut must lie INSIDE the
copy of H_v immediately preceding j and its level satisfies u<v.
Otherwise that copy lies between the cuts, giving S>=S_v and
x>=M_v>d. Inside this copy put P_loc for its mass before i. The
subcopies of H_u immediately before and after i yield

    P>=P_loc, x>=M_u,
    1+P_loc=M_v-(h_i-1)-x.

Also h_i-1<=d/c<=r M_v/c and x<d<=r M_v. For fixed x, the factor
(1+P+h_i+S)/(1+P) decreases with P, so substituting P_loc in (29)
gives

    U_ij/K_j
      <=(h_i-1)^2 M_v^2/
          [(M_v-(h_i-1)-x)^2 x(x+d)]
      <r^2/[2(1-r-r/c)^2]
      <=648/841<1.                                    (30)

The penultimate step uses h_i-1<=r M_u<=r x and x/(x+d)<1/2.
For the last, r<=9/20 and c>=12/5 imply 1-r-r/c>=29/80.

It remains to include the two small levels. If v=0, then d=a<1/2 and
epsilon<=d. Equation (28) is at most d^2/(1+d)+2d^2<=2/3. If v=1,

Combining (14),(27)--(30), every member of the complete constant-tail
mechanism in Section6 has normalized error at most K_n(H_m). Therefore

    max{Q_m(d_0), K_n(H_m),
        supremum of the Section6 constant-tail scores}
      =1/(2S_m+1),
    limsup B_n times this maximum <=2/e<1.             (31)

This is a quantitative failure of a concrete retained-history mechanism
on the ASSIGNED constant-level family. Its tail bound allows all
dimensions, intercepts and positive values once its prefix and angle
range are fixed. Thus retuning only its two cuts, its angle inside (25),
or its final constant-gradient plane cannot produce the target comparison
for all appended b: b=d_0 already defeats that possibility.

The unrestricted W_n may be larger. In particular, (31) gives no upper

evidence:
# Near-critical ruler: complete quadratic screen and a quantitative cap obstruction

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof candidate. No solver, numerical sweep, or
fact_submit was used. All new estimates are proved here; prior unverified
findings are not premises. Accepted fact `b98bb807d514e80d` supplies the
definitions and validity of K_n and the exact benchmark recursions; accepted
fact `1252b8823bb5a290` supplies smooth-convex interpolation. This does not
upper-bound the unrestricted W_n and does not settle the project target.

## 1. Exact schedule and all quadratic curvatures, including arbitrary b

Fix an integer m>=2. Within this document write

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j),
    n=2^m-1, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

The parameters c,a remain fixed for this entire horizon. They are not
recomputed when j changes. The symbol H_j here names a schedule, not the
conjugate jet quadratic from the project glossary. Put r=c-2 and A_mass=a/r.
Counting the occurrences of each level gives, for 0<=j<=m,

    S_j=2^j-1+a(c^j-2^j)/(c-2),
    M_j=A_mass c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j.                       (1)

There are 2^(m-j-1) occurrences of d_j in H_m. Its scalar multiplier at
curvature t in [0,1] is exactly

    P_m(t)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-d_j t)^(2^(m-j-1)).     (2)

Let p_m be H_m without its final d_0 and let h^(m,b)=(p_m,b), b>=0. Then

    sum h^(m,b)=S_m-d_0+b,
    R_(m,b)(t)=(1-bt) product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-d_j t)^N_j,
    N_0=2^(m-1)-1, N_j=2^(m-j-1) for 1<=j<m.           (3)

The exact worst normalized quadratic objective over ALL finite dimensions
is

    Q_m(b)=max_(0<=t<=1) t R_(m,b)(t)^2.                (4)

Indeed diagonalizing a positive semidefinite Hessian bounded by the identity
makes the normalized error a weighted average of the displayed scalar
quantities. A scalar quadratic attains the maximum. Zero eigenvalues have
zero objective contribution; affine translations to a minimizer change
neither calculation. Thus this is a full quadratic-class computation.

For an exact finite characterization of (4), subdivide [0,1] at all its
distinct interior roots 1/d_j and, when b>0, 1/b. On each root-free open
interval the logarithmic derivative of the nonzero objective is

    L(t)=1/t-2b/(1-bt)-2sum_j N_j d_j/(1-d_j t),
    L'(t)=-1/t^2-2b^2/(1-bt)^2
                    -2sum_j N_j d_j^2/(1-d_j t)^2<0.   (5)

Consequently there is exactly one interior maximizer between consecutive
roots, also between zero and the first root. On the last interval the
maximum is either its unique root of L or t=1. Values at roots are zero.
Coincident roots are combined, and b=0 simply removes its term. Equations
(3)--(5) specify the complete spectrum without a numerical sweep.

The unit-curvature values alone are

    P_m(1)=-(ac)^(2^m-1)c^(-m),
    R_(m,b)(1)=(1-b)(ac)^(2^m-2)c^(1-m).                (6)

They are not used as a replacement for (4).

## 2. Exact single-cut screen for every appended b

For a cut with step d, preceding mass P and following mass T, the accepted
cut value is (d-1)_+^2/[(1+P)^2(1+2T)]. For a fixed d and total schedule
mass S, its reciprocal denominator is

    D(P)=(1+P)^2[1+2(S-d-P)].

Its derivative has the sign of 2(S-d)-3P. Therefore its minimum on any
closed interval is attained at an endpoint. Among all occurrences of a
given level it suffices to check the first and last occurrence.

For h^(m,b), all levels 1<=j<m remain present. Their first and last
preceding masses are, respectively,

    P_j^first=S_j, P_j^last=S_m-d_j-S_j.                (7)

Their following masses are S_m-d_0+b-d_j-P. At level zero, after deleting
the original last occurrence, the endpoint preceding masses are

    P_0^first=0, P_0^last=S_m-2d_0-d_1,                 (8)

with following masses S_m-2d_0+b and d_1+b. For m=2 the two occurrences
in (8) refer to the same remaining index. The appended b contributes

    (b-1)_+^2/(1+S_m-d_0)^2.                           (9)

Taking the maximum of the cuts in (7)--(9) and
1/[1+2(S_m-d_0+b)] is EXACTLY K_n(h^(m,b)). No omitted internal cut can
be larger, by the denominator argument. In particular the accepted final
cut already proves W_n(h^(m,b))>=1/B_n whenever

    b>=1+(1+S_m-d_0)/sqrt(B_n).                        (10)

The global Huber term proves the same comparison whenever
b<=(B_n-1)/2-(S_m-d_0), if that right side is nonnegative. These tests use
the actual B_n, not a guessed dyadic constant.

## 3. An exact all-cut result at the original final step

For the remainder take m>=128 unless indicated, and first set b=d_0, so
the actual schedule is H_m. The following rational bounds will be used:

    12/5<lambda<c<49/20<5/2,
    3/8<a<lambda-2<1/2,
    ac>=127/128>7/8,
    0<a<c-2=r<=9/20.                                   (11)

For example lambda<17/7 gives
c<2193/896<49/20 for m>=128; a=(1-1/m)/c then exceeds3/8.
The upper bound a<lambda-2 follows from a=(m-1)/[(m+1)lambda].
Consequently 0<A_mass<1, and (1) gives

    M_j<=c^j, M_(j+1)<=c M_j,
    a c^j<=r M_j.                                      (12)

Let M=M_(m-1). For a first occurrence of any level j, P=S_j and its
following mass is at least S_(m-1). Its cut is at most
r^2/(2M-1). For a last occurrence, its preceding mass is at least
S_(m-1), and its following mass is S_j. Since x^2/(2x-1) is increasing
for x>=1 and M_j<=M, its cut is also at most

    r^2 M_j^2/[M^2(2M_j-1)]<=r^2/(2M-1).              (13)

These statements include the unique central occurrence, for which the
first and last positions coincide. Using c<=5/2, r<=1/2 and M>=1,

    r^2(2M_m-1)<= (5M-1)/4 <= 2M-1.

Thus every single-cut term is no larger than the global Huber term:

    K_n(H_m)=1/(2S_m+1).                               (14)

## 4. Full-spectrum quadratic bound at b=d_0

This argument controls every t in [0,1], not only t=1. Write
v_j=a c^j t and, for the partial ruler H_j,

    Y_j=c v_j |P_j(t)|.

If no level 0,...,m-1 satisfies d_j t>=1, all factors in (2) are
nonnegative, and 1-u<=exp(-u) gives

    t P_m(t)^2<=t exp(-2S_m t)<=1/(2e S_m).             (15)

The last maximum is over all nonnegative t, so it also bounds the actual
restricted interval. Suppose instead that j is the first level with
d_j t>=1. If j=0, Y_0=ac t<=1. If j>=1, all factors in P_j are
nonnegative and t<=1/(1+a)<=8/11. Equations (1), (11) give

    t S_j>=v_j/r-t,
    Y_j<=c v_j exp(-v_j/r+t)<=cr exp(t-1)<1.            (16)

Here the maximum of v exp(-v/r) is r/e, cr<5/4, and
exp(3/11)>1+3/11=14/11>5/4. For every subsequent level l>=j the
factor is on its nonpositive side, and the exact recursion is

    Y_(l+1)=[1-(1-t)/v_l]Y_l^2<=Y_l^2<=1.             (17)

The bracket lies in [0,1]. If an earlier factor is zero the conclusion
holds directly as well. Therefore

    t P_m(t)^2<=1/[c^2 a^2 c^(2m)t]
                      <=d_(m-1)/(c^2 a^2 c^(2m)),      (18)

using t>=1/d_(m-1). Equations (15),(18) prove the explicit full-spectrum
estimate

    Q_m(d_0)<=max{1/(2e S_m),
                 (1+a c^(m-1))/(c^2 a^2 c^(2m))}.      (19)

Both entries are strictly below (14). For the first, S_m>=1 gives
(2S_m+1)/(2e S_m)<=3/(2e)<3/4. For the second, using (12) and ac>7/8,

    (2S_m+1)(1+a c^(m-1))/(c^2 a^2 c^(2m))
       <=2/[(ac)^2 c^m]+2/[c^2 ac]
       <=16/49+25/63=2233/3087<3/4.                   (20)

For the first term of this last bound it already suffices that m>=3
and c>2. Thus, with considerable slack,

    Q_m(d_0)<(3/4)K_n(H_m).                            (21)

## 5. Exact benchmark comparison, with no fitted constant

Let rho=log_2(lambda). The accepted benchmark defines the primitive mass
C_n=S_circle(n)+1 with join

    Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,

and B_n with join G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2. We prove directly
from these recursions that

    C_n<=(n+1)^rho, B_n<=1+4n^rho.                     (22)

Put F(t)=(1+t)^rho-1, t>0. Direct differentiation, with t=exp(z), gives

    d^2/dz^2 log F(exp z)
      =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)[(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/F(t)^2>0.

The strict inequality follows by integrating the positive derivative of
(1+t)^rho-1-rho t for t>0. Convexity at z and -z gives
F(t)F(1/t)>=F(1)^2=(lambda-1)^2=2. If A=t^rho B and
D=(1+t)^rho B, this says (D-A)(D-B)>=2AB, or
D^2-(A+B)D-AB>=0. Hence

    Omega(A,B)<=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho.

Zero arguments follow by continuity. Induction in the primitive
recursion proves the first bound in (22). Since G(A,D)<=4A+D,
induction in the dominant recursion, with a split k and l=n-k-1,
gives B_n<=1+4[(k+1)^rho+l^rho]<=1+4n^rho. The last inequality follows
by integrating the increasing derivative of x^rho, including l=0.

In our family (1) implies

    M_m/lambda^m
       =(1+1/m)^m[A_mass+(1-A_mass)(2/c)^m] -> e,        (23)

since A_mass->1 and 2/c is bounded below1. Thus the EXACT finite bound

    K_n(H_m) B_n
      <=[1+4(2^m-1)^rho]/(2M_m-1)                     (24)

has limit 2/e<1. This uses an upper bound derived for the actual B_n
at every integer horizon; it assumes no asymptotic phase or decimal
value for B_n/lambda^m. In particular, the full quadratic and all-cut
baseline is strictly below U_n^ZJ for every sufficiently large m.

## 6. Retained two-block geometry and all constant tails in its cap range

Here is the precise mechanism tested next. For ANY two selected cuts i<j
of an arbitrary schedule, let P be the mass before i, S the mass strictly
between i and j, T the mass after j, and define

    M_0=1+P, M_1=1+S,
    A=(h_i-1)/M_0, epsilon=(h_j-1)/M_1, sigma=2T+1.

Assume h_i,h_j>1 and choose the cap-range angle

    0<kappa<=A/(1+epsilon).                            (25)

Use the retained prefix gradients and proximal point

    p=(1,0)/M_0,
    q=(-kappa,sqrt(kappa(A-kappa)))/M_1,
    X=(-A,0), y=X-M_1 q, d=-M_1 q.                    (26)

These prefix data are actual jets of the single Moreau envelope of
J(z)=max(0,<p,z>,<q,z>), starting at (1,0). Before the first checkpoint
the proximal points are (1-(u+1)/M_0,0), 0<=u<=P, so the p-plane is
active. That checkpoint, of size1+A M_0, sends its input p to X. In
the second block, the proposed proximal points X-tq, 1<=t<=M_1, have

    <q,X-tq>=(A kappa/M_1)(1-t/M_1)>=0,
    <q-p,X-tq>
      =A kappa/M_1+A/M_0
          -t[A kappa/M_1^2+kappa/(M_0 M_1)]
      >=(A-kappa)/M_0>0.

This verifies every actual old query, even if individual ordinary steps
are large. At the second checkpoint its jet is

    x_j=y+q, g_j=q, f_j=||q||^2/2.

For completeness, the envelope minimizes J(z)+||x-z||^2/2. This has a
unique minimizer, and an active-plane slope g at z proves optimality at
x=z+g. At two proximal points, monotonicity of the subgradients gives
||g-g'||^2<=<g-g',x-x'>, hence a 1-Lipschitz gradient. The two minimizing
inequalities identify the derivative as g; joint convexity proves
convexity of the envelope. Thus the claimed function has the required
global regularity, not only valid formal data.

The second checkpoint, of size1+M_1 epsilon, sends the iterate to
X_tail=y+epsilon d. The optimum jet is (0,0,0). Every interpolant of
this prefix has origin as an actual closest minimizer to (1,0): the
retained first checkpoint jet (p,p,||p||^2/2), interpolated with any
minimizer z, forces <p,z><=0. Its squared distance from (1,0) is
therefore at least1, attained at origin. This normalization persists
for all extensions below.

Allow ANY legal continuation with a single common gradient g at every
tail query, including the terminal sample; allow affine intercepts,
positive values and extra dimensions, and retain every prefix jet.
Its endpoint is y+epsilon d-Tg. The accepted interpolation inequality
from this endpoint to the old jet (y+q,q,||q||^2/2) gives

    2f_end<=2epsilon<d,g>-sigma||g||^2
                         <=epsilon^2||d||^2/sigma
                         =A kappa epsilon^2/sigma.

This uses a retained old query, not a reset to a new problem. From (25),
EVERY such constant-tail continuation obeys the exact universal cap

    2f_end<=U_ij:=A^2 epsilon^2/[(1+epsilon)(1+2T)].     (27)

In particular it covers all angles and all optimized tail planes of the
previous explicit two-checkpoint cap policy. It does not cover angles
kappa>A/(1+epsilon), different two-block prefixes, or variable-gradient
tails. No claim that (27) is attained for every pair is needed below.

## 7. The complete cap-range mechanism is dominated by K on H_m

Return to the full H_m, m>=128. For a selected pair i<j let their levels
be u,v; write d=a c^v=h_j-1, x=1+S, and epsilon=d/x. The individual
accepted cut terms at i and j are K_i,K_j. Direct cancellation gives

    U_ij/K_i=epsilon^2/(1+epsilon)
                          +2d epsilon/(1+2T),          (28)
    U_ij/K_j=(h_i-1)^2(1+P+h_i+S)^2
                          /[(1+P)^2 x(x+d)].           (29)

Every occurrence of level v has a full H_v immediately after it, so
T>=S_v. If v>=2 then M_v>=M_2=4+2a+ac>5, and by (11),(12),

    2d/(1+2T)<=2r M_v/(2M_v-1)<=10r/9<=1/2.

Consequently, for epsilon<=1, (28) is at most1.

If epsilon>1, then x<d. The first selected cut must lie INSIDE the
copy of H_v immediately preceding j and its level satisfies u<v.
Otherwise that copy lies between the cuts, giving S>=S_v and
x>=M_v>d. Inside this copy put P_loc for its mass before i. The
subcopies of H_u immediately before and after i yield

    P>=P_loc, x>=M_u,
    1+P_loc=M_v-(h_i-1)-x.

Also h_i-1<=d/c<=r M_v/c and x<d<=r M_v. For fixed x, the factor
(1+P+h_i+S)/(1+P) decreases with P, so substituting P_loc in (29)
gives

    U_ij/K_j
      <=(h_i-1)^2 M_v^2/
          [(M_v-(h_i-1)-x)^2 x(x+d)]
      <r^2/[2(1-r-r/c)^2]
      <=648/841<1.                                    (30)

The penultimate step uses h_i-1<=r M_u<=r x and x/(x+d)<1/2.
For the last, r<=9/20 and c>=12/5 imply 1-r-r/c>=29/80.

It remains to include the two small levels. If v=0, then d=a<1/2 and
epsilon<=d. Equation (28) is at most d^2/(1+d)+2d^2<=2/3. If v=1,
then d=ac<1. Unless i is the one level-zero step immediately before j,
the intervening mass includes H_1, so epsilon<=1/2 and T>=S_1>=1;
(28) is then at most1/6+1/3=1/2. For that one adjacent pair x=1 and
h_i-1=a. Equation (29) is bounded by

    a^2(2+a)^2/(1+ac)<=1/(1+ac)<1,

because a<=sqrt(2)-1 implies a(2+a)<=1. This covers EVERY ordered pair,
including pairs near the end and repeated occurrences of either level.

Combining (14),(27)--(30), every member of the complete constant-tail
mechanism in Section6 has normalized error at most K_n(H_m). Therefore

    max{Q_m(d_0), K_n(H_m),
        supremum of the Section6 constant-tail scores}
      =1/(2S_m+1),
    limsup B_n times this maximum <=2/e<1.             (31)

This is a quantitative failure of a concrete retained-history mechanism
on the ASSIGNED constant-level family. Its tail bound allows all
dimensions, intercepts and positive values once its prefix and angle
range are fixed. Thus retuning only its two cuts, its angle inside (25),
or its final constant-gradient plane cannot produce the target comparison
for all appended b: b=d_0 already defeats that possibility.

The unrestricted W_n may be larger. In particular, (31) gives no upper
certificate for it, no primitive-validity conclusion, and no decision of
the original all-schedule/all-horizon problem. The remaining exact branch
is to leave (25), change more than two prefix cells, or allow genuinely
varying gradients within the remaining ruler block while retaining all
queried jets and the closest-minimizer normalization.

## 8. The entire accepted alternating-ray family also collapses to K

We now invoke the exact ray recurrence from accepted fact
`1fca3e5dd555cb4a`. No unverified ray exclusion is used. For any two
indices i<j in H_m, write P,S for their preceding and intervening masses,
and let u,v be their levels. Put r_u=a c^u and r_v=a c^v. We claim

    r_u r_v<(1+P)(1+S).                               (32)

If u>=v, or if i lies before the full H_v immediately preceding j,
the local copies give 1+P>=M_u and 1+S>=M_v. Thus (32) follows from
r_u<=r M_u, r_v<=r M_v and r<1.

Otherwise u<v and i lies inside that preceding H_v. Define P_loc there.
The local H_u copies on both sides of i give

    1+P_loc>=M_u, 1+S>=M_u,
    (1+P_loc)+(1+S)=M_v-r_u.

Expanding [(1+P_loc)-M_u][(1+S)-M_u]>=0 shows

    (1+P)(1+S)>=M_u(M_v-r_u-M_u).

For fixed u define D_v=M_u(M_v-r_u-M_u)-r_u r_v.
At v=u+1, the identity M_(u+1)=2M_u+r_u gives

    D_(u+1)=M_u^2-c r_u^2
               >=(1-cr^2)M_u^2>0,

since cr^2<=3969/8000<1. At successive levels,

    D_(v+1)-D_v=M_u M_v+[M_u-(c-1)r_u]r_v>0,

because (c-1)r<=261/400<1. This proves (32) for every pair, including
the small levels with empty local blocks.

Suppose a ray construction selected at least two checkpoints i,j. Its
first two gradients and first old offset are

    m_0=1/(1+P), m_1=r_u m_0/(1+S), O_1=P m_0.

By (32), the second-return budget satisfies

    r_v m_1-O_1
       =m_0[r_u r_v/(1+S)-P]<m_0.                    (33)

With exactly two checkpoints, the terminal old-slope constraint requires
this quantity to be at least (1+T)m_0>=m_0. With three or more, the next
nonterminal gradient is this quantity divided by1 plus its block mass,
and hence is strictly below m_0, violating same-ray slope monotonicity.
Thus no accepted ray construction has two or more checkpoints. The
zero- and one-checkpoint cases recover K exactly, so

    F_ray_n(H_m)=K_n(H_m)=1/(2S_m+1).                  (34)

## 9. The complete universal complex lens is also below Huber

This concerns the accepted Lens_n and maximal path-value Gap_h from fact
`dfde2fa326c908bf`, not the larger schedule-dependent domain D_h. The
accepted bound is

    Gap_(H_m)(z)<=(2alpha-|z|^2)|P_m(z)|^2,
    z=alpha+i beta,
    kappa_lens=alpha-|z|^2>=|beta|cot(pi/(n+2)).        (35)

All chronological prefix jets and their interpolation cycles remain those
of the accepted definition. We only bound their actual terminal polynomial.
We prove, for m>=128,

    sup_(z in Lens_n) Gap_(H_m)(z)<1/(2S_m+1).         (36)

The endpoints z=0 and z=1 follow directly: the former has zero error,
and at the latter the upper bound in (35) is P_m(1)^2, covered by (21).
Every other lens point has 0<alpha<1 and kappa_lens>0. Put

    delta=tan(pi/(n+2))<=1/100,
    tau_z=|1-z|^2/(2kappa_lens),
    q_decay=99/100.

The delta bound follows from tan x<=2x for 0<=x<=1/2 and pi<4,
since n=2^m-1. The tangent inequality follows from sin x<=x and
cos x>=1-x^2/2>=7/8 on that interval. From the lens inequality,

    |beta|<=delta alpha(1-alpha),
    kappa_lens>=alpha(1-alpha)(1-delta^2/4),
    tau_z<=F_delta(1-alpha)/(2alpha),
    F_delta=(1+delta^2)/(1-delta^2/4)<101/100.           (37)

Consider a partial ruler H_j all of whose levels l<j satisfy
a c^l<tau_z, with j>=1. In particular tau_z>a>3/8, and (37) gives
alpha<101/176<3/5. Each step d_l of H_j satisfies

    d_l alpha<(1+tau_z)alpha
       <=alpha+F_delta(1-alpha)/2<81/100.              (38)

Its real factor is therefore positive, at least19/100. The inequalities
log(1-u)<=-u and log(1+u)<=u imply

    log|1-d_l z|
      <=-d_l alpha+d_l^2 beta^2/[2(19/100)^2].

Sum with the exact multiplicities of the partial ruler. Its sum of
squared steps is at most its largest step times S_j, and (38) bounds
that largest step by81/(100alpha). Hence

    |P_j(z)|<=exp[-(1-12delta^2)alpha S_j]
                       <=exp(-q_decay alpha S_j).    (39)

For the numerical coefficient here,
(81/100)/[2(19/100)^2]=4050/361<12, and
1-12/10000>99/100. This is a symbolic bound; no spectral sampling occurs.

If no level l<m reaches a c^l>=tau_z, (39) applies to H_m. From (35),

    Gap_(H_m)(z)<=2alpha exp(-2q_decay S_m alpha)
                        <=1/(q_decay e S_m).

Since S_m>=2 and e>8/3, its ratio to Huber is strictly less than

    (5/2)/(q_decay(8/3))=125/132<1.                   (40)

Otherwise let j<m be the first level with a c^j>=tau_z. Put
Y_j=c a c^j |z| |P_j(z)|. If j=0, Y_0=ac|z|<=ac<1.
If j>=1, (39) and S_j>=a c^j/r-1 give, by maximizing
v exp(-q_decay v/r) over v>=0,

    Y_j<= [cr sqrt(1+delta^2)/q_decay]
                              exp(q_decay alpha-1)
       <=(9/8)exp(-2/5)<1.                           (41)

and dividing their product by99/100 gives a number below9/8.
Also alpha<3/5 and exp(2/5)>1+2/5>9/8.

For every level l>=j, the definition of tau_z gives exactly

    |1-d_l z|^2
      =a^2 c^(2l)|z|^2+|1-z|^2-2a c^l kappa_lens
      <=a^2 c^(2l)|z|^2.

Consequently the ruler recursion implies Y_(l+1)<=Y_l^2, so Y_m<=1.
If alpha>1/16, (35) and |z|>=alpha imply that the ratio of its bound
to Huber is at most

    (2S_m+1) 32/[c^2 a^2 c^(2m)]
      <=64/[(ac)^2 c^m]<128/2^m<1.                   (42)

If alpha<=1/16, then tau_z>=(1-alpha)/(2alpha)>=15/2>a,

                  <(9/8)(16/15)(3/8)=9/20<1/2.

Equation (35) is therefore at most

    1/[8c^2 a^2 c^(2m)alpha]
       <=d_(m-1)/[4c^2 a^2 c^(2m)].                  (43)

By (20), its ratio to Huber is less than3/16. Equations (40)--(43)
cover every lens point and prove (36). Consequently

    V_lens(H_m)=K_n(H_m)=F_ray_n(H_m)=1/(2S_m+1).      (44)

claim: C32 global three-step capacity screen: any primitive h=(u,v,w) with T=1+u+v+w>=3+2sqrt2 is either exactly Silver or must lie in the asymmetric region sqrt2<u<7/4, 1<v<2, 1<w<sqrt2, T<7, u+w>=2T/(1+sqrt2)-2. evidence:
# A necessary asymmetric region for a three-step capacity improvement

Status: complete candidate reductions and a scoped optimization result;
NOT verifier-accepted. No solver or fact_submit. The public max4 candidates
5b4359baa88bf3e4 and 500d209094028aef suggested the witnesses; all needed
legal data and deductions are included here, not used as unverified facts.
Accepted input: smooth-convex interpolation in 1252b8823bb5a290.

## 1. Statement

For h=(u,v,w) in [0,infinity)^3 put T=1+u+v+w. Write V_h for the
intrinsic primitive energy defined below. Call h primitive if V_h>=0
on every finite-dimensional convex differentiable 1-smooth GD run with
a minimizer. Put t=sqrt(2), lambda=1+t, and T_0=lambda^2=3+2t.

If h is primitive and T>=T_0, then either

    h=(t,2,t), T=T_0,

or necessarily

    t<u<7/4,   1<v<2,   1<w<t,
    T_0<=T<7,  u+w>=2T/lambda-2.                   (1)

The scalar constraints below further restrict the remaining region.
This does NOT exclude region (1) and does NOT prove the global
three-step capacity bound. It is a global, orientation-sensitive
reduction beyond the existing local and fixed-middle-step results.

For the remaining region, the one-parameter completion of the mixed
two-dimensional witness in Section5 cannot strengthen its original
endpoint choice. Every finite interpolation inequality is checked.

## 2. Actual witnesses and all their legality conditions

For any legal run use

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0,
    V_h=2sum_(i<3)h_i(f_i-f_3)
         +sum_(i<3)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
         -(T-1)T||g_3||^2.

For data with f_i=<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2 and x_3=g_3, set
y_i=x_i-g_i. Expansion gives

    Q_ij=<g_i-g_j,y_j>, Q_(i,3)=0,
    V_h=||x_0||^2-T^2||g_3||^2.                   (2)

All witnesses used below have these properties and include the legal
optimum jet (0,0,0). Besides the finite Q conditions, optimum legality
requires <g_i,y_i>>=0; the other direction is saturated by the value
formula. A feasible finite array is realized by the conjugate maximum
of quadratics in accepted 1252b8823bb5a290. Thus the arrays specify
fixed globally smooth convex functions with a minimizer.

The interval-projection witness at any selected step b, with ordinary
sums P,Q, has gradient 1 before b and -(b-1)/(Q+1) after it, starting
at P+1 and ending at its negative threshold, when b>1. Formula (2)
gives the necessary cut condition

    T(b-1)_+<=(P+1)(Q+1).                         (3)

This is a direct fixed clipped-derivative construction, including zero
ordinary steps. Apply it at the first and last step to obtain

    u,w<=M(T):=2T/(T+1)<2.                        (4)

For u,v,w>1 abbreviate

    a=u-1, A=u+1, r=v-1, D=w+1, eta=r/D;
    T=A+D+r.

The full-curvature quadratic f(x)=x^2/2, x_0=1, gives

    F_Q=1-T^2 a^2 r^2(w-1)^2>=0.                  (5)

The middle-cut interval, with x=(A,1,-r,-eta) and
g=(1,1,-eta,-eta), gives

    F_B=A^2-T^2 eta^2>=0, or Tr<=AD.              (6)

If r(w-1)<=1, the one-sided Huber derivative min(x,1), started at A,
has x=(A,1,-r,r(w-1)) and g=(1,1,-r,r(w-1)). It gives

    F_C=A^2-T^2 r^2(w-1)^2>=0.                   (7)

When eta a<1, a two-dimensional mixed witness gives

    F_N=a u F_B+(1+eta)u^2(2-u^2)>=0.             (8)

Here is its complete verification. Combine the middle-cut base array
from (6) with the auxiliary scalar array

    x_aux=(1,-a,ra,eta a),
    g_aux=(1,-a,eta a,eta a),
    f_aux,i=x_aux,i*g_aux,i-g_aux,i^2/2.

The auxiliary proximal points are (0,0,w eta a,0). Its only positive
finite residual is Q_aux,(0,2)=(1-eta a)w eta a. Every optimum
inequality is legal because g_aux,i*y_aux,i>=0. The base proximal
points are (u,0,-w eta,0); its Q_(0,2)=-(1+eta)w eta and all its
residuals are nonpositive. With

    epsilon=(1+eta)/[a(1-eta a)],

take the orthogonal sum of the base and sqrt(epsilon) times the
auxiliary points and gradients, with the summed values. Residuals add;
the sole positive auxiliary edge is exactly canceled and every other
edge is nonpositive. The energy equals

    F_B+epsilon(1-T^2 eta^2 a^2)
       =F_N/[a(1-eta a)].                         (9)

For the algebra use 1-a^2 A^2=u^2(2-u^2). This proves (8) with
all actual edges, rather than an assumed two-dimensional interpolant.

## 3. A uniform box where all four witnesses apply

Assume T>=T_0 and all the cut conditions (3). First v>1. Otherwise
T=1+u+v+w<=2+2M(T), so T^2-5T-2<=0. At T=T_0 this polynomial
equals 2t>0 and it increases thereafter, a contradiction.

Thus r>0 and the middle cut (6) applies. As T=A+D+r,

    T(T-A-D)<=AD<=(A+D)^2/4,
    T<=lambda(A+D)/2<=lambda(M(T)+1).

Consequently

    T^2+(1-3lambda)T-lambda<=0.                    (10)

Its left side increases for T>=T_0, and at T=7 equals
56-22lambda>0 because lambda<5/2. Hence T<7 and (4) gives
u,w<7/4.

Both u and w exceed1. If, for example, u<=1, then A<=2, D<11/4,
so r=T-A-D>T-19/4. But

    Tr>T(T-19/4)>=T_0(T_0-19/4)
       =11/4+5t/2>11/2>AD,

contradicting the middle cut. The argument for w is identical.

On this entire necessary box the extra hypotheses of (7) and (8) hold:

    r(w-1)<=A(w^2-1)/T<363/(64T_0)<1,
    eta a<=Aa/T=(u^2-1)/T<33/(16T_0)<1.           (11)

For the first strict numerical comparison, 363<64T_0 is equivalent
to 171<128sqrt(2), and squaring gives 29241<32768. Thus no local
neighborhood restriction is being silently used in this global screen.
The earlier inequality T<=lambda(A+D)/2 also gives

    u+w>=2T/lambda-2>=2t.                         (12)

## 4. Excluding three of the four endpoint orientations

Suppose u<=t. By (12), w>=t. Since T>=T_0 and w<2, the difference
between the two sides of the necessary inequality Tr(w-1)<=A is
at least

    T_0(T_0-t-w-2)(w-1)-(t+1)
       =T_0(w-t)(2-w)>=0.                         (13)

It is strictly positive unless u=w=t and T=T_0. In that exceptional
case v=2. Hence every other candidate must have u>t.

Suppose next that also w>=t. On the rectangle [t,M(T)]^2 consider

    q_T(u,w)=T(u-1)(w-1)(T-u-w-2).

This function is strictly concave in either endpoint with the other
fixed. Its minimum is attained at a corner. At T=T_0, M(T_0)=1+t/2,
the corner values are

    q_(T_0)(t,t)=1,
    q_(T_0)(t,M(T_0))=q_(T_0)(M(T_0),t)=lambda/2>1,
    q_(T_0)(M(T_0),M(T_0))=lambda/2>1.

Each corner value strictly increases with T>=T_0. All its positive
factors increase; in particular the derivatives of
T-t-M(T)-2 and T-2M(T)-2 are respectively
1-2/(T+1)^2 and 1-4/(T+1)^2, both positive.
Thus q_T>1 except at the single point T=T_0,u=w=t. This contradicts
the quadratic condition (5). Every nonexceptional candidate therefore
satisfies u>t>w.

Finally its middle step is less than2. For u>t the expression F_N in
(8), with u,w held fixed, strictly decreases as r>0 increases: the
negative squared term in F_B decreases, while u^2(2-u^2)<0.
At r=1 a direct expansion gives

    D^2 F_N/u
       =P_u(D):=u^2 D^2+(4-2u^2-u^3)D-(u-1)(u+2)^2.

This polynomial has one positive and one negative root, since its
leading coefficient is positive and its constant term negative. Also

    P_u(lambda)=-(lambda+1)u^3-2u^2+4(lambda+1)<0

for u>t: the right side vanishes at t and has strictly negative
derivative for u>0. Its positive root is therefore beyond lambda,
and P_u(D)<0 for 0<D<=lambda. Since w<t gives D<lambda, F_N<0
at r=1 and at every r>=1. Necessarily r<1, proving (1).

The remaining constraints can be written without a mixed-energy
abbreviation. In the box (1), a primitive candidate must satisfy

    Tr<=AD,
    T a r(w-1)<=1,
    u^2+u-1+u(2-u^2)eta-(u-1)T^2 eta^2>=0.        (14)

The last expression is F_N/u after expansion. No sufficiency of (14)
is asserted, and no global feasibility or infeasibility conclusion for
this remaining box is claimed.

## 5. Optimizing a continuous auxiliary completion does not improve F_N

Work in box (1) and assume the scalar tests F_B,F_Q>=0. Keep the same
base array in (6), but vary the auxiliary third gradient. Put k=ra<1
and choose z in [k/(w+1),k]. Use

    x_aux=(1,-a,k,k-wz),
    g_aux=(1,-a,z,k-wz),
    f_aux,i=x_aux,i*g_aux,i-g_aux,i^2/2.

Every GD equation is exact. The sole possibly nonzero proximal point
is y_aux,2=k-z>=0. The residuals entering query2 are

    Q_aux,(0,2)=(1-z)(k-z),
    Q_aux,(1,2)=(-a-z)(k-z)<=0,
    Q_aux,(3,2)=(k-(w+1)z)(k-z)<=0.

Every other finite residual is zero, and every optimum constraint is
valid. For z<k the complete legal range of mixing coefficients is

    0<=epsilon<=epsilon_max(z)
       =(1+eta)w eta/[(1-z)(k-z)].                 (15)

The same active edge is exactly canceled at the upper endpoint.
The mixed energy is

    F_B+epsilon[1-T^2(k-wz)^2].                    (16)

Let q=k-wz, A_0=w-k>0, B_0=k(w-1)>0. The quadratic test says
T B_0<=1. Since q ranges from q_0=k/(w+1) down to -B_0, the bracket
in (16) can be negative only when q>1/T. In that case epsilon_max
is optimal. Apart from its positive constant factor, the improvement
over F_B is

    R(q)=(T^2 q^2-1)/[(q+A_0)(q+B_0)].

For q>1/T its derivative has numerator

    T^2(A_0+B_0)q^2+2(T^2 A_0B_0+1)q+(A_0+B_0)>0.

The greatest improvement is therefore at the largest q=q_0, namely
z=k/(w+1)=eta a. This is exactly the auxiliary choice in (8)--(9).
If q_0<=1/T there is no negative auxiliary energy anywhere in the
family. At z=k all auxiliary proximal points are zero and its energy
is F_Q>=0, so this boundary supplies no additional improvement.

Thus the original mixed witness is already optimal in this whole
one-parameter completion family, with arbitrary admissible mixture
weight. Repairing the remaining region (1) requires another change of
geometry or a separate algebraic argument, rather than this retuning.

## 6. Reversal caution

The downloaded and read Grimmer--Shu--Wang paper arXiv:2410.16249v2,
Section3.1, and Zhang--Jiang arXiv:2410.12395, Proposition5.5, establish
reversal properties for their recursively constructed basic schedules.
The checked statements do not supply reversal invariance for every
primitive schedule. No reversal theorem is used in Sections1--5.
The asymmetric region (1) cannot be discarded by silently swapping
u and w.
