evidence:
# Near-critical ruler: complete quadratic screen and a quantitative cap obstruction

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof candidate. No solver, numerical sweep, or
fact_submit was used. All new estimates are proved here; prior unverified
findings are not premises. Accepted fact `b98bb807d514e80d` supplies the
definitions and validity of K_n and the exact benchmark recursions; accepted
fact `1252b8823bb5a290` supplies smooth-convex interpolation. This does not
upper-bound the unrestricted W_n and does not settle the project target.

## 1. Exact schedule and all quadratic curvatures, including arbitrary b

Fix an integer m>=2. Within this document write

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j),
    n=2^m-1, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

The parameters c,a remain fixed for this entire horizon. They are not
recomputed when j changes. The symbol H_j here names a schedule, not the
conjugate jet quadratic from the project glossary. Put r=c-2 and A_mass=a/r.
Counting the occurrences of each level gives, for 0<=j<=m,

    S_j=2^j-1+a(c^j-2^j)/(c-2),
    M_j=A_mass c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j.                       (1)

There are 2^(m-j-1) occurrences of d_j in H_m. Its scalar multiplier at
curvature t in [0,1] is exactly

    P_m(t)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-d_j t)^(2^(m-j-1)).     (2)

Let p_m be H_m without its final d_0 and let h^(m,b)=(p_m,b), b>=0. Then

    sum h^(m,b)=S_m-d_0+b,
    R_(m,b)(t)=(1-bt) product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-d_j t)^N_j,
    N_0=2^(m-1)-1, N_j=2^(m-j-1) for 1<=j<m.           (3)

The exact worst normalized quadratic objective over ALL finite dimensions
is

    Q_m(b)=max_(0<=t<=1) t R_(m,b)(t)^2.                (4)

Indeed diagonalizing a positive semidefinite Hessian bounded by the identity
makes the normalized error a weighted average of the displayed scalar
quantities. A scalar quadratic attains the maximum. Zero eigenvalues have
zero objective contribution; affine translations to a minimizer change
neither calculation. Thus this is a full quadratic-class computation.

For an exact finite characterization of (4), subdivide [0,1] at all its
distinct interior roots 1/d_j and, when b>0, 1/b. On each root-free open
interval the logarithmic derivative of the nonzero objective is

    L(t)=1/t-2b/(1-bt)-2sum_j N_j d_j/(1-d_j t),
    L'(t)=-1/t^2-2b^2/(1-bt)^2
                    -2sum_j N_j d_j^2/(1-d_j t)^2<0.   (5)

Consequently there is exactly one interior maximizer between consecutive
roots, also between zero and the first root. On the last interval the
maximum is either its unique root of L or t=1. Values at roots are zero.
Coincident roots are combined, and b=0 simply removes its term. Equations
(3)--(5) specify the complete spectrum without a numerical sweep.

The unit-curvature values alone are

    P_m(1)=-(ac)^(2^m-1)c^(-m),
    R_(m,b)(1)=(1-b)(ac)^(2^m-2)c^(1-m).                (6)

They are not used as a replacement for (4).

## 2. Exact single-cut screen for every appended b

For a cut with step d, preceding mass P and following mass T, the accepted
cut value is (d-1)_+^2/[(1+P)^2(1+2T)]. For a fixed d and total schedule
mass S, its reciprocal denominator is

    D(P)=(1+P)^2[1+2(S-d-P)].

Its derivative has the sign of 2(S-d)-3P. Therefore its minimum on any
closed interval is attained at an endpoint. Among all occurrences of a
given level it suffices to check the first and last occurrence.

For h^(m,b), all levels 1<=j<m remain present. Their first and last
preceding masses are, respectively,

    P_j^first=S_j, P_j^last=S_m-d_j-S_j.                (7)

Their following masses are S_m-d_0+b-d_j-P. At level zero, after deleting
the original last occurrence, the endpoint preceding masses are

    P_0^first=0, P_0^last=S_m-2d_0-d_1,                 (8)

with following masses S_m-2d_0+b and d_1+b. For m=2 the two occurrences
in (8) refer to the same remaining index. The appended b contributes

    (b-1)_+^2/(1+S_m-d_0)^2.                           (9)

Taking the maximum of the cuts in (7)--(9) and
1/[1+2(S_m-d_0+b)] is EXACTLY K_n(h^(m,b)). No omitted internal cut can
be larger, by the denominator argument. In particular the accepted final
cut already proves W_n(h^(m,b))>=1/B_n whenever

    b>=1+(1+S_m-d_0)/sqrt(B_n).                        (10)

The global Huber term proves the same comparison whenever
b<=(B_n-1)/2-(S_m-d_0), if that right side is nonnegative. These tests use
the actual B_n, not a guessed dyadic constant.

## 3. An exact all-cut result at the original final step

For the remainder take m>=128 unless indicated, and first set b=d_0, so
the actual schedule is H_m. The following rational bounds will be used:

    12/5<lambda<c<49/20<5/2,
    3/8<a<lambda-2<1/2,
    ac>=127/128>7/8,
    0<a<c-2=r<=9/20.                                   (11)

For example lambda<17/7 gives
c<2193/896<49/20 for m>=128; a=(1-1/m)/c then exceeds3/8.
The upper bound a<lambda-2 follows from a=(m-1)/[(m+1)lambda].
Consequently 0<A_mass<1, and (1) gives

    M_j<=c^j, M_(j+1)<=c M_j,
    a c^j<=r M_j.                                      (12)

Let M=M_(m-1). For a first occurrence of any level j, P=S_j and its
following mass is at least S_(m-1). Its cut is at most
r^2/(2M-1). For a last occurrence, its preceding mass is at least
S_(m-1), and its following mass is S_j. Since x^2/(2x-1) is increasing
for x>=1 and M_j<=M, its cut is also at most

    r^2 M_j^2/[M^2(2M_j-1)]<=r^2/(2M-1).              (13)

These statements include the unique central occurrence, for which the
first and last positions coincide. Using c<=5/2, r<=1/2 and M>=1,

    r^2(2M_m-1)<= (5M-1)/4 <= 2M-1.

Thus every single-cut term is no larger than the global Huber term:

    K_n(H_m)=1/(2S_m+1).                               (14)

## 4. Full-spectrum quadratic bound at b=d_0

This argument controls every t in [0,1], not only t=1. Write

## 6. Retained two-block geometry and all constant tails in its cap range

Here is the precise mechanism tested next. For ANY two selected cuts i<j
of an arbitrary schedule, let P be the mass before i, S the mass strictly
between i and j, T the mass after j, and define

    M_0=1+P, M_1=1+S,
    A=(h_i-1)/M_0, epsilon=(h_j-1)/M_1, sigma=2T+1.

Assume h_i,h_j>1 and choose the cap-range angle

    0<kappa<=A/(1+epsilon).                            (25)

Use the retained prefix gradients and proximal point

    p=(1,0)/M_0,
    q=(-kappa,sqrt(kappa(A-kappa)))/M_1,
    X=(-A,0), y=X-M_1 q, d=-M_1 q.                    (26)

These prefix data are actual jets of the single Moreau envelope of
J(z)=max(0,<p,z>,<q,z>), starting at (1,0). Before the first checkpoint
the proximal points are (1-(u+1)/M_0,0), 0<=u<=P, so the p-plane is
active. That checkpoint, of size1+A M_0, sends its input p to X. In
the second block, the proposed proximal points X-tq, 1<=t<=M_1, have

    <q,X-tq>=(A kappa/M_1)(1-t/M_1)>=0,
    <q-p,X-tq>
      =A kappa/M_1+A/M_0
          -t[A kappa/M_1^2+kappa/(M_0 M_1)]
      >=(A-kappa)/M_0>0.

This verifies every actual old query, even if individual ordinary steps
are large. At the second checkpoint its jet is

    x_j=y+q, g_j=q, f_j=||q||^2/2.

For completeness, the envelope minimizes J(z)+||x-z||^2/2. This has a
unique minimizer, and an active-plane slope g at z proves optimality at
x=z+g. At two proximal points, monotonicity of the subgradients gives
||g-g'||^2<=<g-g',x-x'>, hence a 1-Lipschitz gradient. The two minimizing
inequalities identify the derivative as g; joint convexity proves
convexity of the envelope. Thus the claimed function has the required
global regularity, not only valid formal data.

The second checkpoint, of size1+M_1 epsilon, sends the iterate to
X_tail=y+epsilon d. The optimum jet is (0,0,0). Every interpolant of
this prefix has origin as an actual closest minimizer to (1,0): the
retained first checkpoint jet (p,p,||p||^2/2), interpolated with any
minimizer z, forces <p,z><=0. Its squared distance from (1,0) is
therefore at least1, attained at origin. This normalization persists
for all extensions below.

Allow ANY legal continuation with a single common gradient g at every
tail query, including the terminal sample; allow affine intercepts,
positive values and extra dimensions, and retain every prefix jet.
Its endpoint is y+epsilon d-Tg. The accepted interpolation inequality
from this endpoint to the old jet (y+q,q,||q||^2/2) gives

    2f_end<=2epsilon<d,g>-sigma||g||^2
                         <=epsilon^2||d||^2/sigma
                         =A kappa epsilon^2/sigma.

This uses a retained old query, not a reset to a new problem. From (25),
EVERY such constant-tail continuation obeys the exact universal cap

    2f_end<=U_ij:=A^2 epsilon^2/[(1+epsilon)(1+2T)].     (27)

In particular it covers all angles and all optimized tail planes of the
previous explicit two-checkpoint cap policy. It does not cover angles
kappa>A/(1+epsilon), different two-block prefixes, or variable-gradient
tails. No claim that (27) is attained for every pair is needed below.

       -sigma||g_end-epsilon d/sigma||^2.             (54)

For the H_m geometry, the first term is bounded by gamma K, where
gamma=5949/6088 and K=1/(2S_m+1), by the complete calculation (45)--(51).
Therefore any such witness reaching 2f_end>=1/B_n must satisfy

    2<g_end,Delta_tail>
       >=1/B_n-gamma K
                   +sigma||g_end-epsilon d/sigma||^2. (55)

The true closest-minimizer normalization is still1 by the first retained
checkpoint jet. In particular, (24) implies the quantitative necessary
condition

    liminf B_n * 2<g_end,Delta_tail> >=1-2gamma/e>0     (56)

for any unbounded sequence of successful witnesses of this form.
This requirement keeps every parameter loss. Merely introducing new
gradient directions is insufficient: if
<g_end,g_l>>=||g_end||^2 at every positive tail step, the left side
of (55) is nonpositive. It includes all collinear contracting tails
g_l=c_l g_end with c_l>=1, and all changes g_l=g_end+w_l with
<g_end,w_l>=0. Neither class can escape the obstruction.

When T>0 and g_end!=0, Cauchy--Schwarz additionally gives

    sum_l t_l||g_l-g_end||^2
      >= [ (1/B_n-gamma K)_+ ]^2/[4T||g_end||^2]        (57)

for any successful witness. Equation (55) is stronger because it
retains the sign of the required terminal correlation and the square
loss. No sufficient construction with the required positive correlation
has been established. This is a necessary quantitative interface, not a
new lower bound on W_n and not an assertion of feasibility.

## 12. A different positive-height prefix, and its first failed shortcut

The preceding obstruction fixes the zero height at the second checkpoint.
One can change that geometry while retaining a legal function and exact
normalization. Fix M_0,M_1>=1, A>0, epsilon>0, choose

    0<=kappa<=A, 0<=nu^2<=kappa(A-kappa),
    v= kappa^2+nu^2,
    p=(1,0)/M_0, q=(-kappa,nu)/M_1,
    X=(-A,0), d=-M_1q, y=X+d,
    delta_second=(A kappa-v)/M_1>=0.                  (58)

Use the same actual ordinary blocks and checkpoints of sizes1+A M_0
and1+M_1 epsilon. The one fixed envelope of max(0,<p,z>,<q,z>)
realizes the first two blocks: the first p-plane comparison is unchanged;
in the second block, for 1<=t<=M_1,

    <q,X-tq>=A kappa/M_1-tv/M_1^2>=delta_second>=0,
    <p,X-tq>=(-A+t kappa/M_1)/M_0<=0.

Every query is thus legal. The second checkpoint jet has proximal point
y and value f_j=delta_second+||q||^2/2. The origin is the true closest
minimizer by the same saturated first checkpoint jet, without assuming
anything about the subsequent interpolant.

For ANY legal constant-gradient tail of total mass T, write sigma=2T+1.
The retained second-checkpoint inequality and the optimum inequality,
completed separately as squares, give

    2f_end<=min {
      2delta_second+epsilon^2 v/sigma,
      [A^2-2A(1+epsilon)kappa+(1+epsilon)^2v]/sigma
    }.                                                (59)

These are simultaneous necessary conditions, not an attained formula.
All incoming interpolation inequalities to the old positive-height
queries must still be imposed to produce a witness. They are not removed
by the accepted unqueried-terminal reduction: these are constraints on
the queried tail itself.

The tempting shortcut of treating the first term of (59) as an attainable
retained-height payoff is false. Take epsilon=1, kappa=A/2 and nu=0.
Then delta_second=A^2/(4M_1)>0, but

    X_tail=y+epsilon d=(-A,0)+2(A/2,0)=0.

This is the retained minimizer, so every subsequent gradient and every
terminal error are zero, for EVERY nonnegative tail. The first term
of (59) is A^2/(2M_1)+A^2/(4sigma)>0, whereas the optimum term is zero.
This is an explicit legal fixed-function counterexample to that shortcut,
not merely inconsistent formal data. It also shows why raising the
checkpoint height cannot be evaluated independently of its location.

The screened next tasks are consequently precise: either construct an
actual varying tail satisfying (55) with every old-query inequality, or
solve the joint positive-height prefix/tail constraints behind (58)--(59)
and obtain a value at least1/B_n for all appended b. No such payoff
comparison is claimed here. The present round's completed result is the
quantitative baseline and two-block-mechanism obstruction (53).

claim: C33 complete GLOBAL three-step capacity theorem candidate: every primitive nonnegative h=(u,v,w) satisfies 1+u+v+w<=3+2sqrt2, with equality ONLY at (sqrt2,2,sqrt2), whose full nonnegative interpolation certificate is explicit. Stronger: every other h with capacity>=3+2sqrt2 has an actual negative-energy witness with ALL incoming-terminal Q_(i,3)=0, so even arbitrary individual signed terminal credits cannot enlarge this capacity/equality set. evidence:
# Exact global three-step primitive capacity, including arbitrary terminal credit

Status: complete self-contained candidate, NOT verifier-accepted. No
solver or fact_submit was used. The two polynomial identities and their
explicit coefficient sign proofs are included in full; no numerical
calculation or computational artifact is a proof premise.

The public max4 candidates 5b4359baa88bf3e4 and 500d209094028aef suggested
the mixed witness. Every ingredient used here is proved explicitly;
those unverified findings and the earlier max3 C32 are not premises.
The sole accepted predecessor is smooth-convex interpolation fact
1252b8823bb5a290.

## 1. Theorem and scope

For any nonnegative three-step schedule h=(u,v,w), put T=1+u+v+w.
For a legal convex differentiable 1-smooth GD run define

    V_h=2sum_(i<3)h_i(f_i-f_3)
        +sum_(i<3)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
        -(T-1)T||g_3||^2.

Call h primitive if V_h>=0 for every such finite-dimensional run with
a minimizer. Put t=sqrt(2), lambda=1+t and T_0=lambda^2=3+2t.

Then every primitive h satisfies

    T<=T_0.

Equality holds only for h=(t,2,t), and an explicit universally valid
interpolation certificate below proves attainment.

More strongly, if T>=T_0 and h!=(t,2,t), there is a legal finite-dimensional
run with V_h<0 and ALL Q_(i,3)=0, i=0,1,2. Consequently replacing V_h
by V_h minus ANY real linear combination of those three incoming-terminal
interpolation residuals cannot permit a larger capacity, or another
equality schedule. This is a necessity statement for arbitrary terminal
credit, not a sufficiency assertion for negative credit at Silver.

This proves the exact capacity at length three only. It does not bound
all-length primitive capacities and does not resolve the unrestricted
asymptotic normalized-objective target.

Sections2--4 first reduce any possible exception to

    t<u<7/4, 1<v<2, 1<w<t, T_0<=T<7,
    u+w>=2T/lambda-2.                              (R)

Section5 eliminates this entire remaining region.

## 2. Actual witnesses and all their legality conditions

For any legal run use

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0,
    V_h=2sum_(i<3)h_i(f_i-f_3)
         +sum_(i<3)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
         -(T-1)T||g_3||^2.

For data with f_i=<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2 and x_3=g_3, set
y_i=x_i-g_i. Expansion gives

    Q_ij=<g_i-g_j,y_j>, Q_(i,3)=0,
    V_h=||x_0||^2-T^2||g_3||^2.                   (2)

All witnesses used below have these properties and include the legal
optimum jet (0,0,0). Besides the finite Q conditions, optimum legality
requires <g_i,y_i>>=0; the other direction is saturated by the value
formula. A feasible finite array is realized by the conjugate maximum
of quadratics in accepted 1252b8823bb5a290. Thus the arrays specify
fixed globally smooth convex functions with a minimizer.

The interval-projection witness at any selected step b, with ordinary
sums P,Q, has gradient 1 before b and -(b-1)/(Q+1) after it, starting
at P+1 and ending at its negative threshold, when b>1. Formula (2)
gives the necessary cut condition

    T(b-1)_+<=(P+1)(Q+1).                         (3)

This is a direct fixed clipped-derivative construction, including zero
ordinary steps. Apply it at the first and last step to obtain

    u,w<=M(T):=2T/(T+1)<2.                        (4)

For u,v,w>1 abbreviate

    a=u-1, A=u+1, r=v-1, D=w+1, eta=r/D;
    T=A+D+r.

The full-curvature quadratic f(x)=x^2/2, x_0=1, gives

    F_Q=1-T^2 a^2 r^2(w-1)^2>=0.                  (5)

The middle-cut interval, with x=(A,1,-r,-eta) and
g=(1,1,-eta,-eta), gives

    F_B=A^2-T^2 eta^2>=0, or Tr<=AD.              (6)

If r(w-1)<=1, the one-sided Huber derivative min(x,1), started at A,
has x=(A,1,-r,r(w-1)) and g=(1,1,-r,r(w-1)). It gives

    F_C=A^2-T^2 r^2(w-1)^2>=0.                   (7)

When eta a<1, a two-dimensional mixed witness gives

    F_N=a u F_B+(1+eta)u^2(2-u^2)>=0.             (8)

Here is its complete verification. Combine the middle-cut base array
from (6) with the auxiliary scalar array

    x_aux=(1,-a,ra,eta a),
    g_aux=(1,-a,eta a,eta a),
    f_aux,i=x_aux,i*g_aux,i-g_aux,i^2/2.

The auxiliary proximal points are (0,0,w eta a,0). Its only positive
finite residual is Q_aux,(0,2)=(1-eta a)w eta a. Every optimum
inequality is legal because g_aux,i*y_aux,i>=0. The base proximal
points are (u,0,-w eta,0); its Q_(0,2)=-(1+eta)w eta and all its
residuals are nonpositive. With

    epsilon=(1+eta)/[a(1-eta a)],

take the orthogonal sum of the base and sqrt(epsilon) times the
auxiliary points and gradients, with the summed values. Residuals add;
the sole positive auxiliary edge is exactly canceled and every other
edge is nonpositive. The energy equals

    F_B+epsilon(1-T^2 eta^2 a^2)
       =F_N/[a(1-eta a)].                         (9)

For the algebra use 1-a^2 A^2=u^2(2-u^2). This proves (8) with
all actual edges, rather than an assumed two-dimensional interpolant.

## 3. A uniform box where all four witnesses apply

Assume T>=T_0 and all the cut conditions (3). First v>1. Otherwise
T=1+u+v+w<=2+2M(T), so T^2-5T-2<=0. At T=T_0 this polynomial
equals 2t>0 and it increases thereafter, a contradiction.

Thus r>0 and the middle cut (6) applies. As T=A+D+r,

    T(T-A-D)<=AD<=(A+D)^2/4,
    T<=lambda(A+D)/2<=lambda(M(T)+1).

Consequently

    T^2+(1-3lambda)T-lambda<=0.                    (10)

Its left side increases for T>=T_0, and at T=7 equals
56-22lambda>0 because lambda<5/2. Hence T<7 and (4) gives
u,w<7/4.

Both u and w exceed1. If, for example, u<=1, then A<=2, D<11/4,
so r=T-A-D>T-19/4. But

    Tr>T(T-19/4)>=T_0(T_0-19/4)
       =11/4+5t/2>11/2>AD,

contradicting the middle cut. The argument for w is identical.

On this entire necessary box the extra hypotheses of (7) and (8) hold:

    r(w-1)<=A(w^2-1)/T<363/(64T_0)<1,
    eta a<=Aa/T=(u^2-1)/T<33/(16T_0)<1.           (11)

For the first strict numerical comparison, 363<64T_0 is equivalent
to 171<128sqrt(2), and squaring gives 29241<32768. Thus no local
neighborhood restriction is being silently used in this global screen.
The earlier inequality T<=lambda(A+D)/2 also gives

    u+w>=2T/lambda-2>=2t.                         (12)

## 4. Excluding three of the four endpoint orientations

Suppose u<=t. By (12), w>=t. Since T>=T_0 and w<2, the difference
between the two sides of the necessary inequality Tr(w-1)<=A is
at least

    T_0(T_0-t-w-2)(w-1)-(t+1)
       =T_0(w-t)(2-w)>=0.                         (13)

It is strictly positive unless u=w=t and T=T_0. In that exceptional
case v=2. Hence every other candidate must have u>t.

Suppose next that also w>=t. On the rectangle [t,M(T)]^2 consider

    q_T(u,w)=T(u-1)(w-1)(T-u-w-2).

This function is strictly concave in either endpoint with the other
fixed. Its minimum is attained at a corner. At T=T_0, M(T_0)=1+t/2,
the corner values are

    q_(T_0)(t,t)=1,
    q_(T_0)(t,M(T_0))=q_(T_0)(M(T_0),t)=lambda/2>1,
    q_(T_0)(M(T_0),M(T_0))=lambda/2>1.

Each corner value strictly increases with T>=T_0. All its positive
factors increase; in particular the derivatives of
T-t-M(T)-2 and T-2M(T)-2 are respectively
1-2/(T+1)^2 and 1-4/(T+1)^2, both positive.
Thus q_T>1 except at the single point T=T_0,u=w=t. This contradicts
the quadratic condition (5). Every nonexceptional candidate therefore
satisfies u>t>w.

Finally its middle step is less than2. For u>t the expression F_N in
(8), with u,w held fixed, strictly decreases as r>0 increases: the
negative squared term in F_B decreases, while u^2(2-u^2)<0.
At r=1 a direct expansion gives

    D^2 F_N/u
       =P_u(D):=u^2 D^2+(4-2u^2-u^3)D-(u-1)(u+2)^2.

This polynomial has one positive and one negative root, since its
leading coefficient is positive and its constant term negative. Also

    P_u(lambda)=-(lambda+1)u^3-2u^2+4(lambda+1)<0

for u>t: the right side vanishes at t and has strictly negative
derivative for u>0. Its positive root is therefore beyond lambda,
and P_u(D)<0 for 0<D<=lambda. Since w<t gives D<lambda, F_N<0
at r=1 and at every r>=1. Necessarily r<1, proving the preliminary reduction (R).

The remaining constraints can be written without a mixed-energy
abbreviation. In the region (R), a primitive candidate must satisfy

    Tr<=AD,
    T a r(w-1)<=1,
    u^2+u-1+u(2-u^2)eta-(u-1)T^2 eta^2>=0.        (14)

The last expression is F_N/u after expansion. Section5 proves these
necessary inequalities are incompatible with the remaining endpoint cut
throughout (R).



## 5. Exact elimination of the remaining asymmetric region

Assume (R), the endpoint cut u<=2T/(T+1), and F_N,F_Q>=0.
Continue to write a=u-1, A=u+1, D=w+1, and put K=T-A.
Thus r=K-D and eta=(K-D)/D.

For fixed u,D in (R), F_N strictly decreases with T>=T_0:
its negative term -a u T^2 eta^2 strictly decreases, and its other
T-dependent term has coefficient u^2(2-u^2)<0.
The quantity

    T a (T-A-D)(D-2)

strictly increases with T there. The endpoint cut says
T>=u/(2-u). Therefore any putative feasible T induces feasible necessary
inequalities at the smaller mass

    T_min=max{T_0,u/(2-u)}.                        (15)

Here and below D is unchanged. At this smaller mass K-D>0 still holds,
because T_min>=T_0, u<7/4, D<lambda, and
T_0-11/4-lambda=t-3/4>0.

For the remainder of this section set T=T_min and K=T-A. Define

    B=u^2+u-1,
    N(D)=a(A^2-T^2)D^2
          +K[2aT^2+u(2-u^2)]D-aT^2K^2,
    Q(D)=T a(K-D)(D-2)-1.                         (16)

Thus N(D)=D^2 F_N/u>=0 and Q(D)<=0. Let

    kappa=(T^2-A^2)/T>0,
    ell=aT^2(K-2)+KB+2aA^2>0,
    c_0=-aK[T^2(K-2)+2A^2]+(T^2-A^2)/T.

The positivity of ell follows from K>2, a>0, B>0. Subtraction of the
quadratic coefficients gives the exact identity

    N(D)-kappa Q(D)=ell D+c_0.                    (17)

Hence D>=D_L:=-c_0/ell. Moreover Q is strictly increasing for every
D<=lambda, since

    Q'(D)=T a(K+2-2D),
    K+2-2lambda>=T_0-u+1-2lambda=2-u>0.

It is therefore enough to prove Q(D_L)>0: then D>=D_L and D<lambda
would imply Q(D)>0, a contradiction.

The switch in (15) is exactly at

    M_0=2T_0/(T_0+1)=1+t/2.

### 5.1 First interval: t<u<=M_0, T=T_0

Clearing the positive denominator ell^2 gives

    ell^2 Q(D_L)
       =-T_0 a c_0^2-T_0 a(K+2)c_0 ell
          -(2T_0 a K+1)ell^2
       =(u-t) P_8(u).                             (18)

Here P_8 is the following degree-eight polynomial, with coefficients
listed in ascending order of powers of u:

    13696+9680t,
    -44720-31632t,
    42848+30300t,
    -4028-2832t,
    -13912-9832t,
    7640+5396t,
    -1664-1179t,
    163+116t,
    -6-4t.

Identity (18) follows by substitution of ell,c_0 and t^2=2; all
quantities in it have been specified explicitly.

For 0<=z<=1 put u=t+(1-t/2)z. Write
B_(d,k)(z)=binomial(d,k) z^k(1-z)^(d-k). Direct expansion gives

    P_8(t+(1-t/2)z)=sum_(k=0)^8 beta_k B_(8,k)(z),

with the following EXACT coefficients:

    beta_0=768+544t,
    beta_1=762+539t,
    beta_2=(5144+3632t)/7,
    beta_3=9573/14+13539t/28,
    beta_4=3044/5+3022t/7,
    beta_5=57287/112+81003t/224,
    beta_6=3131/8+1915t/7,
    beta_7=15827/64+21623t/128,
    beta_8=79+783t/16.

Every coefficient is strictly positive. The Bernstein basis terms are
nonnegative and sum to one, so P_8(u)>0 throughout [t,M_0].
As u>t, equation (18) proves Q(D_L)>0 on this first interval.

### 5.2 Second interval: M_0<=u<7/4, T=u/(2-u)

Put p=u, q=2-u>0, and K_num=p-Aq. Define the explicit polynomials

    ell_num=a p^2(K_num-2q)+K_num B q^2+2aA^2 q^3,
    c_num=-a p K_num[p^2(K_num-2q)+2A^2 q^3]
            +(p^2-A^2 q^2)q^3,
    X=-c_num, Y=p q ell_num.

These are just cleared versions of the same ell and c_0:

    ell=ell_num/q^3,
    c_0=c_num/(p q^4),
    D_L=X/Y, Y>0.

Substitution into Q gives the second exact identity

    q^2 Y^2 Q(D_L)
      =p a(K_num Y-qX)(X-2Y)-q^2 Y^2
      =u(u-2)^3(u^2-2)^2 P_13(u),                 (19)

where

    P_13(u)=
       2u^13-9u^12-16u^11+96u^10+28u^9-428u^8
       +248u^7+480u^6-160u^5-656u^4+256u^3
       +288u^2-64u-64.

All denominator factors are positive; (19) is an ordinary polynomial
identity, checkable by multiplying the displayed polynomials.

We prove P_13(u)<0 on [M_0,7/4] by an explicit sign certificate.
First,

    P_13(M_0)=(-1807+1277t)/64<0,

because 1807^2-2*1277^2=3791>0. Next, the derivative has the exact
Bernstein expansion on [5/3,2]

    29229255 P_13'(5/3+z/3)
       =sum_(k=0)^12 b_k B_(12,k)(z), 0<=z<=1,

where the integer coefficients in increasing k are

    -822569770,
    -1552896015,
    -2651133300,
    -4264197048,
    -6587625132,
    -9878494050,
    -14470817670,
    -20793631500,
    -29391880320,
    -40950087840,
    -56318574240,
    -76541675760,
    -102886977600.

Every b_k is strictly negative, and 29229255>0. Thus P_13 decreases
strictly on [5/3,2], which contains [M_0,7/4]. The asserted negative
sign follows from its value at M_0.

In (19), u>0, (u-2)^3<0, (u^2-2)^2>0, and P_13(u)<0. Therefore
Q(D_L)>0 on the whole second interval too.

Both alternatives in (15) now contradict (16)--(17). This eliminates
(R), so the only possible primitive schedule with T>=T_0 is Silver.

## 6. Attainment and the signed-terminal extension

At h=(t,2,t), the following nonnegative multipliers, with every
unlisted multiplier zero, give an exact identity:

    lambda_01=2,
    lambda_10=2lambda,
    lambda_21=2t lambda,
    lambda_31=lambda_13=2lambda,
    lambda_23=2lambda^2+2t lambda,
    lambda_32=2lambda^3,

    V_h+sum_(i!=j) lambda_ij Q_ij=0.               (20)

Substitute x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i and t^2=2 to verify (20) by matching
each function coefficient and each gradient inner product. For example,
the finite value divergences are (-2t,-4,-2t,4+4t), exactly canceling
the four coefficients of V_h. The remaining gradient coefficients all
vanish. Since Q_ij<=0 and every multiplier is nonnegative, (20) proves
V_h>=0 in every finite dimension, establishing attainment.

If T>=T_0 and h is not Silver, the preceding contradiction shows that
at least one of the explicitly constructed cut, quadratic, one-sided
Huber, or two-dimensional mixed witnesses has strictly negative energy.
All those witnesses have x_3=g_3 and the saturated value formula, so
Q_(i,3)=0 for every i<3. Thus for any real numbers beta_0,beta_1,beta_2,
that same witness satisfies

    V_h-sum_(i<3) beta_i Q_(i,3)=V_h<0.

It also rules out a full PSD intrinsic identity whose only possibly
negative interpolation coefficients are on these incoming-terminal
edges: the signed edges vanish, while every other nonnegative
coefficient multiplies a nonpositive Q. This proves the stronger
necessity statement without a dual-attainment assumption.

## 7. What remains open

The theorem gives exactly

    max_{primitive h of length3} (1+sum h)=(1+sqrt(2))^2,

with a unique maximizer, and the same necessary capacity/equality
restriction under arbitrary incoming-terminal credit. It does not
give the required all-length capacity induction, arbitrary-tail
certificate re-selection, or a constant-preserving connection from
primitive energy to the original normalized objective problem.

Thus even arbitrary signed incoming-terminal credit cannot improve three-step primitive capacity; Silver is uniquely maximal. The omitted old two-cut witness forces u<8/5 in C32's residual box, where the quadratic and mixed witnesses contradict each other. No solves or verifier calls; the original all-horizon target remains open.
evidence:
# Three-step capacity with arbitrary signed terminal credit

Status: complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. No SDP/PEP or
fact_submit call. This closes the proposed three-step discovery domain if
the candidate survives verification. It does not settle the general signed
cone question or the original all-horizon normalized objective target.

## 1. Statement and definitions

Let h=(u,v,w) be a nonnegative three-step schedule, let T=1+u+v+w, and put
t=sqrt(2), lambda=1+t, T_0=lambda^2=3+2t. Along gradient descent on a convex
differentiable function f with 1-Lipschitz gradient and a minimizer, write
x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i, g_i=grad f(x_i), f_i=f(x_i), and

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_h=2sum_(i<3)h_i(f_i-f_3)+sum_(i<3)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                             -(T-1)T||g_3||^2,
 J_h=sum_(i<3)h_i Q_(i,3), E_theta=V_h-theta J_h.

Claim. If T>=T_0 and h differs from (t,2,t), there is a fixed, finite-dimensional
convex differentiable 1-smooth function, with a minimizer, whose full h-run has

              V_h<0 and Q_(i,3)=0 for every i<3.       (1)

Consequently, for EVERY real theta, universal validity of E_theta>=0 with
T>=T_0 forces h=(t,2,t). The same necessary conclusion holds for any intrinsic
certificate V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij whose values cancel, whose remainder is PSD
on the complete independent formal gradient space, and whose multipliers are
nonnegative except for arbitrary signs on incoming-terminal finite pairs.
No validity-versus-certifiability equivalence is assumed.

At h=(t,2,t), an explicit ordinary primitive certificate is given in Section 7.
Therefore, for each theta>=0, the exact maximum three-step capacity in the
E_theta-valid class and in its nonnegative-certificate class is T_0, uniquely
attained by Silver. The arbitrary-signed-certificate class has that same
maximum. In particular the conclusion applies throughout 0<=theta<1.

The proof includes the required domain reductions directly. C32 and earlier
max4 findings motivated them, but are not used as unverified premises.

## 2. Legal projection witnesses and the first four constraints

Here is a self-contained way to turn each finite array below into a fixed
legal function. Suppose its GD equations hold, its terminal point satisfies
x_3=g_3, and its assigned values are

 f_i=<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2.

Set y_i=x_i-g_i. Expansion gives

 Q_ij=<g_i-g_j,y_j>, Q_(i,3)=0,
 V_h=||x_0||^2-T^2||g_3||^2.                         (2)

If every finite Q_ij<=0 and <g_i,y_i>>=0, take K=conv{0,g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3}.
Those inequalities say precisely <y_j,z-g_j><=0 for every vertex z of K and
hence for every z in K. Thus g_j=P_K(x_j). The function

 F_K(x)=max_(z in K)[<x,z>-||z||^2/2]

interpolates all assigned values and gradients. The projection normal
inequalities imply <P_K(x)-P_K(x'),x-x'>>=||P_K(x)-P_K(x')||^2, so P_K is
1-Lipschitz. The maximizing formula gives
0<=F_K(x+d)-F_K(x)-<P_K(x),d><=<P_K(x+d)-P_K(x),d><=||d||^2,
which proves differentiability with gradient P_K. Thus F_K is globally convex
and 1-smooth; it has minimum F_K(0)=0. No unverified interpolation theorem is
needed for these arrays.

At any selected step b>1, with preceding and following sums P,Q, use derivative
clip(x,-(b-1)/(Q+1),1) and start at P+1. The preceding gradients are 1 and the
following gradients are -(b-1)/(Q+1), ending at that negative threshold.
The function obtained by integration has all the properties in (2). Its
energy yields the necessary cut inequality

              T(b-1)_+ <= (P+1)(Q+1).               (3)

For b<=1 this inequality is automatic. This includes schedules with zero
steps. The first and last cuts give

              u,w <= M(T):=2T/(T+1)<2.              (4)

For u,v,w>1 write a=u-1, A=u+1, r=v-1, D=w+1, eta=r/D.
The following additional inequalities are necessary if no witness (1) exists:

 F_Q=1-T^2 a^2 r^2(w-1)^2 >=0,                     (5)
 F_B=A^2-T^2 eta^2 >=0,                            (6)
 F_C=A^2-T^2 r^2(w-1)^2 >=0,                       (7)
 F_N=a u F_B+(1+eta)u^2(2-u^2) >=0.                (8)

For (5), use f(x)=x^2/2 and x_0=1. For (6), use the middle cut in (3),
whose x=(A,1,-r,-eta), g=(1,1,-eta,-eta). For (7), provided r(w-1)<=1,
use derivative min(x,1), start at A, and obtain
x=(A,1,-r,r(w-1)), g=(1,1,-r,r(w-1)). It is a fixed convex 1-smooth
function with minimum at0, and its terminal point is inside its quadratic
part. Each of these functions satisfies (2).

For (8), provided eta a<1, combine the middle-cut base from (6) with the
auxiliary array

 x_aux=(1,-a,ra,eta a), g_aux=(1,-a,eta a,eta a),
 f_aux,i=x_aux,i*g_aux,i-g_aux,i^2/2.

The auxiliary normals are (0,0,w eta a,0). Its only positive finite residual
is Q_aux,(0,2)=(1-eta a)w eta a. Every outgoing optimum inequality holds,
since each g_aux,i*y_aux,i is nonnegative. In the base array,
Q_base,(0,2)=-(1+eta)w eta, and all finite residuals are nonpositive.
Take their orthogonal sum with auxiliary scale sqrt(epsilon), where

                   epsilon=(1+eta)/[a(1-eta a)].

Residuals add, the sole positive auxiliary edge is canceled exactly, every
other finite edge is nonpositive, and every optimum condition holds.
The projection construction above realizes one fixed legal function. Its
energy is F_B+epsilon(1-T^2 eta^2 a^2)=F_N/[a(1-eta a)]; the denominator
is positive. The equality follows by 1-a^2 A^2=u^2(2-u^2).
The terminal point stays core, so every incoming-terminal residual is zero.

## 3. Complete reduction to the asymmetric region

Assume T>=T_0 and assume, for contradiction, that every applicable witness
above has nonnegative energy. First v>1: otherwise T<=2+2M(T) gives
T^2-5T-2<=0, whereas at T_0 this polynomial equals 2t>0 and it increases
thereafter. Thus r>0 and the middle cut applies, initially with A=u+1,D=w+1.
Since T=A+D+r, it gives

 T(T-A-D)<=AD<=(A+D)^2/4,
 T<=lambda(A+D)/2<=lambda(M(T)+1).

Hence T^2+(1-3lambda)T-lambda<=0. The polynomial increases for T>=T_0,
and its value at7 is 56-22lambda>0 because lambda<5/2. Thus T<7, and
u,w<M(7)=7/4. Both endpoints exceed1: if u<=1, then A<=2,D<11/4 and
r>T-19/4, so Tr>T(T-19/4)>=T_0(T_0-19/4)=11/4+5t/2>11/2>AD,
a contradiction. The proof for w is identical.

The extra hypotheses needed in Section 2 now hold everywhere in this box:

 r(w-1)<=A(w^2-1)/T<363/(64T_0)<1,
 eta a<=Aa/T=(u^2-1)/T<33/(16T_0)<1.                (9)

For the first numerical inequality, 363<64T_0 follows from
171<128sqrt(2), whose square is 29241<32768. Also

                   u+w>=2T/lambda-2>=2t.            (10)

If u<=t, then w>=t. The left-minus-right difference in the necessary
inequality Tr(w-1)<=A from (7) is at least
T_0(T_0-t-w-2)(w-1)-(t+1)=T_0(w-t)(2-w)>=0.
It is positive except when u=w=t,T=T_0; equality then gives v=2.
Thus every nonexceptional candidate has u>t.

If w>=t as well, consider q_T(u,w)=T(u-1)(w-1)(T-u-w-2) on
[t,M(T)]^2. It is strictly concave in each endpoint separately. Its minimum
is at a corner; strict concavity excludes equality at an interior endpoint
when corner minima have already been identified. At T_0, since
M(T_0)=1+t/2, the four corner values are 1,lambda/2,lambda/2,lambda/2,
with the value1 only at (t,t). All four corner values strictly increase with
T>=T_0: their factors are positive and increasing, including
T-t-M(T)-2 and T-2M(T)-2, whose derivatives are respectively
1-2/(T+1)^2 and 1-4/(T+1)^2. Thus (5) excludes this case except Silver.
Every other candidate has u>t>w.

For such endpoints, F_N strictly decreases as r>0 increases, with u,w fixed:
the negative squared term in F_B decreases and u^2(2-u^2)<0. At r=1,

 D^2 F_N/u=u^2 D^2+(4-2u^2-u^3)D-(u-1)(u+2)^2=:P_u(D).

This quadratic has one positive and one negative root. At D=lambda,
P_u(lambda)=-(lambda+1)u^3-2u^2+4(lambda+1)<0 for u>t: it vanishes
at t and has negative derivative in u>0. Its positive root is therefore
beyond lambda. Since D<lambda, F_N<0 when r=1, and then also for r>=1.
Necessarily r<1. We have proved, with every witness hypothesis checked,

       t<u<7/4, 1<v<2, 1<w<t, T_0<=T<7,
                       u+w>=2T/lambda-2.             (11)

## 4. The additional two-cut witness forces u<8/5

Here the different letters R=u-1, k=v-1, C=w+1, B=v+w+1=C+k+1 are used
to avoid confusing the first and second bridge. Thus T=B+R+1.
Set eta_1=R/B, zeta=k/C, p=-1/R. Consider the two scalar arrays

 x_base=(1,-R,-C eta_1,-eta_1),
 g_base=(1,-eta_1,-eta_1,-eta_1),
 x_aux=(p,1,-k,-zeta), g_aux=(p,1,-zeta,-zeta).

Both obey the same three GD steps; assign values by f=g*x-g^2/2.
Their normal arrays are respectively
(0,-(B-1)eta_1,-w eta_1,0) and (0,0,-w zeta,0).
The base is an actual clipped-derivative trajectory. Within (11),
R zeta<3/8<1. The auxiliary array's only positive residual is
Q_aux,(0,2)=w zeta(1/R-zeta); all its other finite residuals are zero
except Q_aux,(1,2)<0. Every optimum inequality holds in both arrays.
The base residual Q_base,(0,2)=-(1+eta_1)w eta_1 cancels that positive
edge when the orthogonal auxiliary scale is sqrt(epsilon_1), where

             epsilon_1=eta_1(1+eta_1)/[zeta(1/R-zeta)].

All other finite inequalities remain nonpositive. The projection realization
in Section 2 supplies a fixed globally legal function; its terminal point is
core and every incoming-terminal Q is zero. Its energy is

 V_mix=1-T^2 eta_1^2+epsilon_1(R^(-2)-T^2 zeta^2)
      =(C+kB)(B+R)/[B^2 k(C-Rk)]
                     *{C-Rk[1+R(T+1)]}.             (12)

The prefactor is positive. For an algebra audit, substitute
epsilon_1=R^2 C^2(B+R)/[B^2 k(C-Rk)], put the two energy terms over
that denominator, and use B=C+k+1,T=B+R+1. Thus nonnegative energy forces

                    R k[1+R(T+1)]<=C.              (13)

In (11), w<t and T>=T_0 imply
k=T-2-u-w>1+t-u=t-R, C<lambda. Therefore (13) implies

            R(t-R)[1+(T_0+1)R]<lambda.              (14)

The function H(R)=R(t-R)(1+(T_0+1)R) strictly increases on
t-1<R<3/4. Indeed its derivative is
t-2R+(T_0+1)R(2t-3R); here t-2R>-1/10, T_0+1>6,
R>2/5 and 2t-3R>1/2, so H'(R)>11/10>0. These bounds follow from
7/5<t<3/2. At R=3/5,

           H(3/5)=(201t+27)/125>1+t,

because the difference is (76t-98)/125>0. Thus (14) forces R<3/5,
or u<8/5. This is the extra information absent from the four-test screen.

## 5. The quadratic witness forces a small imbalance

Fix the u,w now under consideration and reduce the formal capacity to T_0,
that is, put v_0=T_0-1-u-w. Write

 q=t-1, delta=u-t, z=t-w, d=delta-z=u+w-2t.

By (10), (11), and Section 4,

       0<delta<8/5-t<1/5, 0<z<=delta,
                   0<=d<delta, v_0=2-d>1.           (15)

For fixed u,w, the product T(u-1)(w-1)(T-u-w-2) increases with T when
T-u-w-2>0. Thus (5) at the actual capacity implies its version at T_0.
Since T_0 q^2=1, that version is

             (q+delta)(q-delta+d)(1-d)<=q^2.

Expanding and rearranging gives

 d[(q+delta)(1-d)-q^2+delta^2]<=delta^2.

Because d<=delta, the bracket is at least (1-q)(q+delta)>0. Hence

 d/delta <= delta/[(1-q)(q+delta)] < 4/7 < 3/5.     (16)

For the strict bound, the fraction increases with delta, so delta<1/5
reduces it to 1/[(1-q)(5q+1)]. Since 2/5<q<1/2,
(1-q)(5q+1)>=7/4: subtracting 7/4 gives
(1/2-q)(5q-3/2)>=0. This proves (16) by rational bounds alone.

## 6. The mixed witness contradicts that small imbalance

For fixed u,w and u>t, write eta=(T-u-w-2)/(w+1). An exact expression is

 F_N/u = u^2+u-1+u(2-u^2)eta-(u-1)T^2 eta^2.       (17)

It strictly decreases with T in the relevant range, because eta increases,
u(2-u^2)<0, u-1>0, and eta>0. Thus F_N>=0 at the actual T would imply
F_N>=0 at T_0. At T_0, hold u=t+delta fixed and vary d; then
w=t-delta+d and eta=(1-d)/(lambda-delta+d). This eta strictly decreases
with d, while the right side of (17) strictly decreases with eta. Thus
F_N/u at T_0 strictly increases with d.

By (16), it suffices to show negativity at the LARGER comparison value
d=3delta/5, that is, w=t-2delta/5 and v_0=2-3delta/5.
Let D=w+1,A=u+1,r=v_0-1 at this comparison point. The numerator

 N(delta)=D^2 F_N/u
         =(u-1)(A^2 D^2-T_0^2 r^2)
                              +(T_0-A)D u(2-u^2)

expands exactly to

 N(delta)=delta[ -4-18t/5
          +(376+294t)delta/25
          -(128+70t)delta^2/25
          +(29-3t)delta^3/25
          -6delta^4/25 ].                           (18)

For 0<delta<1/5, discard the two negative higher-order terms and use
delta<=1/5, delta^3<=1/125, and 29-3t<29. The bracket is at most

 -4-18t/5+(376+294t)/125+29/3125
                   =-(3071+3900t)/3125<0.           (19)

Thus N(delta)<0, contradicting the required nonnegative F_N at T_0.
This eliminates every candidate in (11). Consequently the original assumption
that all the listed legal witnesses have nonnegative energy is impossible
for T>=T_0 outside Silver. A negative witness from this finite explicit list
therefore supplies (1), with its whole trajectory and all terminal slacks.

## 7. Attainment and precise consequences

At h=(t,2,t), use the following nonnegative finite-pair multipliers:

 lambda_01=2, lambda_10=2lambda,
 lambda_21=2t lambda, lambda_31=lambda_13=2lambda,
 lambda_23=2lambda^2+2t lambda, lambda_32=2lambda^3,

with every unlisted entry zero. Expansion of the four value coefficients
and ten independent gradient monomials, using t^2=2, gives

                       V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij=0.

Hence V_h>=0 on every legal trajectory. For theta>=0, adding theta h_i
to every incoming-terminal multiplier gives a nonnegative certificate for
E_theta with the same zero remainder. This proves all the attainment claims.

If a putative arbitrary-signed incoming-terminal certificate exists for a
non-Silver h with T>=T_0, evaluate it on (1): the signed terms vanish, all
other multiplier terms are nonpositive, and the PSD remainder would be
at most V_h<0. This is a contradiction on the full formal matrix.

The result is an exact three-step capacity statement, not a claim that
E_theta-validity always forces ordinary primitivity below this capacity or
for longer schedules. It supplies no new upper schedule and no asymptotic
comparison with U_n^ZJ. All mathematics in this note remains unverified.

evidence:
# Exact two-cell objective and the positive-height ruler obstruction

Status: a self-contained UNVERIFIED candidate. No numerical search or
fact_submit. The accepted interpolation fact `1252b8823bb5a290` is the
only correctness premise in Sections 1--4. For the ruler specialization,
this file is part of the JOINT candidate with the complete independent
derivations in `max_near_critical_ruler_audit.md`; the shared publication
includes both texts. No unverified finding is adopted as an accepted fact.

## 1. The entire two-cell class has the exact single-cut value

Fix two finite, possibly empty lists of nonnegative GD steps, with sums
S and T. Put a checkpoint b>=0 between them. Consider all convex
differentiable 1-smooth functions f on any finite-dimensional Euclidean
space, with a minimizer x_star, and an initial point at distance R>0
from x_star. Require that one vector q is the gradient at EVERY query
in the first ordinary block and at its ending checkpoint query, and
that one vector g is the gradient at EVERY query after the checkpoint,
including the terminal sample. Allow q=g, arbitrary values, arbitrary
affine offsets, and any additional dimensions.

Then the supremum of 2(f_end-f_star)/R^2 in this entire class is exactly

    max { 1/[1+2(S+b+T)],
          (b-1)_+^2/[(1+S)^2(1+2T)] }.                 (1)

Both alternatives are attained by explicit scalar functions with unique
minimizer 0. The statement includes b=0, b=1 and zero ordinary steps.
It upper-bounds every legal interpolant in the class, not just the
envelope of a prescribed set of homogeneous planes.

Translate the chosen minimizer to 0 and subtract f_star. Set

    M=1+S, epsilon=(b-1)/M, sigma=1+2T, k=sigma/M.

Write the initial point as -R e, with ||e||=1. The last first-block
query is x_j=-R e-(M-1)q. Its proximal point and height are

    y=-R e-Mq, delta=f(x_j)-||q||^2/2.

The two interpolation inequalities with the optimum imply

    0<=delta<=<q,y>.

Define the dimensionless scalars

    z=-M<q,e>/R, w=M^2||q||^2/R^2.

Cauchy--Schwarz and the preceding bound give

    z^2<=w<=z, 0<=z<=1,
    delta<=R^2(z-w)/M.                                (2)

There is no restriction on q's direction beyond these necessary
conditions. In particular positive height and nonzero plane intercepts
are included, since delta may be any legal value below this upper bound.

Put d=-Mq. The checkpoint sends x_j to y+epsilon d. The terminal
point is y+epsilon d-Tg. The outgoing terminal interpolation inequality
to x_j, and the one to the optimum, give respectively

    2f_end<=2delta+2epsilon<g,d>-sigma||g||^2,
    2f_end<=2<g,y+epsilon d>-sigma||g||^2.              (3)

For every s in [0,1], weight the optimum inequality by s and the
old-query inequality by 1-s, then complete a square in g. This yields

    2f_end<=2(1-s)delta
             +||-R s e+(epsilon+s)d||^2/sigma
             -sigma||g-[-R s e+(epsilon+s)d]/sigma||^2.

Drop only the final nonpositive square and use (2). Thus

    (sigma/R^2) 2f_end <= J_s(z,w),                    (4)
    J_s = s^2+[2k(1-s)-2s(epsilon+s)]z
                  +[(epsilon+s)^2-2k(1-s)]w.

Every weight in this calculation is nonnegative. The old jet and the
actual optimum have both been retained at their actual positions.

## 2. A complete symbolic bound for (4)

First suppose epsilon>=1. Take s=1. Since w<=z and 0<=z<=1,

    J_1<=1+(epsilon^2-1)z<=epsilon^2.                  (5)

Next suppose 0<=epsilon<=1 and

    k(1-epsilon)<=2epsilon^2.

Take s=epsilon. The terms in (4) rearrange exactly as

    J_epsilon=epsilon^2
          +[2k(1-epsilon)-4epsilon^2](z-w)
          <=epsilon^2.                               (6)

In the remaining regime -1<epsilon<=1 and

    k(1-epsilon)>=2epsilon^2,

define

    D=1+2epsilon+k,
    s_0=(epsilon+k)/D,
    z_0=1/[k+2(1+epsilon)],
    L_0=k/[k+2(1+epsilon)],
    C_0=(1+epsilon)[k+2(1+epsilon)]
                    [2epsilon^2-k(1-epsilon)]/D^2.

Here D>0, 0<=s_0<=1, and C_0<=0. To check the first two assertions
when epsilon<0, use the physical identity

    k+epsilon=(2T+b)/M>=0,
    D=(1+epsilon)+(k+epsilon)>0.

Expansion of the coefficients in (4) gives the exact identity

    J_(s_0)(z,w)
       =L_0+C_0[(z-z_0)^2+w-z^2]<=L_0.              (7)

For clarity, the coefficient of w is C_0, that of z is -2C_0 z_0,
and the constant is L_0+C_0 z_0^2=s_0^2. These checks establish (7)
without any exchange of maximization and minimization.

All negative epsilon are covered by (7), apart from epsilon=-1:
indeed epsilon>=-1/M>=-1, and k>=-epsilon when epsilon<0, so

    k(1-epsilon)-2epsilon^2
       >=-epsilon(1+epsilon)>=0.

If epsilon=-1, necessarily M=1 and b=0. Taking s=1 in (4) gives
J_1=1 for all z,w, hence 2f_end<=R^2/sigma, which is exactly the
first alternative of (1). This includes T=0; no denominator vanishes.

For epsilon>=0, comparison of L_0 and epsilon^2 gives

    L_0>=epsilon^2
       iff epsilon<=1 and k(1-epsilon)>=2epsilon^2.

Thus (5)--(7) cover every b>=0 and give

    2f_end/R^2 <= max {1/[sigma+2M(1+epsilon)],
                       (epsilon_+)^2/sigma}.

Since sigma+2M(1+epsilon)=1+2(S+b+T), this is (1)'s upper bound.
This argument never assumes that a separately optimized height bound
or distance bound is attained. Their convex combination is essential.

## 3. Actual attaining functions and all-query checks

Let U=S+b+T and a=R/(1+2U). For the first alternative use the symmetric
Huber function whose derivative is clip(x,-a,a), whose value at 0 is 0,
and start at x_0=R. At every supplied query the cumulative step mass u
satisfies 0<=u<=U and

    x(u)=R-u a>=R-U a=(1+U)a>=a.

Hence every actual gradient is a, and the normalized final objective
is [2aR-(2U+1)a^2]/R^2=1/(1+2U). The derivative is continuous,
nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz; its unique zero is 0.

For the second alternative suppose b>1. Put

    p=R/M, a=R epsilon/sigma>0,
    f'(x)=max(-a,min(p,x)), f(0)=0.

This derivative again defines one convex differentiable 1-smooth
function with unique minimizer 0. Before the checkpoint every query
is R-u p>=p for 0<=u<=S, so its gradient is p. The checkpoint starts
at p and lands at -(b-1)p=-R epsilon. On the tail, every cumulative
mass v in [0,T] gives

    x(v)=-R epsilon+v a
         <=-R epsilon+T a=-(T+1)a<=-a.

Thus every tail gradient, including the terminal one, is -a. Its exact
normalized objective is

    [2aR epsilon-(2T+1)a^2]/R^2=epsilon^2/sigma.

The same fixed function realizes every individual prescribed step in
its actual order. When b<=1 the second alternative of (1) is zero and
the first construction already attains the maximum. This proves (1).

## 4. Positive-height two-block prefixes cannot evade the bound

## 1. Exact schedule and all quadratic curvatures, including arbitrary b

Fix an integer m>=2. Within this document write

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j),
    n=2^m-1, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

The parameters c,a remain fixed for this entire horizon. They are not
recomputed when j changes. The symbol H_j here names a schedule, not the
conjugate jet quadratic from the project glossary. Put r=c-2 and A_mass=a/r.
Counting the occurrences of each level gives, for 0<=j<=m,

    S_j=2^j-1+a(c^j-2^j)/(c-2),
    M_j=A_mass c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j.                       (1)

There are 2^(m-j-1) occurrences of d_j in H_m. Its scalar multiplier at
curvature t in [0,1] is exactly

    P_m(t)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-d_j t)^(2^(m-j-1)).     (2)

Let p_m be H_m without its final d_0 and let h^(m,b)=(p_m,b), b>=0. Then

    sum h^(m,b)=S_m-d_0+b,
    R_(m,b)(t)=(1-bt) product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-d_j t)^N_j,
    N_0=2^(m-1)-1, N_j=2^(m-j-1) for 1<=j<m.           (3)

The exact worst normalized quadratic objective over ALL finite dimensions
is

    Q_m(b)=max_(0<=t<=1) t R_(m,b)(t)^2.                (4)

Indeed diagonalizing a positive semidefinite Hessian bounded by the identity
makes the normalized error a weighted average of the displayed scalar
quantities. A scalar quadratic attains the maximum. Zero eigenvalues have
zero objective contribution; affine translations to a minimizer change
neither calculation. Thus this is a full quadratic-class computation.

For an exact finite characterization of (4), subdivide [0,1] at all its
distinct interior roots 1/d_j and, when b>0, 1/b. On each root-free open
interval the logarithmic derivative of the nonzero objective is

    L(t)=1/t-2b/(1-bt)-2sum_j N_j d_j/(1-d_j t),
    L'(t)=-1/t^2-2b^2/(1-bt)^2
                    -2sum_j N_j d_j^2/(1-d_j t)^2<0.   (5)

Consequently there is exactly one interior maximizer between consecutive
roots, also between zero and the first root. On the last interval the
maximum is either its unique root of L or t=1. Values at roots are zero.
Coincident roots are combined, and b=0 simply removes its term. Equations
(3)--(5) specify the complete spectrum without a numerical sweep.

The unit-curvature values alone are

    P_m(1)=-(ac)^(2^m-1)c^(-m),
    R_(m,b)(1)=(1-b)(ac)^(2^m-2)c^(1-m).                (6)

They are not used as a replacement for (4).

Its derivative has the sign of 2(S-d)-3P. Therefore its minimum on any
closed interval is attained at an endpoint. Among all occurrences of a
given level it suffices to check the first and last occurrence.

    D_(u+1)=M_u^2-c r_u^2
               >=(1-cr^2)M_u^2>0,

since cr^2<=3969/8000<1. At successive levels,

    D_(v+1)-D_v=M_u M_v+[M_u-(c-1)r_u]r_v>0,

because (c-1)r<=261/400<1. This proves (32) for every pair, including
the small levels with empty local blocks.

Suppose a ray construction selected at least two checkpoints i,j. Its
first two gradients and first old offset are

    m_0=1/(1+P), m_1=r_u m_0/(1+S), O_1=P m_0.

By (32), the second-return budget satisfies

    r_v m_1-O_1
       =m_0[r_u r_v/(1+S)-P]<m_0.                    (33)

With exactly two checkpoints, the terminal old-slope constraint requires
this quantity to be at least (1+T)m_0>=m_0. With three or more, the next
nonterminal gradient is this quantity divided by1 plus its block mass,
and hence is strictly below m_0, violating same-ray slope monotonicity.
Thus no accepted ray construction has two or more checkpoints. The
zero- and one-checkpoint cases recover K exactly, so

    F_ray_n(H_m)=K_n(H_m)=1/(2S_m+1).                  (34)

## 9. The complete universal complex lens is also below Huber

This concerns the accepted Lens_n and maximal path-value Gap_h from fact
`dfde2fa326c908bf`, not the larger schedule-dependent domain D_h. The
accepted bound is

    Gap_(H_m)(z)<=(2alpha-|z|^2)|P_m(z)|^2,
    z=alpha+i beta,
    kappa_lens=alpha-|z|^2>=|beta|cot(pi/(n+2)).        (35)

All chronological prefix jets and their interpolation cycles remain those
of the accepted definition. We only bound their actual terminal polynomial.
We prove, for m>=128,

    sup_(z in Lens_n) Gap_(H_m)(z)<1/(2S_m+1).         (36)

The endpoints z=0 and z=1 follow directly: the former has zero error,
and at the latter the upper bound in (35) is P_m(1)^2, covered by (21).
Every other lens point has 0<alpha<1 and kappa_lens>0. Put

    delta=tan(pi/(n+2))<=1/100,
    tau_z=|1-z|^2/(2kappa_lens),
    q_decay=99/100.

The delta bound follows from tan x<=2x for 0<=x<=1/2 and pi<4,
since n=2^m-1. The tangent inequality follows from sin x<=x and
cos x>=1-x^2/2>=7/8 on that interval. From the lens inequality,

    |beta|<=delta alpha(1-alpha),
    kappa_lens>=alpha(1-alpha)(1-delta^2/4),
    tau_z<=F_delta(1-alpha)/(2alpha),
    F_delta=(1+delta^2)/(1-delta^2/4)<101/100.           (37)

Consider a partial ruler H_j all of whose levels l<j satisfy
a c^l<tau_z, with j>=1. In particular tau_z>a>3/8, and (37) gives
alpha<101/176<3/5. Each step d_l of H_j satisfies

    d_l alpha<(1+tau_z)alpha
       <=alpha+F_delta(1-alpha)/2<81/100.              (38)

Its real factor is therefore positive, at least19/100. The inequalities
log(1-u)<=-u and log(1+u)<=u imply

    log|1-d_l z|
      <=-d_l alpha+d_l^2 beta^2/[2(19/100)^2].

Sum with the exact multiplicities of the partial ruler. Its sum of
squared steps is at most its largest step times S_j, and (38) bounds
that largest step by81/(100alpha). Hence

    |P_j(z)|<=exp[-(1-12delta^2)alpha S_j]
                       <=exp(-q_decay alpha S_j).    (39)

For the numerical coefficient here,
(81/100)/[2(19/100)^2]=4050/361<12, and
1-12/10000>99/100. This is a symbolic bound; no spectral sampling occurs.

If no level l<m reaches a c^l>=tau_z, (39) applies to H_m. From (35),

    Gap_(H_m)(z)<=2alpha exp(-2q_decay S_m alpha)
                        <=1/(q_decay e S_m).

Since S_m>=2 and e>8/3, its ratio to Huber is strictly less than

    (5/2)/(q_decay(8/3))=125/132<1.                   (40)

Otherwise let j<m be the first level with a c^j>=tau_z. Put
Y_j=c a c^j |z| |P_j(z)|. If j=0, Y_0=ac|z|<=ac<1.
If j>=1, (39) and S_j>=a c^j/r-1 give, by maximizing
v exp(-q_decay v/r) over v>=0,

    Y_j<= [cr sqrt(1+delta^2)/q_decay]
                              exp(q_decay alpha-1)
       <=(9/8)exp(-2/5)<1.                           (41)

Indeed cr<=441/400, sqrt(1+delta^2)<=10001/10000,
and dividing their product by99/100 gives a number below9/8.
Also alpha<3/5 and exp(2/5)>1+2/5>9/8.

For every level l>=j, the definition of tau_z gives exactly

    |1-d_l z|^2
      =a^2 c^(2l)|z|^2+|1-z|^2-2a c^l kappa_lens
      <=a^2 c^(2l)|z|^2.

Consequently the ruler recursion implies Y_(l+1)<=Y_l^2, so Y_m<=1.
If alpha>1/16, (35) and |z|>=alpha imply that the ratio of its bound
to Huber is at most

    (2S_m+1) 32/[c^2 a^2 c^(2m)]
      <=64/[(ac)^2 c^m]<128/2^m<1.                   (42)

If alpha<=1/16, then tau_z>=(1-alpha)/(2alpha)>=15/2>a,
so j>=1. The same estimate before (41) now gives

    Y_j<=(9/8)exp(1/16)/e
                  <(9/8)(16/15)(3/8)=9/20<1/2.

Here exp(t)<=1/(1-t) for 0<=t<1 follows termwise from its series,
and e>8/3 follows by retaining its terms through degree four.
There is at least one update after index j, hence Y_m<1/4. The fact
that tau_z<=a c^(m-1), together with
|1-z|^2>=1-2alpha and kappa_lens<=alpha, yields

    alpha>=1/[2(1+a c^(m-1))]=1/(2d_(m-1)).

Equation (35) is therefore at most

    1/[8c^2 a^2 c^(2m)alpha]
       <=d_(m-1)/[4c^2 a^2 c^(2m)].                  (43)

By (20), its ratio to Huber is less than3/16. Equations (40)--(43)
cover every lens point and prove (36). Consequently

    V_lens(H_m)=K_n(H_m)=F_ray_n(H_m)=1/(2S_m+1).      (44)

Combining (21), (31), (34), (44) gives the same exact 2/e limit-superior
obstruction even after including ALL accepted single-cut, alternating-ray,
and universal-lens baselines, as well as the complete quadratic class and
the retained two-block constant-tail mechanism from Section6. The full
schedule-dependent complex domain, general multidimensional nonlinear
orbits, and variable-gradient tails remain outside this statement.

## 10. Remove the angle restriction: every constant tail of this two-block prefix

The cap-angle condition (25) is not needed for the following stronger
obstruction. Allow EVERY 0<=kappa<=A in the two-block prefix (26), and
retain all its actual jets and the optimum jet. The prefix legality
calculation in Section6 still holds: the only strict comparison there
becomes nonnegative at kappa=A. At kappa=0 the second block is already
at a minimum. The argument proving origin is the closest minimizer is
unchanged. For ANY legal constant-gradient tail, (27)'s derivation before
using the cap range gives

    2f_end<=A kappa epsilon^2/(1+2T)
                  <=A^2 epsilon^2/(1+2T).             (45)

No claim that this outgoing upper bound is attainable is made. We show
its right side is itself smaller than the old Huber value on H_m.

First strengthen (32). Define q_pair=c r^2<1/2, r=c-2 as before.
For ANY selected i<j, with their levels u,v and preceding/intervening
masses P,S, one has

    R_pair:=(h_i-1)(h_j-1)/[(1+P)(1+S)]<=q_pair.       (46)

In the outside-copy case of Section8 the bound r^2 already suffices.
In the inside-copy case its denominator is at least
M_u(M_v-r_u-M_u). Write theta=r_u/M_u<=r and z=M_v/M_u.
Here z>=M_(u+1)/M_u=2+theta and r_v<=r M_v. Consequently

    R_pair<=theta r z/(z-1-theta)
              <=theta r(2+theta)<=r^2(2+r)=q_pair.    (47)

The middle inequality follows because z/(z-1-theta) decreases for
z>1+theta. This includes u=0. It proves (46) with an explicit uniform
margin, not just the strict inequality used for the ray exclusion.

Let p=1+P, x=1+S, t=1+T and let r_i=h_i-1, r_j=h_j-1.
Here p,x,t are positive scalars, not the vector p from Section6. The
palindrome H_m gives the same (46) in the reverse chronological order:

    r_i r_j/(t x)<=q_pair.

Every cut has its own H_level on both sides. Thus r_i<=r p and
r_j<=r t. Combining these three bounds yields

    R_pair<=q_pair,
    p<=q_pair t/R_pair,
    x<=r^2 t/R_pair.                                  (48)

All quantities divided by are positive. The exact total mass is

    M_m=p+x+t+r_i+r_j
           <=(1+r)(p+t)+x.

Substituting (48), and then R_pair<=q_pair, gives

    R_pair M_m/t
       <=(1+r)R_pair+(1+r)q_pair+r^2
       <=D_pair:=2(1+r)q_pair+r^2.

Therefore

    R_pair<=min(q_pair,D_pair t/M_m).                 (49)

This retains both the true preceding mass and the true remaining tail;
neither is absorbed into a new initialization distance.

Write M=M_m, q=q_pair and D=D_pair temporarily. Since M>=8 and
D/q=2(1+r)+1/c<=199/60<4, the crossover t_0=qM/D exceeds1.
The function t^2/(2t-1) is increasing for t>=1 and 1/(2t-1) is
decreasing. Maximizing the bound from (49) on the two sides of t_0
therefore gives the exact elementary envelope

    R_pair^2/(2t-1)
       <=q^2/(2qM/D-1)=qD/(2M-D/q).                  (50)

For the permitted parameters,

    qD<=661/800,
    D/q<=199/60.

Indeed q<1/2, r<=9/20 give
D<=29/20+81/400=661/400, and the displayed formula for D/q gives
its bound using c>=12/5. Consequently, since M>=8,

    [R_pair^2/(2t-1)] / [1/(2M-1)]
       <=(661/800)(2M-1)/(2M-199/60)
       <=5949/6088<1.                                (51)

The ratio in the middle decreases with M because199/60>1; its value
at M=8 is5949/6088. Equations (45),(51) prove that EVERY legal
constant-gradient extension of ANY angle in (26) satisfies

    2f_end<=(5949/6088)/(2S_m+1).                     (52)

This covers all choices of the two checkpoints, all ordinary block
contents in their actual order, both endpoint angles, affine offsets,
positive values, additional dimensions, and arbitrary interpolation
choices for the tail, provided that its gradient is constant at all
actual tail queries and the terminal point. If no such tail exists the
statement is vacuous. No tail feasibility or direction optimization is
silently assumed. At kappa=0 its error is zero as noted above.

In particular, removing only the cap-angle restriction is NOT an escape
from the quantitative obstruction. Sections1--10 give the single joint
conclusion, for m>=128 and the original appended b=d_0:

    max{all quadratic scores, F_ray_n(H_m), V_lens(H_m),
        all Section10 two-block constant-tail scores}
       =K_n(H_m)=1/(2S_m+1),
    limsup of B_n times this maximum <=2/e<1.          (53)

The original all-schedule target remains unresolved. The remaining
geometric change must alter the retained two-block prefix itself or use
varying gradients inside the remaining ruler tail. The full
schedule-dependent complex domain and the other unrestricted mechanisms
identified in Section9 are also still open.

## 11. A quantitative requirement for a genuinely varying tail

Keep ANY angle 0<=kappa<=A in the exact retained prefix (26), but now
permit a varying tail. Denote its physical steps by t_l>=0, its gradients
at those queries by g_l, its terminal gradient by g_end, and put

    T=sum_l t_l, sigma=2T+1,
    Delta_tail=sum_l t_l(g_end-g_l).

This notation changes neither the prescribed steps nor the retained jets.
Its terminal point is y+epsilon d-sum_l t_l g_l. The outgoing
interpolation inequality to the retained jet (y+q,q,||q||^2/2) is

    2f_end<=2epsilon<d,g_end>-sigma||g_end||^2
                                  +2<g_end,Delta_tail>.

Completing the square gives the more useful exact bound

    2f_end<=A kappa epsilon^2/sigma
       +2<g_end,Delta_tail>
       -sigma||g_end-epsilon d/sigma||^2.             (54)

For the H_m geometry, the first term is bounded by gamma K, where
gamma=5949/6088 and K=1/(2S_m+1), by the complete calculation (45)--(51).
Therefore any such witness reaching 2f_end>=1/B_n must satisfy

    2<g_end,Delta_tail>
       >=1/B_n-gamma K
                   +sigma||g_end-epsilon d/sigma||^2. (55)

The true closest-minimizer normalization is still1 by the first retained
checkpoint jet. In particular, (24) implies the quantitative necessary
condition

    liminf B_n * 2<g_end,Delta_tail> >=1-2gamma/e>0     (56)

for any unbounded sequence of successful witnesses of this form.
This requirement keeps every parameter loss. Merely introducing new
gradient directions is insufficient: if
<g_end,g_l>>=||g_end||^2 at every positive tail step, the left side
of (55) is nonpositive. It includes all collinear contracting tails
g_l=c_l g_end with c_l>=1, and all changes g_l=g_end+w_l with
<g_end,w_l>=0. Neither class can escape the obstruction.

When T>0 and g_end!=0, Cauchy--Schwarz additionally gives

    sum_l t_l||g_l-g_end||^2
      >= [ (1/B_n-gamma K)_+ ]^2/[4T||g_end||^2]        (57)

for any successful witness. Equation (55) is stronger because it
retains the sign of the required terminal correlation and the square
loss. No sufficient construction with the required positive correlation
has been established. This is a necessary quantitative interface, not a
new lower bound on W_n and not an assertion of feasibility.

## 12. A different positive-height prefix, and its first failed shortcut

The preceding obstruction fixes the zero height at the second checkpoint.
One can change that geometry while retaining a legal function and exact
normalization. Fix M_0,M_1>=1, A>0, epsilon>0, choose

    0<=kappa<=A, 0<=nu^2<=kappa(A-kappa),
    v= kappa^2+nu^2,
    p=(1,0)/M_0, q=(-kappa,nu)/M_1,
    X=(-A,0), d=-M_1q, y=X+d,
    delta_second=(A kappa-v)/M_1>=0.                  (58)

Use the same actual ordinary blocks and checkpoints of sizes1+A M_0
and1+M_1 epsilon. The one fixed envelope of max(0,<p,z>,<q,z>)
realizes the first two blocks: the first p-plane comparison is unchanged;
in the second block, for 1<=t<=M_1,

    <q,X-tq>=A kappa/M_1-tv/M_1^2>=delta_second>=0,
    <p,X-tq>=(-A+t kappa/M_1)/M_0<=0.

Every query is thus legal. The second checkpoint jet has proximal point
y and value f_j=delta_second+||q||^2/2. The origin is the true closest
minimizer by the same saturated first checkpoint jet, without assuming
anything about the subsequent interpolant.

For ANY legal constant-gradient tail of total mass T, write sigma=2T+1.
The retained second-checkpoint inequality and the optimum inequality,
completed separately as squares, give

    2f_end<=min {
      2delta_second+epsilon^2 v/sigma,
      [A^2-2A(1+epsilon)kappa+(1+epsilon)^2v]/sigma
    }.                                                (59)

These are simultaneous necessary conditions, not an attained formula.
All incoming interpolation inequalities to the old positive-height
queries must still be imposed to produce a witness. They are not removed
by the accepted unqueried-terminal reduction: these are constraints on
the queried tail itself.

The tempting shortcut of treating the first term of (59) as an attainable
retained-height payoff is false. Take epsilon=1, kappa=A/2 and nu=0.
Then delta_second=A^2/(4M_1)>0, but

    X_tail=y+epsilon d=(-A,0)+2(A/2,0)=0.

This is the retained minimizer, so every subsequent gradient and every
terminal error are zero, for EVERY nonnegative tail. The first term
of (59) is A^2/(2M_1)+A^2/(4sigma)>0, whereas the optimum term is zero.
This is an explicit legal fixed-function counterexample to that shortcut,
not merely inconsistent formal data. It also shows why raising the
checkpoint height cannot be evaluated independently of its location.

The screened next tasks are consequently precise: either construct an
actual varying tail satisfying (55) with every old-query inequality, or
solve the joint positive-height prefix/tail constraints behind (58)--(59)
and obtain a value at least1/B_n for all appended b. No such payoff
comparison is claimed here. The present round's completed result is the
quantitative baseline and two-block-mechanism obstruction (53).

claim: Quantitative physical-length consequence of the complete three-step credit capacity proof: any schedule assembled by the stated Omega/phi primitive joins from ordinary benchmark-capped leaves and arbitrary three-step E_theta-valid leaves, then by the stated psi dominant joins, satisfies W_N(H)>=U_N^ZJ at EVERY horizon. evidence:
# Three-step capacity with arbitrary signed terminal credit

Status: complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. No SDP/PEP or
fact_submit call. This closes the proposed three-step discovery domain if
the candidate survives verification. It does not settle the general signed
cone question or the original all-horizon normalized objective target.

## 1. Statement and definitions

Let h=(u,v,w) be a nonnegative three-step schedule, let T=1+u+v+w, and put
t=sqrt(2), lambda=1+t, T_0=lambda^2=3+2t. Along gradient descent on a convex
differentiable function f with 1-Lipschitz gradient and a minimizer, write
x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i, g_i=grad f(x_i), f_i=f(x_i), and

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_h=2sum_(i<3)h_i(f_i-f_3)+sum_(i<3)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                             -(T-1)T||g_3||^2,
 J_h=sum_(i<3)h_i Q_(i,3), E_theta=V_h-theta J_h.

Claim. If T>=T_0 and h differs from (t,2,t), there is a fixed, finite-dimensional
convex differentiable 1-smooth function, with a minimizer, whose full h-run has

              V_h<0 and Q_(i,3)=0 for every i<3.       (1)

Consequently, for EVERY real theta, universal validity of E_theta>=0 with
T>=T_0 forces h=(t,2,t). The same necessary conclusion holds for any intrinsic
certificate V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij whose values cancel, whose remainder is PSD
on the complete independent formal gradient space, and whose multipliers are
nonnegative except for arbitrary signs on incoming-terminal finite pairs.
No validity-versus-certifiability equivalence is assumed.

At h=(t,2,t), an explicit ordinary primitive certificate is given in Section 7.
Therefore, for each theta>=0, the exact maximum three-step capacity in the
E_theta-valid class and in its nonnegative-certificate class is T_0, uniquely
attained by Silver. The arbitrary-signed-certificate class has that same
maximum. In particular the conclusion applies throughout 0<=theta<1.

The proof includes the required domain reductions directly. C32 and earlier
max4 findings motivated them, but are not used as unverified premises.

## 2. Legal projection witnesses and the first four constraints

Here is a self-contained way to turn each finite array below into a fixed
legal function. Suppose its GD equations hold, its terminal point satisfies
x_3=g_3, and its assigned values are

 f_i=<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2.

Set y_i=x_i-g_i. Expansion gives

 Q_ij=<g_i-g_j,y_j>, Q_(i,3)=0,
 V_h=||x_0||^2-T^2||g_3||^2.                         (2)

If every finite Q_ij<=0 and <g_i,y_i>>=0, take K=conv{0,g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3}.
Those inequalities say precisely <y_j,z-g_j><=0 for every vertex z of K and
hence for every z in K. Thus g_j=P_K(x_j). The function

 F_K(x)=max_(z in K)[<x,z>-||z||^2/2]

interpolates all assigned values and gradients. The projection normal
inequalities imply <P_K(x)-P_K(x'),x-x'>>=||P_K(x)-P_K(x')||^2, so P_K is
1-Lipschitz. The maximizing formula gives
0<=F_K(x+d)-F_K(x)-<P_K(x),d><=<P_K(x+d)-P_K(x),d><=||d||^2,
which proves differentiability with gradient P_K. Thus F_K is globally convex
and 1-smooth; it has minimum F_K(0)=0. No unverified interpolation theorem is
needed for these arrays.

At any selected step b>1, with preceding and following sums P,Q, use derivative
clip(x,-(b-1)/(Q+1),1) and start at P+1. The preceding gradients are 1 and the
following gradients are -(b-1)/(Q+1), ending at that negative threshold.
The function obtained by integration has all the properties in (2). Its
energy yields the necessary cut inequality

              T(b-1)_+ <= (P+1)(Q+1).               (3)

For b<=1 this inequality is automatic. This includes schedules with zero
steps. The first and last cuts give

              u,w <= M(T):=2T/(T+1)<2.              (4)

For u,v,w>1 write a=u-1, A=u+1, r=v-1, D=w+1, eta=r/D.
The following additional inequalities are necessary if no witness (1) exists:

 F_Q=1-T^2 a^2 r^2(w-1)^2 >=0,                     (5)
 F_B=A^2-T^2 eta^2 >=0,                            (6)
 F_C=A^2-T^2 r^2(w-1)^2 >=0,                       (7)
 F_N=a u F_B+(1+eta)u^2(2-u^2) >=0.                (8)

For (5), use f(x)=x^2/2 and x_0=1. For (6), use the middle cut in (3),
whose x=(A,1,-r,-eta), g=(1,1,-eta,-eta). For (7), provided r(w-1)<=1,
use derivative min(x,1), start at A, and obtain
x=(A,1,-r,r(w-1)), g=(1,1,-r,r(w-1)). It is a fixed convex 1-smooth
function with minimum at0, and its terminal point is inside its quadratic
part. Each of these functions satisfies (2).

For (8), provided eta a<1, combine the middle-cut base from (6) with the
auxiliary array

 x_aux=(1,-a,ra,eta a), g_aux=(1,-a,eta a,eta a),
 f_aux,i=x_aux,i*g_aux,i-g_aux,i^2/2.

The auxiliary normals are (0,0,w eta a,0). Its only positive finite residual
is Q_aux,(0,2)=(1-eta a)w eta a. Every outgoing optimum inequality holds,
since each g_aux,i*y_aux,i is nonnegative. In the base array,
Q_base,(0,2)=-(1+eta)w eta, and all finite residuals are nonpositive.
Take their orthogonal sum with auxiliary scale sqrt(epsilon), where

                   epsilon=(1+eta)/[a(1-eta a)].

Residuals add, the sole positive auxiliary edge is canceled exactly, every
other finite edge is nonpositive, and every optimum condition holds.
The projection construction above realizes one fixed legal function. Its
energy is F_B+epsilon(1-T^2 eta^2 a^2)=F_N/[a(1-eta a)]; the denominator
is positive. The equality follows by 1-a^2 A^2=u^2(2-u^2).
The terminal point stays core, so every incoming-terminal residual is zero.

## 3. Complete reduction to the asymmetric region

Assume T>=T_0 and assume, for contradiction, that every applicable witness
above has nonnegative energy. First v>1: otherwise T<=2+2M(T) gives
T^2-5T-2<=0, whereas at T_0 this polynomial equals 2t>0 and it increases
thereafter. Thus r>0 and the middle cut applies, initially with A=u+1,D=w+1.
Since T=A+D+r, it gives

 T(T-A-D)<=AD<=(A+D)^2/4,
 T<=lambda(A+D)/2<=lambda(M(T)+1).

Hence T^2+(1-3lambda)T-lambda<=0. The polynomial increases for T>=T_0,
and its value at7 is 56-22lambda>0 because lambda<5/2. Thus T<7, and
u,w<M(7)=7/4. Both endpoints exceed1: if u<=1, then A<=2,D<11/4 and
r>T-19/4, so Tr>T(T-19/4)>=T_0(T_0-19/4)=11/4+5t/2>11/2>AD,
a contradiction. The proof for w is identical.

The extra hypotheses needed in Section 2 now hold everywhere in this box:

 r(w-1)<=A(w^2-1)/T<363/(64T_0)<1,
 eta a<=Aa/T=(u^2-1)/T<33/(16T_0)<1.                (9)

For the first numerical inequality, 363<64T_0 follows from
171<128sqrt(2), whose square is 29241<32768. Also

                   u+w>=2T/lambda-2>=2t.            (10)

If u<=t, then w>=t. The left-minus-right difference in the necessary

T_0(T_0-t-w-2)(w-1)-(t+1)=T_0(w-t)(2-w)>=0.
It is positive except when u=w=t,T=T_0; equality then gives v=2.

If w>=t as well, consider q_T(u,w)=T(u-1)(w-1)(T-u-w-2) on

For such endpoints, F_N strictly decreases as r>0 increases, with u,w fixed:

 D^2 F_N/u=u^2 D^2+(4-2u^2-u^3)D-(u-1)(u+2)^2=:P_u(D).

This quadratic has one positive and one negative root. At D=lambda,

       t<u<7/4, 1<v<2, 1<w<t, T_0<=T<7,
                       u+w>=2T/lambda-2.             (11)

## 4. The additional two-cut witness forces u<8/5

Here the different letters R=u-1, k=v-1, C=w+1, B=v+w+1=C+k+1 are used
to avoid confusing the first and second bridge. Thus T=B+R+1.
Set eta_1=R/B, zeta=k/C, p=-1/R. Consider the two scalar arrays

 x_base=(1,-R,-C eta_1,-eta_1),
 g_base=(1,-eta_1,-eta_1,-eta_1),
 x_aux=(p,1,-k,-zeta), g_aux=(p,1,-zeta,-zeta).

Both obey the same three GD steps; assign values by f=g*x-g^2/2.
Their normal arrays are respectively
(0,-(B-1)eta_1,-w eta_1,0) and (0,0,-w zeta,0).
The base is an actual clipped-derivative trajectory. Within (11),
R zeta<3/8<1. The auxiliary array's only positive residual is
Q_aux,(0,2)=w zeta(1/R-zeta); all its other finite residuals are zero
except Q_aux,(1,2)<0. Every optimum inequality holds in both arrays.
The base residual Q_base,(0,2)=-(1+eta_1)w eta_1 cancels that positive
edge when the orthogonal auxiliary scale is sqrt(epsilon_1), where

             epsilon_1=eta_1(1+eta_1)/[zeta(1/R-zeta)].

All other finite inequalities remain nonpositive. The projection realization
in Section 2 supplies a fixed globally legal function; its terminal point is
core and every incoming-terminal Q is zero. Its energy is

 V_mix=1-T^2 eta_1^2+epsilon_1(R^(-2)-T^2 zeta^2)
      =(C+kB)(B+R)/[B^2 k(C-Rk)]
                     *{C-Rk[1+R(T+1)]}.             (12)

The prefactor is positive. For an algebra audit, substitute
epsilon_1=R^2 C^2(B+R)/[B^2 k(C-Rk)], put the two energy terms over

                    R k[1+R(T+1)]<=C.              (13)

In (11), w<t and T>=T_0 imply
k=T-2-u-w>1+t-u=t-R, C<lambda. Therefore (13) implies

            R(t-R)[1+(T_0+1)R]<lambda.              (14)

t-1<R<3/4. Indeed its derivative is
t-2R+(T_0+1)R(2t-3R); here t-2R>-1/10, T_0+1>6,
R>2/5 and 2t-3R>1/2, so H'(R)>11/10>0. These bounds follow from
