# Positive interior heights do not rescue the consecutive Markov ruler relay

Status: complete UNVERIFIED candidate. No solver or fact_submit allocation.
This is a whole-mechanism obstruction with an explicit data domain, including
all positive interior margins, actual old queries, actual displacement, and
free unqueried terminal gradient. It is NOT an upper bound on unrestricted
W_n. Mathematical premises are accepted interpolation fact
`1252b8823bb5a290` and the exact benchmark definitions in
`b98bb807d514e80d`. All additional calculations are proved in this document.

## 1. Schedule, complete family, and claimed comparison

For an integer m>=128, fix throughout the horizon

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    H_0=(), H_(l+1)=(H_l,1+a c^l,H_l), n=2^m-1,
    M_l=1+sum H_l, r_l=a c^l, r=c-2,
    K=1/(2M_m-1).

Select the FIRST occurrences of consecutive checkpoint levels u,...,v,
where 0<=u<=v<=m-1. Write k=v-u. The initial ordinary block is H_u;
between the first occurrences of levels l and l+1 the ordinary block is
H_l. Thus its capacities (one plus its actual mass) are

    C_u=M_u, C_l=M_(l-1) for u<l<=v.

Choose ANY endpoint margins w_l in [0,r_l]. Define

    tau_l=C_l+w_l, A_l=r_l-w_l.

For each u<=l<v with positive A_l choose

    0<beta_l<=A_l/tau_(l+1), theta_l=A_l/tau_(l+1).

Let e_u,...,e_v be orthonormal. The ACTUAL Euclidean vectors are

    g_u=e_u/tau_u, alpha_u=1/tau_u,
    g_(l+1)=-beta_l g_l+z_(l+1),
    z_(l+1) orthogonal to all earlier vectors,
    ||z_(l+1)||^2=alpha_l^2 beta_l(theta_l-beta_l),
    alpha_(l+1)^2=theta_l beta_l alpha_l^2.

Zero degeneracies are interpreted by the same recurrence without division
by a zero norm. A zero prescribed gradient has prescribed value zero, so
in a legal realization its actual point is a minimizer and every later
iterate remains there. Such cases have zero final error and require no
separate positive-gradient estimates below.

Start at X_u=e_u. Let X_l be the actual start of ordinary block l and

    Y_l=X_l-tau_l g_l,
    X_(l+1)=Y_l-A_l g_l,
    Y_(l+1)=Y_l-A_l g_l-tau_(l+1)g_(l+1).       (1)

These are precisely the actual GD displacements: an ordinary block of
mass C_l-1 followed by checkpoint 1+r_l has mass C_l+r_l, and
tau_l+A_l=C_l+r_l.

At EVERY actual query in block l, including its checkpoint query, let t
be the ordinary cumulative mass already executed. Prescribe

    x=Y_l+(tau_l-t)g_l,
    grad f(x)=g_l,
    f(x)=(tau_l-t-1/2)alpha_l^2,  0<=t<=C_l-1. (2)

The endpoint proximal height is w_l alpha_l^2. No height is discarded or
assigned independently of a position and a value. Include the optimum
sample f(0)=0, grad f(0)=0. Consider EVERY single convex differentiable
1-smooth function realizing these data, in arbitrary finite dimension.
Its values or gradients away from these samples are not fixed.

Execute checkpoint v and then the whole remaining actual ruler tail,
of total mass T. Its start is

    X=Y_v-A_v g_v.                                  (3)

Require one arbitrary common gradient q at the QUERIED samples of this
remaining tail. The terminal gradient is free. Allow all terminal-cell
values, offsets, and extra dimensions. Equivalently complete this entire
queried prefix by the maximal interpolant of accepted 1252b8823bb5a290,
with every old anchor retained; other legal completions are also covered.

Every legal member of this entire family has true initial distance one
and satisfies

    2 f(x_n) <= Gamma K, Gamma=31360/38557<5/6.       (4)

The uniform asymptotic comparison to the ACTUAL exact benchmark is

    limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) 2 f(x_n)
                <= 2/[e(1+sqrt(2))] < 1.            (5)

Both bounds are uniform over u,v, every margin and correlation, every
legal interpolant, and every allowed terminal cell. Thus repeated
positive interior heights in this explicit Markov family do not supply
a benchmark-level witness.

## 2. All-query legality, with no omitted remote plane

The accepted interpolation inequality in proximal notation is

    delta_j >= delta_i + <g_i,y_j-y_i>,
    y_i=x_i-g_i, delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2.             (6)

For the data (2) put d=tau_l-t-1. Then

    y=Y_l+d g_l, delta=d alpha_l^2,
    w_l<=d<=tau_l-1.

For i<j define

    P_ij=product_(l=i)^(j-1) beta_l,
    Qprod_ij=product_(l=i)^(j-1) theta_l,
    R_l=A_l-tau_(l+1) beta_l>=0,
    L_ij=sum_(l=i)^(j-1) (-1)^(l-i) R_l P_il,

with empty product one. Directly from (1) and the vector recurrence,

    <g_i,g_j>=(-1)^(j-i) alpha_i^2 P_ij,
    alpha_j^2=alpha_i^2 P_ij Qprod_ij,
    <g_i,Y_j>=-alpha_i^2 L_ij for i<j,
    <g_i,Y_j>=0 for i>=j.                            (7)

To verify the last identity, each increment
DeltaY_l=Y_(l+1)-Y_l=-A_l g_l-tau_(l+1)g_(l+1)
is orthogonal to g_(l+1) because
<g_l,g_(l+1)>=-beta_l alpha_l^2 and
tau_(l+1)alpha_(l+1)^2=A_l beta_l alpha_l^2.
Every later gradient is a scalar multiple of g_(l+1) plus fresh
orthogonal directions, so DeltaY_l is orthogonal to all those gradients.
Since Y_u=0, summation proves the claimed identity. Taking the earlier
gradient inner products of the same increments proves the formula for
L_ij, including its signs.

We will prove theta_l<=r<1 below; hence beta_l<1 and Qprod_ij<1. By (7),
every proposed future supporting plane g_j has value at an old proximal
query Y_i+d g_i at most its current value d alpha_i^2. The comparison
holds at odd lag by its negative sign and at even lag because P_ij<=1.

current plane is exactly

    alpha_i^2 [-L_ij+d P_ij((-1)^(j-i)-Qprod_ij)].        (8)

For even lag the exact strongest condition is

    L_ij >= (tau_j-1)P_ij(1-Qprod_ij),  j-i even.        (9)

For odd lag no extra condition is needed once (9) holds for all even
lags: at lag one L=R_i>=0; at larger odd lag,
L_ij=L_(i,j-1)+P_(i,j-1) R_(j-1)>=0 by (9), and the
d coefficient in (8) is negative. Thus (9), for all even pairs, is a
NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT complete legality test for the prescribed
relay data. Queries inside a block require no additional comparisons:
their d coordinates lie between the two actual endpoint queries.

For sufficiency construct the ONE fixed function

    J(z)=max(0,<g_u,z>,...,<g_v,z>),
    f_min(x)=min_z [J(z)+||x-z||^2/2].                (10)

All comparisons just proved say that the selected g_l is a subgradient
of J at the proposed y. Its subgradient inequality plus the quadratic
term proves y is the unique minimizer in (10), with value and gradient

||g(x)-g(x')||^2<=<g(x)-g(x'),x-x'>. The two minimizing
inequalities then identify the envelope derivative as g and prove its

genuine realization whenever (9) holds. Necessity of (9) follows from
(6) for the actual endpoint query in block i and first query in block j.
This also shows that no other interpolant can evade (9).

The bound below is for ALL interpolants of (2), not only (10). In
particular it never assumes a virtual Y_l is a minimizer of another
interpolant. That unsupported inference would lose the positive-height
and location distinction that this calculation is intended to retain.

For any legal interpolant, the first checkpoint sample is
x=(w_u+1)g_u, f=(w_u+1/2)alpha_u^2. Apply interpolation
with ANY minimizer z. Since its minimum is zero, (6) gives
<g_u,z><=0. Therefore <e_u,z><=0, and
||e_u-z||^2=1+||z||^2-2<e_u,z>>=1.

## 3. One retained old query still forces a fixed correlation loss

Use (9) at j=l+2. With P=beta_l beta_(l+1) its exact form is

    A_l-beta_l(tau_(l+1)+A_(l+1))

## 4. Exact location energy, including every retained height

The increments DeltaY_l defined after (7) are mutually orthogonal. For
l<j, DeltaY_j is a linear combination of g_j,g_(j+1), both orthogonal to
DeltaY_l. They are also orthogonal to g_v. Their exact squared norms are

Hence the ACTUAL post-checkpoint point (3) obeys the telescoping identity

    ||X||^2
      = A_u^2 alpha_u^2
            +sum_(i=u+1)^v (A_i^2-tau_i^2)alpha_i^2. (16)

All transverse displacement from the starting point is present in this
identity. Positive heights enter via

    A_i^2-tau_i^2
      =(r_i+C_i)(r_i-C_i-2w_i) <= r_i^2-C_i^2.      (17)

Define s=c r>1, rho=3/4 and eta=rho s^2. The inequality s>1 follows

    s<=273/256, eta<=223587/262144<1.

C_i=M_(u+j-1)<=c^(j-1) M_u. The norm recurrence and (15) give

       <= r^2 rho eta^(j-1) if 1<=j<k,
       <= r^2 eta^(k-1)     if j=k.                  (18)

No positive height is added as an independent payoff; it has already

## 5. Actual terminal displacement and free-gradient completion

The entire right copy H_(m-1) lies after every selected first occurrence,
so T>=M_(m-1)-1. Its final step is b=1+a<3/2. Set M=M_(m-1).
There is at least one queried tail sample, and the last queried position
is X-(T-b)q. Optimum interpolation and smoothness on the ACTUAL final
step give, for every legal completion,

    2f(x_n)
      <=2<q,X>-(2T+1-b^2)||q||^2
      <=||X||^2/(2T+1-b^2).                         (21)

The denominator is positive because M>=2^(m-1)>57. This argument
does not prescribe the terminal gradient and does not replace the
full maximal interpolant by a reduced-anchor function. It is a necessary
bound on that same full interpolant, using its retained last query.

Since M_m<=c M, (13) and b^2<=9/4 imply

    (2M_m-1)/(2T+1-b^2)
       <=(2c M-1)/(2M-13/4) <5/2.                  (22)

To check the last inequality, its right side minus its left numerator
after multiplication by the positive denominator is at least

Status: complete UNVERIFIED candidate. No solver or fact_submit allocation.
This is a whole-mechanism obstruction with an explicit data domain, including
all positive interior margins, actual old queries, actual displacement, and
free unqueried terminal gradient. It is NOT an upper bound on unrestricted
W_n. Mathematical premises are accepted interpolation fact
`1252b8823bb5a290` and the exact benchmark definitions in
`b98bb807d514e80d`. All additional calculations are proved in this document.

## 1. Schedule, complete family, and claimed comparison

For an integer m>=128, fix throughout the horizon

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    H_0=(), H_(l+1)=(H_l,1+a c^l,H_l), n=2^m-1,
    M_l=1+sum H_l, r_l=a c^l, r=c-2,
    K=1/(2M_m-1).

Select the FIRST occurrences of consecutive checkpoint levels u,...,v,
where 0<=u<=v<=m-1. Write k=v-u. The initial ordinary block is H_u;
between the first occurrences of levels l and l+1 the ordinary block is
H_l. Thus its capacities (one plus its actual mass) are

    C_u=M_u, C_l=M_(l-1) for u<l<=v.

Choose ANY endpoint margins w_l in [0,r_l]. Define

    tau_l=C_l+w_l, A_l=r_l-w_l.

For each u<=l<v with positive A_l choose

    0<beta_l<=A_l/tau_(l+1), theta_l=A_l/tau_(l+1).

Let e_u,...,e_v be orthonormal. The ACTUAL Euclidean vectors are

    g_u=e_u/tau_u, alpha_u=1/tau_u,
    g_(l+1)=-beta_l g_l+z_(l+1),
    z_(l+1) orthogonal to all earlier vectors,
    ||z_(l+1)||^2=alpha_l^2 beta_l(theta_l-beta_l),
    alpha_(l+1)^2=theta_l beta_l alpha_l^2.

Zero degeneracies are interpreted by the same recurrence without division
by a zero norm. A zero prescribed gradient has prescribed value zero, so
in a legal realization its actual point is a minimizer and every later
iterate remains there. Such cases have zero final error and require no
separate positive-gradient estimates below.

Start at X_u=e_u. Let X_l be the actual start of ordinary block l and

    Y_l=X_l-tau_l g_l,
    X_(l+1)=Y_l-A_l g_l,
    Y_(l+1)=Y_l-A_l g_l-tau_(l+1)g_(l+1).       (1)

These are precisely the actual GD displacements: an ordinary block of
mass C_l-1 followed by checkpoint 1+r_l has mass C_l+r_l, and
tau_l+A_l=C_l+r_l.

At EVERY actual query in block l, including its checkpoint query, let t
be the ordinary cumulative mass already executed. Prescribe

    x=Y_l+(tau_l-t)g_l,
    grad f(x)=g_l,
    f(x)=(tau_l-t-1/2)alpha_l^2,  0<=t<=C_l-1. (2)

The endpoint proximal height is w_l alpha_l^2. No height is discarded or
assigned independently of a position and a value. Include the optimum
sample f(0)=0, grad f(0)=0. Consider EVERY single convex differentiable
1-smooth function realizing these data, in arbitrary finite dimension.
Its values or gradients away from these samples are not fixed.

Execute checkpoint v and then the whole remaining actual ruler tail,
of total mass T. Its start is

    X=Y_v-A_v g_v.                                  (3)

Require one arbitrary common gradient q at the QUERIED samples of this
remaining tail. The terminal gradient is free. Allow all terminal-cell
values, offsets, and extra dimensions. Equivalently complete this entire
queried prefix by the maximal interpolant of accepted 1252b8823bb5a290,
with every old anchor retained; other legal completions are also covered.

Every legal member of this entire family has true initial distance one
and satisfies

    2 f(x_n) <= Gamma K, Gamma=31360/38557<5/6.       (4)

The uniform asymptotic comparison to the ACTUAL exact benchmark is

    limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) 2 f(x_n)
                <= 2/[e(1+sqrt(2))] < 1.            (5)

Both bounds are uniform over u,v, every margin and correlation, every
legal interpolant, and every allowed terminal cell. Thus repeated
positive interior heights in this explicit Markov family do not supply

## 2. All-query legality, with no omitted remote plane

The accepted interpolation inequality in proximal notation is

    y_i=x_i-g_i, delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2.             (6)

For the data (2) put d=tau_l-t-1. Then

    y=Y_l+d g_l, delta=d alpha_l^2,
    w_l<=d<=tau_l-1.

For i<j define

    P_ij=product_(l=i)^(j-1) beta_l,
    Qprod_ij=product_(l=i)^(j-1) theta_l,
    R_l=A_l-tau_(l+1) beta_l>=0,
    L_ij=sum_(l=i)^(j-1) (-1)^(l-i) R_l P_il,

with empty product one. Directly from (1) and the vector recurrence,

    <g_i,g_j>=(-1)^(j-i) alpha_i^2 P_ij,
    alpha_j^2=alpha_i^2 P_ij Qprod_ij,
    <g_i,Y_j>=-alpha_i^2 L_ij for i<j,
    <g_i,Y_j>=0 for i>=j.                            (7)

DeltaY_l=Y_(l+1)-Y_l=-A_l g_l-tau_(l+1)g_(l+1)
is orthogonal to g_(l+1) because
<g_l,g_(l+1)>=-beta_l alpha_l^2 and
tau_(l+1)alpha_(l+1)^2=A_l beta_l alpha_l^2.
Every later gradient is a scalar multiple of g_(l+1) plus fresh
orthogonal directions, so DeltaY_l is orthogonal to all those gradients.
Since Y_u=0, summation proves the claimed identity. Taking the earlier
gradient inner products of the same increments proves the formula for
L_ij, including its signs.

We will prove theta_l<=r<1 below; hence beta_l<1 and Qprod_ij<1. By (7),
every proposed future supporting plane g_j has value at an old proximal
query Y_i+d g_i at most its current value d alpha_i^2. The comparison
holds at odd lag by its negative sign and at even lag because P_ij<=1.
For an old plane i at a later query in block j, its value minus the
current plane is exactly

    alpha_i^2 [-L_ij+d P_ij((-1)^(j-i)-Qprod_ij)].        (8)

For even lag the exact strongest condition is

    L_ij >= (tau_j-1)P_ij(1-Qprod_ij),  j-i even.        (9)

For odd lag no extra condition is needed once (9) holds for all even
lags: at lag one L=R_i>=0; at larger odd lag,
L_ij=L_(i,j-1)+P_(i,j-1) R_(j-1)>=0 by (9), and the
d coefficient in (8) is negative. Thus (9), for all even pairs, is a
NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT complete legality test for the prescribed
relay data. Queries inside a block require no additional comparisons:
their d coordinates lie between the two actual endpoint queries.

For sufficiency construct the ONE fixed function

    J(z)=max(0,<g_u,z>,...,<g_v,z>),
    f_min(x)=min_z [J(z)+||x-z||^2/2].                (10)

All comparisons just proved say that the selected g_l is a subgradient
of J at the proposed y. Its subgradient inequality plus the quadratic
term proves y is the unique minimizer in (10), with value and gradient
given by (2). To recall the elementary smoothness argument, adding two
proximal subgradient inequalities gives
||g(x)-g(x')||^2<=<g(x)-g(x'),x-x'>. The two minimizing
inequalities then identify the envelope derivative as g and prove its
1-Lipschitz property; joint convexity proves convexity. Thus (10) is a
genuine realization whenever (9) holds. Necessity of (9) follows from
(6) for the actual endpoint query in block i and first query in block j.
This also shows that no other interpolant can evade (9).

The bound below is for ALL interpolants of (2), not only (10). In
particular it never assumes a virtual Y_l is a minimizer of another
interpolant. That unsupported inference would lose the positive-height
and location distinction that this calculation is intended to retain.

For any legal interpolant, the first checkpoint sample is
x=(w_u+1)g_u, f=(w_u+1/2)alpha_u^2. Apply interpolation
with ANY minimizer z. Since its minimum is zero, (6) gives
<g_u,z><=0. Therefore <e_u,z><=0, and
||e_u-z||^2=1+||z||^2-2<e_u,z>>=1.
Origin is a minimizer. The actual closest-minimizer distance is exactly
one for every legal completion, including the maximal one.

Use (9) at j=l+2. With P=beta_l beta_(l+1) its exact form is

## 4. Exact location energy, including every retained height

All transverse displacement from the starting point is present in this

      =(r_i+C_i)(r_i-C_i-2w_i) <= r_i^2-C_i^2.      (17)

For k=0, ||X||^2<=r^2<=Xi_m gives the same result. Since the
right side increases with c,r on the stated range,

    Xi_m <= (49/256)/(4-3(273/256)^2)
          =12544/38557 <1/3.                        (20)

No positive height is added as an independent payoff; it has already
affected both the incoming amplitude and actual outgoing location.

## 8. Arbitrary later affine intercepts obey the SAME bound

There is a stronger version that does not prescribe homogeneous function
values at any relay block after the first. Keep EXACTLY the positions,

evidence:
# Critical ruler: fixed asymmetric derivatives with within-block variation

Status: complete mathematical CANDIDATE, not verifier-accepted. No numerical
solver or fact_submit is allocated to this round. All new ingredients are
proved together below. Earlier C23/C24/C26 concern a different ruler and are
motivation, not premises. The only accepted input is the exact benchmark
recurrence in fact b98bb807d514e80d. This does not upper-bound unrestricted W.

## 1. The actual schedule and two whole-family statements

Fix the actual horizon parameter m>=128. Hold

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j),
    n=2^m-1, S_j=sum H_j, K=1/(2S_m+1)

fixed throughout the run. Set r_s=c-2 and A_mass=a/r_s. Direct summation gives

    S_j+1=A_mass c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j.                 (1)

For a number p_grow in[1/2,1), put beta_grow=1-p_grow and

    C_grow=(p_grow/beta_grow)^p_grow.

Choose two locally absolutely continuous profiles G_+,G_- on[0,infinity),
equal to t on[0,1], with

    0<=t G_sigma'(t)<=p_grow G_sigma(t) a.e. for t>1,
    1/kappa_ray<=G_+(t)/G_-(t)<=kappa_ray for t>=1.    (2)

Here kappa_ray>=1 and sigma denotes either sign. For any core radius R>0
and curvature mu in(0,1], define ONE FIXED derivative and its objective by

    g(sigma R t)=sigma mu R G_sigma(t),
    f(x)=integral_0^x g(s) ds.                       (3)

All parameters and the entire profiles may depend on m; they cannot change
during GD. These classes allow unbounded radial secant variation, asymmetry,
and arbitrarily many nonperiodic knots. Ordinary ruler subblocks need not
have constant gradients. Initial points are arbitrary and are not saturated.

Statement A, reciprocal cores. Suppose

    1/2<=p_grow<=3/4, kappa_ray C_grow<=23/10,
    mu=1/d_r for ANY integer r>=0.                  (4)

Every trajectory on H_m which strictly crosses zero hits zero subsequently.
The exact supremum, over the profiles, radius and nonzero initial point, is

    sup 2f(x_n)/x_0^2=1/(2S_m+d_r).                 (5)

This is attained by a symmetric Huber derivative. For r>=m there is no
strict crossing, and the same conclusion holds. In particular the maximum
over r in this class is 1/(2S_m+d_0)<K.

Statement B, arbitrary small curvatures. Suppose instead

    1/2<=p_grow<=2/3, kappa_ray C_grow<=7/4,
    0<mu<=1/d_2.                                   (6)

No resonance or reciprocal-curvature condition is imposed. Every trajectory
obeys

    2f(x_n)/x_0^2<=K.                              (7)

The supremum over this entire class lies between 1/(2S_m+d_2) and K.
Since d_2 is bounded uniformly in m, its ratio to K tends to one.

A concrete scalable piecewise-linear subclass in (6) can be fixed before
any query as follows. Put T=4^m. On each ray independently partition[1,T]
by arbitrary knots whose successive ratios are at most4, and interpolate
the values sqrt(t) linearly. Beyond T keep the value sqrt(T) constant;
inside[0,1] use t. The two partitions may differ and may have any number
of additional horizon-dependent knots. For example, one partition has
knots4^k, and the other has1,2,8,...,2*4^(m-1),4^m. Any segment with
endpoint ratio q<=4 has maximal elasticity sqrt(q)/(1+sqrt(q))<=2/3.
On[1,T] its chord is between(2sqrt(2)/3)sqrt(t) and sqrt(t): the minimum
chord-to-square-root ratio is2q^(1/4)/(1+sqrt(q)), minimized at q=4.
Thus the two complete profiles are comparable with
kappa_ray=3/(2sqrt(2)), including their common outer plateau. Their
product kappa_ray C_grow=3/2^(5/6)<7/4, verified by raising to the
sixth power:729*128<117649. Taking, for instance, mu=1/(2d_2) and R=1
gives explicit fixed functions with checked spatial order, slopes and
trapezoidal areas. The theorem covers every initial point for these
functions, rather than choosing derivative pieces afresh at queries.

For BOTH classes the exact benchmark from b98bb807d514e80d satisfies

    limsup B_(2^m-1) sup 2f(x_n)/x_0^2<=2/e<1.       (8)

Thus these specified whole scalar mechanisms cannot reach the required
benchmark on the near-critical diagnostic. This is not an all-scalar bound.

## 2. Legality, areas, and uniform schedule estimates

Integrating (2) gives 1<=G_sigma(t)<=t^p_grow<=t for t>=1. Also
0<=G_sigma'(t)<=p_grow t^(p_grow-1)<=1. The unit core and continuity at1
therefore make each profile nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz. Across the origin,
G_+(t)+G_-(u)<=t+u proves the same bound. Hence (3) is nondecreasing,
mu-Lipschitz, and continuous. Its integral is convex, differentiable and
1-smooth, with unique minimizer0. Its complete values, including all outer
areas, are

    f(sigma R t)=mu R^2 F_sigma(t),
    F_sigma(t)=t^2/2                           for t<=1,
    F_sigma(t)=1/2+integral_1^t G_sigma(v)dv     for t>=1. (9)

Consequently0 is the actual closest minimizer, and the normalization in (5)
and (7) is precisely the original squared distance x_0^2.

The following rational bounds hold for every m>=128:

    12/5<c<49/20, c<56/23,
    2/5<a<1/lambda<5/12,
    127/128<=ac<1, 0<a<r_s<1/2, 0<A_mass<1.       (10)

For c<56/23, use sqrt(2)<99/70, so
c<(169/70)(129/128)=21801/8960<56/23. The other c bound follows too.
Since a=(m-1)/[(m+1)lambda], a<1/lambda=lambda-2<r_s. Its lower bound
follows from a>=(127/128)/(49/20)=635/1568>2/5. Equation (1) implies

    S_j+1<=c^j,
    d_(j+1)/d_j=c-(c-1)/d_j<c.                    (11)

We will also need

    S_j>= (7/4)d_j for every j>=3.                (12)

Indeed S_j-(7/4)d_j equals
a(1/r_s-7/4)c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j-11/4, which increases with j.
For j=3, S_3=7+a(4+2c+c^2)>1603/125, whereas
d_3=1+(ac)c^2<2801/400. The inequality
1603/125>(7/4)(2801/400) proves (12).

## 3. A complete crossing-clock inequality

Abbreviate p=p_grow, beta=1-p and C=C_grow. On either ray define

    Clock_sigma(t)=integral_1^t dv/G_sigma(v), t>0.

It is log t in the core. Outside the core put q_t=t/G_sigma(t).
The derivative condition gives q_t'>=beta/G_sigma(t), and hence

    Clock_sigma(t)<=(q_t-1)/beta, t>=1.            (13)

For every h>1 and every strict overshoot z=hG_sigma(t)-t>0,

    Clock_sigma(z)<= C h-1/beta.                  (14)

Here h is a normalized stepsize mu d_j, not the physical stepsize d_j.
We prove all cases, including short crossing steps and core endpoints.

If z<=1, the bound G_sigma(t)<=t^p holds for every t>=0, also inside the
core. Maximizing h t^p-t by differentiation gives

    z<=(beta C h)^(1/beta).

Thus log z<=log(beta C h)/beta<=C h-1/beta.

If z>=1 and t<=1, then h>=2, and monotonicity gives
Clock_sigma(z)<=z-1<=h-2. This is <=C h-1/beta because
C>=1/(2beta). To prove the latter, the function
p log p+beta log beta is increasing for p>=1/2 and equals-log2 at1/2;
therefore beta C=p^p beta^beta>=1/2.

If z,t>=1 and z>=t, monotonicity and (13) yield

    Clock_sigma(z)<=(q_t-1)/beta+(z-t)/G_sigma(t)
                   =h+(1/beta-2)q_t-1/beta
                   <=h/(2beta)-1/beta<=C h-1/beta,

where q_t<=h/2 and p>=1/2 were used.

Finally, if1<=z<=t, integrating (2) between z and t gives
G_sigma(z)>=G_sigma(t)(z/t)^p. Therefore

    z/G_sigma(z)<=q_t^p(h-q_t)^beta
                  <=p^p beta^beta h=beta C h.

The maximum in the last inequality occurs at q_t=p h; this follows by
differentiating p log q+beta log(h-q). Equation (13) proves (14).

Write D=C h-1/beta. If a crossing lands on the other ray, its new clock
is at most kappa_ray D when D>=0: use the pointwise profile comparison
and integrate if z>=1; for z<1 the new clock is negative. If D<0,
(14) forces z<1, and BOTH ray clocks equal log z, so the new clock is
at most D, with no comparison-factor loss. A noncrossing nonzero step
reduces its own clock by at least h, since

    integral_(t-hG_sigma(t))^t dv/G_sigma(v)>=h.

We also have Clock_sigma(t)<=t-1 for all t>0, using G_sigma>=1 outside
the core and log t<=t-1 inside it.

## 4. Reciprocal cores: every crossing is annihilated

Assume (4), and put sigma_clock=kappa_ray C and
tau_clock=kappa_ray/beta. The function C=(p/(1-p))^p increases for
p>=1/2, so C<=3^(3/4)<23/10. In particular the class is nonempty
throughout the asserted p range. Also (10) gives

    sigma_clock<=23/10<1/r_s.

Since p/beta>=1 and p<=1, C<=(p/beta), so

    tau_clock-sigma_clock=kappa_ray(1/beta-C)>=1.  (15)

If a trajectory ever reaches zero, it stays there. Otherwise choose its
last strict crossing. A crossing requires h=mu d_j>1 because G_sigma(t)<=t.
Thus its level j is greater than r. Every occurrence of d_j in the ruler
is immediately followed by a complete H_j. This copy of H_j contains a
last occurrence of d_r, followed by H_r. The physical mass before that
last d_r, measured from the start of this copy of H_j, is

    S_j-S_r-d_r.                                 (16)

Suppose the overshoot radius z is greater than1. Section3 bounds its
target clock by sigma_clock d_j/d_r-tau_clock. Define
D_j=S_j-sigma_clock d_j. By (1),

    D_j=a(1/r_s-sigma_clock)c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j-1-sigma_clock

is increasing. Consequently

    S_j-S_r-d_r-(sigma_clock d_j-tau_clock d_r)
      =D_j-D_r+(tau_clock-sigma_clock-1)d_r>=0.    (17)

There is no subsequent crossing by our choice of the last one. Each
subsequent nonzero step decreases the target clock by its normalized
stepsize. Equations (16)-(17) force the path into the core by the last
d_r in that copy of H_j. If z<=1 it is already in the core; a
noncrossing core step keeps it there. The last d_r then maps x to
x-d_r mu x=0. This proves the annihilation assertion without assuming
that an arbitrary earlier core entry is permanent.

For completeness, a run with no crossing, on either ray, has final
radius v and gradient magnitude u. Monotonicity gives
|x_0|>=v+S_m u. Since the actual derivative is mu-Lipschitz,

    f(x_n)<=u v-u^2/(2mu).

This follows by integrating the bound |g(t)|<=min(mu|t|,u) from0 to
the final point. Therefore

    2f(x_n)<=2|x_0|u-(2S_m+1/mu)u^2
             <=x_0^2/(2S_m+1/mu).                 (18)

For G_+=G_-=min(t,1), start at x_0=R(1+2mu S_m). Every gradient on
the trajectory equals mu R, all iterates remain beyond the core, and
x_n=R(1+mu S_m). Substitution into (9) gives equality in (18).
Together with annihilation this proves (5), including r>=m.

## 5. Nonresonant cores: a uniform actual-map attraction bound

Assume (6), and abbreviate

    b_j=mu d_j, U_j=mu S_j, eta=7/4,
    rho_core=1/8, k_env=1/8, A_env=c/8.

Let I be the first level with t=b_I>1 and put J=I+1. Because mu<=1/d_2,
I>=3. Also1<t<c by (11). If the horizon m<=I, all its normalized
steps are<=1, so no crossing occurs and (18) already proves (7).

First, ANY crossing run on ANY whole H_j ends at radius less than
rho_core in normalized coordinates x/R. Select its last strict crossing,
at some level l>=I>=3, with h=b_l>1. The following full H_l has
normalized mass U_l>=eta h, by (12). Use Section3 with D=C h-1/beta.

If D>=0, the terminal clock is bounded by
(kappa_ray C-eta)h-kappa_ray/beta. This increases with kappa_ray
at fixed h, so under kappa_ray C<=eta it is at most

    -eta/(beta C)<-105/32.

To justify the strict constant, beta C=p^p beta^beta increases on
[1/2,2/3] and is at most4^(1/3)/3<8/15. If D<0, the terminal clock
is at most(C-eta)h-1/beta<=C-eta-1/beta<=-eta-1=-11/4,
using C<=p/beta and C<=eta. Since exp(11/4)>8, both cases give

    |Phi_j(x/R)|<rho_core for every crossing run.  (19)

Here Phi_j is the actual map of the SAME fixed function under H_j.
A noncrossing, nonzero run starting at radius v instead satisfies

    Clock(radius_end)<=v-1-U_j.                  (20)

We now prove the actual-map invariant, for j>=J and0<=q<=rho_core,

    |x/R|<=q b_j implies
    |Phi_j(x/R)|<=min(A_env q,k_env rho_core).     (21)

This controls both possible signs without assuming an odd map or
asserting that a reachable image is a centered interval.

Base j=J. All steps of H_I are at most1, so a core-started run stays
in the quadratic core. Its multiplier P is nonnegative and
P<=exp(-U_I)<=exp(-eta t). The middle step t has radius factor t-1,
and (t-1)P<(c-1)exp(-eta)<1. Thus a core-started whole H_J stays
in the core and has absolute multiplier Q=(t-1)P^2. Furthermore

    b_J Q<=c t(t-1)exp(-2eta t)
           <=3c/(16eta^3)<=3/35<1/8.             (22)

For the middle inequality use exp(2eta t)>(2eta t)^3/6 and
(t-1)/t^2<=1/4. Also rho_core b_J<c^2/8<1. Thus every input in
(21) is a core input, and its endpoint is at most k_env q, which
implies both bounds in (21).

Induction j>J. Write the actual word as H_(j-1),d_(j-1),H_(j-1),
and let v_1 be the radius after its first block.

If c q<=rho_core, the induction hypothesis applies to the first
block because b_j<=c b_(j-1). It gives
v_1<=min(A_env c q,k_env rho_core)<=q, since A_env c=c^2/8<1.
Thus v_1<=rho_core. The middle step uses the quadratic core and
has output radius |1-b_(j-1)|v_1<=b_(j-1)v_1. The second block,
using parameter v_1 in the induction hypothesis, gives
radius_end<=min(A_env q,k_env rho_core).

If c q>rho_core, then v_1<=rho_core as well. A crossing first block
uses (19). A noncrossing first block uses (20) and (12):

    Clock(v_1)<=rho_core b_j-1-U_(j-1)
               <=-(eta/c-rho_core)b_j-1<-3.       (23)

For the last inequality, eta/c>5/7. Also j>=I+2 and d_I>=d_3>6,
so

    b_j>=b_(I+2)>d_(I+2)/d_I
        =c^2-(c^2-1)/d_I
        >(5c^2+1)/6>5,                            (24)

where c^2>lambda^2>29/5. Therefore the right side of (23) is less
than-1-5(5/7-1/8)=-221/56<-3. Since exp3>8, (23) implies the
desired v_1<rho_core. A zero iterate is harmless. The middle step
now has radius at most b_(j-1)rho_core, so the second induction
application gives radius_end<=k_env rho_core. Because q>rho_core/c
and A_env=c k_env, this also is at most A_env q. The induction is
complete. Notice that it explicitly handles partial-block entries and
subsequent exits; first entry is never presumed permanent capture.

## 6. Nonresonant full objective, with original distance retained

No-crossing runs obey (18), and hence have normalized gap<=K.
For a crossing run with m>=J, (19) places the endpoint in the core.
If its initial normalized radius v_0 is at most rho_core b_m,
(21) gives radius_end<=A_env v_0/b_m. If v_0>rho_core b_m,
(19) gives radius_end<rho_core. In either case, using the complete
core area in (9),

    2f(x_n)/x_0^2<=mu/b_m^2.                     (25)

For m>=I+2, (24), a>2/5 and (11) yield

    b_m d_m>5a c^m>2c^m>2S_m+1.

Since mu/b_m^2=1/(b_m d_m), (25) is strictly below K.

It remains to check the base horizon m=J=I+1, where (25) alone
would discard useful information. If v_0<=1, the entire run stays
in the quadratic core by the base argument, so its normalized gap
is mu Q^2<mu/64. If v_0>1 and the run crosses, (19) gives the same
strict bound mu/64. Finally

    mu(2S_m+1)<2mu c^m<2b_m/a<2c^2/a<125/4<64.

Here b_m=b_J<c^2, c<5/2 and a>2/5 were used. Thus mu/64<K.
This proves (7) for all cases. The lower end of the asserted squeeze
is the Huber construction in Section4 with mu=1/d_2. It belongs to
(6), and has normalized payoff1/(2S_m+d_2).

## 7. Exact benchmark comparison

We use ONLY the exact recursions in accepted fact b98bb807d514e80d.
Write C_n=S_circle(n)+1. Their mass joins are

    Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,
    Gamma(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2,
    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(k+l=n-1) Omega(C_k,C_l),
    B_n=max_(k+l=n-1) Gamma(C_k,B_l).

Put rho=log_2(lambda). We give the needed sharper estimates directly:

    C_n<=(n+1)^rho, B_n<=1+4n^rho.                (26)

Let E(t)=(1+t)^rho-1. With t=exp z, differentiation gives

    d^2/dz^2 log E(exp z)
      =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)[(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/E(t)^2>0.

The strict inequality follows by differentiating (1+t)^rho-1-rho t.
Convexity at z,-z yields E(t)E(1/t)>=E(1)^2=2. For A=t^rho B
and D=(1+t)^rho B this means (D-A)(D-B)>=2AB, so

    Omega(A,B)<=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho.

Induction proves the first assertion of (26). The inequality
Gamma(A,D)<=4A+D follows by squaring sqrt(D^2+8AD)<=D+4A.
Induction using (k+1)^rho+l^rho<=(k+l+1)^rho proves the second.

Finally A_mass tends to1, (1+1/m)^m tends to e, and (2/c)^m tends to0.
Equation (1) gives (S_m+1)/lambda^m ->e. Hence the ACTUAL finite
benchmark, without any fitted dyadic constant or phase assumption, obeys

    K B_(2^m-1)
      <=[1+4(2^m-1)^rho]/(2S_m+1) ->2/e.          (27)

Both (5) and (7) imply (8).

## 8. Scope and the next real gap

No external theorem was used as a black box. Exact scalar-order/area
constructions and the earlier fixed13/5 clock arguments informed this
choice of family, but every estimate on the actual near-critical word
has been derived here, with uniform constants.

The restrictions are substantive: a common quadratic neighborhood;
outer logarithmic slope at most3/4 in the reciprocal case, or2/3 in
the small-curvature nonresonant case; a specified ray-comparison bound;
and, for the latter case, mu<=1/d_2. General nonresonant curvatures
above1/d_2, independent core curvatures, outer ramps with logarithmic
slope near or above1, or profiles without a common quadratic core are
not covered. No upper bound on all scalar functions, no unrestricted
W_n upper bound, and no completion of the project target is asserted.

There is an exact countertest against silently removing resonance from
the annihilation conclusion. Take mu=1, G_+=G_-=min(t,1), R=1, and
epsilon=[2 product_(h in H_m)(1+h)]^(-1)>0 as the initial point.
Every prefix radius is below1/2, by induction using the bound1+h for
each update, so the whole trajectory uses g(x)=x. All h=d_j exceed1;
therefore every update strictly crosses zero and none reaches it.
Its final normalized objective is the strictly positive quantity

    product_(h in H_m)(h-1)^2
      =(ac)^(2(2^m-1)) c^(-2m).

For the last identity, the multiplicity of d_j is2^(m-j-1), the total
is n=2^m-1, and the multiplicity-weighted sum of j is n-m (induction
in m verifies this identity). This refutes the extended annihilation
claim, not an objective bound at K. Also S_1/d_1<3/4 and
S_2/d_2<3/2 on the actual parameter range, so the uniform7/4 waiting
budget used in Section5 cannot be imported to the first three levels.
The latter strict inequality follows from
S_2-(3/2)d_2=3/2+a(2+c-(3/2)c^2)<0 using a>2/5,c>12/5.

Status: UNVERIFIED joint candidate. No fact_submit allocation, numerical
solver or sweep. All needed arguments are written below; earlier candidates
are not correctness premises. The original exact-profile target remains open.

For the near-critical word and every legal member of the entire real
two-predecessor family below, including EVERY independent split fraction,
the normalized objective of ANY full terminal completion obeys

    score_free/K <21(3/4)^(N/2),                         (T1)

provided m>=512 and N=2^(m-r)>=32. In particular it is below7/27.

to zero if N tends to infinity. The actual GD, all old/future normals,
true initial distance and primitive defect are included.

## 1. The word, real flow and complete legality test

Let lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j), n=2^m-1.
Fix 0<=r<=m-5, let k=m-r, N=2^k, M=1+sum H_r, and q=a c^r/M.
Write

    A=1+q,
    q_i=q c^(nu_2(i+1)), tau_i=1+q_i, T_i=M tau_i, i<N-1,
    tau_(N-1)=t>=1, T_(N-1)=Mt.

Here nu_2 is the binary valuation of a positive integer. These N phases
are the actual copies of H_r in H_m, and every intervening physical
checkpoint is 1+Mq_i. Each phase's ordinary mass is M-1.

Choose ALL theta_j in[0,1] independently for 2<=j<N, positive R_i,
E_i=R_i^2, and actual nonnegative transfers

    a_01=R_1, a_02=theta_2 R_2,
    a_(i,i+1)=(1-theta_(i+1))R_(i+1), i>=1,
    a_(i,i+2)=theta_(i+2)R_(i+2), i>=1,

omitting out-of-range indices. Every coordinate j>=2 receives total
mass R_j from its two preceding coordinates. In the real Euclidean
space R^N with standard orthonormal vectors e_i, set

    p_i=(R_i e_i-sum_(j>i)a_ij e_j)/T_i,
    C=conv(0,p_0,...,p_(N-1)),
    F_C(x)=max_(p in C)(<x,p>-||p||^2/2).

The maximizing point is the Euclidean projection P_C(x). The projection
variational inequality gives its uniqueness and
||P_C(x)-P_C(y)||<=||x-y||. Maximizing-difference inequalities then give
differentiability with grad F_C=P_C; thus F_C is convex and1-smooth.

Start at R_0 e_0. Before every phase i>=1 the exact state is

    X_i=R_i e_i+theta_(i+1)R_(i+1)e_(i+1),

with the last term omitted at i=N-1. Subtract each original physical
step times p_i throughout the ordinary block and its checkpoint.
The total subtraction before phase i+1 is T_i p_i, which exhausts
coordinate i and creates exactly X_(i+1). No physical step is compressed
or reordered in asserting this trajectory.

For completeness, here are ALL normal tests. During phase i>=1 put
z=(ordinary partial mass+1)/M in[1/M,1],
d=theta_(i+1), e=theta_(i+2). Multiplying by M, the current normal value is

 [(tau_i-z)E_i
  -(1-d)(d tau_i+z(1-d))E_(i+1)
  -z e^2 E_(i+2)]/tau_i^2.                               (1)

The only possibly nonzero future values are

 [(d+z(1-d)/tau_i)E_(i+1)
               -z e(1-e)E_(i+2)/tau_i]/tau_(i+1),        (2)
 z e E_(i+2)/(tau_i tau_(i+2)).                           (3)

Every past normal is nonpositive: its positive coordinate has been
exhausted, while the remaining proximal coordinates are nonnegative.
Every other future value is zero. Therefore (1)>=(2),(3),0 at BOTH
z=1/M and z=1 is necessary and sufficient for every actual query in
this phase, since all differences are affine in z. At the root use
its displayed p_0 and test the same two endpoints against p_1,p_2,0;
other future normals vanish and there are no past normals. At the last
phase t>=1 gives its own nonnegative value and all past values are
nonpositive. Out-of-range terms are always omitted.

For any fixed split policy and finite word the family is nonempty:
fix terminal energy1, then choose E_i backward sufficiently large.
Its own coefficient tau_i-z>=q_i>0, and all comparison terms involve
already fixed future energies. Finally choose E_0. The theorem covers
every legal energy choice, not merely this conservative construction.

At every original query,
F_C(x)=<x,p_i>-||p_i||^2/2. Its minimizer set is C^polar. The inequalities
<p_i,z><=0 imply, by backward induction, that every coordinate of z is
nonpositive. Hence the actual closest minimizer to R_0e_0 is0, with
squared initial distance E_0. If htot is the total physical mass of H_m,
the original terminal objective and primitive defect are exactly

 score_C=(2Mt-2M+1)E_(N-1)/(M^2 t^2 E_0),
 V/E_0=1-[(Mt-(M-1)+htot)/(Mt)]^2 E_(N-1)/E_0.            (4)

The second identity follows by summing
2h_i F_i+h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2=||x_i||^2-||x_(i+1)||^2
and then subtracting the defining terminal term of V.

## 2. Uniform parameter bounds

Put M_j=1+sum H_j. The recursion M_(j+1)=2M_j+a c^j gives

 M_j=b c^j+(1-b)2^j,  b=a/(c-2),  0<b<1.

Since a<c-2, a<=a c^j/M_j<c-2, and M_m<=M c^k.
For m>=512 we may use the coarser rational bounds

    2/5<q<7/16,  12/5<c<39/16,  A<23/16,
    Q:=q c^ell>=cq>=1-1/m>=99/100, ell>=1.              (5)

For instance lambda<169/70 and
a>=127/(129lambda)>2540/6321>2/5 establish the lower q bound;
the upper c bound already holds for m>=128.
In addition

 qc<=c(c-2)
    =1+(4+2sqrt(2))/m+(3+2sqrt(2))/m^2
    <1+8/m<=65/64.                                      (6)

## 3. A boundary energy retaining the shared coordinate

Index the ODD phases by j=0,...,J, where J=N/2-1.
At phase i=2j+1 write

 O_j=E_(2j+1), B_j=tau_(2j+1),
 u_j=theta_(2j+2), L_j=E_(2j+2)    (j<J).

Thus B_j=1+Q_j with Q_j=q c^(nu_2(2j+2)) for j<J,
whereas B_J=t is the unqueried-terminal parameter.
Define

 D_j=(A^2/B_j)O_j
            +u_j[u_j-(1-u_j)A/B_j]L_j,  j<J,
 D_J=(A^2/t)O_J.                                        (7)

The second coefficient in D_j CAN BE NEGATIVE. It must not be discarded.
We prove D_j>0 and its quantitative comparison directly from the legal
high phase.

For j<J abbreviate B=B_j, Q=Q_j, u=u_j, O=O_j, L=L_j, and let

    H=(1+uQ)(1-u+B/A).                                   (8)

The high phase's zero comparison at z=1 gives

    Q O >= (1-u)(1+uQ)L+w^2 O_(j+1)
          >= (1-u)(1+uQ)L,                              (9)

where w=theta_(2j+3). We claim

    H D_j >= A O >0.                                     (10)

If the coefficient K_u=u[u-(1-u)A/B] in(7) is nonnegative,
D_j>=A^2 O/B and H>=B/A prove(10).
If K_u<0, put d=1-u>0 and use(9) to upper-bound L. Multiplication
by the negative K_u reverses this bound, giving

 D_j/O >= Z/[B d(1+uQ)],
 Z=A^2 d+Q u(Aq d+B u).

The exact identity

 Z(d+B/A)-ABd
     =A^2 d^2+Q u(Aq d+B u)(d+B/A) >=0

proves(10) after multiplying by H=(1+uQ)(d+B/A).
This includes u=0 or1 via the first case. Thus D_j is a positive energy
even when its displayed residual coefficient is negative.

## 4. Every high/low passage contracts the boundary energy

Fix j<J and abbreviate Bnext=B_(j+1), O'=O_(j+1).
Let zeta=u_(j+1) and L'=L_(j+1) when j+1<J; omit their term at j+1=J.
The high phase's first future comparison is

 Q O >= H L
       +w[w-(1-w)B/A]O'.                                (11)

The following low phase's first future comparison is

 q L >= (1+qw)(1-w+A/Bnext)O'
       +zeta[zeta-(1-zeta)A/Bnext]L'.                    (12)

Both are exact instances of(1)>=(2), with every inherited mass present.
Multiply(11) by q and substitute(12), since H>0.
The coefficient of O' becomes

 C(w)=H(1+qw)(1-w+A/Bnext)
                       +q w[w-(1-w)B/A].               (13)

We show C(w)>=H A^2/Bnext+q for EVERY independent w in[0,1].
First,

 H-(1+B/A)=u[Q(1-u+B/A)-1]>=0,

because Q B/A>1 follows from(5). Consequently C has nonpositive
quadratic coefficient q[(1+B/A)-H], so it is concave in w.
Its smaller endpoint is w=1:

 C(0)-C(1)=H(1-Aq/Bnext)-q>0.

Indeed Bnext>=1, Aq<161/256, H>=1+B/A>2, and
2(1-161/256)-7/16=78/256>0. This proves the assertion.
Equations(7),(11)-(13) therefore imply

    qQ O >= H D_(j+1)+q O_(j+1).                         (14)

Combining(14) with(10) and dropping only the positive q O_(j+1) gives

    D_(j+1) <=(q Q_j/A) D_j.                             (15)

There is NO relation required between w and any earlier odd split.
Every even split is also independent. The positive energy(7), rather
than pointwise elimination of L', is what makes all those changes harmless.

At the root, its first-future endpoint normal gives

 q E_0 >=(1+A/B_0)O_0+u_0[u_0-(1-u_0)A/B_0]L_0
         >=D_0,                                         (16)

because B_0>Aq. Iterating(15) is legitimate by(10), and at the last
boundary D_J=A^2 E_(N-1)/t. The number of factors Q_j is N/2-1;
their high levels sum to N-k-1, as follows from the exact ruler counts
2^(k-ell-1) of each level ell=1,...,k-1. Hence

 D_J/E_0 <= q^(N-1)c^(N-k-1)/A^(N/2-1),

    E_(N-1)/(tE_0)
        <=(qc)^(N-1)c^(-k)/A^(N/2+1).                   (17)

## 5. Free terminal completion and the true initial distance

Retain EVERY original queried jet and the optimum(0,0,0), and consider
ANY convex1-smooth terminal completion f. This includes the maximal
completion from accepted1252b8823bb5a290.

If r>=1, every p_i is actually queried. Interpolation of that jet to
any new minimizer z yields <p_i,z><=0, because its retained value is
<x_i,p_i>-||p_i||^2/2. The triangular inequalities imply that all
coordinates of z are nonpositive. Since0 remains a minimizer, its
distance R_0 remains the TRUE closest-minimizer distance. Additional
orthogonal dimensions cannot decrease it.

The last physical step is h_last=1+a. Smoothness at its retained query
bounds the terminal objective by

 2f(x_n)/E_0
 <=[2Mt-(2M-1)+h_last^2]E_(N-1)/(M^2 t^2 E_0)
 <2E_(N-1)/(MtE_0),

since M>=2+a gives 2M-1-h_last^2>=2-a^2>0.
Set K=1/(2M_m-1); use M_m<=Mc^k and(17) to obtain

    score_free/K <4(qc)^(N-1)/A^(N/2+1).                 (18)

If r=0, the old terminal normal is UNQUERIED and cannot constrain a
new minimizer. The retained initial gradient instead gives, by
1-Lipschitz continuity from any minimizer,

    dist(x_0,argmin f)^2>=||p_0||^2>=E_0/A^2.             (19)

Write Llast=E_(N-2) and v=theta_(N-1). At the last query the actual
position is R_(N-2)e_(N-2)+v R_(N-1)e_(N-1) and its gradient is

    [R_(N-2)e_(N-2)-(1-v)R_(N-1)e_(N-1)]/A.

One smoothness step of length A gives

 2f(x_n)<=(1-A^(-2))Llast
    +[-2v(1-v)/A+(1-2/A-1/A^2)(1-v)^2]E_(N-1)
 <=(1-A^(-2))Llast,                                     (20)

because the bracket is nonpositive for A<23/16.
We now bound Llast through the PRECEDING, queried high boundary D_(J-1).
Its parameters have Q=cq<=65/64 and B=1+Q. From(9) and(7), multiplying
(9) by the positive A^2/(BQ), we get

 D_(J-1)/Llast
 >= A^2(1-u)/(BQ)+u[Aq(1-u)+Bu]/B
 >= [A^2/(BQ)](1-u)+u^2
 >=(3/4)(1-u)+u^2>=39/64>1/2.                            (21)

Here A^2/(BQ)>(49/25)/(8385/4096)>3/4 by(5)-(6).
Using(15)-(16) but omitting the final high passage gives

 Llast/E_0
 <=2q^(N-3)c^(N-k-2)/A^(N/2-2).                         (22)

Combining the ACTUAL distance bound(19), the objective bound(20),
(22) and M_m<=c^k now yields

    score_free/K
      <4(2+q)A^2(qc)^(N-2)/A^(N/2).                    (23)

This second argument neither assumes the old terminal gradient is
queried nor uses it to restrict the new closest minimizer.

## 6. Uniform quantitative bound and the actual exact benchmark

Let z0=65/64>1. To cover qc<1 as well, use
(qc)^(N-1)<=z0^N and (qc)^(N-2)<=z0^N.
The exact rational inequality

    z0^2/A <(65/64)^2/(7/5)=21125/28672<3/4

and the prefactor bounds 4/A<20/7<21 and
4(2+q)A^2<4(39/16)(23/16)^2=82524/4096<21 show from
(18),(23) that

    score_free/K <21(3/4)^(N/2).

For N>=32, (3/4)^4=81/256<1/3, hence this is strictly below
21/81=7/27. For growing N the ratio tends to zero uniformly over every
split fraction, energy, r, t and full terminal completion in the family.

To compare with the ORIGINAL benchmark, use accepted b98bb807d514e80d:
its shifted joins are
Omega(X,Y)=(X+Y+sqrt((X+Y)^2+4XY))/2 and
Gamma(X,D)=2X+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8XD)/2.
Write rho_s=log_2(lambda). For F(z)=(1+z)^rho_s-1, the second derivative
of log F(exp w) is

 rho_s*z*(1+z)^(rho_s-2)*
 [(1+z)^rho_s-1-rho_s*z]/F(z)^2>0.

Convexity at w and-w gives F(z)F(1/z)>=F(1)^2=2. Taking
z=Y^(1/rho_s)/X^(1/rho_s) and comparing the positive root of
t^2-(X+Y)t-XY proves
Omega(X,Y)<=(X^(1/rho_s)+Y^(1/rho_s))^rho_s.
The zero cases follow by continuity. Induction in the accepted recursions
therefore gives 1+S_circle(n)<=(n+1)^rho_s.
Since Gamma(X,D)<=4X+D, another induction gives

    B_n<=1+4n^rho_s.

The exact mass formula in Section2 gives M_m/lambda^m->exp(1), so

    limsup K B_(2^m-1)<=2/exp(1).

Consequently every sequence in the stated range has

    limsup B_(2^m-1)*score_free<=14/[27 exp(1)]<1,

with limit superior zero when N tends to infinity.

## 7. Scope and the surviving gap

This is the complete nonnegative two-predecessor incidence class:
every coordinate can merge arbitrary fractions from its two immediate
predecessors, every split can depend on the entire word and horizon,
and every compatible positive energy is allowed. No stationarity, parity
constancy, small variation, or independent-child assumption remains.
The proof includes every actual phase and full terminal completion.

It still assumes a positive triangular coordinate transfer with memory
two. It does not cover transfers from three or more preceding phases,
signed transfers, or reactivating an exhausted coordinate. Cases N<32
are outside the stated uniform bound (separate small-window candidates
exist, but are not invoked here). Most importantly it is NOT an upper
bound on unrestricted W_n(H_m), and it does not settle the original
all-horizon/all-schedule exact-profile problem.

glossary.theta_j: Independent fraction of coordinate-j mass transferred by phase j-2 in the displayed real two-predecessor DAG.
glossary.E_i: Squared coordinate mass R_i^2 at phase i.
glossary.O_j: E_(2j+1), the squared mass of an odd phase.
glossary.B_j: 1+q c^(nu_2(2j+2)) for an odd checkpoint phase, and t for the final odd phase; this is distinct from the exact benchmark B_n.
glossary.u_j: theta_(2j+2), the even-coordinate split immediately after odd phase j.
glossary.L_j: E_(2j+2), the squared mass of the low phase immediately after odd phase j.
glossary.D_j: A^2 O_j/B_j+u_j[u_j-(1-u_j)A/B_j]L_j, the positive boundary energy retaining the possibly negative future-coordinate coefficient; terminal value A^2 O_J/t.
glossary.H: (1+uQ)(1-u+B/A), the coefficient in the queried high phase's first future-normal comparison.
glossary.K: 1/(2M_m-1), the canonical Huber score of the actual word.
glossary.score_free: 2f(x_n)/dist(x_0,argmin f)^2 for any convex 1-smooth completion retaining every original query and the optimum.

author: max
claim: Mixed-sign fresh Markov interface: complete all-old-query legality is explicit, and EVERY positive adjacent coefficient t_l>0 must pay eta_(l+1)-eta_l >=||z_(l+1)||²/t_l>=0. Starting from the separating eta_u=0 jet, total positive-innovation charge is bounded by affine-intercept decreases at negative transitions. Thus homogeneous intercepts cannot support fresh positive innovations, while Huber t=1,z=0 retains zero charge. An exact actual-ruler negative-then-positive prefix with both innovations nonzero and ALL query/value comparisons satisfied shows the paid mechanism is nonempty. No full-tail payoff or whole mixed-sign W bound is claimed.
evidence:
# Positive fresh transitions require an actual intercept budget

Status: candidate, not verifier-accepted. No numerical or fact_submit budget
is allocated. This is an exact interface and a scoped homogeneous-family
obstruction, NOT a claimed full mixed-sign payoff bound. The construction
and inequality retain every actual query and its value. Accepted input:
the smooth-convex interpolation and construction in1252b8823bb5a290.

## 1. Intrinsic data and a real Gram construction

Fix the actual near-critical ruler from TASK, with m>=128,
c=(1+sqrt2)(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c, r_l=a c^l, d_l=1+r_l,
H_0=(), H_(l+1)=(H_l,d_l,H_l), M_l=1+sum H_l.
Select consecutive first-occurrence levels u,...,v. The ordinary block
before the first selected checkpoint has capacity C_u=M_u, and
C_l=M_(l-1) for u<l<=v. Capacity is one plus the actual block sum.
The total displacement coefficient in ordinary block l plus its
checkpoint is D_l=C_l+r_l.

Start at x_0=e_u with norm1, optimum0, and parallel g_u=e_u/tau_u.
Choose tau_l>=C_l, and put

    w_l=tau_l-C_l, B_l=tau_l-D_l=w_l-r_l.

For each nonzero transition choose t_l of the same sign as B_l, and
define theta_l=B_l/tau_(l+1). Require

    t_l(theta_l-t_l)>=0.

Let alpha_u=1/tau_u. With fresh orthonormal directions e_(l+1), set

    g_(l+1)=t_l g_l+z_(l+1),
    z_(l+1)=alpha_l sqrt(t_l(theta_l-t_l)) e_(l+1),
    alpha_(l+1)^2=t_l theta_l alpha_l^2.            (1)

Each fresh vector is orthogonal to the entire earlier span. Thus (1)
is an actual finite-dimensional Euclidean construction, not a formal
covariance prescription. Positive t_l are additionally restricted to
t_l<=1; every legal instance must obey this by the argument below.
Negative transitions automatically have |t_l|<=c-2<1: because
B_l<0, |theta_l|=(r_l-w_l)/tau_(l+1)<=r_l/M_l<=c-2.
The last inequality follows from
M_l=[a/(c-2)]c^l+[1-a/(c-2)]2^l and0<a<c-2.

Write X_l for the actual block start, X_u=e_u, and define

    Y_l=X_l-tau_l g_l,
    X_(l+1)=Y_l+B_l g_l,
    Y_(l+1)=Y_l+B_l g_l-tau_(l+1)g_(l+1).          (2)

These are exactly GD displacements because tau_l-B_l=D_l.
Choose an affine intercept eta_l in

    -w_l alpha_l^2<=eta_l<=0, eta_u=0.             (3)

At EVERY actual ordinary-block query, including its checkpoint query,
with executed ordinary mass s, prescribe

    x=Y_l+(tau_l-s)g_l,
    gradient=g_l,
    f(x)=eta_l+(tau_l-s-1/2)alpha_l^2,
    0<=s<=C_l-1.                                  (4)

This determines all actual values, not merely endpoint heights. The
proximal point is y=x-g_l=Y_l+d g_l, with d=tau_l-s-1 in
[w_l,tau_l-1]; the proximal value is delta=f(x)-alpha_l^2/2
=eta_l+d alpha_l^2. Include the optimum sample at0 with value0.

Conversely, ANY legal first-order fresh Markov relay with a radial first
gradient and the stated separating first jet eta_u=0 has this intrinsic
representation: set
tau_l=<g_l,X_l>/||g_l||^2. The two optimum interpolation inequalities
give tau_l>=C_l and exactly the interval(3). Actual constant gradients
force the affine values(4). Since a fresh z is orthogonal to X_(l+1),
the identity

    tau_(l+1) alpha_(l+1)^2=t_l B_l alpha_l^2      (5)

forces (1), including its innovation norm. A zero next gradient gives
a minimizer and a stationary remaining trajectory, which may be treated
separately. Thus the nonzero formulas lose no norm freedom in this class.

## 2. Complete all-pair legality, including old-query costs

The interpolation inequality from1252b8823bb5a290 in proximal variables is

    delta_j>=delta_i+<g_i,y_j-y_i>.                (6)

The increments in (2) are orthogonal to the next gradient by (5), and
therefore to every later gradient by freshness and the first-order
recurrence. Since Y_u=0, this gives <g_j,Y_i>=0 for j>=i.
For i<j put

    T_ij=product_(l=i)^(j-1) t_l,
    R_ij=alpha_j^2/alpha_i^2,
    L_ij=sum_(l=i)^(j-1)(B_l-tau_(l+1)t_l)T_il,
    T_ii=1.

The exact old inner products are

    <g_i,g_j>=alpha_i^2 T_ij,
    <g_i,Y_j>=alpha_i^2 L_ij.                     (7)

In particular |T_ij|<=1. Define

    d_ij=tau_j-1 if T_ij>=R_ij, and d_ij=w_j otherwise.

Besides(3), the necessary and sufficient conditions for ALL ordered
relay query pairs are precisely, for every i<j,

    eta_j-eta_i<=w_i alpha_i^2(1-T_ij),
    eta_j-eta_i>=alpha_i^2[L_ij+d_ij(T_ij-R_ij)].  (8)

To prove this, the plane eta_j+<g_j,.> minus the current plane at
an old proximal query Y_i+d g_i equals
eta_j-eta_i+d alpha_i^2(T_ij-1). It is largest at d=w_i.
The old plane minus the current plane at a query Y_j+d g_j equals
eta_i-eta_j+alpha_i^2[L_ij+d(T_ij-R_ij)]. Its maximum is at the
endpoint d_ij as defined. Thus (8) is equivalent to every cross-block
ordered inequality, including both endpoints and all interior queries.
Within a block the inequalities are equalities. The optimum comparisons
are exactly (3). The accepted interpolation construction therefore
supplies ONE convex differentiable1-smooth function for precisely these
legal data. This does not drop later terminal-cell anchors when one
extends the instance: they must be added to the same interpolation test.

The first eta_u=0 jet also certifies true distance1 to the minimizer set.
For any minimizer z, its interpolation inequality with that jet gives
0>=eta_u+<g_u,z>, so <e_u,z><=0. Hence ||e_u-z||>=1, and the
included minimizer0 attains1. No alternative closer minimizer changes
the normalization.

## 3. Positive transition cost: an exact innovation budget

Consider a positive adjacent coefficient t=t_l>0, abbreviating
tau'=tau_(l+1), C'=C_(l+1), B=B_l, theta=B/tau'. Legality and(5)
force B>0, so w_l>r_l. Adjacent actual queries lie a distance
d_l g_l apart. Adding their two ordered smooth interpolation inequalities
gives cocoercivity

    d_l(1-t)alpha_l^2>=||g_l-g_(l+1)||^2.

Thus0<t<=1. The PSD construction also gives t<=theta. From (8),
the EXACT lower bound on the intercept increase across this pair is

 eta_(l+1)-eta_l >=alpha_l^2 E_l,

 E_l=B(1-t)+t(theta-1),                 if theta<=1,
 E_l=B(1-t)+C't(theta-1),               if theta>=1.       (9)

The first case uses the next block's FIRST query; the second case uses
its actual endpoint. Both are old-query costs, not free value choices.

In either case E_l>=theta-t. For theta<=1,

    E_l=theta(tau'-1)(1-t)+(theta-t)>=theta-t.

For theta>=1, B=theta tau'>=theta C', and1-t>=0, so

    E_l>=C'[theta(1-t)+t(theta-1)]=C'(theta-t)>=theta-t.

The actual innovation norm from (1) is
||z_(l+1)||^2=t(theta-t)alpha_l^2. Consequently EVERY positive
transition satisfies

    eta_(l+1)-eta_l >= ||z_(l+1)||^2/t_l >=0.      (10)

This retains independent innovation norms; it is not an assumption
that all gradients have the same size. In particular, if all affine
intercepts are zero, every positive transition has zero fresh innovation.

The polar inequalities <p_i,z><=0 force every coordinate of z
nonpositive by backward induction. Since0 is a minimizer, it is the
actual closest minimizer to R_0e_0, with squared distance E_0.
Every queried value is <x,p_i>-||p_i||^2/2. If htot=sum H_m, the
original normalized objective and primitive defect are exactly

 score_C=(2Mt-2M+1)E_(N-1)/(M^2 t^2 E_0),
 V/E_0=1-[(Mt-(M-1)+htot)/(Mt)]^2 E_(N-1)/E_0.            (6)

For the defect, sum the exact identity
2h_iF_i+h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2=||x_i||^2-||x_(i+1)||^2
and subtract the defining terminal term.

## 2. A transfer bound retaining the entire squared tail

Define the positive boundary energy

    Z_i=U_i D_i/tau_i, i>=1.                             (7)

At the terminal phase Z_(N-1)=E_(N-1)/t.
The endpoint comparison of phase i with phase i+1 gives, from(2)-(3),

 q_i U_i D_i>=u_i(U_i+u_i)W_i
                   +tau_i(tau_i U_i+u_i)D_(i+1)/tau_(i+1).

Since W_i>=beta_(i+1)^2>=D_(i+1)/U_(i+1) and U_(i+1)=U_i+u_i,
the squared-tail term must pay at least u_i D_(i+1). Therefore

 Z_(i+1)/Z_i
 <=q_i tau_i(U_i+u_i)/
           [tau_i^2 U_i+u_i(tau_i+tau_(i+1))]            (8)
 <=max(q_i/tau_i, q_i tau_i/(tau_i+tau_(i+1))).

The last inequality follows by viewing the ratio as a positive
denominator-weighted average of its values at u_i=0 and U_i=0;
U_i is actually positive, so no endpoint singularity is used.

At the root, its endpoint comparison with phase1 gives

 q E_0>=u_0^2W_0+A u_0 D_1/tau_1
       >=u_0 D_1+A u_0 D_1/tau_1.

Here D_1<=u_0 beta_1^2<=u_0 W_0. Since U_1=u_0, this becomes

    Z_1/E_0<=q/(A+tau_1).                                (9)

These inequalities explicitly retain the growing source sum U_i and
the older-coordinate residual W_i. Dropping either would give a false
apparent gain from accumulating many branches.

## 3. Multiply the exact ruler factors

The mass recursion gives, with b=a/(c-2) in(0,1),

    M_j=1+sum H_j=b c^j+(1-b)2^j.

Consequently M_m<=Mc^k and a<=q<c-2. For m>=512 use

 2/5<q<7/16, 12/5<c<39/16,
 cq>=1-1/m>=99/100,
 qc<=c(c-2)<1+8/m<=65/64.                                (10)

For example lambda<169/70 and a>=127/(129lambda)>2540/6321>2/5
give the first lower bound. The expansion
c(c-2)=1+(4+2sqrt(2))/m+(3+2sqrt(2))/m^2 gives the last one.

At a LOW phase tau_i=A and tau_(i+1)>=1. Since A q<1,

    A^2<A+tau_(i+1),

so the first alternative in(8) is larger and the factor is at most q/A.

At a HIGH phase tau_i=B=1+Q with Q>=99/100, its next phase is low,
tau_(i+1)=A. The bounds imply BQ>A, so B^2>B+A and the second
alternative in(8) is larger. The factor is at most QB/(B+A).

Write B_1=1+cq=tau_1 (not the benchmark with the same letter).
There are N/2-1 high phases, with levels summing to N-k-1, and the
same number of low phases after the root. Thus (8)-(9) give

 Z_(N-1)/E_0
 <=(qc)^(N-1)c^(-k)/[(A+B_1)A^(N/2-1)]
               *product_(high i) tau_i/(tau_i+A)
 <=(qc)^(N-1)c^(-k)/[(A+B_1)A^(N/2-1)].                  (11)

The count follows directly from 2^(k-ell-1) high checkpoints at level
ell=1,...,k-1. No asymptotic replacement of the physical word is made.

## 4. Full terminal completion and the actual distance

Let f be ANY convex1-smooth completion retaining all queried jets and
the optimum(0,0,0), including the maximal completion in accepted
1252b8823bb5a290.

If r>=1, every p_i is actually queried. Interpolation to any new
minimizer z gives <p_i,z><=0, since the retained value is
<x_i,p_i>-||p_i||^2/2. The triangular inequalities force its coordinates
nonpositive, so0 remains the true closest minimizer at distance R_0.
Additional orthogonal dimensions cannot lower the distance.

The last physical step is h_last=1+a. Its actual retained query gives

 2f(x_n)/E_0
 <=[2Mt-(2M-1)+h_last^2]E_(N-1)/(M^2 t^2 E_0)
 <2E_(N-1)/(MtE_0),

because M>=2+a yields 2M-1-h_last^2>=2-a^2>0.
Put K=1/(2M_m-1). Use M_m<=Mc^k and(11):

 score_free/K
 <[4A/(A+B_1)](qc)^(N-1)/A^(N/2)
 <2(qc)^(N-1)/A^(N/2).                                 (12)

The last inequality uses B_1>A.

If r=0, the old terminal gradient is UNQUERIED. Use instead the
Lipschitz-gradient lower bound

    dist(x_0,argmin f)^2>=||p_0||^2>=E_0/A^2.             (13)

At the final query i=N-2, put v=U_i/U_(i+1) in(0,1]. Its position is
R_i e_i+v R_(i+1)e_(i+1), and its gradient is
[R_i e_i-(1-v)R_(i+1)e_(i+1)]/A. One smoothness step of length A gives

 2f(x_n)<=(1-A^(-2))E_i
 +[-2v(1-v)/A+(1-2/A-1/A^2)(1-v)^2]E_(i+1)
 <=(1-A^(-2))E_i.                                       (14)

The bracket is nonpositive for A<23/16.

The final low phase's own zero comparison says

 q E_i>=u_i(AU_i+u_i)beta_(i+1)^2.

Since Z_i=[E_i-u_i U_i beta_(i+1)^2]/A, it follows that

    Z_i>=E_i/A^2.                                       (15)

To check this explicitly, the subtracted numerator is at most
q U_i E_i/(AU_i+u_i)<=q E_i/A; A-q=1 then proves(15).

Repeat the product(8)-(9) but omit the final low factor q/A. It yields

 Z_(N-2)/E_0
 <=q^(N-2)c^(N-k-1)/[(A+B_1)A^(N/2-2)].

Combine(13)-(15), multiply by K^(-1)<2c^k, and use A^2-1=q(2+q):

 score_free/K
 <[2(2+q)A^4/(A+B_1)](qc)^(N-1)/A^(N/2)
 <7(qc)^(N-1)/A^(N/2).                                 (16)

For the numerical rational constant, A+B_1>3 and
2(39/16)(23/16)^4/3=21827598/3145728<7.

No unqueried normal has been used to constrain the new minimizer.
The terminal bound follows only from retained queries and their actual
physical last displacement.

## 5. Uniform payoff and the original exact benchmark

Set z0=65/64>1. Then (qc)^(N-1)<=z0^N even when qc<1.
Also

    z0^2/A<(65/64)^2/(7/5)=21125/28672<3/4.

Equations(12),(16) prove

    score_free/K<7(3/4)^(N/2).

For N>=16, (3/4)^4=81/256<1/3 gives score_free/K<7/9.
If N grows, the ratio tends to zero uniformly in all source weights,
target weights, energies, r, terminal margin and full completion.

For the exact benchmark use accepted b98bb807d514e80d and write
rho_s=log_2(lambda). Put F(z)=(1+z)^rho_s-1. The second derivative of
log F(exp w) equals

 rho_s*z*(1+z)^(rho_s-2)*
 [(1+z)^rho_s-1-rho_s*z]/F(z)^2>0.

Thus F(z)F(1/z)>=F(1)^2=2 by midpoint convexity in w. Comparing the
positive root of t^2-(X+Y)t-XY with
(X^(1/rho_s)+Y^(1/rho_s))^rho_s proves

    Omega(X,Y)<=(X^(1/rho_s)+Y^(1/rho_s))^rho_s.

Induction in the accepted primitive recursion gives
1+S_circle(n)<=(n+1)^rho_s. Since the accepted dominant join
Gamma(X,D)=2X+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8XD)/2 is at most4X+D,
its recursion then gives B_n<=1+4n^rho_s.
The displayed exact mass formula gives M_m/lambda^m->exp(1), hence

    limsup K B_(2^m-1)<=2/exp(1).

We conclude

    limsup B_(2^m-1)*score_free<=14/[9 exp(1)]<1,

with limit superior zero whenever N tends to infinity.

## 6. Scope

The source weights may vary arbitrarily, vanish after the root, and
depend on the horizon. Every future coordinate has a potentially
unbounded number of contributing parents. Every old and future normal
and the true normalization are explicit. This is a complete exclusion
of separable positive incoming profiles, including free terminal data.

It does not cover a general a_ij whose column profiles are not
proportional. In particular two independent temporal source profiles,
signed transfer, or reactivation of old coordinates remain outside it.
It does not upper-bound unrestricted W and does not prove the original
exact-profile target.

glossary.u_i: Arbitrary nonnegative source weight, u_0>0, in a_ij=u_i beta_j.
glossary.beta_j: Positive target-coordinate weight in the separable forward transfers.
glossary.U_i: Sum of source weights u_l over l<i.
glossary.R_i: Actual coordinate mass U_i beta_i for i>=1; R_0 is the independent initial mass.
glossary.W_i: Squared future target-weight tail sum_(j>i) beta_j^2, not the unrestricted objective W_n.
glossary.D_i: U_i beta_i^2-u_i W_i, forced positive by the own/zero projection comparison.
glossary.K: Canonical Huber score 1/(2M_m-1), with M_m=1+sum H_m.
glossary.score_free: Actual normalized objective 2f(x_n)/dist(x_0,argmin f)^2 for any convex1-smooth terminal completion retaining all queried jets and the optimum.

# One joint cycle closes fast, intermediate, and slow normal modes together

Status: complete UNVERIFIED candidate. No new fact_submit allocation, solver,
numerical experiment, restart, or worker launch. Accepted inputs:
1252b8823bb5a290 (all prefix interpolation and maximal free completion),

b98bb807d514e80d (the exact benchmark recursions). Every new estimate used

## 1. Actual word and a whole genuinely joint class

Let m>=2^16, lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,

  Fast_m = {1-u/m +/- i sqrt(u-theta)/sqrt(m):

  g_i=(sqrt(w_z) Re[zP_i(z)], sqrt(w_z) Im[zP_i(z)])_z.       (1)

Set tau_m=m/2^28 and C_m=200/49+2/tau_m. For every legal such prefix,

  }.                                                       (2)

This includes the original b=d_0 and the maximal completion with a free

  limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) 2F(x_q-b g_q)
                        <=14379/(6272e)<7/8.                (3)

  2F(x_q-b g_q)>=3/(64S) for EVERY real b.                    (4)

The new result closes simultaneous repair by the stated intermediate

## 2. Uniform physical schedule estimates

For m>=128,

  12/5<c<5/2, 1/3<a<5/12, 0<a/(c-2)<1,
  11/8<=d_0<=3/2, 31/16<=d_1<=2.

Here lambda(lambda-2)=1 gives a/(c-2)<1. The upper c bound follows from
lambda(129/128)<5/2, or sqrt(2)<191/129 after squaring. The a bounds
follow directly; d_0=1+a and d_1=2-1/m give the step bounds.
Counting dyadic multiplicities gives the full-block sum S_j and squared
sum T_j:

  S_j=2^j-1+a(c^j-2^j)/(c-2),
  T_j=2^j-1+2a(c^j-2^j)/(c-2)
                         +a^2(c^(2j)-2^j)/(c^2-2).

Consequently S_j>=[d_j-(c-1)]/(c-2) and S_j<6d_j. For the second bound
use 2^j<=c^j, 1/a<3 and 1/(c-2)<5/2. Whenever d_j>=2000,

  S_j>=(19/10)d_j,
  T_j<=d_j^2/(c^2-2)+2S_j
       <=[25/94+12/2000]d_j^2<(7/25)d_j^2.                 (5)

The T_j bound follows also by subtracting 2S_j from its exact formula.
Here D>2000.

## 3. One actual cycle and its exact recursive defect

For z=alpha+i beta put sigma=|z|^2, kappa=alpha-sigma, and
eta=sigma(1+alpha)-2alpha^2. Let p_j be the polynomial of full H_j
and R_j=p_j(1-d_jz), so p_(j+1)=R_j p_j. Starting locally at 1, set
L_j=sum_(i in H_j)h_i|P_i|^2 and
E_j=sum_(i in H_j)h_i^2 sigma|P_i|^2.

Consider the cycle from the optimum to the end of H_j, backward along
its queries to its start, then to the optimum. Its exact weight is

  Dcal_j=beta^2 L_j-(kappa/2)(1+|p_j|^2+E_j).              (6)

Indeed the backward path area is beta L_j, the optimum edges have zero
area, and the energy is 1+|p_j|^2+E_j. Apply the accepted dfde cycle
identity beta*Area-kappa*Energy/2. Telescoping norms gives

  Dcal_j=[eta/(2alpha)](1+E_j)
                       -[sigma(1-alpha)/(2alpha)]|p_j|^2.

Substitute E_(j+1)=(1+|R_j|^2)E_j+d_j^2 sigma|p_j|^2 and
p_(j+1)=R_jp_j; use
d_j^2 sigma|p_j|^2-|R_j|^2=(2d_j alpha-1)|p_j|^2. This gives

  Dcal_(j+1)=(1+|R_j|^2)Dcal_j
                                +|p_j|^2(kappa+d_j eta).  (7)

The empty-block value is Dcal_0=-kappa. With p_j^-,Dcal_j^- denoting

  Dcal_j-Dcal_j^-
       =d_0 sigma[1-alpha-d_0 kappa]|p_j^-|^2.             (8)

d_0 sigma(1-d_0 alpha+d_0 sigma/2)|p_j^-|^2; the change in the

R_(m-1) and its endpoint is P_q=R_(m-1)p_(m-1)^-. Hence JOINT legality

  sum_z w_z |R_(m-1)(z)|^2 Dcal_(m-1)^-(z)<=0.             (9)

All joint values cancel. No cycle or index is chosen separately by mode.

## 4. Repetition amplifies the FAST positive coefficient

For Fast_m, direct expansion gives

  kappa=theta/m-u^2/m^2>0,
  eta=(u-2theta)/m+(u^2+u theta)/m^2-u^3/m^3>=3/m.

Also alpha>=1-6/m and sigma=alpha-kappa<=1. The first block has

  Dcal_1=d_0 eta-kappa|1-d_0z|^2>=3/m,                    (10)

since d_0>=11/8, kappa<=1/m, and |1-d_0z|<3/5. For the last estimate

Write v=z-1 and A_j=1+1/(a c^j). We have A_j<4, Re v<0 and

The exponential inequality follows by comparing positive power series.

All factors are nonzero since beta!=0. Define Acal_j=Dcal_j/|p_j|^2.

## 5. Intermediate modes and ALL negative credit on the same cycle

For an intermediate mode put t=alpha/r and h_c=2t/r. Then kappa>0,
eta>=sigma(1-2t^2)>0 and h_c>=2000d_0. Call it reached if D>=h_c,

       <=-(19/5)t v+(7/25)v^2<=-6t^2.                  (14)

For the last inequality 19u/5-7u^2/25 is concave on [2,5] with endpoint

A reverse path edge has exact weight

  h sigma(1-h alpha+h sigma/2)|P_i|^2
   =[sigma/(2alpha)](|P_i|^2-|P_(i+1)|^2)
                      +[h^2 sigma eta/(2alpha)]|P_i|^2.

  Dcal_k>=[sigma/(2alpha)](1-|p_k|^2)-alpha
    >=alpha[(1-exp(-6t^2))/(2t^2)-1]>alpha/2.            (15)

The ratio (1-exp(-6s))/s decreases. Even at t^2=1/4 the bracket is
2(1-exp(-3/2))-1>1/2, since
exp(3/2)>1+3/2+9/8+27/48>4. Our t<=1/32 is inside that range.

## 6. Joint elimination, actual last step, and exact benchmark

Set X_fast=sum_fast w_z|P_q|^2,
Y_reached=sum_reached w_z alpha|P_q|^2,
A_slow=sum_slow w_z alpha, A_unreached=sum_unreached w_z alpha.

  tau_m X_fast+(49/100)Y_reached
      <=(129/128)A_slow+(6/5)A_unreached=:Credit.         (19)

For any legal interpolant, optimum interpolation at q and smoothness
along the actual terminal displacement imply, for b in [0,2],

  2F(x_q-b g_q)
   <=sum_z w_z[2alpha-(1+b(2-b))sigma]|P_q|^2
   <=2X_fast+2Y_reached+2A_slow+2A_unreached.             (20)

For the exact comparison, the accepted benchmark has mass joins

  Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,
  G(A,B)=2A+B/2+sqrt(B^2+8AB)/2.

Let rho=log_2lambda and V(t)=(1+t)^rho-1. With t=exp(s),

   =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)[(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/V(t)^2>0.

t=(A/B)^(1/rho), L=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho this reads

From the exact sums and D=1+(1-1/m)c^(m-2),

  S/lambda^m -> e,     D/lambda^m -> e/lambda^2.

Indeed a/(c-2)->1, (1+1/m)^m->e, and (2/lambda)^m->0.
Multiplying (2) by B_n<=1+4n^rho and using tau_m->infinity gives

## 7. Explicit positive weights and EVERY ordered constraint

modes at t_1=1/32,t_2=1/64, r_(j,ell)=t_ell/(1000d_j), and 2m slow

Therefore

(kappa/2)|p_j-p_i|^2 +/- beta A_ij.
Since kappa>=5alpha/6 and sigma T<=alpha/6, (21)--(22) bound them below by

  [1125/3072-1/12]alpha sigma T^2|p_i|^2
                                 >(alpha sigma/4)T^2|p_i|^2.

  epsilon=delta/[2(K+delta)], w_base=1-epsilon,

components are repaired jointly, with a formula rather than numerics.

  H(v)=max_(i in {star,0,...,q})
      {<g_i,x_i>-f_i+<x_i,v-g_i>+||v-g_i||^2/2},

     >=(7/8)(49/64)(7/16)=2401/8192>2/7.

gives (2alpha-alpha^2)||Z||^2>=alpha/2.

For any finite anchor put y_i=x_i-g_i, delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2.
We have ||g_i||^2<=sigma+epsilon M^2<=sigma+delta/8<=2sigma.

  2delta_i>=49alpha/48-2sigma,
  2delta_i+2<x_q-y_i,v_test>-||v_test||^2
    >=alpha[49/48-1/300-101/400-3/3200]>alpha/2.            (25)

We used S>=100, 2sigma/alpha=1/(3S), alpha<=3/3200, and the fact
that other blocks do not contribute to this inner product.

the specified intermediate donors cannot create a leading fast payoff.

radii outside the stated set, notably moderate-angle frequencies with
