evidence:
# C45. Arbitrary positive forward incidence under an aggregate correlation sign

Status: UNVERIFIED joint candidate. No verifier, numerical solver or sweep.
All ingredients are proved here; no earlier candidate is a correctness premise.

Consider the near-critical ruler and arbitrary nonnegative forward transfers,
with ANY number of parents, ANY memory length, and NO factorization. Assume
that adjacent phase gradients have nonpositive inner products and that each
next gradient has nonpositive inner product with the weighted sum of all
strictly older gradients, as written explicitly below. In particular this
holds when EVERY pair of distinct phase gradients has nonpositive inner product.

For m>=512 and N>=16 phases, every legal such flow and every full terminal
completion satisfy

    score_free/K<7(3/4)^(N/2)<7/9.

Therefore limsup B_(2^m-1)*score_free<=14/(9e)<1, and this limit superior
is zero if N grows. These sign conditions are essential hypotheses of this
candidate; no unrestricted objective upper bound is asserted.

## 1. Real geometry, all normal tests, and the exact sign hypothesis

Set lambda=1+sqrt(F2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j). Fix 0<=r<=m-4, let
k=m-r, N=2^k, M=1+sum H_r, q=a c^r/M, A=1+q, and put

 q_i=q c^(nu_2(i+1)), tau_i=1+q_i, T_i=M tau_i, i<N-1,
 tau_(N-1)=t>=1, T_(N-1)=Mt.

The symbol nu_2 denotes binary valuation. The N ordinary phases are exactly
the physical H_r copies, with mass M-1; each nonfinal phase is followed by
the actual checkpoint1+Mq_i.

Choose arbitrary transfers a_ij>=0 for i<j and masses

    R_0>0, R_j=sum_(i<j)a_ij>0 for j>=1, E_i=R_i^2.

In the real space R^N with standard orthonormal basis define

 p_i=(R_i e_i-sum_(j>i)a_ij e_j)/T_i,
 C=conv(0,p_0,...,p_(N-1)),
 F_C(x)=max_(p in C)(<x,p>-||p||^2/2).

Its gradient is Euclidean projection onto C, by the projection variational
inequality and maximizing-difference inequalities. That projection is
nonexpansive; thus F_C is convex and1-smooth.

For i>=0 and j>i put r_j^(i)=sum_(l<i)a_lj, an actual inherited coordinate
mass. The exact phase state is

    X_i=R_i e_i+sum_(j>i)r_j^(i)e_j,

where the root sum vanishes. Subtracting T_i p_i exhausts coordinate i and
creates X_(i+1); every individual physical step is retained.

Define

 V_i=E_i-sum_(j>i)a_ij r_j^(i),
 C_i=sum_(j>i)a_ij[r_j^(i)+a_ij],
 Delta_ij=a_ij R_j-sum_(l>j)a_il a_jl, i<j.               (F1)

Direct expansion gives

    Delta_ij=-T_i T_j <p_i,p_j>.                         (F2)

For the complete normal test put z=(ordinary partial mass+1)/M in[1/M,1].
Multiplying all normal values by M, the own value is

    [(tau_i-z)V_i-z C_i]/tau_i^2,                        (F3)

and a future-j value is

    [sum_(l<i)Delta_lj+(z/tau_i)Delta_ij]/tau_j.           (F4)

Past normal values are nonpositive since their positive coordinates have
been exhausted and all remaining proximal coordinates are nonnegative.
Comparing(F3) with zero and EVERY(F4) at BOTH z=1/M and z=1 is necessary
and sufficient for all actual queries. All differences are affine. At the
last phase t>=1 suffices because there is no outgoing transfer or future
normal. This keeps the full old-query and future-query test explicit.

Every legal nonterminal phase has

    q_i V_i>=C_i>=0.                                    (F5)

In fact V_i>0: if C_i>0 use(F5); if C_i=0 all outgoing transfers vanish
and V_i=E_i>0. At the terminal phase V_(N-1)=E_(N-1)>0.

The additional sign hypothesis, for i=1,...,N-2, is

 F_i:=sum_(l<i)Delta_(l,i+1)>=0,
 G_i:=Delta_(i,i+1)>=0.                                 (F6)

By(F2), this means <p_i,p_(i+1)><=0 and
<sum_(l<i)T_l p_l,p_(i+1)><=0. Thus it is IMPLIED by all pairwise
nonpositive gradient correlations, but allows some positive older pair
correlations if the entire indicated sum still has the stated sign.
No assumption that (F6) follows from arbitrary positive transfers is made.

The class is nonempty. For example take only root-to-later transfers
a_0j=R_j and no outgoing transfers from j>=1. Set E_(N-1)=1, then choose
E_i backward large enough that
q_i E_i/tau_i^2>=max_(j>i) E_j/tau_j. Finally choose
qE_0>=sum_(j>=1)E_j+A max_(j>=1)E_j/tau_j.
These give every endpoint normal above, and their correlations obey(F6).

Every original queried value is <x,p_i>-||p_i||^2/2. The polar inequalities
<p_i,z><=0 imply backward that every coordinate of z is nonpositive.
Consequently0 is the actual closest minimizer to R_0e_0, with distance R_0.
Writing htot=sum H_m, the original objective and primitive defect are

 score_C=(2Mt-2M+1)E_(N-1)/(M^2t^2E_0),
 V/E_0=1-[(Mt-(M-1)+htot)/(Mt)]^2 E_(N-1)/E_0.            (F7)

Here V without a subscript is the project primitive defect; V_i in(F1)
is the phase energy numerator. Formula(F7) follows from the terminal state
and the exact identity
2hF+h(1-h)||g||^2=||x||^2-||x-hg||^2 along the original trajectory.

## 2. The boundary transfer uses only the two aggregate signs

Set Z_i=V_i/tau_i>0. At the final phase Z_(N-1)=E_(N-1)/t.
By direct summation in(F1),

    F_i+G_i=V_(i+1).                                    (F8)

The current squared-transfer cost also satisfies

 C_i>=a_(i,i+1)R_(i+1)>=Delta_(i,i+1)=G_i,                (F9)

because R_(i+1)=r_(i+1)^(i)+a_(i,i+1) and all products omitted from
C_i are nonnegative; the second inequality discards the shared-tail sum
subtracted in Delta.

The endpoint future-i+1 comparison(F3)-(F4), together with(F9), gives

 q_i V_i>=C_i+tau_i[tau_i F_i+G_i]/tau_(i+1)
 >=[tau_i^2 F_i+(tau_i+tau_(i+1))G_i]/tau_(i+1).

Using(F6),(F8), this implies

 Z_(i+1)/Z_i
 <=q_i tau_i(F_i+G_i)/
      [tau_i^2 F_i+(tau_i+tau_(i+1))G_i]
 <=max(q_i/tau_i, q_i tau_i/(tau_i+tau_(i+1))).           (F10)

The denominator is positive since F_i+G_i=V_(i+1)>0. The last ratio
is a positive denominator-weighted average of its endpoint ratios.

At the root, V_1=Delta_01>0, while
C_0=sum_(j>0)a_0j^2>=R_1^2>=Delta_01.
Its endpoint comparison with phase1 therefore gives

    Z_1/E_0<=q/(A+tau_1).                                (F11)

No factorization, finite memory, or scalar common direction was used.
The only sign step is the weighted-ratio bound under(F6).
## 3. Multiply the exact ruler factors

The mass recursion gives, with b=a/(c-2) in(0,1),

    M_j=1+sum H_j=b c^j+(1-b)2^j.

Consequently M_m<=Mc^k and a<=q<c-2. For m>=512 use

 2/5<q<7/16, 12/5<c<39/16,
 cq>=1-1/m>=99/100,
 qc<=c(c-2)<1+8/m<=65/64.                                (10)

For example lambda<169/70 and a>=127/(129lambda)>2540/6321>2/5
give the first lower bound. The expansion
c(c-2)=1+(4+2sqrt(2))/m+(3+2sqrt(2))/m^2 gives the last one.

At a LOW phase tau_i=A and tau_(i+1)>=1. Since A q<1,

    A^2<A+tau_(i+1),

so the first alternative in(F10) is larger and the factor is at most q/A.

At a HIGH phase tau_i=B=1+Q with Q>=99/100, its next phase is low,
tau_(i+1)=A. The bounds imply BQ>A, so B^2>B+A and the second
alternative in(F10) is larger. The factor is at most QB/(B+A).

Write B_1=1+cq=tau_1 (not the benchmark with the same letter).
There are N/2-1 high phases, with levels summing to N-k-1, and the
same number of low phases after the root. Thus (F10)-(F11) give

 Z_(N-1)/E_0
 <=(qc)^(N-1)c^(-k)/[(A+B_1)A^(N/2-1)]
               *product_(high i) tau_i/(tau_i+A)
 <=(qc)^(N-1)c^(-k)/[(A+B_1)A^(N/2-1)].                  (11)

The count follows directly from 2^(k-ell-1) high checkpoints at level
ell=1,...,k-1. No asymptotic replacement of the physical word is made.

## 4. Full terminal completion and the actual distance

Let f be ANY convex1-smooth completion retaining all queried jets and
the optimum(0,0,0), including the maximal completion in accepted
1252b8823bb5a290.

If r>=1, every p_i is actually queried. Interpolation to any new
minimizer z gives <p_i,z><=0, since the retained value is
<x_i,p_i>-||p_i||^2/2. The triangular inequalities force its coordinates
nonpositive, so0 remains the true closest minimizer at distance R_0.
Additional orthogonal dimensions cannot lower the distance.

The last physical step is h_last=1+a. Its actual retained query gives

 2f(x_n)/E_0
 <=[2Mt-(2M-1)+h_last^2]E_(N-1)/(M^2 t^2 E_0)
 <2E_(N-1)/(MtE_0),

because M>=2+a yields 2M-1-h_last^2>=2-a^2>0.
Put K=1/(2M_m-1). Use M_m<=Mc^k and(11):

 score_free/K
 <[4A/(A+B_1)](qc)^(N-1)/A^(N/2)
 <2(qc)^(N-1)/A^(N/2).                                 (12)

The last inequality uses B_1>A.

If r=0, the old terminal gradient is UNQUERIED. Use instead the
Lipschitz-gradient lower bound

    dist(x_0,argmin f)^2>=||p_0||^2>=E_0/A^2.             (13)

At the final query i=N-2, put
v=r_(i+1)^(i)/R_(i+1) in[0,1]. Its position is
R_i e_i+v R_(i+1)e_(i+1), and its gradient is
[R_i e_i-(1-v)R_(i+1)e_(i+1)]/A. One smoothness step of length A gives

 2f(x_n)<=(1-A^(-2))E_i
 +[-2v(1-v)/A+(1-2/A-1/A^2)(1-v)^2]E_(i+1)
 <=(1-A^(-2))E_i.                                       (14)

The bracket is nonpositive for A<23/16.

Write b=a_(i,i+1) and d=r_(i+1)^(i). The final low phase's
own zero comparison says qE_i>=A b d+b^2. Since Z_i=(E_i-bd)/A,
it follows that

    Z_i>=E_i/A^2.                                       (15)

Indeed bd<=qE_i/A, and A-q=1 then proves the displayed bound.

Repeat the product(F10)-(F11) but omit the final low factor q/A. It yields

 Z_(N-2)/E_0
 <=q^(N-2)c^(N-k-1)/[(A+B_1)A^(N/2-2)].

Combine(13)-(15), multiply by K^(-1)<2c^k, and use A^2-1=q(2+q):

 score_free/K
 <[2(2+q)A^4/(A+B_1)](qc)^(N-1)/A^(N/2)
 <7(qc)^(N-1)/A^(N/2).                                 (16)

For the numerical rational constant, A+B_1>3 and
2(39/16)(23/16)^4/3=21827598/3145728<7.

No unqueried normal has been used to constrain the new minimizer.
The terminal bound follows only from retained queries and their actual
physical last displacement.

## 5. Uniform payoff and the original exact benchmark

Set z0=65/64>1. Then (qc)^(N-1)<=z0^N even when qc<1.
Also

    z0^2/A<(65/64)^2/(7/5)=21125/28672<3/4.

Equations(12),(16) prove

    score_free/K<7(3/4)^(N/2).

For N>=16, (3/4)^4=81/256<1/3 gives score_free/K<7/9.
If N grows, the ratio tends to zero uniformly in all nonnegative transfers obeying(F6), energies, r, terminal margin and full completion.

For the exact benchmark use accepted b98bb807d514e80d and write
rho_s=log_2(lambda). Put F(z)=(1+z)^rho_s-1. The second derivative of
log F(exp w) equals

 rho_s*z*(1+z)^(rho_s-2)*
 [(1+z)^rho_s-1-rho_s*z]/F(z)^2>0.

Thus F(z)F(1/z)>=F(1)^2=2 by midpoint convexity in w. Comparing the
positive root of t^2-(X+Y)t-XY with
(X^(1/rho_s)+Y^(1/rho_s))^rho_s proves

    Omega(X,Y)<=(X^(1/rho_s)+Y^(1/rho_s))^rho_s.

Induction in the accepted primitive recursion gives
1+S_circle(n)<=(n+1)^rho_s. Since the accepted dominant join
Gamma(X,D)=2X+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8XD)/2 is at most4X+D,
its recursion then gives B_n<=1+4n^rho_s.
The displayed exact mass formula gives M_m/lambda^m->exp(1), hence

    limsup K B_(2^m-1)<=2/exp(1).

We conclude

    limsup B_(2^m-1)*score_free<=14/[9 exp(1)]<1,

with limit superior zero whenever N tends to infinity.

## 6. Scope and the sign needed to escape

This excludes every legal nonnegative forward-incidence construction
satisfying(F6), regardless of memory length, number of parents, graph size,
or factorization rank. It includes all pairwise nonpositive-gradient
families, but also permits positive older pairs that cancel in the
specified weighted sum. All original phases and full terminal completion
are covered.

An escaping positive-incidence witness must violate at least one of these
two aggregate signs somewhere: it needs either a positive adjacent
gradient correlation or a positive correlation of the next gradient with
the entire strictly older weighted gradient sum. A positive remote pair
alone is insufficient if the aggregate signs still hold.

This is a necessary condition within the displayed forward-incidence
geometry, not a construction attaining the benchmark. Arbitrary flows
violating(F6), signed transfers, and reactivation of old coordinates remain
open. It is not an upper bound on unrestricted W or a proof of the original
exact-profile theorem.

# Unequal quadratic rays on the actual critical ruler

accepted input is the benchmark recurrence in b98bb807d514e80d. This result

    g(x)=u x for x>=0, g(x)=v x for x<=0,
    f(x)=u x^2/2 for x>=0, f(x)=v x^2/2 for x<=0.       (1)

The derivative is continuous, nondecreasing and1-Lipschitz; f is convex,
differentiable and1-smooth, with minimizer0. For positive curvatures the
minimizer is unique. Both curvatures may depend arbitrarily on m. For every
nonzero starting point, exact GD with H_m satisfies

  2f(x_n)/x_0^2 <= E_m := max{
       1/(2e S_m),
       d_(m-1)/(c^2 a^2 c^(2m)),
       r^2/(2e S_(m-1))
  } < (3/4)K.                                         (2)

For the exact benchmark B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1,

    limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) E_m <= 2/e^2 <1.     (3)

The same upper bound holds for arbitrary finite orthogonal direct sums
of (1), with positive coordinate curvatures, translations of their unique
minimizer and arbitrary orthogonal changes of basis. Thus independent
one-sided quadratic curvatures, including horizon-dependent unequal cores
that extend over the entire rays, cannot supply the target witness here.

## 2. Parameter estimates and the scalar product

Directly from the ruler recurrence,

    M_j=(a/r)c^j+(1-a/r)2^j.                           (4)

For m>=128 the following deliberately loose rational bounds hold:

    12/5<lambda<c<49/20<5/2,
    3/8<a<lambda-2<1/2,
    ac=1-1/m>7/8, 0<a<r<1/2, cr<5/4.                 (5)

For example lambda<17/7 gives c<2193/896<49/20.
Then a>(127/128)/(49/20)>3/8; also
a=(m-1)/[(m+1)lambda]<1/lambda=lambda-2<r.
Equation(4) implies

    S_j >= a c^j/r-1,
    M_j<=c^j, M_(j+1)<=c M_j.                         (6)

Let

    P_j(t)=product_(l=0)^(j-1)(1-d_l t)^(2^(j-l-1)),
    P_0(t)=1.                                        (7)

Before the first level crossing for curvature t all these factors are
positive and

    0<P_j(t)<=exp(-S_j t).                            (8)

We first prove (2) when u>=v>0 and neither d_j u nor d_j v equals1.
Reflection deals with v>u. Positive homogeneity reduces initial points
to+1 and-1. Finally, finite compositions of the continuous maps
x -> x-d_j g(x), and the objective itself, are continuous in u,v.
This extends the proved inequalities to zero factors and zero curvatures.

Define p and q as the first nonnegative levels with d_p u>1 and d_q v>1,
respectively. They exist because a>0,c>1,u,v>0, and p<=q.

## 3. Same crossing level: two swapping maps

Suppose p=q<m. H_p preserves both signs, and H_(p+1) swaps them.
Write A_j for the magnitude at the end of H_j starting at+1, and B_j
for that starting at-1. At j=p+1,

    A_(p+1)=(d_p u-1)P_p(u)P_p(v),
    B_(p+1)=(d_p v-1)P_p(u)P_p(v).                    (9)

All subsequent H_j also swap signs: the three maps H_j, the central
d_j step and H_j each swap. Consequently, for j>=p+1,

    A_(j+1)=(d_j v-1)A_j^2,
    B_(j+1)=(d_j u-1)B_j^2.                          (10)

For either of these recurrences, let t be the output-ray curvature
(v for A, u for B), let Z_j be its magnitude, and put

    Y_j=c a c^j t Z_j.

An exact substitution in(10) gives

    Y_(j+1)=[1-(1-t)/(a c^j t)]Y_j^2 <= Y_j^2.        (11)

The bracket lies in[0,1] because all these levels cross and t<=1.

It remains to control the actual entry value, including both curvatures.
If p=0, (9) gives

    c a c v A_1=c^2 a v(d_0 u-1)<=(ac)^2 v<=1,

and the other starting sign has the symmetric bound.
If p>=1, then u,v<1/d_(p-1)<=1/d_0<8/11. Put
U=a c^p u and V=a c^p v. From(6),(8),(9),

    c a c^(p+1) v A_(p+1)
       <=c^2 U V exp(-(U+V)/r+u+v)
       <=(cr)^2 exp(u+v-2)<1.                        (12)

The middle inequality maximizes z exp(-z/r) at z=r. The last uses
cr<5/4 and exp(6/11)>1+6/11+18/121=205/121>25/16.
The bound for B is identical with u,v exchanged. Iterating(11) proves
Y_m<=1 for both initial signs. Since the terminal curvature t crosses
at a level<=m-1, t>1/d_(m-1), and hence

    2f(x_n)=t Z_m^2
       <=1/(c^2 a^2 c^(2m)t)
       <=d_(m-1)/(c^2 a^2 c^(2m)).                  (13)

## 4. Different crossing levels: an exact sign reset

Suppose p<q and p<m. The level-p step maps the high-curvature ray to
the low-curvature ray and preserves the low ray. Thus H_(p+1) maps
BOTH signs to the low ray. Every subsequent H_j still has this
constant sign map, because the final H_j in H_(j+1) returns to that
ray regardless of what the central step does.

For p+1<=j<=q, low-ray initial data have not yet crossed, so

    B_j=P_j(v),
    A_j=D_p P_j(v)/[P_p(v)(1-d_p v)],
    D_p=(d_p u-1)P_p(u).                             (14)

One can also obtain this identity by splitting the actual run into its
initial high-ray H_p and d_p step, followed by low-ray steps of total
mass S_j-S_p-d_p. No queries or spatial pieces are chosen independently.

For j>=q the central step crosses from low to high, after which H_j
returns to low. The exact magnitude recurrences are

    A_(j+1)=(d_j v-1)A_j^2,
    B_(j+1)=(d_j v-1)A_j B_j.                        (15)

In particular, with Z_j=max(A_j,B_j),
Z_(j+1)<=(d_j v-1)Z_j^2. Therefore the scaled Y_j=c a c^j v Z_j
again satisfies(11), with <= in place of its first equality.

Assume first q<m. We prove the needed entry Y_q<=1.
For B_q=P_q(v), q>=1 and v<1/d_(q-1)<=1/d_0<8/11. With
V=a c^q v, (6),(8) give

    c V B_q <= c V exp(-V/r+v)
               <=cr exp(v-1)<1,                    (16)

where exp(3/11)>1+3/11>5/4 was used.

For A_q observe that S_q-S_p-d_p>=S_(q-1), because p<=q-1 and
S_p+d_p<=S_(q-1)+d_(q-1). Equation(14) therefore gives

    A_q<=D_p exp(-v S_(q-1)).                        (17)

If p>=1, setting U=a c^p u and using(6),(8) yields

    D_p<=U exp(-U/r+u)<=r exp(u-1).

Since u,v<8/11, (17) implies

    c V A_q<=c r exp(u-1)V exp(-V/(cr)+v)
                <=(cr)^2 exp(u+v-2)<1.              (18)

If p=0,q=1, the entry is exact:
A_1=d_0u-1<=a, and c a c v A_1<=(ac)^2v<=1.
If p=0,q>=2, use D_0<=a and v<1/d_0<8/11 in(17) to get

    c V A_q<=a c^2 r exp(v-1)
                <=cr exp(v-1)<1,                    (19)

because ac<1. Equations(16),(18),(19) cover every entry regime. Now
(15),(11) give Y_m<=1. The terminal ray is low, whose curvature
v>1/d_(m-1), so (13) applies to BOTH starting signs.

Assume instead q>=m. Starting on the low ray never crosses and gives
v P_m(v)^2<=1/(2e S_m) by(8). Starting on the high ray crosses once
at level p, after which every actual step preserves the low ray. The
exact decomposition underlying(14) and the proved bound D_p<=r give

    A_m<=r exp[-v(S_m-S_p-d_p)]
         <=r exp(-v S_(m-1)).

Consequently

    2f(x_n)=v A_m^2<=r^2/(2e S_(m-1)).               (20)

Finally, if p>=m neither ray crosses: (8) gives the first term in(2)
for each initial sign. This completes all generic cases, and continuity
as explained above completes (2)'s non-strict upper bound.

## 5. Uniform finite and benchmark constants

Each of the three entries in E_m is less than(3/4)K.
For the first, S_m>=1 and e>2 give

    (2S_m+1)/(2e S_m)<=3/(2e)<3/4.

For the second, M_m<=c^m and ac>7/8 imply

 (2S_m+1)d_(m-1)/(c^2 a^2 c^(2m))
  <= 2/[(ac)^2 c^m]+2/[c^2 ac]
  <= 16/49+25/63=2233/3087<3/4.                      (21)

Here c>2,m>=3 bound the first summand, and c>12/5 bounds the second.
For the third, put S=S_(m-1)>=1. Since S_m<=c(S+1)-1, c<5/2,r<1/2,

    (2S_m+1)r^2/(2e S)
       <=r^2(4c-1)/(2e)<9/(8e)<3/4.                 (22)

For completeness, derive the benchmark bound directly from the accepted
recurrence rather than use another unverified candidate as a premise.
Write rho=log_2(lambda), C_N=S_circle(N)+1. Its mass join is
Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2. The dominant join is
G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

For t>0 set F(t)=(1+t)^rho-1. With t=exp(z), differentiation gives

 (d^2/dz^2)log F(exp(z))
 =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)[(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/F(t)^2>0.

The bracket is positive because rho>1. Convexity at z,-z therefore
gives F(t)F(1/t)>=F(1)^2=2. If A=t^rho B and D=(1+t)^rho B, this
says (D-A)(D-B)>=2AB, or D^2-(A+B)D-AB>=0. It follows that
Omega(A,B)<=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho. Induction in the accepted
primitive recurrence yields C_N<=(N+1)^rho. Since G(A,D)<=4A+D,
induction in the accepted dominant recurrence gives

    B_N<=1+4N^rho.                                  (23)

At a split N=k+l+1 the induction uses
(k+1)^rho+l^rho<=(k+l+1)^rho; this holds for nonnegative arguments
because rho>1. The base N=0 is B_0=1.

Equation(4) and the actual horizon-dependent parameters give

    c^m/lambda^m -> e,
    S_m/c^m ->1, S_(m-1)/c^(m-1)->1,
    a->1/lambda, r->1/lambda.

Multiplying the three entries in E_m by the upper bound(23), at
N=2^m-1, gives limits at most, respectively,

    2/e^2, 4/(e lambda^2), 2/(e^2 lambda).           (24)

The first is the largest: lambda>1 and 2e<lambda^2. One elementary
check is e<49/18<11/4 while lambda^2>29/5>11/2. The e bound follows
by bounding the factorial tail from3 onward by a geometric series
with first term1/6 and ratio1/4. This proves(3), uniformly over all
horizon-dependent choices of curvatures and starting signs.

For finite orthogonal direct sums, the GD recursions separate by
coordinate and the normalized terminal objective is a weighted average
of coordinate normalized objectives, with weights proportional to their
squared initial displacements. This proves the stated extension.

## 6. Scope and audit

The crucial new mechanism is the exact constant-sign map when the two
curvatures have different crossing levels. It is not an assertion that
all scalar maps are controlled by their largest secant. Spatially varying
derivatives can give amplitude-dependent crossing levels, so their
recursive maps need not be sign-constant and equations(14)-(15) fail.

No saturated initial jet, equal-ray curvature, fixed-m-independent
curvature or small-core-curvature assumption was made. Zero factors
and zero curvatures are included by an actual continuity argument.
The objective in every case is the complete area in(1), with true
initial distance to the unique minimizer for u,v>0. This is a precisely
scoped obstruction, not the original all-schedule theorem.

The literature check used Matlas for the sign-switching model; its hits
were not applicable. The exact local copy of Altschuler--Parrilo,
arXiv:2309.16530, Section2 and the opening of Section3, was read for
the ruler recursion and the importance of full trajectory consistency.
No external theorem is a premise of this proof; the altered ruler's
mass formula and all estimates were rederived above.

claim: C45 stronger scope: arbitrary nonnegative forward flows need NO adjacent-correlation sign and NO low-phase sign. It suffices that at each HIGH phase i the next low gradient p_(i+1) has nonpositive correlation with sum_(l<i)T_l p_l. Under only this condition the same complete free-terminal bound score/K<7(3/4)^(N/2) holds (m>=512,N>=16). evidence:
# C45, enlarged scope. Only high-phase older-history signs are needed

Status: UNVERIFIED joint candidate. No verifier, numerical solver or sweep.
All ingredients are proved here; no earlier candidate is a correctness premise.

Consider the near-critical ruler and arbitrary nonnegative forward transfers,
with ANY number of parents, ANY memory length, and NO factorization. Assume ONLY that after each HIGH phase, the next gradient has nonpositive
inner product with the weighted sum of all strictly older phase gradients,
as written explicitly below. Every adjacent gradient correlation is free,
and every low-phase correlation is free. In particular the hypothesis holds
when EVERY pair of distinct phase gradients has nonpositive inner product.

For m>=512 and N>=16 phases, every legal such flow and every full terminal
completion satisfy

    score_free/K<7(3/4)^(N/2)<7/9.

Therefore limsup B_(2^m-1)*score_free<=14/(9e)<1, and this limit superior
is zero if N grows. These sign conditions are essential hypotheses of this
candidate; no unrestricted objective upper bound is asserted.

## 1. Real geometry, all normal tests, and the exact sign hypothesis

Set lambda=1+sqrt(F2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j). Fix 0<=r<=m-4, let
k=m-r, N=2^k, M=1+sum H_r, q=a c^r/M, A=1+q, and put

 q_i=q c^(nu_2(i+1)), tau_i=1+q_i, T_i=M tau_i, i<N-1,
 tau_(N-1)=t>=1, T_(N-1)=Mt.

The symbol nu_2 denotes binary valuation. The N ordinary phases are exactly
the physical H_r copies, with mass M-1; each nonfinal phase is followed by
the actual checkpoint1+Mq_i.

Choose arbitrary transfers a_ij>=0 for i<j and masses

    R_0>0, R_j=sum_(i<j)a_ij>0 for j>=1, E_i=R_i^2.

In the real space R^N with standard orthonormal basis define

 p_i=(R_i e_i-sum_(j>i)a_ij e_j)/T_i,
 C=conv(0,p_0,...,p_(N-1)),
 F_C(x)=max_(p in C)(<x,p>-||p||^2/2).

Its gradient is Euclidean projection onto C, by the projection variational
inequality and maximizing-difference inequalities. That projection is
nonexpansive; thus F_C is convex and1-smooth.

For i>=0 and j>i put r_j^(i)=sum_(l<i)a_lj, an actual inherited coordinate
mass. The exact phase state is

    X_i=R_i e_i+sum_(j>i)r_j^(i)e_j,

where the root sum vanishes. Subtracting T_i p_i exhausts coordinate i and
creates X_(i+1); every individual physical step is retained.

Define

 V_i=E_i-sum_(j>i)a_ij r_j^(i),
 C_i=sum_(j>i)a_ij[r_j^(i)+a_ij],
 Delta_ij=a_ij R_j-sum_(l>j)a_il a_jl, i<j.               (F1)

Direct expansion gives

    Delta_ij=-T_i T_j <p_i,p_j>.                         (F2)

For the complete normal test put z=(ordinary partial mass+1)/M in[1/M,1].
Multiplying all normal values by M, the own value is

    [(tau_i-z)V_i-z C_i]/tau_i^2,                        (F3)

and a future-j value is

    [sum_(l<i)Delta_lj+(z/tau_i)Delta_ij]/tau_j.           (F4)

Past normal values are nonpositive since their positive coordinates have
been exhausted and all remaining proximal coordinates are nonnegative.
Comparing(F3) with zero and EVERY(F4) at BOTH z=1/M and z=1 is necessary
and sufficient for all actual queries. All differences are affine. At the
last phase t>=1 suffices because there is no outgoing transfer or future
normal. This keeps the full old-query and future-query test explicit.

Every legal nonterminal phase has

    q_i V_i>=C_i>=0.                                    (F5)

In fact V_i>0: if C_i>0 use(F5); if C_i=0 all outgoing transfers vanish
and V_i=E_i>0. At the terminal phase V_(N-1)=E_(N-1)>0.

The additional sign hypothesis is imposed ONLY when i is a HIGH phase,
namely odd i with 1<=i<=N-3:

    F_i:=sum_(l<i)Delta_(l,i+1)>=0.                      (F6)

Always write G_i=Delta_(i,i+1), but impose NO sign on G_i. By(F2),
condition(F6) is exactly <sum_(l<i)T_l p_l,p_(i+1)><=0 at high phases.
It follows from pairwise nonpositive correlations, but permits arbitrary
positive adjacent correlations and cancellations among older pairs.
No assumption that(F6) follows from arbitrary positive transfers is made.

The class is nonempty. For example take only root-to-later transfers
a_0j=R_j and no outgoing transfers from j>=1. Set E_(N-1)=1, then choose
E_i backward large enough that
q_i E_i/tau_i^2>=max_(j>i) E_j/tau_j. Finally choose
qE_0>=sum_(j>=1)E_j+A max_(j>=1)E_j/tau_j.
These give every endpoint normal above, and their correlations obey(F6).

Every original queried value is <x,p_i>-||p_i||^2/2. The polar inequalities
<p_i,z><=0 imply backward that every coordinate of z is nonpositive.
Consequently0 is the actual closest minimizer to R_0e_0, with distance R_0.
Writing htot=sum H_m, the original objective and primitive defect are

 score_C=(2Mt-2M+1)E_(N-1)/(M^2t^2E_0),
 V/E_0=1-[(Mt-(M-1)+htot)/(Mt)]^2 E_(N-1)/E_0.            (F7)

Here V without a subscript is the project primitive defect; V_i in(F1)
is the phase energy numerator. Formula(F7) follows from the terminal state
and the exact identity
2hF+h(1-h)||g||^2=||x||^2-||x-hg||^2 along the original trajectory.

## 2. All low phases are automatic; high phases need only the older sum

Set Z_i=V_i/tau_i>0. At the final phase Z_(N-1)=E_(N-1)/t.
By direct summation in(F1),

    F_i+G_i=V_(i+1).                                    (F8)

The current squared-transfer cost also satisfies

 C_i>=a_(i,i+1)R_(i+1)>=Delta_(i,i+1)=G_i,                (F9)

because R_(i+1)=r_(i+1)^(i)+a_(i,i+1) and all products omitted from
C_i are nonnegative; the second inequality discards the shared-tail sum
subtracted in Delta.

The endpoint future-i+1 comparison(F3)-(F4), together with
C_i>=max(0,G_i), gives

 q_i V_i >=[tau_i^2 V_(i+1)-tau_i q_i G_i
                              +tau_(i+1)max(0,G_i)]/tau_(i+1).   (F9a)

If G_i<=0, the two extra terms are nonnegative. Thus

    Z_(i+1)/Z_i<=q_i/tau_i.                             (F10a)

If G_i>=0, the extra coefficient of G_i in(F9a) is
Delta_cap=tau_(i+1)-tau_i q_i.
At a LOW phase tau_i=A and Delta_cap>=1-Aq>0, so(F10a)
holds for arbitrary F_i and G_i, without ANY correlation-sign condition.

At a HIGH phase tau_i=B=1+Q and tau_(i+1)=A, one has
Delta_cap=A-BQ<0. The only hypothesis(F6) gives
G_i<=F_i+G_i=V_(i+1). Multiplication by the negative Delta_cap
therefore bounds the right side of(F9a) below by
[B^2+A-BQ]V_(i+1)/A=(A+B)V_(i+1)/A. Consequently

    Z_(i+1)/Z_i<=q_i tau_i/(tau_i+tau_(i+1)).            (F10b)

The elementary parameter signs Aq<1 and BQ>A are established below.
When G_i<=0 at a high phase, (F10a) is stronger since BQ>A.
Thus in all cases the same phasewise transfer bound holds:

 Z_(i+1)/Z_i
 <=max(q_i/tau_i, q_i tau_i/(tau_i+tau_(i+1))).           (F10)

No adjacent-correlation sign is required, and no low-phase sign is required.

At the root, V_1=Delta_01>0, while
C_0=sum_(j>0)a_0j^2>=R_1^2>=Delta_01.
Its endpoint comparison with phase1 therefore gives

    Z_1/E_0<=q/(A+tau_1).                                (F11)

No factorization, finite memory, or scalar common direction was used.
The only extra sign is the older-sum hypothesis(F6) at high phases.

## 3. Multiply the exact ruler factors

The mass recursion gives, with b=a/(c-2) in(0,1),

    M_j=1+sum H_j=b c^j+(1-b)2^j.

Consequently M_m<=Mc^k and a<=q<c-2. For m>=512 use

 2/5<q<7/16, 12/5<c<39/16,
 cq>=1-1/m>=99/100,
 qc<=c(c-2)<1+8/m<=65/64.                                (10)

For example lambda<169/70 and a>=127/(129lambda)>2540/6321>2/5
give the first lower bound. The expansion
c(c-2)=1+(4+2sqrt(2))/m+(3+2sqrt(2))/m^2 gives the last one.

At a LOW phase tau_i=A and tau_(i+1)>=1. Since A q<1,

    A^2<A+tau_(i+1),

so the first alternative in(F10) is larger and the factor is at most q/A.

At a HIGH phase tau_i=B=1+Q with Q>=99/100, its next phase is low,
tau_(i+1)=A. The bounds imply BQ>A, so B^2>B+A and the second
alternative in(F10) is larger. The factor is at most QB/(B+A).

Write B_1=1+cq=tau_1 (not the benchmark with the same letter).
There are N/2-1 high phases, with levels summing to N-k-1, and the
same number of low phases after the root. Thus (F10)-(F11) give

 Z_(N-1)/E_0
 <=(qc)^(N-1)c^(-k)/[(A+B_1)A^(N/2-1)]
               *product_(high i) tau_i/(tau_i+A)
 <=(qc)^(N-1)c^(-k)/[(A+B_1)A^(N/2-1)].                  (11)

The count follows directly from 2^(k-ell-1) high checkpoints at level
ell=1,...,k-1. No asymptotic replacement of the physical word is made.

## 4. Full terminal completion and the actual distance

Let f be ANY convex1-smooth completion retaining all queried jets and
the optimum(0,0,0), including the maximal completion in accepted
1252b8823bb5a290.

If r>=1, every p_i is actually queried. Interpolation to any new
minimizer z gives <p_i,z><=0, since the retained value is
<x_i,p_i>-||p_i||^2/2. The triangular inequalities force its coordinates
nonpositive, so0 remains the true closest minimizer at distance R_0.
Additional orthogonal dimensions cannot lower the distance.

The last physical step is h_last=1+a. Its actual retained query gives

 2f(x_n)/E_0
 <=[2Mt-(2M-1)+h_last^2]E_(N-1)/(M^2 t^2 E_0)
 <2E_(N-1)/(MtE_0),

because M>=2+a yields 2M-1-h_last^2>=2-a^2>0.
Put K=1/(2M_m-1). Use M_m<=Mc^k and(11):

 score_free/K
 <[4A/(A+B_1)](qc)^(N-1)/A^(N/2)
 <2(qc)^(N-1)/A^(N/2).                                 (12)

The last inequality uses B_1>A.

If r=0, the old terminal gradient is UNQUERIED. Use instead the
Lipschitz-gradient lower bound

    dist(x_0,argmin f)^2>=||p_0||^2>=E_0/A^2.             (13)

At the final query i=N-2, put
v=r_(i+1)^(i)/R_(i+1) in[0,1]. Its position is
R_i e_i+v R_(i+1)e_(i+1), and its gradient is
[R_i e_i-(1-v)R_(i+1)e_(i+1)]/A. One smoothness step of length A gives

 2f(x_n)<=(1-A^(-2))E_i

has positive real part. Its negative argument is
atan(h r sin theta/(1-h r cos theta)). The sum of these arguments is at most

  rS sin theta/(1-rS cos theta)
      <=[R/(1-R)]theta<=theta/2.

Thus arg phi_i(z) lies in [theta/2,theta]; both Re phi_i(z) and
Im phi_i(z) are nonnegative. The zero parameter is immediate.

Let expectation denote the finite weighted sum and put mu_i=E phi_i.
A direct expansion, with z,v independent under the same weights, gives

  Re[E(phi_i conj(phi_j))-mu_i conj(mu_j)]
   =(1/2)E_(z,v) Re[(phi_i(z)-phi_i(v))
                                conj(phi_j(z)-phi_j(v))]>=0.  (8)

Set e=x_0, G_i=<e,g_i>=Re mu_i, u_i=g_i-G_i e. Then G_i>=0 and

  <u_i,u_j>
    =Re[E(phi_i conj(phi_j))-mu_i conj(mu_j)]
                                  +(Im mu_i)(Im mu_j)>=0. (9)

This establishes one joint cone directly from the probability law. It is
not the union of separate single-mode legality statements.

## 3. The explicit PSD rank-one coupling

In real coordinates y=(y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4), let
v=(Re omega,-Im omega,-Re omega,Im omega). The map T:R^4->R^5 is

  T y=(sqrt(w_1)y_1,sqrt(w_1)y_2,
       sqrt(w_2)y_3,sqrt(w_2)y_4,sqrt(rho_coup)<v,y>).

Its Gram metric is exactly

  T^T T=diag(w_1,w_1,w_2,w_2)+rho_coup vv^T,

which is real positive definite for w_1,w_2>0. Formula (3) is precisely
T applied to the two polynomial blocks, so it gives actual vectors and
a fixed linear realization. The fifth coordinate of e=x_0 is zero.
It does not change G_i; it adds rho_coup U_i U_j to (9), where

  U_i=Re[omega(phi_i(z_1)-phi_i(z_2))].

Under (4a), U_i=|z_1-z_2| Re a_i(z_1,z_2)>0, so the cone is preserved
for every rho_coup>=0.

For arbitrary orientation, put A=phi_i(z_1)-phi_i(z_2) and
B=phi_j(z_1)-phi_j(z_2). The elementary identity

  Re(omega A) Re(omega B)
    =(Re(A conj B)+Re(omega^2 A B))/2
    >=(Re(A conj B)-|A||B|)/2
    >=-d^2 |A||B|

follows from (7). The two-point covariance term in (8) equals
w_1w_2 Re(A conj B), which is at least
w_1w_2(1-2d^2)|A||B|. The imaginary-mean term is nonnegative.
Thus every transverse pair remains nonnegative whenever

  rho_coup <= [(1-2d^2)/d^2] w_1w_2.                    (10)

At d=12/17 the ratio is 1/144; at d=16/31 it is 449/256.
This proves (4b)--(5).

For clarity these vectors really permit a nonnormal operator. Let
Z=diag(C(z_1),C(z_2)), where
C(alpha+i beta)=[[alpha,-beta],[beta,alpha]].
On R^5 set A_coup=T Z (T^T T)^(-1)T^T, zero on the orthogonal complement
of im T. Then A_coup x_i=g_i. If rho_coup>0 and, for example, omega=1
and z_1,z_2 have the same positive imaginary part but different real
parts, its complex eigenvectors T(e_1-i e_2) and T(e_3-i e_4) have
distinct eigenvalues and inner product -rho_coup!=0. Hence A_coup is
not normal. To justify that implication directly, normality gives
||(A-lambda I)u||=||(A^*-conj(lambda)I)u||; an eigenvector for lambda
is then also an adjoint eigenvector, forcing eigenvectors of distinct
eigenvalues to be orthogonal. No generic covariance kernel is used.

## 4. Exact cone bound with all queried anchors retained

Here is the entire cone argument, so no earlier unverified result is a
proof premise. It applies to any legal queried data with ||x_0||=1 and

  g_i=G_i e+u_i,  G_i>=0, <e,u_i>=0, <u_i,u_j>>=0.

Put X_i=1-sum_(t<i)h_t G_t, W_i=sum_(t<i)h_t u_t, so
x_i=X_i e-W_i and X_i>=X_q. Add the two actual inequalities
Q_(q,i)<=0 and Q_(i,star)<=0 from accepted 1252b8823bb5a290:

  f_q<=<g_q,x_q>+<g_i-g_q,x_i>
                         -||g_i||^2/2-||g_i-g_q||^2/2.   (11)

For i=q the optimum inequality alone gives the same formula.
The transverse part of the first two terms is exactly

  -<u_q,W_q-W_i>-<u_i,W_i><=0.

The transverse contributions of the two squared norms are nonpositive
as well. Choose an actual index i minimizing G_i and write p=G_i>=0.
Then G_q>=p, X_i>=X_q, and X_q<=1-Sp, whence

  2f_q<=2p-(2S+1)p^2-(G_q-p)^2.                          (12)

For b in [0,2], smoothness subtracts b(2-b)||g_q||^2 from (12).
Since G_q>=p>=0, this subtracts at least b(2-b)p^2. Completing the
square in p proves (2), for every interpolant and its free terminal
gradient. No interpolation constraints within the prefix were deleted.

## 5. A concrete legal, nonnormal, positively coupled family

Let m>=128, lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j), and n=2^m-1.
Keep a,c fixed within the horizon, remove the ORIGINAL last d_0 step
from H_m, and retain all queries through q=n-1. Its sum S exceeds 100.
Put

  z_1=(6+2i sqrt(7))/(64S),   z_2=(3+2i sqrt(7))/(64S),
  omega=1.

Both lie in (1), with |z_1|=1/(8S), |z_2|=sqrt(37)/(64S), and their
difference is real positive. Thus the whole coupling class (4a) applies.
The following choice proves it contains actually legal examples with
rho_coup>0, not just formal vectors.

For the base z_1 write alpha=3/(32S), sigma=1/(64S^2), p_i=P_i(z_1).
All factors contract and 7/8<=|p_i|<=1. Define
f_0^base=3alpha/4 and
f_(i+1)^base=f_i^base-h_i sigma(1-alpha h_i/2)|p_i|^2.
Then 7alpha/12<=f_i^base<=3alpha/4, because the decrements total at
most sigma S=alpha/6.

Every base ordered residual, including the optimum, is <=-delta with
delta=alpha sigma/8. Here are the full estimates. For i<j set
T_seg=sum_(i<=s<j)h_s. Telescoping contracting factors gives

  |p_j-p_i|>=(15/16)|z_1|T_seg |p_i|.

The signed area of the closed polygon i,...,j,i is
sigma sum_(i<=s<t<j)h_s h_t Im(conj(p_s)p_t).
Telescoping the subproduct minus its conjugate bounds
|Im(conj(p_s)p_t)|<=|p_i|^2 |Im z_1| T_seg.
Thus |beta Area|<=sigma^2 T_seg^3 |p_i|^2/2.
Subtracting direct-edge work from summed trapezoidal work shows that
the two ordered slacks are
(kappa/2)|p_j-p_i|^2 +/- beta Area. With
kappa>=5alpha/6 and sigma T_seg<=alpha/6, both are at least

  [1125/3072-1/12]alpha sigma T_seg^2|p_i|^2
                              >(alpha sigma/4)T_seg^2|p_i|^2>delta.

The last inequality uses every actual step >1 and |p_i|>=7/8.
The optimum lower slack is >=7alpha/12-sigma/2>alpha/2.
The optimum upper slack is >=alpha[1/64-49/(768S)]>alpha/100>delta.

Put M=exp(S), K=4M^2, K_row=16M^2, and choose

  epsilon=delta/[8(K+delta)], w_1=1-epsilon, w_2=epsilon,
  rho_coup=delta/(8K_row)>0, f_i=(1-epsilon)f_i^base.

Give the second normal block temporary zero values. Since all relevant
|z|<=1, its ordered residuals are <=K. The two normal blocks therefore
have joint residual at most -delta+epsilon(K+delta)=-7delta/8.
For the added unscaled row with position Re(P_i(z_1)-P_i(z_2))
and gradient Re(phi_i(z_1)-phi_i(z_2)), each position
and gradient has magnitude <=2M. With zero temporary values, its
ordered residual is at most K_row. Adding the PSD row contributes at
most rho_coup K_row=delta/8, so EVERY distinct ordered residual obeys

  Q_ij<=-3delta/4<0,                                    (13)

including every optimum pair. All cycles hold on the SAME coupled data.

The actual interpolant in R^5 is explicitly

  H(v)=max_(i in {star,0,...,q})
       {<g_i,x_i>-f_i+<x_i,v-g_i>+||v-g_i||^2/2},
  F(x)=sup_v{<x,v>-H(v)}.

Accepted 1252b8823bb5a290 makes it finite, convex, differentiable and
1-smooth, with F(0)=min F=0 and every queried jet retained.
The chosen initial distance remains exactly one.

## 6. Fixed-function payoff for every real final step

Let Z_test be the orthogonal projection of the first normal block of x_q
onto the line perpendicular to its corresponding queried gradient,
with zero coordinates in the other normal block and in the coupled row.
Then <Z_test,g_q>=0,
||Z_test||^2>=(7/8)(49/64)(7/16)>2/7. Set v_test=alpha Z_test.

For the optimum anchor,
2<x_q,v_test>-||v_test||^2=(2alpha-alpha^2)||Z_test||^2>=alpha/2.
For every finite anchor put y_i=x_i-g_i, delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2.
Here

  ||g_i||^2<=sigma+epsilon M^2+4rho_coup M^2
              <=sigma+delta/16<=2sigma,

and the first-block norm of x_q-y_i is <=(1+1/S)/8<=101/800.
Thus 2delta_i>=49alpha/48-2sigma and

  2delta_i+2<x_q-y_i,v_test>-||v_test||^2
    >=alpha[49/48-1/300-101/400-3/3200]>alpha/2.

Both the extra block and the coupled row have zero inner product with
v_test. Evaluating the same conjugate F at v_test proves

  2F(x_q-b g_q)>=alpha/2=3/(64S)

for EVERY real b, since v_test is orthogonal to g_q. Every actual
anchor, including the optimum, was checked. The true terminal gradient
is unrestricted.

## 7. Exact benchmark normalization and scope

For the actual near-critical word, c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
d_j=1+a c^j, n=2^m-1, and
S=2^m-1+a(c^m-2^m)/(c-2)-d_0. Thus S/lambda^m->e.
The bound (2) includes the original final b=d_0 in [0,2].

The exact recursions of b98bb807d514e80d give C_j=S_circle(j)+1 and
B_j via Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2 and
G(A,B)=2A+B/2+sqrt(B^2+8AB)/2. With rho=log_2lambda,
V(t)=(1+t)^rho-1 has

  d^2/ds^2 log V(exp(s))
   =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)[(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/V(t)^2>0,
  t=exp(s).

Convexity at s,-s gives V(t)V(1/t)>=2, which yields
Omega(A,B)<=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho after substituting
t=(A/B)^(1/rho) and expanding (L-A)(L-B)>=2AB.
Induction gives C_j<=(j+1)^rho; G(A,B)<=4A+B then gives
B_j<=1+4j^rho. Balanced primitive splits and a dominant split with
right length zero also give B_(2^m-1)>=2lambda^(m-1).
Consequently, uniformly over the whole normal and specified coupled
classes and every b in [0,2],

  limsup B_n 2F(x_q-b g_q)<=2/e<1.

The explicit nonnormal R^5 construction, for every real b, satisfies

  liminf B_n 2F(x_q-b g_q)>=3/(32lambda e)>0.

These are exact normalization losses, not a sharp unrestricted profile
claim. No all-b sharpness of the upper bound is asserted.

The unrestricted rank-one coupling is still open: a sufficiently large
unaligned row can have opposite signs at different queries, and the
joint transverse-cone argument then requires additional analysis.
The original all-schedule/all-horizon target remains unproved.

evidence:
# One joint cycle closes fast, intermediate, and slow normal modes together

Status: complete UNVERIFIED candidate. No new fact_submit allocation, solver,
numerical experiment, restart, or worker launch. Accepted inputs:
1252b8823bb5a290 (all prefix interpolation and maximal free completion),
dfde2fa326c908bf (the algebraic complex-cycle identity), and
b98bb807d514e80d (the exact benchmark recursions). Every new estimate used
below is proved here. Earlier unverified spectral findings are not premises.

## 1. Actual word and a whole genuinely joint class

Let m>=2^16, lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j), n=2^m-1.
Parameters a,c remain fixed within the horizon. Remove the ORIGINAL last
d_0 step of H_m to obtain the executed prefix H_m^-, of length q=n-1.
Put S=sum H_m^-, D=d_(m-1), and P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z),
0<=i<=q. The original last displacement is x_q-d_0 g_q.

Allow any finite probability distribution on the union of

  Fast_m = {1-u/m +/- i sqrt(u-theta)/sqrt(m):
                           5<=u<=6, 1/2<=theta<=1},
  Intermediate_m = {z: r=|z|>0, t=Re(z)/r in (0,1/32],
                                          r<=t/(1000d_0)},
  Slow_m = {z: 0<r=|z|<=1/(8S), 1/2<=Re(z)/r<=3/4},

and optionally z=0. Both imaginary signs are allowed. For probability
weights w_z use actual vectors in the orthogonal sum of real planes:

  x_i=(sqrt(w_z) Re P_i(z), sqrt(w_z) Im P_i(z))_z,
  g_i=(sqrt(w_z) Re[zP_i(z)], sqrt(w_z) Im[zP_i(z)])_z.       (1)

Thus ||x_0||=1. Allow arbitrary JOINT values f_i satisfying EVERY ordered
prefix constraint Q_ij<=0, including the optimum jet (0,0,0).
Individual component legality and separability of values are not assumed.
Set tau_m=m/2^28 and C_m=200/49+2/tau_m. For every legal such prefix,
every convex 1-smooth interpolant F with F(0)=min F=0, and every b in [0,2],

  2F(x_q-b g_q) <= max{
      (2+129 C_m/128) 3/(32S),
      (2+6 C_m/5)/(512D)
  }.                                                       (2)

This includes the original b=d_0 and the maximal completion with a free
terminal gradient. Uniformly over all these choices,

  limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) 2F(x_q-b g_q)
                        <=14379/(6272e)<7/8.                (3)

This bounds the displayed union, not all normal spectra or unrestricted
W_n. Sections 7--8 give a definite finite mixture with ALL weights positive
and one fixed interpolant satisfying

  2F(x_q-b g_q)>=3/(64S) for EVERY real b.                    (4)

The new result closes simultaneous repair by the stated intermediate
modes, rather than merely uniting earlier separate class exclusions.

## 2. Uniform physical schedule estimates

For m>=128,

  12/5<c<5/2, 1/3<a<5/12, 0<a/(c-2)<1,
  11/8<=d_0<=3/2, 31/16<=d_1<=2.

Here lambda(lambda-2)=1 gives a/(c-2)<1. The upper c bound follows from
lambda(129/128)<5/2, or sqrt(2)<191/129 after squaring. The a bounds
follow directly; d_0=1+a and d_1=2-1/m give the step bounds.
Counting dyadic multiplicities gives the full-block sum S_j and squared
sum T_j:

  S_j=2^j-1+a(c^j-2^j)/(c-2),
  T_j=2^j-1+2a(c^j-2^j)/(c-2)
                         +a^2(c^(2j)-2^j)/(c^2-2).

Consequently S_j>=[d_j-(c-1)]/(c-2) and S_j<6d_j. For the second bound
use 2^j<=c^j, 1/a<3 and 1/(c-2)<5/2. Whenever d_j>=2000,

  S_j>=(19/10)d_j,
  T_j<=d_j^2/(c^2-2)+2S_j
       <=[25/94+12/2000]d_j^2<(7/25)d_j^2.                 (5)

The T_j bound follows also by subtracting 2S_j from its exact formula.
Here D>2000.

## 3. One actual cycle and its exact recursive defect

For z=alpha+i beta put sigma=|z|^2, kappa=alpha-sigma, and
eta=sigma(1+alpha)-2alpha^2. Let p_j be the polynomial of full H_j
and R_j=p_j(1-d_jz), so p_(j+1)=R_j p_j. Starting locally at 1, set
L_j=sum_(i in H_j)h_i|P_i|^2 and
E_j=sum_(i in H_j)h_i^2 sigma|P_i|^2.

Consider the cycle from the optimum to the end of H_j, backward along
its queries to its start, then to the optimum. Its exact weight is

  Dcal_j=beta^2 L_j-(kappa/2)(1+|p_j|^2+E_j).              (6)

Indeed the backward path area is beta L_j, the optimum edges have zero
area, and the energy is 1+|p_j|^2+E_j. Apply the accepted dfde cycle
identity beta*Area-kappa*Energy/2. Telescoping norms gives
1-|p_j|^2=2alpha L_j-E_j. Thus when alpha>0,

  Dcal_j=[eta/(2alpha)](1+E_j)
                       -[sigma(1-alpha)/(2alpha)]|p_j|^2.

Substitute E_(j+1)=(1+|R_j|^2)E_j+d_j^2 sigma|p_j|^2 and
p_(j+1)=R_jp_j; use
d_j^2 sigma|p_j|^2-|R_j|^2=(2d_j alpha-1)|p_j|^2. This gives

  Dcal_(j+1)=(1+|R_j|^2)Dcal_j
                                +|p_j|^2(kappa+d_j eta).  (7)

The empty-block value is Dcal_0=-kappa. With p_j^-,Dcal_j^- denoting
the same objects after removing the actual last d_0,

  Dcal_j-Dcal_j^-
       =d_0 sigma[1-alpha-d_0 kappa]|p_j^-|^2.             (8)

To check (8), the removed reverse edge has weight
d_0 sigma(1-d_0 alpha+d_0 sigma/2)|p_j^-|^2; the change in the
optimum-to-end edge is (sigma/2)(|p_j|^2-|p_j^-|^2). Their sum is (8).

Use the LAST H_(m-1)^- copy inside H_m^-. Its starting polynomial is
R_(m-1) and its endpoint is P_q=R_(m-1)p_(m-1)^-. Hence JOINT legality
of the SAME indexed, oriented cycle, including the actual optimum, gives

  sum_z w_z |R_(m-1)(z)|^2 Dcal_(m-1)^-(z)<=0.             (9)

All joint values cancel. No cycle or index is chosen separately by mode.

## 4. Repetition amplifies the FAST positive coefficient

For Fast_m, direct expansion gives

  kappa=theta/m-u^2/m^2>0,
  eta=(u-2theta)/m+(u^2+u theta)/m^2-u^3/m^3>=3/m.

Also alpha>=1-6/m and sigma=alpha-kappa<=1. The first block has

  Dcal_1=d_0 eta-kappa|1-d_0z|^2>=3/m,                    (10)

since d_0>=11/8, kappa<=1/m, and |1-d_0z|<3/5. For the last estimate
use |beta|<=1/20, d_0 alpha>1, and
|1-d_0z|<=1/2+3/40<3/5. Thus each fast mode is already individually
illegal on the initial d_0 step.

Write v=z-1 and A_j=1+1/(a c^j). We have A_j<4, Re v<0 and
|v|^2<=6/m, whence |1+A_jv|^2<=1+96/m and
|1+A_jv|<=exp(48/m). The exact product INCLUDING the bridge is

  |R_j|=a(ac)^(2^j-1)
          product_(ell<j)|1+A_ell v|^(2^(j-ell-1))
          |1+A_jv|.

Its last product has total exponent 2^j. Since ac=1-1/m<1, if
2^j<=m/1024, then

  |R_j|<(5/12)exp(3/64)
        <=(5/12)/(1-3/64)=80/183<1/2.                   (11)

The exponential inequality follows by comparing positive power series.

All factors are nonzero since beta!=0. Define Acal_j=Dcal_j/|p_j|^2.
Equation (7) becomes, for j>=1,

  Acal_(j+1)=(1+|R_j|^(-2))Acal_j
                          +(kappa+d_j eta)/|R_j|^2.

It stays positive and nondecreasing at every later level, and grows by
at least 5 at each level satisfying (11). Let
k=floor(log_2(m/1024)). Then k>=1, k<m-1 and 2^k>m/2048.
Since |p_1|<1,

  Acal_(m-1)>=Acal_k>=3*5^(k-1)/m
               >=3*4^(k-1)/m>3m/2^24>=m/2^23.           (12)

The removed last factor obeys |1-d_0z|^2>=1/9, since
d_0 alpha-1>1/3. The subtracted coefficient in (8) is at most 9/m:
sigma<=1, kappa>0, d_0<=3/2 and 1-alpha<=6/m. Therefore

  Dcal_(m-1)^-/|p_(m-1)^-|^2
      >=m/(9*2^23)-9/m>=m/(18*2^23)>=tau_m.              (13)

The middle inequality needs m^2>=162*2^23, which holds for m>=2^16.
Its contribution to (9) is at least tau_m|P_q|^2. This includes every
changed small-step and truncation constant, uniformly in the horizon.

## 5. Intermediate modes and ALL negative credit on the same cycle

For an intermediate mode put t=alpha/r and h_c=2t/r. Then kappa>0,
eta>=sigma(1-2t^2)>0 and h_c>=2000d_0. Call it reached if D>=h_c,
and choose its first d_k>=h_c. All steps of H_k contract, d_k>=2000,
and v=d_kr is in [2t,5t]. By (5) and log(1+x)<=x,

  log|p_k|^2<=-2alpha S_k+sigma T_k
       <=-(19/5)t v+(7/25)v^2<=-6t^2.                  (14)

For the last inequality 19u/5-7u^2/25 is concave on [2,5] with endpoint
values 162/25 and 12, both >=6. Nonzero imaginary parts avoid roots.

A reverse path edge has exact weight

  h sigma(1-h alpha+h sigma/2)|P_i|^2
   =[sigma/(2alpha)](|P_i|^2-|P_(i+1)|^2)
                      +[h^2 sigma eta/(2alpha)]|P_i|^2.

Add the two optimum edges and discard nonnegative terms to obtain

  Dcal_k>=[sigma/(2alpha)](1-|p_k|^2)-alpha
    >=alpha[(1-exp(-6t^2))/(2t^2)-1]>alpha/2.            (15)

The ratio (1-exp(-6s))/s decreases. Even at t^2=1/4 the bracket is
2(1-exp(-3/2))-1>1/2, since
exp(3/2)>1+3/2+9/8+27/48>4. Our t<=1/32 is inside that range.
Since |p_k|<=1 and kappa+d_jeta>0, recursion (7) propagates
Dcal_(m-1)>=(alpha/2)|p_(m-1)|^2.

Furthermore d_0alpha<=t^2/1000<=1/4000 and d_0sigma<=alpha/1000,
so |1-d_0z|^2>=1999/2000. Subtracting (8), with its coefficient at
most d_0sigma, gives

  Dcal_(m-1)^-
    >=alpha(1999/4000-1/1000)|p_(m-1)^-|^2
    >=(49alpha/100)|p_(m-1)^-|^2.                       (16)

radii outside the stated set, notably moderate-angle frequencies with
rS of order one or larger, can change the sign and size of the cycle
coefficient. Nonnormal coupling and the original all-schedule/all-horizon
exact-profile target remain unresolved.


## 10. A broader donor-localization consequence on the same cycle

Slow_m by the ENTIRE complex disk |z|<=R/S, with no sign or angle
restriction, where R>=1/8 may depend on m. Retain Fast_m and the same

  tau_m X_fast+(49/100)Y_reached

       exp(2R) R(1+R^2/2)/S,

every chronological product has modulus <=exp(r times its executed
mass). Let R_start be the polynomial at the start of the selected last
copy. The two optimum-edge squared moduli are each <=exp(2R).

whose sum is <=1, proves (26). The zero mode again contributes zero.

  S X_fast

   ->0.                                                    (27)

Thus the positive fast part of the terminal upper functional (20) is
o(1/S), uniformly for ALL b in [0,2], even when donors have arbitrary
complex arguments and scaled moduli growing as (log m)/4, together with
the full specified intermediate class. This is stronger than a list of
bounded scaled-frequency exclusions.

This does NOT mean that the projected non-fast data remain legal after
discarding the fast blocks, or that their optimal objective is unchanged.
Equation (27) only controls their fast endpoint moment in the SAME joint
legal data and hence its explicitly bounded contribution to (20). It is
not an upper bound on the entire enlarged class or on W_n.

The all-positive construction of Sections 7--8 is already contained in

not their count. Thus every ordered pair and the fixed all-real-b payoff

# Joint covariance and an explicit nonnormal rank-one coupling

Status: complete UNVERIFIED candidate; no routine fact_submit allocation,
numerical solver, or new worker round. Accepted inputs are
1252b8823bb5a290 (interpolation and free completion), dfde2fa326c908bf
(polynomial notation), and b98bb807d514e80d (benchmark recursions).
All new geometry, inequalities, and construction checks appear below.

## 1. Exact whole-class bounds on any retained schedule

Let h_0,...,h_(q-1)>=0 have sum S>0. Let
P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z), 0<=i<=q, and phi_i(z)=zP_i(z).
For ANY finite probability weights w_z at complex parameters satisfying

  Re z>=0,             S|z|<=1/3,                       (1)

form the real orthogonal-block vectors
x_i=(sqrt(w_z)Re P_i(z),sqrt(w_z)Im P_i(z))_z and
g_i=(sqrt(w_z)Re phi_i(z),sqrt(w_z)Im phi_i(z))_z.
Thus x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i and ||x_0||=1.

Assume arbitrary JOINT legal values f_i, including the optimum (0,0,0).
For every interpolating convex 1-smooth F with minimum zero, and every
genuinely free terminal step b in [0,2],

  2F(x_q-b g_q)<=1/[2S+1+b(2-b)].                        (2)

The statement is about all weights and all joint values; it does not infer
legality of the separate modes. A reflected complex block has the same
Gram data and fixes the initial direction. Thus we may take Im z>=0
independently in each normal block when proving this theorem.

There is also a specific nonnormal extension. Take TWO different parameters
z_1,z_2 with Re z_l,Im z_l>=0 and S|z_l|<=1/3, and weights w_1,w_2>0
with sum one. Take
a complex number omega with |omega|=1, and rho_coup>=0. Append the coordinate

  x_i^(5)=sqrt(rho_coup) Re[omega(P_i(z_1)-P_i(z_2))],
  g_i^(5)=sqrt(rho_coup) Re[omega(phi_i(z_1)-phi_i(z_2))]   (3)

to the four normal coordinates. It starts at zero, so ||x_0||=1 exactly.
The same bound (2) holds for EVERY jointly legal prefix of these actual
five-dimensional vectors under either of the following conditions:

  (a) omega(z_1-z_2)>0 is real; rho_coup is arbitrary, or
  (b) rho_coup<=w_1 w_2/144; omega is arbitrary.             (4)

These are whole coupling classes, with no bound on the conditioning in (a).
At the smaller radius S|z_l|<=1/4, condition (b) improves to

  rho_coup<=(449/256)w_1w_2.                              (5)

Only this explicit finite-dimensional rank-one coupling is claimed;
arbitrary cross-mode covariance is not being reparameterized.

## 2. Divided differences and a finite covariance identity

Work in the convex quarter disk Re z,Im z>=0, |z|S<=R. For every factor,

  |1-hz|^2=1-2h Re z+h^2|z|^2<=exp(h^2|z|^2).

All prefix products and products omitting any factors therefore have
modulus <=exp(R^2/2), since sum h^2<=S^2. Telescoping P_i-1 and
differentiating its product give

  |P_i-1|<=|z|S exp(R^2/2),
  |zP_i'|<=|z|S exp(R^2/2),
  |phi_i'-1|<=2R exp(R^2/2).                             (6)

For R=1/3, exp(1/18)<=18/17 by positive power series comparison.
Thus all derivatives lie in the disk centered at 1 of radius
d=12/17<1/sqrt(2). For R=1/4 one may instead take d=16/31.

For any two distinct z,v in the quarter disk, define
a_i(z,v)=[phi_i(z)-phi_i(v)]/(z-v). Integrating phi_i' along the straight
segment between them shows |a_i-1|<=d. A complex number a in this disk
has positive real part and |arg a|<=arcsin d. Indeed
2Re a>=|a|^2+1-d^2>=2|a|sqrt(1-d^2).
Consequently, for every i,j and every z,v,

  Re[(phi_i(z)-phi_i(v))conj(phi_j(z)-phi_j(v))]
   >=(1-2d^2)|z-v|^2 |a_i(z,v)||a_j(z,v)|>=0.             (7)

The coincident-parameter case is zero. At R=1/3, 1-2d^2=1/289.

We also need the signs of the means, not just covariance. Write nonzero
z=r exp(i theta), 0<=theta<=pi/2. Since hr<=R<=1/3, each factor
has positive real part. Its negative argument is
atan(h r sin theta/(1-h r cos theta)). The sum of these arguments is at most

  rS sin theta/(1-rS cos theta)
      <=[R/(1-R)]theta<=theta/2.

Thus arg phi_i(z) lies in [theta/2,theta]; both Re phi_i(z) and
Im phi_i(z) are nonnegative. The zero parameter is immediate.

Let expectation denote the finite weighted sum and put mu_i=E phi_i.
A direct expansion, with z,v independent under the same weights, gives

  Re[E(phi_i conj(phi_j))-mu_i conj(mu_j)]
   =(1/2)E_(z,v) Re[(phi_i(z)-phi_i(v))
                                conj(phi_j(z)-phi_j(v))]>=0.  (8)

Set e=x_0, G_i=<e,g_i>=Re mu_i, u_i=g_i-G_i e. Then G_i>=0 and

  <u_i,u_j>
    =Re[E(phi_i conj(phi_j))-mu_i conj(mu_j)]
                                  +(Im mu_i)(Im mu_j)>=0. (9)

This establishes one joint cone directly from the probability law. It is
not the union of separate single-mode legality statements.

## 3. The explicit PSD rank-one coupling

In real coordinates y=(y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4), let
v=(Re omega,-Im omega,-Re omega,Im omega). The map T:R^4->R^5 is

  T y=(sqrt(w_1)y_1,sqrt(w_1)y_2,
       sqrt(w_2)y_3,sqrt(w_2)y_4,sqrt(rho_coup)<v,y>).

Its Gram metric is exactly

  T^T T=diag(w_1,w_1,w_2,w_2)+rho_coup vv^T,

which is real positive definite for w_1,w_2>0. Formula (3) is precisely
T applied to the two polynomial blocks, so it gives actual vectors and
a fixed linear realization. The fifth coordinate of e=x_0 is zero.
It does not change G_i; it adds rho_coup U_i U_j to (9), where

  U_i=Re[omega(phi_i(z_1)-phi_i(z_2))].

Under (4a), U_i=|z_1-z_2| Re a_i(z_1,z_2)>0, so the cone is preserved
for every rho_coup>=0.

For arbitrary orientation, put A=phi_i(z_1)-phi_i(z_2) and
B=phi_j(z_1)-phi_j(z_2). The elementary identity

  Re(omega A) Re(omega B)
    =(Re(A conj B)+Re(omega^2 A B))/2
    >=(Re(A conj B)-|A||B|)/2
    >=-d^2 |A||B|

follows from (7). The two-point covariance term in (8) equals
w_1w_2 Re(A conj B), which is at least
w_1w_2(1-2d^2)|A||B|. The imaginary-mean term is nonnegative.
Thus every transverse pair remains nonnegative whenever

  rho_coup <= [(1-2d^2)/d^2] w_1w_2.                    (10)

On R^5 set A_coup=T Z (T^T T)^(-1)T^T, zero on the orthogonal complement

not normal. To justify that implication directly, normality gives
||(A-lambda I)u||=||(A^*-conj(lambda)I)u||; an eigenvector for lambda
is then also an adjoint eigenvector, forcing eigenvectors of distinct
eigenvalues to be orthogonal. No generic covariance kernel is used.

1-smooth, with F(0)=min F=0 and every queried jet retained.
The chosen initial distance remains exactly one.

## 6. Fixed-function payoff for every real final step

Let Z_test be the orthogonal projection of the first normal block of x_q
onto the line perpendicular to its corresponding queried gradient,
with zero coordinates in the other normal block and in the coupled row.
Then <Z_test,g_q>=0,
||Z_test||^2>=(7/8)(49/64)(7/16)>2/7. Set v_test=alpha Z_test.

For the optimum anchor,
2<x_q,v_test>-||v_test||^2=(2alpha-alpha^2)||Z_test||^2>=alpha/2.
For every finite anchor put y_i=x_i-g_i, delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2.
Here

  ||g_i||^2<=sigma+epsilon M^2+4rho_coup M^2
              <=sigma+delta/16<=2sigma,

and the first-block norm of x_q-y_i is <=(1+1/S)/8<=101/800.
Thus 2delta_i>=49alpha/48-2sigma and

  2delta_i+2<x_q-y_i,v_test>-||v_test||^2
    >=alpha[49/48-1/300-101/400-3/3200]>alpha/2.

Both the extra block and the coupled row have zero inner product with
v_test. Evaluating the same conjugate F at v_test proves

  2F(x_q-b g_q)>=alpha/2=3/(64S)

for EVERY real b, since v_test is orthogonal to g_q. Every actual
anchor, including the optimum, was checked. The true terminal gradient
is unrestricted.

## 7. Exact benchmark normalization and scope

For the actual near-critical word, c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
d_j=1+a c^j, n=2^m-1, and
S=2^m-1+a(c^m-2^m)/(c-2)-d_0. Thus S/lambda^m->e.
The bound (2) includes the original final b=d_0 in [0,2].

The exact recursions of b98bb807d514e80d give C_j=S_circle(j)+1 and
B_j via Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2 and
G(A,B)=2A+B/2+sqrt(B^2+8AB)/2. With rho=log_2lambda,
V(t)=(1+t)^rho-1 has

  d^2/ds^2 log V(exp(s))
   =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)[(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/V(t)^2>0,
  t=exp(s).

Convexity at s,-s gives V(t)V(1/t)>=2, which yields
Omega(A,B)<=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho after substituting
t=(A/B)^(1/rho) and expanding (L-A)(L-B)>=2AB.
Induction gives C_j<=(j+1)^rho; G(A,B)<=4A+B then gives
B_j<=1+4j^rho. Balanced primitive splits and a dominant split with
right length zero also give B_(2^m-1)>=2lambda^(m-1).
Consequently, uniformly over the whole normal and specified coupled
classes and every b in [0,2],

  limsup B_n 2F(x_q-b g_q)<=2/e<1.

The explicit nonnormal R^5 construction, for every real b, satisfies

  liminf B_n 2F(x_q-b g_q)>=3/(32lambda e)>0.

These are exact normalization losses, not a sharp unrestricted profile
claim. No all-b sharpness of the upper bound is asserted.

The unrestricted rank-one coupling is still open: a sufficiently large
unaligned row can have opposite signs at different queries, and the
joint transverse-cone argument then requires additional analysis.
The original all-schedule/all-horizon target remains unproved.


## 8. A second complete model: sign reversal with arbitrary coupling strength

The alignment hypothesis cannot be diagnosed by looking only at the sign
of the added coordinate. Here is a different whole two-block model, whose
added queried gradients DO change sign when rho_coup>0, but whose full joint legality
still implies (2) for every coupling amplitude.

Let all retained h_i be positive, their sum S>=100, and their last entry
h_(q-1)<=2. Put

  z_1=(1+i)/(10S), z_2=(2+i)/(10S), w_1=w_2=1/2,
  Omega_proj=-1/10+i.

Append the coordinate sqrt(rho_coup) Re[Omega_proj(P_i(z_1)-P_i(z_2))]
and its corresponding gradient coordinate, for arbitrary rho_coup>=0.
This is (3) with a nonunit projection; equivalently replace omega by
Omega_proj/|Omega_proj| and multiply the amplitude by |Omega_proj|^2.
The explicit PSD realization of Section 3 applies unchanged.

For EVERY jointly legal prefix of these vectors, and every b in [0,2],

  2F(x_q-b g_q)<=1/[2S+1+b(2-b)].                        (14)

There is no amplitude or conditioning bound. We prove (14) by deriving
the joint cone from the actual adjacent interpolation constraints.

Write zeta_1=(1+i)/10, zeta_2=(2+i)/10 and tau_i=sum_(t<i)h_t/S.
Let e_k(i) be the k-th elementary symmetric polynomial of the nonnegative
numbers h_t/S, t<i, with e_0=1 and e_k=0 above their count.
Then e_1=tau_i and 0<=e_k<=tau_i^k/k!<=1/k!.
Define Hom_k=sum_(l=0)^k zeta_1^(k-l)zeta_2^l and
q_k=Re(Omega_proj Hom_k). Direct multiplication gives

  q_0=-1/10, q_1=-23/100, q_2=-47/500, q_3=-237/10000.    (15)

If U_i is the unscaled added gradient and B_i is the unscaled added
coordinate of A_coup g_i, polynomial subtraction gives EXACTLY

  U_i=-(1/(10S)) sum_(k>=0)(-1)^k e_k(i)q_k,
  B_i=-(1/(10S^2)) sum_(k>=0)(-1)^k e_k(i)q_(k+1),
  U_(i+1)=U_i-h_i B_i.                                   (16)

These sums are finite. Since |zeta_l|<1/4 and |Omega_proj|<101/100,
|q_k|<=(101/100)(k+1)4^(-k).

In the second sum of (16), the tail after k=2 has absolute value <1/250.
Indeed its first majorant is (101/100)*5/1536, and each subsequent
term is at most 3/40 times its predecessor. Together with (15) and
0<=tau_i<=1, e_2<=1/2, this proves

  -1/4 < sum_(k>=0)(-1)^k e_k q_(k+1) < -13/100,
  13/(1000S^2)<B_i<1/(40S^2).                            (17)

For the first sum of (16), the tail after k=3 has absolute value <1/1000:
its first majorant is (101/100)*5/6144 and later ratios are <=3/50.
The k=3 term is nonnegative. If tau_i>=49/50, (15) gives

  sum_(k>=0)(-1)^k e_k q_k
    >=-1/10+(23/100)(49/50)-(47/500)/2-1/1000
    >3/40,
  U_i<-3/(400S).                                        (18)

Thus U_i decreases strictly from U_0=1/(100S) and is negative at q-1
and q, since tau_(q-1)>=1-2/S>=49/50. This is an actual sign reversal,
for every prescribed retained schedule in the stated class.

We next bound the transverse covariance of the two NORMAL blocks alone.
Their factors contract, since h|z_l|<=|zeta_l|<1/4<2Re(zeta_l)/|zeta_l|.
The finite expansion
phi_i(z_l)=S^(-1)sum_k(-1)^k e_k zeta_l^(k+1) shows

  Im phi_i(z_1)>=(1/S)(1/10-1/50-1/1440),
  Im phi_i(z_2)>=(1/S)(1/10-1/25-1/1440).

Here the k=2 terms have nonnegative imaginary parts; the remaining
tail is bounded by (1/1536)/(1-1/16)=1/1440.
Their mean imaginary part is consequently >=69/(1000S).

At radius 1/4, Section 2 gives d=16/31, Re(a_i conj(a_j))>=
(449/961)|a_i||a_j| and |a_i|>=15/31 for divided differences.
Since |z_1-z_2|=1/(10S), the two-point covariance in (8) is at least

  [449*225/(4*961^2*100)]/S^2 > 1/(4000S^2).

Adding the imaginary means as in (9), the two normal blocks therefore
have, for EVERY i,j, transverse inner product

  >[(69/1000)^2+1/4000]/S^2>1/(200S^2).                  (19)

Now apply the ACTUAL ordered pair constraints between i and i+1,
for each i<q. Their sum gives
<g_i,A_coup g_i>>=||A_coup g_i||^2>=0, because h_i>0.
The normal contribution is at most

  (1/2)sum_l Re(z_l)|z_l|^2|P_i(z_l)|^2<=3/(500S^3).

Consequently if U_i<0, the positive B_i from (17) satisfies

  rho_coup |U_i| B_i <=3/(500S^3).                      (20)

This is joint legality, including the added row; no scalar row is assumed
legal by itself.

If U_i U_j>=0, the coupled row cannot hurt (19). Otherwise take i<j,
so 0<U_i<=1/(100S) and U_j<0. If j<q, (17),(20) give

  rho_coup U_i|U_j| <=3/(650S^2).

For j=q use (20) at q-1. Equations (17)--(18) and h_(q-1)<=2 give

  |U_q|/|U_(q-1)|
      <=1+[2/(40S^2)]/[3/(400S)]
      <=16/15.

Thus in EVERY case the magnitude of a negative added pair contribution
is <=8/(1625S^2). Combining with (19),

  <u_i,u_j> >= [1/200-8/1625]/S^2=1/(13000S^2)>0.         (21)

The initial-direction projections remain nonnegative by Section 2.
The fully reproduced cone proof in Section 4 now proves (14).
The sign reversal by itself does not evade the common interpolation
constraints, even at arbitrarily large proposed amplitude.

## 9. A legal realization of the sign-reversing model and its payoff

Apply Section 8 to the actual retained near-critical word. Its last
executed step is d_1=2-1/m<2, and every retained step exceeds one.
Here is an explicit positive rho_coup and one fixed interpolant.

For each of the two NORMAL modes of Section 8 define alpha_l=Re z_l,
sigma_l=|z_l|^2, p_i,l=P_i(z_l), and values

  f_0,l=alpha_l/2,
  f_(i+1),l=f_i,l-h_i sigma_l(1-alpha_l h_i/2)|p_i,l|^2.

Their factors contract and |p_i,l|>=3/4. Since
sigma_l S<=alpha_l/4,
alpha_l/4<=f_i,l<=alpha_l/2.
Each has every ordered residual <=-delta, for
delta=1/(4000S^3). We provide the checks instead of imposing legality.

For an interval of mass T_seg, telescoping gives the chord lower bound
(7/8)|z_l|T_seg|p_i,l|. The same polygon identity used in Section 5
gives |beta_l Area|<=sigma_l^2 T_seg^3|p_i,l|^2/2.
Here kappa_l>=99alpha_l/100 and sigma_l T_seg<=alpha_l/4.
Thus either ordered pair slack is at least

  [(99/200)(49/64)-1/8]alpha_l sigma_l T_seg^2|p_i,l|^2
       >(alpha_l sigma_l/4)T_seg^2|p_i,l|^2
       >=alpha_l sigma_l/8>=delta.

The last step uses T_seg>1 and |p_i,l|>=3/4.
The optimum lower slack is >=alpha_l/4-sigma_l/2>alpha_l/5.
The upper slack is >=
(alpha_l-sigma_l/2)(9/16)-alpha_l/2>alpha_l/20>delta.

Use their equal weighted values f_i=(f_i,1+f_i,2)/2.
Let M=exp(S) and choose rho_coup=delta/(128M^2)>0.
For the unscaled added row, each position and gradient has magnitude
at most 4M, so every ordered zero-value residual is at most64M^2.
Adding it to the two normal blocks yields Q_ij<=-delta/2 for EVERY
distinct finite or optimum ordered pair. The explicit conjugate
interpolant from Section 5 is therefore legal on R^5.
It is nonnormal by the distinct-eigenvector argument in Section 3:
for this projection their inner product is -rho_coup|Omega_proj|^2!=0.
Its added gradient actually changes sign by (16)--(18).

For an all-final-step payoff let Z_test be the projection of the first
normal block of x_q perpendicular to its first-block gradient, with
zero coordinates in the second block and in the coupled row. Then

  <Z_test,g_q>=0, ||Z_test||^2>=(1/2)(9/16)(1/2)=9/64.

Take v_test=Z_test/(20S). The optimum anchor yields
2<x_q,v_test>-||v_test||^2>=(39/(400S))(9/64)>1/(100S).

For every finite anchor y_i=x_i-g_i, delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2,
we have f_i>=3/(80S), ||g_i||^2<=1/(20S^2), and the first-block norm
of x_q-y_i is <=(1+1/S)/10<=101/1000. Hence

  2delta_i+2<x_q-y_i,v_test>-||v_test||^2
    >=3/(40S)-1/(20S^2)-101/(10000S)-1/(400S^2)
    >1/(100S).

These inequalities check every actual anchor, including the optimum.
The same conjugate evaluation as Section 6 proves for the SAME fixed F

  2F(x_q-b g_q)>=1/(100S) for EVERY real b.                (22)

Thus the whole arbitrary-amplitude sign-reversing model has the exact
upper cap (14), while it has a fully legal positive-coupling construction
of benchmark order. On the actual near-critical word its limsup ratio
is <=2/e for b in [0,2], and the constructed all-real-b liminf ratio is
>=1/(50lambda e)>0. No conclusion about all unaligned couplings follows.

claim: C49 covers arbitrary nonnegative forward-incidence graphs with a sparse set of positive older-history correlations: no rank, memory, degree or adjacent-correlation restriction. For m>=512,N>=128, if at most Jbad<=N/128 high phases have <X_i,p_(i+1)><0, EVERY legal member and full terminal completion has score_free/K<7 exp(-N/32)<7/16 and limsup B_n score_free<=7/(8e)<1. evidence:
# C49. Sparse high-history violations cannot rescue any positive flow

Status: UNVERIFIED joint candidate. No verifier or numerical computation.
Every argument is included internally; earlier candidates are motivation
only, not correctness premises.

For the near-critical ruler, m>=512 and N>=128, let Jbad count high phases
where the next low gradient is positively correlated with the entire
strictly older weighted gradient sum. For arbitrary nonnegative forward
incidence, every legal member and every full terminal completion satisfy

    score_free/K<7 exp(-N/32)<7/16 when Jbad<=N/128.

Consequently limsup B_(2^m-1)*score_free<=7/(8e)<1 in that range.
If N grows and Jbad=o(N), the normalized benchmark payoff tends to zero.
There is no rank, memory, degree, or adjacent-correlation restriction.

## 1. Real geometry, all normal tests, and the history count

Set lambda=1+sqrt(F2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j). Fix 0<=r<=m-7, let
k=m-r, N=2^k, M=1+sum H_r, q=a c^r/M, A=1+q, and put

 q_i=q c^(nu_2(i+1)), tau_i=1+q_i, T_i=M tau_i, i<N-1,
 tau_(N-1)=t>=1, T_(N-1)=Mt.

The symbol nu_2 denotes binary valuation. The N ordinary phases are exactly
the physical H_r copies, with mass M-1; each nonfinal phase is followed by
the actual checkpoint1+Mq_i.

Choose arbitrary transfers a_ij>=0 for i<j and masses

    R_0>0, R_j=sum_(i<j)a_ij>0 for j>=1, E_i=R_i^2.

In the real space R^N with standard orthonormal basis define

 p_i=(R_i e_i-sum_(j>i)a_ij e_j)/T_i,
 C=conv(0,p_0,...,p_(N-1)),
 F_C(x)=max_(p in C)(<x,p>-||p||^2/2).

Its gradient is Euclidean projection onto C, by the projection variational
inequality and maximizing-difference inequalities. That projection is
nonexpansive; thus F_C is convex and1-smooth.

For i>=0 and j>i put r_j^(i)=sum_(l<i)a_lj, an actual inherited coordinate
mass. The exact phase state is

    X_i=R_i e_i+sum_(j>i)r_j^(i)e_j,

where the root sum vanishes. Subtracting T_i p_i exhausts coordinate i and
creates X_(i+1); every individual physical step is retained.

Define

 V_i=E_i-sum_(j>i)a_ij r_j^(i),
 C_i=sum_(j>i)a_ij[r_j^(i)+a_ij],
 Delta_ij=a_ij R_j-sum_(l>j)a_il a_jl, i<j.               (F1)

Direct expansion gives

    Delta_ij=-T_i T_j <p_i,p_j>.                         (F2)

For the complete normal test put z=(ordinary partial mass+1)/M in[1/M,1].
Multiplying all normal values by M, the own value is

    [(tau_i-z)V_i-z C_i]/tau_i^2,                        (F3)

and a future-j value is

    [sum_(l<i)Delta_lj+(z/tau_i)Delta_ij]/tau_j.           (F4)

Past normal values are nonpositive since their positive coordinates have
been exhausted and all remaining proximal coordinates are nonnegative.
Comparing(F3) with zero and EVERY(F4) at BOTH z=1/M and z=1 is necessary
and sufficient for all actual queries. All differences are affine. At the
last phase t>=1 suffices because there is no outgoing transfer or future
normal. This keeps the full old-query and future-query test explicit.

Every legal nonterminal phase has

    q_i V_i>=C_i>=0.                                    (F5)

In fact V_i>0: if C_i>0 use(F5); if C_i=0 all outgoing transfers vanish
and V_i=E_i>0. At the terminal phase V_(N-1)=E_(N-1)>0.

For every high phase i (odd i with1<=i<=N-3), define

 F_i=sum_(l<i)Delta_(l,i+1), G_i=Delta_(i,i+1).
 Call the phase exceptional when F_i<0. Let Jbad be their number
 and let Lbad=sum_(exceptional i)nu_2(i+1).              (F6)

No correlation-sign condition is imposed. At nonexceptional high phases
F_i>=0; all adjacent correlations and all low-phase correlations remain
arbitrary. By(F2), exceptionality means positive correlation of the next
low gradient with the entire strictly older weighted gradient sum.

The class is nonempty. For example take only root-to-later transfers
a_0j=R_j and no outgoing transfers from j>=1. Set E_(N-1)=1, then choose
E_i backward large enough that
q_i E_i/tau_i^2>=max_(j>i) E_j/tau_j. Finally choose
qE_0>=sum_(j>=1)E_j+A max_(j>=1)E_j/tau_j.
These give every endpoint normal above, and they have no exceptional high phase.

Every original queried value is <x,p_i>-||p_i||^2/2. The polar inequalities
<p_i,z><=0 imply backward that every coordinate of z is nonpositive.
Consequently0 is the actual closest minimizer to R_0e_0, with distance R_0.
Writing htot=sum H_m, the original objective and primitive defect are

 score_C=(2Mt-2M+1)E_(N-1)/(M^2t^2E_0),
 V/E_0=1-[(Mt-(M-1)+htot)/(Mt)]^2 E_(N-1)/E_0.            (F7)

Here V without a subscript is the project primitive defect; V_i in(F1)
is the phase energy numerator. Formula(F7) follows from the terminal state
and the exact identity
2hF+h(1-h)||g||^2=||x||^2-||x-hg||^2 along the original trajectory.

## 2. Low phases and nonexceptional high phases

Set Z_i=V_i/tau_i>0. At the final phase Z_(N-1)=E_(N-1)/t.
By direct summation in(F1),

    F_i+G_i=V_(i+1).                                    (F8)

The current squared-transfer cost also satisfies

 C_i>=a_(i,i+1)R_(i+1)>=Delta_(i,i+1)=G_i,                (F9)

because R_(i+1)=r_(i+1)^(i)+a_(i,i+1) and all products omitted from
C_i are nonnegative; the second inequality discards the shared-tail sum
subtracted in Delta.

The endpoint future-i+1 comparison(F3)-(F4), together with
C_i>=max(0,G_i), gives

 q_i V_i >=[tau_i^2 V_(i+1)-tau_i q_i G_i
                              +tau_(i+1)max(0,G_i)]/tau_(i+1).   (F9a)

If G_i<=0, the two extra terms are nonnegative. Thus

    Z_(i+1)/Z_i<=q_i/tau_i.                             (F10a)

If G_i>=0, the extra coefficient of G_i in(F9a) is
Delta_cap=tau_(i+1)-tau_i q_i.
At a LOW phase tau_i=A and Delta_cap>=1-Aq>0, so(F10a)
holds for arbitrary F_i and G_i, without ANY correlation-sign condition.

At a HIGH phase tau_i=B=1+Q and tau_(i+1)=A, one has
Delta_cap=A-BQ<0. If this high phase is nonexceptional, definition(F6) gives
G_i<=F_i+G_i=V_(i+1). Multiplication by the negative Delta_cap
therefore bounds the right side of(F9a) below by
[B^2+A-BQ]V_(i+1)/A=(A+B)V_(i+1)/A. Consequently

    Z_(i+1)/Z_i<=q_i tau_i/(tau_i+tau_(i+1)).            (F10b)

The elementary parameter signs Aq<1 and BQ>A are established below.
When G_i<=0 at a high phase, (F10a) is stronger since BQ>A.
Thus at every low phase and every NONEXCEPTIONAL high phase,

 Z_(i+1)/Z_i
 <=max(q_i/tau_i, q_i tau_i/(tau_i+tau_(i+1))).           (F10)

No adjacent-correlation sign is required, and no low-phase sign is required.

At the root, V_1=Delta_01>0, while
C_0=sum_(j>0)a_0j^2>=R_1^2>=Delta_01.
Its endpoint comparison with phase1 therefore gives

    Z_1/E_0<=q/(A+tau_1).                                (F11)

No factorization, finite memory, or scalar common direction was used.
This argument is used only at the nonexceptional high phases. We next
bound every exceptional phase without any sign assumption.

## 3. A universal bound for every exceptional high phase

For every phase let ||p_i|| be the actual Euclidean gradient norm.
The definitions in Section1 give

 M^2||p_i||^2=(V_i+C_i)/tau_i^2.

At a nonterminal phase(F5) gives C_i<=q_i V_i; nonnegative transfers
give V_i<=E_i<=M^2 tau_i^2||p_i||^2. At the terminal phase these estimates
follow directly from its one-coordinate vector. Hence

    M^2||p_i||^2<=Z_i<=tau_i M^2||p_i||^2.              (P1)

Compare the endpoints of two adjacent ordinary blocks in the ORIGINAL
fixed function F_C. They are

 y_i=X_i-(M-1)p_i,
 y_(i+1)=X_i-M tau_i p_i-(M-1)p_(i+1).

Their gradients are p_i,p_(i+1), including the prescribed old terminal
gradient if this is the last block. Projection variational inequalities
give firm nonexpansiveness directly: for p=P_C(x),r=P_C(y),
<x-p,r-p><=0 and <y-r,p-r><=0 imply
<x-y,p-r>>=||p-r||^2.
Apply this to y_i,y_(i+1). Their difference is
(Mq_i+1)p_i+(M-1)p_(i+1). Expansion and division by M gives

 ||p_(i+1)||^2
 <=q_i||p_i||^2+(1-q_i)<p_i,p_(i+1)>.                   (P2)

If q_i>=1, Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the right side by
q_i||p_i||^2+(q_i-1)||p_i||||p_(i+1)||. Setting
r=||p_(i+1)||/||p_i|| yields (r-q_i)(r+1)<=0.
If q_i<=1 the corresponding inequality is (r-1)(r+q_i)<=0.
Thus universally

    ||p_(i+1)||<=max(1,q_i)||p_i||.                     (P3)

The normals are nonzero by their positive diagonal.
At every high phase Q=q_i>=99/100 one must be careful: Q may be
slightly BELOW1. The universal bound is therefore max(1,Q), not Q.
To account for this, put Qhat=max(1,Q). Since Q>=1-1/m,
Qhat/Q<=m/(m-1)<=512/511 for m>=512.

Using(P1)-(P3) and tau_(i+1)=A gives

    Z_(i+1)<=A Qhat^2 Z_i.                              (P4)

Relative to the nonexceptional factor QB/(A+B), B=1+Q, this costs at most

 A Qhat^2(A+B)/(QB)
  =Aq(1+A/B)(Qhat/Q)^2 c^ell
  <=kappa c^ell,  kappa=9/8, ell=nu_2(i+1).             (P5)

For an explicit rational check use
Aq(1+A/B)<220731/203776, as q<7/16,A<23/16,B>=199/100.
Multiplying by(512/511)^2 still gives a number below9/8:
8*220731*512^2 <9*203776*511^2.

memory, parent counts, edge weights, and exceptional correlation sizes.

rho_s=log_2(lambda). Put F(z)=(1+z)^rho_s-1. The second derivative
