Every graph edge is nonnegative, but no gradient-correlation sign is
assumed globally. Every old/future normal and every original physical
step is retained. The bounds cover full terminal completion and its true
closest-minimizer distance, including the unqueried-terminal-gradient
case r=0. The gradient bound(P2) was used only for the original realized
function; the completion's last gradient was never fixed.

An escaping positive-flow family with N tending to infinity therefore
requires exceptional older-history correlation at a positive density
of high phases. A finite or sublinear set of unusually strong merges
cannot suffice. A dense set is only a necessary condition, not a useful
witness or a sufficiency claim.

The statement still concerns the defined positive triangular incidence
geometry. Dense exceptional histories, signed transfers, reactivated
coordinates and varying gradients within an ordinary block remain open.
It is not an unrestricted W upper bound and does not settle the project's
original exact-profile target.

# C51: a full exact H3 certificate and explicit Huber certificate coordinates

Status: complete candidate proof, **not verifier-accepted**. No new verifier
allocation and no additional optimization call. The only mathematical
predecessor is accepted fact `1252b8823bb5a290`. The numerical solve guided the
choice of rational coefficients; its values, eigenvalues and inferred
multipliers are not proof premises.

This supplies a concrete full-objective certificate for the actual m=3
schedule. It does not prove a growing-horizon certificate or resolve the
original exact-profile problem.

## 1. A lossless parameterization at the Huber value

Fix n>=1 and any nonnegative schedule h=(h0,...,h_(n-1)) with sum S>0.
Set P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t for 0<=i<=n, h_n=0, and tau=1/(2S+1).
Use the independent formal vectors (x0,g0,...,gn), the GD identities
xi=x0-sum_(t<i)h_t gt, and all ordered interpolation residuals

    Qij=fi-fj+<gi,xj-xi>+||gi-gj||^2/2,

with the optimum jet equal to zero. Every legal trajectory satisfies Qij<=0
by fact1252b8823bb5a290.

Choose an arbitrary array r_ij>=0 for 0<=i<n and 0<=j<=n, j!=i, and set
r_ii=0. These are all finite multipliers whose source is a queried prefix
sample; there is no support restriction among them. Define

    mu_i = [2h_i+sum_(j=0)^n r_ij(P_i-P_j)]/(2S-P_i),  i<n,             (1)
    mu_n = 2-sum_(i<n)mu_i,
    beta_i=mu_i+sum_(j=0)^n r_ij-sum_(k<n)r_ki,          i<n.            (2)

The denominators in (1) are positive, since 2S-P_i>=S>0. Define the
complete multiplier array by

    lambda_(star,i)=0,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i,                 0<=i<=n,
    lambda_ij=r_ij,                      0<=i<n, j finite, j!=i,
    lambda_(n,i)=beta_i,                 0<=i<n.                       (3)

For the moment mu and beta may have either sign. Their eventual
nonnegativity will be checked explicitly.

Let e_i be the standard basis of the real space of dimension n+1, indexed 0,...,n. Put

    p_i=sum_(t<i)h_t e_t,
    v_ij=p_i-p_j,
    A_i*= e_i e_i^T/2+(e_i p_i^T+p_i e_i^T)/2,
    A_ij=(e_i v_ij^T+v_ij e_i^T)/2
                           +(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^T/2,
    A=sum_i mu_i A_i*+sum_(i!=j finite)lambda_ij A_ij,
    M=[[tau,-mu^T/2],[-mu/2,A]],
    Z_hub=A-mu mu^T/(4tau),
    K_hub=Z_hub restricted to rows/columns 0,...,n-1.                          (4)

All matrices in (4) are full formal coefficient matrices, not restrictions
to a recovered primal trajectory. The exact identity is

    tau||x0||^2-2fn+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Qij
                       =(x0,g0,...,gn)^T M (x0,g0,...,gn).             (5)

Here vector-valued quadratic notation means the corresponding sum of
inner products in any finite-dimensional real Euclidean space.

The sufficient and necessary certificate tests in these coordinates are

         r_ij>=0,  mu_i>=0,  beta_i>=0,  K_hub>=0.                        (6)

More precisely, (6) is equivalent to existence of this full certificate,
and every full certificate at level tau is represented by some r.

### Proof of the identity and the nullspace condition

At a prefix finite node i<n, equation (2) makes outgoing minus incoming
flow zero. At n it is

    mu_n+sum_i beta_i-sum_i r_(i,n)
      =sum_i mu_i=2.

Thus every fi coefficient in (5) cancels. Expanding each Q gives exactly
the matrices in (4), including the initial-vector cross coefficient
-mu_i/2. This proves (5).

Let 1 denote the all-ones vector of length n+1, and define the finite drift
d_i=sum_(j finite)lambda_ij(P_i-P_j). Directly from (4) and the value flow,

              2(A1)_i=2h_i+(1+P_i)mu_i+d_i.                          (7)

For a detailed derivation, the term e_i v_ij^T+v_ij e_i^T contributes
lambda_ij(P_i-P_j) to coordinate i and
h_k lambda_ij(1_(k<i)-1_(k<j)) to coordinate k. The difference-square
term annihilates 1. For k<n, summing the latter cut term over all finite
edges gives h_k[2-sum_(i>k)mu_i] by finite value flow. The star terms
contribute (1+P_k)mu_k+h_k sum_(i>k)mu_i. The two tail sums cancel.
For k=n both cut terms vanish and h_n=0. This establishes (7) for all k.

For i<n, equations (1) and (7) imply

              (A1)_i=mu_i/(2tau).                                    (8)

Also sum_i mu_i=2, so the x0 row of M annihilates
v_H=(1,tau,...,tau).

To establish the last gradient row without assuming it, use the exact
Huber jets

    x0=1, xi=1-tau P_i, gi=tau,
    fi=tau xi-tau^2/2, f_star=g_star=x_star=0.                         (9)

They are the GD trajectory of the fixed scalar function that is x^2/2
on |x|<=tau and tau|x|-tau^2/2 elsewhere. Since P_i<=S, every finite
xi>=tau. Every finite-source Qij in (3) is zero, and 2fn=tau.
Evaluate the polynomial identity (5) at (9): v_H^T M v_H=0, without any
positivity assumption on the coefficients. All rows except possibly the
last already annihilate v_H, and its last coordinate tau is positive.
Consequently the last row also annihilates it. We have

              M v_H=0,  A1=mu/(2tau),  Z_hub 1=0.                    (10)

Completing the x0 square in (5) gives a positive initial square plus the
gradient form with matrix Z_hub. Since Z_hub 1=0, for every scalar coordinate vector
z=(z0,...,zn),

    z^T Z_hub z=(z0-zn,...,z_(n-1)-zn)^T K_hub
                                      (z0-zn,...,z_(n-1)-zn).         (11)

Hence M>=0 iff K_hub>=0. If the signs in (6) hold, (5) proves
2fn<=tau||x0||^2 on every legal trajectory in every dimension. The exact
Huber function (9) attains equality. Normalization from the predecessor
then gives W_n(h)=tau.

### Why these coordinates cover every tight full certificate

Let any nonnegative full certificate at level tau be given. Evaluate it
on (9). The only strict interpolation residuals are those leaving star:

    Q_(star,i)=-tau[1-tau(P_i+1)]<0,

because P_i<=S and 1-tau(S+1)=S/(2S+1)>0. The objective gap is zero.
Full PSD and nonnegative multipliers therefore force lambda_(star,i)=0
and Mv_H=0. The value flow implies sum mu_i=2. Applying (7) to the
prefix rows gives (1), and the flow at each prefix node gives (2).
Take r to be the actual finite prefix-source multipliers of the original
certificate. This reconstructs every coefficient, proving the asserted
losslessness. This argument does not delete incoming terminal edges.

## 2. The actual seven-step word and rational coefficients

Write t=sqrt(2), a=(1+t)/2 and b=1+8(1+t)/9. For the assigned m=3
parameters c_3=(4/3)(1+t), a_3=1/[2(1+t)], the actual word is exactly

    h=(a,5/3,a,b,a,5/3,a),
    S=(65+26t)/9,  tau=9/(139+52t).                                  (12)

No steps have been contracted or replaced. Use r=R_int/10^6, where R_int has
rows i=0,...,6 and columns j=0,...,7:

       0  12935   7196    7116   3081  2983  2929  3123
   54548      0   9076   29849  11139  7899  5596  5450
   30421  27844      0  227407   8150  7203  5823  5265

    9541  13214  13036   70218      0 16219  9699  7434

    6981   9672  10333  207590 167381 32994     0 13402

Equations (1)--(4) specify every remaining multiplier and every entry of
the exact 9x9 residual in Q(sqrt(2)). All finite off-diagonal r are

    mu_1 [143370,143371]     beta_1 [8213,8214]
    mu_2 [106957,106958]     beta_2 [12312,12313]
    mu_3 [390815,390816]     beta_3 [248522,248523]

The zero star-source multipliers here are an explicit algebraic choice
required by exact Huber complementarity. They are not a silent
truncation of the solver's small positive coefficients.

## 3. Full PSD, certified with a fixed rational interval calculation

Here is the precise arithmetic specification behind all the enclosures,
so no floating eigenvalue or optimization output is a premise. Take

    D=10^18,
    l=1414213562373095048, u=l+1.

The integer inequalities l^2<2D^2<u^2 put t in [l/D,u/D]. Represent
each intermediate interval by two integers [L,U] denoting [L/D,U/D].
Addition and negation use their exact endpoint rules. For multiplication,
take the minimum and maximum of the four endpoint integer products,
divide by D, and round the lower endpoint down and upper endpoint up.
For division by an interval not containing zero, take the minimum and
maximum of the four rational quotients (numerator endpoint times D,

All input rationals are enclosed by the same outward rule. These rules

    (L_ldl)_ik=[(K_hub)_ik-sum_(j<k)(L_ldl)_ij (L_ldl)_kj d_j]/d_k,
                                      i>k, k=0,...,6.                (13)

Here D_ldl denotes the diagonal matrix with entries d_0,...,d_6.

    d_3 [6594,6595]

Throughout this calculation require d_j<M_j at the levels being used.
Define the following exact scalar recurrence:

    Z_0=1, t_0=1,
    z_j=(M_j+d_j)/(M_j-d_j),
    r_j=1+2z_j=(3M_j+d_j)/(M_j-d_j),
    Z_(j+1)=r_j Z_j,
    t_(j+1)=(1+sqrt(4 Z_(j+1)-3))/2,
    delta_j=Z_j-r_j d_j^2.                              (1)

Thus Z_j=t_j^2-t_j+1. All r_j>1, so the square roots are real and
t_j>=1. This fixes every parameter; there is no numerical optimization.

Here is the actual nonnegative array lambda^(j) on C_ij. Its base has only
lambda^0_(star,0)=1. Suppose its block has length n=n_j, sum S=S_j,
and put p=n, q=2n+1, b=1+d_j, z=z_j, r=r_j, t=t_j, t'=t_(j+1).

1. Embed the old array on the left sample indices {0,...,p,star}.
2. Add r times the old array on {p+1,...,q,star}.
3. For each right queried index i=p+1,...,q-1, whose physical step is h_i,
   add z h_i to entries (p,i) and (q,i), and subtract 2z h_i from (star,i).
4. Add the following six sparse corrections:

    (p,q): z,                 (q,p): z d_j,
    (p,star): -S,             (q,star): 2S+b-rS,
    (star,p): b-t,            (star,q): t'-rt.           (2)

The corrections individually may be signed, but the FINAL array is
nonnegative. In fact its optimum entries are exactly

    lambda_(star,i)=h_i for i<q,
    lambda_(star,q)=t',
    lambda_(i,star)=0 for i<q,
    lambda_(q,star)=2S+b.                                (3)

To verify this inductively, left interior entries are unchanged, the old
left terminal entry t becomes b, right interior entries become
(r-2z)h_i=h_i, and the right terminal entry becomes t'. Incoming optimum
entries at the left terminal cancel, and the right terminal entry becomes
2S+b. Every other update either embeds a nonnegative old coefficient or
adds z h_i, z, or z d_j. This proves actual coefficient signs, including
all optimum edges, rather than just signs of an auxiliary matrix.

## 2. Complete identity and calibration

There is an exact gradient-only remainder E_j, defined on all the formal
gradients of the block, such that

    ||x_start||^2-||x_end-t_j g_end||^2-2t_j f_end
       =sum lambda^(j)_ik C_ik + E_j.                  (4)

Its recursion is

    E_0=0,
    E_(j+1)=E_j(left)+r_j E_j(right)
                         +delta_j ||g_p||^2.            (5)

Here each child is evaluated at its actual chronological sample indices.
In particular E_j contains no terminal-gradient term of its own: its
variables are only the midpoint gradients of all internal recursion nodes.

We verify (4)--(5) without omitting any function coefficient. Denote the
left endpoint and gradient by x,g and the right endpoint and gradient by
y,v. Their values are f,F. The weighted right displacement is

    w=sum_(p<i<q) h_i g_i=x-bg-y.

The rank-one correction in step 3 sums to

    2zS(f+F)-zS(||g||^2+||v||^2)
                         -2z<w,x+y-g-v>.               (6)

Combine the two child identities, the correction (6), and (2). The
coefficient of f is

    2[(z-1)S-b+z-zd_j]=0,

because z(S+2-b)=S+b. The coefficient of F is -2t', and every
interior value has already canceled within its child and (6). The
optimum value is zero under normalization; before normalization the
total value flow cancels it against the terminal coefficient.

The x^2, <x,g>, <x,v>, <y,g>, and <g,v> coefficients all cancel.
The remaining expression is

    ||x_start||^2-||y-t'v||^2-2t'F
       +(r d_j^2-Z_j)||g||^2
       +(Z_(j+1)-r Z_j)||v||^2
       -E_j(left)-r E_j(right).

The last gradient coefficient is zero by (1). This is exactly (4)--(5).
This calculation also follows by direct expansion of (6); the cancellations
use only z(S+2-b)=S+b and r=1+2z.

The calibration is exact. Set lambda=1+sqrt(2), a=1/lambda, c=lambda.
Then M_j=lambda^j, d_j=lambda^(j-1), z_j=lambda, r_j=lambda^2,
Z_j=M_j^2, and delta_j=0 at every level. Thus E_j=0 and (4) is a
valid full initial-distance certificate at the undeformed silver word.
It is the canonical endpoint-square guarantee, not a claim that this
particular certificate attains the sharper Huber constant.

For an arbitrary real q_cert, the SAME nonnegative array supplies the
following fully value-canceled candidate objective matrix:

    q_cert ||x_0||^2-2 f_n
       +sum_(i!=k) [2 lambda^(m)_ki/t_m] Q_ik
     =(q_cert-1/t_m)||x_0||^2
       +[||x_n-t_m g_n||^2+E_m]/t_m.                 (7)

This explicitly includes the true initial vector and the optimum index.
Its validity as an upper bound depends on FULL PSD of the right side.

## 3. An exact negative midpoint for the assigned parameters

Now set m>=128, epsilon=1/m, and use the assigned family

    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c.

For these parameters 2<c<3 and 0<a<c-2<1. The exact mass formula is

    M_j=A c^j+(1-A)2^j,  A=a/(c-2),                 (8)

so 0<A<1 and M_j-d_j=A(3-c)c^j+(1-A)2^j>0.
Thus every coefficient in the proposed array is defined and nonnegative.

Nevertheless delta_2<0. Here is a finite exact proof with an explicit
parameter interval, not a limiting differential equation. Put s=sqrt(2).
For j=0,1,2, write r_j=N_j/D_j, where

    N_0=(2+s)+(4-s)epsilon,
    D_0=(2-s)+s epsilon,
    N_1=(4+3s)+(9-3s)epsilon-epsilon^2,
    D_1=s+(3-s)epsilon+epsilon^2,
    N_2=(10+7s)+(19-5s)epsilon-(4+s)epsilon^2
                                                 -(1+s)epsilon^3,
    D_2=(2+s)+(5-3s)epsilon+s epsilon^2
                                                 +(1+s)epsilon^3.

All denominator coefficients are positive. Since d_2=lambda(1-epsilon^2),

    delta_2=P(epsilon)/(D_0 D_1 D_2),
    P=N_0 N_1 D_2-lambda^2(1-epsilon^2)^2 N_2 D_0 D_1.

The coefficients of P, in increasing degree 0 through 10, are

    0,
    -112-96s,
    -96-84s,
    640+12s,
    528+368s,
    88+92s,
    -320-167s,
    -202-158s,
    -2-4s,
    42+30s,
    10+7s.                                           (9)

These coefficients follow by multiplying the displayed degree-at-most-three
polynomials. A tiny exact Q(sqrt(2)) polynomial multiplication independently
checked the list; the displayed identity is the mathematical evidence.
Using s<3/2, the sum of absolute upper bounds for coefficients of degree
at least two is 3311. Consequently, for 0<epsilon<=1/128,

    P(epsilon)/epsilon
       <=-112-96s+3311 epsilon
       <-112+3311/128<0.                             (10)

For comparison, the first derivative is

    delta_2=-(48+28sqrt(2))epsilon+O(epsilon^2).

The same negative coefficient occurs at the finite diagnostic m=3:

    P(1/3)=(-1059632-2141552sqrt(2))/59049<0.

The three relevant denominators are positive there as well. This agrees
with failure of the ARRAY even though max3's unrestricted numerical H_3
diagnostic reported a Huber match. That diagnostic is not used as a premise.

## 4. Negative FULL formal directions, and limits of repairs

Every occurrence of a level-two midpoint contributes

    omega_i delta_2 ||g_i||^2

to E_m, with omega_i>0, a product of right-child weights r_j from its
ancestors. There are K=2^(m-3) such indices. Their actual step is the same
number b_2=1+d_2. No other term of E_m uses any of those gradient
coordinates, by the diagonal recursion (5).

First choose one such index i, set x_0=0, g_i=v!=0, all other queried
gradients zero, and g_n=-(b_2/t_m)v. Then

    x_n=-b_2 v, x_n-t_m g_n=0, E_m=omega_i delta_2||v||^2<0.

Thus (7) is not PSD for ANY q_cert. Merely increasing the initial-distance
coefficient does not repair the proposed array.

There is a larger obstruction when m>=4. Work first with scalar formal
gradients, put x_0=g_n=0, allow arbitrary g_i at the K selected indices
subject to sum_i g_i=0, and set every other gradient to zero. This is a
subspace D of dimension K-1 on which

    x_n=0, g_(n-1)=0,
    E_m=delta_2 sum_i omega_i g_i^2<0

for every nonzero vector. The weights need not coincide. It follows that:

* Any added quadratic depending only on x_0,x_n,g_n,g_(n-1) vanishes on D.
* Replacing only the final physical step leaves every position unchanged
  on D, because g_(n-1)=0. With the same array, the negative evaluation
  persists for every prescribed final-step replacement and every q_cert.
* Any PSD matrix addition of rank less than K-1 has a nonzero kernel vector
  in D, by dimension counting, and therefore cannot repair the full matrix.

The last statement is about additions to this fixed matrix. Changing
relative interpolation multipliers may have an indefinite difference and
is NOT excluded. Likewise a correction of growing rank is not excluded.
The selected vectors deliberately do not satisfy the interpolation
constraints; no legal lower witness, no W upper bound, and no impossibility
theorem for H_m is inferred.

## 5. Fixed-constant deformations: the same ansatz always fails for tau>0

Consider the allowed neighboring family

    c=lambda(1+tau/m), a=(1-sigma/m)/c,                (11)

with fixed real tau,sigma, for all sufficiently large m. Positivity and
d_j<M_j hold uniformly over the word once 0<a<1 and 2<c<3: indeed

    M_j/d_j=1/(c-2)
               +[1/a-1/(c-2)](2/c)^j

lies between 1/a and 1/(c-2), both greater than one.

If tau>0, the specified multiplier recursion always develops a negative
coefficient at a FIXED level as m tends to infinity. If sigma+tau<0,
then d_0>1/lambda and delta_0=1-r_0 d_0^2<0, since
d maps to d^2(3+d)/(1-d) is strictly increasing for 0<d<1 and equals
one at d=1/lambda.

For sigma+tau>=0 the fixed level j=4 suffices. To show this, temporarily
regard epsilon as a real variable tending to zero and set

    u=2/lambda, D=sigma+(1+lambda^2)tau,
    T_j=lambda^2 tau-D u^j.

Differentiation at epsilon=0 of the explicit finite formulas gives

    M_j(0)=lambda^j,
    (d/depsilon)log M_j |0=j tau-D(1-u^j),
    (d/depsilon)(d_j/M_j)|0=(1/lambda)T_j.

For r(x)=(3+x)/(1-x), (d/dx)log r at x=1/lambda equals 2.
Using 1-u=1/lambda^2 and
2(1/lambda-1/lambda^2)/(1-u)=2sqrt(2), equation (1) therefore gives

    (d/depsilon)[delta_j/M_j^2]|0
       =2sqrt(2)[tau(j-lambda^2)-D(1-2u^j)].          (12)

One can also verify (12) by summing the finite geometric series for T_j.
At j=4, 4-lambda^2<0 and 1-2u^4>0. The latter follows from
u^4=272-192sqrt(2)<1/2; squaring 543<384sqrt(2) verifies it with
positive sides. Moreover D>=lambda^2 tau>0. Thus (12) is strictly
negative. The expression is an analytic finite rational function near
zero, so delta_4<0 for every sufficiently large m. This uses a derivative
at one fixed finite depth, not an unproved continuum recurrence.

The same full-vector argument as in Section 4 then excludes the array and
its stated endpoint or fixed-rank patches. This generalization does not
exclude a different full certificate for any of the deformed schedules.

## 6. Rechecking the exact comparison and an actual deformation filter

Set rho=log_2(lambda). From the accepted exact recursions, primitive shifted
mass C_n=S_circle(n)+1 has join

    Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,

and the benchmark B_n has join

    G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

Here is a proof of C_n<=(n+1)^rho and B_n<=1+4n^rho, retained rather
than assuming the earlier draft comparison. Define F(t)=(1+t)^rho-1.
For t=exp(z), direct differentiation gives

    d^2/dz^2 log F(exp(z))
      =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)
        [(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/F(t)^2>0.

The numerator bracket is positive since rho>1 and its derivative is
rho[(1+t)^(rho-1)-1]>0. Convexity at z,-z gives
F(t)F(1/t)>=F(1)^2=(lambda-1)^2=2. With A=t^rho B and
E=(1+t)^rho B, this implies (E-A)(E-B)>=2AB, so

    Omega(A,B)<=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho.

Induction in the primitive recursion gives its claimed bound. Also
G(A,D)<=4A+D. If k+l+1=n, the dominant induction now gives

    B_n<=1+4[(k+1)^rho+l^rho]<=1+4n^rho.

The last inequality follows from superadditivity of t^rho on nonnegative
arguments, which follows by integrating its increasing derivative.

For (11), the exact mass formula (8) gives

    M_m/lambda^m
      =(1+tau/m)^m [A+(1-A)(2/c)^m] -> exp(tau).       (13)

Thus the actual benchmark satisfies

    limsup B_(2^m-1)/(2M_m-1)<=2 exp(-tau).             (14)

In particular tau=1 recovers 2/e. This comparison alone is not an
objective upper bound; the failed matrix in Section 4 cannot supply one.

There is also a useful LOWER bound for the exact benchmark. Balanced
primitive joins give C_(2^j-1)>=lambda^j. Put b_0=1 and

    b_(j+1)=G(1,b_j)/lambda.

Balanced dominant joins imply B_(2^j-1)>=b_j lambda^j. The map in this
recursion is strictly increasing. Its fixed point above one is

    b_infty=sqrt(2)(1+lambda^(-1/2))>2.                (15)

To verify the fixed point, squaring the equation G(1,b)=lambda b
gives lambda(lambda-1)b^2-4lambda b+4=0; the positive root (15)
satisfies the original equation, whereas the smaller algebraic root does
not. Alternatively uniqueness above one follows because
G(1,b)/b=2/b+1/2+sqrt(1+8/b)/2 is strictly decreasing. Since
1<b_1=4/lambda<b_infty, monotonicity shows b_j increases to b_infty.

This yields an ACTUAL legal-witness filter even when the final step is
replaced arbitrarily. Let P_m=S_m-(1+d_0) be the sum of the queried prefix
before that final step, and prescribe any b_m>=0. For P_m>=1, the two
accepted Huber/cut witnesses give

    W_(n_m)(H_m with final step b_m)
       >=max{1/(2P_m+2b_m+1),
                    (b_m-1)_+^2/(P_m+1)^2}
       >=1/(2P_m+3+2sqrt(P_m)).                       (16)

For b_m<=1+sqrt(P_m), the first term proves (16). For larger b_m, the
second is at least P_m/(P_m+1)^2, which is at least its right side
because P_m^2+P_m+2P_m sqrt(P_m)-1>=0 for P_m>=1.
Equations (13), (15), and (16) prove the uniform statement

    liminf_m B_(n_m) W_(n_m)(modified word)
                     >=b_infty/(2 exp(tau)).           (17)

Consequently no fixed asymptotic separation below the benchmark is possible
within these fixed-constant deformations, even with an arbitrary final step,
when tau<=log(b_infty/2). This is a legal lower-bound conclusion for that
parameter region. It is distinct from the formal-matrix obstruction for
tau>0, and does not settle the assigned tau=1 family.

## 7. A richer exact join, with the unresolved full-matrix issue exposed

The following calculation records the next concrete repair interface. It
does not assert that a scalar local condition closes the target.

Replace the canonical child storage by

    I=||x_start||^2-||x_end-u0 g_end||^2-2v0 f_end
       =sum lambda C+E,
    Z=(u0-1)^2+v0,
    k=S+u0-v0>=0.

Assume its optimum entries are h_i on (star,i), u0 on the terminal
(star,end), zero on other (i,star), and k on (end,star); retain the
ENTIRE gradient remainder E. These properties hold for the calibrated
canonical family. They are assumptions of this interface, not all full
certificates.

Use two nonnegative correction weights A0,B0. Scale the right child by
r=1+A0+B0. For each right queried i add A0 h_i on (p,i), B0 h_i on
(q,i), and -(A0+B0)h_i on (star,i). Choose cross coefficients p0,q0>=0
with

    p0-q0=b+(1-A0)S.

Adjust optimum entries to physical h_i, terminal u1, and
k1=2S+b+u1-v1>=0 exactly as in (2), with child k in place of S.
Thus the actual final array is nonnegative provided the named scalar
coefficients and u1,k1 are nonnegative. Put

    d=b-1, M=S+1, t=A0-B0,
    H=M+d-B0(M-d)-t M,
    ell=p0-B0-t,
    Z1=(u1-1)^2+v1,
    V=x_p-x_q-g_p+g_q.

Full coefficient expansion, including all function values, gives

    E_new=E_left+r E_right
       +t||V||^2+2<V,(H-ell)g_p+ell g_q>
       +(Z-rd^2)||g_p||^2+(rZ-Z1)||g_q||^2.           (18)

For example the canonical construction sets A0=B0=z, p0=z,
q0=zd, H=ell=t=0 and Z1=rZ, recovering (5).
To check (18), first use D=x_p-x_q. The local coefficients of
D^2, D g_p, D g_q are t,-2(ell+t-H),2(ell+t).
Substituting D=V+g_p-g_q makes the g_p g_q coefficient zero and gives
exactly the displayed diagonal and cross terms. The value coefficient
at p is 2[(A0-1)S-b+p0-q0]=0 and the terminal coefficient is -2v1.

Demanding the isolated three-vector matrix in (18) be PSD is only a
SUFFICIENT restriction. It forces Z>=rd^2 and Z1<=rZ, and risks
repeating the already recorded scalar-deficit failure. The useful open
question is whether the FULL child remainders can pay for an indefinite
local term.

There is a finite exact way to retain that information for this array
class. Define the gradient moment z_block=sum h_i g_i+g_end. If a child
remainder is decomposed into nonnegative internal squares plus the sharp
two-variable form

    a0||z_block||^2+2b0<z_block,g_end>+c0||g_end||^2,

then the parent remainder before elimination is the explicit four-variable
form, in L=z_left, g=g_p, R=z_right, e=g_q,

    a0||L||^2+2b0<L,g>+c0||g||^2
      +r[a0||R||^2+2b0<R,e>+c0||e||^2]
      +t||d g+R||^2+2<d g+R,(H-ell)g+ell e>
      +(Z-rd^2)||g||^2+(rZ-Z1)||e||^2.                (19)

The parent moment is exactly z_parent=L+d g+R. Substituting
L=z_parent-dg-R and completing squares in g,R gives its next
two-variable form when the corresponding eliminated block is PSD and
the cross columns lie in its range. Negative eliminated directions are
full-matrix obstructions and must not be dropped. This is an explicit
recursively generated multiplier family and exact remainder interface;
no choice of its free parameters or uniform constant establishing the
requested asymptotic separation has yet been proved.

The original target remains open. The finished result of this attempt is
the fully exhibited obstruction to (1)--(7), the exact parameter filter
(17), and the identified need to change the full recursive array rather
than inflate its endpoint bound.

# Direct objective gluing on the actual critical words

Status: UNVERIFIED joint calculation and certificate-space obstruction.
No solver and no fact_submit. The negative formal vectors below are NOT legal
smooth-convex trajectories. They refute a specified full multiplier array and
its stated repairs, not the schedule or the original profile conjecture.

The only mathematical predecessor used is accepted fact
`1252b8823bb5a290` for interpolation, and `b98bb807d514e80d` for the

1. Embed the old array on the left sample indices {0,...,p,star}.
2. Add r times the old array on {p+1,...,q,star}.
3. For each right queried index i=p+1,...,q-1, whose physical step is h_i,
   add z h_i to entries (p,i) and (q,i), and subtract 2z h_i from (star,i).
4. Add the following six sparse corrections:

    (p,q): z,                 (q,p): z d_j,
    (p,star): -S,             (q,star): 2S+b-rS,
    (star,p): b-t,            (star,q): t'-rt.           (2)

The corrections individually may be signed, but the FINAL array is
nonnegative. In fact its optimum entries are exactly

    lambda_(star,i)=h_i for i<q,
    lambda_(star,q)=t',
    lambda_(i,star)=0 for i<q,
    lambda_(q,star)=2S+b.                                (3)

To verify this inductively, left interior entries are unchanged, the old
left terminal entry t becomes b, right interior entries become
(r-2z)h_i=h_i, and the right terminal entry becomes t'. Incoming optimum
entries at the left terminal cancel, and the right terminal entry becomes
2S+b. Every other update either embeds a nonnegative old coefficient or
adds z h_i, z, or z d_j. This proves actual coefficient signs, including
all optimum edges, rather than just signs of an auxiliary matrix.

There is an exact gradient-only remainder E_j, defined on all the formal
gradients of the block, such that

    ||x_start||^2-||x_end-t_j g_end||^2-2t_j f_end
       =sum lambda^(j)_ik C_ik + E_j.                  (4)

Its recursion is

    E_0=0,
    E_(j+1)=E_j(left)+r_j E_j(right)
                         +delta_j ||g_p||^2.            (5)

Here each child is evaluated at its actual chronological sample indices.
In particular E_j contains no terminal-gradient term of its own: its
variables are only the midpoint gradients of all internal recursion nodes.

We verify (4)--(5) without omitting any function coefficient. Denote the
left endpoint and gradient by x,g and the right endpoint and gradient by
y,v. Their values are f,F. The weighted right displacement is

    w=sum_(p<i<q) h_i g_i=x-bg-y.

The rank-one correction in step 3 sums to

    2zS(f+F)-zS(||g||^2+||v||^2)
                         -2z<w,x+y-g-v>.               (6)

Combine the two child identities, the correction (6), and (2). The
coefficient of f is

## 4. Negative FULL formal directions, and limits of repairs

Every occurrence of a level-two midpoint contributes

    omega_i delta_2 ||g_i||^2

to E_m, with omega_i>0, a product of right-child weights r_j from its
ancestors. There are K=2^(m-3) such indices. Their actual step is the same
number b_2=1+d_2. No other term of E_m uses any of those gradient
coordinates, by the diagonal recursion (5).

First choose one such index i, set x_0=0, g_i=v!=0, all other queried
gradients zero, and g_n=-(b_2/t_m)v. Then

    x_n=-b_2 v, x_n-t_m g_n=0, E_m=omega_i delta_2||v||^2<0.

Thus (7) is not PSD for ANY q_cert. Merely increasing the initial-distance
coefficient does not repair the proposed array.

There is a larger obstruction when m>=4. Work first with scalar formal
gradients, put x_0=g_n=0, allow arbitrary g_i at the K selected indices
subject to sum_i g_i=0, and set every other gradient to zero. This is a
subspace D of dimension K-1 on which

    x_n=0, g_(n-1)=0,
    E_m=delta_2 sum_i omega_i g_i^2<0

for every nonzero vector. The weights need not coincide. It follows that:

* Any added quadratic depending only on x_0,x_n,g_n,g_(n-1) vanishes on D.
* Replacing only the final physical step leaves every position unchanged
  on D, because g_(n-1)=0. With the same array, the negative evaluation
  persists for every prescribed final-step replacement and every q_cert.
* Any PSD matrix addition of rank less than K-1 has a nonzero kernel vector
  in D, by dimension counting, and therefore cannot repair the full matrix.

The last statement is about additions to this fixed matrix. Changing
relative interpolation multipliers may have an indefinite difference and
is NOT excluded. Likewise a correction of growing rank is not excluded.
The selected vectors deliberately do not satisfy the interpolation
constraints; no legal lower witness, no W upper bound, and no impossibility
theorem for H_m is inferred.

## 5. Fixed-constant deformations: the same ansatz always fails for tau>0

Consider the allowed neighboring family

    c=lambda(1+tau/m), a=(1-sigma/m)/c,                (11)

with fixed real tau,sigma, for all sufficiently large m. Positivity and
d_j<M_j hold uniformly over the word once 0<a<1 and 2<c<3: indeed

    M_j/d_j=1/(c-2)
               +[1/a-1/(c-2)](2/c)^j

lies between 1/a and 1/(c-2), both greater than one.

If tau>0, the specified multiplier recursion always develops a negative
coefficient at a FIXED level as m tends to infinity. If sigma+tau<0,
then d_0>1/lambda and delta_0=1-r_0 d_0^2<0, since
d maps to d^2(3+d)/(1-d) is strictly increasing for 0<d<1 and equals
one at d=1/lambda.

For sigma+tau>=0 the fixed level j=4 suffices. To show this, temporarily
regard epsilon as a real variable tending to zero and set

    u=2/lambda, D=sigma+(1+lambda^2)tau,
    T_j=lambda^2 tau-D u^j.

Differentiation at epsilon=0 of the explicit finite formulas gives

    M_j(0)=lambda^j,
    (d/depsilon)log M_j |0=j tau-D(1-u^j),
    (d/depsilon)(d_j/M_j)|0=(1/lambda)T_j.

For r(x)=(3+x)/(1-x), (d/dx)log r at x=1/lambda equals 2.
Using 1-u=1/lambda^2 and
2(1/lambda-1/lambda^2)/(1-u)=2sqrt(2), equation (1) therefore gives

    (d/depsilon)[delta_j/M_j^2]|0
       =2sqrt(2)[tau(j-lambda^2)-D(1-2u^j)].          (12)

One can also verify (12) by summing the finite geometric series for T_j.
At j=4, 4-lambda^2<0 and 1-2u^4>0. The latter follows from
u^4=272-192sqrt(2)<1/2; squaring 543<384sqrt(2) verifies it with
positive sides. Moreover D>=lambda^2 tau>0. Thus (12) is strictly
negative. The expression is an analytic finite rational function near
zero, so delta_4<0 for every sufficiently large m. This uses a derivative
at one fixed finite depth, not an unproved continuum recurrence.

The same full-vector argument as in Section 4 then excludes the array and
its stated endpoint or fixed-rank patches. This generalization does not
exclude a different full certificate for any of the deformed schedules.

## 6. Rechecking the exact comparison and an actual deformation filter

Set rho=log_2(lambda). From the accepted exact recursions, primitive shifted
mass C_n=S_circle(n)+1 has join

    Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,

and the benchmark B_n has join

    G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

Here is a proof of C_n<=(n+1)^rho and B_n<=1+4n^rho, retained rather
than assuming the earlier draft comparison. Define F(t)=(1+t)^rho-1.
For t=exp(z), direct differentiation gives

    d^2/dz^2 log F(exp(z))
      =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)
        [(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/F(t)^2>0.

The numerator bracket is positive since rho>1 and its derivative is
rho[(1+t)^(rho-1)-1]>0. Convexity at z,-z gives
F(t)F(1/t)>=F(1)^2=(lambda-1)^2=2. With A=t^rho B and
E=(1+t)^rho B, this implies (E-A)(E-B)>=2AB, so

    Omega(A,B)<=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho.

Induction in the primitive recursion gives its claimed bound. Also
G(A,D)<=4A+D. If k+l+1=n, the dominant induction now gives

    B_n<=1+4[(k+1)^rho+l^rho]<=1+4n^rho.

The last inequality follows from superadditivity of t^rho on nonnegative
arguments, which follows by integrating its increasing derivative.

For (11), the exact mass formula (8) gives

    M_m/lambda^m
      =(1+tau/m)^m [A+(1-A)(2/c)^m] -> exp(tau).       (13)

Thus the actual benchmark satisfies

    limsup B_(2^m-1)/(2M_m-1)<=2 exp(-tau).             (14)

In particular tau=1 recovers 2/e. This comparison alone is not an
objective upper bound; the failed matrix in Section 4 cannot supply one.

There is also a useful LOWER bound for the exact benchmark. Balanced
primitive joins give C_(2^j-1)>=lambda^j. Put b_0=1 and

    b_(j+1)=G(1,b_j)/lambda.

Balanced dominant joins imply B_(2^j-1)>=b_j lambda^j. The map in this
recursion is strictly increasing. Its fixed point above one is

    b_infty=sqrt(2)(1+lambda^(-1/2))>2.                (15)

To verify the fixed point, squaring the equation G(1,b)=lambda b
gives lambda(lambda-1)b^2-4lambda b+4=0; the positive root (15)
satisfies the original equation, whereas the smaller algebraic root does
not. Alternatively uniqueness above one follows because
G(1,b)/b=2/b+1/2+sqrt(1+8/b)/2 is strictly decreasing. Since
1<b_1=4/lambda<b_infty, monotonicity shows b_j increases to b_infty.

This yields an ACTUAL legal-witness filter even when the final step is
replaced arbitrarily. Let P_m=S_m-(1+d_0) be the sum of the queried prefix
before that final step, and prescribe any b_m>=0. For P_m>=1, the two
accepted Huber/cut witnesses give

    W_(n_m)(H_m with final step b_m)
       >=max{1/(2P_m+2b_m+1),
                    (b_m-1)_+^2/(P_m+1)^2}
       >=1/(2P_m+3+2sqrt(P_m)).                       (16)

For b_m<=1+sqrt(P_m), the first term proves (16). For larger b_m, the
second is at least P_m/(P_m+1)^2, which is at least its right side
because P_m^2+P_m+2P_m sqrt(P_m)-1>=0 for P_m>=1.
Equations (13), (15), and (16) prove the uniform statement

    liminf_m B_(n_m) W_(n_m)(modified word)
                     >=b_infty/(2 exp(tau)).           (17)

Consequently no fixed asymptotic separation below the benchmark is possible
within these fixed-constant deformations, even with an arbitrary final step,
when tau<=log(b_infty/2). This is a legal lower-bound conclusion for that
parameter region. It is distinct from the formal-matrix obstruction for
tau>0, and does not settle the assigned tau=1 family.

    Y_j <= (25/4) exp[-2^(j-2)/(2m)].                 (30)

For j=ceil(log_2 m)+4, the right side is at most (25/4)exp(-2)<2,
because exp(2)>1+2+2^2/2=5>25/8. But (28) requires
Y_j>=r>=2+d_j/M_j>2. Hence this continuation must fail no later
than that level; for m>=128 the level is strictly below m.

The same upper recurrence bounds ANY continuation within the isolated
PSD-local-square restriction (28) that starts at Z_2<=M_2^2: smaller
Z or smaller r cannot improve the later bound. Such a continuation can
fail earlier, including from an endpoint root or a different coefficient
sign, but cannot survive to the required horizon. This is a limitation
of (28), not of the general full recurrence (18). Allowing H or ell to
be nonzero and using the entire indefinite local/positive child matrix
interaction remains outside this obstruction.

An independent tiny rational coefficient audit in
`research/direct_gluing_exact_audit.py` checked the one-step seed, a
subcritical three-step join, and a supercritical seven-step join. It matched
EVERY function and FULL Gram coefficient exactly and checked every final
multiplier sign using Fraction arithmetic. The audit is an algebra check
on the displayed construction, not verifier acceptance or a substitute
for the written derivation.

## 9. The sharp-storage zero mode also obstructs general mixed joins

There is a stronger, precise restriction on attempts to repair (29) merely
by choosing nonzero H or ell. It does not require the local matrix to be
PSD separately.

Suppose the FULL child remainder E is PSD and, for every endpoint vector
g, there is a choice of all its internal formal gradients with

    z_block=kappa g, E=0, kappa^2=Z.                  (31)

The H_3 remainder constructed above has this property with
kappa=-M_2/(d_2/M_2)=-M_2^2/d_2 and Z=Z_3. Attainment follows
directly from the square decompositions in (22), (26), and (27): all
zero-square conditions specify actual formal gradients, not only an
infimum. A formal block may be embedded twice independently while sharing
only the prescribed starting position; its gradient remainder is
translation invariant.

Consider ANY join of the full family (18), with arbitrary nonnegative
actual multipliers and arbitrary H,ell, and suppose its WHOLE remainder
is PSD. Fix a nonzero terminal vector e and select the right child at
its zero mode z_right=kappa e. Select the left child with endpoint

    g_p=-(kappa/d)e, z_left=kappa g_p, E_left=0.

Then E_right=0 and V=d g_p+z_right=0. Every cross-block term in
(18) therefore vanishes, leaving exactly

    E_new=[Z^2/d^2-Z1]||e||^2.                       (32)

Consequently full PSD NECESSARILY requires Z1<=Z^2/d^2. This argument
uses actual full formal directions of both children; it is not a local
diagonal test.

If equality is imposed in (32), the same nonzero vector has zero parent
remainder and

    z_parent=z_left+V=-(Z/d)e.

Thus property (31) propagates with kappa1=-Z/d and kappa1^2=Z1.
Inductively, a continuation that saturates this storage bound at every
join obeys (29) even with arbitrary H and ell and with every child matrix
retained. It cannot escape the storage collapse by changing those mixed
coefficients alone.

More explicitly, starting at Z_2=M_2^2 and saturating from level two,

    Z_m=d_m^2 c^2 T^(2^(m-2)),
    log Z_m <= 2log a+(2m+2)log c-2^(m-2)/(2m) -> -infinity.

Here d_m=a c^m is just the next level's scalar, and the bound on T was
proved in Section 8. For a positive endpoint objective weight v_m one
always has v_m<=Z_m, since Z_m=(u_m-1)^2+v_m. Hence the resulting
objective level q_m=1/v_m is at least 1/Z_m and cannot establish the
required decreasing error, much less the exact benchmark separation.

This is a conditional obstruction to repeated SHARP storage selection.
A strict sacrifice of storage together with changed relative multipliers
may remove the zero mode (31), and a different full certificate family
need not have it. Those possibilities remain open. The next meaningful
test must therefore preserve the full two-variable remainder and allow
genuinely nonsaturating intermediate choices; it cannot simply perturb
the mixed coefficients while keeping the same sharp endpoint recursion.

# A chronological chain closes the full zero-initial coupling space

Status: complete candidate proof, UNVERIFIED. No routine fact submission is
allocated. The only correctness inputs used are facts 1252b8823bb5a290
(necessary interpolation inequalities and smoothness) and b98bb807d514e80d
(the exact benchmark recursions). Every new estimate is given below. Earlier
unverified spectral and covariance findings are not premises.

## 1. Actual schedule, full added space, and claim

Let lambda=1+sqrt(2). For an integer m>=128 put
c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c, d_j=1+a c^j. Within this horizon these
parameters are fixed. Set H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j), n=2^m-1,
q=n-1, and let h be H_m with ONLY its original last step d_0 removed.
Write S=sum h_t. For 0<=i<=q put P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z).
Fix zeta_1=(1+i)/2, zeta_2=(4+i)/2, and z_l=zeta_l/S.

For a pair of complex numbers define the real column

 J(v_1,v_2)=(Re(v_1-v_2), Im v_1, Im v_2)^T.

Let w be arbitrary in [0,1] and T be ANY real matrix with three columns,
with no upper bound on its entries or number of rows. Define Euclidean data

 x_i=(sqrt(w)Re P_i(z_1),sqrt(w)Im P_i(z_1),
      sqrt(1-w)Re P_i(z_2),sqrt(1-w)Im P_i(z_2),
      T J(P_i(z_1),P_i(z_2))),
 g_i=(sqrt(w)Re[z_1 P_i(z_1)],sqrt(w)Im[z_1 P_i(z_1)],
      sqrt(1-w)Re[z_2 P_i(z_2)],sqrt(1-w)Im[z_2 P_i(z_2)],
      T J(z_1 P_i(z_1),z_2 P_i(z_2))).                    (1)

Then ||x_0||=1 and x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i. Every real linear functional
on (v_1,v_2) that vanishes at (1,1) is a linear combination of the three
components of J: its two real coefficients must sum to zero, and its two
imaginary coefficients are unrestricted. Thus (1) includes EVERY PSD
addition annihilating the initial vector, added orthogonally to the two
normal blocks. Write M=T^T T; it is an arbitrary PSD 3 by 3 matrix.

Suppose arbitrary JOINT queried values are interpolated by a convex
differentiable 1-smooth function F, with F(0)=0=min F and grad F(x_i)=g_i.
No separate modal values or modal legality are assumed. Then, for every
sufficiently large m, uniformly over w,T,F and b in [0,2],

                 2F(x_q-b g_q) <= 2/(3S).               (2)

For B_n=1/U_n^ZJ=2S_bullet(n)+1 this implies

 limsup_(m->infinity) sup_(w,T,F,b) B_n 2F(x_q-b g_q)
                       <= 8/(3e) < 64/65 < 1.           (3)

The actual final step b=d_0 lies in [0,2]. The statement concerns exactly
the displayed spectral family. It does not bound unrestricted W_n(H_m),
arbitrary spectra, or every possible metric on the two-mode cyclic space.

## 2. Two exact shared interpolation inequalities

Use Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0 from the accepted
fact 1252b8823bb5a290. First sum Q_(0,star) and Q_(t+1,t) for every
0<=t<q. The values telescope, and GD gives

 f_q <= <g_0,x_0>-sum_(t<q) h_t<g_(t+1),g_t>
                -||g_0||^2/2-sum_(t<q)||g_(t+1)-g_t||^2/2.

Dropping only the explicitly nonnegative squared terms yields

 f_q <= <g_0,x_0>-sum_(t<q)h_t<g_(t+1),g_t>.             (4)

Second, for any actual queried r, sum Q_(q,r) and Q_(r,star), and drop
their two squared terms. This gives

 f_q <= <g_q,x_q>+<g_r-g_q,x_r>.                         (5)

Choose r=2^(m-1), the query immediately AFTER the largest bridge. Both
inequalities concern the same joint transcript and the same function.
Their convex combination uses the fixed coefficients

                theta=6/25 on (4), 1-theta=19/25 on (5). (6)

For scaled gradients U_i=J(zeta_1 P_i(z_1),zeta_2 P_i(z_2)), and
Y_i=J(P_i(z_1),P_i(z_2)), let sym(u,v)=(uv^T+vu^T)/2. Define

 E_m=sum_(t<q) (h_t/S) sym(U_(t+1),U_t),
 Kplus_m=sym(U_q,Y_q)+sym(U_r-U_q,Y_r),
 K_m=(19/25)Kplus_m-(6/25)E_m.                          (7)

For l=1,2 let e_t=h_t/S and p_i,l=P_i(z_l), and define

 C_l,m=Re zeta_l-|zeta_l|^2 sum_(t<q)
                   e_t |p_t,l|^2(1-e_t Re zeta_l),
 Dplus_l,m=Re[zeta_l p_q,l conj(p_q,l)
                     +zeta_l(p_r,l-p_q,l)conj(p_r,l)],
 D_l,m=(6/25)C_l,m+(19/25)Dplus_l,m.                    (8)

The initial added coordinates are zero. Substituting (1) into (4)--(6)
therefore gives the EXACT finite-word bound

             S f_q <= w D_1,m+(1-w)D_2,m+trace(M K_m).  (9)

The proof will show K_m is negative definite and D_l,m<1/3 for all
sufficiently large m. Crucially these properties will hold at each such
FINITE m before allowing M to vary or grow without bound.

## 3. Limit word and continuity of its chronological work

Directly summing the multiplicity of every step gives

 S=2^m-2-a+a(c^m-2^m)/(c-2),      S/lambda^m -> e,
 d_(m-1-j)/S -> delta lambda^(-j),
 delta=1-2/lambda=3-2sqrt(2).                            (10)

Here a->1/lambda, (1+1/m)^m->e, and lambda(lambda-2)=1. The largest
normalized step has limit delta. The normalized limiting word consists
of a central step delta, two copies with central step delta/lambda,
four copies with central step delta/lambda^2, and so on, with their
recursive chronology retained. The total mass at level j is
delta(2/lambda)^j; the total mass is one.

Its truncation after N largest levels is the finite word obtained from
H <- (H,d,H), starting empty and using, in ascending order,

 d=delta/lambda^(N-1), ..., delta/lambda, delta.

The omitted mass is exactly epsilon_N=(2/lambda)^N. This definition
does not introduce any new physical terminal step.

For the four modal numbers

 zeta_1, conjugate(zeta_1), zeta_2, conjugate(zeta_2),

every normalized factor satisfies |1-d zeta|<=1 whenever 0<=d<=1/5:
expanding the square reduces this to d<=2Re(zeta)/|zeta|^2, whose
minimum here is 16/17. All limiting steps and, eventually, all actual
normalized steps satisfy the stronger bound d<1/5.

Deleting steps of total mass tau from such a chronological word changes
any modal prefix product by at most |zeta|tau. To see this, telescope
the deletion one factor at a time; all other factors have modulus<=1,
and the deleted factor differs from one by d zeta.

For any two of the four modal numbers A,B define the scalar work moment

 W_word(A,B)=sum_t d_t P_t(A)P_t(B)[1-d_t(A+B)/2].        (11)

The bracket is the average of 1-d_t A and 1-d_t B, so its modulus is
at most one. Deleted terms have total modulus<=tau. At retained terms,
the change in the two-product is at most (|A|+|B|)tau. Since the total
step mass is at most one,

 |W_word-W_deleted| <= (1+|A|+|B|)tau.                  (12)

After multiplying by AB this is <23tau, because |A|,|B|<=sqrt(17)/2
<21/10 and |AB|<=17/4. Expressing the three real coordinates J in these
four complex modes uses rows with absolute coefficient sums 2,1,1.
Consequently deleting mass tau changes any entry of the real work
matrix by less than 92tau. We use the simpler uniform bound 100tau.
The normal work terms have error less than 23tau.

These inequalities prove existence of the infinite-word moments. They
also prove convergence from the ACTUAL words in (10). Indeed, retain
only their N largest levels. The resulting finite word converges to
the displayed N-level truncation, including its chronological order.
For fixed N the deleted normalized mass converges to epsilon_N:
the normalized total mass is exactly one and the retained masses
converge individually. Apply (12), first let m tend to infinity, and
then let N tend to infinity. The removed original d_0 is among the
deleted levels when m>N, so this argument also handles it explicitly.
We obtain E_m->E and convergence of the two normal work coefficients.

The left-half product and bridge/endpoint products are

 L(zeta)=product_(j>=1)(1-delta lambda^(-j)zeta)^(2^(j-1)),
 p_l=L(zeta_l),   v_l=(1-delta zeta_l)p_l,
 t_l=p_l v_l.                                          (13)

For the actual words, the corresponding products are exactly
v_l,m=(1-d_(m-1)z_l)p_l,m and
t_l,m=(1-d_(m-1)z_l)p_l,m^2/(1-d_0 z_l).
The last denominator tends to one. Deletion of a small total mass and
the same product bound prove convergence to (13). Thus K_m and D_l,m
converge entrywise to the quantities K,D_l given by (7)--(8) and the
limiting work moments.

## 4. Finite rational enclosures of the fixed limiting coefficients

Everything in this section is bounded arithmetic for one fixed
coefficient matrix; no PEP or optimization evaluation is used.

For the product (13) define mu_s=delta^s/(lambda^s-2). Absolutely
convergent logarithmic expansion gives

 log L(zeta)=-sum_(s>=1)mu_s zeta^s/s.

Let A_10 be the sum through s=10. Since mu_2<1/125,
|zeta|^2<=17/4, and eta=|zeta|delta/lambda<3/20, the omitted tail is

 <=mu_2 |zeta|^2 eta^9/[11(1-eta)] < 1/10^9.           (14)

The bound on mu_s used here is mu_s<=mu_2(delta/lambda)^(s-2), obtained
directly by summing the positive powers of the left-half step sizes.
Compute exp(A_10) through degree18. The bounds Re A_10<0 and |A_10|<1
give exponential tail <3/19!. Perturbing its argument by (14) changes
the exponential by <(10^-9)/(1-10^-9). Hence error 2/10^9 in each real
component safely covers both tails.

For the moment (11), its exact concatenation recurrence is short.
If a word has products p_A,p_B and moment W, appending its central
step d and another copy gives

 p_A,new=p_A^2(1-dA),  p_B,new=p_B^2(1-dB),
 W_new=W[1+p_A p_B(1-dA)(1-dB)]
                     +d p_A p_B[1-d(A+B)/2].           (15)

The first copy contributes W, the central step gives the last term,
and the second copy is multiplied by p_A p_B(1-dA)(1-dB), proving
the identity. Use N=112 levels in (15). The rational bound

                 100(2/lambda)^112 < 1/10^7             (16)

and (12) supply the error for every resulting real work coefficient.

For a completely specified finite arithmetic procedure, use the interval

 r_- = 1.41421356237309504880168872420969807856967187537694,
 r_+ = r_-+10^-50

for sqrt(2); its squared endpoints straddle 2. Set lambda=1+[r_-,r_+]
and delta=1-2/lambda. Interval additions, products, and positive
reciprocals enclose their exact values. After every intermediate
operation round its lower endpoint down and upper endpoint up to a
multiple of 10^-60. This only enlarges an enclosure and prevents
denominator growth. Evaluate A_10, then its degree18 exponential using
t_0=1, t_j=t_(j-1)A_10/j. Add the componentwise error in (14). For
the work moments, use (15) on all sixteen pairs of the four modes.

The coefficients expressing J in these four modes, in that order, are

 c_1=(1/2,1/2,-1/2,-1/2),
 c_2=(-i/2,i/2,0,0), c_3=(0,0,-i/2,i/2).

The real work matrix entries are
E_kl=Re sum_(r,s)c_kr c_ls zeta_r zeta_s W(zeta_r,zeta_s).
The two normal chain coefficients are
C_1=1/2-(1/2)W(zeta_1,conjugate(zeta_1)) and
C_2=2-(17/4)W(zeta_2,conjugate(zeta_2)).
Add error interval [-10^-7,10^-7] to these expressions. This includes
(16); all preceding rounding errors are already in the intervals.

The following outward rational enclosures result. Finite decimals are
exact rational numbers; the margins are deliberately larger than the
rounding errors.

| quantity | enclosing interval |
|---|---|
| Re p_1 | [.7952608488,.7952608529] |
| Im p_1 | [-.1687257189,-.1687257148] |
| Re p_2 | [.4200940450,.4200940491] |
| Im p_2 | [-.0920602833,-.0920602792] |
| E_11 | [.3738957,.3738960] |
| E_12 | [-.1629610,-.1629607] |

| E_22 | [.0952537,.0952540] |

Substituting the directly computed intervals in (7)--(8), at theta=6/25,
gives

 19/100 < D_1 < 193/1000,       329/1000 < D_2 < 33/100,
 -132/1000 < K_11 < -131/1000,
 21/10000 < K_11 K_22-K_12^2 < 22/10000,
 -18/10^8 < det K < -15/10^8.                           (17)

These are finite rational inequalities obtained by the displayed
recurrences, without eigenvalue computation. The three successive
diagonal pivots in completing the square are
K_11, (K_11 K_22-K_12^2)/K_11, det K/(K_11 K_22-K_12^2).

The companion chain_anchor_interval_check.py implements these exact
interval operations and asserts (17). Its first version was stopped
because an unrounded exponential expression caused denominator growth.
The corrected version rounds the intermediate log/exponential terms
and the fixed-size moment recurrence; it exits zero. An earlier
ordinary floating-point exploration was not used as proof: repeated
squaring of factors extremely close to one loses significant small-step
mass in floating arithmetic. The rational calculation and its explicit
tail estimates are the evidence for (17).

## 5. Finite-word uniformity, free terminal step, and exact benchmark

Entrywise convergence and the strict inequalities (17) imply that for
all sufficiently large m, the EXACT K_m is negative definite and
D_l,m<1/3. None of those coefficients depends on w or T. Since
trace(T^T T K_m) is a sum of nonpositive row quadratic forms, (9) gives
F(x_q)<=1/(3S), uniformly even for coupling matrices diverging with m.

Integration of the 1-Lipschitz gradient along the final segment gives

 F(x_q-b g_q)<=F(x_q)-b(1-b/2)||g_q||^2<=F(x_q),

for all b in [0,2]. The terminal gradient and value are free; this
proves (2) for the same interpolating F.

Here is the comparison with the exact project benchmark, proved rather
than imported from an unverified finding. Let rho=log_2 lambda,
C_k=S_circle(k)+1, and B_k=2S_bullet(k)+1. The accepted recursions give

 C_0=B_0=1,
 C_n=max_(0<=j<n)Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
 B_n=max_(0<=j<n)G(C_j,B_(n-j-1)),
 Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,
 G(A,B)=2A+B/2+sqrt(B^2+8AB)/2.

For V(t)=(1+t)^rho-1, differentiation gives, with t=exp u,

 d^2/du^2 log V(exp u)
 =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)[(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/V(t)^2 > 0.

The bracket vanishes at zero and has positive derivative for t>0.
Convexity at u and -u implies V(t)V(1/t)>=V(1)^2=2. If A,B>0 and
M=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho, this means (M-A)(M-B)>=2AB;
the positive root of this quadratic is Omega(A,B). Thus
Omega(A,B)<=M and induction gives C_k<=(k+1)^rho.
The inequality sqrt(B^2+8AB)<=B+4A yields G(A,B)<=B+4A.
Using u^rho+v^rho<=(u+v)^rho for nonnegative u,v proves by induction
B_n<=1+4n^rho. The latter inequality follows by differentiating
(1+t)^rho-t^rho, whose minimum for t>=0 is one.

At n=2^m-1, n^rho/lambda^m->1 and S/lambda^m->e by (10).
Multiplying (2) by B_n proves (3). Finally e>sum_(j=0)^4 1/j!=65/24,
so 8/(3e)<64/65.

## 6. Why the chronology is necessary in this certificate

Define chi(v_1,v_2)=Re(v_1-v_2)/4+Im v_1/5+Im v_2.
It vanishes at (1,1). Apply it to the left, right, and endpoint modal
pairs in (13), obtaining y_-,y_+,y_q and, after multiplication by
the modal zeta values, u_-,u_+,u_q. The coefficients of its squared
amplitude in the two individual bridge-anchor bounds are

 k_-=u_q y_q+(u_--u_q)y_-,
 k_+=u_q y_q+(u_+-u_q)y_+.

The same rational product enclosures give

        23/100000 < k_- < 24/100000,
       103/100000 < k_+ < 104/100000.                    (18)

Every convex combination of just these two anchor matrices therefore
has a strictly positive direction. This refutes a purely algebraic
extension of the two-anchor method to the full three-dimensional
space. It is NOT a legal high-payoff construction. Adding the actual
chronological chain supplies a different constraint and yields (17).

## 7. Scope that remains

The proof covers arbitrary PSD zero-initial additions to the displayed
two normal blocks, arbitrary joint values, and the free terminal step.
It does not cover arbitrary inner products that couple an added
coordinate to the initial direction, nor other scaled spectra. A
general PSD metric on the whole four-dimensional cyclic space has
additional initial-direction cross terms. Extending a coefficient
certificate to that space requires controlling those terms as well;
negative definiteness on J alone is insufficient. The project's
all-schedule exact-profile target remains unresolved.

glossary.M: PSD added-coordinate metric T^T T; no bound on amplitude or horizon dependence.

glossary.W_word: Bilinear chronological moment sum d_t P_t(A)P_t(B)[1-d_t(A+B)/2].
glossary.epsilon_N: Omitted normalized mass (2/lambda)^N after keeping the N largest levels of the limiting recursive word.
glossary.chi: Real row Re(v1-v2)/4+Im(v1)/5+Im(v2), positive on BOTH individual bridge-anchor quadratic matrices.

substitution; no interpolation constraints are imposed on test vectors.

Fix a>0,c>0 and define

    d_j=a c^j,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+d_j,H_j),
    n_j=2^j-1, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

The initial block in the certificate recursion is H_1=(1+a), not H_0.
For each block choose real u_j,v_j, with final v_m>0, and a multiplier array
lambda^(j) on its samples and star. Require the following star pattern:

    lambda_(star,i)=h_i             for every queried i<n_j,
    lambda_(star,n_j)=u_j,
    lambda_(i,star)=0               for i<n_j,
    lambda_(n_j,star)=s_j,
    s_j=S_j+u_j-v_j.                                      (1)

Here s_j is only an incoming optimum multiplier, not the stepsize sum S_j.
All final actual multipliers must be nonnegative if the array is to certify
an objective bound. We will prove a necessary condition even without using
those signs. Assume exact cancellation of every function-value coefficient
in the identity defining the gradient-only remainder E_j:

    ||x_start||^2-||x_end-u_j g_end||^2-2v_j f_end
            =sum lambda^(j)_ik C_ik+E_j.                  (2)

Put

    Z_j=(u_j-1)^2+v_j,
    z_j=sum_(i<n_j) h_i g_i+g_end.                         (3)

The seed may be ANY one-step array satisfying (1)--(2). Its remainder need
not be PSD. In particular this includes the primitive one-step seed in the
shared construction, with u_1=M_1,v_1=2M_1-1 and
E_1=(2-(1+a)^2)||g_0-g_1||^2.

Here is the permitted join. Write n=n_j,p=n,q=2n+1,S=S_j,
d=d_j,b=1+d,M=M_j. Choose parameters A,B,P,Q with

    r=1+A+B,
    P-Q=b+(1-A)S.                                       (4)

Embed one copy of the old array on the left block and r times the same
array on the right block. For every right queried index i=p+1,...,q-1 add

    A h_i to (p,i), B h_i to (q,i),
    -(A+B)h_i to (star,i).                               (5)

Add the following six sparse corrections:

    (p,q): P,                    (q,p): Q,
    (p,star): -s_j,              (q,star): s_(j+1)-r s_j,
    (star,p): b-u_j,             (star,q): u_(j+1)-r u_j.  (6)

No restriction to H=ell=0, greedy choices of Z, PSD local terms, rank-one
child remainders, or PSD child remainders is imposed. The final objective
matrix must still be PSD on the full formal space. Nonnegative actual
coefficients, when they hold, include all the star coefficients in (1);
requiring A,B,P,Q>=0 is a sufficient way to preserve the other signs.

The desired result is a necessary condition for ANY such recursion. It is
therefore valid for every choice of its parameters that passes all actual
sign tests, including choices depending on the target horizon.

## 2. The complete local identity

Define

    t=A-B,
    H=M+d-B(M-d)-t M,
    ell=P-A,
    V=x_p-x_q-g_p+g_q.

The exact recursion for the entire gradient remainder is

    E_(j+1)=E_j(left)+r E_j(right)
       +t||V||^2+2<V,(H-ell)g_p+ell g_q>
       +(Z_j-rd^2)||g_p||^2+(rZ_j-Z_(j+1))||g_q||^2.    (7)

We verify both the value and quadratic coefficients. Write x=x_p,g=g_p,
y=x_q,e=g_q, and w=sum_(p<i<q)h_i g_i=x-bg-y. Summing (5) gives

    2AS f_p+2BS f_q-AS||g||^2-BS||e||^2
                      -2<w,A(x-g)+B(y-e)>.             (8)

This follows by expanding a summand: the coefficient of each f_i and of
each ||g_i||^2 cancels, leaving the displayed linear and bilinear terms.
The value coefficient at p in the two children plus (5)--(6) is

    -2v_j+2AS+2(P-Q)-2s_j-2(b-u_j)
       =2[(A-1)S+P-Q-b]=0.

The coefficient at q is

    -2r v_j+2BS-2(P-Q)+2(s_(j+1)-r s_j)
                         -2(u_(j+1)-r u_j)=-2v_(j+1).

This uses (1),(4) and r=1+A+B. All other values have already canceled.

For completeness, the quadratic parts of the six expressions used in (6)
are respectively

    C_pq: 2<e,y-x>-||g-e||^2,
    C_qp: 2<g,x-y>-||g-e||^2,
    C_pstar: -||g||^2,       C_qstar: -||e||^2,
    C_starp: 2<g,x>-||g||^2,
    C_starq: 2<e,y>-||e||^2.

Subtract their weighted sum and (8) from the new potential minus the two
child potentials. With D=x-y, all dependence on the separate x,y cancels.
The resulting coefficients, using the convention that cross coefficients
multiply twice the stated inner product, are

    ||D||^2: t,
    <D,g>: H-ell-t,               <D,e>: ell+t,
    ||g||^2: Z_j-rd^2+t-2H+2ell,
    ||e||^2: rZ_j-Z_(j+1)+t+2ell,
    <g,e>: H-2ell-t.

Substituting V=D-g+e gives (7). Thus (7) concerns the full original
gradient space, not only a condensed boundary form.

## 3. A formal template on which all mixed terms vanish

Define nonzero signed scalars

    k_1=2+a=M_1,
    k_(j+1)=-k_j^2/d_j,       j>=1.                       (9)

For each block H_j and each vector e, there is an explicit formal gradient
assignment, linear in e, with terminal gradient e such that

    z_j=k_j e,
    E_j=(k_j^2-Z_j)||e||^2.                              (10)

Crucially this is true for EVERY parameter choice in (4)--(6). The same
template (9) works after a change of the storage variables, multiplier
weights, or mixed boundary terms.

First check the seed carefully. From (1)--(2), subtraction of the star
terms gives the intrinsic identity

    E_j=2sum_(i<n_j)h_i(f_i-f_end)
          +sum_(i<n_j)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
          +(M_j-Z_j)||g_end||^2
          -sum_(i!=k finite)lambda^(j)_ik C_ik.          (11)

To obtain (11), use
||x_start||^2-||x_end||^2
 =2sum h_i<g_i,x_i>-sum h_i^2||g_i||^2
and s_j=S_j+u_j-v_j. This also verifies that no hypothesis s_j=0 is needed.

Assign both seed gradients equal to e, and set the formal values
f_i=<e,x_i>-||e||^2/2. Every finite C_ik is then zero. More generally,
for a constant-gradient block with prefix sums P_i,
f_i-f_end=(S_j-P_i)||e||^2 and

    2sum h_i(S_j-P_i)+sum h_i(1-h_i)=S_j(S_j+1).

The latter equality follows from
sum_i h_i sum_(t>=i)h_t=(S_j^2+sum_i h_i^2)/2.
Equation (11) therefore evaluates to (M_j^2-Z_j)||e||^2.
For H_1, z_1=(2+a)e=k_1 e, proving (10). The auxiliary values merely
evaluate a polynomial identity; they are not claimed to be feasible jets.

Suppose (10) holds at level j. In the right child use its template with
terminal vector e. In the left child use its template with terminal vector

    g=-k_j e/d_j.

The block displacement gives exactly

    V=d_j g+z_right=0,
    z_parent=z_left+d_j g+z_right=z_left=k_j g=k_(j+1)e.  (12)

Evaluating the ENTIRE right side of (7), rather than discarding any child
part, now gives

    E_(j+1)
      =(k_j^2-Z_j)||g||^2+r(k_j^2-Z_j)||e||^2
           +(Z_j-rd_j^2)||g||^2+(rZ_j-Z_(j+1))||e||^2
      =[(k_j^2-rd_j^2)k_j^2/d_j^2+r k_j^2-Z_(j+1)]||e||^2
      =(k_j^4/d_j^2-Z_(j+1))||e||^2.

This is (10) at the parent. Neither E_j>=0 nor Z_j=k_j^2 was used.
In particular reducing Z at an earlier join does not remove the test:
its resulting positive template energy is carried exactly into the next
calculation and cancels with that join's storage terms.

## 4. Even changing the final initial-distance coefficient cannot repair it

Write u=u_m,v=v_m>0,k=k_m,Z=(u-1)^2+v. The full objective certificate
generated by the final array, at any proposed level q_cert, is

    M_cert=q_cert||x_0||^2-2f_n
                         +sum_(i!=j) (2lambda^(m)_ji/v) Q_ij
       =(q_cert-1/v)||x_0||^2
                         +[||x_n-u g_n||^2+E_m]/v.       (13)

The whole formula follows from (2) and C_ij=-2Q_ji. Its actual
interpolation multipliers are nonnegative when the lambda array is.

Apply (10), keep the initial formal vector x_0 independent, and write e
for the terminal template vector. Since z_m=k e,

    x_n-u g_n=x_0-(k+u-1)e.

Set beta=k+u-1. The restriction of v M_cert to the two independent
scalar coordinates in x_0,e has matrix

                    [ q_cert v      -beta       ]
                    [   -beta       2k beta-v   ].       (14)

Indeed its second diagonal is
beta^2+k^2-Z=2k(k+u-1)-v. Full PSD requires (14) PSD.
Its lower diagonal cannot be zero: PSD would then force beta=0, making
that diagonal -v<0. Consequently 2k beta-v>0, and its determinant gives

    q_cert >= beta^2/[v(2k beta-v)] >= 1/k^2.             (15)

For the last inequality use the exact identity

    k^2 beta^2-v(2k beta-v)=(v-k beta)^2>=0.

Both denominators are positive. Thus (15) holds whether E_m is PSD or
indefinite, whether q_cert equals 1/v or is increased, and whether any
child storage was selected greedily. All nonlinear mixing parameters in
(7) have vanished from the necessary bound.

This is a full-space certificate obstruction. Passing the test on legal
sampled trajectories alone would not suffice, since the formal gradient
assignment used in (10) is generally not a legal transcript.

## 5. Quantitative growing-horizon consequence for the assigned words

Fix an integer m>=128, set epsilon=1/m, lambda=1+sqrt(2), and use the
actual assignment

    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c,
    d_j=(1-epsilon)c^(j-1), 1<=j<=m.

The symbol d_m is used only to express the recurrence solution; H_m uses
the bridges d_0,...,d_(m-1). Put

    R=(2+a)/[c(1-epsilon)].

Solving (9) in absolute value gives

    |k_j|=(1-epsilon)c^j R^(2^(j-1)),   1<=j<=m.          (16)

To check (16), divide |k_j| by c d_j. This ratio is R at j=1 and
is squared at every next step, since d_(j+1)=c d_j.

There is a strict gap below one in R, with an explicit uniform constant:

    1-R = epsilon[2-lambda^2 epsilon(1+epsilon)]
                  /[lambda^2(1+epsilon)^2(1-epsilon)]
          > epsilon/4.                                  (17)

For the equality multiply by c^2(1-epsilon). Its numerator is
lambda^2(1+epsilon)^2(1-epsilon)
 -[lambda^2+(2lambda-1)epsilon]
 =2epsilon-lambda^2 epsilon^2(1+epsilon),
using lambda^2=2lambda+1. For the inequality, lambda^2<6 and
epsilon<=1/128 imply

    2-lambda^2 epsilon(1+epsilon)>7/4,
    lambda^2(1+epsilon)^2(1-epsilon)<7.

Also R>0 from its definition. The bound 1-x<=exp(-x), proved for
0<=x<1 by integrating the derivative of log(1-x), now yields

    |k_m| < c^m exp[-2^(m-3)/m].                         (18)

Here c<5/2: sqrt(2)<10/7 gives
c<(17/7)(129/128)=2193/896<5/2. Combining (15),(18) gives

    q_cert > (2/5)^(2m) exp[2^(m-2)/m] -> infinity.       (19)

The limit follows because 2^m/m^2 tends to infinity: its successive ratio
is 2m^2/(m+1)^2>3/2 for all m>=7. In particular the exponential term in
the logarithm of (19) dominates the linear term 2m log(5/2).

Already for every m>=128, (18) gives |k_m|<1 and hence q_cert>1.
For an explicit elementary comparison, exp(1)>1+1+1/2+1/6>5/2, so
log(5/2)<1, while 2^(m-3)>m^2 for every m>=16 by checking m=16
and noting that 2m^2/(m+1)^2>1 thereafter. Thus the exponent in (18),
after bounding c^m by exp(m), is negative.

No upper coefficient from this family can therefore approach the small
objective levels needed for a comparison with the exact Zhang--Jiang
profile. This is stronger than failure of the previously chosen H=ell=0
rule: all the mixed terms, all retained child matrices, all earlier
storage choices, and arbitrary q_cert were included in the derivation.

## 6. Scope and the surviving repair directions

The obstruction covers exactly the repeated-copy array (4)--(6), started
from any H_1 seed with the star pattern (1). The identity requires neither
PSD child remainders nor local PSD checks, and the final test includes x_0
and every original gradient coordinate. It also permits nonzero incoming
terminal optimum weights s_j and arbitrary u_j,v_j consistent with (1).

It does NOT exclude another complete interpolation array for H_m. In
particular C51's finite H_3 certificate uses a different unrestricted
array, and is consistent with this result. The obstruction also does not
automatically cover independent internal coefficient changes at a parent,
additional interpolation edges or corrections outside (5)--(6), a
different star pattern, or a different seed size allowed to grow with m.

The concrete repair requirement is now an algebraic one: a useful changed
array must act nontrivially on the template (10)--(12). Altering only the
local V-dependent terms cannot do that. Nor can changing Z alone, since
the precise earlier template energy is propagated in (10).

For literature context, the gluing-plus-rank-one-plus-sparse architecture
is present in Altschuler--Parrilo, arXiv:2309.16530v1, Theorem 3.4 and its
proof in Sections 3.1--3.2. The exact paper was downloaded and read. No
statement from that paper is imported into this proof, and its certificate
for the undeformed silver schedule is not claimed to apply after the
present parameter deformation.

All new claims here remain candidates until verifier acceptance. The
original unrestricted target remains unresolved.

Exact DP induction gives B_n<=lambda P_n; P_n<=(n+1)^rho and P_(2^m-1)=lambda^m, rho=log_2lambda. On actual critical H_m, limsup B_(2^m-1) K_Hub,m<=lambda/(2e), so q_m/K_Hub,m<2e/lambda asymptotically suffices. In particular q_m<=1/M_m gives limsup q_m B<=lambda/e<1. evidence:
Definitions from accepted b98bb807d514e80d: P_n=S_circle(n)+1, B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1, P0=B0=1. Their exact recursions are P_n=max_(k+l=n-1)F(P_k,P_l), B_n=max_(k+l=n-1)G(P_k,B_l), with F(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2 and G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2.

SCALAR COMPARISON. Set alpha=2lambda-1=lambda(4-lambda)>0, L=(4x+lambda^2 y)/alpha. Its coefficients exceed1, so L>=x+y. Exact expansion gives alpha^2[L^2-(x+y)L-xy]=(2x/lambda-sqrt2 lambda y)^2>=0. Thus L>=F(x,y), the positive root of z^2-(x+y)z-xy=0. At z=lambda F(x,y), the polynomial defining G(x,lambda y) evaluates to z^2-(4x+lambda y)z+4x^2=x[4x+lambda^2 y-alpha F(x,y)]>=0. Also z>=lambda(x+y)>=(4x+lambda y)/2, so it lies above the larger root G. Equality holds for x=0 and for x/y=lambda^2/sqrt2 with y>0. Homogeneity gives G(x,c y)/c=G(x/c,y), strictly decreasing in c for x>0, so any c<lambda fails at that equality point. No squaring-sign condition was omitted.

DP INDUCTION. G is nondecreasing in its second argument. If B_l<=lambda P_l, then G(P_k,B_l)<=G(P_k,lambda P_l)<=lambda F(P_k,P_l). Taking maxima proves B_n<=lambda P_n from the base.

DYADIC PRIMITIVE BOUND, NO PROFILE LIMIT. Let rho=log_2lambda>1. For t>0 put D(t)=(1+t)^rho-1 and g(z)=log D(exp z). With t=exp z, differentiation gives g''(z)=rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)[(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/D(t)^2>0. The bracket is positive by its derivative rho[(1+t)^(rho-1)-1]>0 and its zero value at0. Consequently D(t)D(1/t)>=D(1)^2=(lambda-1)^2=2. For x,y>0 put A=x^(1/rho),B=y^(1/rho),T=(A+B)^rho. This inequality gives (T-x)(T-y)>=2xy, so T^2-(x+y)T-xy>=0; T>=x+y by superadditivity of the power, and hence F(x,y)<=T. Zero arguments follow directly. Induction now gives P_n<=(n+1)^rho. Balanced joins give P_(2^m-1)>=lambda^m, hence equality. Therefore B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^(m+1) at every m.

ACTUAL NORMALIZATION. For c_m=lambda(1+1/m),a_m=(1-1/m)/c_m and H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_m c_m^j,H_j), M_j=1+sum H_j satisfies M_(j+1)=2M_j+a_m c_m^j. Thus M_m=A_m c_m^m+(1-A_m)2^m, A_m=a_m/(c_m-2)->1, and M_m/lambda^m->e. Define explicitly K_Hub,m=1/(2M_m-1), without presuming that this equals every earlier K notation. Then limsup B K_Hub<=lambda/(2e). If a genuine full certificate supplies q_m<=C K_Hub,m+o(K_Hub,m) for any C<2e/lambda, then limsup q_m B<=C lambda/(2e)<1. Equivalently q_m M_m has limsup<e/lambda as a sufficient condition. In particular q_m<=1/M_m would give limsup q_m B<=lambda/e<1; lambda<5/2<e. This is a sufficient scalar threshold only, not an upper certificate. The same proof yields thresholds 2exp(tau)/lambda and exp(tau)/lambda for the fixed deformation c_m=lambda(1+tau/m),a_m=(1-sigma/m)/c_m. All new statements remain unverified candidates; accepted b98 provides definitions, and all new inequalities are proved here rather than using unverified findings as premises.
