evidence:
# Independent proof weights: an exact join and a full-matrix obstruction

Status: joint, self-contained UNVERIFIED candidate. No solver and no
fact_submit. This is a failure of explicitly specified multiplier families,
not a lower witness for the schedules and not a resolution of the target.

The accepted mathematical input is the interpolation inequality from
fact `1252b8823bb5a290`. The weighted-history approach was informed by
Grimmer--Shu--Wang, *Composing Optimized Stepsize Schedules for Gradient
Descent*, arXiv:2410.16249, Proposition 4 and its proof, and by the public
finite candidate C51 (047c257795dc59ba). Neither unverified C51 nor an
external composability theorem is used as a proof premise. In particular,
no quadratic-product equality or primitive hypothesis is imposed here.

## 1. Full objective certificate with independent proof weights

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. For distinct sampled indices use

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0,
    C_ij=-2Q_ji
        =2(f_i-f_j)+2<g_j,x_j-x_i>-||g_i-g_j||^2 >=0.

Set C_ii=0. All positions are the actual GD substitutions. The formal
vectors x_0,g_0,...,g_n remain independent.

For a block h of length n, write S=sum h_i, P=x_start-x_end=sum h_i g_i.
Choose nonnegative proof weights w_0,...,w_n with D=sum w_i>0, and define

    W=sum_i w_i g_i,
    J_w=2sum_i w_i(f_i-f_end)+sum_i w_i||g_i||^2
          +2sum_i w_i<g_i,x_start-x_i>-||W||^2.

The exact identity, retaining the initial distance, is

    ||x_start||^2-2D f_end+2sum_i w_i Q_(i,star)
        =||x_start-W||^2+J_w.                         (1)

Suppose a finite-edge array lambda_ij>=0 gives

    J_w=sum_(finite i!=j) lambda_ij C_ij+R.            (2)

Its necessary and sufficient value cancellation is

    out_i-in_i=w_i-D 1_(i=end),                       (3)

where out_i=sum_j lambda_ij and in_i=sum_j lambda_ji.
For every real q the resulting complete full objective identity is

    q||x_start||^2-2f_end
      +2/D sum_i w_i Q_(i,star)
      +2/D sum_(finite i!=j) lambda_ij Q_ji
       =(q-1/D)||x_start||^2
          +[||x_start-W||^2+R]/D.                    (4)

Every multiplier in (4) is nonnegative. At q=1/D, its full PSD condition
is exactly R>=0, since x_start can be set equal to W in the formal space.
This formulation places no equality between the proof weights and h.

When D=2S+1, all finite gradients equal to one give J_w=0 after using
f_i-f_end=S-P_i, where P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t. These are legal Huber jets
with x_start=D and x_i=D-P_i. Every finite C_ij is zero. Consequently
R(1,...,1)=0, and if R is PSD then R annihilates the all-ones vector.

## 2. A first-gradient condition for EVERY such full certificate

Assume n>=1 and h_0=1+a with a>0. Let e_0 mean the formal assignment
g_0=1 and every other block gradient zero. All finite positions after
the first step have the same displacement h_0 from the start. Directly
from (2)--(3),

    R(e_0)=w_0-w_0^2+out_0-(2h_0-1)in_0
          =2w_0-w_0^2-2a in_0.                      (5)

Thus the g_0 diagonal of the full unscaled matrix
||x_start-W||^2+R at x_start=0 is

    2w_0-2a in_0.                                   (6)

This calculation uses all finite edges, without a support assumption.
In particular any PSD certificate needs in_0<=w_0/a.

Also every PSD certificate in this form has w_0>0. Indeed, if w_0=0,
(5) and PSD force in_0=out_0=0. Hence no finite edge touches index 0.
Every remaining finite position difference cancels the term h_0 g_0.
In J_w, however, the g_0 cross coefficient with g_i is 2h_0 w_i for
i>0. At least one such w_i is positive because D>0. R would then have
a zero g_0 diagonal and a nonzero g_0 row, impossible for a PSD matrix:
the two-variable restriction 2bxy+cy^2 with b!=0 takes negative values.

## 3. The complete four-fan join, with both moments retained

Take two certificates (2) on the same physical block h, with proof
weights w^L,w^R, each of mass D=2S+1; the two arrays and remainders
may differ. Let p=n be the left endpoint and q=2n+1 the parent endpoint.
Insert the actual bridge b=1+d, d>=0, and denote

    M=S+1, T=M+d, M'=2M+d, S'=M'-1, D'=2M'-1,
    g=g_p, e=g_q,
    P_L=sum_(left queried i) h_i g_i,
    P_R=sum_(right queried i) h_i g_i,
    W_L=sum_(left samples i) w^L_i g_i,
    W_R=sum_(right samples i) w^R_i g_i.

Choose nonnegative u,r,A,E and real B,C,k,l,p0,q0. The proposed parent weights
are u w^L on the left, r w^R on the right, with k added at p and l at q.
Require every FINAL parent weight to be nonnegative and

    (u+r)D+k+l=D'.                                  (7)

Set gamma_L=u+C+E and gamma_R=r+A+B. Embed gamma_L times the entire
left finite array and gamma_R times the entire right finite array.
Add the following endpoint fans, omitting self edges:

    C w^L_i on (p,i),    E w^L_i on (q,i),   i in left samples,
    A w^R_i on (p,i),    B w^R_i on (q,i),   i in right samples.

Finally add p0 on (p,q) and q0 on (q,p), where

    p0-q0=(u-A+E)D+k.                               (8)

Require gamma_L,gamma_R>=0 and EVERY FINAL finite coefficient to be
nonnegative. The corrections B,C,p0,q0 may themselves be negative when
already present coefficients compensate them. Positivity is checked
after addition, rather than separately on each correction. A,E are
cross-copy fan coefficients whose edges to queried interiors are absent
from the child arrays; they must be nonnegative when those weights are
positive. No earlier interpolation constraint is silently removed; the
final array is the explicitly stated sum.
Define W'=u W_L+r W_R+k g+l e. The exact
parent identity has remainder

    R'=gamma_L R_L+gamma_R R_R+F,                    (9)

where the COMPLETE local quadratic is

    F=gamma_L||W_L||^2+gamma_R||W_R||^2-||W'||^2
       +2r<W_R,P_L+b g>
       +k||g||^2+2k<g,P_L>
       +l||e||^2+2l<e,P_L+b g+P_R>
       -2(C+E)<W_L,P_L>-2C<W_L,g>
       -2E<W_L,b g+P_R+e>
       +(A+C)D||g||^2+(B+E)D||e||^2
       +2A d<g,W_R>-2B<W_R,P_R+e>
       +p0[||g||^2+||e||^2+2d<g,e>+2<e,P_R>]
       +q0[-(2b-1)||g||^2+||e||^2-2<g,e>-2<g,P_R>]. (10)

Here P_L and W_L are genuinely distinct; none of their cross terms has
been discarded. To verify (9)--(10), the four fan identities are

    sum_L w_i C_(p,i)
       =-J_L-||W_L||^2+2<W_L,P_L+g>-D||g||^2,
    sum_L w_i C_(q,i)
       =-J_L-||W_L||^2+2<W_L,P_L+b g+P_R+e>
                                            -D||e||^2-2D(f_p-f_q),
    sum_R w_i C_(p,i)
       =2D(f_p-f_q)-J_R-||W_R||^2
                                            -2d<g,W_R>-D||g||^2,
    sum_R w_i C_(q,i)
       =-J_R-||W_R||^2+2<W_R,P_R+e>-D||e||^2.       (11)

Expanding J of the concatenated weights and subtracting (11) leaves
the value coefficient 2[(u-A+E)D+k-p0+q0](f_p-f_q), which is zero
by (8), and exactly (10). This proves every value and Gram coefficient.

### Full undeformed Silver calibration of this interface

For a block whose proof weights are (h_0,...,h_(n-1),M), one has
D=2M-1 and W=P+M g_end. Substitution in J gives

    V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)
          +sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-SM||g_n||^2.

In (9)--(10) choose, for 0<=d<M,

    z=(M+d)/(M-d), u=r=1, A=B=z, C=E=0,
    k=1+d-M, l=M+d,
    p0=z(1-M), q0=z d.                              (11a)

Although p0 can be negative, its FINAL (p,q) coefficient is zM+p0=z,
and the (q,p) coefficient is z d. All other new entries are nonnegative;
the midpoint proof weight becomes 1+d and the terminal weight M'.
The child scales are 1 and 1+2z. Substituting W_L=P_L+Mg and W_R=P_R+Me
into the FULL quadratic (10), without falsely treating dependent
moments as independent, yields exactly

    F=[M^2-(1+2z)d^2]||g||^2
            +[(1+2z)M^2-(2M+d)^2]||e||^2.          (11b)

Set lambda=1+sqrt(2), M=lambda^j and d=lambda^(j-1).
Then z=lambda, 1+2z=lambda^2 and M'=lambda M, so both
coefficients in (11b) vanish. Starting with the empty block, weight 1
and zero finite array, induction gives a full Huber-level certificate
for every undeformed Silver word, with zero remainder. At the first
step its finite entries are lambda and 1. This is a proved algebraic
calibration; no primitive or composability theorem is imported.

The independence assumption below is essential: these calibrated
Silver certificates have W=P+Mg_end and do not satisfy it.

## 4. A whole-family obstruction when the left moments are independent

Assume the two child remainders are PSD. Suppose that the left queried
weight vector (w^L_0,...,w^L_(n-1)) is not proportional to the physical
step vector (h_0,...,h_(n-1)). Then the three formal linear forms
(P_L,W_L,g) are independent. The terminal gradient is an independent
coordinate, and the two queried coefficient rows are linearly independent.

If (9) were PSD, it would annihilate the all-ones gradient vector, as
would both child remainders. Hence F must be stationary at

    P_L=P_R=S, W_L=W_R=D, g=e=1.

The P_L derivative in (10), divided by 2, is

    rD+k+l-(C+E)D=D'-gamma_L D.

The W_L derivative, divided by 2, is

    gamma_L D-uD'-CM-EM'.

Independence of P_L,W_L,g therefore forces

    gamma_L=gamma:=D'/D,
    CM+EM'=D'(1-u),
    E=[gamma S-u(D'-M)]/(M+d).                      (12)

Since E>=0, every member of this four-fan family satisfying full PSD
at the Huber value necessarily obeys

    u/gamma<=S/(D'-M)= (M-1)/(3M+2d-1).             (13)

On the other hand, evaluate the FULL parent matrix (4) at x_start=0,
g_0=1 and every other parent gradient zero. The additional incoming
finite mass at index 0 is (C+E)w^L_0. Formula (6) gives its unscaled
value exactly as

    2w^L_0[(1+a)u-a gamma]-2a gamma in^L_0.          (14)

The child has w^L_0>0 by Section 2. Thus the parent matrix is strictly
negative whenever

    (M-1)/(3M+2d-1) < a/(1+a).                     (15)

Equivalently, (15) says (1-2a)M<1+2ad. A simple sufficient domain is

    a>=2/5, d/M>=a.                                (16)

Indeed 2a^2+2a-1>=3/25>0 there, so
(1-2a)M-2ad <=(1-2a-2a^2)M<0<1.

Consequently NO such Huber-tight four-fan join is possible in (16)
when the left child has independent physical and proof moments.
The conclusion allows signed corrections B,C,p0,q0 subject to actual
final multiplier positivity. Its proof only needs E>=0. The child
arrays may be dense and contain all ordered finite pairs;
the obstruction does not result from deleting their earlier edges.

The proportional queried-weight case is expressly outside this argument.
So is a different cross-block edge pattern, a nonsaturated objective
construction that changes the weights and multipliers, or a general
unrestricted certificate. This is not a nonexistence theorem for H_m.

## 5. An explicit recursively specified candidate, rejected at every q

There is a particularly simple fully specified instance of (9). For
every join put V=D'-M=3M+2d-1 and

    gamma=D'/D, z=gamma(M+d)/V,
    u=gamma-2z=gamma S/V,
    r=gamma-z=gamma S'/V,
    k=(3z-gamma)D=bD'/V,
    l=0, A=z, B=0, C=2z, E=0, p0=q0=0.             (17)

For S>0 and d>=0 all of gamma,z,u,r,k are positive. Equations (7)
and (8) hold exactly: u+r=2gamma-3z and k=(3z-gamma)D.
Thus the rule is:

* scale both complete old finite arrays by gamma;
* add 2z w^L_i on (p,i) throughout the left block;
* add z w^R_i on (p,i) throughout the right block;
* use proof weights (u w^L, r w^R), adding k at p.

All FINAL finite coefficients and optimum coefficients in (4) are
nonnegative. Every value cancels; the full remainder is (9)--(10).
Unlike Section 4, this is an explicit array at every depth, even after
its PSD test fails, and does not require any moment-rank hypothesis.

For a one-step seed h=1+a with 0<a<=1/2, take

    w=(1+2a,2), D=3+2a,
    lambda_(0,1)=2, lambda_(1,0)=1-2a,
    R=(1-2a)||g_0-g_1||^2.                          (18)

Direct expansion gives (2) with these coefficients. This is a full
Huber-level objective certificate. At the undeformed Silver one-step
benchmark a=sqrt(2)-1, all coefficients are nonnegative and
R=(3-2sqrt(2))||g_0-g_1||^2. Thus the seed is calibrated exactly.

Nevertheless, (17) already fails at the undeformed three-step Silver
join. Its M=1+sqrt(2), d=1 and a=sqrt(2)-1 satisfy (16), so (14)
is negative. This calibration failure is not suppressed by extending
the formula to deformed words.

More strongly, the recursively specified array (17)--(18) has a
negative full g_0 diagonal at EVERY join satisfying (16), even if the
child remainder has already become indefinite. To see this, (14)
uses only the child value flow, the nonnegative finite coefficients,
and w^L_0>0. All of those hold inductively for the actual array; PSD
of the child is not needed. Its left weight is multiplied by u>0.
Equations (13), (15), and (17) therefore make (14) strictly negative.

In particular q can be arbitrarily large in (4): x_start=0 makes the
q term vanish, so changing the bound without changing the actual
multiplier array cannot repair it. The negative assignment is a formal
full-matrix test, NOT a legal interpolated function trajectory.

## 6. Application to the actual horizon-dependent critical word

Let lambda=1+sqrt(2), m>=64,

    c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    d_j=a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+d_j,H_j).

Within this fixed horizon, use (18) on H_1 and (17) at every later join.
Let M_j=1+sum H_j. Directly from the word,

    M_0=1, M_(j+1)=2M_j+d_j,
    M_j=[a/(c-2)]c^j+[1-a/(c-2)]2^j.              (19)

We have 0<a<c-2, hence d_j/M_j>=a for every j: write
M_j/c^j=A+(1-A)(2/c)^j<=1 with A=a/(c-2) in (0,1).
Also a>=2/5 for m>=64. The function (m-1)/(m+1) increases, and at
m=64 this is equivalent to 63sqrt(2)>=89, whose square is the strict
integer inequality 7938>7921. The seed satisfies a<sqrt(2)-1<1/2.

Thus every join from H_1 onward satisfies (16). For every m>=64 the
full final matrix generated by this explicit array is negative on
x_0=0, g_0 nonzero, all other gradients zero, for EVERY q. This is an
actual full-matrix obstruction for the stated critical parameters,
not just an asymptotic scalar calculation or a matrix tested on a
selected primal family.

Replacing only the final physical step by any prescribed nonnegative
number leaves this negative evaluation unchanged: its gradient is zero,
so every substituted position is unchanged. The same array remains
value-canceling. This observation excludes that repair to this array,
not independently chosen certificates for a modified schedule.

## 7. What remains open

The new family genuinely permits proof weights different from the
physical steps and retains both moments in every full coefficient.
Its failure is caused by the exact incompatibility between the
Huber common-gradient kernel and the first-gradient diagonal.

The target requires some q_m B_(2^m-1)<1 asymptotically, not necessarily
Huber equality. Neither the original schedules nor this weaker upper
target are ruled out. Unrestricted cross-block interior edges, a
nonsaturated rule with a different multiplier array, and proportional
queried-weight certificates remain possible. None has been proved to
give the required growing-horizon upper bound here.

Thus the successful terminal/zero-step selector cannot be extended to deleting positive-step vertices by ANY choice of redistributed remaining coefficients.
evidence: Let n>=1, h>=0, and let lambda>=0 cancel every value in q||x0||^2-2fn+sum lambda_ik Q_ik for a finite real q, with all original gradients independent and xi=x0-sum_(t<i)h_t gt. The necessary finite value flow is out_i-in_i=2*1_(i=n). Suppose h_j>0 and every interpolation coefficient incident to j is0. Put T_cut={j+1,...,n}, and let C_out,C_in be the actual multiplier sums crossing this cut in the two directions, optimum included in its complement. Summing the value flow over T_cut gives C_out-C_in=2, hence C_out>=2. Set scalar formal x0=0, g_i=0 for i<j, g_j=t, g_i=1 for i>j. No incident edge uses the gradient g_j, so every norm-difference term is independent of t. All positions inside T_cut acquire the common term -h_j t, while earlier/optimum positions do not. Thus the only t terms are from edges sourced inside T_cut and targeting its complement, each contributing +lambda_ik h_j t. Every other edge either has equal position shifts or source gradient0. evidence:
# Chronological and optimum anchors control every metric of two complex modes

Status: complete candidate proof, UNVERIFIED. No routine fact submission is
allocated. The only correctness inputs used are facts 1252b8823bb5a290
(necessary interpolation inequalities and smoothness) and b98bb807d514e80d
(the exact benchmark recursions). Every new estimate is given below. Earlier
unverified spectral and covariance findings are not premises.

## 1. Actual schedule, full added space, and claim

Let lambda=1+sqrt(2). For an integer m>=128 put
c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c, d_j=1+a c^j. Within this horizon these
parameters are fixed. Set H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j), n=2^m-1,
q=n-1, and let h be H_m with ONLY its original last step d_0 removed.
Write S=sum h_t. For 0<=i<=q put P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z).
Fix zeta_1=(1+i)/2, zeta_2=(4+i)/2, and z_l=zeta_l/S.

For a pair of complex numbers define the real column

 J(v_1,v_2)=(Re(v_1-v_2), Im v_1, Im v_2)^T.

Let w be arbitrary in [0,1] and T be ANY real matrix with three columns,
with no upper bound on its entries or number of rows. Define Euclidean data

 x_i=(sqrt(w)Re P_i(z_1),sqrt(w)Im P_i(z_1),
      sqrt(1-w)Re P_i(z_2),sqrt(1-w)Im P_i(z_2),
      T J(P_i(z_1),P_i(z_2))),
 g_i=(sqrt(w)Re[z_1 P_i(z_1)],sqrt(w)Im[z_1 P_i(z_1)],
      sqrt(1-w)Re[z_2 P_i(z_2)],sqrt(1-w)Im[z_2 P_i(z_2)],
      T J(z_1 P_i(z_1),z_2 P_i(z_2))).                    (1)

Then ||x_0||=1 and x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i. Every real linear functional
on (v_1,v_2) that vanishes at (1,1) is a linear combination of the three
components of J: its two real coefficients must sum to zero, and its two
imaginary coefficients are unrestricted. Thus (1) includes EVERY PSD
addition annihilating the initial vector, added orthogonally to the two
normal blocks. Write M=T^T T; it is an arbitrary PSD 3 by 3 matrix.

Suppose arbitrary JOINT queried values are interpolated by a convex
differentiable 1-smooth function F, with F(0)=0=min F and grad F(x_i)=g_i.
No separate modal values or modal legality are assumed. Then, for every
sufficiently large m, uniformly over w,T,F and b in [0,2],

                 2F(x_q-b g_q) <= 2/(3S).               (2)

For B_n=1/U_n^ZJ=2S_bullet(n)+1 this implies

 limsup_(m->infinity) sup_(w,T,F,b) B_n 2F(x_q-b g_q)
                       <= 8/(3e) < 64/65 < 1.           (3)

The actual final step b=d_0 lies in [0,2]. The statement concerns exactly
the displayed spectral family. Sections 8--9 prove a broader result: for
ANY real linear map A from C^2, viewed as R^4, to a finite-dimensional
Euclidean space, with ||A(1,1)||=1, set

 x_i=A(P_i(z_1),P_i(z_2)),
 g_i=A(z_1 P_i(z_1),z_2 P_i(z_2)).

For arbitrary jointly legal values and all b in [0,2], eventually,
uniformly over these maps and their conditioning,

 2F(x_q-b g_q)<=21/(20S),
 limsup sup B_n 2F(x_q-b g_q)<=21/(8e)<63/65<1.          (19)

Thus the broader result includes every PSD metric on the complete
four-dimensional two-mode evaluation space, including initial-direction
cross terms. Neither result bounds unrestricted W_n(H_m) or arbitrary
spectra. The number of modes is fixed at the two specified parameters.

## 2. Two exact shared interpolation inequalities

Use Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0 from the accepted
fact 1252b8823bb5a290. First sum Q_(0,star) and Q_(t+1,t) for every
0<=t<q. The values telescope, and GD gives

 f_q <= <g_0,x_0>-sum_(t<q) h_t<g_(t+1),g_t>
                -||g_0||^2/2-sum_(t<q)||g_(t+1)-g_t||^2/2.

Dropping only the explicitly nonnegative squared terms yields

 f_q <= <g_0,x_0>-sum_(t<q)h_t<g_(t+1),g_t>.             (4)

Second, for any actual queried r, sum Q_(q,r) and Q_(r,star), and drop
their two squared terms. This gives

 f_q <= <g_q,x_q>+<g_r-g_q,x_r>.                         (5)

Choose r=2^(m-1), the query immediately AFTER the largest bridge. Both
inequalities concern the same joint transcript and the same function.
Their convex combination uses the fixed coefficients

                theta=6/25 on (4), 1-theta=19/25 on (5). (6)

For scaled gradients U_i=J(zeta_1 P_i(z_1),zeta_2 P_i(z_2)), and
Y_i=J(P_i(z_1),P_i(z_2)), let sym(u,v)=(uv^T+vu^T)/2. Define

 E_m=sum_(t<q) (h_t/S) sym(U_(t+1),U_t),
 Kplus_m=sym(U_q,Y_q)+sym(U_r-U_q,Y_r),
 K_m=(19/25)Kplus_m-(6/25)E_m.                          (7)

For l=1,2 let e_t=h_t/S and p_i,l=P_i(z_l), and define

 C_l,m=Re zeta_l-|zeta_l|^2 sum_(t<q)
                   e_t |p_t,l|^2(1-e_t Re zeta_l),
 Dplus_l,m=Re[zeta_l p_q,l conj(p_q,l)
                     +zeta_l(p_r,l-p_q,l)conj(p_r,l)],
 D_l,m=(6/25)C_l,m+(19/25)Dplus_l,m.                    (8)

The initial added coordinates are zero. Substituting (1) into (4)--(6)
therefore gives the EXACT finite-word bound

             S f_q <= w D_1,m+(1-w)D_2,m+trace(M K_m).  (9)

The proof will show K_m is negative definite and D_l,m<1/3 for all
sufficiently large m. Crucially these properties will hold at each such
FINITE m before allowing M to vary or grow without bound.

## 3. Limit word and continuity of its chronological work

Directly summing the multiplicity of every step gives

 S=2^m-2-a+a(c^m-2^m)/(c-2),      S/lambda^m -> e,
 d_(m-1-j)/S -> delta lambda^(-j),
 delta=1-2/lambda=3-2sqrt(2).                            (10)

Here a->1/lambda, (1+1/m)^m->e, and lambda(lambda-2)=1. The largest
normalized step has limit delta. The normalized limiting word consists
of a central step delta, two copies with central step delta/lambda,
four copies with central step delta/lambda^2, and so on, with their
recursive chronology retained. The total mass at level j is
delta(2/lambda)^j; the total mass is one.

Its truncation after N largest levels is the finite word obtained from
H <- (H,d,H), starting empty and using, in ascending order,

 d=delta/lambda^(N-1), ..., delta/lambda, delta.

The omitted mass is exactly epsilon_N=(2/lambda)^N. This definition
does not introduce any new physical terminal step.

For the four modal numbers

 zeta_1, conjugate(zeta_1), zeta_2, conjugate(zeta_2),

every normalized factor satisfies |1-d zeta|<=1 whenever 0<=d<=1/5:
expanding the square reduces this to d<=2Re(zeta)/|zeta|^2, whose
minimum here is 16/17. All limiting steps and, eventually, all actual
normalized steps satisfy the stronger bound d<1/5.

Deleting steps of total mass tau from such a chronological word changes
any modal prefix product by at most |zeta|tau. To see this, telescope
the deletion one factor at a time; all other factors have modulus<=1,
and the deleted factor differs from one by d zeta.

For any two of the four modal numbers A,B define the scalar work moment

 W_word(A,B)=sum_t d_t P_t(A)P_t(B)[1-d_t(A+B)/2].        (11)

The bracket is the average of 1-d_t A and 1-d_t B, so its modulus is
at most one. Deleted terms have total modulus<=tau. At retained terms,
the change in the two-product is at most (|A|+|B|)tau. Since the total
step mass is at most one,

 |W_word-W_deleted| <= (1+|A|+|B|)tau.                  (12)

After multiplying by AB this is <23tau, because |A|,|B|<=sqrt(17)/2
<21/10 and |AB|<=17/4. Expressing the three real coordinates J in these
four complex modes uses rows with absolute coefficient sums 2,1,1.
Consequently deleting mass tau changes any entry of the real work
matrix by less than 92tau. We use the simpler uniform bound 100tau.
The normal work terms have error less than 23tau.

These inequalities prove existence of the infinite-word moments. They
also prove convergence from the ACTUAL words in (10). Indeed, retain
only their N largest levels. The resulting finite word converges to
the displayed N-level truncation, including its chronological order.
For fixed N the deleted normalized mass converges to epsilon_N:
the normalized total mass is exactly one and the retained masses
converge individually. Apply (12), first let m tend to infinity, and
then let N tend to infinity. The removed original d_0 is among the
deleted levels when m>N, so this argument also handles it explicitly.
We obtain E_m->E and convergence of the two normal work coefficients.

The left-half product and bridge/endpoint products are

 L(zeta)=product_(j>=1)(1-delta lambda^(-j)zeta)^(2^(j-1)),
 p_l=L(zeta_l),   v_l=(1-delta zeta_l)p_l,
 t_l=p_l v_l.                                          (13)

For the actual words, the corresponding products are exactly
v_l,m=(1-d_(m-1)z_l)p_l,m and
t_l,m=(1-d_(m-1)z_l)p_l,m^2/(1-d_0 z_l).
The last denominator tends to one. Deletion of a small total mass and
the same product bound prove convergence to (13). Thus K_m and D_l,m
converge entrywise to the quantities K,D_l given by (7)--(8) and the
limiting work moments.

## 4. Finite rational enclosures of the fixed limiting coefficients

Everything in this section is bounded arithmetic for one fixed
coefficient matrix; no PEP or optimization evaluation is used.

For the product (13) define mu_s=delta^s/(lambda^s-2). Absolutely
convergent logarithmic expansion gives

 log L(zeta)=-sum_(s>=1)mu_s zeta^s/s.

Let A_10 be the sum through s=10. Since mu_2<1/125,
|zeta|^2<=17/4, and eta=|zeta|delta/lambda<3/20, the omitted tail is

 <=mu_2 |zeta|^2 eta^9/[11(1-eta)] < 1/10^9.           (14)

The bound on mu_s used here is mu_s<=mu_2(delta/lambda)^(s-2), obtained
directly by summing the positive powers of the left-half step sizes.
Compute exp(A_10) through degree18. The bounds Re A_10<0 and |A_10|<1
give exponential tail <3/19!. Perturbing its argument by (14) changes
the exponential by <(10^-9)/(1-10^-9). Hence error 2/10^9 in each real
component safely covers both tails.

For the moment (11), its exact concatenation recurrence is short.
If a word has products p_A,p_B and moment W, appending its central
step d and another copy gives

 p_A,new=p_A^2(1-dA),  p_B,new=p_B^2(1-dB),
 W_new=W[1+p_A p_B(1-dA)(1-dB)]
                     +d p_A p_B[1-d(A+B)/2].           (15)

The first copy contributes W, the central step gives the last term,
and the second copy is multiplied by p_A p_B(1-dA)(1-dB), proving
the identity. Use N=112 levels in (15). The rational bound

                 100(2/lambda)^112 < 1/10^7             (16)

and (12) supply the error for every resulting real work coefficient.

For a completely specified finite arithmetic procedure, use the interval

 r_- = 1.41421356237309504880168872420969807856967187537694,
 r_+ = r_-+10^-50

for sqrt(2); its squared endpoints straddle 2. Set lambda=1+[r_-,r_+]
and delta=1-2/lambda. Interval additions, products, and positive
reciprocals enclose their exact values. At each stored log-series,
exponential-series, or word-recursion update, round the lower endpoint
down and upper endpoint up to a
multiple of 10^-60. This only enlarges an enclosure and prevents
denominator growth. Evaluate A_10, then its degree18 exponential using
t_0=1, t_j=t_(j-1)A_10/j. Add the componentwise error in (14). For
the work moments, use (15) on all sixteen pairs of the four modes.

The coefficients expressing J in these four modes, in that order, are

 c_1=(1/2,1/2,-1/2,-1/2),
 c_2=(-i/2,i/2,0,0), c_3=(0,0,-i/2,i/2).

The real work matrix entries are
E_kl=Re sum_(r,s)c_kr c_ls zeta_r zeta_s W(zeta_r,zeta_s).
The two normal chain coefficients are
C_1=1/2-(1/2)W(zeta_1,conjugate(zeta_1)) and
C_2=2-(17/4)W(zeta_2,conjugate(zeta_2)).
Add error interval [-10^-7,10^-7] to these expressions. This includes
(16); all preceding rounding errors are already in the intervals.

The following outward rational enclosures result. Finite decimals are
exact rational numbers; the margins are deliberately larger than the
rounding errors.

|---|---|

Substituting the directly computed intervals in (7)--(8), at theta=6/25,
gives

 19/100 < D_1 < 193/1000,       329/1000 < D_2 < 33/100,

These are finite rational inequalities obtained by the displayed

The companion chain_anchor_interval_check.py implements these exact
interval operations and asserts (17). Its first version was stopped
because an unrounded exponential expression caused denominator growth.
The corrected version rounds the intermediate log/exponential terms
and the fixed-size moment recurrence; it exits zero. An earlier
ordinary floating-point exploration was not used as proof: repeated
squaring of factors extremely close to one loses significant small-step
mass in floating arithmetic. The rational calculation and its explicit
tail estimates are the evidence for (17).

## 5. Finite-word uniformity, free terminal step, and exact benchmark

Entrywise convergence and the strict inequalities (17) imply that for
all sufficiently large m, the EXACT K_m is negative definite and
D_l,m<1/3. None of those coefficients depends on w or T. Since
trace(T^T T K_m) is a sum of nonpositive row quadratic forms, (9) gives
F(x_q)<=1/(3S), uniformly even for coupling matrices diverging with m.

Integration of the 1-Lipschitz gradient along the final segment gives

 F(x_q-b g_q)<=F(x_q)-b(1-b/2)||g_q||^2<=F(x_q),

for all b in [0,2]. The terminal gradient and value are free; this
proves (2) for the same interpolating F.

Here is the comparison with the exact project benchmark, proved rather
than imported from an unverified finding. Let rho=log_2 lambda,
C_k=S_circle(k)+1, and B_k=2S_bullet(k)+1. The accepted recursions give

 C_0=B_0=1,
 C_n=max_(0<=j<n)Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
 B_n=max_(0<=j<n)G(C_j,B_(n-j-1)),
 Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,
 G(A,B)=2A+B/2+sqrt(B^2+8AB)/2.

For V(t)=(1+t)^rho-1, differentiation gives, with t=exp u,

 d^2/du^2 log V(exp u)
 =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)[(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/V(t)^2 > 0.

The bracket vanishes at zero and has positive derivative for t>0.
Convexity at u and -u implies V(t)V(1/t)>=V(1)^2=2. If A,B>0 and
M=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho, this means (M-A)(M-B)>=2AB;
the positive root of this quadratic is Omega(A,B). Thus
Omega(A,B)<=M and induction gives C_k<=(k+1)^rho.
The inequality sqrt(B^2+8AB)<=B+4A yields G(A,B)<=B+4A.
Using u^rho+v^rho<=(u+v)^rho for nonnegative u,v proves by induction
B_n<=1+4n^rho. The latter inequality follows by differentiating
(1+t)^rho-t^rho, whose minimum for t>=0 is one.

At n=2^m-1, n^rho/lambda^m->1 and S/lambda^m->e by (10).
Multiplying (2) by B_n proves (3). Finally e>sum_(j=0)^4 1/j!=65/24,
so 8/(3e)<64/65.

## 6. Why the chronology is necessary in this certificate

Define chi(v_1,v_2)=Re(v_1-v_2)/4+Im v_1/5+Im v_2.
It vanishes at (1,1). Apply it to the left, right, and endpoint modal
pairs in (13), obtaining y_-,y_+,y_q and, after multiplication by
the modal zeta values, u_-,u_+,u_q. The coefficients of its squared
amplitude in the two individual bridge-anchor bounds are

 k_-=u_q y_q+(u_--u_q)y_-,
 k_+=u_q y_q+(u_+-u_q)y_+.

The same rational product enclosures give

        23/100000 < k_- < 24/100000,
       103/100000 < k_+ < 104/100000.                    (18)

Every convex combination of just these two anchor matrices therefore
has a strictly positive direction. This refutes a purely algebraic
extension of the two-anchor method to the full three-dimensional
space. It is NOT a legal high-payoff construction. Adding the actual
chronological chain supplies a different constraint and yields (17).

## 7. Scope of the first coefficient bound

The bound (2) covers arbitrary PSD zero-initial additions to the two
normal blocks. Negative definiteness on J alone does not establish (2)
for arbitrary metrics: the initial-direction cross terms must also be
controlled. The next section does this with an additional actual
interpolation bound and a larger, explicitly paid coefficient. It uses
no unverified result as a premise: the complete coefficient derivation
and all estimates are part of this same proof.

## 8. Full initial-direction correlations and the third inequality

Let A be any map in the broader claim (19), and put e=A(1,1), so ||e||=1.
Write a(v_1,v_2)=Re v_1. The scalar map <e,A(v_1,v_2)> has value one
at (1,1), and therefore equals a+c^T J for some real column c in R^3.
The orthogonal projection of A onto e-perpendicular annihilates (1,1),
so it has the form T J, where T has range perpendicular to e. Hence

 A(v)=e[a(v)+c^T J(v)]+T J(v).                          (20)

This is an exact decomposition of EVERY normalized map A, not a
restriction to a chosen initial direction. The matrix M=T^T T is PSD
and c is unrestricted. Both may depend arbitrarily on m.

Apply the combination (6) to (20). At finite m it gives

 S f_q <= k00_m+2 k0_m^T c+c^T K_m c+trace(M K_m).      (21)

Here K_m is still (7). To specify the new coefficients, set
a_i=Re P_i(z_1), u_i=Re[zeta_1 P_i(z_1)],
u_init=(-3/2,1/2,1/2)^T. Define the scalar and vector work moments

 E00_m=sum_t e_t u_(t+1)u_t,
 E0_m=sum_t e_t[u_(t+1)U_t+u_t U_(t+1)]/2.

The coefficient formulas, with r the post-bridge query, are

 k00_m=(19/25)[u_q a_q+(u_r-u_q)a_r]+(6/25)[1/2-E00_m],
 k0_m=(19/50)[u_q Y_q+U_q a_q+(u_r-u_q)Y_r+(U_r-U_q)a_r]
                                  +(6/25)[u_init/2-E0_m]. (22)

All these moments converge by the same deletion proof (12). They use
the same sixteen scalar moments (15). In that formula the coefficient
row for a is c_0=(1/2,1/2,0,0). Thus E00 and E0_j are the real parts
of the contractions with c_0,c_0 and c_0,c_j respectively, with the
same error bound 10^-7. Alternatively E00=1/2-C_1-E_22, since the
first normal block is the sum of its real and imaginary coordinates.

For precision, direct outward interval calculation in the procedure
of Section 4 gives

 k00 in [.26264513,.26264525],
 k0_1 in [-.10147100,-.10147092],
 k0_2 in [.03390797,.03390804],
 k0_3 in [.03049014,.03049021].                          (23)

The coefficient from (21) alone is too large after unrestricted square
completion. This is a limitation of that bound, not a legal adversary.
The needed additional inequality is simply the ACTUAL Q_(q,star)<=0:

                   S f_q <= <S g_q,x_q>.               (24)

Its omitted squared gradient term is nonnegative. Add tau=2/3 times
(24) to (21), and divide by 1+tau=5/3. The actual weights on the
chronological chain, post-bridge anchor and optimum anchor are
18/125,57/125,2/5, respectively. They are nonnegative and sum to one.

Before dividing, define

 Kbar_m=K_m+tau sym(U_q,Y_q),
 kbar_m=k0_m+(tau/2)(u_q Y_q+U_q a_q),
 kbar00_m=k00_m+tau u_q a_q.                            (25)

Then

 (1+tau) S f_q <= kbar00_m+2 kbar_m^T c
                            +c^T Kbar_m c+trace(M Kbar_m). (26)

The limiting coefficients from the same rational procedure satisfy

 -.082622 < Kbar_11 < -.082621,
 .0007105 < Kbar_11 Kbar_22-Kbar_12^2 < .0007106,
 -81/10^9 < det Kbar < -79/10^9.                        (27)

In particular Kbar is negative definite. For an entirely specified
arithmetic check of the remaining scalar, let cof_ji(Kbar) denote its
cofactor obtained by deleting row j and column i, with sign (-1)^(i+j).
Evaluate

 R_full = (3/5)[kbar00
           -sum_(i,j)kbar_i cof_ji(Kbar) kbar_j/det Kbar].

The direct enclosing interval from (15), (22), (25) is

            .5173 < R_full < .5205 < 21/40.             (28)

These cofactor formulas use only products, sums, and division by the
strictly negative interval in (27). No eigenvalue or optimization
routine is needed. The companion initial_cross_coefficient_check.py
implements this same fixed coefficient arithmetic. Its finer interval
is [.5173336917833667,.5204116728479283]. These displayed endpoints
report the outward rational result; the exact coarse inequalities
(27)--(28) are the claimed bounds.

For finite m sufficiently large, Kbar_m is negative definite and
R_full,m<21/40 by convergence and the strict margins. Completing the
square gives

 kbar00_m+2 kbar_m^T c+c^T Kbar_m c
 =kbar00_m-kbar_m^T Kbar_m^(-1)kbar_m
  +(c+Kbar_m^(-1)kbar_m)^T Kbar_m(c+Kbar_m^(-1)kbar_m)
 <=(5/3) R_full,m.

Also trace(M Kbar_m)<=0. Equation (26) gives F(x_q)<=21/(40S), uniformly
over ALL normalized maps A, including arbitrarily growing initial
correlations and transverse metrics. The same final descent inequality
as in Section 5 proves the first assertion of (19).

One scope audit can be stated explicitly. The scalar row a+5chi, with
chi from Section 6, has unit initial value. Its coefficient in the
original combination (21) lies in (.374,.375), exceeding 1/3. Thus
one cannot extend the OLD1/3 coefficient just by ignoring the initial
cross terms. This row is not a legal counterexample: if its scaled
terminal gradient is U and scaled derivative is V, the exact limiting
coefficient UV is in (-.084,-.082). At the actual last retained
adjacent pair, cocoercivity implies UV>=V^2/S, so this scalar row
fails legality for sufficiently large m. The third inequality and
square completion prove (19) without assuming that this row, or any
other unsupported coefficient direction, is realizable.

## 9. A self-contained benchmark envelope sufficient for the full metric

This proof needs only the following weaker scalar comparison, which
is established here directly:

             G(x,(5/2)y) <= (5/2)Omega(x,y), x,y>=0.    (29)

Let k=5/2 and p=Omega(x,y). The plane
R=(16/15)x+(5/3)y bounds p from above. Indeed R>=max(x,y), and

 (R-x)(R-y)-2xy
  =(16x^2-40xy+250y^2)/225
  =[16(x-5y/4)^2+225y^2]/225 >=0.

Since p is the larger root of (p-x)(p-y)=2xy, this proves p<=R.
The number G(x,ky) is the larger root of
t^2-(4x+ky)t+4x^2=0. Substituting t=kp and using
p^2=(x+y)p+xy gives

 (kp)^2-(4x+ky)kp+4x^2
        =x[4x+(25/4)y-(15/4)p] >=0.

Moreover p>=x+y, so kp>=2x+(k/2)y, the vertex of the quadratic.
It follows that kp is at least its larger root, proving (29).
The reasoning includes x=0 or y=0; these cases also follow directly.

The function G is nondecreasing in its second nonnegative argument,
as follows immediately from its formula. Starting from B_0=C_0=1,
induction in the accepted recursions and (29) gives

 B_n=max_j G(C_j,B_(n-j-1))
     <=max_j G(C_j,(5/2)C_(n-j-1))
     <=(5/2)max_j Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1))=(5/2)C_n.

Section 5 already proved C_n<=(n+1)^rho directly from the recursions.
Therefore B_(2^m-1)<=(5/2)lambda^m. Together with S/lambda^m->e and
the first bound in (19), this proves

 limsup sup B_n 2F(x_q-b g_q)<=21/(8e)<63/65,

where the strict inequality uses e>65/24. No numerical estimate for
the benchmark or presumed global profile limit enters this comparison.
The stronger coefficient 1+sqrt2 requested elsewhere is not assumed.

## 10. Remaining target

Every normalized common PSD metric for THESE two complex modes is
covered, with full joint prefix legality, exact initial distance, and
free final value/gradient. The result is still an upper bound for a
restricted adversary family. It supplies neither an upper certificate
on the entire formal PEP space nor a matching legal lower witness for
the original problem. Additional spectral support, growing modal
dimension, and nonlinear trajectory mechanisms remain outside the
statement. The all-schedule exact-profile target is unresolved.

evidence:
# Relaxed objective certificates: a full four-fan null-template obstruction

Status: complete self-contained UNVERIFIED candidate. No solver and no
fact_submit. This is a formal certificate-family obstruction, not a legal
lower witness and not a resolution of the original minimax problem.

The latest guidance asks for q above the Huber value to be tested separately.
This argument does not use Huber complementarity or a Huber kernel condition.
The shared C53 calculation (694fb2dacb4f7389) suggested its null template;
every identity and estimate needed here is proved again, with additional
left-history fans, arbitrary child scaling, and the relaxed objective.
Only fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies a mathematical predecessor: the
normalized smooth-convex interpolation inequalities.

## 1. Full objective identity and a relaxed proof-weight choice

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Let

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0,
    C_ij=-2Q_ji
        =2(f_i-f_j)+2<g_j,x_j-x_i>-||g_i-g_j||^2 >=0,

and put C_ii=0. All positions use the exact physical GD recursion.
Every formal vector x_0,g_0,...,g_n is independent.

At a block h of length n put S=sum h_i, M=S+1, P=sum h_i g_i, and fix

    w_i=h_i for i<n, w_n=1, D=sum w_i=M,
    W=P+g_n,
    J_rel=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)
                   +sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2.    (1)

The same quantity can be written

    J_rel=2sum_i w_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_i w_i||g_i||^2
       +2sum_i w_i<g_i,x_0-x_i>-||W||^2.

To check this, expand ||sum h_i g_i||^2 and use
2sum_i h_i<g_i,sum_(t<i)h_t g_t>
=||sum h_i g_i||^2-sum_i h_i^2||g_i||^2.

Suppose finite nonnegative coefficients lambda_ij give the exact identity

    J_rel=sum_(finite i!=j)lambda_ij C_ij+R.          (2)

All function coefficients cancel if and only if

    out_i-in_i=w_i-M 1_(i=n).                       (3)

For EVERY real q the corresponding FULL objective polynomial is

    q||x_0||^2-2f_n
       +2/M sum_i w_i Q_(i,star)
       +2/M sum_(finite i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ji
      =(q-1/M)||x_0||^2+[||x_0-W||^2+R]/M.          (4)

This follows by expanding the optimum interpolation terms. All actual
multipliers are nonnegative. The array fixes Q_(star,i) multipliers to
zero; general relaxed certificates need not have that property.
If R were PSD, (4) at q=1/M would be the requested weaker objective
upper bound. This is genuinely above the Huber value when S>0.

## 2. The actual four-fan recursion, with signed corrections allowed

Use two copies of the same block. Let p be the left endpoint and q_end
the parent endpoint. Insert bridge b=1+d with d>0, and write

    g=g_p, e=g_(q_end), M'=2M+d,
    P_L=x_start-x_p, P_R=x_(p+1)-x_(q_end),
    W_L=P_L+g, W_R=P_R+e,
    V=d g+W_R, W_parent=W_L+V.

Choose level-dependent A,E>=0 and real B,C,p0,q0. Set

    gamma_L=1+C+E, gamma_R=1+A+B,
    p0-q0=(1-A+E)M+d.                              (5)

Require gamma_L,gamma_R>=0. Scale the COMPLETE left and right child
finite arrays by gamma_L and gamma_R. Add the fans

    C w_i on (p,i),       E w_i on (q_end,i),   i in left samples,
    A w_i on (p,i),       B w_i on (q_end,i),   i in right samples,

omitting self edges, and add p0 on (p,q_end) and q0 on (q_end,p).
Require EVERY FINAL finite multiplier nonnegative. In particular B,C,
p0,q0 can be signed when their actual resulting entries are nonnegative.
The new proof weights are the old physical weights in each queried
copy, with the left terminal weight changed from 1 to b, and the
right terminal weight retained as 1. Thus D_parent=M', exactly as in (1).

No earlier interpolation constraints are deleted. The final array is
the explicit sum just given. Its value flow is (3); alternatively the
following expansion checks every value coefficient directly.

The four weighted fan identities, derived by expanding C, are

    sum_L w_i C_(p,i)
       =-J_L-||W_L||^2+2<W_L,P_L+g>-M||g||^2,
    sum_L w_i C_(q_end,i)
       =-J_L-||W_L||^2+2<W_L,P_L+b g+P_R+e>
                                     -M||e||^2-2M(f_p-f_(q_end)),
    sum_R w_i C_(p,i)
       =2M(f_p-f_(q_end))-J_R-||W_R||^2
                                     -2d<g,W_R>-M||g||^2,
    sum_R w_i C_(q_end,i)
       =-J_R-||W_R||^2+2<W_R,P_R+e>-M||e||^2.       (6)

After adding the child identities and these fans, the only remaining
function coefficient is
2[(1-A+E)M+d-p0+q0](f_p-f_(q_end)), which is zero by (5).
Substitute P_L=W_L-g and P_R=W_R-e in the quadratic terms. The exact
FULL gradient remainder is

    R_parent=gamma_L R_L+gamma_R R_R+F_rel,

    F_rel=-(C+E)||W_L||^2+(A-B)||W_R||^2
       -2E<W_L,W_R+d g>
       +2(Ad-q0)<g,W_R>+2p0<W_R,e>
       +(gamma_L M-d^2-2dq0)||g||^2
       +(gamma_R M-2M-d)||e||^2+2p0d<g,e>.          (7)

This retains both physical displacements through the displayed W_L,W_R
and retains every child matrix. It is not a local-PSD assumption.

## 3. Exact undeformed calibration

Let lambda=1+sqrt(2). For the undeformed Silver word, M=lambda^j and
d=lambda^(j-1) at level j. Choose

    A=B=lambda, C=E=0, p0=0, q0=lambda d,
    gamma_L=1, gamma_R=lambda^2.                    (8)

Start with the one-step finite array lambda_(0,1)=lambda,
lambda_(1,0)=1, physical step sqrt(2). Direct expansion gives
R=M(M-1)||g_end||^2 at this seed. Equation (5) holds in (8) because
(1-lambda)M+d=-lambda d. All final coefficients are nonnegative.

Assuming the same remainder formula for both children, (7) proves it
for the parent. The g coefficient from the left child cancels
M-lambda^2 d^2=M-M^2. The e coefficient is
lambda^2 M(M-1)+lambda^2 M-M'=M'^2-M'. All mixed coefficients are
zero. Thus the relaxed identity passes the FULL undeformed benchmark
at every depth, with its true initial distance and all values canceled.

## 4. A formal template for EVERY allowed choice of the new fans

For the deformed word H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+d_j,H_j), let
M_j=1+sum H_j. Define signed numbers

    kappa_1=M_1=2+a,
    kappa_(j+1)=-kappa_j^2/d_j.                     (9)

Every array produced by (5)--(7) has a recursively specified scalar
formal-gradient template with terminal gradient e such that

    W_j=kappa_j e,
    R_j=(kappa_j^2-M_j)e^2.                         (10)

At the one-step seed, take both formal gradients equal to e. The two
finite C residuals are zero after setting f_0-f_1=h_0 e^2. Equation
(1) gives R_1=M_1(M_1-1)e^2=(kappa_1^2-M_1)e^2 for ANY seed array
satisfying (3). PSD of the seed is not needed for this calculation.

For the induction use a right template with terminal e and a left
template with terminal g=-kappa_j e/d_j. Then

    V=d_j g+W_R=0,
    W_parent=W_L+V=kappa_j g=kappa_(j+1)e.

On V=0, the COMPLETE local expression (7) becomes

    F_rel=-(gamma_L-1)||W_L||^2
          +(gamma_L M_j-gamma_R d_j^2)||g||^2
          +(gamma_R M_j-M_(j+1))||e||^2.            (11)

Indeed W_R=-d_j g cancels both p0 mixed terms and the E term. Adding
gamma_L R_L+gamma_R R_R and W_L=kappa_j g cancels gamma_L, gamma_R
and M_j, leaving (kappa_j^4/d_j^2-M_(j+1))e^2. This proves (10).
No child PSD, attained zero, greedy storage selection, or saturation
assumption occurs anywhere in this induction.

Now insert (10) into the FULL initial-distance identity (4). After
multiplication by M_j its restriction to independent scalar x_0,e is

             [ M_j q       -kappa_j     ]
             [ -kappa_j  2kappa_j^2-M_j ].           (12)

If 2kappa_j^2<M_j this matrix is negative at x_0=0,e=1 for EVERY q.
If the lower diagonal is positive, PSD would force

    q>=kappa_j^2/[M_j(2kappa_j^2-M_j)]>=1/kappa_j^2.

The last comparison is exactly (kappa_j^2-M_j)^2>=0. Thus merely
increasing q cannot repair the late negative diagonal.

## 5. Explicit failure at the actual critical horizon

Put m>=128, epsilon=1/m, c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c and
d_j=a c^j=(1-epsilon)c^(j-1). All parameters are fixed within this
whole word. Solving (9) in absolute value gives

    |kappa_m|=(1-epsilon)c^m Rcrit^(2^(m-1)),
    Rcrit=(2+a)/[(1-epsilon)c].                     (13)

The formula holds at j=1 by definition, and squaring and dividing by
d_j proves the next term. Direct subtraction gives

    1-Rcrit=epsilon[2-lambda^2 epsilon(1+epsilon)]
                    /[lambda^2(1-epsilon)(1+epsilon)^2]
             >=epsilon/4.                         (14)

For the inequality, lambda^2<6, the numerator bracket exceeds 7/4,
and the denominator is less than 6(129/128)^2<25/4. Their ratio is
therefore greater than 7/25>1/4. Also 0<Rcrit<1.
Since 1-t<=exp(-t) and c<3,

    |kappa_m|<3^m exp[-2^(m-3)/m]
               <=(3/exp(2))^m<2^(-m).              (15)

Here 2^(m-4)>=m^2 holds at m=128 and propagates by induction because
2m^2>=(m+1)^2 for m>=3. Also exp(2)>6 follows from the four positive
series terms 1+2+2+4/3. Since M_m>=1, (15) implies
2kappa_m^2<M_m. Equation (12) is therefore a concrete negative FULL
matrix restriction at the actual target horizon, for every real q.

This excludes all arrays in the stated relaxed four-fan family,
including arbitrary nonsaturating child remainders and all the signed
corrections permitted by actual coefficient positivity. It does not
exclude unrestricted relaxed certificates. In particular independent
nonsaturated history weights, different interior cross-copy edges,
and nonzero optimum-source multipliers are not covered. The formal
template is not asserted to be a legal interpolated function.

The original uniform lower theorem and a rigorous fixed asymptotic
separation both remain unproved.

evidence:
# Growing Newton temporal spaces on the actual critical word

Status: complete draft candidates, UNVERIFIED. No solver, numerical evaluation,
installation or fact_submit. Accepted facts 1252b8823bb5a290 (interpolation and
normalization) and b98bb807d514e80d (the exact benchmark and its elementary
envelope) are the only correctness inputs. Every new estimate is proved here.
These are obstructions for specified growing temporal spaces, not an upper
bound for the unrestricted worst-case objective and not the original target.

## 1. Actual word, queried prefix and a genuinely restricted growing space

Fix m>=128 and keep the following parameters fixed within that horizon:

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j),
    n=2^m-1, q=n-1.

The prescribed queried-prefix steps h_0,...,h_(q-1) are H_m with its last
entry d_0 removed. Queries are indexed 0,...,q; the last free step is b in
[0,2], including the original b=d_0. Write

    P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z), 0<=i<=q.

Choose a REAL monic polynomial chi of degree r, with 1<=r<=q. For a
polynomial p let [p] denote its remainder modulo chi. This is an r-dimensional
real vector space; use coefficients in 1,z,...,z^(r-1) as its real coordinates.
Let T be ANY real linear map from this space into any finite-dimensional
Euclidean space, with ||T[1]||=1. Put

    x_i=T[P_i],       g_i=T[z P_i],     0<=i<=q.          (1)

The map, ambient dimension, metric, coefficients and polynomial can all depend
on m. Singular maps are allowed. Initial correlations are unrestricted. The
identity P_(i+1)=P_i-h_i zP_i proves the ACTUAL GD recursion for (1).

All queried values f_i remain joint variables. Assume that the data (1), those
values and the optimum jet (0,0,0) belong to ONE convex differentiable function
F with 1-Lipschitz gradient. Thus the initial distance to this designated
minimizer is exactly one. All conclusions below hold for EVERY interpolant of
these jets; no terminal gradient identity is assumed after the last step b.

This is a fixed r-dimensional temporal space, even when the physical image
dimension is larger. For r=m it retains m independent Newton coefficients.
More generally the theorem below permits a degree much larger than m but
strictly smaller than the full n+1-node representation of arbitrary data.

## 2. The full computable all-pair law and function realization

Let J be multiplication by z modulo chi, let v_0 be the coefficient vector of
1, and define

    v_(i+1)=(I-h_i J)v_i,    w_i=Jv_i,    M=T^T T.

Then x_i=T v_i, g_i=T w_i, M is a REAL PSD matrix, and v_0^T M v_0=1.
Conversely every real PSD M has a real Euclidean factor T. With
v_star=w_star=0 and f_star=0, the necessary and sufficient full interpolation
law is, for EVERY distinct ordered pair i,j in {star,0,...,q},

 f_i-f_j+w_i^T M(v_j-v_i)
                   +(w_i-w_j)^T M(w_i-w_j)/2 <=0.       (2)

This is exactly Q_ij<=0 in fact 1252b8823bb5a290, evaluated on the stated
vectors. No pair or common value is replaced by a componentwise condition.
For feasible data that fact constructs an actual function explicitly:

 cjet_j=<g_j,x_j>-f_j,
 H(v)=max_j {cjet_j+<x_j,v-g_j>+||v-g_j||^2/2},
 F_max(x)=sup_v {<x,v>-H(v)}.

The maximum includes the optimum jet. The function is finite, convex and
1-smooth, interpolates every queried value and gradient, and has minimum zero
at zero. This provides a function realization, not just a Gram representation.

For a Newton basis with roots theta_1,...,theta_r, repetitions allowed,
the basis polynomials are N_k(z)=product_(ell=1)^k(z-theta_ell), 0<=k<r.
Multiplication obeys zN_k=theta_(k+1)N_k+N_(k+1), with N_r=0 in the quotient.
Thus J is a bidiagonal Newton chain in that basis. For nonreal conjugate
roots the original real monomial coordinates, or real and imaginary parts of
the Newton coordinates, give the same REAL law (2); a complex matrix is not
being called a real PSD metric.

## 3. Exact level resonance: a complete growing-span annihilation obstruction

The level d_j occurs 2^(m-j-1) times in H_m. In the retained prefix the
counts are

    N_0=2^(m-1)-1, N_j=2^(m-j-1), 1<=j<m.              (3)

Let mu_j=1/d_j. Suppose

    chi(z)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(z-mu_j)^(r_j),
    0<=r_j<=N_j,     1<=sum r_j<=q.                    (4)

Since P_q(z)=product_j(1-d_j z)^(N_j), chi divides P_q. Thus x_q=g_q=0
in (1), for EVERY map T and every common metric, regardless of its condition
number or initial correlations. Every legal interpolant has

                    2F(x_q-b g_q)=0                    (5)

for every real b. This includes one independent Newton direction at EVERY
recursive large-step level (r=m), as well as every growing multiplicity
permitted by the actual counts (3). It also handles confluent derivatives:
vanishing to order r_j, not merely vanishing once, is the exact requirement.

One can add a SINGLE zero root, chi=z product_j(z-mu_j)^(r_j), provided its
degree is <=q. Then chi divides zP_q, so g_q=0. The position need not be zero,
but legality says it is a minimizer of F; again (5) holds. Adding a second
zero root is not covered: a nonzero constant terminal gradient may survive.

For the simple positive roots r_j=1, all factors have occurred by the first
central top-level step (index 2^(m-1)-1). The model already reaches zero after
that step. This uses the actual chronology; (3) is the more general terminal
criterion for growing confluent blocks.

## 4. Near-unit roots: quantitative obstruction with growing Jordan depth

Suppose EVERY complex root theta of the real polynomial chi satisfies

                         |theta-1|<=1/(32m).            (6)

Roots may be arbitrarily close, repeated, nonreal, or depend on the horizon.
There is no bound on T or on a Jordan-chain condition number. For every legal
prefix (1) and every b in [0,2],

 2F(x_q-b g_q)
 <=3600 c^(-2m)(384m r^(3/2))^(2r)
                              exp[-3n/(2m)].           (7)

Consequently the ratio to the EXACT benchmark U_n^ZJ=1/B_n tends uniformly
to zero whenever

             r log(384m r^(3/2))=o(n/m).                (8)

In particular r=m is covered. There is also an explicit larger range:

 1<=r<=floor(n/(32m^2))  implies
 2F(x_q-b g_q)<=3600 exp[-11n/(8m)].                    (9)

This closes an entire growing polynomial/Jordan space, not just a direct sum
of individually legal modes. It does not cover a fixed-width disk about one,
slow roots near zero, or arbitrary spectra.

### 4.1 Elementary parameter and product estimates

The rational inequalities 12/5<lambda<17/7 and m>=128 give

    12/5<c<5/2, 3/8<a<1/2, 11/8<d_0<3/2.             (10)

For example c<2193/896<5/2 and
a>(127/128)/(5/2)=127/320>3/8. Also ac=1-1/m.

Let mathcal_P_m(z) be the product for the COMPLETE word H_m. Its multiplicity
formula gives

 mathcal_P_m(z)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-d_j z)^(2^(m-j-1)),
 |mathcal_P_m(1)|=(ac)^n c^(-m).                       (11)

Indeed sum_j 2^(m-j-1)=n and sum_j j2^(m-j-1)=n-m, each proved by induction
using H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j). For z=1+w with |w|=R=1/(16m),

 |1-d_j z| <= a c^j (1+4|w|),

because d_j/(a c^j)=1+1/(a c^j)<11/3<4. Therefore 1+t<=exp(t) and
1-1/m<=exp(-1/m) imply

 |mathcal_P_m(z)|<=c^(-m) exp[-3n/(4m)].               (12)

On that circle, |1-d_0 z|>=a-d_0R>1/3 by (10). Since the retained product
is P_q=mathcal_P_m/(1-d_0z), put

 E_m=3 c^(-m) exp[-3n/(4m)].

Then

             |P_q(z)|<=E_m,  |zP_q(z)|<=2E_m          (13)

on the whole circle. The damping estimate is for complex z, not a real-axis
estimate incorrectly differentiated across a growing Jordan block.

### 4.2 Legal early queries bound every polynomial image, without conditioning

Write D_r=product_(t<r)(1+h_t). Fact 1252b8823bb5a290 gives
||x_i||<=product_(t<i)(1+h_t)<=D_r for all 0<=i<r: this follows directly from
||grad F(x)||<=||x|| and the actual recursion. All these queries are retained.

The polynomials P_0,...,P_(r-1) have successive degrees and nonzero leading
coefficients, so they form a basis of degree-<r polynomials. Moreover

                zP_i=(P_i-P_(i+1))/h_i.                (14)

Every h_i>1. Thus multiplying a polynomial of degree <=r-2 by z increases
the l1 norm of its coefficients in the P-basis by at most a factor two.
Multiplying instead by z-theta increases that norm by at most 2+|theta|<=4
for the roots in (6). Starting with P_0=1 proves

                     ||T[N_k]||<=4^k D_r, k<r.        (15)

If N_k has complex coefficients, extend T complex linearly and use the usual
Hermitian norm. Its expansion in the REAL x_i still proves (15) by the
triangle inequality. No inverse Vandermonde or inverse root-separation factor
occurs, and no bound on the common metric was imposed.

In the first r chronological steps, a level j occurs only if 2^j<=r. Since
c<5/2<2^(3/2), h_t<=1+(1/2)r^(3/2) there. Hence

                     D_r<=(3r^(3/2))^r.               (16)

This is deliberately a loose legal-trajectory bound. Its exponential cost
depends on the temporal degree r, not on the full horizon n.

### 4.3 A separation-free Newton remainder bound, including repeated roots

For completeness the required contour identity is proved here. For any
ordered roots theta_1,...,theta_r inside the circle |z-1|=R, put
N_k(t)=product_(ell<=k)(t-theta_ell). Direct telescoping gives

 1/(z-t)=sum_(k=0)^(r-1) N_k(t)/N_(k+1)(z)
                         +N_r(t)/[(z-t)N_r(z)].        (17)

For a polynomial p define

 C_k=(1/(2pi i)) integral_(|z-1|=R) p(z)/N_(k+1)(z) dz.

Multiplying (17) by p(z) and integrating shows
p(t)-sum C_k N_k(t) is divisible by N_r(t)=chi(t): for t inside the circle,
the remainder term is chi(t) times an analytic function. Thus it and its
required derivatives vanish at every root, with the specified multiplicities.
A polynomial vanishes with those multiplicities iff it is divisible by chi,
as follows by successive division by each linear factor. The polynomial sum
has degree<r, so it is exactly [p]. The integral identity for polynomials is
also obtainable by expanding in powers about the circle's center and
integrating each finite/geometric series; no node-separation hypothesis occurs.

For (6), each |z-theta_ell|>=1/(32m) on the circle. If |p(z)|<=E there,

                       |C_k|<=2(32m)^k E.              (18)

Combining (15), (18) and the geometric sum with 128m>=2 gives

 ||T[p]||<=2ED_r sum_(k<r)(128m)^k
                        <=4ED_r(128m)^r.              (19)

This proof covers collisions of roots directly. The explicit root ordering
need not preserve real coefficients term by term, since the final remainder
of a real polynomial by real chi is real.

Apply (19) to p=P_q and p=zP_q using (13) and (16). With

 K_mr=12 c^(-m)(384m r^(3/2))^r exp[-3n/(4m)],

we get ||x_q||<=K_mr and ||g_q||<=2K_mr. For 0<=b<=2 the actual final
position y=x_q-b g_q satisfies ||y||<=5K_mr. Since F has minimum zero at zero
and is 1-smooth, 2F(y)<=||y||^2. This proves (7), including every possible
terminal interpolation and the original last step d_0.

### 4.4 Exact benchmark comparison and the explicit degree range

We retain the actual B_n from b98bb807d514e80d, rather than replacing the
target by a guessed profile constant. The bound on the actual normalized
ratio is B_n times the right side of (7). The accepted elementary estimate

             B_n<=1+4n^p, p=log_2(3),                 (20)

is sufficient to show this exact ratio tends to zero under (8): its logarithm
contributes O(m), whereas n/m grows exponentially in m. No unverified C54
comparison is a premise, and no inference about a whole-schedule upper bound
is made.

For r<=n/(32m^2), use r<n<2^m. The inequalities log384<6, logm<=m/16 for
m>=128, 6<=m/16, and log2<3/4 give

 log(384m r^(3/2))<2m.

For logm<=m/16, the difference m/16-logm is positive at128 and has positive
derivative for m>=128. Consequently the positive exponent in (7) is at most
4mr<=n/(8m). Dropping c^(-2m)<=1 gives (9). Multiplying (9) by the exact B_n
and then using (20) proves the asserted uniform negligible profile ratio.

## 5. Actual nonquadratic, full-rank realizations in the growing class

The class in Section4 is not empty and is not restricted to quadratic data.
Here is a finite, symbolic, quantitative construction for every m>=128 and
2<=r<=q. This is a nonvacuity calibration, not a new strong lower witness.

Choose a rational alpha in

              (1-1/(64m), 1-1/(128m))                 (21)

such that all P_i(alpha), 0<=i<=q, are nonzero and pairwise distinct. Such a
choice exists: each P_i is a nonzero polynomial, and P_i-P_j is nonzero for
i!=j because their degrees differ. Only finitely many real roots are
forbidden, whereas the interval contains infinitely many rational numbers.
This is a finite algebraic specification, not a request for numerical search.

Let e_0,...,e_(r-1) be the orthonormal basis of R^r and let N_shift e_k=e_(k+1)
for k<r-1, N_shift e_(r-1)=0. For epsilon>0 set

 A_epsilon=alpha I+epsilon N_shift,
 X_i=P_i(A_epsilon)e_0, G_i=A_epsilon X_i,
 V_i=(alpha/2)||X_i||^2.                               (22)

Take optimum data zero, and put nu=1/4. Define transformed jets

 G'_i=(G_i-nu X_i)/(1-nu),
 V'_i=(V_i-nu||X_i||^2/2)/(1-nu).                      (23)

At epsilon=0 these are the jets of the scalar quadratic of curvature
alpha'=(alpha-nu)/(1-nu), lying strictly in (0,1), at points
P_i(alpha)e_0. All points, including the optimum, are distinct. Thus EVERY
ordered residual is strictly negative:

 Q'_ij(0)=-alpha'(1-alpha')||X_i(0)-X_j(0)||^2/2<0.

For epsilon variable each Q'_ij(epsilon) is a real polynomial, since all
quantities in (22)--(23) are polynomial. Define the exact finite constants

 delta=min_(i!=j)(-Q'_ij(0))>0,
 D=1+sum_(i!=j) sum_(k>=1) |coefficient_(epsilon^k) Q'_ij|,
 epsilon=min(1/2,delta/(2D)).                           (24)

All indices here include star and every query. The sums are finite and
provide a computable algebraic law, not a solver oracle. Since epsilon<=1,
|Q'_ij(epsilon)-Q'_ij(0)|<=epsilon D<=delta/2. Thus all transformed ordered
inequalities are strictly satisfied. Fact1252 constructs a convex 1-smooth
interpolant K of them. The single function

                F(x)=(1-nu)K(x)+nu||x||^2/2           (25)

is convex, 1-smooth and nu-strongly convex, has its UNIQUE minimizer at zero,
and interpolates EVERY original (X_i,G_i,V_i). Its actual GD follows (22)
with the prescribed steps. X_0=e_0 has TRUE initial distance exactly one.

These data have the representation (1) with chi=(z-alpha)^r and
T[p]=p(A_epsilon)e_0. The r vectors e_0,A_epsilon e_0,...,
A_epsilon^(r-1)e_0 are linearly independent: in the standard basis their
coefficient matrix is triangular with nonzero diagonal epsilon^k. Thus T is
injective and its REAL common metric is positive definite. The first r
positions X_0,...,X_(r-1) also form a basis, since their polynomials have
successive degrees and nonzero leading coefficients.

No quadratic function with a minimizer at zero can interpolate these
gradients. Its Hessian would be symmetric and would have to equal
A_epsilon on that basis, whereas A_epsilon is nonsymmetric for r>=2 and
epsilon>0. Thus (25) is genuinely nonquadratic on the required jet data.

There is an exact positive terminal payoff, even uniformly over all real b.
Write p0=P_q(alpha)!=0 and p1=P'_q(alpha). The first two coordinates of X_q
and G_q are respectively

            (p0,epsilon p1),
            (alpha p0,epsilon(alpha p1+p0)).

Their determinant is epsilon p0^2. Minimizing the squared distance from the
first vector to the line spanned by the second gives, for every real b,

 2F(X_q-b G_q)
 >=nu||X_q-b G_q||^2
 >=nu epsilon^2 p0^4 /
                 [alpha^2 p0^2+epsilon^2(alpha p1+p0)^2] >0.  (26)

The line-distance identity follows by completing the scalar square in b;
the denominator is nonzero since alpha p0!=0. All quantities are fixed by
(21)--(24) and the actual word. For degrees covered by Section4, (7) also
applies, so this positive payoff is nevertheless asymptotically negligible
against the exact B_n profile. It is not presented as an improved adversary.

## 6. Source audit, scope and the remaining interface

Carl de Boor, "Divided Differences," Surveys in Approximation Theory1
(2005),46--69, arXiv:math/0502036, Proposition7 identifies Newton truncation
with the Hermite remainder; Proposition25 gives the bidiagonal multiplication
formula; equations(49)--(51) give its contour representation. The exact paper
and these proofs were read. Polynomial, repeated-node and real-coordinate
definitions match this application. Sections2 and4.3 re-prove the required
finite algebra rather than importing an unchecked numerical formula.

Downloaded PDF: downloads/deboor_divided_differences.pdf.
Relevant browser extraction: downloads/deboor_relevant_browser_extract.txt.
The local pdftotext command and existing Python PDF extractors were unavailable;
no installation was attempted. Matlas returned no directly applicable theorem
for the two mechanism queries; browser search supplied the exact paper.

These drafts close two SPECIFIED growing-span classes. Exact reciprocal roots
at every scale annihilate, while a near-unit cluster with growing Jordan depth
is controlled uniformly over all common metrics by legal early positions.
Neither proof extends by spectral radius alone to arbitrary metrics or to
slow nodes of order1/S_m. In particular, adding a zero root of multiplicity
>=2 to the resonant class leaves polynomial/constant-gradient suffix data and
is genuinely outside the annihilation proof. A changed generator at each
block is also outside this common-quotient class.

The all-pair law (2) for unrestricted chi of degree n+1 would simply reproduce
the original finite interpolation problem. Nothing here treats that
theorem-strength interface as a solved mechanism. The exact all-schedule
profile target remains unresolved, and there is no new verified fact.
