claim: C55 enlarged-family obstruction (complete proof candidate, UNVERIFIED): the exact prescribed H2 three-boundary seed followed by arbitrary repeated-copy joins plus nonnegative balanced pairs (p,q-1) cannot certify a useful objective bound on the critical horizon-dependent word. Every full PSD objective certificate in this family, even with arbitrary relaxed q_cert, must satisfy q_cert>(2/5)^(2m) exp(2^(m-3)/m), hence q_cert>1 for m>=128 and q_cert tends to infinity. This is a certificate-family obstruction, not a legal adversary or a statement about unrestricted certificates/the actual schedule.
evidence:
# C55: the prescribed three-boundary queried-pair recurrence is insufficient

Status: **complete scoped proof candidate, not verifier-accepted**. No
optimization or verifier allocation is used. The predecessor
`1252b8823bb5a290` supplies the interpolation convention and the requirement
that an objective certificate be positive semidefinite on all the original
formal vectors. Everything specific to this recursive family is derived
below. Prior C53/C55 findings are motivation, not mathematical premises.

The result covers precisely the H2 seed and the repeated-copy join with the
added balanced pair described below, including arbitrary horizon-dependent
join parameters and storage choices. It does not cover arbitrary seeds,
independent internal array corrections, or unrestricted certificates for the
same schedule. The test vectors are formal vectors, not a legal function.

## 1. Statement and notation

Fix an integer m>=128 and define

    epsilon=1/m, lambda=1+sqrt(2),
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c,
    d_j=a c^j,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+d_j,H_j),
    n_j=2^j-1, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

All steps are predetermined and strictly positive; the bridges grow with
the recursion level. No upper bound on the steps is assumed. The claims
below concern this explicit family, not arbitrary nonnegative schedules.

For formal gradients substitute the actual GD recursion with smoothness
one and optimum jet zero. For distinct samples define

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    C_ij=-2 Q_ji
        =2(f_i-f_j)+2<g_j,x_j-x_i>-||g_i-g_j||^2.

The accepted predecessor proves C_ij>=0 for legal smooth convex data.
Formal vectors used to test a quadratic certificate need not be legal.

An array at level j has storage parameters u_j,v_j and star pattern

    lambda_(star,i)=h_i              (i<n_j),
    lambda_(star,n_j)=u_j,
    lambda_(i,star)=0                (i<n_j),
    lambda_(n_j,star)=s_j=S_j+u_j-v_j.                 (1)

Here lambda_ik denotes a multiplier array on C_ik; the scalar lambda without
indices denotes 1+sqrt(2). The full identity defines its remainder E_j:

    ||x_start||^2-||x_end-u_j g_end||^2-2v_j f_end
                   =sum lambda_ik C_ik+E_j,
    Z_j=(u_j-1)^2+v_j,
    z_j=sum_(i<n_j) h_i g_i+g_end.                    (2)

Start from the exact H2 seed in Section 2, and for j=2,...,m-1 apply any
join in Section 3, with a balanced multiplier gamma_j>=0 on the queried
pair (p,q-1). The same child array is embedded on the left and multiplied
by r_j>=0 on the right. All actual final multipliers must be nonnegative
to give a certificate. One may use any real u_j,v_j, with v_m>0, and need
not require positive semidefinite child or local remainders.

Then, if the complete objective matrix at level q_cert is PSD, necessarily

    q_cert >= 1/k_m^2
           > (2/5)^(2m) exp[2^(m-3)/m],              (3)

where the signed numbers k_j are defined in Section 5. The last expression
tends to infinity. In particular q_cert>1 for m>=128, so this family cannot
supply v_m>=M_m with E_m PSD, nor any useful bounded objective coefficient.
This is an obstruction for the enlarged C55 recurrence, not an upper or
lower bound on the actual schedule's worst-case objective.

The proof retains every internal child square and every new pair term. Its
key change from C53 is that the last-query gradient is c times the terminal
gradient, instead of equal to it.

## 2. The exact seed, its signs, and its attained boundary form

Put

    b0=1+a, M=M_1=2+a, d=d_1=1-epsilon,
    x=d/M, eta=x^2+2x-1, a0=(2-b0^2)/b0^2.

The one-step seed H1=(b0) has finite multipliers

    lambda_01=M, lambda_10=1,

star multipliers lambda_(star,0)=b0, lambda_(star,1)=M, and no incoming
star multipliers. Set u_1=M, v_1=2M-1, hence Z_1=M^2. Direct expansion in
(2) gives

    E_1=(2-b0^2)||g_0-g_1||^2.

To obtain H2, use the join of Section 3 with gamma=0 and

    A=1/x, B=2+x, r=3+x+1/x, t=1/x-2-x,
    P=(1+M eta)/x, Q=M,
    u_2=M_2=2M+d, v_2=2M_2-1.                        (4)

Here 1<b0<sqrt(2), 3/8<x<sqrt(2)-1, and eta<0. For the upper bound on x,
with s=sqrt(2)-1=1/lambda, expansion gives

    d-sM=-epsilon[1-2s^2/(1+epsilon)]<0.

The lower bound follows from d>=127/128 and M<5/2. Thus a0,t>0.
Moreover eta>=-7/64, so 1+M eta>1-35/128>0. Consequently A,B,P,Q,r are
positive. The physical star pattern has s_1=s_2=0, and the update described
in Section 3 yields nonnegative actual star multipliers as well.

For the four gradients of H2 define

    U=b0(g_0-g_1), V0=b0(g_2-g_3), D0=g_1-g_3.

Expanding the complete join gives

    E_2=a0||U||^2+(r a0+t)||V0||^2
                         +M^2(-eta)||D0||^2.          (5)

For an explicit coefficient check, (4) gives H=-t(M+d), ell=-tM in (8)
below. Substitute V=d g_1+b0 g_2+g_3, Z_1=M^2, Z_2=(2M+d)^2 into (8).
The mixed V0,D0 coefficient is A d-M=0; the D0 square coefficient is
M^2(1-2x-x^2). The two seed remainders provide a0||U||^2+r a0||V0||^2.
The remaining term is t||V0||^2, establishing (5).

Changing u_2,v_2 and only the two terminal star coefficients in (1) adds
(M_2^2-Z_2)||g_3||^2 to (5). Thus the obstruction also permits these
storage changes at the seed. The finite seed coefficients remain fixed.

With (z,e,w)=(z_2,g_3,g_2), the boundary relation is

    z-M_2 e=U+V0+(M+d)D0.

All three boundary vectors are independent. Set c0=M^2(-eta), l0=M+d.
The exact identity

    a0||U||^2+c0||D0||^2
      =a0 c0/(c0+a0 l0^2) ||U+l0 D0||^2
           +||a0 l0 U-c0 D0||^2/(c0+a0 l0^2)

has its second square equal to zero for every prescribed value of
U+l0 D0. Therefore the sharp, attained boundary form is

    K_2(z,e,w)=A2||z-M_2 e-b0(w-e)||^2
                         +B2||w-e||^2
                         +(M_2^2-Z_2)||e||^2,
    A2=[1/a0+(1+x)^2/(-eta)]^(-1),
    B2=(r a0+t)b0^2.                                 (6)

No unattainability of boundary minimizers is assumed in what follows.

## 3. The actual enlarged array and the full local identity

At a join write n=n_j, p=n, q=2n+1, S=S_j, M=M_j, d=d_j, b=1+d.
Choose A,B,P,Q with

    r=1+A+B, P-Q=b+(1-A)S.

Embed the old array on the left and r times that array on the right.
For each right queried index p<i<q add

    A h_i to (p,i), B h_i to (q,i),
    -(A+B)h_i to (star,i).

Add the six corrections

    (p,q):P, (q,p):Q,
    (p,star):-s_j, (q,star):s_(j+1)-r s_j,
    (star,p):b-u_j, (star,q):u_(j+1)-r u_j.            (7)

Finally add gamma>=0 to both (p,q-1) and (q-1,p). These are actual queried
samples. This balanced change preserves every function-value flow and
every star multiplier. It adds no incoming unqueried-terminal constraint.

For example A,B,P,Q>=0, u_j>=0 and s_j>=0 at the relevant levels suffice
for nonnegative actual arrays when the seed is nonnegative: right queried
star coefficients become (r-A-B)h_i=h_i; the two terminal star coefficients
become b and u_(j+1); the two incoming terminal star coefficients become
zero and s_(j+1). All other entries are copied or receive nonnegative
additions. The obstruction allows all real A,B,P,Q satisfying the flow
identity and r>=0, so it also covers choices whose signs are certified by
a more detailed inspection of the actual array.

Write g=g_p, e=g_q, w=g_(q-1), and define

    t=A-B,
    H=M+d-B(M-d)-tM,
    ell=P-A,
    V=x_p-x_q-g+e=d g+z_right.

The complete remainder identity is

    E_next=E_left+r E_right
       +t||V||^2+2<V,(H-ell)g+ell e>
       +(Z_j-rd^2)||g||^2+(rZ_j-Z_next)||e||^2
       +2gamma<g-w,e+a w-V>.                          (8)

Here a is the fixed parameter in b0=1+a, since every block ends with that
same step b0. To verify the new term, x_(q-1)=x_q+b0 w gives

    -gamma(C_(p,q-1)+C_(q-1,p))
       =2gamma[||g-w||^2-<g-w,x_p-x_(q-1)>]
       =2gamma<g-w,e+a w-V>.

For completeness the old part of (8) can be checked before the pair is
added. Put D=x_p-x_q and W=sum_(p<i<q)h_i g_i=x_p-b g-x_q. The rank
correction sums to

    2AS f_p+2BS f_q-AS||g||^2-BS||e||^2
                      -2<W,A(x_p-g)+B(x_q-e)>.

The value coefficient at p becomes

    -2v_j+2AS+2(P-Q)-2s_j-2(b-u_j)
            =2[(A-1)S+P-Q-b]=0.

The value coefficient at q becomes -2v_next using r=1+A+B and (1).
After subtracting the correction from the new potential minus the two
child potentials, the quadratic coefficients are

    D^2:t, (D,g):H-ell-t, (D,e):ell+t,
    g^2:Z_j-rd^2+t-2H+2ell,
    e^2:rZ_j-Z_next+t+2ell, (g,e):H-2ell-t,

where a mixed coefficient multiplies twice the indicated inner product.
Substituting V=D-g+e proves the old part of (8). Thus (8) is an identity
on the full formal space, with every inherited remainder retained.

## 4. Explicit eliminated matrix and every singular range condition

This section records the exact recurrence being obstructed, including
its singular cases. Write an attained child boundary form as

    K(z,e,w)=alpha||z||^2+2beta<z,e>+2chi<z,w>
                        +delta||e||^2+2etaK<e,w>+phi||w||^2.

In (8) substitute E_left=K(L,g,u)+its internal remainder and
E_right=K(R,e,w)+its internal remainder. The six-variable form has
parent boundary z=L+d g+R. Eliminate X=(g,u,R) and retain Y=(z,e,w).
After L=z-d g-R, its symmetric matrix is

                         [ D_el  B_el ]
                         [ B_el^T C_el].

Its entries are exactly

    D_el(1,1)=(alpha+t-r)d^2-2beta d+delta
                                      +2d(H-ell-gamma)+Z_j,
    D_el(1,2)=etaK-d chi,
    D_el(1,3)=d(alpha+t)-beta+H-ell-gamma,
    D_el(2,2)=phi,
    D_el(2,3)=-chi,
    D_el(3,3)=(1+r)alpha+t;

    B_el=[ -d alpha+beta,  d ell+gamma, gamma(a+d);
                 chi,          0,              0;
               -alpha,     r beta+ell,       r chi+gamma ];

    C_el=[ alpha,          0,                    0;
              0, r delta+rZ_j-Z_next,  r etaK-gamma;
              0,       r etaK-gamma,    r phi-2a gamma ].  (9)

The full six-variable matrix is PSD if and only if all of the following
hold:

    D_el is PSD;
    B_el^T xi=0 for EVERY xi in ker(D_el);
    C_el-B_el^T D_el^dagger B_el is PSD.                (10)

The middle condition is equivalently that every column of B_el belongs to
the range of D_el. The dagger is the inverse on its positive eigenspaces
and zero on its kernel. To prove (10), first restrict to Y=0. A nonzero
cross coefficient against a null vector of D_el makes the form unbounded
below by scaling that null direction. Once these coefficients vanish,
complete the square on the positive eigenspaces. This proves both
necessity and sufficiency, including every rank of D_el.

When the children have exact attained decompositions with PSD internal
remainders and r>=0, (10) is also equivalent to PSD of the entire parent
remainder: the independent boundary data can be lifted while setting all
internal child squares to zero. The new sharp boundary form is the last
Schur complement in (10). No such interpretation is needed for the
obstruction below: it directly evaluates the original E_j and does not
assume that any earlier elimination passed.

## 5. A different formal seed survives every new queried pair

Define

    k_2=M_2+6epsilon, theta=c.

At the H2 seed choose the following explicit four gradients, all multiples
of an arbitrary vector e:

    g_0=(2-c+6epsilon/b0)e,
    g_1=e, g_2=c e, g_3=e.                            (11)

Then the exact boundary is

    z_2=k_2 e, g_end=e, g_last_query=c e.

Indeed z_2=b0 g_0+(1+d_1)g_1+b0 g_2+g_3=(M_2+6epsilon)e.
In (5), D0=0, V0=b0(c-1)e, and U=[6epsilon-b0(c-1)]e.
We next prove the strict energy inequality

    E_2 < (k_2^2-Z_2)||e||^2                         (12)

for e!=0, for every m>=128. This includes all internal seed squares.

First, a>2/5. In fact sqrt(2)<10/7 gives lambda<17/7, so

    a >= (127/129)(7/17)=889/2193 >2/5.

Also a<s=sqrt(2)-1, b0<sqrt(2), M>12/5 and c<5/2. To bound a0, use

    b0=sqrt(2)-2s epsilon/(1+epsilon),
    2-b0^2<4sqrt(2)s epsilon=4(2-sqrt(2))epsilon
                                          <(12/5)epsilon,
    b0^2>49/25.

Therefore a0<(60/49)epsilon<(5/4)epsilon. Since 3/8<x<s<1/2,

    r=3+x+1/x<37/6<25/4.

Furthermore

    s-x=epsilon[1-2s^2/(1+epsilon)]/M<(5/12)epsilon,
    t=(s-x)(1+1/(sx))<(5/12)(23/3)epsilon<4epsilon.

The estimate on 1/(sx) uses s>2/5 and x>3/8. We have
0<6epsilon<b0(c-1), because 6epsilon<=3/64 and b0,c-1>7/5. Hence

    ||U||^2 <= b0^2(c-1)^2||e||^2,
    b0^2(c-1)^2<2(3/2)^2=9/2.

Substitution into the FULL seed formula (5) gives

    E_2-(M_2^2-Z_2)||e||^2
       <=[(r+1)a0+t] b0^2(c-1)^2||e||^2
       <[(29/4)(5/4)+4](9/2)epsilon||e||^2
       =(1881/32)epsilon||e||^2
       <60epsilon||e||^2.

Finally M_2=5-epsilon+2a>5, so

    k_2^2-M_2^2=12M_2 epsilon+36epsilon^2>60epsilon.

This proves (12). In particular the argument has not replaced the full
seed by an unattainable boundary minimum or dropped a positive square.

## 6. A uniform subcritical gap and its exact propagation

Set

    R0=k_2/(c d_2)=(M_2+6epsilon)/[(1-epsilon)c^2].

We have the explicit bound

    0<R0<1-epsilon/4.                                (13)

For its proof expand the available gap using lambda^2=2lambda+1:

    (c d_2-M_2)/epsilon
      =[6sqrt(2)+epsilon-2lambda^2 epsilon^2
                                  -lambda^2 epsilon^3]/(1+epsilon).

This is greater than 8. Indeed after subtracting 8 and multiplying by
1+epsilon, the numerator is

    6sqrt(2)-8-7epsilon-2lambda^2 epsilon^2-lambda^2 epsilon^3
      >2/5-7/128-12/128^2-6/128^3>0.

Consequently c d_2-k_2>2epsilon. Since c d_2=(1-epsilon)c^2<25/4,

    1-R0>8epsilon/25>epsilon/4,

as claimed.

Now define signed numbers recursively by

    k_(j+1)=-k_j^2/d_j, j>=2.                         (14)

For every block H_j there is a formal gradient assignment linear in its
terminal vector e such that

    z_j=k_j e, g_end=e, g_last_query=c e,
    E_j <= (k_j^2-Z_j)||e||^2.                        (15)

This holds simultaneously for every permitted choice of the join and
storage parameters, including choices depending on the target horizon.
The seed is (11)-(12). For the induction step put the right child on its
template with terminal e, and the left child on its template with terminal

    g=-k_j e/d_j.

Then V=d_j g+z_right=0, and the parent moment is

    z_next=z_left+d_j g+z_right=k_j g=k_(j+1)e.

Its last-query gradient remains c e. The crucial NEW pair term in (8) is

    2gamma(-k_j/d_j-c)(1+a c)||e||^2.                 (16)

It is nonpositive at every level. At j=2, k_2>0 proves this directly. For
j>=3, k_j<0; solving (14) gives

    |k_j|=(1-epsilon)c^j R0^(2^(j-2)),
    |k_j|/d_j=c R0^(2^(j-2))<c.                     (17)

Thus (16) is negative for gamma>0 and e!=0, since 1+a c=2-epsilon>0.

The other mixed local terms vanish because V=0. Since r>=0, the two
complete child estimates in (15) retain their direction under addition.
Keeping their full values and the nonpositive new pair term gives

    E_next <= (k_j^2-Z_j)||g||^2
                 +r(k_j^2-Z_j)||e||^2
                 +(Z_j-rd_j^2)||g||^2+(rZ_j-Z_next)||e||^2
             = (k_j^4/d_j^2-Z_next)||e||^2,

which is exactly (15) at the parent. No local PSD, nonsingularity, greedy
storage, or rank assumption was used.

In co-coercivity language the pair has

    C_(p,q-1)+C_(q-1,p)
          =2(2-epsilon)(c+k_j/d_j)||e||^2>=0.

This explains why a nonnegative weight on this actual pair cannot repair
this new formal template. The old C53 template had the opposite sign on
some such pairs; those are different formal vectors.

## 7. The original initial-vector objective conversion

Let u=u_m, v=v_m>0, Z=(u-1)^2+v and k=k_m. For the final array the full
objective certificate at any level q_cert is

    M_cert=q_cert||x_0||^2-2f_n
                     +sum_(i!=j) (2lambda_ji/v)Q_ij
           =(q_cert-1/v)||x_0||^2
                     +[||x_n-u g_n||^2+E_m]/v.        (18)

This follows directly from (2) and C_ij=-2Q_ji. In particular E_m PSD
and nonnegative actual multipliers yield the bound q_cert=1/v. The
normalization is the project's 2(f_n-f_star)/(L||x_0-x_star||^2), by the
scaling in predecessor `1252b8823bb5a290`.

Keep x_0 independent of the formal template in (15), and set
beta0=k+u-1. Since z_m=k e,

    x_n-u g_n=x_0-beta0 e.

The restriction of v M_cert is bounded ABOVE by the two-variable form
with matrix

                  [ q_cert v    -beta0       ]
                  [  -beta0    2k beta0-v    ].        (19)

The difference is a nonnegative multiple of ||e||^2, by (15). If the
original M_cert is PSD, this upper matrix must therefore also be PSD.
Its second diagonal is positive: if it were zero, PSD would force
beta0=0, making that diagonal -v<0. Its determinant now implies

    q_cert >= beta0^2/[v(2k beta0-v)] >=1/k^2,

where the last step is exactly

    k^2 beta0^2-v(2k beta0-v)=(v-k beta0)^2>=0.

This includes arbitrary increases of q_cert and indefinite child or final
remainders. It tests the original x_0 variable, not only the condensed
gradient state.

From (13),(17) and 1-x<=exp(-x),

    |k_m|<c^m exp[-2^(m-4)/m].                        (20)

Thus (3) follows from c<5/2. The logarithm of its right side is
2^(m-3)/m-2m log(5/2), which tends to infinity because 2^m/m^2 tends to
infinity. Its successive ratio is 2m^2/(m+1)^2>3/2 for m>=7.
For m>=128, (20) also gives |k_m|<1: log(5/2)<1 follows from
exp(1)>1+1+1/2+1/6>5/2, and 2^(m-4)>m^2 for m>=128. The latter inequality
holds at 128 and is preserved since 2m^2/(m+1)^2>1. Hence q_cert>1.

## 8. Undeformed calibration and scope checks

Set epsilon=0, so a=1/lambda, c=lambda. Then b0=sqrt(2), M_j=lambda^j,
d_j=lambda^(j-1), a0=t=eta=0, and the physical seed E_2 is identically
zero. At each higher join choose

    A=B=lambda, r=lambda^2, t=H=ell=0,
    P=lambda, Q=M_j,
    u_j=(1+sqrt(4M_j^2-3))/2, v_j=u_j, Z_j=M_j^2.

The same storage choice can be made at H2 by its permitted terminal-star
change, preserving E_2=0. It has s_j=S_j>=0. The flow equation follows
from M_j=lambda d_j, and (8) with gamma=0 gives E_next=0. Every actual
multiplier is nonnegative by Section 3. This is an exact valid undeformed
calibration of the full array and the objective conversion (18).

If one retains the physical H2 storage u_2=M_2,v_2=2M_2-1 instead, the
seed still has Z_2=M_2^2; switching to the displayed u_j,v_j at the next
level likewise changes only the two terminal star coefficients and is
allowed. No calibration identity is being carried from a differently
normalized performance measure.

At epsilon=0 the obstruction template has k_2=M_2 and R0=1, so it yields
only q_cert>=lambda^(-2m), entirely compatible with the valid bound
1/u_m of order lambda^(-m). The strict horizon-dependent gap in (13)
is essential.

The hypothesis r>=0 is exactly the scaling restriction in the C55 state
recurrence, not an extra PSD assumption on its children. It is also
forced by nonnegative final arrays in this prescribed construction. The
seed has the positive coefficient lambda_01=M. At every larger level,
the first two queried samples retain this coefficient unchanged, because
they lie in the left child and none of the join corrections touches their
ordered pair. In a right child the corresponding ordered pair has
coefficient rM and is untouched by the parent's fan, sparse, and new-pair
corrections. In the final leftmost occurrence of any such join it remains
untouched by all higher joins. Thus a negative r at any level would leave
a negative actual coefficient in the final array. This also shows that
the proof covers arrays required to be nonnegative only at the final
level. The case r=0 is already included in the energy induction.

The seed restriction matters: the result does not assert that every H2
array has (5), or that every three-boundary seed is covered. A different
seed has to be tested against the seed-energy and last-query conditions
(12),(15). Arbitrary additional queried pairs can change (16); no claim
about those corrections is made here. Likewise the formal template need
not satisfy omitted interpolation constraints, so it is not an actual
lower witness for H_m. Accepted terminal completion removes no queried
prefix constraints and cannot justify dropping them.

This analysis makes no lower-bound claim for schedules with zero steps.
The accepted predecessor handles those schedules without identifying
duplicated formal gradients. Any future unrestricted conclusion would
still have to retain both zero-step and arbitrarily-large-step cases.

All new mathematics in this file remains a proof candidate. The exact
minimax/profile target remains unresolved, and the fact graph is unchanged.

## 9. Reproducibility of the algebraic audit

One fixed rational substitution in the six-variable identity (9) was
checked by polarization of its 21 coefficients, and the four rational
constant margins in Sections 5-6 were checked exactly. These were tiny
arithmetic checks, not optimization or a numerical search. The displayed
expansions and inequalities are the proof; the checks are not premises.

For architecture context, the exact local text of Altschuler--Parrilo,
arXiv:2309.16530, Theorem 3.4 and its helper-lemma proof was reread. No
theorem from that paper is imported; its undeformed recursion motivated
the array, whose modified full identity is proved in Section 3.

claim: Quantitative arbitrary-q queried-cut candidate: every nonnegative FULL objective certificate obeys an exact 3x3 PSD capacity inequality in h_j, actual incident/cross-cut flow, initial-distance coupling and target-position first moments. A full three-interval/two-cut matrix and exact singular rules are derived. An explicit h=(1,1),q=1/5 certificate refutes dropping the moments, while a supplied long-step family refutes nonnegative-flow closure under direct Schur elimination. evidence:
# Quantitative queried cuts of full objective certificates

Status: complete self-contained candidate calculations, NOT verifier-accepted.
Current TASK/master_guidance closes routine verification and numerical search;
neither a solver nor fact_submit is used. Every new calculation below belongs
to this single proof package, not to a chain of unverified premises. The only
accepted mathematical dependency is fact `1252b8823bb5a290`, for the exact
normalized problem, interpolation necessity, and attained full certificates.

## 1. The unchanged target and the full certificate hypothesis

For a finite nonnegative schedule h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), W_n(h) is the
supremum of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over every finite
dimension, convex differentiable f with L-Lipschitz gradient and a minimizer
x_star, and x_0 != x_star, using x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L) grad f(x_i).
The exact benchmark is U_n^ZJ=1/B_n, B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1, with the original
phi/psi recursions in accepted fact `b98bb807d514e80d`. The affirmative
target remains: for every epsilon>0, all sufficiently large n and EVERY
nonnegative length-n schedule have W_n(h)>=(1-epsilon)/B_n. A negative
answer requires a fixed positive relative improvement along unbounded
horizons by actual full-objective upper bounds. Neither outcome is claimed.

Work at smoothness one and let x_0,g_0,...,g_n be independent formal vectors.
Set x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. All finite f_i
are independent formal scalars. Put I={star,0,...,n}, lambda_ii=0, and

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

A supplied full certificate consists of a finite real q_cert and ACTUAL
lambda_ij>=0 for which

 M=q_cert||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij                 (1)

has every value coefficient zero and is PSD on the full original formal
space. In particular the finite-node flows obey

 out_i-in_i=2*1_(i=n).                                         (2)

No optimum-source edge is forbidden. No support, symmetrizability,
positive-definiteness, h_i<2, or Huber equality assumption is made.
Zero-step gradients remain independent.

Necessity of Q_ij<=0 on legal instances (accepted1252b8823bb5a290) gives
W_n(h)<=q_cert for any such certificate. Conversely, that SAME accepted
fact supplies a full certificate at q_cert=W_n(h) for every nonnegative
h, including empty/all-zero schedules, by positive-step attainment and
explicit zero-step lifting. Thus any universal necessary inequality proved
below can be applied to at least one attained certificate at the actual W.
An inequality involving the multipliers of a particular supplied certificate
is not by itself a multiplier-free lower bound on W.

Every feasible q_cert is positive. Setting all gradients to zero first
gives q_cert>=0. Summing (2) yields
sum_i lambda_(i,star)=2+sum_i lambda_(star,i)>=2. If q_cert=0, set all
finite gradients to the same scalar1. The coefficient of scalar x_0 in
M is then -sum_i lambda_(i,star)<0, so M is unbounded below. This excludes0.

## 2. A nontrivial queried-cut capacity inequality

Fix a queried index j<n, write b_cut=h_j, and let T_cut={j+1,...,n}.
Its complement in I includes the optimum and indices0,...,j. Define

 s_tail=sum_(j<t<n)h_t,
 ell_tail(k)=sum_(j<t<k)h_t for k in T_cut,
 C_in=sum_(i outside T_cut,k in T_cut)lambda_ik,
 C_out=sum_(i in T_cut,k outside T_cut)lambda_ik,
 F_cut=sum_(k in T_cut)lambda_(j,k),
 B_cut=sum_(k in T_cut)lambda_(k,j),
 I_cut=sum_(i!=j)lambda_(i,j),
 J_forward=sum_(k in T_cut)ell_tail(k) lambda_(j,k),
 J_in=sum_(i outside T_cut,k in T_cut)ell_tail(k) lambda_ik,
 mu_query=lambda_(j,star),
 mu_tail=sum_(i in T_cut)lambda_(i,star).

These are actual array sums, including every remote edge and optimum edge.
Summing (2) over T_cut gives C_out-C_in=2. Set

 A_cut=I_cut-b_cut F_cut,
 D_cut=1+2s_tail+C_in+J_in,
 K_cut=b_cut C_out-F_cut-B_cut-J_forward.                       (3)

The following matrix is necessarily PSD:

              [ q_cert       -mu_query/2       -mu_tail/2 ]
 T_query   =  [ -mu_query/2    A_cut             K_cut/2   ].    (4)
              [ -mu_tail/2    K_cut/2            D_cut     ]

Proof. Evaluate (1) on the formal subspace

 x_0=z,  g_i=0 (i<j),  g_j=u,  g_i=v (i>j).

All value coefficients have already canceled, so they may be set to0.
Only finite-source edges to star contribute z; their total is
-<z,mu_query*u+mu_tail*v>. The coefficient of ||u||^2 in the norm
terms is (out_j+in_j)/2=I_cut, since j<n. The only additional diagonal
terms are -h_j lambda_(j,k)||u||^2 for k>j. This gives A_cut.

For the ||v||^2 coefficient, set u=z=0. A tail point k then has
x_k=-ell_tail(k)v, and a non-tail finite point has position0. Within-tail
position terms sum to

 sum_(k in T_cut)ell_tail(k)(out_k^internal-in_k^internal).

Use (2) to replace the internal divergence by
2*1_(k=n)-out_k^cross+in_k^cross. The outgoing cross position terms
add back sum_k ell_tail(k)out_k^cross. This leaves
2s_tail+J_in. The cross norm terms are
(C_out+C_in)/2=1+C_in; internal norm terms are zero. Hence D_cut.

For the coefficient of <u,v>, norm terms give -(F_cut+B_cut).
An edge j->k with k in T_cut contributes -ell_tail(k)<u,v>, totaling
-J_forward. An edge sourced in T_cut and targeting its complement
has the position shift +b_cut*u, totaling b_cut C_out<u,v>.
All other position terms have either zero source gradient or cancel
the common tail shift. These are exactly K_cut. Thus the restriction is

 q_cert||z||^2-<z,mu_query*u+mu_tail*v>
                   +A_cut||u||^2+K_cut<u,v>+D_cut||v||^2,

whose scalar coefficient matrix is (4). Since the original polynomial
is PSD on every formal vector, its restriction is PSD. This restriction
is a necessary test, not an assertion that its formal vectors are legal
trajectories, and it deletes no edge from the original certificate.

Complete the independent z square, using q_cert>0. Put

 a_cut=A_cut-mu_query^2/(4q_cert),
 d_cut=D_cut-mu_tail^2/(4q_cert),
 k_cut=K_cut-mu_query*mu_tail/(2q_cert).

Then (4) is equivalent to

 a_cut>=0, d_cut>=0, k_cut^2<=4a_cut*d_cut.                     (5)

In particular, when d_cut>0 the quantitative incidence cost is

 I_cut >= b_cut F_cut + mu_query^2/(4q_cert)
              + [b_cut C_out-F_cut-B_cut-J_forward
                       -mu_query*mu_tail/(2q_cert)]^2/(4d_cut). (6)

When d_cut=0 the square numerator in (6) must be zero and the remaining
condition is I_cut>=b_cut F_cut+mu_query^2/(4q_cert). There is no division
by a vanished residual and no strict-PSD assumption. Equivalently,

 |b_cut C_out-F_cut-B_cut-J_forward
                     -mu_query*mu_tail/(2q_cert)|
       <=2 sqrt((I_cut-b_cut F_cut-mu_query^2/(4q_cert))
                 *(1+2s_tail+C_in+J_in-mu_tail^2/(4q_cert))).   (7)

If every edge incident to j vanishes, I_cut=F_cut=B_cut=J_forward=
mu_query=0. Then (5) forces b_cut C_out=0. Since C_out>=2, b_cut=0.
This recovers the qualitative incidence obstruction, now as the zero-cost
case of an exact quantitative condition at every finite certificate level.
If b_cut=0 there is no contradiction; the zero-step case is included.

For an alternative exact q cost define

 Z_cut=[ A_cut K_cut/2 ; K_cut/2 D_cut ],
 m_cut=(mu_query,mu_tail)^T.

Condition (4) is equivalent to Z_cut>=0, m_cut in Range(Z_cut), and

 q_cert >= (1/4) m_cut^T Z_cut^+ m_cut.                         (8)

Here Z_cut^+ inverts its positive eigenvalues and vanishes on its kernel.
For proof, diagonalize the real symmetric Z_cut. A component of m_cut
on a zero eigenvector would give an unbounded linear polynomial in that
free direction. Once these components vanish, complete one square for
each positive eigenvalue. This proves necessity and sufficiency, including
all singular cases. If 4A_cut D_cut-K_cut^2>0, the right side is explicitly

 (D_cut*mu_query^2-K_cut*mu_query*mu_tail+A_cut*mu_tail^2)
                         /(4A_cut D_cut-K_cut^2).             (9)

## 3. Why total cut flow cannot replace its position moment

Here is ONE exact supplied certificate. Take n=2, h=(1,1), q_cert=1/5,
with the following nonzero multipliers and every other multiplier zero:

 lambda_02=1, lambda_10=1, lambda_21=2,
 lambda_(1,star)=1, lambda_(2,star)=1.                          (10)

All coefficients are nonnegative. The finite flows are respectively0,0,2.
With x_1=x_0-g_0 and x_2=x_0-g_0-g_1, direct expansion of (1) gives

 M=(1/5)||x_0-(5/2)(g_1+g_2)||^2
                                      +(3/4)||g_1-g_2||^2.   (11)

For an explicit coefficient check, the sum of the position terms in (10)
is -<x_0,g_1+g_2>-||g_0||^2+<g_0,g_1>+<g_0,g_2>
+3<g_1,g_2>. The norm terms add ||g_0||^2+2||g_1||^2+2||g_2||^2
-<g_0,g_1>-<g_0,g_2>-2<g_1,g_2>. Their sum is exactly the expansion
of (11) after adding q_cert||x_0||^2. This is full PSD with the
original independent g_0 present as a kernel direction.

For j=0, T_cut={1,2}, the exact data are

 b_cut=1, s_tail=1, C_in=1, C_out=3,
 F_cut=B_cut=I_cut=1, J_forward=J_in=1,
 mu_query=0, mu_tail=2,
 A_cut=0, D_cut=5, K_cut=0.

Thus (4) is the singular rank-one square (z-5v)^2/5, and (8) gives
the exact cost1/5. Dropping the target-position moment J_in would assert

 mu_tail^2 <= 4q_cert(1+2s_tail+C_in),                          (12)

which here reads4<=16/5, false. Equivalently, that proposed scalar cost
would falsely require q_cert>=1/4. Dropping J_forward from K_cut likewise
produces K_cut=1 while A_cut=0, falsely rejecting the same full certificate.
Therefore unweighted cross-cut flow cannot be substituted in these exact
capacity tests. The actual remote edge0->2, whose target lies one unit
of step mass into the tail, supplies the missing moment. This refutes
(12), not every conceivable scalar invariant or an existential re-selection.

## 4. A general interval restriction and an explicit two-cut test

Partition {0,...,n} into m nonempty chronological interval blocks
B_0,...,B_(m-1), including n in the final block. Let

 H_r=sum_(i in B_r,i<n)h_i,
 ell_r(i)=sum_(t in B_r,t<i)h_t for i in B_r,
 Lambda_rs=sum_(i in B_r,j in B_s)lambda_ij for r!=s,
 Lambda_(r,star)=sum_(i in B_r)lambda_(i,star)=mu_r,
 Lambda_(star,r)=sum_(i in B_r)lambda_(star,i),
 E_rs=sum_(i in B_r,j in B_s)ell_s(j)lambda_ij for r!=s,
 E_(star,r)=sum_(j in B_r)ell_r(j)lambda_(star,j),
 in_r^cross=sum_(a!=r)Lambda_ar,

where the last sum includes a=star. E is a target-position FIRST MOMENT,
not an arbitrary error term. Only off-diagonal block data are needed.
Temporarily write E_rr for the analogous internal sum during the proof.
Set every g_i=u_r on B_r, while leaving x_0=z independent.

The complete restricted polynomial is

 q_cert||z||^2-sum_r mu_r<z,u_r>
             +sum_r D_r^blk||u_r||^2+sum_(r<s)K_rs^blk<u_r,u_s>,  (13)

where

 D_r^blk=(1+2H_r)*1_(r=m-1)
       +sum_(a!=r)(Lambda_ar+E_ar)-H_r sum_(s>r)Lambda_rs,     (14)

 K_rs^blk=H_r(mu_s+sum_(t<=r)Lambda_st)
       -H_s sum_(t>s)Lambda_rt
       -Lambda_rs-Lambda_sr-E_rs-E_sr       (r<s).             (15)

The sums in (15) have only finite block indices; all appearances of the
optimum in its position term are in mu_s. These identities hold even
for arbitrary flow arrays before imposing PSD, and every original edge
is included through these exact sums.

Proof. Write p_i=sum_(a<r)H_a u_a+ell_r(i)u_r for i in B_r, so
x_i=z-p_i. Position terms equal

 -sum_r mu_r<z,u_r>
 +sum_r sum_(i in B_r)out_i<u_r,p_i>
 -sum_(r,s finite)sum_(i in B_r,j in B_s)lambda_ij<u_r,p_j>.

For ||u_r||^2 the local part of the first sum is
sum_(i in B_r)ell_r(i)out_i. By node flow (2) this equals
sum_a E_ar+2H_r*1_(r=m-1), with a including r and star. The second
sum subtracts E_rr and H_r sum_(s>r)Lambda_rs. The cross norm coefficient
is (out_r^cross+in_r^cross)/2=in_r^cross+1_(r=m-1). Combining proves(14).

For r<s, sources in B_r contribute
-H_s sum_(t>s)Lambda_rt-E_rs to the coefficient of <u_r,u_s>.
Sources in B_s contribute
H_r(out_s-sum_(t>r)Lambda_st)-E_sr
=H_r(mu_s+sum_(t<=r)Lambda_st)-E_sr.
The norm terms contribute -Lambda_rs-Lambda_sr. Their sum is(15).

Let Z_blk be the m by m matrix with diagonal D_r^blk and off-diagonal
K_rs^blk/2, and let mu_blk=(mu_0,...,mu_(m-1))^T. Necessarily

 Z_blk>=0, mu_blk in Range(Z_blk),
 q_cert >= (1/4)mu_blk^T Z_blk^+ mu_blk.                       (16)

This follows from the same elementary square completion proved for(8).
It is EXACT for the chosen restricted subspace, hence only necessary for
the full certificate unless every block is a singleton.

For a concrete TWO-CUT statement take B_0={0,...,k-1},
B_1={k,...,l-1}, B_2={l,...,n}, where1<=k<l<=n. Then

 D_0^blk=sum_(a!=0)(Lambda_a0+E_a0)-H_0(Lambda_01+Lambda_02),
 D_1^blk=sum_(a!=1)(Lambda_a1+E_a1)-H_1 Lambda_12,
 D_2^blk=1+2H_2+sum_(a!=2)(Lambda_a2+E_a2),
 K_01^blk=H_0(mu_1+Lambda_10)-H_1 Lambda_02
                              -Lambda_01-Lambda_10-E_01-E_10,
 K_02^blk=H_0(mu_2+Lambda_20)-Lambda_02-Lambda_20-E_02-E_20,
 K_12^blk=H_1(mu_2+Lambda_20+Lambda_21)
                              -Lambda_12-Lambda_21-E_12-E_21. (17)

The diagonal sums include star. Define
d_r=D_r^blk-mu_r^2/(4q_cert) and
c_rs=K_rs^blk/2-mu_r*mu_s/(4q_cert).
Full PSD implies all d_r>=0, c_rs^2<=d_r*d_s, and the additional
coupled two-cut condition

 d_0 d_1 d_2+2c_01 c_02 c_12
              -d_0 c_12^2-d_1 c_02^2-d_2 c_01^2>=0.          (18)

Conversely these principal-minor conditions make the restricted3 by3
Schur matrix PSD. To justify the singular cases without a theorem black
box: if some d_r=0, its two pair tests force both adjacent c entries0
and the remaining2 by2 criterion suffices. If all d_r>0, eliminate the
first diagonal; the remaining2 by2 matrix has nonnegative diagonal from
the pair tests and determinant det(original)/d_0>=0. Square completion
then proves PSD. Thus(18) retains the simultaneous two-cut correlation,
including degenerate kernels, rather than checking two separate cuts.

As a normalization check, the ONE-BLOCK case of(14) has S=sum h_i,
nu_i=lambda_(star,i), nu=sum_i nu_i, mu=2+nu, and

 D=1+2S+sum_i(1+sum_(t<i)h_t)nu_i
                  <=1+2S+(1+S)nu.

Consequently q_cert>=mu^2/(4D)>=1/(1+2S). The last inequality is exactly

 (1+2S)(2+nu)^2-4(1+2S+(1+S)nu)
                      =(1+2S)nu^2+4S nu>=0.

This recovers the familiar Huber bound without incorrectly suppressing
optimum-source edges at q_cert>Huber. The empty horizon is m=1,H_0=0.

## 5. What does and does not close under another cut

There IS an exact matrix update with explicitly retained boundary data.
Merge neighboring blocks r,s=r+1 into B. For an outside source block a,

 H_B=H_r+H_s, mu_B=mu_r+mu_s,
 Lambda_aB=Lambda_ar+Lambda_as,
 E_aB=E_ar+E_as+H_r Lambda_as,
 Lambda_Ba=Lambda_ra+Lambda_sa,
 E_Ba=E_ra+E_sa.                                              (19)

The formulas for a=star use the same target moment. They follow by
shifting every target in B_s by H_r in its new local elapsed coordinate.
Algebraically merging means setting u_r=u_s in(13), so
D_B^blk=D_r^blk+D_s^blk+K_rs^blk and
K_Ba^blk=K_ra^blk+K_sa^blk, with symmetric interpretation of K.
The matrix is a congruence of the finer matrix. A further split requires
the actual finer Lambda and E data; it cannot be recovered from(19) by
knowing only aggregate totals. Conditions become no weaker under refinement
because the tested formal subspace increases.

One may instead eliminate a block variable by minimizing(13). If D_r^blk>0,
the exact Schur update on the other blocks is

 q_new=q_cert-mu_r^2/(4D_r^blk),
 mu_s,new=mu_s-mu_r K_rs^blk/(2D_r^blk),
 D_s,new=D_s^blk-(K_rs^blk)^2/(4D_r^blk),
 K_st,new=K_st^blk-K_rs^blk K_rt^blk/(2D_r^blk).               (20)

If D_r^blk=0, PSD requires mu_r=0 and every K_rs^blk=0, so this is a
zero row and can be removed without division. These claims follow by
completing D_r^blk||u_r-[mu_r z-sum_(s!=r)K_rs^blk u_s]/(2D_r^blk)||^2.
They preserve PSD as matrix statements. They need not preserve nonnegative
optimum flow or the normalized full-objective certificate class.

Here is an exact supplied FAMILY showing that failure. For any b_long>2,
take n=1,h_0=b_long,

 q_cert=b_long^2-2b_long+2,
 lambda_(0,star)=lambda_(star,0)=2b_long^2,
 lambda_(1,star)=2,

and every other coefficient0. The flows are0,2 and every coefficient is
nonnegative. Its complete full-space identity is

 M=2b_long^2||g_0-x_0/2+g_1/(2b_long)||^2
                              +(1/2)||g_1+(b_long-2)x_0||^2. (21)

Expanding gives q_cert||x_0||^2-2b_long^2<x_0,g_0>-2<x_0,g_1>
+2b_long^2||g_0||^2+2b_long<g_0,g_1>+||g_1||^2, which is exactly(1)
for the stated multipliers. Thus there is no feasibility or duality
assumption hidden in this example. Eliminating g_0 yields the last square
in(21), whose effective optimum coefficient is

 mu_1,new=2-b_long<0.                                         (22)

In a genuine full certificate on the remaining vectors, the coefficient
of -<x_0,g_1> must be the nonnegative actual lambda_(1,star).
Thus this Schur elimination does NOT close in that cone. It also changes
the initial-distance coefficient to (b_long-2)^2/2. A purported exact
constant-preserving step cannot discard these changes. The example refutes
automatic direct Schur heredity, not the possibility of another nonnegative
re-selection at the same original q_cert.

The interval state (H,Lambda,E,mu,Z_blk) therefore closes algebraically
under coarsening or refinement WHEN the actual finer data are retained.
It is not a fixed-dimensional scalar capacity state. At singleton blocks
ell_r=0, the substitution is the identity on all original gradients; then
(16), together with nonnegative multipliers and flow, is exactly the
original full-certificate feasibility problem. Merely refining all the way
to that matrix is a change of coordinates, not a solution of the profile.

## 6. Precise implication for W and the remaining obstacle

For a fixed partition, or a chosen collection of partitions, define L_test(h)
as the infimum of q>0 over all finite nonnegative arrays with the original
flow(2) that pass the corresponding exact restricted matrices. Every true
full certificate is feasible for that relaxation. In particular the attained
certificate at q=W_n(h), supplied by accepted1252b8823bb5a290 including
all zero steps, is feasible. Therefore

                         W_n(h)>=L_test(h).                  (23)

This direction is justified by that explicit accepted attainment theorem,
not by an unspecified conic strong-duality slogan. No attainment of the
relaxed infimum is asserted or needed. A lower bound on q for just one
selected array would not prove(23) with that particular array's value.

To prove the affirmative target using these tests one must still establish,
for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large n, uniformly in h>=0,
that their feasible flow/moment states cost at least(1-epsilon)/B_n.
Neither(6), (18), nor(19) proves that estimate. A bounded-state separator
dominated by the exact primitive/dominant F/G recursions has not been found.
Dropping moments is disproved by(10); direct Schur cone closure is disproved
by(21). Retaining the entire singleton state leaves a theorem equivalent to
the original minimax comparison. That closure route is BLOCKED, not routine.

Deliverable of this round: a quantitative single queried-cut necessity,
an explicit simultaneous two-cut determinant with all actual moments,
their exact singular/zero-step rules, and two scoped supplied-certificate
obstructions to unjustified scalar closure. The all-horizon target remains
unresolved; no new accepted fact or actual asymptotic match is claimed.

glossary.ell_tail(k): Step mass elapsed inside T_cut before target index k.
glossary.C_in: Actual interpolation multiplier mass entering T_cut from its complement, including optimum source.

glossary.B_cut: Actual backward multiplier mass from T_cut into selected query j.
glossary.I_cut: Total actual incoming multiplier mass at queried node j.
glossary.J_forward: Forward multiplier mass from j into T_cut weighted by target elapsed step mass.
glossary.J_in: All multiplier mass entering T_cut weighted by target elapsed step mass.

glossary.K_cut: b_cut C_out-F_cut-B_cut-J_forward, the selected-query/tail cross coefficient.

# Quantitative queried cuts of full objective certificates

Status: complete self-contained candidate calculations, NOT verifier-accepted.
Current TASK/master_guidance closes routine verification and numerical search;
neither a solver nor fact_submit is used. Every new calculation below belongs
to this single proof package, not to a chain of unverified premises. The only
accepted mathematical dependency is fact `1252b8823bb5a290`, for the exact
normalized problem, interpolation necessity, and attained full certificates.

## 1. The unchanged target and the full certificate hypothesis

For a finite nonnegative schedule h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), W_n(h) is the
supremum of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over every finite
dimension, convex differentiable f with L-Lipschitz gradient and a minimizer
x_star, and x_0 != x_star, using x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L) grad f(x_i).
The exact benchmark is U_n^ZJ=1/B_n, B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1, with the original
phi/psi recursions in accepted fact `b98bb807d514e80d`. The affirmative
target remains: for every epsilon>0, all sufficiently large n and EVERY
nonnegative length-n schedule have W_n(h)>=(1-epsilon)/B_n. A negative
answer requires a fixed positive relative improvement along unbounded
horizons by actual full-objective upper bounds. Neither outcome is claimed.

Work at smoothness one and let x_0,g_0,...,g_n be independent formal vectors.
Set x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. All finite f_i
are independent formal scalars. Put I={star,0,...,n}, lambda_ii=0, and

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

A supplied full certificate consists of a finite real q_cert and ACTUAL
lambda_ij>=0 for which

 M=q_cert||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij                 (1)

has every value coefficient zero and is PSD on the full original formal
space. In particular the finite-node flows obey

 out_i-in_i=2*1_(i=n).                                         (2)

No optimum-source edge is forbidden. No support, symmetrizability,
positive-definiteness, h_i<2, or Huber equality assumption is made.
Zero-step gradients remain independent.

Necessity of Q_ij<=0 on legal instances (accepted1252b8823bb5a290) gives
W_n(h)<=q_cert for any such certificate. Conversely, that SAME accepted
fact supplies a full certificate at q_cert=W_n(h) for every nonnegative
h, including empty/all-zero schedules, by positive-step attainment and
explicit zero-step lifting. Thus any universal necessary inequality proved
below can be applied to at least one attained certificate at the actual W.
An inequality involving the multipliers of a particular supplied certificate
is not by itself a multiplier-free lower bound on W.

Every feasible q_cert is positive. Setting all gradients to zero first
gives q_cert>=0. Summing (2) yields
sum_i lambda_(i,star)=2+sum_i lambda_(star,i)>=2. If q_cert=0, set all
finite gradients to the same scalar1. The coefficient of scalar x_0 in
M is then -sum_i lambda_(i,star)<0, so M is unbounded below. This excludes0.

## 2. A nontrivial queried-cut capacity inequality

Fix a queried index j<n, write b_cut=h_j, and let T_cut={j+1,...,n}.
Its complement in I includes the optimum and indices0,...,j. Define

 s_tail=sum_(j<t<n)h_t,
 ell_tail(k)=sum_(j<t<k)h_t for k in T_cut,
 C_in=sum_(i outside T_cut,k in T_cut)lambda_ik,
 C_out=sum_(i in T_cut,k outside T_cut)lambda_ik,
 F_cut=sum_(k in T_cut)lambda_(j,k),
 B_cut=sum_(k in T_cut)lambda_(k,j),
 I_cut=sum_(i!=j)lambda_(i,j),
 J_forward=sum_(k in T_cut)ell_tail(k) lambda_(j,k),
 J_in=sum_(i outside T_cut,k in T_cut)ell_tail(k) lambda_ik,
 mu_query=lambda_(j,star),
 mu_tail=sum_(i in T_cut)lambda_(i,star).

These are actual array sums, including every remote edge and optimum edge.
Summing (2) over T_cut gives C_out-C_in=2. Set

 A_cut=I_cut-b_cut F_cut,
 D_cut=1+2s_tail+C_in+J_in,
 K_cut=b_cut C_out-F_cut-B_cut-J_forward.                       (3)

The following matrix is necessarily PSD:

              [ q_cert       -mu_query/2       -mu_tail/2 ]
 T_query   =  [ -mu_query/2    A_cut             K_cut/2   ].    (4)
              [ -mu_tail/2    K_cut/2            D_cut     ]

Proof. Evaluate (1) on the formal subspace

 x_0=z,  g_i=0 (i<j),  g_j=u,  g_i=v (i>j).

All value coefficients have already canceled, so they may be set to0.
Only finite-source edges to star contribute z; their total is
-<z,mu_query*u+mu_tail*v>. The coefficient of ||u||^2 in the norm
terms is (out_j+in_j)/2=I_cut, since j<n. The only additional diagonal
terms are -h_j lambda_(j,k)||u||^2 for k>j. This gives A_cut.

For the ||v||^2 coefficient, set u=z=0. A tail point k then has
x_k=-ell_tail(k)v, and a non-tail finite point has position0. Within-tail
position terms sum to

 sum_(k in T_cut)ell_tail(k)(out_k^internal-in_k^internal).

Use (2) to replace the internal divergence by
2*1_(k=n)-out_k^cross+in_k^cross. The outgoing cross position terms
add back sum_k ell_tail(k)out_k^cross. This leaves
2s_tail+J_in. The cross norm terms are
(C_out+C_in)/2=1+C_in; internal norm terms are zero. Hence D_cut.

For the coefficient of <u,v>, norm terms give -(F_cut+B_cut).
An edge j->k with k in T_cut contributes -ell_tail(k)<u,v>, totaling
-J_forward. An edge sourced in T_cut and targeting its complement
has the position shift +b_cut*u, totaling b_cut C_out<u,v>.
All other position terms have either zero source gradient or cancel
the common tail shift. These are exactly K_cut. Thus the restriction is

 q_cert||z||^2-<z,mu_query*u+mu_tail*v>
                   +A_cut||u||^2+K_cut<u,v>+D_cut||v||^2,

whose scalar coefficient matrix is (4). Since the original polynomial
is PSD on every formal vector, its restriction is PSD. This restriction
is a necessary test, not an assertion that its formal vectors are legal
trajectories, and it deletes no edge from the original certificate.

Complete the independent z square, using q_cert>0. Put

 a_cut=A_cut-mu_query^2/(4q_cert),
 d_cut=D_cut-mu_tail^2/(4q_cert),
 k_cut=K_cut-mu_query*mu_tail/(2q_cert).

Then (4) is equivalent to

 a_cut>=0, d_cut>=0, k_cut^2<=4a_cut*d_cut.                     (5)

In particular, when d_cut>0 the quantitative incidence cost is

 I_cut >= b_cut F_cut + mu_query^2/(4q_cert)
              + [b_cut C_out-F_cut-B_cut-J_forward
                       -mu_query*mu_tail/(2q_cert)]^2/(4d_cut). (6)

When d_cut=0 the square numerator in (6) must be zero and the remaining
condition is I_cut>=b_cut F_cut+mu_query^2/(4q_cert). There is no division
by a vanished residual and no strict-PSD assumption. Equivalently,

 |b_cut C_out-F_cut-B_cut-J_forward
                     -mu_query*mu_tail/(2q_cert)|
       <=2 sqrt((I_cut-b_cut F_cut-mu_query^2/(4q_cert))
                 *(1+2s_tail+C_in+J_in-mu_tail^2/(4q_cert))).   (7)

If every edge incident to j vanishes, I_cut=F_cut=B_cut=J_forward=
mu_query=0. Then (5) forces b_cut C_out=0. Since C_out>=2, b_cut=0.
This recovers the qualitative incidence obstruction, now as the zero-cost
case of an exact quantitative condition at every finite certificate level.
If b_cut=0 there is no contradiction; the zero-step case is included.

For an alternative exact q cost define

 Z_cut=[ A_cut K_cut/2 ; K_cut/2 D_cut ],
 m_cut=(mu_query,mu_tail)^T.

Condition (4) is equivalent to Z_cut>=0, m_cut in Range(Z_cut), and

 q_cert >= (1/4) m_cut^T Z_cut^+ m_cut.                         (8)

Here Z_cut^+ inverts its positive eigenvalues and vanishes on its kernel.
For proof, diagonalize the real symmetric Z_cut. A component of m_cut
on a zero eigenvector would give an unbounded linear polynomial in that
free direction. Once these components vanish, complete one square for
each positive eigenvalue. This proves necessity and sufficiency, including
all singular cases. If 4A_cut D_cut-K_cut^2>0, the right side is explicitly

 (D_cut*mu_query^2-K_cut*mu_query*mu_tail+A_cut*mu_tail^2)
                         /(4A_cut D_cut-K_cut^2).             (9)

## 3. Why total cut flow cannot replace its position moment

Here is ONE exact supplied certificate. Take n=2, h=(1,1), q_cert=1/5,
with the following nonzero multipliers and every other multiplier zero:

 lambda_02=1, lambda_10=1, lambda_21=2,
 lambda_(1,star)=1, lambda_(2,star)=1.                          (10)

All coefficients are nonnegative. The finite flows are respectively0,0,2.
With x_1=x_0-g_0 and x_2=x_0-g_0-g_1, direct expansion of (1) gives

 M=(1/5)||x_0-(5/2)(g_1+g_2)||^2
                                      +(3/4)||g_1-g_2||^2.   (11)

For an explicit coefficient check, the sum of the position terms in (10)
is -<x_0,g_1+g_2>-||g_0||^2+<g_0,g_1>+<g_0,g_2>
+3<g_1,g_2>. The norm terms add ||g_0||^2+2||g_1||^2+2||g_2||^2
-<g_0,g_1>-<g_0,g_2>-2<g_1,g_2>. Their sum is exactly the expansion
of (11) after adding q_cert||x_0||^2. This is full PSD with the
original independent g_0 present as a kernel direction.

For j=0, T_cut={1,2}, the exact data are

 b_cut=1, s_tail=1, C_in=1, C_out=3,
 F_cut=B_cut=I_cut=1, J_forward=J_in=1,
 mu_query=0, mu_tail=2,
 A_cut=0, D_cut=5, K_cut=0.

Thus (4) is the singular rank-one square (z-5v)^2/5, and (8) gives
the exact cost1/5. Dropping the target-position moment J_in would assert

 mu_tail^2 <= 4q_cert(1+2s_tail+C_in),                          (12)

which here reads4<=16/5, false. Equivalently, that proposed scalar cost
would falsely require q_cert>=1/4. Dropping J_forward from K_cut likewise
produces K_cut=1 while A_cut=0, falsely rejecting the same full certificate.
Therefore unweighted cross-cut flow cannot be substituted in these exact
capacity tests. The actual remote edge0->2, whose target lies one unit
of step mass into the tail, supplies the missing moment. This refutes
(12), not every conceivable scalar invariant or an existential re-selection.


## 7. The correct mass-only relaxation, with its explicit loss

One CAN remove the actual first moments at a single cut if their loss is
paid explicitly. Nonnegative h and lambda imply

 0<=J_forward<=s_tail F_cut,
 0<=J_in-J_forward<=s_tail(C_in-F_cut).

In particular the valid scalar tail bound is

 q_cert>=mu_tail^2/[4(1+2s_tail+(1+s_tail)C_in)].               (24)

Proof: in(4), the z,v principal minor gives mu_tail^2<=4q_cert D_cut,
and D_cut<=1+2s_tail+(1+s_tail)C_in. The supplied certificate(10) has
equality in(24). Thus(24), which pays the full possible elapsed mass,
survives that example whereas the unweighted replacement(12) does not.

There is also a closed elimination of the TWO moment bounds from the
coupled query test. Write a=a_cut from(5) only within this paragraph, and
define the scalar data

 R_mom=b_cut C_out-F_cut-B_cut-mu_query*mu_tail/(2q_cert),
 E_mom=1+2s_tail+C_in+s_tail(C_in-F_cut)-mu_tail^2/(4q_cert),
 U_mom=s_tail F_cut.

Every true certificate necessarily satisfies

 a>=0, E_mom+R_mom+a>=0,
 dist(R_mom+2a,[0,U_mom])^2<=4a(E_mom+R_mom+a).              (25)

Here dist denotes the ordinary distance of a real number from the stated
closed interval. For proof put t=J_forward. Then0<=t<=U_mom and
d_cut<=E_mom+t. Equation(5) gives

 (R_mom-t)^2<=4a(E_mom+t), E_mom+t>=0.

Completing the scalar square gives
(t-(R_mom+2a))^2<=4a(E_mom+R_mom+a). For a>0, this is possible
for t in the interval exactly when the last two conditions in(25) hold;
the square inequality itself forces E_mom+t>=0. For a=0 the same
conditions require t=R_mom in[0,U_mom] and E_mom+R_mom>=0, which is
the correct zero-residual rule. This proves(25) including degeneracy.

Conversely(25) is sufficient for the ABSTRACT moment relaxation of(5):
choose such a t and set J_forward=t, J_in=t+s_tail(C_in-F_cut).
These values satisfy the two displayed interval bounds and yield(5).
No claim is made that those abstract moments arise from actual target
indices or a common array across several cuts. It is precisely that
cross-cut realizability/correlation information that(25) relaxes.
The scalar relaxation is therefore a genuine necessary inequality,
not a constant-preserving F/G separator or an exact iterative closure.
