# C55: the prescribed three-boundary queried-pair recurrence is insufficient

Status: **complete scoped proof candidate, not verifier-accepted**. No
optimization or verifier allocation is used. The predecessor
`1252b8823bb5a290` supplies the interpolation convention and the requirement
that an objective certificate be positive semidefinite on all the original
formal vectors. Everything specific to this recursive family is derived
below. Prior C53/C55 findings are motivation, not mathematical premises.

The result covers precisely the H2 seed and the repeated-copy join with the
added balanced pair described below, including arbitrary horizon-dependent
join parameters and storage choices. It does not cover arbitrary seeds,
independent internal array corrections, or unrestricted certificates for the
same schedule. The test vectors are formal vectors, not a legal function.
Section 10 also allows an arbitrary balanced pair inside the seed and both
of the last two queried points at every higher join, with an explicit larger
horizon threshold.

## 1. Statement and notation

Fix an integer m>=128 and define

    epsilon=1/m, lambda=1+sqrt(2),
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c,
    d_j=a c^j,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+d_j,H_j),
    n_j=2^j-1, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

All steps are predetermined and strictly positive; the bridges grow with
the recursion level. No upper bound on the steps is assumed. The claims
below concern this explicit family, not arbitrary nonnegative schedules.

For formal gradients substitute the actual GD recursion with smoothness
one and optimum jet zero. For distinct samples define

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    C_ij=-2 Q_ji
        =2(f_i-f_j)+2<g_j,x_j-x_i>-||g_i-g_j||^2.

The accepted predecessor proves C_ij>=0 for legal smooth convex data.
Formal vectors used to test a quadratic certificate need not be legal.

An array at level j has storage parameters u_j,v_j and star pattern

    lambda_(star,i)=h_i              (i<n_j),
    lambda_(star,n_j)=u_j,
    lambda_(i,star)=0                (i<n_j),
    lambda_(n_j,star)=s_j=S_j+u_j-v_j.                 (1)

Here lambda_ik denotes a multiplier array on C_ik; the scalar lambda without
indices denotes 1+sqrt(2). The full identity defines its remainder E_j:

    ||x_start||^2-||x_end-u_j g_end||^2-2v_j f_end
                   =sum lambda_ik C_ik+E_j,
    Z_j=(u_j-1)^2+v_j,
    z_j=sum_(i<n_j) h_i g_i+g_end.                    (2)

Start from the exact H2 seed in Section 2, and for j=2,...,m-1 apply any
join in Section 3, with a balanced multiplier gamma_j>=0 on the queried
pair (p,q-1). The same child array is embedded on the left and multiplied
by r_j>=0 on the right. All actual final multipliers must be nonnegative
to give a certificate. One may use any real u_j,v_j, with v_m>0, and need
not require positive semidefinite child or local remainders.

Then, if the complete objective matrix at level q_cert is PSD, necessarily

    q_cert >= 1/k_m^2
           > (2/5)^(2m) exp[2^(m-3)/m],              (3)

where the signed numbers k_j are defined in Section 5. The last expression
tends to infinity. In particular q_cert>1 for m>=128, so this family cannot
supply v_m>=M_m with E_m PSD, nor any useful bounded objective coefficient.
This is an obstruction for the enlarged C55 recurrence, not an upper or
lower bound on the actual schedule's worst-case objective.

The proof retains every internal child square and every new pair term. Its
key change from C53 is that the last-query gradient is c times the terminal
gradient, instead of equal to it.

## 2. The exact seed, its signs, and its attained boundary form

Put

    b0=1+a, M=M_1=2+a, d=d_1=1-epsilon,
    x=d/M, eta=x^2+2x-1, a0=(2-b0^2)/b0^2.

The one-step seed H1=(b0) has finite multipliers

    lambda_01=M, lambda_10=1,

star multipliers lambda_(star,0)=b0, lambda_(star,1)=M, and no incoming
star multipliers. Set u_1=M, v_1=2M-1, hence Z_1=M^2. Direct expansion in
(2) gives

    E_1=(2-b0^2)||g_0-g_1||^2.

To obtain H2, use the join of Section 3 with gamma=0 and

    A=1/x, B=2+x, r=3+x+1/x, t=1/x-2-x,
    P=(1+M eta)/x, Q=M,
    u_2=M_2=2M+d, v_2=2M_2-1.                        (4)

Here 1<b0<sqrt(2), 3/8<x<sqrt(2)-1, and eta<0. For the upper bound on x,
with s=sqrt(2)-1=1/lambda, expansion gives

    d-sM=-epsilon[1-2s^2/(1+epsilon)]<0.

The lower bound follows from d>=127/128 and M<5/2. Thus a0,t>0.
Moreover eta>=-7/64, so 1+M eta>1-35/128>0. Consequently A,B,P,Q,r are
positive. The physical star pattern has s_1=s_2=0, and the update described
in Section 3 yields nonnegative actual star multipliers as well.

For the four gradients of H2 define

    U=b0(g_0-g_1), V0=b0(g_2-g_3), D0=g_1-g_3.

Expanding the complete join gives

    E_2=a0||U||^2+(r a0+t)||V0||^2
                         +M^2(-eta)||D0||^2.          (5)

For an explicit coefficient check, (4) gives H=-t(M+d), ell=-tM in (8)
below. Substitute V=d g_1+b0 g_2+g_3, Z_1=M^2, Z_2=(2M+d)^2 into (8).
The mixed V0,D0 coefficient is A d-M=0; the D0 square coefficient is
M^2(1-2x-x^2). The two seed remainders provide a0||U||^2+r a0||V0||^2.
The remaining term is t||V0||^2, establishing (5).

Changing u_2,v_2 and only the two terminal star coefficients in (1) adds
(M_2^2-Z_2)||g_3||^2 to (5). Thus the obstruction also permits these
storage changes at the seed. The finite seed coefficients remain fixed.

With (z,e,w)=(z_2,g_3,g_2), the boundary relation is

    z-M_2 e=U+V0+(M+d)D0.

All three boundary vectors are independent. Set c0=M^2(-eta), l0=M+d.
The exact identity

    a0||U||^2+c0||D0||^2
      =a0 c0/(c0+a0 l0^2) ||U+l0 D0||^2
           +||a0 l0 U-c0 D0||^2/(c0+a0 l0^2)

has its second square equal to zero for every prescribed value of
U+l0 D0. Therefore the sharp, attained boundary form is

    K_2(z,e,w)=A2||z-M_2 e-b0(w-e)||^2
                         +B2||w-e||^2
                         +(M_2^2-Z_2)||e||^2,
    A2=[1/a0+(1+x)^2/(-eta)]^(-1),
    B2=(r a0+t)b0^2.                                 (6)

No unattainability of boundary minimizers is assumed in what follows.

## 3. The actual enlarged array and the full local identity

At a join write n=n_j, p=n, q=2n+1, S=S_j, M=M_j, d=d_j, b=1+d.
Choose A,B,P,Q with

    r=1+A+B, P-Q=b+(1-A)S.

Embed the old array on the left and r times that array on the right.
For each right queried index p<i<q add

    A h_i to (p,i), B h_i to (q,i),
    -(A+B)h_i to (star,i).

Add the six corrections

    (p,q):P, (q,p):Q,
    (p,star):-s_j, (q,star):s_(j+1)-r s_j,
    (star,p):b-u_j, (star,q):u_(j+1)-r u_j.            (7)

Finally add gamma>=0 to both (p,q-1) and (q-1,p). These are actual queried
samples. This balanced change preserves every function-value flow and
every star multiplier. It adds no incoming unqueried-terminal constraint.

For example A,B,P,Q>=0, u_j>=0 and s_j>=0 at the relevant levels suffice
for nonnegative actual arrays when the seed is nonnegative: right queried
star coefficients become (r-A-B)h_i=h_i; the two terminal star coefficients
become b and u_(j+1); the two incoming terminal star coefficients become
zero and s_(j+1). All other entries are copied or receive nonnegative
additions. The obstruction allows all real A,B,P,Q satisfying the flow
identity and r>=0, so it also covers choices whose signs are certified by
a more detailed inspection of the actual array.

Write g=g_p, e=g_q, w=g_(q-1), and define

    t=A-B,
    H=M+d-B(M-d)-tM,
    ell=P-A,
    V=x_p-x_q-g+e=d g+z_right.

The complete remainder identity is

    E_next=E_left+r E_right
       +t||V||^2+2<V,(H-ell)g+ell e>
       +(Z_j-rd^2)||g||^2+(rZ_j-Z_next)||e||^2
       +2gamma<g-w,e+a w-V>.                          (8)

Here a is the fixed parameter in b0=1+a, since every block ends with that
same step b0. To verify the new term, x_(q-1)=x_q+b0 w gives

    -gamma(C_(p,q-1)+C_(q-1,p))
       =2gamma[||g-w||^2-<g-w,x_p-x_(q-1)>]
       =2gamma<g-w,e+a w-V>.

For completeness the old part of (8) can be checked before the pair is
added. Put D=x_p-x_q and W=sum_(p<i<q)h_i g_i=x_p-b g-x_q. The rank
correction sums to

    2AS f_p+2BS f_q-AS||g||^2-BS||e||^2
                      -2<W,A(x_p-g)+B(x_q-e)>.

The value coefficient at p becomes

    -2v_j+2AS+2(P-Q)-2s_j-2(b-u_j)
            =2[(A-1)S+P-Q-b]=0.

The value coefficient at q becomes -2v_next using r=1+A+B and (1).
After subtracting the correction from the new potential minus the two
child potentials, the quadratic coefficients are

    D^2:t, (D,g):H-ell-t, (D,e):ell+t,
    g^2:Z_j-rd^2+t-2H+2ell,
    e^2:rZ_j-Z_next+t+2ell, (g,e):H-2ell-t,

where a mixed coefficient multiplies twice the indicated inner product.
Substituting V=D-g+e proves the old part of (8). Thus (8) is an identity
on the full formal space, with every inherited remainder retained.

## 4. Explicit eliminated matrix and every singular range condition

This section records the exact recurrence being obstructed, including
its singular cases. Write an attained child boundary form as

    K(z,e,w)=alpha||z||^2+2beta<z,e>+2chi<z,w>
                        +delta||e||^2+2etaK<e,w>+phi||w||^2.

In (8) substitute E_left=K(L,g,u)+its internal remainder and
E_right=K(R,e,w)+its internal remainder. The six-variable form has
parent boundary z=L+d g+R. Eliminate X=(g,u,R) and retain Y=(z,e,w).
After L=z-d g-R, its symmetric matrix is

                         [ D_el  B_el ]
                         [ B_el^T C_el].

Its entries are exactly

    D_el(1,1)=(alpha+t-r)d^2-2beta d+delta
                                      +2d(H-ell-gamma)+Z_j,
    D_el(1,2)=etaK-d chi,
    D_el(1,3)=d(alpha+t)-beta+H-ell-gamma,
    D_el(2,2)=phi,
    D_el(2,3)=-chi,
    D_el(3,3)=(1+r)alpha+t;

    B_el=[ -d alpha+beta,  d ell+gamma, gamma(a+d);
                 chi,          0,              0;
               -alpha,     r beta+ell,       r chi+gamma ];

    C_el=[ alpha,          0,                    0;
              0, r delta+rZ_j-Z_next,  r etaK-gamma;
              0,       r etaK-gamma,    r phi-2a gamma ].  (9)

The full six-variable matrix is PSD if and only if all of the following
hold:

    D_el is PSD;
    B_el^T xi=0 for EVERY xi in ker(D_el);
    C_el-B_el^T D_el^dagger B_el is PSD.                (10)

The middle condition is equivalently that every column of B_el belongs to
the range of D_el. The dagger is the inverse on its positive eigenspaces
and zero on its kernel. To prove (10), first restrict to Y=0. A nonzero
cross coefficient against a null vector of D_el makes the form unbounded
below by scaling that null direction. Once these coefficients vanish,
complete the square on the positive eigenspaces. This proves both
necessity and sufficiency, including every rank of D_el.

When the children have exact attained decompositions with PSD internal
remainders and r>=0, (10) is also equivalent to PSD of the entire parent
remainder: the independent boundary data can be lifted while setting all
internal child squares to zero. The new sharp boundary form is the last
Schur complement in (10). No such interpretation is needed for the
obstruction below: it directly evaluates the original E_j and does not
assume that any earlier elimination passed.

## 5. A different formal seed survives every new queried pair

Define

    k_2=M_2+6epsilon, theta=c.

At the H2 seed choose the following explicit four gradients, all multiples
of an arbitrary vector e:

    g_0=(2-c+6epsilon/b0)e,
    g_1=e, g_2=c e, g_3=e.                            (11)

Then the exact boundary is

    z_2=k_2 e, g_end=e, g_last_query=c e.

Indeed z_2=b0 g_0+(1+d_1)g_1+b0 g_2+g_3=(M_2+6epsilon)e.
In (5), D0=0, V0=b0(c-1)e, and U=[6epsilon-b0(c-1)]e.
We next prove the strict energy inequality

    E_2 < (k_2^2-Z_2)||e||^2                         (12)

for e!=0, for every m>=128. This includes all internal seed squares.

First, a>2/5. In fact sqrt(2)<10/7 gives lambda<17/7, so

    a >= (127/129)(7/17)=889/2193 >2/5.

Also a<s=sqrt(2)-1, b0<sqrt(2), M>12/5 and c<5/2. To bound a0, use

    b0=sqrt(2)-2s epsilon/(1+epsilon),
    2-b0^2<4sqrt(2)s epsilon=4(2-sqrt(2))epsilon
                                          <(12/5)epsilon,
    b0^2>49/25.

Therefore a0<(60/49)epsilon<(5/4)epsilon. Since 3/8<x<s<1/2,

    r=3+x+1/x<37/6<25/4.

Furthermore

    s-x=epsilon[1-2s^2/(1+epsilon)]/M<(5/12)epsilon,
    t=(s-x)(1+1/(sx))<(5/12)(23/3)epsilon<4epsilon.

The estimate on 1/(sx) uses s>2/5 and x>3/8. We have
0<6epsilon<b0(c-1), because 6epsilon<=3/64 and b0,c-1>7/5. Hence

    ||U||^2 <= b0^2(c-1)^2||e||^2,
    b0^2(c-1)^2<2(3/2)^2=9/2.

Substitution into the FULL seed formula (5) gives

    E_2-(M_2^2-Z_2)||e||^2
       <=[(r+1)a0+t] b0^2(c-1)^2||e||^2
       <[(29/4)(5/4)+4](9/2)epsilon||e||^2
       =(1881/32)epsilon||e||^2
       <60epsilon||e||^2.

Finally M_2=5-epsilon+2a>5, so

    k_2^2-M_2^2=12M_2 epsilon+36epsilon^2>60epsilon.

This proves (12). In particular the argument has not replaced the full
seed by an unattainable boundary minimum or dropped a positive square.

## 6. A uniform subcritical gap and its exact propagation

Set

    R0=k_2/(c d_2)=(M_2+6epsilon)/[(1-epsilon)c^2].

We have the explicit bound

    0<R0<1-epsilon/4.                                (13)

For its proof expand the available gap using lambda^2=2lambda+1:

    (c d_2-M_2)/epsilon
      =[6sqrt(2)+epsilon-2lambda^2 epsilon^2
                                  -lambda^2 epsilon^3]/(1+epsilon).

This is greater than 8. Indeed after subtracting 8 and multiplying by
1+epsilon, the numerator is

    6sqrt(2)-8-7epsilon-2lambda^2 epsilon^2-lambda^2 epsilon^3
      >2/5-7/128-12/128^2-6/128^3>0.

Consequently c d_2-k_2>2epsilon. Since c d_2=(1-epsilon)c^2<25/4,

    1-R0>8epsilon/25>epsilon/4,

as claimed.

Now define signed numbers recursively by

    k_(j+1)=-k_j^2/d_j, j>=2.                         (14)

For every block H_j there is a formal gradient assignment linear in its
terminal vector e such that

    z_j=k_j e, g_end=e, g_last_query=c e,
    E_j <= (k_j^2-Z_j)||e||^2.                        (15)

This holds simultaneously for every permitted choice of the join and
storage parameters, including choices depending on the target horizon.
The seed is (11)-(12). For the induction step put the right child on its
template with terminal e, and the left child on its template with terminal

    g=-k_j e/d_j.

Then V=d_j g+z_right=0, and the parent moment is

    z_next=z_left+d_j g+z_right=k_j g=k_(j+1)e.

Its last-query gradient remains c e. The crucial NEW pair term in (8) is

    2gamma(-k_j/d_j-c)(1+a c)||e||^2.                 (16)

It is nonpositive at every level. At j=2, k_2>0 proves this directly. For
j>=3, k_j<0; solving (14) gives

    |k_j|=(1-epsilon)c^j R0^(2^(j-2)),
    |k_j|/d_j=c R0^(2^(j-2))<c.                     (17)

Thus (16) is negative for gamma>0 and e!=0, since 1+a c=2-epsilon>0.

The other mixed local terms vanish because V=0. Since r>=0, the two
complete child estimates in (15) retain their direction under addition.
Keeping their full values and the nonpositive new pair term gives

    E_next <= (k_j^2-Z_j)||g||^2
                 +r(k_j^2-Z_j)||e||^2
                 +(Z_j-rd_j^2)||g||^2+(rZ_j-Z_next)||e||^2
             = (k_j^4/d_j^2-Z_next)||e||^2,

which is exactly (15) at the parent. No local PSD, nonsingularity, greedy
storage, or rank assumption was used.

In co-coercivity language the pair has

    C_(p,q-1)+C_(q-1,p)
          =2(2-epsilon)(c+k_j/d_j)||e||^2>=0.

This explains why a nonnegative weight on this actual pair cannot repair
this new formal template. The old C53 template had the opposite sign on
some such pairs; those are different formal vectors.

## 7. The original initial-vector objective conversion

Let u=u_m, v=v_m>0, Z=(u-1)^2+v and k=k_m. For the final array the full
objective certificate at any level q_cert is

    M_cert=q_cert||x_0||^2-2f_n
                     +sum_(i!=j) (2lambda_ji/v)Q_ij
           =(q_cert-1/v)||x_0||^2
                     +[||x_n-u g_n||^2+E_m]/v.        (18)

This follows directly from (2) and C_ij=-2Q_ji. In particular E_m PSD
and nonnegative actual multipliers yield the bound q_cert=1/v. The
normalization is the project's 2(f_n-f_star)/(L||x_0-x_star||^2), by the
scaling in predecessor `1252b8823bb5a290`.

Keep x_0 independent of the formal template in (15), and set
beta0=k+u-1. Since z_m=k e,

    x_n-u g_n=x_0-beta0 e.

The restriction of v M_cert is bounded ABOVE by the two-variable form
with matrix

                  [ q_cert v    -beta0       ]
                  [  -beta0    2k beta0-v    ].        (19)

The difference is a nonnegative multiple of ||e||^2, by (15). If the
original M_cert is PSD, this upper matrix must therefore also be PSD.
Its second diagonal is positive: if it were zero, PSD would force
beta0=0, making that diagonal -v<0. Its determinant now implies

    q_cert >= beta0^2/[v(2k beta0-v)] >=1/k^2,

where the last step is exactly

    k^2 beta0^2-v(2k beta0-v)=(v-k beta0)^2>=0.

This includes arbitrary increases of q_cert and indefinite child or final
remainders. It tests the original x_0 variable, not only the condensed
gradient state.

From (13),(17) and 1-x<=exp(-x),

    |k_m|<c^m exp[-2^(m-4)/m].                        (20)

Thus (3) follows from c<5/2. The logarithm of its right side is
2^(m-3)/m-2m log(5/2), which tends to infinity because 2^m/m^2 tends to
infinity. Its successive ratio is 2m^2/(m+1)^2>3/2 for m>=7.
For m>=128, (20) also gives |k_m|<1: log(5/2)<1 follows from
exp(1)>1+1+1/2+1/6>5/2, and 2^(m-4)>m^2 for m>=128. The latter inequality
holds at 128 and is preserved since 2m^2/(m+1)^2>1. Hence q_cert>1.

## 8. Undeformed calibration and scope checks

Set epsilon=0, so a=1/lambda, c=lambda. Then b0=sqrt(2), M_j=lambda^j,
d_j=lambda^(j-1), a0=t=eta=0, and the physical seed E_2 is identically
zero. At each higher join choose

    A=B=lambda, r=lambda^2, t=H=ell=0,
    P=lambda, Q=M_j,
    u_j=(1+sqrt(4M_j^2-3))/2, v_j=u_j, Z_j=M_j^2.

The same storage choice can be made at H2 by its permitted terminal-star
change, preserving E_2=0. It has s_j=S_j>=0. The flow equation follows
from M_j=lambda d_j, and (8) with gamma=0 gives E_next=0. Every actual
multiplier is nonnegative by Section 3. This is an exact valid undeformed
calibration of the full array and the objective conversion (18).

If one retains the physical H2 storage u_2=M_2,v_2=2M_2-1 instead, the
seed still has Z_2=M_2^2; switching to the displayed u_j,v_j at the next
level likewise changes only the two terminal star coefficients and is
allowed. No calibration identity is being carried from a differently
normalized performance measure.

At epsilon=0 the obstruction template has k_2=M_2 and R0=1, so it yields
only q_cert>=lambda^(-2m), entirely compatible with the valid bound
1/u_m of order lambda^(-m). The strict horizon-dependent gap in (13)
is essential.

The hypothesis r>=0 is exactly the scaling restriction in the C55 state
recurrence, not an extra PSD assumption on its children. It is also
forced by nonnegative final arrays in this prescribed construction. The
seed has the positive coefficient lambda_01=M. At every larger level,
the first two queried samples retain this coefficient unchanged, because
they lie in the left child and none of the join corrections touches their
ordered pair. In a right child the corresponding ordered pair has
coefficient rM and is untouched by the parent's fan, sparse, and new-pair
corrections. In the final leftmost occurrence of any such join it remains
untouched by all higher joins. Thus a negative r at any level would leave
a negative actual coefficient in the final array. This also shows that
the proof covers arrays required to be nonnegative only at the final
level. The case r=0 is already included in the energy induction.

The seed restriction matters: the result does not assert that every H2
array has (5), or that every three-boundary seed is covered. A different
seed has to be tested against the seed-energy and last-query conditions
(12),(15). Arbitrary additional queried pairs can change (16); no claim
about those corrections is made here. Likewise the formal template need
not satisfy omitted interpolation constraints, so it is not an actual
lower witness for H_m. Accepted terminal completion removes no queried
prefix constraints and cannot justify dropping them.

An explicit violated pair for (11) is already present in its H2 seed:
g_1=e, g_2=c e and x_1-x_2=(1+d_1)e give

    C_12+C_21=2(1-c)(d_1+c)||e||^2<0.

This directly prevents interpreting the formal template as a legal
adversary, regardless of how function values are assigned. The extra
seed pair on these indices is addressed by a different template next.

This analysis makes no lower-bound claim for schedules with zero steps.
The accepted predecessor handles those schedules without identifying
duplicated formal gradients. Any future unrestricted conclusion would
still have to retain both zero-step and arbitrarily-large-step cases.

All new mathematics in this file remains a proof candidate. The exact
minimax/profile target remains unresolved, and the fact graph is unchanged.

## 9. Reproducibility of the algebraic audit

One fixed rational substitution in the six-variable identity (9) was
checked by polarization of its 21 coefficients, and the four rational
constant margins in Sections 5-6 were checked exactly. These were tiny
arithmetic checks, not optimization or a numerical search. The displayed
expansions and inequalities are the proof; the checks are not premises.

For architecture context, the exact local text of Altschuler--Parrilo,
arXiv:2309.16530, Theorem 3.4 and its helper-lemma proof was reread. No
theorem from that paper is imported; its undeformed recursion motivated
the array, whose modified full identity is proved in Section 3.

## 10. Seed-pair freedom and two trailing queries still do not suffice

This is a uniform enlargement of the SAME joint proof, not an invocation
of its unverified earlier sections as accepted facts. All identities and
the objective conversion needed here have their derivations above.

Take m>=100000. In the H2 seed allow any nonnegative common addition
gamma_seed to lambda_12 and lambda_21. Keep its other finite coefficients
as in Section 2 and permit the same arbitrary terminal-star changes. At
every higher join permit BOTH balanced queried pairs

    (p,q-1), (q-1,p) with common multiplier gamma_1>=0;
    (p,q-2), (q-2,p) with common multiplier gamma_2>=0.  (21)

The two gamma values may be chosen independently at every level and may
depend on m. Keep all other join freedoms in Section 3. This includes
the proposed three-boundary family with a freely reweighted seed pair,
as well as the analogous family that retains the two last query gradients.

Every full PSD objective certificate in this enlarged family satisfies

    q_cert > (2/5)^(2m) exp[2^(m-1)/(625m)] -> infinity. (22)

No bound on the sizes of the nonnegative gamma values is imposed. The
proof does not require PSD of the modified seed or any intermediate child.

### 10.1 Explicit replacement template and its uniform seed estimate

Put sigma=1/100 and define the positive seed moment

    k_2=d_1 c^2-sigma epsilon=c d_2-sigma epsilon.

The new four seed gradients are

    g_0=[k_2-1-c(M+d_1)]e/b0,
    g_1=c e, g_2=c e, g_3=e.                         (23)

They give z_2=k_2 e. In particular BOTH last query gradients equal c e.
Since g_1=g_2, their balanced interpolation sum is identically zero,
including its function-value cancellation. Thus gamma_seed changes
neither the seed energy on (23) nor the following estimates.

Continue writing d=d_1, M=M_1, and put

    Uc=k_2-1-c(M_2-1),
    c0=M^2-2Md-d^2,
    B0=(r a0+t)b0^2+c0,
    F(epsilon)=k_2^2-M_2^2-a0 Uc^2-B0(c-1)^2.        (24)

Formula (5) evaluated on (23) has U=Uc e, V0=b0(c-1)e,
D0=(c-1)e. Therefore F(epsilon)>=0 implies exactly

    E_2 <= (k_2^2-Z_2)||e||^2,

including the complete seed remainder and all seed-pair additions.
We now establish the explicit uniform lower bound

    F(epsilon)>(6/25)epsilon for 0<epsilon<=1/100000.  (25)

All quantities in (24) are smooth functions of epsilon on [0,1/128].
The expression does not divide by a0 or eta, so it is regular at zero.
Write b=sqrt(2) for the next derivative computation only. At epsilon=0,

    M_2=k_2=lambda^2, Uc=-(4+2b), c-1=b,
    a0=t=c0=B0=0,
    a0'=4-2b, t'=16-10b, c0'=6b-4,
    B0'=36-10b,
    k_2'-M_2'=6b-sigma.

Here a=sqrt(2)-1 at zero and a'=-2a there; differentiating the explicit
definitions in (4),(24) gives all the displayed derivatives. In particular

    [a0 Uc^2+B0(c-1)^2]'(0)
       =(4-2b)(4+2b)^2+2(36-10b)=104-4b,
    F(0)=0,
    F'(0)=40b-56-2sigma lambda^2>11/25.              (26)

For the strict rational margin, b>707/500 follows by squaring positive
numbers, and lambda^2<6. Hence 40b-56>14/25 and
2sigma lambda^2<3/25.

For transparency, the following elementary derivative bounds hold
throughout [0,1/128]. The three columns are upper bounds for the absolute
values of the quantity, its first derivative, and its second derivative.

    quantity                  value     first     second
    b0                           3/2       1          2
    M                            5/2       1          2
    d                            1         1          0
    c                            5/2       5/2        0
    M_2                          6         3          4
    k_2                          7        20         40
    a0                           1         4         20
    d/M                          1/2       1          2
    M/d                          3         4         12
    r                            7         5         14
    t                            6         5         14
    b0^2                         3         3          8
    c0                          13        14         22
    r a0+t                      13        38        208
    B0                          52       167       1000
    Uc                          21        40         65
    Uc^2                       441      1680       6000
    (c-1)^2                      3         8         13. (27)

Here are sufficient details to reproduce every derivative bound. We have
2<M<5/2, 127/128<=d<=1, and

    a'=-2(sqrt(2)-1)/(1+epsilon)^2,
    a''=4(sqrt(2)-1)/(1+epsilon)^3,
    a0=2/b0^2-1.

Thus |a'|<1, |a''|<2, |a0'|<4 and |a0''|<20, using b0>1. The quotient
rules give

    (d/M)'=d'/M-dM'/M^2,
    (d/M)''=-2d'M'/M^2-dM''/M^2+2d(M')^2/M^3,
    (M/d)'=M'/d+M/d^2,
    (M/d)''=M''/d+2M'/d^2+2M/d^3.

These yield the corresponding rows of (27); r=3+d/M+M/d and
t=M/d-2-d/M give the next rows. Since c0=M^2-2Md-d^2, its derivative
bounds follow by the product rule: the second derivative is bounded by
2(1+5)+2(2+2)+2=22. The product r a0+t has bounds 13,38,208.
Multiplying it by b0^2 and adding c0 gives bounds

    13*3+13=52,
    38*3+13*3+14=167,
    208*3+2*38*3+13*8+22=978<1000

for B0. For k_2=d c^2-sigma epsilon, direct differentiation gives
|k_2'|<20 and |k_2''|<40. The definitions M_2=5-epsilon+2a and
Uc=k_2-1-c(M_2-1) give

    |Uc|<7+1+(5/2)*5<21,
    |Uc'|<20+(5/2)*5+(5/2)*3=40,
    |Uc''|<40+2*(5/2)*3+(5/2)*4=65.

The last two rows of (27) then follow by differentiating squares.

Using (27) in (24),

    |(a0 Uc^2)''|<20*441+2*4*1680+6000=28260,
    |(B0(c-1)^2)''|<1000*3+2*167*8+52*13=6348,
    |(k_2^2-M_2^2)''|<2*20^2+2*7*40+2*3^2+2*6*4=1426.

Their sum is less than 40000, so |F''|<40000. Integrating the second
derivative twice, with (26), gives

    F(epsilon)>(11/25)epsilon-20000epsilon^2
                    >=(6/25)epsilon

on the claimed interval. This proves (25) without relying on numerical
approximations or an unspecified continuity threshold.

### 10.2 Both pairs have the sign that defeats every nonnegative weight

Start (14) with the new k_2. Its critical ratio satisfies

    0<R0=k_2/(c d_2)=1-sigma epsilon/(d_1 c^2)
                                  <1-epsilon/625,    (28)

because d_1 c^2<25/4 and sigma=1/100. Put the right child on its new
template and the left on the template with terminal g=-k_j e/d_j.
This again gives V=0, z_next=k_(j+1)e, and both trailing query gradients
c e. Equation (17), with this R0, still gives

    -k_j/d_j<=c

at every level: k_2>0, and all later k_j are negative with absolute ratio
|k_j|/d_j=c R0^(2^(j-2))<c.

For the second-last query write w1=g_(q-1), w2=g_(q-2). The last two
physical steps are b0 and 1+d_1. Its exact additional remainder is

    -gamma_2(C_(p,q-2)+C_(q-2,p))
      =2gamma_2<g-w2,e+b0 w1+d_1 w2-V>.              (29)

This follows by substituting
x_(q-2)=x_q+b0 w1+(1+d_1)w2 into the pair identity. On the new template,
the first and second pairs' contributions are respectively

    2gamma_1(-k_j/d_j-c)(1+a c)||e||^2,
    2gamma_2(-k_j/d_j-c)[1+(b0+d_1)c]||e||^2.

Both are nonpositive. The seed pair contributes zero. Retaining all
child remainders in (8),(29) therefore proves (15) with the new k_j,
word for word by the displayed addition in Section 6. This is an actual
full-remainder argument and does not depend on a particular method of
condensing its four boundary vectors.

Finally the original x_0 test (18)-(19), with its proof above, implies
q_cert>=1/k_m^2. From (28),

    |k_m|<c^m exp[-2^(m-2)/(625m)],

which gives (22). The bound on |k_m| is below one for m>=100000: the inequality
2^(m-2)>625m^2 holds at m=128 and is preserved by the increasing ratio
2m^2/(m+1)^2. Combining with log(5/2)<1 proves q_cert>1 in the stated
range.

This enlargement still fixes the non-pair finite coefficients of the H2
seed. It does not close arbitrary H2 seeds or additional independent
interpolation changes. In particular it does not assert an obstruction
for all fixed-size boundary states. It rules out two concrete suggested
repairs with all their weights free, and leaves the unrestricted problem
and the actual schedule distinct.

# Bulk binary interpolation kernels: full-space identities and exact obstructions

Status: self-contained UNVERIFIED candidate, round12. No optimization and no
fact_submit. This is an obstruction to the precisely defined multiplier
organizations below, not a legal hard function or a decision of the project.
Only accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies a mathematical predecessor: its
signed smooth-convex interpolation residual and full-certificate framework.
Every new identity and bound used in this document is proved here jointly.

## 1. Exact operator form on the original formal space

Fix n>=1, N=n+1, h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), and normalize L=1 and the
optimum sample to x_star=g_star=f_star=0. The N+1 vectors
x_0,g_0,...,g_n remain independent. Put

    x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i) h_t g_t,
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

For actual smooth-convex samples Q_ij<=0, by fact1252b8823bb5a290.
Let lambda_ij>=0 denote the coefficient of Q_ij. A full upper certificate
at level q has all finite value coefficients zero and is the PSD form

    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij.       (1)

Define the strictly lower triangular N by N matrix T by
T_it=h_t for t<i and T_it=0 otherwise, and put V=I+T. For a real
matrix B, Sym(B)=(B+B^T)/2. Let e_n be the last coordinate vector
and 1 the vector with every coordinate equal to1.

Here is an exact operator parameterization useful for specifying structured
arrays. Choose an N by N real matrix A satisfying

    A_ij<=0 for i!=j,
    b=A1>=0,
    a=A^T1-2e_n>=0,                                  (2)

where inequalities on vectors are coordinatewise. Set

    lambda_ij=-A_ij  (finite distinct i,j),
    lambda_(i,star)=b_i,  lambda_(star,i)=a_i.          (3)

All actual coefficients are nonnegative. With r_i=sum_(j!=i)lambda_ij,
c_i=sum_(j!=i)lambda_ji, one has A_ii=r_i+b_i and
a_i=r_i+b_i-c_i-2*1_(i=n). Thus the value coefficient at i in (1) is
r_i+b_i-c_i-a_i-2*1_(i=n)=0, including at the terminal.

Expanding every quadratic term in (1) gives the complete matrix

    M(q) = [x_0;g]^T [[q, -b^T/2],[-b/2, G]] [x_0;g],
    G=Sym(A V)-e_n e_n^T.                            (4)

The notation means sums of Euclidean inner products when the formal vectors
have dimension greater than1. To check (4), write K_ij=lambda_ij for i!=j
and K_ii=0. The finite position terms equal
g^T[diag(r)-K]Tg. The star position terms equal
-<x_0,sum b_i g_i>+g^T diag(b)Tg. The squared-gradient terms equal
g^T[diag(r+b)-Sym(K)-e_n e_n^T]g, using the just-checked value flow.
Adding them proves (4). Conversely a finite nonnegative array with the
required value flow gives (2)--(4). This identity alone is a reformulation,
not progress on unrestricted PSD; the restricted cone studied next is
specified independently of that unknown PSD inequality.

## 2. A genuine bulk cone: directed binary-coordinate operators

Take N=2^m, m>=1, n=N-1, and index the finite samples in chronological
binary order. At each bit k choose numbers

    u_k>=0, v_k>=0, 0<=u_k-v_k<=2, kappa_k>=0,
    A_k=[[u_k,-v_k],[-u_k,v_k+2]].                   (5)

The two column sums of A_k are0 and2; its two row sums are
u_k-v_k and2+v_k-u_k, both nonnegative. Embed A_k at bit k with
identity matrices on the other bits. Choose arbitrary delta_i>=0 and put

    A=sum_(k=1)^m kappa_k (I tensor ... tensor A_k tensor ... tensor I)
                   +diag(delta_0,...,delta_n).       (6)

An off-diagonal entry in (6) is nonzero only between indices differing in
one bit. For each setting of the other m-1 bits, the edge0->1 at bit k
has coefficient kappa_k v_k, and the reverse edge has coefficient
kappa_k u_k. This is a scalable bulk organization with m*2^(m-1)
interior cross-block pairs. It is not the endpoint-fan join. The same
two-node factor is used in every context at a given bit; that equality
of contexts is a real restriction.

Let s=sum kappa_k. Then b=A1>=0. At a finite index i with binary bits i_k,

    a_i=2sum_k kappa_k i_k+delta_i-2*1_(i=n).

Consequently (2), hence all actual signs and all value coefficients, hold
if and only if

    t:=2s+delta_n >=2.                              (7)

There is no prohibition on outgoing optimum edges: all these a_i are
retained. The delta_i permit arbitrary additional equal weights on
Q_(i,star) and Q_(star,i). The initial coefficient q is free. Incoming
terminal edges are allowed; no terminal or queried pair is deleted.

## 3. Full one-step calibration

The cone contains a valid one-step seed throughout 0<H<=sqrt(2). Put
M=1+H, take physical step h_0=H, and choose

    A_H=[[2,-2/M],[-2,2+2/M]], delta=0, kappa=1.

Its actual coefficients are

    lambda_01=2/M, lambda_10=2,
    lambda_(0,star)=2H/M, lambda_(1,star)=2/M,
    lambda_(star,0)=lambda_(star,1)=0.

Direct expansion proves

    (1/M)||x_0||^2-2f_1+sum lambda_ij Q_ij
      = [||x_0-Hg_0-g_1||^2
             +(2-H^2)||g_0-g_1||^2+M(M-1)||g_1||^2]/M.       (8)

The value coefficient at0 is2/M-2+2H/M=0, and that at1,
including -2f_1, is2-2/M+2/M-2=0. Expanding the three squares verifies
all gradient and initial-distance coefficients. Every square coefficient
in (8) is nonnegative. In particular H=sqrt(2) gives the full undeformed
Silver seed, and the actual critical h_0=1+a_m also lies in this interval
for m>=128, as checked below. The next obstruction therefore concerns
the proposed tensor extension, rather than an invalid local seed.

## 4. Exact constant lower barrier for the entire cone (5)--(7)

Claim. If h_0=H>=7/5, no array (5)--(7), at ANY depth m, can make the
full matrix (4) PSD with q<=1/8. All remaining steps may be arbitrary
nonnegative numbers. All u_k,v_k,kappa_k and delta_i may depend on the
horizon. The local factors need not be calibrated as in Section3.

Proof. Define the nonnegative numbers

    U=sum kappa_k u_k,
    R=sum kappa_k v_k,
    B=U-R>=0,
    z=B+delta_0>=0,
    t=2sum kappa_k+delta_n>=2.                       (9)

The symbol R in this section is only a scalar coefficient sum, not an
objective or a gradient remainder. At the all-zero binary index0,

    b_0=z,
    G_00=U+delta_0-HR=z-(H-1)R.                    (10)

For (10), every off-diagonal neighbor of index0 is later than0,
T_j0=H at every such neighbor, and the total outgoing coefficient is R.
At the all-one index n,

    b_n=t-B,
    G_nn=t+R-1.                                    (11)

For (11), column n of V has only its diagonal entry1, and
A_nn=sum kappa_k(v_k+2)+delta_n=t+R.

The source condition gives sum b_i-sum a_i=2. If q=0 and the full
matrix were PSD, every entry in its initial row would be zero, hence
b=0, contradicting this condition and a>=0. A negative q also violates
PSD. Thus suppose 0<q<=1/8.

The principal matrix in x_0,g_0 must be PSD. By (10), its determinant
and lower diagonal require

    z^2 <=4q[z-(H-1)R],
    z-(H-1)R>=0.                                   (12)

In particular z<=4q and B<=z<=4q. Rearranging (12) as

    (z-2q)^2+4q(H-1)R<=4q^2

also gives R<=q/(H-1). Since H>=7/5 and q<=1/8,

    B<=1/2,  R<=5/16.                              (13)

The other principal matrix, in x_0,g_n, has positive lower diagonal
t+R-1>=1. By (11), its determinant requires

    q >= (t-B)^2/[4(t+R-1)].                        (14)

Using (13), t>=2, and t+R-1<t gives

    q > (t-1/2)^2/(4t)
       >= (3t/4)^2/(4t)
       =9t/64 >=9/32.

The middle inequality uses t-1/2>=3t/4, which follows from t>=2.
This contradicts q<=1/8, completing the proof. No Schur complement
of an omitted subspace, no Huber equality, and no positivity restricted
to legal transcripts were used: these are necessary principal tests
on the full original formal space.

## 5. Application to undeformed and actual critical words

For undeformed Silver, h_0=sqrt(2)>7/5. Thus the local full PSD seed
(8) cannot be extended with (5)--(7) to any upper coefficient tending
to0. In particular it cannot maintain the benchmark q=1/lambda^m
once lambda^m>=8, where lambda=1+sqrt(2).

For the assigned critical word, m>=128, epsilon=1/m,
c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c, and
H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j). Its first physical step is
H=1+a. The radical bounds12/5<lambda<17/7 imply

    a >=127/(129lambda)>889/2193>2/5,
    a <1/lambda=sqrt(2)-1.

The last rational comparison follows from4445>4386. Hence
7/5<H<sqrt(2), so both the valid seed (8) and the obstruction apply.
The total shifted mass M_m=1+sum H_m is at least2^m, since every one
of its2^m-1 steps exceeds1. Thus the desired q_m=O(1/M_m) tends to0
and is excluded by q>1/8 for this cone. This conclusion does not use
the unverified C54 scalar comparison as a mathematical premise.

Scope. Independent context-dependent edge weights, connections changing
more than one bit, arbitrary dense tensor kernels, and independent changes
to the local finite coefficient arrays are NOT excluded. In particular
the full PEP certificate cone is much larger. The scalar obstruction does
not prove that the actual critical schedule is bad. The structural defect
of (6) is precise: the same coefficient totals R,U control both the first
gradient and the terminal, while the terminal value source requires t>=2.
Increasing q or diagonal optimum storage cannot remove that defect at
the required vanishing scale.

## 6. A separate exact screen for symmetric bulk multiplier arrays

This section concerns ANY array with lambda_ij=lambda_ji for all finite
distinct i,j, including arbitrary complete bipartite, dyadic hierarchical,
or Walsh-diagonal nonnegative kernels. Optimum incidence may be arbitrary
as long as the value flow holds. It is a different restriction from (6).

Identify R^2 with C, with <u,v>=Re(conj(u)v). Set zeta=(1+i)/2 and
define a formal trajectory

    p_0=1, p_(i+1)=(1-h_i zeta)p_i,
    x_i=p_i, g_i=zeta p_i, f_i=|p_i|^2/4.           (15)

It obeys the physical GD equations exactly and has ||x_0||=1. Since
Re(zeta)=|zeta|^2=1/2, direct expansion gives

    Q_(i,star)=Q_(star,i)=0,
    Q_ij=(1/2)Im(conj(p_i)p_j)=-Q_ji.              (16)

The individual finite Q need not be nonpositive. These are formal test
vectors, not asserted to be a legal smooth-convex transcript. On (15),
the quadratic form of a symmetric finite array equals

    M(q)=q-|p_n|^2/2.

Full PSD therefore requires q>=|p_n|^2/2, irrespective of every optimum
edge. For the recursive word with h-levels1+a c^k, define

    T_j=|p_(2^j-1)|^2,
    d_k=(1+a^2 c^(2k))/2.

Then T_0=1 and T_(j+1)=d_j T_j^2, since the word contains two
identical child products and the single bridge. Both undeformed Silver
(a=1/lambda,c=lambda) and the actual critical word for m>=128 satisfy
a>2/5 and c>12/5. Consequently

    d_0>4/7, d_1>19/20, d_2>3, d_3>15,
    T_4=d_0^8 d_1^4 d_2^2 d_3
         >(4/7)^8(19/20)^4*135 >6/5.                (17)

The four rational inequalities in (17) follow by evaluating
(1+(2/5)^2(12/5)^(2k))/2 at k=0,1,2,3. For the final comparison,
the left rational product reduces to900778752/720600125; its numerator
times5 minus6 times its denominator is180293010>0. For k>=4, d_k>1.
It follows inductively that for every j>=4,

    T_j>(6/5)^(2^(j-4)),
    q>(1/2)(6/5)^(2^(j-4)).                        (18)

Thus the symmetric multiplier organization fails even the undeformed
calibration, exponentially in the number of leaves. This is not a
limitation on Laplacian SLACK matrices produced from directed arrays.

For a general directed finite array, the same computation yields instead
the exact necessary directed-area inequality

    q +(1/2)sum_(i<j)(lambda_ij-lambda_ji)
                      Im(conj(p_i)p_j) >= T_m/2.    (19)

Equation (19) identifies an actual contribution that is lost on replacing
an array by its symmetric part. It is necessary only, not sufficient for
full PSD or interpolation feasibility.

## 7. Exact tensor contraction for the remaining directed dense family

For the same recursive word and any complex zeta, let P_j be its scalar
terminal GD polynomial on H_j and define

    tau_(j+1)=(1-(1+a c^j)zeta)P_j, P_0=1.

The full sample-position vector p^(j) of length2^j obeys

    p^(0)=(1), p^(j+1)=[p^(j);tau_(j+1)p^(j)],
    p^(m)=(1,tau_m) tensor ... tensor(1,tau_1).     (20)

This is proved by applying the identical child GD polynomial after the
bridge; P_(j+1)=tau_(j+1)P_j is its last entry.

If a proposed dense finite multiplier kernel (before discarding its
diagonal) is K=eta times the tensor product of real nonnegative2 by2
matrices B_m,...,B_1, then

    p^* K p=eta product_k [B_k,00+B_k,11|tau_k|^2
                             +B_k,01 tau_k+B_k,10 conj(tau_k)].       (21)

This follows by distributing the finite tensor sums. Diagonal entries
contribute real numbers and thus do not affect the imaginary part.
At zeta=(1+i)/2, (19) is equivalently

    q+(1/2)Im(p^*Kp)>=T_m/2.                       (22)

For a finite nonnegative sum of such product kernels, sum the expressions
(21). This is an analytic contraction test for a PRESCRIBED low-complexity
kernel, not a sufficient PSD invariant. It leaves the genuinely directed
dense product family open; applying (4) with arbitrary unspecified A and
calling its PSD a remaining lemma would merely restate the original PEP
and is explicitly BLOCKED as a proof route.

## 8. Literature and scope of this round

Read as method context: Bok and Altschuler, "Accelerating Proximal Gradient
Descent via Silver Stepsizes", arXiv:2412.05497, Theorem9, Definition13,
Lemma14 and its proof, with the local PDF and extracted text retained.
That work's Laplacian is a slack matrix in auxiliary proximal subgradients,
not a symmetric multiplier array. Its exact silver identities do not
supply an upper certificate for the critical deformation here. No theorem
from the paper is used as a correctness premise in Sections1--7.

This package records two distinct scoped obstructions and a directed
tensor contraction screen. It adds no verified fact and does not resolve
either the uniform lower-bound target or a strict asymptotic separation.

## 9. Dense tensor kernels and arbitrary nonnegative mixtures: the same barrier

The coordinate sum in (6) is not essential. Here is a strictly larger,
genuinely dense coefficient cone, with independent cross-block pairs
differing in arbitrarily many bits. Its assumptions are explicit; no
arbitrary unknown full matrix is being hidden inside its definition.

At every bit k choose a two by two matrix

    P_k=[[1-v_k,u_k],[v_k,c_k-u_k]],
    0<=u_k<=v_k<=1,  u_k<=c_k<=1-v_k+u_k.           (23)

All entries are nonnegative, all row and column sums are at most1, and
the first column sum is exactly1. These properties follow directly:
the row sums are1-v_k+u_k and c_k+v_k-u_k; the column sums are1,c_k.
Conversely every nonnegative two by two matrix with these row/column
properties has the representation (23).

Take any finite number of products, with factors P_(ell,k) satisfying
(23), and choose eta_ell>=0 and delta_i>=0. Define

    P_ell=P_(ell,m) tensor ... tensor P_(ell,1),
    A=sum_ell eta_ell(I-P_ell)+diag(delta).          (24)

Thus EVERY actual finite multiplier is the concrete nonnegative sum

    lambda_ij=sum_ell eta_ell product_k P_(ell,k)[i_k,j_k], i!=j.   (25)

The diagonal of P is not an interpolation edge. The definition of A
sets the star coefficients via (3), rather than treating a diagonal
as a free nonnegative interpolation constraint. Its row sums b are
nonnegative because each P_ell has row sums at most1. Every column
sum of A is nonnegative. The only additional requirement for a>=0 is

    t=sum_ell eta_ell(1-product_k c_(ell,k))+delta_n>=2.          (26)

At all other indices the subtraction2e_n in (2) is zero. Equations
(24)--(26) therefore check every actual sign and all value coefficients.
The number of mixture terms and every parameter may depend on m; no
bounded-rank or fixed-library assumption is imposed.

This cone contains the valid seed of Section3. For any0<H<=sqrt(2),
put M=1+H, eta=4, and take a single factor

    P_H=[[1/2,1/(2M)],[1/2,1/2-1/(2M)]].           (27)

It has u=1/(2M),v=c=1/2, satisfies (23), and
4(I-P_H)=A_H. Equation (8) is its full one-step calibration. More
generally the cone contains all coordinate sums (6), including their
nonnegative limits: write a local two-node A_k as eta(I-P_k) with eta
large enough to keep both diagonal entries of P_k nonnegative, and
put identity factors at every other bit. Its row/column bounds follow
from those of A_k. The delta remains unchanged.

We now prove that every full PSD certificate from (24)--(26), on any
schedule with h_0>=7/5, still requires q>1/8.

For one product, temporarily omit the mixture label and put

    D0=product_k(1-v_k), L0=product_k(1-v_k+u_k),
    Dn=product_k(c_k-u_k), Cn=product_k c_k,
    Ln=product_k(c_k+v_k-u_k).

These are respectively the first diagonal, first row sum, last diagonal,
last column sum, and last row sum of P. The first column sum is1.
All are nonnegative and the row and column sums are at most1.

Two elementary product inequalities are decisive:

    0<=Ln-Cn<=1-L0,
    0<=Cn-Dn<=L0-D0.                                (28)

To prove them, for nonnegative vectors s,d define
F_d(s)=product_k(s_k+d_k)-product_k s_k. Its expansion is the sum
over nonempty subsets J of product_(k in J)d_k times
product_(k not in J)s_k. Each coefficient is nonnegative, so F_d
is coordinatewise nondecreasing in s.
For the first inequality of (28), set d_k=v_k-u_k>=0.
Then c_k<=1-d_k by (23), and

    Ln-Cn=F_d(c)<=F_d(1-d)=1-product_k(1-d_k)=1-L0.

For the second, set d_k=u_k. Since c_k-u_k<=1-v_k,

    Cn-Dn=F_u(c-u)<=F_u(1-v)=L0-D0.

Now restore the mixture label and define

    B_L=sum_ell eta_ell(1-L0_ell),
    R_L=sum_ell eta_ell(L0_ell-D0_ell),
    B_R=sum_ell eta_ell(Ln_ell-Cn_ell),
    R_R=sum_ell eta_ell(Cn_ell-Dn_ell).

Every number is nonnegative. By (28),

    B_R<=B_L, R_R<=R_L.                             (29)

The actual first and last coefficients of the full matrix (4) are

    z=b_0=B_L+delta_0,
    G_00=z-(h_0-1)R_L,
    b_n=t-B_R,
    G_nn=t+R_R-1.                                   (30)

For the first diagonal, the finite outgoing row sum at0 is R_L and
each such target j>0 has T_j0=h_0. For the last diagonal use
A_nn=sum eta(1-Dn)+delta_n=t+R_R and column n of V as before.
These prove (30) on the original formal space.

If0<q<=1/8 and the matrix were PSD, its x_0,g_0 principal submatrix
would imply exactly as in (12)

    B_L<=z<=4q<=1/2,
    R_L<=q/(h_0-1)<=5/16.

Equations (29)--(30) and the x_0,g_n principal submatrix would then
give, using t>=2,

    q >=(t-B_R)^2/[4(t+R_R-1)]
       >(t-1/2)^2/(4t)>=9/32,

a contradiction. Levels q<=0 are excluded by the same source/initial-row
argument in Section4. This proves q>1/8 for the entire dense mixture cone.

The critical and undeformed applications in Section5 follow unchanged.
The obstruction allows all directions of optimum incidence, all actual
interior pairs, arbitrarily many mixture terms, and arbitrary diagonal
optimum storage. It rules out this normalized tensor CONE, not all
nonnegative tensor-product arrays: a factor violating its first-column
normalization or its row/column bounds can leave the cone. Nor does it
cover a correction with negative mixture weights even if the final edge
array is nonnegative. The product inequalities (28), not a mere change
of basis or an assumed Huber kernel, are the mechanism behind the bound.

## 10. General first-query budget and required context variation

For context and a possible next mutation, the first part of the preceding
test is universal. In ANY nonnegative full certificate with h_0=H>1,
write b_0=lambda_(0,star) and r_0=sum_(j=1)^n lambda_0j. The x_0,g_0
principal submatrix is

    [[q,-b_0/2],[-b_0/2,b_0-(H-1)r_0]].             (31)

This follows directly from the general expansion (4), with no restrictions
on incoming terminal edges, optimum-source edges, or the rest of the array.
Since q>0, its determinant implies

    b_0<=4q, r_0<=q/(H-1).                          (32)

The proof is the identity
(b_0-2q)^2+4q(H-1)r_0<=4q^2. The earlier arbitrary-q queried-cut
draft367cf22cf1bd54cc retains more variables and all target-position
moments; (31)--(32) are compatible with that larger interface. They are
rederived here jointly, not imported from an unverified draft.

If a contextual extension of the binary-coordinate array has first
totals B_L,R_L and terminal totals B_R,R_R as in (30), t>=2, and
obeys B_R<=K B_L and R_R<=K R_L for some K>=1, then the same proof
shows

    q>1/(8K), provided h_0>=7/5.                    (33)

Indeed q<=1/(8K) would imply B_R<=1/2,R_R<=5/16 and also q<=1/8,
which reproduces the contradiction. Thus a useful q=O(1/M_m) in this
contextual extension requires K at least a constant times M_m. A bounded
change of context weights cannot repair the cone. This quantitative
condition is necessary only; it does not assert that larger variation
will make the full matrix PSD or that every possible certificate admits
this contextual parameterization.

evidence:
# Growing Newton temporal spaces on the actual critical word

Status: complete draft candidates, UNVERIFIED. No solver, numerical evaluation,
installation or fact_submit. Accepted facts 1252b8823bb5a290 (interpolation and
normalization) and b98bb807d514e80d (the exact benchmark and its elementary
envelope) are the only correctness inputs. Every new estimate is proved here.
These are obstructions for specified growing temporal spaces, not an upper
bound for the unrestricted worst-case objective and not the original target.

## 1. Actual word, queried prefix and a genuinely restricted growing space

Fix m>=128 and keep the following parameters fixed within that horizon:

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j),
    n=2^m-1, q=n-1.

The prescribed queried-prefix steps h_0,...,h_(q-1) are H_m with its last
entry d_0 removed. Queries are indexed 0,...,q; the last free step is b in
[0,2], including the original b=d_0. Write

    P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z), 0<=i<=q.

Choose a REAL monic polynomial chi of degree r, with 1<=r<=q. For a
polynomial p let [p] denote its remainder modulo chi. This is an r-dimensional
real vector space; use coefficients in 1,z,...,z^(r-1) as its real coordinates.
Let T be ANY real linear map from this space into any finite-dimensional
Euclidean space, with ||T[1]||=1. Put

    x_i=T[P_i],       g_i=T[z P_i],     0<=i<=q.          (1)

The map, ambient dimension, metric, coefficients and polynomial can all depend
on m. Singular maps are allowed. Initial correlations are unrestricted. The
identity P_(i+1)=P_i-h_i zP_i proves the ACTUAL GD recursion for (1).

All queried values f_i remain joint variables. Assume that the data (1), those
values and the optimum jet (0,0,0) belong to ONE convex differentiable function
F with 1-Lipschitz gradient. Thus the initial distance to this designated
minimizer is exactly one. All conclusions below hold for EVERY interpolant of
these jets; no terminal gradient identity is assumed after the last step b.

This is a fixed r-dimensional temporal space, even when the physical image
dimension is larger. For r=m it retains m independent Newton coefficients.
More generally the theorem below permits a degree much larger than m but
strictly smaller than the full n+1-node representation of arbitrary data.

## 2. The full computable all-pair law and function realization

Let J be multiplication by z modulo chi, let v_0 be the coefficient vector of
1, and define

    v_(i+1)=(I-h_i J)v_i,    w_i=Jv_i,    M=T^T T.

Then x_i=T v_i, g_i=T w_i, M is a REAL PSD matrix, and v_0^T M v_0=1.
Conversely every real PSD M has a real Euclidean factor T. With
v_star=w_star=0 and f_star=0, the necessary and sufficient full interpolation
law is, for EVERY distinct ordered pair i,j in {star,0,...,q},

 f_i-f_j+w_i^T M(v_j-v_i)
                   +(w_i-w_j)^T M(w_i-w_j)/2 <=0.       (2)

This is exactly Q_ij<=0 in fact 1252b8823bb5a290, evaluated on the stated
vectors. No pair or common value is replaced by a componentwise condition.
For feasible data that fact constructs an actual function explicitly:

 cjet_j=<g_j,x_j>-f_j,
 H(v)=max_j {cjet_j+<x_j,v-g_j>+||v-g_j||^2/2},
 F_max(x)=sup_v {<x,v>-H(v)}.

The maximum includes the optimum jet. The function is finite, convex and
1-smooth, interpolates every queried value and gradient, and has minimum zero
at zero. This provides a function realization, not just a Gram representation.

For a Newton basis with roots theta_1,...,theta_r, repetitions allowed,
the basis polynomials are N_k(z)=product_(ell=1)^k(z-theta_ell), 0<=k<r.
Multiplication obeys zN_k=theta_(k+1)N_k+N_(k+1), with N_r=0 in the quotient.
Thus J is a bidiagonal Newton chain in that basis. For nonreal conjugate
roots the original real monomial coordinates, or real and imaginary parts of
the Newton coordinates, give the same REAL law (2); a complex matrix is not
being called a real PSD metric.

## 3. Exact level resonance: a complete growing-span annihilation obstruction

The level d_j occurs 2^(m-j-1) times in H_m. In the retained prefix the
counts are

    N_0=2^(m-1)-1, N_j=2^(m-j-1), 1<=j<m.              (3)

Let mu_j=1/d_j. Suppose

    chi(z)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(z-mu_j)^(r_j),
    0<=r_j<=N_j,     1<=sum r_j<=q.                    (4)

Since P_q(z)=product_j(1-d_j z)^(N_j), chi divides P_q. Thus x_q=g_q=0
in (1), for EVERY map T and every common metric, regardless of its condition
number or initial correlations. Every legal interpolant has

                    2F(x_q-b g_q)=0                    (5)

for every real b. This includes one independent Newton direction at EVERY
recursive large-step level (r=m), as well as every growing multiplicity
permitted by the actual counts (3). It also handles confluent derivatives:
vanishing to order r_j, not merely vanishing once, is the exact requirement.

One can add a SINGLE zero root, chi=z product_j(z-mu_j)^(r_j), provided its
degree is <=q. Then chi divides zP_q, so g_q=0. The position need not be zero,
but legality says it is a minimizer of F; again (5) holds. Adding a second
zero root is not covered: a nonzero constant terminal gradient may survive.

For the simple positive roots r_j=1, all factors have occurred by the first
central top-level step (index 2^(m-1)-1). The model already reaches zero after
that step. This uses the actual chronology; (3) is the more general terminal
criterion for growing confluent blocks.

such that all P_i(alpha), 0<=i<=q, are nonzero and pairwise distinct. Such a

This is a finite algebraic specification, not a request for numerical search.

Let e_0,...,e_(r-1) be the orthonormal basis of R^r and let N_shift e_k=e_(k+1)
for k<r-1, N_shift e_(r-1)=0. For epsilon>0 set

 A_epsilon=alpha I+epsilon N_shift,
 X_i=P_i(A_epsilon)e_0, G_i=A_epsilon X_i,
 V_i=(alpha/2)||X_i||^2.                               (22)

 V'_i=(V_i-nu||X_i||^2/2)/(1-nu).                      (23)

At epsilon=0 these are the jets of the scalar quadratic of curvature
alpha'=(alpha-nu)/(1-nu), lying strictly in (0,1), at points

ordered residual is strictly negative:

 Q'_ij(0)=-alpha'(1-alpha')||X_i(0)-X_j(0)||^2/2<0.

For epsilon variable each Q'_ij(epsilon) is a real polynomial, since all
quantities in (22)--(23) are polynomial. Define the exact finite constants

 delta=min_(i!=j)(-Q'_ij(0))>0,
 D=1+sum_(i!=j) sum_(k>=1) |coefficient_(epsilon^k) Q'_ij|,

provide a computable algebraic law, not a solver oracle. Since epsilon<=1,

is convex, 1-smooth and nu-strongly convex, has its UNIQUE minimizer at zero,
and interpolates EVERY original (X_i,G_i,V_i). Its actual GD follows (22)
with the prescribed steps. X_0=e_0 has TRUE initial distance exactly one.

These data have the representation (1) with chi=(z-alpha)^r and
T[p]=p(A_epsilon)e_0. The r vectors e_0,A_epsilon e_0,...,

No quadratic function with a minimizer at zero can interpolate these

of X_i is P_i(theta_0)/sqrt(m), so all queried points and zero are distinct.
Every ordered transformed Q' is consequently strictly negative, by the exact
quadratic formula -<X_i-X_j,B(I-B)(X_i-X_j)>/2 for B=(D_diag-nu I)/(1-nu).

Define delta and the coefficient bound D_coeff as in (24), using these new
polynomial residuals. Also let R(epsilon) have columns X_0,...,X_(m-1), put
d_det=det R(0), and put D_det=1+sum_(k>=1)|[epsilon^k] det R(epsilon)|.
The m distinct diagonal entries and the successive degrees of the P_i give
d_det!=0 by the polynomial evaluation/Vandermonde argument: a degree<m
polynomial vanishing at all m distinct entries is zero. Set

 epsilon=min(1/2,delta/(2D_coeff),|d_det|/(2D_det))>0.   (38b)

Every Q' remains strictly negative and det R(epsilon) remains nonzero, by
the same coefficient-sum bounds as (24). Fact1252 constructs K, and
F=(1-nu)K+nu||x||^2/2 gives one1-smooth nu-strongly convex function with
the stated jets, UNIQUE minimizer0 and initial distance exactly1.

The polynomial chi=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(z-theta_j) is an allowed member of
Section7 with r=m: only the bottom-level root is shifted, within its allowed
disk. Moreover chi(A_epsilon)=0. One direct check uses the lower bidiagonal
Newton multiplication matrix J with diagonal theta_j and lower entries1:
A_epsilon=S J S^(-1) for S=diag(1,epsilon,...,epsilon^(m-1)), and chi(J)=0
by its quotient definition. Thus T[p]=p(A_epsilon)X_0 is the required REAL
quotient map. The nonzero determinant in (38b) makes it injective, so its
common metric is positive definite and all m temporal directions are present.

No quadratic with minimum at zero interpolates these data, since its symmetric
Hessian would have to equal the nonsymmetric A_epsilon on the position basis
X_0,...,X_(m-1). The function therefore has genuinely nonquadratic queried data.
At the original final step b=d_0, the first coordinate is unaffected by the
strictly lower triangular part, giving the quantitative positive payoff

 2F(X_q-d_0G_q)>= (nu/m)(1-d_0 theta_0)^2 P_q(theta_0)^2>0.  (38c)

The factors are nonzero by construction. Inequality (28) also holds, so this
is a positive but negligible payoff. It is not claimed as a new mechanism
that improves the quadratic or single-cut benchmark.

## 8. A double-zero root really survives: an actual legal scope counterexample

It would be false to extend the annihilation conclusion from a simple zero
root to a double zero root, or to assume that the terminal constant gradient
has nonnegative correlation with the eliminated component. The counterexample
below uses the ACTUAL critical word and has a unique minimizer and distance1.
It is the already verified single-cut mechanism in b98bb807d514e80d, written
explicitly in the new growing Newton coordinates to audit their scope.

Let S_total=sum H_m, d=d_0 and T_tail=S_total-d. Define

 A_tail=(d-1)/(2T_tail+1)>0,
 f'(x)=max(-A_tail,min(1,x)), f(0)=0, x_0=1.           (39)

This derivative is monotone, continuous and1-Lipschitz, so its integral is
one convex1-smooth function with unique minimizer0. The first query has
gradient1; after the actual first step d the point is

 x_1=1-d=-A_tail(2T_tail+1).

Every later query stays at most -A_tail(T_tail+1)<-A_tail, since the remaining
total step mass is T_tail. Thus every later gradient is the constant -A_tail.
At the actual end of H_m the full normalized payoff is exactly

             2f(x_n)=(d-1)^2/(2T_tail+1)>0.            (40)

In fact this also REFUTES extension of the super-small bound (28) to a double
zero root, for every m>=128. Count the levels to obtain

 1+S_total=A_mass c^m+(1-A_mass)2^m,
 A_mass=a/(c-2) in(0,1).

Here A_mass<1 follows from ac<1=lambda(lambda-2)<c(c-2). Hence S_total<c^m,
and (10) implies

                  2f(x_n)>(3/64)c^(-m).               (40a)

This exceeds100000 exp(-m^3/4): logc<1 and
log(100000*64/3)<15, while m^3/4-m>15 for m>=128.
Thus the zero-root multiplicity in Section7 is quantitatively load-bearing,
not only needed for the exact-zero statement in Section3.

All ordered constraints, including every queried value and the optimum, hold
because these are actual jets of the single explicitly defined function (39).

This transcript belongs to the growing class

              chi=z^2 product_(j=0)^(m-1)(z-mu_j),     (41)

of degree m+2. To specify the real map T on the quotient, define it directly
on a polynomial p by

 T[p]=u p(0)+v p'(0)+d w p(mu_0),
 v=-A_tail, w=1+A_tail, u=1-dw.                       (42)

Evaluation at0, the derivative at0 and evaluation atmu_0 all vanish on
multiples of chi, so this is a well-defined quotient map. The remaining
level coordinates are allowed but have zero image. For every i,

 x_i=u-s_i v+d w P_i(mu_0),
 g_i=v+w P_i(mu_0),  s_i=sum_(t<i)h_t.

P_0(mu_0)=1 and P_i(mu_0)=0 for every i>=1, because the first step is d_0.
Thus these formulas reproduce exactly (39), and T[1]=u+dw=1. The common
metric T^T T is real PSD; no nonlinear or time-dependent map has been used.
In particular v*(dw)=-A_tail d(1+A_tail)<0. Hence the tempting cross-term
inequality <v,eliminated_component>>=0 is already false on legal data.

The function is genuinely nonquadratic on the transcript: a quadratic with
minimum at0 and g_0=1 atx_0=1 would have curvature1, while its gradient atx_1
would be1-d, not -A_tail. For large positive T_tail these differ. Its exact
payoff is the known weak first-cut bound, so (40) is NOT an improved
adversary or a profile resolution. It proves only that a double-zero
residual and its negative cross terms must be handled in any extension of
Sections3 or7. Arbitrary shifted upper-level nodes, double-zero blocks and
changing generators remain open after these scoped obstructions.

evidence:
# C56: a legal two-dimensional repair and its unavoidable normalization cost

Status: **complete scoped joint proof candidate, not verifier-accepted**.
No optimization or fact_submit is allocated. The only mathematical
predecessor is accepted fact `1252b8823bb5a290`, for smooth-convex
interpolation, its explicit conjugate construction, and exact unqueried
terminal completion. The scalar template is defined and analyzed here;
no unverified C53/C55 claim is used as a premise.

This is a primal construction for the actual critical schedule. It produces
one globally defined convex smooth function, with all queried data jointly
legal, in dimension two. Its limitation is quantitative: the specific
repair mechanism cannot retain the very large formal objective ratio.
Neither this construction nor its obstruction decides the actual worst-case
performance of the schedule or the unrestricted minimax problem.

## 1. Schedule and a completely specified scalar formal trajectory

Fix m>=128 and put

    epsilon=1/m, lambda=1+sqrt(2),
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c,
    d_j=a c^j,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+d_j,H_j),
    n_j=2^j-1, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

Write h=H_m, n=n_m, S=S_m, M_m=1+S, and

    b0=1+a, b1=1+d_1=2-epsilon,
    h_max=1+d_(m-1).

Every step is greater than one; the largest step is the central bridge.
All choices depend only on the fixed horizon, before an oracle is queried.

Define signed template moments

    k_2=M_2+6epsilon,
    k_(j+1)=-k_j^2/d_j for j>=2.                       (1)

For an H2 block whose terminal gradient is the scalar v, prescribe

    g_0=(2-c+6epsilon/b0)v,
    g_1=v, g_2=c v, g_3=v.                           (2)

Start this block at x_0=k_2 v and use its actual GD steps. Directly,
b0 g_0+b1 g_1+b0 g_2+g_3=k_2 v, so x_3=v.
At a higher H_(j+1) block with terminal gradient v, use the level-j
template with terminal v on the right and with terminal

    v_left=-k_j v/d_j

on the left. Start the parent at x_start=k_(j+1)v. Since its left queried
displacement is (k_j-1)v_left, its left endpoint is v_left. Its bridge
then ends at -d_j v_left=k_j v, exactly the prescribed right start.
The right endpoint is v. This proves the actual chronological GD recursion
of the formal positions and gradients at every level.

Use terminal gradient 1 at the root. Thus

    x_0=k_m, x_n=g_n=1,
    x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i.

For each scalar sample put y_i=x_i-g_i. Every H2 seed endpoint has y=0.
Inside a seed with terminal v, define G0=2-c+6epsilon/b0. Its gradients
and proximal coordinates, in order, are

    gradients:   (G0, 1, c, 1) v,
    proximal:    (k_2-G0, 1+d_1+b0 c, 1+a c, 0) v.     (3)

The template is not legal. In the rightmost seed the two queried indices
i=n-2 and j=n-1 have gradients 1,c and displacement x_i-x_j=b1.
Their sum of smooth-convex residuals, independently of function values, is

    Q_ij+Q_ji=(c-1)(d_1+c)>0,                        (4)

where Q is defined below. Thus no scalar function can realize these jets.

For the size estimates needed in the repair, the critical ratio obeys

    R0=k_2/(c d_2)<1-epsilon/4,
    |k_j|=(1-epsilon)c^j R0^(2^(j-2)).                (5)

Here is a direct verification of the strict gap. Since M_2=5-epsilon+2a,

    (c d_2-M_2)/epsilon
      =[6sqrt(2)+epsilon-2lambda^2 epsilon^2
                                  -lambda^2 epsilon^3]/(1+epsilon)>8.

For the last inequality subtract 8 after multiplying by 1+epsilon and use

    6sqrt(2)-8-7epsilon-2lambda^2 epsilon^2-lambda^2 epsilon^3
      >2/5-7/128-12/128^2-6/128^3>0.

It follows that c d_2-k_2>2epsilon, while c d_2<25/4. This proves the
first inequality in (5); the second follows by squaring the ratio at each
step of (1). Every absolute left-child scale |k_j|/d_j is less than c.
Consequently every seed's absolute terminal amplitude is at most c^(m-2).

The elementary bounds c<5/2, k_2<6, |G0|<1, and b0<sqrt(2)<3/2 give
from (3)

    |g_i|<3c^m, |y_i|<7c^m                           (6)

for every sample. For clarity, k_2<6 follows from
M_2<5+6/7 and 6epsilon<=3/64; and
G0 lies between -1/2 and 2-12/5+3/64<0. These bounds include the terminal
sample, with the optimum sample g_star=y_star=0 added separately.

Equation (5) also gives

    |k_m|<c^m exp[-2^(m-4)/m] ->0.

Thus the formal choice f_n=1/2 would have an enormous ratio 1/k_m^2. It
is precisely this initially tiny normalization that the repair must pay for.

## 2. One explicit extra coordinate repairs ALL interpolation inequalities

Choose any curvature

    0<kappa<1/h_max,

and define the monotone quadratic trajectory

    xi_0=1, xi_(i+1)=(1-kappa h_i)xi_i,
    xi_star=0.

All xi_i are positive and strictly decreasing. This is a single extra
coordinate; no incompatible instances are averaged. For a scalar T>0
set the proposed two-dimensional jets to

    X_i=(x_i,T xi_i),
    G_i=(g_i,T kappa xi_i),
    f_i=[g_i^2+T^2 kappa xi_i^2]/2,
    X_star=G_star=0, f_star=0.                        (7)

The entire vector GD recursion is exact:
X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i G_i. The scalar first coordinate by itself is still not a
legal function; the final interpolating function will be jointly convex
in both coordinates and is not asserted to be a separable sum.

Use the accepted interpolation convention

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2.

Direct expansion gives the FULL all-pair law, including every star pair:

    Q_ij=g_i(y_j-y_i)
                   -T^2 kappa(1-kappa)(xi_i-xi_j)^2/2. (8)

The first term follows by substituting f_i^formal=g_i^2/2 and x_i=g_i+y_i;
the second is the residual for the quadratic t -> kappa t^2/2. Thus the
same function values and the same two coordinates are tested against all
ordered pairs, not merely against one aggregated dual form.

From (6), g_i(y_j-y_i)<=42c^(2m). For any two distinct finite indices,
their xi displacement is at least one adjacent displacement, and

    xi_i-xi_(i+1)=kappa h_i xi_i>kappa xi_n.

For an optimum pair xi_i>=xi_n>kappa xi_n, since kappa<1. Therefore
the completely explicit choice

    T^2=84c^(2m)/[kappa^3(1-kappa)xi_n^2]+k_m^2        (9)

makes every Q_ij<=0. There is no optimization or nearest-feasible-point
problem hidden in (9): every quantity is an explicit scalar or product
of the predetermined steps.

To produce one actual function, let J={star,0,...,n}, and define on R^2

    H(v)=max_(i in J) {
       <G_i,X_i>-f_i+<X_i,v-G_i>+||v-G_i||^2/2 },
    F(X)=sup_v {<X,v>-H(v)}.                         (10)

By accepted fact `1252b8823bb5a290`, F is finite everywhere, convex,
differentiable with gradient Lipschitz constant one, and interpolates every
jet in (7). Formally this use of the predecessor is obtained by appending
one zero step to h, so all indices 0,...,n are queried prefix samples.
The predecessor explicitly permits that zero step. All the required
prefix interpolation inequalities were proved in (8)-(9).

The minimizer of F is UNIQUE and equals zero. Indeed write

    H(v)=||v||^2/2+
           max_(i in J){<X_i-G_i,v>+||G_i||^2/2-f_i}.

At v=0, the star term is zero, whereas every other intercept is

    ||G_i||^2/2-f_i=-T^2 kappa(1-kappa)xi_i^2/2<0.

There are finitely many terms. In a neighborhood of zero only the star
term is active, so H(v)=||v||^2/2 there. The set of minimizers of its
conjugate is the subgradient set of H at zero, which here is {0}.
This last assertion can also be checked from the defining supremum:
F(X)=0 requires <X,v><=H(v) for all v, hence X=0 by taking arbitrarily
small positive and negative v; and H(v)>=||v||^2/2 gives F(0)=0.

Consequently the TRUE squared distance to the closest minimizer is

    dist(X_0,argmin F)^2=k_m^2+T^2.                  (11)

There is no artificial enlargement from choosing a remote minimizer.
The exact normalized terminal payoff of the constructed function is

    P_assigned=[1+T^2 kappa xi_n^2]/[k_m^2+T^2].       (12)

Multiplying F by any L>0 gives a convex function with L-Lipschitz gradient,
the same GD trajectory for steps h_i/L, and the same project-normalized
payoff 2(F(X_n)-F_star)/dist(X_0,argmin F)^2.

## 3. This is a nonzero legal witness, with a fully quantified scale

For the explicit choice kappa=1/(2S), we have kappa h_i<=1/2, so it is in
the permitted range. For 0<=z<=1/2,

    log(1-z)>=-2z,

because the derivative of log(1-z)+2z is (1-2z)/(1-z)>=0 and its value
at zero is zero. It follows that xi_n>=exp(-2kappa S)=exp(-1).
Since (9) gives T^2>=k_m^2, (12) yields the explicit lower bound

    P_assigned >= kappa xi_n^2/2
                       >=exp(-2)/(4S).               (13)

This is an actual legal two-dimensional witness with order 1/S payoff.
It does not claim a new worst-case lower bound beyond what simpler
quadratic or Huber examples already provide. Its purpose is to make the
proposed deformation of the formal template fully concrete and legal.

## 4. One retained QUERY pair forces a cubic normalization cost

The cost is not an artifact of the conservative sufficient amplitude (9).
Take ANY T>0 and ANY function values for which the queried positions and
gradients (7) are jointly legal with minimizer zero. Keep only the queried
pair i=n-2, j=n-1; no terminal sample is used in this argument.

In the first coordinate the rightmost H2 seed has

    g_i=1, g_j=c, x_i-x_j=b1,
    Q_ij^formal+Q_ji^formal=(c-1)(d_1+c)=:D_bad.

Function values cancel in this sum, so these equalities remain valid for
arbitrary proposed values. In the second coordinate

    xi_i-xi_j=kappa b1 xi_i.

The necessary sum of the TWO original interpolation inequalities is
therefore exactly

    D_bad-T^2 kappa^3(1-kappa)b1^2 xi_(n-2)^2<=0.

Thus every feasible repair in this stated geometry must obey

    T^2 >= D_bad/[kappa^3(1-kappa)b1^2 xi_(n-2)^2].    (14)

We have D_bad>4: c-1>4/3 and d_1+c>3. Also b1<=2 and xi_(n-2)<=1.
Consequently

    1/T^2<kappa^3, and T^2>kappa^(-3)>h_max^3.        (15)

This is a necessary inequality for the original queried geometry. Changing
function values or applying maximal completion at the last unqueried point
cannot remove it. It explains the cubic price: the quadratic coordinate's
adjacent displacement is proportional to kappa, and its interpolation
slack is proportional to another kappa times the squared displacement.

For the assigned terminal values, combining (12),(15) gives

    P_assigned < kappa xi_n^2+kappa^3
               <=1/[2 exp(1) S]+h_max^(-3).           (16)

Here xi_n<=exp(-kappa S), from 1-z<=exp(-z), and
max_(t>=0) t exp(-2St)=1/[2 exp(1)S], as follows by differentiating.

## 5. Maximal terminal completion also pays the cost

Keep only the queried jets i<n with the assigned values (7), together
with the optimum. Use the accepted maximal prefix interpolant from
`1252b8823bb5a290` to complete the last unqueried point. This is a legal
single global function, and its value at X_n is maximal among all
interpolants of those prefix jets. The strict negative intercepts in
Section 2 still apply to every retained non-star jet, so its minimizer
is again uniquely zero. Thus (11) is still the actual closest-minimizer
distance. No terminal gradient or terminal value is imposed in this part.

There is a uniform upper bound on this maximal terminal payoff. More
generally it applies to any legal prefix with the displayed X_i,G_i and
minimizer zero, for its ratio normalized by ||X_0||^2. Let i=n-1 be the
last queried point. Interpolation with the optimum gives

    f_i<=<G_i,X_i>-||G_i||^2/2.

The smoothness inequality on the actual final step X_n=X_i-b0 G_i gives

    F(X_n)<=f_i-b0(1-b0/2)||G_i||^2.

These two inequalities imply

    2F(X_n)<=2<G_i,X_i>-(1+2b0-b0^2)||G_i||^2.        (17)

Here g_i=c, x_i=1+b0 c, and the second coordinate is (T xi_i,T kappa xi_i).
Since 1+2b0-b0^2>0, the right side is at most

    2c+(b0^2-1)c^2+2T^2 kappa xi_i^2
                     <12+2T^2 kappa xi_i^2.

Divide by k_m^2+T^2, apply (15), and use
xi_i<=exp[-kappa(S-b0)]. The normalized completed payoff satisfies

    P_completed < 12kappa^3+2kappa exp[-2kappa(S-b0)]
                 <=12h_max^(-3)+1/[exp(1)(S-b0)].     (18)

The denominator S-b0 is positive. This bound holds uniformly in the
curvature 0<kappa<1/h_max and in every feasible amplitude T. In particular
it covers the explicit repair (9) and exact maximal unqueried-terminal
completion. Every queried-prefix constraint, especially (14), is retained.

As m tends to infinity, S tends to infinity and b0 stays bounded. Also

    M_m<=1+n h_max<2^m h_max,
    h_max>(127/128)lambda^(m-2),
    M_m/h_max^3 < 2^m/h_max^2 ->0.

The last limit follows from 2/lambda^2<1. Equations (16),(18) therefore
give the explicit leading-scale bounds

    limsup M_m P_assigned <=1/[2 exp(1)],
    limsup M_m P_completed <=1/exp(1)<1.              (19)

Hence this whole monotone single-quadratic-coordinate repair mechanism
cannot supply a witness separating the schedule's actual worst case from
the proposed objective level 1/M_m. Its canonical repaired functions have
a genuine unique minimizer, so this failure is not caused by a loose choice
of normalization point. It is caused by the retained adjacent queried
pair (4), which forces the normalization cost (14).

## 6. Exact scope and the remaining repair requirement

The constructive statement covers the original C55 formal trajectory
with one monotone quadratic auxiliary coordinate and the explicit
conjugate function (10). The necessary cost (14) does not depend on the
values, while the unique-minimizer assertion is proved for the two
canonical functions with assigned prefix values: the full-jet interpolant
and its maximal unqueried-terminal completion. For arbitrary different
prefix values or different interpolants, (18) concerns the specified
minimizer zero; it does not silently assert that zero is their closest
minimizer.

No assertion is made about oscillating auxiliary coordinates, multiple
independent repair directions, a changed first-coordinate trajectory,
different knot/value rules, or a completely different adversary. The
result also does not claim that every fixed-dimensional witness has this
cost. The curvature restriction 0<kappa<1/h_max is essential to this
particular monotone repair and is displayed throughout.

The original target quantifies over arbitrary nonnegative schedules,
including zeros and unbounded positive steps. The present construction
uses a strictly positive schedule with growing bridges; it does not
replace those quantifiers. The appended zero step is only a precise way
to apply the already accepted full-prefix interpolation theorem.

For the next primal repair, a concrete requirement is now visible: the
auxiliary coordinates must supply order-one adjacent co-coercivity at
the rightmost H2 defect without paying order kappa^(-3) initial energy,
or the scalar gradients at that pair must be changed. This is a test of
a proposed new construction, not a theorem-equivalent claim that such a
repair exists or has negligible cost.

All new claims here remain draft evidence. There is no new accepted fact,
no unrestricted upper bound for W_n(H_m), and no resolution of the exact
Zhang--Jiang profile problem.
