# A double-zero Newton chain with a tilted projection realization

Status: complete UNVERIFIED candidate for a precisely stated growing-span
class, plus an explicit open positive-height interface. No optimization,
installation or fact_submit. The only fact inputs are 1252b8823bb5a290
(all-pair interpolation and its explicit function construction) and
b98bb807d514e80d (the exact benchmark recursions). All new claims below are
proved within this joint draft. This is not the original all-schedule target.

## 1. Actual chronology and the surviving double-zero representation

Fix m>=128 and, throughout this horizon, keep

 lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
 d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j),
 n=2^m-1, q=n-1.

Let h_0,...,h_(q-1) be H_m with its last d_0 removed. Queries are0,...,q;
the final step b is any number in[0,2], including the original b=d_0. Write

 s_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, S=s_q, P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z),
 mu_j=1/d_j, p_ij=P_i(mu_j).

Also write S_j=sum H_j, so S_total=S_m and S=S_m-d_0. Useful elementary
bounds are12/5<c<5/2,3/8<a<1/2 and11/8<d_0<3/2. To check them, use
12/5<1+sqrt2<17/7 and m>=128: c<2193/896<5/2 and
a>(127/128)/(5/2)=127/320>3/8. The other bounds follow immediately.
The ratios d_j/d_(j+1) decrease with j because (1+u)/(1+cu) decreases in u;
their initial value is less than(3/2)/(2-1/128)=192/255<4/5.

Consider the real polynomial quotient

                 chi(z)=z^2 product_(j=0)^(m-1)(z-mu_j).       (1)

Its dimension is m+2, and it contains the double-zero direction which is NOT
annihilated by the schedule. Every real linear map from this quotient has
unique vector coefficients u,v,w_0,...,w_(m-1) such that

 T[p]=u p(0)+v p'(0)+sum_j d_j w_j p(mu_j).

Indeed the evaluation/derivative map into these m+2 coordinates is injective:
its kernel consists of polynomials divisible by chi; on degree<m+2 the
kernel is zero. Equality of dimensions makes it an isomorphism. The positive
factors d_j only rescale these coordinates.

Thus the actual common-quotient data are exactly

 R_i=sum_j p_ij w_j, Z_i=sum_j d_j p_ij w_j,
 x_i=u-s_i v+Z_i, g_i=v+R_i, ||x_0||=||u+Z_0||=1.     (2)

All vectors are real and their common Gram matrix may be ANY PSD matrix,
including arbitrary initial correlations and singular limits. No mode is
assumed individually legal and no metric is assumed diagonal.
The polynomial identity for P_(i+1) proves x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i.

The first occurrence of d_j has step index2^j-1. Hence

 p_ij>0 for0<=i<2^j, and p_ij=0 for i>=2^j.            (3)

Before that first occurrence all steps are strictly less than d_j, so all
factors are positive. At that occurrence a zero factor appears and remains.
In particular every R_i and Z_i vanishes for i>=2^(m-1). These queries form
the genuine constant-gradient suffix x_i=u-s_i v, g_i=v.

For arbitrary shared values f_i, the complete nonstar interpolation law is

 f_i-f_j+<v+R_i,(s_i-s_j)v+Z_j-Z_i>
                                  +||R_i-R_j||^2/2<=0.        (4)

The optimum constraints are

 ||v+R_i||^2/2<=f_i
       <=<v+R_i,u-s_i v+Z_i>-||v+R_i||^2/2.            (5)

Every ordered pair in (4) remains. These are exactly the accepted fact's
inequalities, so together with a real Gram realization they are sufficient
for ONE actual convex1-smooth interpolant, including every queried value and
the optimum. This is a restricted m+2-dimensional temporal system, not the
unrestricted n+1-node reparameterization of the original problem.

## 2. A definite function-realization proposal: tilted squared distance

For the chosen mechanism define

                 y_i=x_i-R_i=u-s_i v+sum_j(d_j-1)p_ij w_j.

Choose the shared values

                    f_i=||R_i||^2/2+<v,x_i>-||v||^2/2.       (6)

At the optimum set R_star=-v and y_star=v; formula(6) still gives f_star=0
at x_star=0. Substituting (6) into every original Q_ij gives the exact law

                   Q_ij=<R_i,y_j-y_i><=0              (7)

for ALL ordered pairs i,j in {star,0,...,q}. In particular the original
optimum constraints are retained, rather than imposed separately on modes.

When (7) holds, let C=conv{v,y_0,...,y_q}. For any query i and any c in C,
<R_i,c-y_i><=0. Since x_i=y_i+R_i,

 ||x_i-c||^2=||R_i||^2+||c-y_i||^2-2<R_i,c-y_i>
                                                >=||R_i||^2.

Thus the Euclidean projection of x_i onto C is y_i. The star condition
likewise says that the projection of0 onto C is v. Consequently the actual
function

             F_C(x)=dist(x,C)^2/2+<v,x>-||v||^2/2       (8)

interpolates ALL the prescribed jets and has minimum zero at zero.

For completeness, Euclidean projections onto a closed convex set obey
<P_Cx-P_Cz,x-z>>=||P_Cx-P_Cz||^2, obtained by adding the two projection
normal inequalities. Therefore I-P_C is1-Lipschitz. Comparing the minimum
squared-distance expressions at x and x+d gives differentiability of
dist(x,C)^2/2 with gradient x-P_Cx. This function is convex, since joint
convexity of ||x-c||^2 and convexity of C give the convexity inequality after
taking minima over c. Addition of the linear term preserves convexity and
smoothness. Its gradient at0 is-v+v=0, proving the minimum assertion.

The actual minimizer set is also explicit. The star inequalities give
<v,c>>=||v||^2 for every c in C. Completing the square gives

 F_C(x)=min_(c in C){||x-(c-v)||^2/2+<v,c>-||v||^2}.

Hence argmin F_C={c-v:c in C,<v,c>=||v||^2}. One may require this face to be
the singleton{v}, or require0 to be the closest point in this set to x_0,
when normalizing by the TRUE closest-minimizer distance. The upper result
below holds with any designated minimizer0 and ||x_0||=1, and hence also
with that stronger true-distance convention. The lower calibration has a
unique minimizer, so its denominator is exactly the true distance.

The same obstruction applies to ANY convex1-smooth interpolant whose queried
values obey (6), not only to the particular representative (8). Only the
necessary all-pair law (7) is used in its proof.

## 3. Full obstruction: every level direction j>=2 vanishes

For EVERY legal data set (2),(6),

                       w_j=0 for all2<=j<m.            (9)

No linear independence or sign assumption on the w_j is used. This is an
actual interpolation obstruction, not a negative direction of a formal dual.

Prove(9) in descending order, starting with j=m-1. Assume w_ell=0 for every
ell>j and set

                  i=2^(j-1), l=i+1, p=p_ij.

For j>=2 these are both actual queries before the first d_j step is executed.
Every lower mode has already vanished by (3), so

 R_i=p w_j, R_l=p' w_j,
 p>0, p'=p(1-d_0/d_j)>0, s_l=s_i+d_0.                (10)

The last equality uses h_i=d_0: index2^(j-1) is even, so the next ruler
entry is level zero. All higher mode vectors vanish by the induction.

The two ACTUAL ordered inequalities (7) for i,l give

 p<w_j,y_l-y_i><=0,   -p'<w_j,y_l-y_i><=0.

Since p,p'>0, their scalar common factor must be zero. Expanding the actual
positions y gives

 <w_j,v>=-(1-1/d_j)p||w_j||^2.                        (11)

At the last queried index q, all modes have vanished, so y_q=u-Sv. The
actual REMOTE inequality (7) from i to q is therefore

 0>=<w_j,y_q-y_i>
   =-(S-s_i)<w_j,v>-(d_j-1)p||w_j||^2
   =(d_j-1)p||w_j||^2[(S-s_i)/d_j-1],                (12)

where (11) was substituted and the positive p factor in R_i was divided out.
But S-s_i>d_j: the retained suffix after query i includes the later first
d_j step and also the positive step h_i=d_0. The first d_j occurs before q,
even for j=m-1. Thus every factor in the last expression except ||w_j||^2
is strictly positive. It follows that w_j=0, closing the induction.

The remote pair i,q is load-bearing. Keeping only the adjacent pair would
give (11), not the contradiction. The residual's nonzero negative correlation
with v is explicitly allowed until the remote queried inequality rules it out.

After (9), (3) implies

                         g_i=v for EVERY i>=2.        (13)

Although the proposed temporal basis grew with m, legality has collapsed its
active directions to the two lowest levels and the double-zero block.

## 4. Quantitative full-class objective and an actual nonquadratic calibration

Let

        T_mass=S-d_0-d_1=sum H_m-2d_0-d_1.

For every b in[0,2], every legal transcript in this class and EVERY convex
1-smooth interpolant of its queried jets satisfy

       2F(x_q-b g_q)<=1/[2T_mass+1+b(2-b)].            (14)

The first two actual steps are d_0 in(11/8,3/2) and d_1=2-1/m in(0,2).
Adding the two optimum interpolation inequalities gives <g_i,x_i>>=||g_i||^2.
Thus for h in[0,2],

 ||x_i-hg_i||^2<=||x_i||^2-h(2-h)||g_i||^2<=||x_i||^2.

It follows that ||x_2||<=1. By(13), x_q=x_2-T_mass v. The optimum inequality
at q and final-step smoothness then imply, with t=||v||,

 2F(x_q-bv)<=2<v,x_2>-[2T_mass+1+b(2-b)]||v||^2
            <=2t-[2T_mass+1+b(2-b)]t^2.

Completing the scalar square proves(14). This includes the original b=d_0
and does not constrain the gradient at the unqueried final point.

The class is nonempty, genuinely nonquadratic, and asymptotically attains the
Huber scale. Put S_total=sum H_m, p=1/(2S_total+1), x_0=1, u=1, v=p and
all w_j=0. Choose C=[p,1] in R. Formula(8) gives

                   F_C(x)=dist(x,[p,1])^2/2+px-p^2/2.

This single function is convex and1-smooth with UNIQUE minimizer0: the face
minimizing pc over C is the singleton{p}. Every actual iterate of H_m lies in
[p,1], since x_i=1-p sum_(t<i)h_t and x_n=(S_total+1)/(2S_total+1)>p.
All queried gradients are p, all values have the required form(6), the
initial distance is exactly1, and the normalized final objective is

                            2F_C(x_n)=1/(2S_total+1).  (15)

No quadratic with minimum at0 has the same nonzero gradient at two distinct
scalar queries. Thus the data are nonquadratic. This is a calibration of the
obstruction, not a new improved lower-bound mechanism. Combining(14),(15)
shows the exact supremum over this class is Huber-tight up to a factor
1+O(1/S_total) at the original final step.

## 5. Comparison with the EXACT B_n, with every new bound proved

Keep B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 and U_n^ZJ=1/B_n exactly as defined in accepted
b98bb807d514e80d. For this class the exact ratio is bounded by

                     B_n/[2T_mass+1+b(2-b)].          (16)

Here is a self-contained sufficient upper envelope for this exact expression;
it is not a replacement of the target profile. Put rho=log_2 lambda>1 and
C_k=S_circle(k)+1. The accepted recursions are

 C_n=max_(k+l=n-1)Omega(C_k,C_l),
 Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
 B_n=max_(k+l=n-1)G(C_k,B_l),
 G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,
 C_0=B_0=1.

We first prove C_n<=(n+1)^rho. For t>0 define D(t)=(1+t)^rho-1 and
g(z)=log D(exp z). Direct differentiation, with t=exp z, gives

 g''(z)=rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)
           [(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/D(t)^2>0.

The bracket is positive because it is zero at t=0 and has positive derivative
rho[(1+t)^(rho-1)-1] for t>0. Hence g(z)+g(-z)>=2g(0), or

 D(t)D(1/t)>=(2^rho-1)^2=2.

For x,y>0 put u=x^(1/rho), w=y^(1/rho), Z=(u+w)^rho. This inequality gives
(Z-x)(Z-y)>=2xy, so Z^2-(x+y)Z-xy>=0. Also Z>=x+y, by the increasing
derivative of (u+w)^rho-u^rho in u. Thus Z lies above the positive quadratic
root Omega(x,y), proving Omega(u^rho,w^rho)<=(u+w)^rho. Zero arguments follow
by substitution. Induction in the C recurrence proves the claimed envelope.

Next sqrt(y^2+8xy)<=y+4x for x,y>=0 gives G(x,y)<=y+4x. Using
l^rho+(k+1)^rho<=(l+k+1)^rho for rho>=1, induction proves

                         B_n<=1+4n^rho.               (17)

All recursions and constants refer to the actual B_n; no unverified comparator
from another finding is being adopted as a lemma.

Counting the ruler levels gives

 1+S_j=A_mass c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j, 0<=j<=m,
 A_mass=a/(c-2) in(0,1), A_mass->1.

Indeed ac<1=lambda(lambda-2)<c(c-2), proving A_mass<1. Since
c^m/lambda^m=(1+1/m)^m->exp(1) and2/lambda<1,

             S_total/lambda^m->exp(1),
             T_mass/lambda^m->exp(1).                 (18)

At n=2^m-1, (17) gives B_n<=1+4lambda^m. Equations(16)--(18) therefore imply

 limsup_(m->infinity) B_n sup_class 2F(x_q-b g_q)
                               <=2/exp(1)<1,          (19)

uniformly for b in[0,2]. This completes a full obstruction at the EXACT
benchmark scale for the selected tilted-projection growing-span class.
It is not a theorem about all legal data in the double-zero quotient(1).

## 6. What survives: positive joint heights and their exact first charge

The collapse proof depends precisely on the value law(6). It does not extend
automatically to arbitrary jointly legal values, including positive offsets.
The surviving interface can be stated exactly without dropping any pairs.

For arbitrary legal values in (2), let

 C_min=f_q-<v,x_q>,
 delta_i=f_i-<v,x_i>-C_min-||R_i||^2/2,
 delta_star=-C_min-||v||^2/2.

The tilted function F(x)-<v,x> has gradient zero at every constant-gradient
suffix query and therefore has global minimum C_min there. Its smooth-convex
optimum inequality implies delta_i>=0 for every query, delta_star>=0, and
delta_i=0 on the constant-gradient suffix. At star set R_star=-v,y_star=v.
The ENTIRE original interpolation system becomes

              delta_i-delta_j+<R_i,y_j-y_i><=0         (20)

for all ordered pairs, together with the stated relation defining
delta_star. The scalar C_min, all these heights and all common vectors belong
to the SAME function. Independent mode-wise values cannot replace them.

Here is a quantitative necessary cost showing how a height can avoid the
zero-height collapse. Suppose some level j>=2 is isolated at the two queries
i=2^(j-1), l=i+1 as in (10), so higher mode vectors are zero. Write

 d=d_j, D=d-1, Delta=d_0, p=p_ij, p'=p(1-Delta/d),
 Vw=<v,w_j>, Bw=||w_j||^2, T_i=S-s_i>d,
 zeta=Vw+(D/d)p Bw.

Expanding (20) for both i,l gives EXACTLY

       Delta p' zeta<=delta_i-delta_l<=Delta p zeta.   (21)

Since p>p'>0, this forces zeta>=0. The actual remote pair i,q gives

              delta_i<=p[T_i zeta-Dp Bw(T_i/d-1)].     (22)

As delta_i>=0, (22) implies
zeta>=(D/d)p Bw(1-d/T_i). Combining with delta_l>=0 and(21) proves

 delta_i>=Delta p'p (D/d)(1-d/T_i)||w_j||^2.           (23)

Every displayed factor in this charge is strictly positive. At zero heights,
it forces w_j=0, agreeing with Section3. With arbitrary positive heights it
is a necessary cost, not an impossibility theorem: that cost could be paid
by the same global function's value budget. No bound on that simultaneous
budget, and no benchmark-scale construction paying it, has yet been proved.

The entire isolated right block gives a stronger, scale-dependent charge.
Let I=2^(j-1), J=2^j-1, assume all higher w_ell vanish, and write
p_t=P_t(mu_j), p_I=P_I(mu_j), p_J=P_J(mu_j), T_J=S-s_J. Every query from I through J has
residual p_t w_j, and all the intervening steps comprise the actual H_(j-1).
For each such step h_t, the same two-pair calculation gives

 delta_t-delta_(t+1)
    >=h_t p_(t+1) [Vw+(D/d)p_t Bw].

The remote inequality J,q and delta_J>=0 give Vw>=-D p_J Bw/T_J.
Since p_t>=p_J and T_J>d, summing yields

 delta_I >= (D/d)(1-d/T_J) Bw sum_(t=I)^(J-1)h_t p_t p_(t+1).

Every intervening h_t/d is at most4/5. Hence p_(t+1)>=p_t/5, while
p_t^2-p_(t+1)^2<=(2h_t/d)p_t^2. The last sum is at least
(d/10)(p_I^2-p_J^2). Therefore

 delta_I >= (d-1)(1-d/T_J)(p_I^2-p_J^2)||w_j||^2/10.  (24)

In particular there is an absolute explicit lower charge at the scale d_j:

                delta_(2^(j-1))>=exp(-28)d_j||w_j||^2/320.  (25)

Here are bounds establishing this constant without a computation. The word
identities in Section5 give S_j< c^j, while d_j>(3/8)c^j; thus S_j/d_j<8/3.
Every step before d_j is at most (4/5)d_j. Integrating the derivative of
log(1-t) gives log(1-t)>=-5t for0<=t<=4/5, so
p_J>=exp(-40/3)>exp(-14). Also
p_J/p_I=P_(H_(j-1))(mu_j)<=exp(-S_(j-1)/d_j)<=exp(-4/25),
because S_(j-1)>=d_(j-2) and d_j<c^2 d_(j-2)<(25/4)d_(j-2).
The elementary bound exp(8/25)>=1+8/25+(8/25)^2/2>4/3 proves
p_I^2-p_J^2>=p_J^2/4>=exp(-28)/4.

The retained suffix after the first d_j includes d_j and at least
S_j-d_0>d_(j-1)>(2/5)d_j of further mass, even if its last d_0 is omitted.
Thus T_J>(7/5)d_j and1-d_j/T_J>2/7>1/4. Finally d_j>2 for j>=2, so
d_j-1>d_j/2. Substituting these three bounds into(24) proves(25).
It charges the largest active isolated level to a positive value height.
It does not yet add charges over lower levels in the presence of higher
nonzero vectors, and it does not bound the initial common value budget.

For clarity, on the constant-gradient suffix all values are exactly
f_i=f_q+(S-s_i)||v||^2, because adding and reversing the interpolation
inequalities between two equal-gradient queries forces equality. For each old
anchor the two directional Q expressions are constant or affine in s_i.
Thus retaining BOTH endpoints of that suffix suffices for its comparisons
with any earlier anchor; every earlier/earlier pair is still required.
The same endpoint statement holds for the maximum of conjugate jet quadratics
in the explicit realization. It does not delete any remote earlier pair.

The original problem remains unresolved. The next concrete question in this
lane is whether nonzero joint heights can pay (21)--(25) through multiple
levels while preserving every old pair and ||u+sum d_jw_j||=1, and produce
the required terminal objective relative to the actual B_n. Another
zero-height or independent-value construction cannot answer that question.

The earlier no-linear-term squared-distance/cone exclusions do not cover
this proposal: the actual gradients here are v+R_i and the minimum belongs
to the tilted function (8). The proof instead uses its exact ordered
interpolation law. Matlas retrieval for collinear normals returned a
self-contracted-curve lemma and cone projection results; none is imported.
No additional external theorem is needed, since the branch reduced to the
already audited all-pair interface in fact1252 and the elementary projection
calculation explicitly proved above. The optional strict-cycle smoothing

# C57: nonlinear ordered repairs have exactly the Huber leading scale

Status: **complete scoped proof candidate; not verifier-accepted**.
No optimization, installation, or fact submission is allocated. The only
accepted mathematical predecessor used below is `1252b8823bb5a290`, for
the necessity and sufficiency of smooth-convex interpolation inequalities
and their explicit conjugate interpolant. Everything specific to the
trajectory, the repair, and its quantitative bound is proved here.

This continues the actual-primal lane. It enlarges the previous single
monotone quadratic auxiliary coordinate to arbitrarily many nonlinear
coordinates, and even to vectors ordered by any fixed acute cone. It gives
an explicit all-pair legal repair and identifies the sharp leading payoff
of the whole stated class. It does not upper-bound unrestricted W_n(H_m).

## 1. The actual schedule and the scalar data that are kept

Fix an integer m>=128, and define

    epsilon=1/m, lambda=1+sqrt(2),
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c,
    d_j=a c^j,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+d_j,H_j).

Let h=H_m, n=2^m-1, S=sum_(t<n)h_t, M=S+1. Define

    b0=1+a, b1=1+d_1=2-epsilon.

The rightmost three steps are (b0,b1,b0). Every step exceeds one.
In particular S>=n, so S tends to infinity with m. The elementary bounds
needed below are

    1<b0<sqrt(2), 1<b1<2, 7/3<c<5/2, d_1+c>3.       (1)

Indeed a<(1+sqrt(2))^(-1)=sqrt(2)-1; d_1=1-epsilon;
c>1+sqrt(2)>12/5; and, using sqrt(2)<10/7,
c<(17/7)(129/128)<5/2. Since epsilon<=1/128, these also
give d_1+c>3.

Here is a complete definition of the scalar formal transcript. Put

    M_2=1+2b0+b1, k_2=M_2+6epsilon,
    k_(j+1)=-k_j^2/d_j, j>=2.

For an H_2 block with terminal scalar gradient v, use successive gradients

    ((2-c+6epsilon/b0)v, v, c v, v),                 (2)

start at k_2 v, and use the three actual GD steps (b0,b1,b0).
The last entry in (2) is the block's endpoint gradient. Its endpoint is v,
because

    b0(2-c+6epsilon/b0)+b1+b0 c+1=k_2.

For H_(j+1), give the right H_j child terminal gradient v and the left
child terminal gradient -k_j v/d_j; start the parent at k_(j+1)v.
The left endpoint is -k_j v/d_j. The bridge 1+d_j moves it to k_j v,
the right child's required start. The right endpoint is v. This verifies
the full chronological GD recursion inductively.

Choose root terminal gradient 1. Denote the resulting scalar positions
by x_i and gradients by g_i, 0<=i<=n. Thus

    x_0=k_m, x_n=g_n=1,
    x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i.

Set y_i=x_i-g_i; in particular y_n=0. No legality is asserted for these
scalar data. We keep x_i for all i, and g_i for the QUERIED indices i<n,
when adding auxiliary coordinates. The final gradient and value may be
chosen freely by a legal interpolating function.

The two final queried indices r=n-2 and s=n-1 satisfy

    g_r=1, g_s=c, x_r-x_s=b1, x_s=1+b0 c.

For the normalized interpolation residual

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2,

their scalar contribution to Q_rs+Q_sr is, for EVERY choice of values,

    D=(c-1)^2+b1(c-1)=(c-1)(d_1+c)>4.              (3)

This pair is inside the queried prefix. Terminal completion cannot
delete it.

## 2. The ordered auxiliary class, including its distance convention

Work in any finite auxiliary Euclidean dimension q>=1, which may depend
arbitrarily on m. Let K be a convex cone that is acute:

    <u,v>>=0 for every u,v in K.

No assertion is made that every cone has this property. The nonnegative
orthant is an example. Consider data

    X_i=(x_i,z_i), 0<=i<=n,
    G_i=(g_i,p_i), 0<=i<n,
    z_(i+1)=z_i-h_i p_i.

Require

    z_i in K for 0<=i<=n,
    p_i in K for 0<=i<n,
    p_t-p_i in K for every 0<=t<i<n.                (4)

These are constraints on the auxiliary coordinates of one JOINT
trajectory. They do not require a separable objective, independent
one-dimensional auxiliary functions, a fixed rank, a quadratic model,
or prescribed function values. For the orthant, (4) means nonnegative
positions and nonnegative, coordinatewise nonincreasing queried gradients.

Assume these queried jets arise from ONE convex differentiable 1-smooth
function F with F(0)=0=min F. Initially write

    R^2=||X_0||^2=k_m^2+||z_0||^2,
    P=2F(X_n)/R^2.

The bound below always holds with this specified-minimizer normalization.
For a statement about the true closest-minimizer distance, explicitly
require that 0 is a closest minimizer to X_0. The constructions in
Sections 4 and 5 have a UNIQUE minimizer 0, so their R is exactly the
true distance. No automatic closest-minimizer claim is made for arbitrary
other interpolants.

The final gradient is unrestricted. In particular the class allows the
pointwise maximal unqueried-terminal completion of any legal prefix
that satisfies (4), whenever the stated normalization condition holds.

## 3. A uniform upper bound for the entire class

Put

    N=S-b0-b1=sum_(t<r)h_t,
    C=1+2b0-b0^2,
    A=2c+(b0^2-1)c^2,
    D0=2S+1-b0^2.

All of N,C,D0 are positive, and 0<A<12 by (1).

First add the two necessary interpolation inequalities for r and s.
Write Delta=p_r-p_s. The actual step has auxiliary displacement
z_r-z_s=b1 p_r. Combining its contribution with (3) gives

    D<=b1<p_r,Delta>-||Delta||^2
       =b1^2||p_r||^2/4-||Delta-(b1/2)p_r||^2.

Consequently

    ||p_r||^2>=4D/b1^2.                             (5)

This necessary bound uses no ordering assumptions and no function values.
The ordering assumption next makes the cost accumulate over the actual
earlier steps:

    z_0-N p_r=z_r+sum_(t<r)h_t(p_t-p_r) in K.

Since p_r is in K and K is acute, expansion of the squared norm yields

    ||z_0||^2>=N^2||p_r||^2,
    R^2>=4D N^2/b1^2>4N^2.                         (6)

For the objective, interpolation at the last query with the optimum and
smoothness on the actual last step give, respectively,

    F(X_s)<=<G_s,X_s>-||G_s||^2/2,
    F(X_n)<=F(X_s)-b0(1-b0/2)||G_s||^2.

These are necessary for every legal completion, with no terminal gradient
assumed. Adding and inserting the displayed scalar last-query data gives

    2F(X_n)<=A+2<p_s,z_s>-C||p_s||^2.               (7)

For t<s, acuteness and p_t-p_s in K imply
<p_t,p_s>>=||p_s||^2. Therefore

    <z_s,p_s>
      =<z_0,p_s>-sum_(t<s)h_t<p_t,p_s>
      <=<z_0,p_s>-(S-b0)||p_s||^2.

Equation (7) becomes

    2F(X_n)<=A+2<z_0,p_s>-D0||p_s||^2
             <=A+||z_0||^2/D0,                     (8)

where the final inequality is the exact completion of the square in p_s.
Dividing by R^2 and using (6) proves the uniform bound

    P <= 1/(2S+1-b0^2) + A b1^2/(4D N^2)
      < 1/(2S+1-b0^2) + 3/(S-b0-b1)^2.             (9)

Since b0,b1 stay bounded and M=S+1, it follows that

    limsup_(m->infinity) M P <= 1/2                 (10)

uniformly over all dimensions, acute cones, jointly legal function values,
and final completions in this class, with the distance convention stated
in Section 2. This is stronger in scope than a fixed-curvature analysis:
there is no curvature parameter in (5)--(10).

## 4. An explicit nonlinear repair of EVERY interpolation pair

The class in Section 2 is nonempty for the actual scalar formal transcript.
Here is an analytic construction with a closed rule and a closed initial
distance formula. It is not a nearest-feasible-point optimization.

Define finite scalars

    Gmax=max(1,max_(0<=i<=n)|g_i|),
    w_l=Gmax|y_(l+1)-y_l|+1,
    u_l=sqrt(2w_l/(h_l-1)),       0<=l<n.

Use n auxiliary coordinates, one for each chronological cut l. In
coordinate l define the 1/h_l-smooth, convex, differentiable function

    psi_l(t)=0                              if t<=0,
             t^2/(2h_l)                    if 0<=t<=h_l u_l,
             u_l t-h_l u_l^2/2              if t>=h_l u_l.

Its two joining values and derivatives agree. Its derivative is
nondecreasing and is Lipschitz with constant 1/h_l<1. Prescribe

    z_i^(l)=u_l sum_(v=i)^l h_v, p_i^(l)=u_l,   if i<=l,
    z_i^(l)=0,                  p_i^(l)=0,     if i>=l+1.

The auxiliary GD recursion holds at every step, including the extinction
step l: its position before that step is h_l u_l and its position after
the step is zero. Earlier sample positions lie in the affine branch of
psi_l. The positions and gradients lie in the nonnegative orthant, and
each gradient decreases exactly once, to zero. Thus (4) holds.

Now prescribe full-vector jets and values, including the terminal,

    X_i=(x_i,z_i), G_i=(g_i,p_i),
    f_i=g_i^2/2+sum_(l<n)psi_l(z_i^(l)), 0<=i<=n,
    X_star=G_star=0, f_star=0.                      (11)

The scalar expression g_i^2/2 is not asserted to come from a legal
one-dimensional function. The final function will be a joint interpolant.

Here is the complete interpolation law. The scalar part of Q_ij is

    g_i(y_j-y_i).

For two finite indices i<j, an auxiliary coordinate with l<i or l>=j
contributes zero in BOTH directions. A cut i<=l<j contributes

    Q_ij^(l)=-w_l,
    Q_ji^(l)=-w_l-u_l^2 sum_(v=i)^(l-1)h_v.        (12)

To verify (12), the earlier point has gradient u_l and value
u_l z_i^(l)-h_l u_l^2/2, whereas the later point has zero position,
gradient, and value. Direct substitution into Q gives the two formulas;
the sum in the second is empty if l=i.

The triangle inequality supplies

    |g_i(y_j-y_i)|, |g_j(y_i-y_j)|
       <=Gmax sum_(l=i)^(j-1)|y_(l+1)-y_l|.

By the definition of w_l, (12) therefore makes BOTH full residuals at
most -(j-i)<0. This checks every distinct finite pair, including pairs
with the terminal; it is not only an adjacent-pair check.

For the optimum pair and i<n, the scalar contributions are

    Q_(i,star)^scalar=-g_i y_i,
    Q_(star,i)^scalar=0.

Because y_n=0, |g_i y_i|<=Gmax sum_(l=i)^(n-1)|y_(l+1)-y_l|.
In each l>=i the forward auxiliary contribution is -w_l, and the reverse
one is -w_l-u_l^2 sum_(v=i)^(l-1)h_v. All l<i contributions are zero.
Thus both optimum residuals are strictly negative. At the terminal,
X_n=G_n=(1,0,...,0), f_n=1/2, and the two optimum residuals are zero.
All ordered interpolation inequalities for (11) have now been checked.

For completeness the actual function is explicit. Let

    Y_i=X_i-G_i, delta_i=f_i-||G_i||^2/2,
    H(v)=||v||^2/2+max_(i in {star,0,...,n})
                            [<Y_i,v>-delta_i],
    F_base(X)=sup_v[<X,v>-H(v)].                    (13)

By accepted fact `1252b8823bb5a290`, this is an everywhere finite convex
differentiable 1-smooth function with all the prescribed jets and the
same actual GD trajectory. It has a UNIQUE minimizer 0, as can also be
checked from (13): for i<n, the l=i term contributes w_i>0 to delta_i,
and every other term is nonnegative. Hence delta_i>0. The star and terminal
have Y=0 and delta=0. In a neighborhood of v=0 their zero affine function
strictly dominates every nonzero queried affine function. Thus H(v)
equals ||v||^2/2 in that neighborhood and its subgradient at 0 is {0}.
The maximizing-vector characterization of (13), proved in the accepted
predecessor, identifies the minimizers of F_base with this subgradient.

Consequently the true squared initial distance is exactly

    R_base^2=k_m^2+
        sum_(l=0)^(n-1) [2w_l/(h_l-1)]
                              [sum_(v=0)^l h_v]^2. (14)

The exact normalized objective is 1/R_base^2. This pure extinction repair
loses the formal large payoff: (6) yields 1/R_base^2<1/(4N^2).
Nevertheless it is a fully specified actual legal object with one common
function, all values, all gradients, and the true initial distance.

## 5. The coefficient 1/2 is sharp for the whole ordered repair class

The uniform upper bound (10) cannot be replaced by a smaller leading
constant for this class. Add one further coordinate to F_base, using the
symmetric Huber function with threshold tau>0,

    Huber_tau(t)=t^2/2                     if |t|<=tau,
                 tau|t|-tau^2/2            if |t|>=tau.

This function is convex and differentiable, its derivative is 1-Lipschitz,
and its minimizer is uniquely 0. Choose any amplitude T>0 and put

    tau=T/(2S+1), z_i^H=T-tau sum_(t<i)h_t.

All sampled positions, including the terminal, exceed tau because
z_n^H=T(S+1)/(2S+1)>tau. All its queried gradients therefore equal tau.
The actual recursion and the nonnegative ordering requirements hold.

On the enlarged space use the direct sum

    F_total(X,t)=F_base(X)+Huber_tau(t).

It is convex and 1-smooth in the product Euclidean norm, as follows by
squaring and adding the separate gradient Lipschitz inequalities. Its
minimizer is uniquely 0, and its first-coordinate queried transcript is
unchanged. Its exact normalized payoff and true distance are

    P_T=[1+T^2/(2S+1)]/[R_base^2+T^2].              (15)

For fixed m, letting T tend to infinity yields 1/(2S+1). For an explicit
horizon-dependent choice take T^2=m R_base^2, which gives

    P_T>= [m/(m+1)]/(2S+1).

Let V_m denote the supremum of the true-distance-normalized payoff over
the ordered repair class of Section 2 with 0 a closest minimizer. The
explicit unique-minimizer examples above and (9) give

    1/(2S+1) <= V_m
       <= 1/(2S+1-b0^2)+3/(S-b0-b1)^2,

and therefore the exact class asymptotic

    lim_(m->infinity) M V_m = 1/2.                 (16)

The lower endpoint is a supremum assertion; no attainment at finite T is
claimed. The explicit T choice already suffices for the limiting lower
bound. This calibrates the obstruction against an actual legal function.

## 6. What a non-ordered repair would have to change

There are exact identities that expose the assumptions used above.
For arbitrary auxiliary positions and gradients obeying GD, define

    J=sum_(t<s)h_t <p_t-p_s,p_s>.

Equation (7), with no ordering assumption, gives

    2F(X_n)<=A+2<z_0,p_s>-D0||p_s||^2-2J
             <=A+||z_0||^2/D0-2J.                 (17)

For the earlier queried gradient define

    B=<z_r,p_r>+sum_(t<r)h_t<p_t-p_r,p_r>.

The exact GD identity is

    <z_0,p_r>=N||p_r||^2+B.                        (18)

In the ordered class J>=0 and B>=0. Equations (17)--(18) hold without
that class restriction, whereas the conclusions J>=0 and B>=0 do not.
For example, retaining the unit formal terminal payoff with R^2 of order
M would require, by (5),(18) and Cauchy--Schwarz,

    B <= R||p_r||-N||p_r||^2,

which is negative for all sufficiently large m whenever R=O(sqrt(M)).
Thus such a normalization-saving repair must supply genuine cancellation
in its cumulative positions/gradients, or modify the scalar queried data.
Similarly, if R^2/M tends to infinity and a family has M P>=1+eta for
some fixed eta>0, then (17) forces

    limsup [M J/R^2] <= -1/4-eta/2.                 (19)

To check (19), divide (17) by R^2, use ||z_0||^2<=R^2,
M/D0->1/2, and M A/R^2->0. This statement is a necessary condition,
not an existence claim for an escaping legal repair.

The original all-schedule profile goal remains open. Equation (16) only
diagnoses this fully specified repair class on this critical positive
schedule. It does not address arbitrary signed or turning auxiliary
gradients, changed first-coordinate queried trajectories, all possible
minimizer locations, or unrestricted smooth convex adversaries. It does
not replace the original zero-step or large-step quantifiers, and is not
a theorem about W_n(H_m). All new conclusions here remain unverified
draft evidence, pending an actual authorized verifier submission.

evidence:
# Joint positive heights with one anisotropic distance metric

Status: complete scoped UNVERIFIED proof candidate. No numerical optimization,
installation, or fact submission. The fact inputs are 1252b8823bb5a290
(smooth-convex interpolation and maximal completion) and b98bb807d514e80d
(the exact benchmark definitions). Every other assertion used below is proved
inside this package. In particular the sharper benchmark comparison is proved
again, rather than treating draft e3c8501149a5c47e as an accepted predecessor.

The class has ONE common positive-height matrix, ONE function, arbitrary
cross-mode and initial inner products, and all normal comparisons. It is a
specific policy for the open positive-height interface, not that entire
interface. The extra normal inequalities below are stronger than ordinary
1-smooth interpolation with the same displayed heights.

## 1. The physical word and the complete joint construction

Fix an integer m>=128 and keep these parameters fixed throughout the horizon:

 lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
 d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j),
 n=2^m-1, q=n-1, S_j=sum H_j.

The queried prefix h_0,...,h_(q-1) is H_m with its last d_0 removed. The
unqueried final step is b in [0,2], including the original b=d_0. Set

 s_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, S=s_q=S_m-d_0,
 p_ij=product_(t<i)(1-h_t/d_j), 0<=j<m.

Here d_0<1+1/lambda=sqrt(2)<3/2 and d_1=2-1/m<2. Also c>lambda>2,
so all d_j are strictly increasing and positive.

For arbitrary vectors u,v,w_0,...,w_(m-1) in a finite-dimensional REAL
Euclidean space define

 R_i=sum_j p_ij w_j, Z_i=sum_j d_j p_ij w_j,
 x_i=u-s_i v+Z_i, g_i=v+R_i, ||x_0||=||u+Z_0||=1.       (1)

There is no independence, orthogonality, or sign assumption on these vectors.
Their Gram matrix is any real PSD matrix, including singular ones. These are
the exact images of the polynomial quotient

                  z^2 product_(j=0)^(m-1)(z-1/d_j).

Indeed its evaluation coordinates p(0),p'(0),p(1/d_j) are independent: a
polynomial in their joint kernel is divisible by the displayed polynomial.
The functional T[p]=u p(0)+v p'(0)+sum_j d_j w_j p(1/d_j) therefore gives
x_i=T[P_i], g_i=T[z P_i], where P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z). The identity
P_(i+1)=(1-h_i z)P_i proves the exact GD recursion in (1).

The first d_j has step index 2^j-1. All preceding steps are smaller, and hence

 p_ij>0 for i<2^j, and p_ij=0 for i>=2^j.              (2)

Let A be ONE selfadjoint positive definite operator and tau its smallest
eigenvalue. The policy to be tested requires

                         I <= tau I <= A <= 2 tau I. (3)

Thus tau>=1. A may depend on m, have arbitrarily large scale, act in an
arbitrarily large space, and mix every mode. Its condition number is at most
two; no common eigenbasis with the w_j is assumed.

Put z_i=x_i-A R_i. At the optimum add

 x_star=0, g_star=0, R_star=-v, z_star=A v.

Require the ENTIRE normal array

       N_ij=<R_i,z_j-z_i> <=0, i,j in {star,0,...,q}. (4)

Let C=conv{z_star,z_0,...,z_q} and use the single actual function

 F_A(x)=min_(z in C) (x-z)^T A^(-1)(x-z)/2
                         +<v,x>-<v,A v>/2.          (5)

Its prescribed values are

       f_i=<v,x_i>-<v,A v>/2+<R_i,A R_i>/2.           (6)

They all use the same matrix A and the same offset. The tilted minimum is
C_min=-<v,A v>/2, because R_i=0 on the suffix after the highest active level.
The positive heights in the existing double-zero interface are exactly

 delta_i=(<R_i,A R_i>-||R_i||^2)/2,
 delta_star=(<v,A v>-||v||^2)/2.                     (7)

All these heights are nonnegative. In particular

 2 delta_i=sum_(j,k) p_ij p_ik <w_j,(A-I)w_k>.

Every cross term is retained; (7) is not a sum of independently chosen legal
modal values. The matrix of these cross terms is PSD because A-I is PSD,
but individual entries can have either sign.

For the original signed 1-smooth interpolation residual from fact1252,
substitution into (6) gives the exact ALL-pair law

 Q_ij=N_ij-<R_i-R_j,(A-I)(R_i-R_j)>/2 <=0.            (8)

The identity includes the optimum, whose value from (6) is zero. The proof
below uses (4), not merely Q_ij<=0. Consequently its conclusion must not be
extended to arbitrary legal values of form (7) without the normal condition.

## 2. Function realization, effective smoothness, and actual minimizers

For each sample i, (4) gives <R_i,z-z_i><=0 for every z in C. Since
x_i-z_i=A R_i,

 (x_i-z)^T A^(-1)(x_i-z)
  =<R_i,A R_i>+(z-z_i)^T A^(-1)(z-z_i)-2<R_i,z-z_i>
  >=<R_i,A R_i>.

Thus z_i is the unique A^(-1)-metric projection of x_i onto C, and (5)
interpolates the prescribed values and gradients. This also holds at star.

Here is a direct smoothness proof. For arbitrary x,y let their projections
be z_x,z_y, and residuals r_x=A^(-1)(x-z_x), r_y=A^(-1)(y-z_y).
Adding the two normal inequalities gives

 <r_x-r_y,z_x-z_y> >=0,
 <r_x-r_y,x-y> >= <r_x-r_y,A(r_x-r_y)>
                                      >=tau||r_x-r_y||^2.   (9)

Cauchy--Schwarz shows ||r_x-r_y||<=||x-y||/tau. Comparing the two minimum
expressions at x and x+d, first with z_x and then with z_(x+d), proves
differentiability of the squared metric distance with gradient r_x: the
upper error after subtracting <r_x,d> is at most ||d||^2/(2tau), and the
reverse comparison together with (9) bounds it below by
-3||d||^2/(2tau). Joint convexity of the squared norm and convexity of C prove
convexity after minimizing in z. Consequently F_A is convex and has gradient
Lipschitz constant at most 1/tau<=1. At zero its gradient is -v+v=0 and its
value is zero. It is everywhere finite.

The actual minimizer set is explicit. The star normal in (4) says
<v,z>>=<v,A v> on C. Completing the square in (5) gives

 F_A(x)=min_(z in C){||x-(z-A v)||_(A^(-1))^2/2
                                      +<v,z>-<v,A v>}.

Therefore

 argmin F_A={z-A v:z in C, <v,z>=<v,A v>}.             (10)

If normalization uses the closest minimizer, require zero to be the closest
point in (10) to x_0, or require the exposed face in (10) to be the singleton
{A v}. The upper result holds for every designated minimizer zero with
||x_0||=1 and hence also when zero is the closest minimizer. The example
below has a unique minimizer.

## 3. The highest active level forces a common curvature budget

Let j be the largest index for which w_j!=0. Suppose j>=2. Consider the TWO
actual queried points i=2^(j-1) and l=i+1. By (2), all lower modes are already
zero and all higher vectors are zero by the choice of j. Thus

 R_i=p w_j, R_l=p' w_j,
 p>0, p'=p(1-d_0/d_j)>0, s_l-s_i=d_0.                (11)

Write d=d_j, w=w_j, D=<w,(d I-A)w>, V=<v,w>. Then

 z_i=u-s_i v+p(d I-A)w,
 z_l=u-(s_i+d_0)v+p'(d I-A)w.

Both directions of (4) for i,l imply <w,z_l-z_i>=0, because their normals
are positive multiples of w. Expanding this equality gives

                            V=-p D/d.               (12)

At the last query q, every residual vanishes, so z_q=u-Sv. The RETAINED
remote normal from i to q gives

 0>=N_iq=p[-(S-s_i)V-pD]
              =p^2 D[(S-s_i)/d-1].                 (13)

The actual retained suffix after i contains the future first d_j step and
also the positive step h_i=d_0. These occur before q, even for j=m-1.
Hence S-s_i>d. Equations (12)--(13) force

                  <w,A w> >= d_j||w||^2,
                  d_j <=2tau.                      (14)

This is a JOINT curvature cost, not a sum of single-mode height charges.
Only the last active level is isolated. All other cross terms remain in
the common A and in (4). No sign of <v,w_k> for other levels is inferred.

For j>=3 there is a third positive-collinear query i+2 before annihilation.
Applying (12) to the next pair replaces p by p'!=p, so D=V=0. Thus the
stronger equality <w,A w>=d_j||w||^2 holds then. This refinement is not
needed for the upper bound; the two-query argument (14) covers j=2 too.

## 4. Whole-class terminal bound, including arbitrary 1-smooth completions

The effective smoothness of F_A and its optimum give, at every query,

               <g_i,x_i> >=tau||g_i||^2.             (15)

This follows by adding the two interpolation inequalities at smoothness
1/tau, a rescaling of the necessity calculation in fact1252. Therefore

 ||x_i-h_i g_i||^2
     <=||x_i||^2-h_i(2tau-h_i)||g_i||^2.              (16)

If j>=2, every step up to and including the first d_j is at most d_j<=2tau.
The whole actual prefix up to r=2^j consequently has ||x_r||<=1. All residuals
are zero from r onward, so with

                 T=S-s_r=S_m-d_0-S_j-d_j,

one has x_q=x_r-Tv and g_q=v. The value inequality at q, again using the
effective smoothness of F_A, gives

                     f_q<=<v,x_q>-tau||v||^2/2.      (17)

Now let F be ANY convex 1-smooth function interpolating all the prescribed
prefix jets and the optimum, not necessarily F_A. It has the same f_q and
g_q, so its unqueried last step obeys

 2F(x_q-bv)<=2f_q-b(2-b)||v||^2
       <=2<v,x_r>-[2T+tau+b(2-b)]||v||^2
       <=1/[2T+tau+b(2-b)], 0<=b<=2.                 (18)

The last inequality is the scalar square completion 2t-D t^2<=1/D, with
t=||v||, D=2T+tau+b(2-b)>0, and ||x_r||<=1. Thus the bound covers the
pointwise maximal 1-smooth completion supplied by accepted fact1252. No
effective-smoothness assumption is imposed on the unqueried extension.

Using tau>=d_j/2, and the increase of both S_j and d_j with j, (18) gives

 2T+tau+b(2-b)
  >=2S_m-2d_0-2S_j-3d_j/2
  >=2S_(m-1)+d_(m-1)/2-2d_0 =: D_m.                (19)

If no j>=2 is active, every residual vanishes at query2. The first two
steps are d_0<3/2 and d_1=2-1/m<2, while tau>=1, so (16) gives ||x_2||<=1.
The same proof of (18) works with T=S_m-2d_0-d_1. Its denominator is at least
2S_m-4d_0-2d_1+1. Subtracting D_m gives

       2S_(m-1)+3d_(m-1)/2-2d_0-2d_1+1>0,

because S_(m-1)>=S_2=2d_0+d_1. This also covers v=0 and the all-zero
residual case. All quantities in D_m are positive as needed for m>=128.

We have proved the UNIFORM whole-policy upper bound

     sup_(all data satisfying (1)--(4), all F completions, b in[0,2])
                      2F(x_q-b g_q) <=1/D_m.         (20)

No prescribed values, old interpolation pairs, initial correlations, or
terminal completion variables have been discarded in defining the class.

## 5. Strict comparison with the exact Zhang--Jiang benchmark

Keep B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 and U_n^ZJ=1/B_n exactly as in accepted b98bb807d514e80d.
Set P_n=S_circle(n)+1. Algebra in those recursions gives

 P_0=B_0=1,
 P_n=max_(k+l=n-1) Omega(P_k,P_l),
 B_n=max_(k+l=n-1) G(P_k,B_l),
 Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
 G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2.

Here is a full proof of the needed comparator. Put alpha=2lambda-1
=lambda(4-lambda)>0 and Llin=(4x+lambda^2 y)/alpha. Its coefficients exceed
one, so Llin>=x+y. Direct expansion using lambda^2=2lambda+1 gives

 alpha^2[Llin^2-(x+y)Llin-xy]
                         =(2x/lambda-sqrt(2)lambda y)^2>=0.

Since Omega is the positive root of z^2-(x+y)z-xy=0, Llin>=Omega(x,y).
At z=lambda Omega(x,y), the quadratic whose larger root is G(x,lambda y)
therefore satisfies

 z^2-(4x+lambda y)z+4x^2
                =x[4x+lambda^2 y-alpha Omega(x,y)]>=0.

Also z>=lambda(x+y)>=(4x+lambda y)/2, placing it to the right of the
quadratic's vertex. Thus G(x,lambda y)<=lambda Omega(x,y) for x,y>=0.
Monotonicity of G in y and induction prove

                             B_n<=lambda P_n.       (21)

For completeness put rho=log_2 lambda>1, Dpow(t)=(1+t)^rho-1 and
ell(z)=log Dpow(exp z). With t=exp z, differentiation gives

 ell''(z)=rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)
          [(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/Dpow(t)^2>0.

The bracket is zero at t=0 and has positive derivative for t>0. Convexity
of ell implies Dpow(t)Dpow(1/t)>=Dpow(1)^2=2. For x,y>0 and
Z=(x^(1/rho)+y^(1/rho))^rho, this implies
(Z-x)(Z-y)>=2xy, so Z^2-(x+y)Z-xy>=0. Also Z>=x+y, as follows by
integrating the increasing derivative of t^rho. Hence Omega(x,y)<=Z;
zero arguments follow by substitution. Induction in P gives
P_n<=(n+1)^rho. Balanced joins at n=2^m-1 give equality there. Consequently

                         B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^(m+1).   (22)

The exact physical mass satisfies

 1+S_j=A_mass c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j,
 A_mass=a/(c-2) ->1.

This follows by solving 1+S_(j+1)=2(1+S_j)+a c^j with S_0=0.
Since c^m/lambda^m=(1+1/m)^m->exp(1),

 S_(m-1)/lambda^(m-1)->exp(1),
 d_(m-1)/lambda^(m-1)->exp(1)/lambda,
 D_m/lambda^(m-1)->exp(1)(lambda+2)/2.               (23)

Combining the EXACT ratio bound B_n/D_m with (22)--(23) proves

 limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) sup_policy,completions,b 2F(x_q-b g_q)
                <=2lambda^2/[exp(1)(lambda+2)]<1.    (24)

The strict gap requires no decimal calculation. The exponential series gives
exp(1)>8/3, and lambda<17/7<5/2. Thus the right side of (24) is strictly less
than 3lambda^2/[4(lambda+2)]=(6lambda+3)/(4lambda+8)<123/124.
The middle rational function is increasing, as its derivative is
36/(4lambda+8)^2>0. All comparisons retain the exact B_n; no benchmark
asymptotic equality was assumed.

## 6. Positive-height nonquadratic calibration at the largest actual level

The policy is not forced to have zero heights or constant queried gradients.
This calibration is not a sharp lower adversary and is not offered as one.
Let d=d_(m-1), tau=d/2>1, U=sqrt(3)/2, epsilon=1/(2d),

 A=diag(d,tau), v=(0,p), p=U/(2S_m+tau),
 u=(0,U), w_(m-1)=(epsilon,0), w_j=0 for j<m-1.

Then x_0=(1/2,U) has norm1, A obeys (3), and

 x_i=(d epsilon p_(i,m-1), U-s_i p),
 g_i=(epsilon p_(i,m-1),p),
 z_i=(0,U-s_i p), z_star=(0,tau p).

The second coordinate stays in [tau p,U], including the final iterate,
because U-S_m p=U(S_m+tau)/(2S_m+tau)>=tau p. Hence C is precisely the
vertical segment {0} x [tau p,U]. Every query residual is horizontal and
orthogonal to every difference of points in C; the star normal points
downward and also obeys (4). The ONE realizing function is

 F_A(x,y)=x^2/(2d)+dist(y,[tau p,U])^2/(2tau)+p y-tau p^2/2.

It is nonquadratic, convex, 1-smooth, and has UNIQUE minimizer (0,0), by
(10). Its gradients vary at every query before the central annihilation,
and all those queries have strictly positive height

 delta_i=(d-1)epsilon^2 p_(i,m-1)^2/2.

The original final objective and true initial distance are exactly

                2F_A(x_n)=3/[4(2S_m+tau)], dist(x_0,argmin F_A)=1.

Thus the curvature cost in (14) is compatible with an actual positive-height
trajectory, but that cost prevents this entire metric policy from reaching
the benchmark constant. The example uses one active resonant mode; the upper
theorem permits all m of them and every common cross correlation. The example
does not establish that all those modes can be independently activated.

## 7. The remaining interface and the abandoned smaller policy

The conclusion is NOT a closure of arbitrary positive joint heights, nor of
arbitrary A. Even with the same quadratic height formula, retaining only
the weaker Q inequalities in (8) does not imply the normals (4). With an
arbitrarily ill-conditioned A, (14) no longer forces every earlier step to
be <=2tau, so the norm budget (16) no longer follows. These are the exact
two missing hypotheses for extending this particular proof.

The preliminary symmetrized modal-energy policy in plan10bd4d79197b0379 set
f_i=<v,x_i>+C+<R_i,Z_i>/2. Its correct joint law is

 Q_ij=-(s_j-s_i)<v,R_i>
       -<R_i-R_j,Z_i-Z_j>/2+||R_i-R_j||^2/2
       +(<R_i,Z_j>-<R_j,Z_i>)/2.

The final antisymmetric term must not be dropped. That policy was not proved
legal or excluded. The anisotropic distance policy (3)--(6) was selected to
make the full joint height payment and function realization explicit.

Matlas retrieval for nilpotent trajectories and for weighted squared-distance
smoothness returned no theorem used here. The exact local text of Taylor,
Hendrickx and Glineur, arXiv:1502.05666, Corollary1 and the proof of Theorem4,
was read for context. No published theorem is an external premise: weighted
projection, smoothness, all-pair legality and the benchmark comparator have
been proved above from finite algebra and the two accepted fact inputs.

evidence:
# C61: projection polytopes retain the unrestricted objective supremum

Status: complete self-contained UNVERIFIED candidate. No numerical evaluation
or verifier submission. Accepted predecessor1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the
finite smooth-convex interpolant. The concrete final application also uses
accepted facte9a55f57461f253c. All additional claims are proved below rather
than importing earlier unverified projection-lift findings as premises.

The new point is normalization by the ACTUAL closest minimizer. Moving far
in a direction of minimizers need not increase initial distance. The earlier
primitive-energy epigraph lifts did not establish this objective comparison.

## 1. Statement and exact scope

Fix any integer n>=0 and finite nonnegative physical word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)).
Use the definition of W_n(h) from accepted1252b8823bb5a290, with smoothness1.
For a nonempty compact convex set K containing0 define

  PFun61_K(X)=max_(G in K)(<X,G>-||G||^2/2).

Let ProjPoly61_n(h) be the supremum of

  2 PFun61_K(X_n)/dist(X_0,argmin PFun61_K)^2,

over polytopes K=conv(0,G_0,...,G_n) in dimension at most n+1 and actual
GD X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i grad PFun61_K(X_i), with positive initial distance.
The symbols G_i in this display are the actual sampled gradients, including
the terminal gradient; repetition and redundant vertices are allowed.

The claim is

                       ProjPoly61_n(h)=W_n(h).                 (1)

This is an equality of SUPREMA; attainment in the projection subclass is
not asserted. Every n+2-vertex polytope is permitted, with arbitrary real
Gram matrix. There is no fixed dimension, conditioning, face-angle, jump,
normal-support, or correlation restriction independent of n. The closest
minimizer is generally NOT the origin, even though0 is a minimizer.

Before taking the compact hull, a quantitative construction uses one
polyhedral epigraph in one extra coordinate. Its minimizer set is exactly
a vertical ray, its closest-minimizer distance is EXACTLY the old distance,
and its normalized objective loss has an explicit O(Lambda^(-2)) bound.
Every queried step and every ordered interpolation pair are retained.

Equation(1) reformulates the full lower-witness problem. It supplies no
choice of K meeting the Zhang--Jiang bound for arbitrary h, and no scalable
description of such a polytope on the near-critical ruler.

## 2. Elementary projection and GD bounds used below

For any nonempty closed convex K containing0, completing the square shows
that the unique maximizer defining PFun61_K is the Euclidean projection
P_K(X). The minimizer of the squared distance exists by coercivity and
closedness, and is unique by strict convexity. Its normal inequality is

  <X-P_K(X),G-P_K(X)><=0 for every G in K.                     (2)

Adding the inequalities for two points gives

  ||P_K(X)-P_K(Y)||^2<=<P_K(X)-P_K(Y),X-Y>.                   (3)

Evaluating the two defining suprema at their maximizers shows
0<=PFun61_K(Y)-PFun61_K(X)-<P_K(X),Y-X>
 <=<P_K(Y)-P_K(X),Y-X><=||Y-X||^2.
Thus PFun61_K is finite, convex, differentiable,1-smooth and has gradientP_K.
It is nonnegative and has minimum0 because0 belongs to K.

For any convex1-smooth function F, the necessary two-point interpolation
inequalities in accepted1252b8823bb5a290 imply, on adding them,

  <grad F(x)-grad F(y),x-y>>=||grad F(x)-grad F(y)||^2.

Consequently T_h(x)=x-h grad F(x) is Lipschitz with constant

  nu(h)=max(1,h-1), h>=0.                                    (4)

Indeed the squared difference of the outputs is at most
||x-y||^2+h(h-2)||grad F(x)-grad F(y)||^2. If h<=2 this is
at most||x-y||^2. If h>2, use the1-Lipschitz gradient bound to obtain
(h-1)^2||x-y||^2. Formula(4) includes h=0 and is also valid for PFun61_K.

Put S=sum_i h_i and A=product_i nu(h_i), with empty product1.
Every partial product and every consecutive product of the nu(h_i) is
at most A because every factor is at least1. If F has a minimizer x_star
and R=||x_0-x_star||, then ||x_i-x_star||<=R A at EVERY queried or terminal
sample. These are elementary finite bounds, not an asymptotic estimate.

## 3. A finite max-affine conjugate core

For now assume a finite nonnegative convex max-affine function psi61 on R^d
is identically0 on a neighborhood of0. Write

  psi61(p)=max(0,max_(j in J){<y_j,p>-delta_j}),
  B=max_(j in J)||y_j||,                                     (5)

where J is finite; take B=0 for the empty family. It is sufficient that
all nonzero y_j have delta_j>0. Terms with y_j=0 and delta_j>=0 can be
removed. Thus psi61 is globally B-Lipschitz, psi61(0)=0, and
0<=psi61(p)<=B||p||. Every subgradient of psi61 has norm at most B: it is a
convex combination of slopes of the active affine functions.

Set

  F61_core(x)=max_p{<x,p>-||p||^2/2-psi61(p)}.                      (6)

The maximizing p is the unique minimizer of
||p-x||^2/2+psi61(p). The strong-subgradient and maximizing-difference
arguments from accepted1252b8823bb5a290 give that F61_core is convex1-smooth
with this maximizer as its gradient. The same arguments also prove these
properties directly for(6). Since psi61>=0 and psi61(0)=0,0 is a minimizer
of F61_core with value0. The flat neighborhood makes it the UNIQUE minimizer:
if x!=0, choose a sufficiently small positive multiple p of x in that
neighborhood; then <x,p>-||p||^2/2>0.

Fix x_0!=0 and run actual GD for F61_core with the supplied full word h.
Use z_i for these original iterates, z_0=x_0, and R=||x_0||.

## 4. The exact epigraph trajectory and its closest minimizer

For any Lambda>0, put e=Lambda^(-2) and define the closed convex polyhedron

  K61_Lambda={(p,s) in R^(d+1): Lambda*s>=psi61(p)}.               (7)

Run actual GD for PFun61_(K61_Lambda) from

  X_0=(x_0,-Lambda).

Write X_i=(x_i,-Lambda*tau_i), with tau_0=1. At any point with tau>=1,
the projection onto(7) has the form

  G=(p,psi61(p)/Lambda),
  p=argmin_q {||q-x||^2/2+tau*psi61(q)+e*psi61(q)^2/2}.           (8)

For fixed q the optimal vertical coordinate is its lowest permitted
coordinate psi61(q)/Lambda, because the point's vertical coordinate is
negative and psi61>=0. Substitution into squared distance proves(8).
The objective in(8) is strongly convex and coercive: psi61 and psi61^2 are
convex, the latter because psi61 is nonnegative. Hence there is one p.
In particular this is a definition of an actual projection, not a relaxed
interpolation or numerical feasibility prescription.

The actual GD recursion is EXACTLY

  x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i p_i,
  tau_(i+1)=tau_i+e*h_i*psi61(p_i).                             (9)

Thus every tau_i>=1. The same K61_Lambda is retained at all steps.

Its function has precisely the minimizer set

  argmin PFun61_(K61_Lambda)={(0,t):t<=0}.                        (10)

For such a point every inner product with(p,s) in K61_Lambda is nonpositive,
so0 maximizes. Conversely, if the horizontal part x is nonzero, a small
p in the flat neighborhood of psi61, of the sign/direction of x, with s=0,
makes <x,p>-||p||^2/2 positive. If the vertical coordinate t is positive,
the permitted vector(0,s) with small s>0 makes ts-s^2/2 positive. These
arguments prove(10) in all cases.

It follows that the closest minimizer to X_0 is EXACTLY

  X_star=(0,-Lambda),  dist(X_0,argmin PFun61_(K61_Lambda))=R.    (11)

No Lambda^2 enters the initial squared distance. The initial norm relative
to the OTHER minimizer0 would be R^2+Lambda^2 and is not the normalization
used here.

## 5. Every interpolation pair, including the closest minimizer

Let psi61_i=psi61(p_i). Optimality in(8) gives a subgradient
s_i in partial psi61(p_i) with

  x_i-p_i=alpha_i s_i, alpha_i=tau_i+e*psi61_i>0.

For a finite max-affine psi61 this chain rule follows, for example, by taking
directional derivatives: the derivative of t->tau*t+e*t^2/2 at psi61_i is
the positive number alpha_i, so the subdifferential of its composition is
alpha_i partial psi61(p_i). Hence

  X_i-G_i=(alpha_i s_i,-Lambda alpha_i).

Use the actual value f_i=<X_i,G_i>-||G_i||^2/2. Direct expansion of the
signed interpolation residual gives

  Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2
      =<X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j>
      =alpha_j[<s_j,p_i-p_j>-(psi61_i-psi_j)]<=0.              (12)

The last sign is the full convex subgradient inequality for psi61. It is
valid for EVERY ordered pair, irrespective of their temporal order.
For the optimum sample in(11), set p_star=0,psi_star=0,tau_star=1,s_star=0.
Flatness makes0 the subgradient there. Formula(12) still applies, giving
in particular Q_(i,star)=-psi61_i<=0. The lifted data therefore retain all
queried, terminal and optimum comparisons with the actual normalization.

## 6. An explicit finite-horizon error bound

All quantities in this section refer to the same fixed h and psi61.
The full GD distance estimate(4), applied about X_star, gives
||X_i-X_star||<=R A and hence ||x_i||<=R A. The projection optimality(8)
also gives ||p_i||<=||x_i||. To see this, write x_i-p_i=alpha_i s_i;
the subgradient inequality at0 gives <s_i,p_i>>=psi61_i>=0, and so
<x_i,p_i>>=||p_i||^2. Thus

  psi61_i<=B R A,
  0<=tau_i-1<=e*S*B R A.                                   (13)

Let p^0=grad F61_core(x_i), so x_i-p^0=s^0 in partial psi61(p^0).
Subtract the two optimality conditions and use subgradient monotonicity:

  ||p_i-p^0||^2
    <=-(alpha_i-1)<s_i,p_i-p^0>
    <=(alpha_i-1)B||p_i-p^0||.

If the difference vanishes there is nothing to divide; otherwise divide
by its positive norm. Since alpha_i-1=(tau_i-1)+e psi61_i, (13) implies

  ||p_i-grad F61_core(x_i)||<=e B^2 R A(S+1).                  (14)

Compare(9) with z_(i+1)=T_(h_i)(z_i) for the same F61_core. Formula(4)
and(14), iterated from x_0=z_0, give at every sample

  ||x_i-z_i||<=e B^2 R A^2 S(S+1).                          (15)

Explicitly each error contribution h_j times the right side of(14) is
multiplied by a subsequent product of nu(h_t), at most A; summing h_j
gives(15). No assumption of uniformly small A or S is made.

At X=(x,-Lambda*tau), formula(8) also yields the value identity

  PFun61_(K61_Lambda)(X)
    =max_p{<x,p>-||p||^2/2-tau psi61(p)-e psi61(p)^2/2}.         (16)

This is at most F61_core(x). Evaluating its maximum at p^0=grad F61_core(x)
gives a reverse lower bound differing by at most
(tau-1)psi61(p^0)+e psi61(p^0)^2/2. At the terminal point, ||p^0||<=||x_n||
<=R A, so(13) bounds this loss by e B^2 R^2 A^2(S+1/2).
Both x_n and z_n lie in the radius R A ball; the gradient of F61_core has
norm at most R A throughout their line segment. Therefore(15) gives

  PFun61_(K61_Lambda)(X_n)
     >=F61_core(z_n)-e R^2 C61_lift(h),

  C61_lift(h)=B^2 A^2[A S(S+1)+S+1/2].                        (17)

Combining with(11), the normalized objective loss is at most

                         2 C61_lift(h)/Lambda^2.              (18)

Every constant is explicit and finite for every finite nonnegative word,
including zeros and the empty word. It is not claimed to be economical.

## 7. Every legal objective can be approximated by such a flat core

Take any original convex differentiable1-smooth F with minimizer0,
F(0)=0 and initial x_0!=0, R=||x_0||. It is harmless if0 was not its
closest minimizer: this is still one of the admissible normalizations in
the definition of W_n(h). For 0<beta<1 set

  F_beta(x)=(1-beta)F(x)+(beta/4)||x||^2.                    (19)

It is beta/2-strongly convex, has UNIQUE minimizer0, and its gradient is
L_beta-Lipschitz with L_beta=1-beta/2<1. It approaches F with its gradient
uniformly on bounded sets. The following explicit finite bound avoids any
unquantified exchange of limits. Let z_i and z_i^beta be their actual
trajectories for h. Both have norm at most R A. On this ball,

  ||grad F_beta-grad F||<=3 beta R A/2,
  |F_beta-F|<=3 beta R^2 A^2/4.

The first inequality follows from ||grad F(x)||<=||x|| and the second
from 0<=F(x)<=||x||^2/2. Iterating(4) as in(15) gives
||z_n^beta-z_n||<=3 beta R A^2 S/2. Consequently the normalized terminal
objective for F_beta differs from that for F by at most

                  beta[3 A^3 S+(3/2)A^2].                 (20)

Use its complete finite jets, including sample n and the zero optimum.
At each finite sample let y_i=z_i^beta-grad F_beta(z_i^beta) and
delta_i=F_beta(z_i^beta)-||grad F_beta(z_i^beta)||^2/2.
The smooth descent inequality with step1/L_beta gives
F_beta(z_i^beta)>=||grad F_beta(z_i^beta)||^2/(2L_beta).
Thus delta_i>0 unless the gradient vanishes. In the latter case strong
convexity gives z_i^beta=0 and y_i=0.

It follows that the finite function

  psi61(p)=max(0,max_(0<=i<=n){<y_i,p>-delta_i})                (21)

has exactly the properties in(5), in particular a flat neighborhood of0.
For example take a positive radius smaller than every
delta_i/||y_i|| with y_i!=0; if none exist, psi61=0 everywhere.
By accepted1252b8823bb5a290, proof paragraph2 applied to the complete
finite index set, F61_core interpolates ALL these jets. Its actual GD for
the unchanged word therefore has the same trajectory and terminal value
as F_beta. This invocation uses only the accepted all-pair construction,
not a reduced or conjecturally legal prefix.

Given any desired normalized loss eta>0, choose beta in(0,1) with the
right side of(20) below eta/2. Then form(21) and choose Lambda>0 with
2C61_lift(h)/Lambda^2<eta/2. Equations(18)--(21) give a real projection-function
instance of normalized payoff at least the original payoff minus eta.
Its exact closest-minimizer distance remains R.

## 8. Compactification and dimension compression prove(1)

For the lifted instance just constructed let G_0,...,G_n be its ACTUAL
gradients and put

  K_fin=conv(0,G_0,...,G_n).

This is a compact polytope contained in K61_Lambda. For every sample i,
G_i belongs to K_fin and was already the unique maximizer over K61_Lambda.
It is consequently also the unique maximizer over K_fin, with the SAME
function value. Induction on the actual GD recursion proves that replacing
K61_Lambda by K_fin preserves every sample, gradient and value in the entire
word, not just its endpoint.

The point X_star=(0,-Lambda) remains a minimizer for the compact hull:
its inner product with each G_i is -psi61_i<=0 and with0 is0. Therefore

  dist(X_0,argmin PFun61_(K_fin))<=||X_0-X_star||=R.            (22)

Shrinking this denominator cannot decrease a nonnegative objective ratio.
If the terminal value is positive, initial distance is positive, since
starting at a minimizer would make the actual GD stationary.

Finally let V=span(G_0,...,G_n), of dimension at most n+1, and orthogonally
project all X_i onto V. The function PFun61_(K_fin) depends only on this
projection, every gradient is already in V, and the same GD recursion and
values hold there. Its full minimizer set is the minimizer set inside V
plus V-perp, so its true initial distance is EXACTLY preserved by this
compression. Choose an orthonormal basis of V to realize it as R^dim(V).
The compact hull still has at most n+2 listed vertices.

This proves ProjPoly61_n(h)>=W_n(h) by arbitrarily accurate approximation of
each positive-payoff legal instance. Conversely every member of this
projection subclass is convex1-smooth with an attained minimum and positive
initial distance, so its ratio is at most W_n(h) by definition. This proves(1).
The positive value of W_n(h), including n=0, is part of the accepted fact;
it also follows by choosing a sufficiently small scalar quadratic curvature.

## 9. Concrete consequence for the now-verified C59 word

Accepted e9a55f57461f253c provides the actual63-step H6 word with epsilon1/6,
and an explicit function F59 in R66 whose conjugate core is the finite
maximum of0 and the planes <Y_i,p>-delta_i. Its proof establishes every
nonstar delta_i>0, so it ALREADY satisfies(5); no perturbation(19) is needed.
Let B=max_i||Y_i||, let A,S have their actual finite values for this H6,
and define C=C61_lift(h59) by(17). All are specified by that accepted fact.

Choose the explicit positive parameter

                    Lambda^2=1+(271100/89)C.

Then the loss in(18) is strictly smaller than89/135550, and

                    56/2711-89/135550=1/50.

Thus the epigraph projection function in R67 has the same true initial
distance as C59 and an actual H6 payoff>1/50>4/M59. Compactification and
span compression give a projection polytope with at most65 vertices in
dimension at most64 with true-distance payoff>1/50>4/M59.

This corollary remains UNVERIFIED pending a separately allocated gate.
It inherits the EXACT epsilon1/6 scope of its accepted input. It does not
assert that the compressed projection function has a unique minimizer,
or that its gradients are the original C59 gradients. No claim about its
six-jump geometry or changed-parameter H_m subwords is made here.

## 10. What this changes and what remains missing

The projection-function route itself is not too small for the objective
problem when true closest-minimizer distance is allowed: arbitrary compact
polytopes already have the full supremum, in the sense of(1). Earlier scoped
failures of cones, distance-squared functions, incidence relays, six-jump
coordinates, or special parabolas do not cover this class.

The target requires an explicit useful K or a lower bound on the entire
polytope game for each physical word. In the actual critical sequence
c_m=(1+sqrt2)(1+1/m), a_m=(1-1/m)/c_m,
H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_m c_m^j,H_j), parameters remain fixed within
each full horizon. This construction cannot replace them by the finite
C59 parameters or reset the vertical state in the right child.

For a chosen near-optimal full transcript, all the information about the
unknown solution is still present in psi61's planes and their joint Gram.
Equation(18) makes any desired finite accuracy attainable, but is not an
analytic policy for choosing those planes as m grows. The compactification
is performed only after the whole actual trajectory, retaining all its
normal comparisons. Treating vertices or copies independently would lose
the load-bearing joint constraints.

Matlas and web background searches were performed for epigraph projection
and smooth interpolation. No retrieved paper theorem is used as a premise.
The proof above is elementary apart from the explicitly cited accepted
finite interpolation construction. Prior shared primitive-lift candidates
motivated the closest-distance check but are not correctness sources.

# C62: anchor the simplex conversion at the actual minimum

Status: UNVERIFIED complete refinement, saved before switching to the new
C60 trajectory TASK. No solver or verifier call. Accepted1252b8823bb5a290
supplies necessary interpolation inequalities; accepted e9a55f57461f253c
supplies the final finite example. Earlier C27 and C61 are not premises.

## Exact independent-gradient conversion

Suppose a legal convex1-smooth GD trajectory has minimizer0, value0 there,
jets(x_i,g_i,f_i), and linearly independent sampled gradients g_0,...,g_m.
Its steps are any supplied nonnegative finite steps for which the samples
are distinct; zero-step repetitions can subsequently be restored. Set

  I_i=<g_i,x_i>-f_i-||g_i||^2/2>=0,
  A_ij=<g_i,g_j>,
  w=-sum_j(A^(-1)I)_j g_j,
  X_i=x_i+w, C=conv(0,g_0,...,g_m).

The Gram A is positive definite and <w,g_i>=-I_i. For every i,j, expansion
using the displayed definition of I gives

  <X_i-g_i,g_j-g_i>
    =f_j-f_i+<g_j,x_i-x_j>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
    =Q_(j,i)<=0.

For the extra vertex0, the normal comparison is
<X_i-g_i,-g_i>=-f_i+||g_i||^2/2=Q_(star,i)<=0.
Consequently P_C(X_i)=g_i, by expanding squared distances to each vertex
and then using convex combinations. The fixed function

  F_C(X)=max_(g in C)(<X,g>-||g||^2/2)

has gradient P_C: projection normal inequalities give firm nonexpansiveness,
and comparing the maximizing expressions gives differentiability. Thus
F_C is globally convex1-smooth and its actual GD visits exactly X_i.
Its values are EXACTLY the original values:

  F_C(X_i)=<x_i+w,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2=f_i.

Moreover w is an actual minimizer because <w,g_i>=-I_i<=0 for all vertices,
and0 is a vertex. It follows that

  dist(X_0,argmin F_C)<=||X_0-w||=||x_0||.                   (1)

Hence the TRUE normalized objective cannot decrease. All gradients, all
their inner products and jumps, every function value, and every physical
step are preserved EXACTLY. No common value shift was made. Projection
onto V=span(g_0,...,g_m) preserves all these data and true closest distance:
F_C depends only on V, and its minimizer set is its minimizer set in V plus
V-perp. The resulting simplex has dimension m+1 and m+2 vertices.

This is compatible with C27's dilution examples: arbitrary translations
with a common added value need not preserve a normalized objective. The
specific translation here uses the slacks relative to the original TRUE
minimum0 and keeps every f_i unchanged. The known minimizer w in(1) is
the missing normalization control.

## Uniform relative approximation by strictly independent gradients

For an arbitrary legal trajectory with R=||x_0||>0, first compress all zero
steps, leaving m strictly positive steps. In R^(m+1) choose

  theta_l=(l+1)/(2(m+2)), 0<=l<=m,
  D=diag(theta_l), z_0=(1,...,1)/sqrt(m+1), q(z)=<z,Dz>/2.

Run that SAME compressed schedule on q. Its gradients at indices0,...,m
are linearly independent: their l-th coordinates are
theta_l product_(t<i)(1-h_t theta_l)/sqrt(m+1); the polynomials of degrees
0,...,m in this expression form a basis, since all compressed h_t>0, and
evaluation at the m+1 distinct nonzero theta_l is invertible. For m=0
the single gradient is nonzero and the same conclusion holds.

Every finite pair of distinct samples has strict interpolation slack:
Q_ij^q=-(z_i-z_j)^T D(I-D)(z_i-z_j)/2<0. The positions are distinct
because the difference of the corresponding polynomials has degree at
most m and cannot vanish at all m+1 nodes. Every z_i is nonzero for the
same root-counting reason, giving strict slacks in both optimum directions.

For any t>0 use the direct-sum function F(x,z)=f(x)+q(z), with initial
point(x_0,tR z_0). This is convex1-smooth and has a minimizer0. Its exact
jets are(x_i,tR z_i),(g_i,tR D z_i),f_i+t^2R^2 q(z_i).
All compressed gradients are independent, and all distinct finite/optimum
interpolation inequalities are strict. Its initial squared norm is
R^2(1+t^2), whereas its terminal value is at least the original f_n.
Applying the anchored conversion just proved therefore gives a strict
simplex projection trajectory with true normalized objective at least

              [2 f_n/R^2]/(1+t^2).                         (2)

The relative factor is independent of the number, magnitudes and order of
steps. Restoring zero steps repeats the corresponding samples and changes
nothing. Taking t to0 proves that the supremum over STRICT simplex vertex
projection trajectories of dimension m+1 is the full W_n(h). This remains
a supremum assertion; finite t perturbs the original function and can make
the Gram extremely ill-conditioned. No conditioning restriction is implied.

## Correct closest-distance Gram game

For an independent simplex let A be its gradient Gram and b_i=<g_i,X_0>.
Let T_ii=1,T_ij=h_j for j<i, and T_ij=0 for j>i, using compressed indices.
Every projection normal comparison is exactly

  b_j-b_i<=(TA)_ij-(TA)_ii,  b_i>=(TA)_ii.                   (3)

The final objective is

  2F_C(X_m)=2b_m-2sum_(i<m)h_i A_im-A_mm.                   (4)

The TRUE initial squared distance to the polar minimizer cone is

  R_C^2=max_(u>=0)[2b^T u-u^T A u].                        (5)

Here u is a vector of nonnegative coefficients, not a physical iterate.
To prove(5), minimize ||X_0-sum_i u_i g_i||^2 over u>=0. Positive
definiteness makes this coercive and strictly convex. At its minimizer,
Au-b>=0 and u_i(Au-b)_i=0, by the one-sided coordinate derivatives. Put
p=sum_i u_i g_i and z=X_0-p. Then z is in the polar cone and <p,z>=0.
For any polar point y, expansion gives
||X_0-y||^2=||p||^2+||z-y||^2-2<p,y>>=||p||^2,
with equality at y=z. Thus the distance is ||p||^2=u^TAu=2b^Tu-u^TAu,
which proves(5). Orthogonal components of X_0 were discarded as above.

Together(2)--(5) give a lossless objective supremum over the COMPLETE
normal-inequality simplex game with the polar distance denominator. The
older expression b^T A^(-1)b is distance to the chosen minimizer0, and
cannot replace(5) in this objective formulation. No inequality comparing
this full game to the benchmark has been proved.

In accepted e9a55f57461f253c the rational core gradients are rows1,...,64
of the lower triangular65by65 integer matrix T divided by10^15. All64
diagonal entries T_ii,1<=i<=64, are strictly positive; their minimum is
8124849466. This follows by reading the frozen defining integers in the
accepted proof. A read-only extraction matched the frozen JSON SHA256
7376e26ca81edc6438c0563e008c845ce439e424bd42f9f65c37a07867d6b113.
The triangular submatrix on columns1,...,64 is therefore invertible.
The64 core gradients are independent, and adding their auxiliary coordinate
does not destroy that independence.

Apply the exact conversion with the actual C59 values and gradients. After
span compression this gives a65-vertex simplex projection function in R64
for the SAME actual H6 epsilon1/6 word, with exactly the C59 full gradient
Gram, exactly its function values, and true initial distance at most R59.
Its payoff is therefore>56/2711>1/50>4/M59. Its jump Gram is unchanged,
so the accepted six-jumps obstruction also holds for this trajectory.
All C59 original ordered residuals were strictly negative, so every sampled
vertex normal is strict against every distinct simplex vertex including0.

This new corollary and the general reduction remain UNVERIFIED; only the
input C59 fact is accepted. No new verification or numerical solve is used.
The conclusion is still finite epsilon1/6; it supplies no analytic simplex
