# C63: a shared-state block bound closes the large horizontal parabolic regime

Status: complete UNVERIFIED analytic candidate following the bounded direct
C60 experiment. No new fact_submit. Accepted b98bb807d514e80d is used for
the exact benchmark definitions; every further estimate below is derived
internally. C60's unverified formulas are reproduced and proved here.

The result is uniform over an explicit domain of initial states. It is NOT
an upper bound on every parabolic start or on unrestricted W_n(h).

## 1. Result, with the actual physical parameters

For m>=5 put

  lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
  H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
  n=2^m-1, S=sum H_m, M=1+S.

All these parameters remain fixed throughout the complete word H_m.
Consider the ONE function and initial state defined in Section2. Its
parameters are r_0!=0,v_0>=0. Let

  R=|r_0|(1+v_0+r_0^2),
  E_par(S)=(2S+3)^2/[8(S+1)^2(2S+1)].

If

                     R >= S sqrt(c-2),                     (1)

then every r_i has the same strict sign as r_0, and its actual normalized
last-iterate objective satisfies

  P_par(H_m;r_0,v_0)<=E_par(S)<1/(2S+1).                    (2)

In particular(1) holds uniformly for ALL initial states

                     r_0^2>=M^(2/3), v_0>=0.               (3)

For the EXACT Zhang--Jiang benchmark U_n^ZJ=1/B_n from the accepted fact,

  B_(2^m-1) sup_(states satisfying(1)) P_par
       <=lambda^(m+1) E_par(S),
  limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) sup_(states satisfying(1)) P_par
       <=lambda/[4 exp(1)]<1/4.                            (4)

No asymptotic equality for B_n is assumed. Section6 proves the scalar upper
envelope needed in(4) directly from its exact finite recurrence.

The payoff bound in(2) also holds for ANY finite nonnegative schedule of
total mass S>=1/2 whenever its whole parabolic trajectory keeps one sign
(allowing absorption at zero). Thus the candidate bound is not inferred
from the finite sample portfolio. What is particular to the ruler is the
proved sufficient initial-state condition(1).

## 2. One global legal function, every pair, and true distance

In R2 define

  K_par={(t,s):s>=t^2/sqrt(2)},
  F_par(X)=max_(g in K_par)(<X,g>-||g||^2/2).

The maximizer is the unique Euclidean projection onto this nonempty closed
convex set: complete the square, use coercivity for existence and strict
convexity for uniqueness. The normal inequalities at two projection points
give firm nonexpansiveness. Comparing the defining maxima shows that F_par
is differentiable with gradient equal to the projection; it is globally
convex and1-smooth. In detail, for the projection p(X),
||p(X)-p(Y)||^2<=<p(X)-p(Y),X-Y>, and
0<=F_par(Y)-F_par(X)-<p(X),Y-X>
 <=<p(Y)-p(X),Y-X><=||Y-X||^2.

For r real and v>=0 put

  u=v+r^2,
  X(r,v)=(r(1+v+r^2),-v/sqrt(2)),
  G(r)=(r,r^2/sqrt(2)).

One has X-G=u(r,-1/sqrt(2)). For any(t,s) in K_par,
<X-G,(t,s)-G><=-(u/2)(t-r)^2<=0. Thus G(r) is the actual gradient
at X(r,v), and substitution gives

  F_par(X(r,v))=r^2(1+v)/2+3r^4/4.                          (5)

For EVERY ordered pair of such samples the complete interpolation residual is

  Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2
      =<X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j>
      =-(v_j+r_j^2)(r_i-r_j)^2/2<=0.                       (6)

The identity follows by writing f_i=<X_i,G_i>-||G_i||^2/2 and expanding.
There is no adjacent-only interpolation condition in this construction.

The minimizer set of F_par is exactly{(0,y):y<=0}. Such a point gives a
nonpositive inner product with every feasible gradient, and0 is feasible.
A point with positive vertical coordinate has a positive value by testing
(0,s) with small positive s. A point with nonzero horizontal coordinate
has a positive value by testing(t,t^2/sqrt(2)) with small t of the same
horizontal sign; the linear term dominates the quadratic and quartic terms.
Hence the closest minimizer to X(r_0,v_0) is(0,-v_0/sqrt(2)), and the
true squared distance is R^2=r_0^2(1+v_0+r_0^2)^2.

For every physical step h>=0 actual GD is described by

  v_plus=v+h r^2,
  r_plus^3+(1+v_plus)r_plus=r(1+v+r^2-h).                  (7)

The cubic's derivative is1+v_plus+3r_plus^2>=1, so it has exactly one real
solution. The horizontal and vertical coordinates in(7) are exactly those
of X-hG. This proves actual GD for the same global F_par at every step.
The normalized payoff is

  P_par=[r_n^2(1+v_n)+(3/2)r_n^4]/R^2.                    (8)

Reflection of the horizontal coordinate sends r to-r and leaves all values
and v unchanged. Thus it suffices to prove the remaining statements with
r_0>0. If r ever becomes zero it remains zero by(7) and the payoff is zero.

## 3. Quantitative block map with one shared vertical state

First suppose a consecutive actual block of total mass T has positive
r-values throughout. At one step, the sign is retained exactly when
h<1+v+r^2. The increasing cubic in(7), evaluated at the OLD positive r,
exceeds its right side by h r(1+r^2)>=0. Consequently

                       0<r_plus<=r.                       (9)

Write the entry state(r_A,v_A), exit state(r_B,v_B), and horizontal
coordinate x=r(1+v+r^2). Telescoping the two ACTUAL recursions gives

  Delta_x=x_A-x_B=sum_(block)h_i r_i,
  Delta_v=v_B-v_A=sum_(block)h_i r_i^2.

Because r_B<=r_i<=r_A, the following complete finite bounds hold:

  T r_B<=Delta_x<=T r_A,
  r_B Delta_x<=Delta_v<=r_A Delta_x,
  T r_B^2<=Delta_v<=T r_A^2,
  Delta_x^2<=T Delta_v.                                   (10)

The final inequality is weighted Cauchy--Schwarz; at T=0 both sides vanish.
In particular the nonlinear block map obeys

  r_B[1+v_B+r_B^2+T]<=r_A(1+v_A+r_A^2).                   (11)

These estimates compose along H_(j+1)=(H_j,b_j,H_j), where b_j=1+a c^j,
by using the ACTUAL exit(r_B,v_B) of the left block as the bridge input,
then the bridge's exit as the right block input. The right copy's v is
never restarted or frozen. Equations(10)--(11) therefore control full
nonlinear blocks with all finite masses and all inherited v explicitly
present; no limiting differential equation is used.

## 4. The first possible turn has a quantitative initial-radius cost

Consider a first step whose output r is nonpositive. All preceding states
were positive and decreasing by(9). Let P be the total earlier step mass,

payoffs occurring without a sign change. The next25 runs used
r0^2=k M^(2/3),v0=0, k in{1/16,1/4,1/2,1,2}, at the same five depths.

For the now-uniformly-excluded k=1 and2 recipes, the numerical M*payoffs
were respectively

  m4:  0.0746391227, 0.1281488193;
  m6:  0.0687903731, 0.1259430663;
  m8:  0.0684937234, 0.1263322527;
  m10: 0.0689648481, 0.1268277425;

Those numbers motivated the proof; none is a premise. No exact B_n was
numerically evaluated or inferred from M. The proof instead uses(19).

Two depth10 runs completed with payoff underflow, and two depth12 runs
stopped at cubic RHS/root underflow; those are not exact zero trajectories.
One further payoff was subnormal. Raw states and original statuses remain
public. An underflow-sensitive turn diagnostic originally multiplied two
tiny r-values; saved-state companions correct it using separate sign tests,
without replaying any trajectory. The repair time is included in the ledger.
No original raw file was overwritten. All raw hashes were checked at closeout.

## 8. Every trajectory with just one turn is also uniformly excluded

This strengthening imposes NO initial-state bound(1). Suppose the actual
parabolic trajectory on H_m has exactly one horizontal sign change.
If it ever hits r=0 then all later values vanish, so only nonzero turns
need be considered. Reflect horizontally so its initial sign is positive.

The normal variable u_i=v_i+r_i^2 is nondecreasing for this entire physical
word, because(7) gives the exact identity

  u_(i+1)-u_i=(h_i-1)r_i^2+r_(i+1)^2>=0.                  (21)

Every h_i>1 here. Before the first turn, any previous step h_t preserved
positivity, so h_t<1+u_t. A later step h_i no larger than that previous
h_t then satisfies h_i<=h_t<1+u_t<=1+u_i and CANNOT turn. Consequently
the first turn occurs at a NEW RECORD step, necessarily the first occurrence
of some level j. In the actual recursive word that step is b_j=1+a c^j,
its prefix is exactly H_j with mass P=S_j, and its suffix mass is

  T=S_m-S_j-b_j>=S_(m-1).                                 (22)

The last inequality follows because S_j+b_j is increasing in j and the
top-level decomposition is S_m=2S_(m-1)+b_(m-1).

Let r>0,u be the state just before this first turn. The positive prefix
has decreasing r-values. Therefore its initial horizontal magnitude R
and the new magnitude R_after obey

  R=r(1+u)+sum_(t<i)h_t r_t>=r(P+1+u),
  R_after=r(h_i-1-u).

The numerator is positive precisely because this step turns. Hence

  R_after/R <=(h_i-1-u)/(P+1+u)
             <=(h_i-1)/(P+1)<c-2.                         (23)

The strict final inequality is(14)--(15), with the actual H_j prefix.
There is no restart of v: the tail starts at the ACTUAL state produced
by the turning step. By hypothesis there is no further turn, so Section5
applies to this suffix with its true initial distance R_after and mass T.
The function and its minimum0 remain identical. Thus

  2F_par(X_n)/R^2
    <=E_par(T)(R_after/R)^2
    <(c-2)^2 E_par(S_(m-1)).                               (24)

For monotonicity used here, logarithmic differentiation gives
E_par'(T)/E_par(T)=4/(2T+3)-2/(T+1)-2/(2T+1)<0; the first term is already
strictly smaller than2/(T+1). The suffix mass in(22) is at least1/2.

Since S_(m-1)/lambda^(m-1)->exp(1), the exact benchmark bound(19) gives

  limsup B_(2^m-1) sup_(all exactly-one-turn initial states) P_par
      <=lambda^2(lambda-2)^2/[4 exp(1)]
       =1/[4 exp(1)]<1/4.                                 (25)

The equality uses lambda(lambda-2)=1. Combining with the zero-turn estimate
(4), every initial state whose actual trajectory has at most one turn has
uniform benchmark limsup at most lambda/[4 exp(1)]<1/4. No initial norm,
vertical-state, amplitude, or smallness restriction was imposed on the
one-turn class. This is a proof about the full actual trajectory and its
retained normal state, not about a constant-gradient single-cut ansatz.

## 9. Remaining interface

Every parabolic start whose trajectory stays on one horizontal side is now
below even the global Huber lower witness by(17). Thus a useful parabolic
mechanism on this ruler must actually TURN. Condition(1) also quantifies
which initial horizontal scales cannot turn. The turning domain
0<R<S sqrt(c-2), with arbitrary coupled r0,v0, is not excluded here.

The k=1/4 finite starts had one turn and small observed M*payoff. Section8
now excludes the ENTIRE one-turn class, independently of those samples.
The k=1/16 starts had several turns; two or more turns remain open. A next
proof must retain how every turn transports BOTH the remaining horizontal
magnitude and the accumulated v into the actual suffix, with its unchanged
physical parameters. After the first turn, a later turn need not be a new
global record; applying the first-record argument afresh would be invalid.
Resetting v or treating the two H_j copies independently is also invalid.

This is a concrete uniform regime result with exact nonlinear block losses,
not a solution of the full parabolic family, the critical diagnostic, or the
original all-schedule exact-profile goal. All new statements remain drafts
until separately authorized independent verification.

# C64 extension: arbitrarily many turns below the first turning threshold

Status: UNVERIFIED. The public combined package appends the COMPLETE C63
proof, including the global function, every interpolation pair, the true
distance, the one-sign block estimates and the exact benchmark comparison.
These are reproduced internal arguments, not unverified predecessor facts.
The only accepted mathematical input is b98bb807d514e80d for its benchmark
definitions. No numerical evaluation or verification is used here.

## Statement

Use exactly the physical H_m, c,a,S_j,M_j and parabolic trajectory from the
attached complete proof, with m>=128. Put d_j=a c^j and u_i=v_i+r_i^2.
Suppose there is a first nonzero horizontal sign change, occurring at level j,
and suppose

                            u_n<=d_j.                      (A)

The first-turn level j is allowed to depend arbitrarily on m. There is no
initial-state bound, fixed turn count or ambient approximation. If absorption
at zero occurs at any time then the final payoff is zero and the bounds below
hold immediately. Otherwise there are exactly2^(m-j)-1 turns.

For j>=1 set

  k=m-j, N=2^k, L_j=d_(j-1)=d_j/c,
  C_j=d_j/(M_j+L_j), beta_j=c C_j.

Then the normalized actual payoff satisfies

  P_par<=E_par(S_j) beta_j^[2(N-1)] c^(-2k),
  B_(2^m-1) P_par<729/1600<1/2.                            (B)

For j=0 it satisfies

  P_par<=(1-1/m)^[2(2^m-1)] c^(-2m),
  B_(2^m-1)P_par<=lambda^(1-m)<1/2.                        (C)

Thus every trajectory satisfying(A) is uniformly below HALF the exact
benchmark for all m>=128, even when its number of turns grows with m.
Together with C63's complete one-turn estimate in the attached proof, the
remaining parabolic case must have AT LEAST TWO turns and u_n>d_j for its
first-turn level j. This does not settle that remaining case or unrestricted W.

## 1. The lower normal threshold persists after the first turn

The exact identity

  u_(i+1)-u_i=(h_i-1)r_i^2+r_(i+1)^2>=0                    (D)

holds because every physical step is greater than1. A sign change occurs
exactly when u_i<d_level(i), since the cubic's right side is r_i(u_i-d_level(i)).
As proved directly in the attached C63 argument, the first turn must occur
at a new record step, hence at the first occurrence of level j. Its preceding
word is exactly H_j, with no earlier turn.

For j>=1, the earlier first occurrence of b_(j-1)=1+d_(j-1) did NOT turn
or annihilate. At its input this implies u>d_(j-1). Monotonicity(D) gives
u>L_j at the first turn and at every later sample. For j=0 simply use u>=0.
Hypothesis(A) and(D) simultaneously give u<=d_j at every sample.

Consequently, after the first turn every lower-level step in H_j preserves
the sign, since its d_level<=L_j<u. Every intervening step of level at
least j reverses the sign, except that an equality can cause absorption,
which has already been separated as zero payoff. The same u and v are
inherited across all copies.

## 2. All complete blocks and all coarse bridges remain in order

The actual word H_m partitions into N=2^(m-j) copies of H_j, interleaved
with N-1 bridges. The excess of the bridge after block ell,0<=ell<N-1, is

                 d_j c^(nu_2(ell+1)),                     (E)

where nu_2 is binary valuation. No physical step is aggregated or replaced
in the actual dynamics; this partition is only for applying proved block
inequalities. The first H_j has one sign by the definition of the first turn.
Every later H_j has one sign by Section1. All finite pair inequalities are
already supplied by the one fixed function in the attached proof.

Let R_ell be the horizontal magnitude at the entry to an H_j block. Just
before its following bridge, let the actual gradient magnitude be |r| and
normal state u. The one-sign block telescope gives

  R_ell>=|r|(M_j+u).

The bridge is a turn, so its resulting horizontal magnitude is
|r|(d_j c^s-u), where s=nu_2(ell+1). Since u>=L_j for j>=1,

  R_(ell+1)/R_ell
    <=(d_j c^s-u)/(M_j+u)
    <=d_j c^s/(M_j+L_j)=C_j c^s.                         (F)

The first inequality also holds for the first bridge: its left H_j was
one-sign, and u>=L_j holds at the BRIDGE, regardless of any smaller u at
the original starting point. Thus no extra initial-band hypothesis was used.

The binary counts give

  sum_(ell=0)^(N-2)nu_2(ell+1)=N-1-k.

One direct proof counts multiples of2^s among1,...,2^k-1 and sums
sum_(s=1)^(k-1)(2^(k-s)-1)=2^k-1-k. Multiplying(F) therefore yields

  R_(N-1)/R_0<=C_j^(N-1)c^(N-1-k)
              =beta_j^(N-1)c^(-k).                       (G)

The final full H_j is one-sign and has its ACTUAL inherited vertical state.
Its true initial distance is R_(N-1), because the closest minimizer of the
fixed parabolic function has the same vertical coordinate. Apply the proved
E_par(S_j) suffix bound, and use(G), to obtain the first inequality in(B).

## 3. Explicit constants and the exact finite benchmark

From the exact mass formula in the attached proof,
d_j/M_j<c-2. Thus

  beta_j=c[d_j/M_j]/[1+(d_j/M_j)/c]
           <c^2(c-2)/(2c-2).                             (H)

For m>=128 one has c<73/30. To check this without decimal input, use
sqrt2<99/70 because9801>9800, and hence
c<(169/70)(129/128)=21801/8960<73/30.
The positive function c^2(c-2)/(2c-2) is increasing for c>2, since both
c^2 and(c-2)/(2(c-1)) are increasing and positive. Consequently

  beta_j<69277/77400<9/10.                                (I)

Also a>2/5: from1-1/m>=127/128 and c<73/30,
a>3810/9344>2/5. Because c-2<1/2, A_mass=a/(c-2)>4/5.
For j>=1, c>12/5 and the exact mass formula give

  S_j>(4/5)c^j-1>(23/60)c^j>c^j/3.                        (J)

The second inequality uses1<(5/12)c^j. The elementary one-sign objective
bound also gives E_par(S)<=3/(8S): bound w+(3/2)q by(3/2)(w+q) in its
proof and maximize t/(S+t)^2<=1/(4S). Thus(J) implies
E_par(S_j)<9/(8c^j).

The attached benchmark proof establishes B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^(m+1) from
the exact finite recurrence, without an assumed asymptotic constant.
Using k=m-j>=1, N-1>=1 and(I), we obtain

  B_(2^m-1)P_par
    <(9/8)(lambda/c)^m [lambda c^(-k)] beta_j^[2(N-1)]
    <(9/8)(1/2)(81/100)=729/1600.

Here(lambda/c)^m=(1+1/m)^(-m)<=1/2 by the binomial theorem, and
lambda c^(-k)<1 for k>=1. This proves the stated finite uniform gap.

## 4. The smallest first-turn level

If j=0 then(A) says u_n<=a. By monotonicity u_i<=a at every query. Every
step has excess d_level>=a; all steps turn unless there is absorption.
Writing x_i=r_i(1+u_i), the exact horizontal update gives

  |x_(i+1)|/|x_i|=(d_level-u_i)/(1+u_i)<=d_level.

There are2^m-1 steps and the sum of their levels is2^m-1-m by the same
binary count. Since a c=1-1/m,

  |x_n|/|x_0|<=a^(2^m-1)c^(2^m-1-m)
                =(1-1/m)^(2^m-1)c^(-m).

At any parabolic state, 2F_par(X)<=x^2, where x is the horizontal
coordinate: by direct subtraction the difference is
r^2[u+u^2-r^2/2]>=0 because u>=r^2. Hence its normalized payoff is at
most the squared displayed ratio. The exact benchmark bound then gives
B P<=lambda^(m+1)c^(-2m)<=lambda^(1-m), proving(C).

## 5. The actual remaining charge, with exact identities

This result allows any number of turns but assumes the terminal normal state
has not passed the first turning excess. It cannot be restarted for free
when u crosses d_j: the remaining word is then only a partial recursive block,
and its first incoming state already contains the prior turn history.

Two exact identities preserve that history for a possible future charge.
Let x_i=r_i(1+u_i), q_i=r_i^2 and define

  Energy_i=x_i^2+v_i^2-v_0^2, Energy_0=R_0^2.

The two-coordinate recursions x_plus=x-h r, v_plus=v+h r^2 give

  Energy_(i+1)-Energy_i=h_i(h_i-2)q_i(1+q_i),
  u_(i+1)-u_i=(h_i-1)q_i+q_(i+1).                         (K)

For the first identity expand both squares and substitute
x_i r_i=q_i(1+v_i+q_i); the v terms cancel. Also Energy_i>=x_i^2 because
v_i>=v_0. This is an AUXILIARY identity; it does not assert that the
rescaled two-dimensional field is a Euclidean gradient, or that Energy
is monotone at steps above2. Its initial value is the TRUE initial squared
distance, so the free vertical starting coordinate is not charged as norm.

A useful next bound must combine the positive large-step terms in(K) with
the normal-level crossing they cause, retaining the partially completed
word. Merely declaring those terms nonpositive, resetting v, or multiplying
full-block bounds across an unproved cut would be invalid. No such bound
is yet established here.


# Complete internal preliminary proof (C63)

# C63: a shared-state block bound closes the large horizontal parabolic regime

Status: complete UNVERIFIED analytic candidate following the bounded direct
C60 experiment. No new fact_submit. Accepted b98bb807d514e80d is used for
the exact benchmark definitions; every further estimate below is derived
internally. C60's unverified formulas are reproduced and proved here.

The result is uniform over an explicit domain of initial states and, in
Section8, over EVERY trajectory with at most one horizontal sign change.
It is NOT an upper bound on every parabolic start or on unrestricted W_n(h).

## 1. Result, with the actual physical parameters

For m>=5 put

  lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
  H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
  n=2^m-1, S=sum H_m, M=1+S.

All these parameters remain fixed throughout the complete word H_m.
Consider the ONE function and initial state defined in Section2. Its
parameters are r_0!=0,v_0>=0. Let

  R=|r_0|(1+v_0+r_0^2),
  E_par(S)=(2S+3)^2/[8(S+1)^2(2S+1)].

If

                     R >= S sqrt(c-2),                     (1)

then every r_i has the same strict sign as r_0, and its actual normalized
last-iterate objective satisfies

  P_par(H_m;r_0,v_0)<=E_par(S)<1/(2S+1).                    (2)

In particular(1) holds uniformly for ALL initial states

                     r_0^2>=M^(2/3), v_0>=0.               (3)

For the EXACT Zhang--Jiang benchmark U_n^ZJ=1/B_n from the accepted fact,

  B_(2^m-1) sup_(states satisfying(1)) P_par
       <=lambda^(m+1) E_par(S),
  limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) sup_(states satisfying(1)) P_par
       <=lambda/[4 exp(1)]<1/4.                            (4)

No asymptotic equality for B_n is assumed. Section6 proves the scalar upper
envelope needed in(4) directly from its exact finite recurrence.

The payoff bound in(2) also holds for ANY finite nonnegative schedule of
total mass S>=1/2 whenever its whole parabolic trajectory keeps one sign
(allowing absorption at zero). Thus the candidate bound is not inferred
from the finite sample portfolio. What is particular to the ruler is the
proved sufficient initial-state condition(1).

## 2. One global legal function, every pair, and true distance

In R2 define

  K_par={(t,s):s>=t^2/sqrt(2)},
  F_par(X)=max_(g in K_par)(<X,g>-||g||^2/2).

The maximizer is the unique Euclidean projection onto this nonempty closed
convex set: complete the square, use coercivity for existence and strict
convexity for uniqueness. The normal inequalities at two projection points
give firm nonexpansiveness. Comparing the defining maxima shows that F_par
is differentiable with gradient equal to the projection; it is globally
convex and1-smooth. In detail, for the projection p(X),
||p(X)-p(Y)||^2<=<p(X)-p(Y),X-Y>, and
0<=F_par(Y)-F_par(X)-<p(X),Y-X>
 <=<p(Y)-p(X),Y-X><=||Y-X||^2.

For r real and v>=0 put

  u=v+r^2,
  X(r,v)=(r(1+v+r^2),-v/sqrt(2)),
  G(r)=(r,r^2/sqrt(2)).

One has X-G=u(r,-1/sqrt(2)). For any(t,s) in K_par,
<X-G,(t,s)-G><=-(u/2)(t-r)^2<=0. Thus G(r) is the actual gradient
at X(r,v), and substitution gives

  F_par(X(r,v))=r^2(1+v)/2+3r^4/4.                          (5)

For EVERY ordered pair of such samples the complete interpolation residual is

  Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2
      =<X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j>
      =-(v_j+r_j^2)(r_i-r_j)^2/2<=0.                       (6)

The identity follows by writing f_i=<X_i,G_i>-||G_i||^2/2 and expanding.
There is no adjacent-only interpolation condition in this construction.

The minimizer set of F_par is exactly{(0,y):y<=0}. Such a point gives a
nonpositive inner product with every feasible gradient, and0 is feasible.
A point with positive vertical coordinate has a positive value by testing
(0,s) with small positive s. A point with nonzero horizontal coordinate
has a positive value by testing(t,t^2/sqrt(2)) with small t of the same
horizontal sign; the linear term dominates the quadratic and quartic terms.
Hence the closest minimizer to X(r_0,v_0) is(0,-v_0/sqrt(2)), and the
true squared distance is R^2=r_0^2(1+v_0+r_0^2)^2.

For every physical step h>=0 actual GD is described by

  v_plus=v+h r^2,
  r_plus^3+(1+v_plus)r_plus=r(1+v+r^2-h).                  (7)

The cubic's derivative is1+v_plus+3r_plus^2>=1, so it has exactly one real
solution. The horizontal and vertical coordinates in(7) are exactly those
of X-hG. This proves actual GD for the same global F_par at every step.
The normalized payoff is

  P_par=[r_n^2(1+v_n)+(3/2)r_n^4]/R^2.                    (8)

Reflection of the horizontal coordinate sends r to-r and leaves all values
and v unchanged. Thus it suffices to prove the remaining statements with
r_0>0. If r ever becomes zero it remains zero by(7) and the payoff is zero.

## 3. Quantitative block map with one shared vertical state

First suppose a consecutive actual block of total mass T has positive
r-values throughout. At one step, the sign is retained exactly when
h<1+v+r^2. The increasing cubic in(7), evaluated at the OLD positive r,
exceeds its right side by h r(1+r^2)>=0. Consequently

                       0<r_plus<=r.                       (9)

Write the entry state(r_A,v_A), exit state(r_B,v_B), and horizontal
coordinate x=r(1+v+r^2). Telescoping the two ACTUAL recursions gives

  Delta_x=x_A-x_B=sum_(block)h_i r_i,
  Delta_v=v_B-v_A=sum_(block)h_i r_i^2.

Because r_B<=r_i<=r_A, the following complete finite bounds hold:

  T r_B<=Delta_x<=T r_A,
  r_B Delta_x<=Delta_v<=r_A Delta_x,
  T r_B^2<=Delta_v<=T r_A^2,
  Delta_x^2<=T Delta_v.                                   (10)

The final inequality is weighted Cauchy--Schwarz; at T=0 both sides vanish.
In particular the nonlinear block map obeys

  r_B[1+v_B+r_B^2+T]<=r_A(1+v_A+r_A^2).                   (11)

These estimates compose along H_(j+1)=(H_j,b_j,H_j), where b_j=1+a c^j,
by using the ACTUAL exit(r_B,v_B) of the left block as the bridge input,
then the bridge's exit as the right block input. The right copy's v is
never restarted or frozen. Equations(10)--(11) therefore control full
nonlinear blocks with all finite masses and all inherited v explicitly
present; no limiting differential equation is used.

## 4. The first possible turn has a quantitative initial-radius cost

Consider a first step whose output r is nonpositive. All preceding states
were positive and decreasing by(9). Let P be the total earlier step mass,
h this step, r its positive input, v its input vertical state, q=r^2,
and u=v+q. Equation(7) forces h>=1+u. Also the prefix bounds(10) give

  v-v_0>=P q,  x_0-x<=sqrt(P(v-v_0)),  x=r(1+u).

Therefore v>=Pq, u<=h-1, and

  x_0<=h sqrt(q)+sqrt(Pv).

For fixed u with v=u-q, the condition v>=Pq says 0<=q<=u/(P+1).
On this interval h sqrt(q)+sqrt(P(u-q)) is nondecreasing in q. For P>0
this follows by differentiation, because h>=1 and u-q>=Pq imply
h^2(u-q)>=Pq. For P=0 it follows directly. Its maximum is therefore
(P+h)sqrt(u/(P+1)). We have proved the necessary condition for a first
turn OR a first annihilation:

  x_0<=(P+h) sqrt[(h-1)/(P+1)].                             (12)

This estimate retains all previous gradient energy in v-v_0; it does not
replace the old trajectory by an independent block instance.

For the actual ruler let S_j=sum H_j and M_j=1+S_j, retaining the SAME
c,a from the enclosing horizon m. Directly from the concatenation,

  M_(j+1)=2M_j+a c^j,
  M_j=A_mass c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j, A_mass=a/(c-2).             (13)

Here 0<a<c-2. Indeed, writing epsilon=1/m and using lambda^2=2lambda+1,

  c(c-2)-(1-epsilon)
    =epsilon(2lambda+3)+lambda^2 epsilon^2>0.

Thus0<A_mass<1, and for every level j

                      a c^j<(c-2) M_j.                    (14)

Before any level-j step the elapsed prefix mass P is at least S_j: the
first occurrence of that level is immediately after its left H_j, and
every later occurrence is later in the positive word. Since h-1=a c^j,

                (h-1)/(P+1)<c-2,  P+h<=S.                 (15)

Combining(12)--(15) makes x_0<S sqrt(c-2) necessary for any first turn or
annihilation. This contradicts(1), proving strict sign preservation for
the ENTIRE actual word, at every depth and every queried sample.

For m>=5, c-2<1: lambda<5/2 and1+1/m<=6/5 give c<3. If(3) holds,
R=|r_0|(1+v_0+r_0^2)>=|r_0|^3>=M>S sqrt(c-2). This proves the claimed
uniform inclusion without depending on any observed numerical state.

## 5. Exact terminal payoff bound for every one-sign trajectory

Apply(10)--(11) to the entire one-sign run, whose total mass is S>=1/2.
Let q=r_n^2 and w=1+v_n. The actual initial horizontal coordinate obeys

  R>=r_n(S+w+q),  w>=1+S q.

If r_n=0 the desired bound holds because the numerator vanishes. Otherwise
(8) gives

  P_par<=(w+(3/2)q)/(S+w+q)^2.                             (16)

Set t=w+q. The constraint on w gives t>=1+(S+1)q, so q<= (t-1)/(S+1).
Consequently the right side of(16) is at most

              [(2S+3)t-1]/[2(S+1)(S+t)^2], t>=1.

Its derivative has the sign of(2S+3)(S-t)+2. At S>=1/2 the maximizing
point t=S+2/(2S+3) lies in the stated domain. Substitution gives exactly

                 E_par(S)=(2S+3)^2/[8(S+1)^2(2S+1)].       (17)

Moreover E_par(S)<1/(2S+1), because
8(S+1)^2-(2S+3)^2=4S^2+4S-1>0 at S>=1/2. Finally
S E_par(S) tends to1/4. This proves(2) and a uniform bound on every
one-sign initial state, not only the sufficient domain(1).

## 6. Exact finite benchmark comparison

From accepted b98bb807d514e80d define P_n=S_circle(n)+1 and B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1.
Their recurrences, after substituting those shifts, are P_0=B_0=1 and

  P_n=max_(k+l=n-1) Omega(P_k,P_l),
  B_n=max_(k+l=n-1) G(P_k,B_l),
  Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
  G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2.

Here is a full proof of the needed comparator, so the earlier unverified
C54 calculation is not used as a premise. Set alpha=2lambda-1=lambda(4-lambda)
and Llin=(4x+lambda^2 y)/alpha. Both coefficients of Llin exceed1, so
Llin>=x+y. Direct expansion, using lambda^2=2lambda+1, gives

  alpha^2[Llin^2-(x+y)Llin-xy]
                   =(2x/lambda-sqrt(2)lambda y)^2>=0.

Thus Llin>=Omega(x,y), the positive root of z^2-(x+y)z-xy=0. At
z=lambda Omega(x,y), the polynomial with larger root G(x,lambda y) obeys

  z^2-(4x+lambda y)z+4x^2
      =x[4x+lambda^2 y-alpha Omega(x,y)]>=0.

Also z>=lambda(x+y)>=(4x+lambda y)/2, so it lies to the right of that
quadratic's vertex. Therefore G(x,lambda y)<=lambda Omega(x,y) for all
x,y>=0. Monotonicity of G in its second variable and induction imply

                         B_n<=lambda P_n.                 (18)

Put rho=log_2 lambda>1, D(t)=(1+t)^rho-1 and ell(z)=log D(exp z).
For t=exp z, differentiation yields

  ell''(z)=rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)[(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/D(t)^2>0.

The bracket vanishes at0 and has positive derivative for t>0. Convexity
of ell therefore gives D(t)D(1/t)>=D(1)^2=2. For x,y>0 let
Z=(x^(1/rho)+y^(1/rho))^rho. Substitution gives
(Z-x)(Z-y)>=2xy and hence Z^2-(x+y)Z-xy>=0. Also Z>=x+y, by integrating
the increasing derivative of the positive power. It follows that
Omega(x,y)<=Z; zero arguments follow directly. Induction in the P recurrence
now gives P_n<=(n+1)^rho, and therefore

                     B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^(m+1).              (19)

Balanced joins in fact attain P_(2^m-1)=lambda^m, although that equality
is not needed for this upper comparison.

For the ACTUAL mass(13), A_mass tends to1, c^m/lambda^m=(1+1/m)^m tends
to exp(1), and (2/lambda)^m tends to0. Hence S/lambda^m tends to exp(1).
Combine(17),(19) to obtain both the finite inequality and the limsup in(4).
The strict comparison lambda/[4 exp(1)]<1/4 follows from
lambda<5/2<exp(1), the latter by the exponential series. No decimal limit
for the benchmark was assumed or evaluated by the experiment.

## 7. What the bounded experiment changed

The CLOSED ledger research/max3_c60_trajectory_budget.json records78 full
state-schedule attempts and0.8192669660056708 measured seconds, including
diagnostic repair and a read-only closeout audit. The remaining18 calls
expired. This is separate from the closed656 conic/PEP calls. No optimizer,
software installation or verifier call was used.

Three exact calibrations checked h=(0),r0=1/2,v0=3/4; h=(2),r0=1,v0=0;
and h=(10/3,50/9),r0=1/2,v0=0. Their exact terminal payoffs are17/32,0,
and518/225. All passed numerically, with scaled cubic residuals below
4e-16. The root formula used was
2sqrt(A/3)*sinh(asinh((3B/(2A))*sqrt(3/A))/3 for r^3+A r=B, A>0.

The first50 actual runs used ten initial recipes at depths4,6,8,10,12:
r0^2 in{1/16,1,m,sqrt(M),M/16,M/4,M,4M} with v0=0, plus
(r0^2,v0)=(1,sqrt(M)) and(sqrt(M),sqrt(M)). They suggested the intermediate
horizontal scale r0^2 proportional to M^(2/3), with many largest observed
payoffs occurring without a sign change. The next25 runs used
r0^2=k M^(2/3),v0=0, k in{1/16,1/4,1/2,1,2}, at the same five depths.

For the now-uniformly-excluded k=1 and2 recipes, the numerical M*payoffs
were respectively

  m4:  0.0746391227, 0.1281488193;
  m6:  0.0687903731, 0.1259430663;
  m8:  0.0684937234, 0.1263322527;
  m10: 0.0689648481, 0.1268277425;
  m12: 0.0694885381, 0.1272377691.

Those numbers motivated the proof; none is a premise. No exact B_n was
numerically evaluated or inferred from M. The proof instead uses(19).

Two depth10 runs completed with payoff underflow, and two depth12 runs
stopped at cubic RHS/root underflow; those are not exact zero trajectories.
One further payoff was subnormal. Raw states and original statuses remain
public. An underflow-sensitive turn diagnostic originally multiplied two
tiny r-values; saved-state companions correct it using separate sign tests,
without replaying any trajectory. The repair time is included in the ledger.
No original raw file was overwritten. All raw hashes were checked at closeout.

## 8. Every trajectory with just one turn is also uniformly excluded

This strengthening imposes NO initial-state bound(1). Suppose the actual
parabolic trajectory on H_m has exactly one horizontal sign change.
If it ever hits r=0 then all later values vanish, so only nonzero turns
need be considered. Reflect horizontally so its initial sign is positive.

The normal variable u_i=v_i+r_i^2 is nondecreasing for this entire physical
word, because(7) gives the exact identity

  u_(i+1)-u_i=(h_i-1)r_i^2+r_(i+1)^2>=0.                  (21)

Every h_i>1 here. Before the first turn, any previous step h_t preserved
positivity, so h_t<1+u_t. A later step h_i no larger than that previous
h_t then satisfies h_i<=h_t<1+u_t<=1+u_i and CANNOT turn. Consequently
the first turn occurs at a NEW RECORD step, necessarily the first occurrence
of some level j. In the actual recursive word that step is b_j=1+a c^j,
its prefix is exactly H_j with mass P=S_j, and its suffix mass is

  T=S_m-S_j-b_j>=S_(m-1).                                 (22)

The last inequality follows because S_j+b_j is increasing in j and the
top-level decomposition is S_m=2S_(m-1)+b_(m-1).

Let r>0,u be the state just before this first turn. The positive prefix
has decreasing r-values. Therefore its initial horizontal magnitude R
and the new magnitude R_after obey

  R=r(1+u)+sum_(t<i)h_t r_t>=r(P+1+u),
  R_after=r(h_i-1-u).

The numerator is positive precisely because this step turns. Hence

  R_after/R <=(h_i-1-u)/(P+1+u)
             <=(h_i-1)/(P+1)<c-2.                         (23)

The strict final inequality is(14)--(15), with the actual H_j prefix.
There is no restart of v: the tail starts at the ACTUAL state produced
by the turning step. By hypothesis there is no further turn, so Section5
applies to this suffix with its true initial distance R_after and mass T.
The function and its minimum0 remain identical. Thus

  2F_par(X_n)/R^2
    <=E_par(T)(R_after/R)^2
    <(c-2)^2 E_par(S_(m-1)).                               (24)

For monotonicity used here, logarithmic differentiation gives
E_par'(T)/E_par(T)=4/(2T+3)-2/(T+1)-2/(2T+1)<0; the first term is already
strictly smaller than2/(T+1). The suffix mass in(22) is at least1/2.

Since S_(m-1)/lambda^(m-1)->exp(1), the exact benchmark bound(19) gives

  limsup B_(2^m-1) sup_(all exactly-one-turn initial states) P_par
      <=lambda^2(lambda-2)^2/[4 exp(1)]
       =1/[4 exp(1)]<1/4.                                 (25)

The equality uses lambda(lambda-2)=1. Combining with the zero-turn estimate
(4), every initial state whose actual trajectory has at most one turn has
uniform benchmark limsup at most lambda/[4 exp(1)]<1/4. No initial norm,
vertical-state, amplitude, or smallness restriction was imposed on the
one-turn class. This is a proof about the full actual trajectory and its
retained normal state, not about a constant-gradient single-cut ansatz.

## 9. Remaining interface

Every parabolic start whose trajectory stays on one horizontal side is now
below even the global Huber lower witness by(17). Thus a useful parabolic
mechanism on this ruler must actually TURN. Condition(1) also quantifies
which initial horizontal scales cannot turn. The turning domain
0<R<S sqrt(c-2), with arbitrary coupled r0,v0, is not excluded here.

The k=1/4 finite starts had one turn and small observed M*payoff. Section8
now excludes the ENTIRE one-turn class, independently of those samples.
The k=1/16 starts had several turns; two or more turns remain open. A next
proof must retain how every turn transports BOTH the remaining horizontal
magnitude and the accumulated v into the actual suffix, with its unchanged
physical parameters. After the first turn, a later turn need not be a new
global record; applying the first-record argument afresh would be invalid.
Resetting v or treating the two H_j copies independently is also invalid.

This is a concrete uniform regime result with exact nonlinear block losses,
not a solution of the full parabolic family, the critical diagnostic, or the
original all-schedule exact-profile goal. All new statements remain drafts
until separately authorized independent verification.

evidence:
# Real character Grams: an explicit legal family and a cycle obstruction

Status: **self-contained joint candidate, not verifier accepted**. This is
round 14, the first round of the sixth max4 launch. No optimization,
parameter search, installation, or fact submission is used. The only
mathematical predecessors are accepted facts `1252b8823bb5a290` (the
necessary smooth-convex interpolation inequalities) and
`b98bb807d514e80d` (the exact benchmark and its elementary bound).
All new formulas used below are proved in this document. The anchored
simplex draft `016467bc5c3eb666` was a construction lead, not a premise.

There are two precisely specified generating rules here.

* Section 2 gives a legal nonuniform character family for every finite
  schedule with all steps strictly greater than 1. It has a common anchor,
  one explicit projection function, all ordered interpolation comparisons,
  and an exact certificate for the true distance. Its exact payoff is
  exponentially small. It is a calibration construction, not a proposed
  sharp lower bound.
* Sections 3--5 study product character weights, with amplitudes defined
  explicitly by saturating every adjacent cocoercivity constraint. All
  characters can be present, including the highest frequencies. For every
  actual critical ruler word H_m with m>=4, every nondegenerate member of
  this policy violates a quantitative three-sample cycle inequality.
  This excludes that policy, not general character kernels or arbitrary
  amplitudes. Section 6 identifies the necessary slack that a different
  amplitude rule must supply.

## 1. Conventions and the fixed-function interface

Normalize smoothness to 1. A schedule h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) has exactly n
algorithm steps and N=n+1 sampled gradients. For vectors g_i and an anchor
X_0 put X_i=X_0-sum_(t<i) h_t g_t. Write

    K_ij=<g_i,g_j>,
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.       (1)

Every ordered Q_ij is nonpositive for legal convex 1-smooth samples, by
accepted fact 1252b8823bb5a290. The optimum sample is (0,0,0) when used.

For a finite convex hull C=conv(0,g_0,...,g_n), define the ONE function

    F_C(X)=max_(v in C)(<X,v>-||v||^2/2).             (2)

Here C and the anchor will be fixed before the trajectory is run. The
maximizer is the Euclidean projection P_C(X), since completing the square
turns the maximization into nearest-point minimization. Existence follows
from compactness; strict convexity of squared distance gives uniqueness.
A vector g in C is this projection exactly when

    <X-g,v-g><=0 for every v in C.                   (3)

Necessity follows by differentiating squared distance along every segment
from g into C. Conversely, expansion of ||X-v||^2 proves sufficiency.
Adding (3) for X and X' gives
||P_C(X)-P_C(X')||^2 <= <X-X',P_C(X)-P_C(X')>.
Comparing the two maximizing expressions in (2) bounds the remainder in
the first-order expansion of F_C by ||X-X'||^2. Thus F_C is differentiable,
grad F_C=P_C, and its gradient is 1-Lipschitz. It is convex and finite.

Because 0 is a vertex, F_C>=0. Its minimizers are exactly the polar cone

    C^polar={Z:<Z,g_i><=0 for all i}.                 (4)

Indeed (3) says P_C(Z)=0 exactly on this cone. These observations prove
the realization interface used below without assuming the C62 draft.

For any proposed samples satisfying (3), set Y_i=X_i-g_i and
f_i=<X_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2. Direct expansion gives

    <Y_i,g_j-g_i>=Q_(j,i),
    <Y_i,-g_i>=-f_i+||g_i||^2/2.                    (5)

Thus checking every vertex, including 0, checks all normals; (2) then
interpolates the stated values and gradients at the prescribed GD points.

## 2. A legal nonuniform character policy with exact true distance

Assume n>=1 and every h_i>1. Define explicit scalar parameters

    H=max_i h_i,
    kappa=min(1,(min_i h_i-1)/4),
    zeta=kappa/(8H),
    eta=kappa/[8(H+kappa+1)],
    gamma_i=eta^i, 0<=i<=n.                          (6)

In particular h_i>=1+4kappa, 0<zeta<1/8, 0<eta<1/8,
zeta H=kappa/8, and (kappa+1)eta<=kappa/8.

Choose d to be the least integer with D=2^d>=N, and use the distinct
standard binary labels of i=0,...,n in F_2^d. No samples or physical steps
are appended. For s in F_2^d let chi_s(i)=(-1)^(s dot i), with the dot
product computed modulo 2 only to select the real sign. Set

    w_0=zeta+(1-zeta)/D,
    w_s=(1-zeta)/D for s!=0,
    g_i=(gamma_i sqrt(w_s) chi_s(i))_(s in F_2^d).     (7)

All D weights are strictly positive and they are nonuniform. For distinct
labels, half the characters have each sign: pairing s with s+e_l for a bit
where the labels differ proves this directly. Hence

    K_ii=gamma_i^2,
    K_ij=zeta gamma_i gamma_j for i!=j,
    K=diag(gamma) C_0 diag(gamma),
    C_0=(1-zeta)I_N+zeta 11^T.                        (8)

This is positive definite, including when N<D. Here 1 is the N-vector
whose entries are all 1, not the constant character itself.

The anchor and the values are also explicit. Put

    v_i=(kappa+1)gamma_i+zeta sum_(t<i) h_t gamma_t,
    tau=zeta sum_i v_i/[1+(N-1)zeta],
    u_i=(v_i-tau)/[(1-zeta)gamma_i],
    X_0=sum_i u_i g_i,
    f_i=(kappa+1/2)gamma_i^2.                         (9)

The letter u here denotes anchor coefficients, not algorithm steps.
Multiplication of (8) shows

    C_0^(-1)=(1-zeta)^(-1)
                  [I_N-zeta 11^T/(1+(N-1)zeta)],
    <X_0,g_i>=gamma_i v_i
       =(kappa+1)gamma_i^2+sum_(t<i)h_t K_ti.         (10)

In particular <X_i,g_i>=(kappa+1)gamma_i^2 and
<X_i-g_i,g_i>=kappa gamma_i^2>0.

### 2.1 Every original ordered comparison

For i<j, substitute (8)--(10) into (1). The two orientations are

    Q_(j,i)=(kappa+1)gamma_j^2-kappa gamma_i^2
         +(h_i-1)zeta gamma_i gamma_j
         +zeta gamma_j sum_(i<t<j)h_t gamma_t,         (11)

    Q_(i,j)=(kappa+1-h_i)gamma_i^2-kappa gamma_j^2
         -zeta gamma_i gamma_j
         -zeta gamma_i sum_(i<t<j)h_t gamma_t.         (12)

For (11), gamma_j/gamma_i<=eta and the geometric sum bounds its right
side divided by gamma_i^2 by

    (kappa+1)eta^2+zeta H eta/(1-eta)-kappa
       <= kappa/64+kappa/56-kappa <0.                (13)

Equation (12) is at most -3kappa gamma_i^2<0. The optimum comparisons are

    Q_(star,i)=-kappa gamma_i^2<0,
    Q_(i,star)=0.                                   (14)

Equations (5) and (11)--(14) prove all vertex normals for the ONE function
(2) with the gradients (7). Consequently actual GD from the anchor (9)
has exactly the supplied gradients and values, in the given order.
There are no independent function values assigned to characters.

### 2.2 Actual polar distance and a complementarity certificate

We next prove u_i>0 in (9); this is essential to the exact denominator.
The sequence v_i is strictly decreasing because

    v_(i+1)-v_i
      =gamma_i[zeta h_i-(kappa+1)(1-eta)]
      <=gamma_i[kappa/8-(kappa+1)+kappa/8]<0.          (15)

Moreover v_n>=zeta h_0 and, for every i,
v_i-v_n<=(kappa+1)gamma_i. Set D_0=1+(N-1)zeta. Then

    D_0(v_n-tau)
      =(1-zeta)v_n-zeta sum_i(v_i-v_n)
      >=zeta[h_0(1-zeta)-(kappa+1)/(1-eta)].          (16)

Since h_0 zeta<=kappa/8 and h_0>=1+4kappa, the first term in brackets
is at least 1+31kappa/8. The second is at most
1+kappa+2(kappa+1)eta<=1+5kappa/4, using eta<1/2.
The bracket is strictly positive. Thus v_i>=v_n>tau and every u_i>0.

For Z in C^polar, (9) now gives <X_0,Z><=0. Therefore

    ||X_0-Z||^2=||X_0||^2+||Z||^2-2<X_0,Z>
                  >=||X_0||^2.                     (17)

The point 0 is in C^polar and achieves equality. Thus 0 is the actual
closest minimizer to X_0, even though F_C can have other minimizers.
Equivalently, u is a strictly positive maximizer in the polar formula
max_(a>=0)(2b^T a-a^T K a), where b_i=<g_i,X_0>: it satisfies Ku=b
and zero stationarity residual, hence complementarity. To check the
maximization directly, for any a the objective is
b^T K^(-1)b-(a-u)^T K(a-u).

The TRUE squared initial distance is consequently

    R^2=||X_0||^2
       =[sum_i v_i^2-zeta(sum_i v_i)^2/D_0]/(1-zeta). (18)

No replacement of the polar distance by the norm to an arbitrary
minimizer has been made. Its equality to that norm follows from (17).

The exact normalized final payoff is

    V_eq(h)=(2kappa+1)eta^(2n)/R^2.                  (19)

Since ||g_0||=1 and <X_0,g_0>=kappa+1, one has
R^2>=(kappa+1)^2. Hence

    0<V_eq(h)<=eta^(2n)<64^(-n).                    (20)

Accepted fact b98bb807d514e80d gives B_n<=1+4n^p for p=log_2 3<2,
so B_n V_eq(h)<(1+4n^p)64^(-n)->0 uniformly over this policy's schedules.
It therefore cannot give the exact profile lower bound.

This failure also occurs in a concrete excess-total-step regime: for
n>=8 take every h_i=n. Then s(h)=n^2 and
4n^p<2n^2 (at n=8 this is 108<128, and n^(2-p) increases).
Thus 1/(1+2s(h))<1/B_n. Both that Huber witness and (19) miss 1/B_n.
For the latter assertion, 1+4n^p<=5n^2<=5*4^(n-1)<64^n for n>=1;
the middle bound follows inductively from (n+1)^2/n^2<=4.
These statements concern the displayed witnesses, not W_n(h).

The scope h_i>1 is intentional; this rule does not cover h_i<=1 or zero
steps. Its non-dyadic version changes the ambient character space, not
the physical horizon, and every comparison above is with the original B_n.

## 3. A different policy: product weights and maximal adjacent amplitudes

Fix any integer d>=1 and distinct chronological binary labels i with
0<=i<=n<2^d. Choose bit correlations -1<rho_l<1, 0<=l<d. They may
depend on the whole prescribed schedule and horizon. Define

    w_s=product_(l=0)^(d-1) ((1+(-1)^(s_l)rho_l)/2),
    c_ij=product_(l: i_l!=j_l)rho_l,
    g_i=(gamma_i sqrt(w_s)chi_s(i))_s.                (21)

Expanding the product of the d two-term sums proves directly that
sum_s w_s chi_s(i)chi_s(j)=c_ij. In particular sum_s w_s=1 and
K_ij=gamma_i gamma_j c_ij. All weights are strictly positive, so the
full Walsh matrix gives independent gradients at distinct labels.
No limit on chronological coordinate jumps is imposed.

For h_i>1, set gamma_0=1 and prescribe

    k_i=c_(i,i+1),
    r_i=[-(h_i-2)k_i
             +sqrt((h_i-2)^2 k_i^2+4(h_i-1))]/2,
    gamma_(i+1)=r_i gamma_i.                         (22)

This is a concrete positive finite formula, not an unknown amplitude
optimization. The r_i is the largest positive adjacent amplitude ratio
allowed by cocoercivity: indeed

    Q_(i,i+1)+Q_(i+1,i)
       =gamma_i^2[r_i^2+(h_i-2)k_i r_i+1-h_i]=0.     (23)

Every adjacent sum is thus exactly zero independently of the values f_i
and anchor. If the entire transcript were legal, each of its two terms
would be zero. The question is whether all the other pairs can coexist
with these local equalities. The following calculation answers it for
the actual critical ruler words.

## 4. Exact triangle identities on three chronological samples

Temporarily label three consecutive samples 0,1,2, with local steps
1+t,1+u, where t,u>0. The local labels need not be their original binary
labels. Suppose their normalized correlations are

    corr(g_0,g_1)=p,
    corr(g_0,g_2)=z,
    corr(g_1,g_2)=p z.                               (24)

Put A=||g_0||>0, r=||g_1||/A>0, q=||g_2||/A>0. Define

    d_1=r^2+(t-1)pr-t,
    d_2=q^2+(u-1)rpzq-u r^2,
    U=t+pr, V=1-pr.                                 (25)

Thus Q_01+Q_10=A^2 d_1 and Q_12+Q_21=A^2 d_2. For arbitrary assigned
values define the two directed triangle sums

    T_rev=Q_20+Q_12+Q_01,
    T_fwd=Q_02+Q_10+Q_21.                            (26)

The anchor and every f_i cancel from these sums. Their exact values are

    T_rev/A^2=d_2+U(qz-1),
    T_fwd/A^2=(1+u)d_1+d_2+V(tu-qz).                (27)

Here is a derivation retaining their orientation. For any anchor set
Y_i=X_i-g_i and N_ij=<Y_i,g_j-g_i>. The array N_ij equals Q_(j,i)
when the values are <X_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2. For any other values the
differences are vertex-potential differences and cancel around a cycle.
Let alpha=N_01 and beta=N_12. Since Y_0-Y_1=tg_0+g_1 and
Y_1-Y_2=ug_1+g_2, expansion gives

    N_10=A^2 d_1-alpha, N_21=A^2 d_2-beta,
    N_02=alpha+beta+A^2[U(qz-1)-d_1],
    N_20=A^2(d_1+d_2)-alpha-beta
                       -A^2[V(qz-tu)-u d_1].        (28)

For the third equality use
r(tp+r)=U+d_1. For the fourth use
r(r-p)=tV+d_1. Summing the appropriate orientations in (28) proves
(27) for arbitrary original values.

Multiplying (27) by V and U respectively yields the identity

    V T_rev+U T_fwd
       =A^2[(U+V)d_2+U(1+u)d_1+UV(tu-1)].           (29)

Under adjacent saturation, d_1=d_2=0. If -1<p<1 then U,V>0 and

    U+V=1+t,
    UV=r^2(1-p^2).                                 (30)

For completeness, r is the positive root of
P(r)=r^2+(t-1)pr-t. If p>0 then P(1/p)=1/p^2-1>0, so pr<1;
if p<=0, V>0 directly. If p<0 then P(-t/p)=t^2(1/p^2-1)>0,
so pr>-t; if p>=0, U>0 directly. The product identity in (30) follows
by substituting d_1=0 in (25).

All six coefficients on the left side of (29) are positive and their
sum is 3(U+V). It follows for ANY anchor and ANY assigned values that

    max_(i!=j in {0,1,2}) Q_ij
       >= (1-p^2)||g_1||^2 (tu-1)/[3(1+t)].         (31)

If tu>1 this is a strict positive obstruction to full interpolation.
It is not merely an inability to choose a convenient anchor or a
failure of one individual function-value assignment.

## 5. Apply the obstruction to the actual H_m, without padding

For a fixed enclosing horizon m>=4 set

    sigma=1+sqrt(2), c=sigma(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    n=2^m-1.                                       (32)

The same a,c are retained inside all subwords. Equivalently the original
step at i is 1+a c^(nu_2(i+1)), where nu_2 is the exponent of 2 dividing
the positive integer i+1. Use the standard chronological binary labels
of the n+1 actual samples in (21).

For any level 3<=k<=m-1, take consecutive original samples

    j_0=2^k-2, j_1=2^k-1, j_2=2^k.                 (33)

Their two actual steps are 1+a and 1+a c^k. Their correlations in (21)
have exactly the form (24), with

    p=rho_0, z=product_(l=1)^k rho_l.                (34)

Indeed the first change flips only bit 0; the last pair flips bits 0
through k; and the outer pair flips bits 1 through k. The higher bits
are unchanged. The same calculation applies to every level-k bridge,
not just the first occurrence in (33).

By (22), d_1=d_2=0. Here t=a<sqrt(2)-1<1/2, u=a c^k, and

    tu=a^2 c^k=(1-1/m)^2 c^(k-2)
       >=(9/16)sigma>9/8.                           (35)

Consequently the original six residuals on (33), for every anchor and
every possible value array, obey

    max Q_ij > (1-rho_0^2)||g_(j_1)||^2/36 >0.       (36)

This excludes the entire product-weight/adjacent-saturation policy on
every actual H_m with m>=4. The bit weights can depend arbitrarily on
m and h inside -1<rho_l<1; there are 2^m positive character weights;
the high-frequency characters are not discarded. No normalized dual
tensor-array obstruction is used: this is an identity for the proposed
PRIMAL gradients and the original interpolation residuals.

For a non-dyadic horizon, the same local obstruction applies whenever
the original unpadded word contains a triple of the form (24) with tu>1.
No universal claim about other non-dyadic words follows.

### Singular boundary is a real escape, with a weak explicit example

The condition |rho_0|<1 cannot be removed from (36). Set rho_0=-1 and
rho_l=1 for l>=1. Only the parity character s=e_0 then has nonzero
weight. With (22), r_i=h_i-1 and the scalar gradients are

    g_i=(-1)^i product_(t<i)(h_t-1).

They are exactly the legal trajectory of F(x)=x^2/2 from x_0=1. This
is a concrete counterexample to extending the impossibility statement
to all singular product kernels. On (32), the exact terminal payoff is

    V_sing=product_(i<n)(h_i-1)^2
          =(1-1/m)^(2n) c^(-2m).                    (37)

To check the last equality, among i+1=1,...,2^m-1 the number with
nu_2(i+1)=k is 2^(m-k-1). Their valuations sum to
sum_(l=1)^(m-1)(2^(m-l)-1)=2^m-m-1=n-m;
hence the product is a^n c^(n-m)=(ac)^n c^(-m), and ac=1-1/m.
The true initial distance is 1. This singular escape is also far below
the exact benchmark, since B_n V_sing<=(1+4n^p)(1-1/m)^(2n)c^(-2m)->0.
For example (1-1/m)^(2n)<=exp(-2n/m), which dominates the polynomial
factor when n=2^m-1. No perturbation argument transfers legality or
constants from this singular example to positive weights.

## 6. Necessary repair cost for unsaturated amplitudes

Retain the product triple (24) and arbitrary positive amplitudes. Define
the actual adjacent cocoercivity slacks

    S_01=-(Q_01+Q_10)=-A^2 d_1,
    S_12=-(Q_12+Q_21)=-A^2 d_2.                      (38)

For a legal transcript these are nonnegative. If |p|<1 and d_1<=0,
then r is at most the positive root of P from Section 4. The same
root estimates used there give U>0,V>0. Therefore every legal
transcript with these three gradients must satisfy, by (29),

    (1+t)S_12+U(1+u)S_01 >= A^2 UV(tu-1).           (39)

If the leaf edge stays saturated, S_01=0 and UV A^2=(1-p^2)||g_1||^2.
Then the bridge alone must pay

    S_12 >= (1-p^2)||g_1||^2(tu-1)/(1+t).            (40)

Thus changing the product weights while retaining all adjacent roots
cannot repair the failure. An amplitude mutation must introduce the
quantified local slack, or a weight mutation must break the correlation
factorization (24), or the construction must use a genuinely singular
case with a separate analysis. These are necessary alternatives only.
Equations (39)--(40) do not imply all other ordered pairs, supply a
common anchor for a repaired policy, or determine an exact payoff.

## 7. Literature engagement and remaining task

Matlas searches for the product Walsh and GD construction mechanisms
returned no directly applicable theorem. The exact paper by Arthur C.
Campello, *Density Estimation on the Binary Hypercube using Transformed
Fourier-Walsh Diagonalizations*, arXiv:2304.05053 (2023), was downloaded
to downloads/2304.05053.pdf. Its Sections 2.1 and 2.3, including the
derivation of the product kernel in equations (26)--(28), were read
through the built-in PDF parser after local pdftotext and Python PDF
libraries were found unavailable. No installation was attempted.

The paper concerns density kernels. Its product structure informs the
chosen correlation policy; it supplies no chronological GD normal
inequality. No external mathematical result is imported into the proof:
the character identities, projection realization, cycle formulas, and
normalization are all derived above.

The original all-schedule exact-profile problem remains unresolved.
The remaining character direction is a concrete non-saturating or
non-product policy that passes the retained cycles AND every other
original pair, has a controlled true polar distance, and attains the
original B_n benchmark. The two rules resolved here do not do that.

evidence:
# An obstruction to adjacent saturation for arbitrary real character weights

Status: **self-contained unverified supplement from round 14**. No numerical
search, optimization, installation, or fact submission. Accepted fact
`1252b8823bb5a290` supplies only the necessary ordered interpolation
inequalities. Every further assertion used here is proved below. The earlier
round-14 product-kernel draft is awareness, not a mathematical predecessor.

This supplement removes the product-weight restriction from the saturation
obstruction, at the cost of a stronger condition on the two physical steps.
It rules out all nondegenerate real sign-kernel policies that saturate both
adjacent cocoercivity constraints at the indicated bridges of actual H_m.
It does NOT rule out arbitrary character amplitudes with nonzero slack.

## 1. The local sign constraint

Take three consecutive actual samples X_0,X_1,X_2, whose local GD steps are
h_0=1+t, h_1=1+u. These are temporary local indices. Let their gradients
have a common real sign representation

    g_i=(gamma_i sqrt(w_s) epsilon_(i,s))_s,
    w_s>=0, sum_s w_s=1, gamma_i>0, epsilon_(i,s) in {-1,1}.

In particular this includes every real character kernel, with arbitrary
nonnegative weights, on any three labels. Multiplying each coordinate by
epsilon_(0,s) does not change its Gram. Set

    A=gamma_0, r=gamma_1/gamma_0, s=gamma_2/gamma_1,
    p=<g_0,g_1>/(gamma_0 gamma_1),
    w=<g_1,g_2>/(gamma_1 gamma_2),
    z=<g_0,g_2>/(gamma_0 gamma_2).                    (1)

The local letter s is an amplitude ratio; it is not the coordinate index
in the preceding display. Regard the weights as a probability measure.
The signs B=epsilon_0 epsilon_1 and D=epsilon_1 epsilon_2 have means p,w,
and E[BD]=z. Since |B-D|=1-BD pointwise, the triangle inequality gives

    z<=1-|p-w|.                                    (2)

This is an elementary real-sign restriction, stronger than positive
semidefiniteness of a generic three-by-three correlation matrix. It needs
no independence of the weights or sign variables. For distinct character
labels and every character weight positive, p,w are strictly inside
(-1,1). The same is true for any nonnegative weights for which the two
adjacent gradients are not parallel or antiparallel.

Assume now

    1/3<t<1, u>1, (3t-1)u>=1+t,
    -1<p<1, -1<w<1,                               (3)

and that both adjacent cocoercivity comparisons are saturated. For
arbitrary values f_i define, as in accepted fact 1252b8823bb5a290,

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

The saturation conditions are exactly

    r^2+(t-1)pr-t=0,
    s^2+(u-1)ws-u=0.                               (4)

Evaluating these quadratics at t,1 and 1,u, respectively, proves

    t<r<1, 1<s<u,
    p=(r^2-t)/[(1-t)r],
    w=(u-s^2)/[(u-1)s].                            (5)

All endpoint signs are strict because of the nondegeneracy in (3).

## 2. One original three-sample cycle is necessarily positive

Set T=Q_02+Q_10+Q_21. Values and the anchor cancel from T. Expand the
three position differences using the two actual steps. Substituting (4)
in the resulting Gram expression gives

    T/A^2=u r(r-p)-r s(z-rw)
         =r s(Z_min-z),
    Z_min=rw+u(r-p)/s.                             (6)

For example, before substitution the Gram expression for T is
-t K_00+K_11+K_22+(t-u-1)K_01+u K_12-K_02, where K_ij=<g_i,g_j>.
The two equalities (4) reduce it to
u(K_11-K_01)+K_12-K_02, proving (6).

Write Z_max=1-|p-w|, so z<=Z_max by (2). The following two factorizations
prove Z_min>Z_max and quantify the positive original cycle.

If w<=p, define

    L_minus=[t(u-1)/r+tu-1]/(1-t).

Substitute (5) and factor to get

    Z_min-Z_max
       =(u-s)(1-r)(L_minus-s)/[s(u-1)].             (7)

For clarity this follows by first writing
s(Z_min-Z_max)=s w(r-1)+ur-s+(s-u)p, substituting w, and factoring
(u-s)[ru-1+(r-1)s-(u-1)p]/(u-1).
Substitution of p from (5) then gives (7).
Moreover

    L_minus-u
       =[t(u-1)(1/r-1)+(3t-1)u-t-1]/(1-t)>0.       (8)

The first term is strictly positive by (5) and the second is
nonnegative by (3). Equations (6)--(8) yield

    T >= A^2 r(u-s)(1-r)(L_minus-s)/(u-1)
       > A^2 r(u-s)^2(1-r)/(u-1)>0.                (9)

If w>=p, define

    L_plus=[t(u-1)/r+1-tu]/(1-t).

The other factorization is

    Z_min-Z_max
       =(u+s)(1+r)(L_plus-s)/[s(u-1)].              (10)

Here s(Z_min-Z_max)=s w(r+1)+ur-s-(u+s)p, and factoring gives
(u+s)[ru+1-(r+1)s-(u-1)p]/(u-1); (5) proves (10).

To show the last factor positive, let s_p be the positive root of
v^2+(u-1)pv-u=0. The function (u-v^2)/[(u-1)v] decreases strictly
for v>0, so w>=p implies s<=s_p. Also (3) implies tu>1, because
t(1+t)>(3t-1) is equivalent to (1-t)^2>0. The polynomial defining
s_p evaluated at v=1/r is

    (u-1/t)(p/r-1)<0.                              (11)

The first factor is positive. The second is negative since (4) gives
r(r-p)=t(1-pr)>0; alternatively substituting (5) gives r>p.
Thus r s_p>1. One has 1-p s_p>0: for p>0 the defining polynomial
at 1/p is 1/p^2-1>0; for p<=0 this is immediate.

At w=p, s=s_p and Z_max=1. Direct substitution in Z_min gives

    Z_min(s_p)-1
       =(1-p^2)(r s_p-1)/(1-p s_p)>0.              (12)

Apply (10) at s_p. Its other factors are positive, hence L_plus>s_p.
Therefore L_plus>s, and

    T >= A^2 r(u+s)(1+r)(L_plus-s)/(u-1)>0.         (13)

In either case at least one of the THREE actual ordered residuals
Q_02,Q_10,Q_21 is at least T/3>0. This holds for every anchor and
every value assignment. A legal convex 1-smooth function cannot realize
these three gradients with the two given steps. No optimum comparison
or additional remote comparison can remove the positive cycle.

## 3. Consequence for actual H_m and arbitrary character weights

Fix m>=32, sigma=1+sqrt(2), c=sigma(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c, and
H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j) for j<m. These are the actual
physical parameters at this enclosing horizon, not reset subword
parameters. The length is n=2^m-1.

Choose ANY nonnegative real character weights summing to 1, not necessarily
product weights. Take distinct labels for the actual n+1 chronological
samples, and positive amplitudes. Whenever the two adjacent normalized
correlations are in (-1,1), the sign inequality (2) applies. In particular
every strictly positive character-weight policy has this property.

At every level-k ruler bridge with k>=4, the preceding step is a leaf:
the two actual steps are 1+a and 1+a c^k. Thus t=a and u=a c^k.
We have

    3/8<a<1/2,
    u >= a c^4=(1-1/m)c^3 > (31/32)(12/5)^3
                                      =1674/125>11. (14)

For the first lower bound, sigma<5/2 and m>=32 give
a>(31/33)(2/5)=62/165>3/8; the upper bound follows from
a<1/sigma=sqrt(2)-1<1/2. For the bound on u use sigma>12/5.
The function (1+t)/(3t-1) decreases for t>1/3 and equals 11 at t=3/8.
Hence (3t-1)u>1+t. All hypotheses of Section 2 hold whenever the two
adjacent comparisons are saturated and nondegenerate.

Consequently every such saturation policy violates an original cycle
on every actual H_m with m>=32. For standard binary labels, one may use
samples 2^k-2,2^k-1,2^k. The proof in fact works for any distinct labels
assigned to those original samples: it uses the universal real-sign
constraint, not a permissible reordering of GD steps.

This strengthens the product-policy result in the first round-14 draft.
Weight dependencies alone cannot save an everywhere-saturated amplitude
policy at these bridges. Some adjacent slack or a separately analyzed
degenerate adjacent correlation is necessary. This is NOT an obstruction
to arbitrary real character Grams with freely changing amplitudes.

## 4. The stronger step condition cannot be replaced by tu>1

Here is an exact local counterexample to that proposed extension. Set

    t=2/5, u=5, r=99/100, s=24/5,
    p=5801/5940, w=-451/480,
    Z_max=1+w-p, Z_min=rw+u(r-p)/s,
    z=(Z_max+Z_min)/2.                              (15)

These parameters satisfy (4) and t u=2>1. However the hypothesis
(3t-1)u>=1+t fails: its two sides are 1 and 7/5. Both adjacent
correlations are strictly between -1 and 1. Equation (7), whose
algebra does not require (3), gives

    L_minus=1295/297 <24/5,
    Z_min-Z_max=-653/14256000<0.                    (16)

The four binary-character weights at labels 0,1,2 in F_2^2 are

    w_00=(1+p+z+w)/4,
    w_10=(1-p+z-w)/4,
    w_01=(1+p-z-w)/4,
    w_11=(1-p-z+w)/4.                              (17)

All are strictly positive. Direct substitution gives p>9/10,
-1<w<-9/10, and p+w>0. The exact correlation interval has length
Z_max-[-1+|p+w|]=2(1-p)=278/5940.
Its loss from Z_max to z is 653/28512000<1/1000<278/5940. Hence z lies strictly
inside both correlation endpoints, which is equivalent to positivity
of all four displayed weights.

With gamma=(1,r,rs), these weights give a positive definite three-gradient
Gram: the full four-label sign matrix is H tensor H for
H=[[1,1],[1,-1]], and H^2=2I proves row independence. Equation (6)
says T<0. The reverse triangle is

    T_rev/A^2=rs(tz+rw)-r(tp+r)<0:                  (18)

the first parentheses are negative (z,w<0), and tp+r>0.
Both adjacent sums vanish by (4). Thus assigning values to make each
adjacent orientation zero also makes BOTH remaining original finite
comparisons negative.

For completeness this local example extends to one actual projection
function, not just a Gram. Define D_0=(1+t)(K_00+K_01)/2 and
D_1=(1+u)(K_11+K_12)/2. Put
f_0=1+max_i K_ii/2+|D_0|+|D_1|, f_1=f_0-D_0,
f_2=f_1-D_1. Then f_i>K_ii/2 for all i, every adjacent Q is zero,
and the outer Q's are negative by (6),(18). Define
b_i=f_i+K_ii/2+sum_(j<i)h_j K_ji and X_0=sum_i(K^(-1)b)_i g_i.
Positive definiteness of K makes this explicit anchor finite. With
X_i=X_0-sum_(j<i)h_j g_j, expansion gives
<X_i-g_i,g_j-g_i>=Q_(j,i)<=0 and
<X_i-g_i,-g_i>=-f_i+K_ii/2<0. Thus the single function
max_(v in conv(0,g_0,g_1,g_2))(<X,v>-||v||^2/2) has exactly these
gradients and values on the two-step trajectory. Completing the square
identifies its gradient as projection; adding the projection normal
inequalities proves the gradient is 1-Lipschitz. It is finite, convex,
and minimized on the nonempty polar cone. This example makes no
payoff claim or claimed equality for its true initial distance.

The example prevents overextending the obstruction to all tu>1, while
Section 3 supplies the stronger condition at the actual higher bridges.

## 5. Status and next direction

Both results are unverified candidates. The precise original-task
obstruction is to the EXPLICIT rule that chooses the maximal positive
root of every adjacent cocoercivity inequality. The proof covers
arbitrary nonnegative character weights whenever the two tested
adjacent correlations are nondegenerate; it does not require product
weights, positive-only correlations, a fixed character count, bounded
conditioning, or chronological label symmetry.

The one-character quadratic with alternating signs remains a legitimate
singular escape and is quantitatively weak as calculated in the first
round-14 joint draft; that draft is not used as a proof premise here.
The next useful construction must specify non-saturating amplitudes
and control their all-pair and true-distance consequences. The original
all-schedule exact-profile target remains unresolved.
