# C65: an amortized threshold budget for the entire parabolic family

Status: COMPLETE PROOF DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. No fact_submit, trajectory experiment,
optimization, installation, or external theorem is used. This is a proposed
closure of the specified parabolic mechanism, NOT of the unrestricted
worst-case functional or the original all-schedule target. The accepted fact
b98bb807d514e80d supplies the definition of the exact benchmark. Every other
argument, including the earlier C60/C63/C64 derivations needed here, is proved
inside this document; those drafts are not assumed as predecessor facts.

## 1. Statement and scope

Fix an integer m>=128. Throughout the WHOLE word, including embedded words,
keep the following enclosing-horizon parameters fixed:

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    n=2^m-1, d_j=a*c^j, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

For this document only, H_j denotes these physical words, not the conjugate
quadratics with the same letter in accepted1252b8823bb5a290. All displayed
scalar r,u,v,x,q and block quantities below are local parabolic variables.

Define one function on the Euclidean plane by

    K_par={(t,s):s>=t^2/sqrt(2)},
    F_par(X)=max_(g in K_par)(<X,g>-||g||^2/2).

For arbitrary r_0!=0 and v_0>=0 start GD at

    X_0=(r_0(1+v_0+r_0^2),-v_0/sqrt(2))

and use the ACTUAL physical word H_m. Write the iterates as

    X_i=(x_i,-v_i/sqrt(2)),
    x_i=r_i(1+u_i), u_i=v_i+r_i^2, q_i=r_i^2.

The true initial squared distance to the minimizer set is

    R_0^2=r_0^2(1+v_0+r_0^2)^2=x_0^2.

The normalized payoff is

    P_par=2F_par(X_n)/R_0^2.

Let B_n=2 S_bullet(n)+1 be the exact Zhang--Jiang denominator defined by
accepted b98bb807d514e80d, with its full finite recurrence reproduced below.
The proposed conclusion is the UNIFORM proper-family bound

    sup_(r_0!=0,v_0>=0) B_(2^m-1) P_par <=729/1600<1/2.       (1)

In particular the previously open domain of two or more horizontal sign
changes WITH a crossing of the first turning threshold is included.

The proof gives the following stronger chronological assertions. Discard an
absorbing trajectory r_i=0, whose payoff is zero. If the first sign change
has level j>=1, put D=d_j. Then

    u_i<(39/20)D<d_(j+1)                                   (2)

at every sample after that turn, whenever j+1 is used as a comparison level.
Here d_(j+1)=cD is a defined number even at the last physical level. If the
first sign change has level0, then

    u_i<3/4<d_1                                            (3)

throughout the trajectory. Thus a first turning threshold may be crossed,
but the NEXT turning threshold cannot be crossed. This assertion is proved
by an inherited-state budget, not assumed as an ordering of turn levels.

For j>=1, set k=m-j, N=2^k,

    L=D/c, C=D/(M_j+L), beta=c*C,
    E(T)=(2T+3)^2/[8(T+1)^2(2T+1)].

The more detailed payoff bounds are

    P_par<=E(S_m)                              if there is no turn;
    P_par<=c^[-2(m-1)]                         if first-turn level j=0;
    P_par<=E(S_j) beta^[2(N-1)] c^(-2k)         if j>=1.       (4)

These conclusions concern exactly F_par and the specified starts and words.
They do not upper-bound W_n(H_m), do not weaken the accepted finite C59
adversary, and do not decide the original all-horizon/all-schedule problem.

## 2. One global function, every pair, the true distance, and actual GD

The set K_par is nonempty, closed and convex. Completing the square shows
that the maximum defining F_par is attained uniquely at the Euclidean
projection p(X) onto K_par: the equivalent minimization is coercive and
strictly convex. The projection normal inequalities at X and Y imply

    ||p(X)-p(Y)||^2<=<p(X)-p(Y),X-Y>.

Hence p is 1-Lipschitz. Comparing the two defining maxima gives

    0<=F_par(Y)-F_par(X)-<p(X),Y-X>
      <=<p(Y)-p(X),Y-X><=||Y-X||^2.

The remainder divided by ||Y-X|| tends to zero, so F_par is differentiable
with gradient p. It is convex as a supremum of affine functions, and its
gradient is 1-Lipschitz on the whole plane.

For r real and v>=0 define

    u=v+r^2,
    X(r,v)=(r(1+u),-v/sqrt(2)),
    G(r)=(r,r^2/sqrt(2)).

One has X-G=u(r,-1/sqrt(2)). For any (t,s) in K_par,

    <X-G,(t,s)-G><=-(u/2)(t-r)^2<=0.

Thus G(r) is the actual projection and gradient, and substitution yields

    F_par(X(r,v))=r^2(1+v)/2+3r^4/4.                       (5)

For EVERY ordered pair of such states, with f_i=F_par(X_i), expansion gives

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2
        =<X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j>
        =-(u_j/2)(r_i-r_j)^2<=0.                           (6)

The construction therefore retains every interpolation pair, not only the
consecutive pairs used in the estimates below.

The minimizer set is exactly {(0,y):y<=0}. At such points all feasible
inner products are nonpositive and the feasible gradient0 gives value0.
A point of positive vertical coordinate has positive value by testing a
small positive vertical gradient. A point of nonzero horizontal coordinate
has positive value by testing (t,t^2/sqrt(2)) with small t of the same
horizontal sign: the linear term dominates the higher powers of t. The
closest minimizer to X_0 is consequently (0,-v_0/sqrt(2)), which proves the
stated true denominator R_0^2. At a later block entry the corresponding
closest distance is its actual horizontal magnitude; the global minimum
value is still0 for this SAME function.

For a physical step h>=0, actual GD is exactly

    v_plus=v+h*r^2,
    r_plus^3+(1+v_plus)r_plus=r(1+v+r^2-h).                 (7)

The cubic's derivative is1+v_plus+3r_plus^2>=1, so it has one real root.
Equation(7) produces exactly the coordinates of X-hG. In particular

    x_plus=x-h*r,
    u_plus-u=(h-1)q+q_plus.                                (8)

Every step of H_m is greater than1, so u is nondecreasing on the actual
trajectory. This monotonicity is NOT asserted for arbitrary smaller steps.
A sign change occurs precisely when u<d_level; equality makes r_plus=0.
Once r is zero, all remaining r-values and objective values are zero.

Another useful pointwise bound, valid at every state, is

    2F_par(X)<=x^2.                                        (9)

Indeed, after substituting q=r^2 and u=v+q, the difference is
q[u+u^2-q/2]>=0 since u>=q.

## 3. One-sign blocks retain both coordinates

Suppose a consecutive actual block has a fixed nonzero sign. By horizontal
reflection it is enough to consider positive r. At a sign-preserving step,
the cubic in(7) evaluated at the OLD r exceeds its right side by h*r(1+r^2).
Since that cubic is increasing, 0<r_plus<=r. Thus for a whole block of mass T,
entry (r_A,v_A), and exit (r_B,v_B),

    Delta_x=x_A-x_B=sum h_i r_i,
    Delta_v=v_B-v_A=sum h_i r_i^2,
    T r_B<=Delta_x<=T r_A,
    r_B Delta_x<=Delta_v<=r_A Delta_x,
    T r_B^2<=Delta_v<=T r_A^2.                              (10)

For either sign, if R_A=|x_A| and u_B=v_B+r_B^2, this proves

    |r_B|(1+T+u_B)<=R_A.                                   (11)

If u_A>=L>=0, it also proves the following vertical charge, including for
any initial part of that block:

    Delta_v<=|r_A| R_A=R_A^2/(1+u_A)<=R_A^2/(1+L).          (12)

No old vertical state is discarded in (10)--(12).

For a complete one-sign trajectory of mass T>=1/2, put w=1+v_B and q=r_B^2.
Then R_A>=sqrt(q)(T+w+q), and w>=1+Tq, using v_A>=0. Thus its payoff with
the true entry distance is at most

    (w+(3/2)q)/(T+w+q)^2.

With t=w+q>=1, one has q<=(t-1)/(T+1), so this is at most

    [(2T+3)t-1]/[2(T+1)(T+t)^2].

The derivative has the sign of (2T+3)(T-t)+2. Its maximum on t>=1 is at
t=T+2/(2T+3), which belongs to that interval for T>=1/2. Substitution gives
E(T) as in(4). Two useful consequences are

    E(T)<=3/(8T)                  for T>=1/2;
    E(T)<9/(32T)                  for T>=8.                 (13)

For the first, bound w+(3/2)q by (3/2)(w+q) and use
t/(T+t)^2<=1/(4T); the displayed E(T) inherits this bound where it applies.
For the second,
T E(T)<[2+1/(T+1)]^2/16<=361/1296<9/32.

## 4. Physical masses, binary accounting, and fixed constants

The recursive mass identity is

    M_(j+1)=2M_j+d_j,
    M_j=A_mass*c^j+(1-A_mass)*2^j,
    A_mass=a/(c-2).                                        (14)

Here 0<a<c-2 and hence 0<A_mass<1. To check the nontrivial strict inequality,
write epsilon=1/m and use lambda^2=2lambda+1:

    c(c-2)-(1-epsilon)
      =epsilon(2lambda+3)+lambda^2 epsilon^2>0.

Consequently

    d_j/M_j<c-2.                                          (15)

For m>=128 the following convenient rational bounds hold:

    12/5<c<73/30<5/2,
    2/5<a<5/12,
    c-2<13/30,
    d_j>=d_1=1-1/m>=127/128                for j>=1.        (16)

For the upper bound on c, sqrt(2)<99/70 gives
c<(169/70)(129/128)=21801/8960<73/30. The lower bound c>12/5 follows from
sqrt(2)>7/5. Also a<(sqrt(2)-1)<5/12, and
a>(127/128)(30/73)=3810/9344>2/5.

Fix j>=1, D=d_j, L=D/c, M=M_j, delta=D/M, C=D/(M+L), beta=cC. Then

    beta=c*delta/(1+delta/c)
         <c^2(c-2)/(2c-2)
         <69277/77400<9/10,
    C<3/8.                                                (17)

The function c^2(c-2)/(2c-2) is increasing for c>2, because both c^2 and
(c-2)/(2(c-1)) are positive and increasing. Substitute c=73/30 for the
second inequality. The last bound uses c>12/5 and beta<9/10.

Let p_2(t) be the number of1s in the binary expansion of a nonnegative
integer t, and let nu_2(t) be the exponent of2 in a positive integer t.
Counting multiples of powers of2 gives

    sum_(k=1)^t nu_2(k)=t-p_2(t).                           (18)

For completeness, write t=sum_s e_s 2^s with e_s in{0,1}. Then
sum_(b>=1)floor(t/2^b)=sum_s e_s(2^s-1)=t-p_2(t).

H_m consists of N=2^(m-j) chronological H_j blocks, indexed
ell=0,...,N-1. Block ell starts at sample ell*2^j, with inherited state
(r_(ell*2^j),v_(ell*2^j)); its bridge input is sample (ell+1)*2^j-1 and
its bridge output is sample (ell+1)*2^j. In particular
R_ell=|x_(ell*2^j)|. The bridge after block ell has excess

    D*c^[nu_2(ell+1)].                                    (19)

This follows by induction from H_(j+k+1)=(H_(j+k),1+d_(j+k),H_(j+k)).
The midpoint bridge has valuation k; the two child bridge lists have
their earlier valuations unchanged. No physical step is aggregated in
the actual dynamics by writing this partition.

We shall need one explicit convergent series. Put rho=81/100. Then for c<5/2,

    sum_(ell>=1) rho^(ell-1)c^[nu_2(ell+1)]<23.             (20)

Separate k=ell+1 by its binary valuation. The s=0 contribution is
rho/(1-rho^2). For s>=1 the contribution is

    t_s=c^s rho^(2^s-2)/(1-rho^(2^(s+1))).

Use rho<5/6 and rho^2<2/3. The contributions for s=0,1,2,3,4 are respectively
strictly less than 3,5,6,5,3. Here the latter four can be bounded by

    (5/2)/(1-(2/3)^2)<5,
    (25/4)(2/3)/(1-(2/3)^4)<6,
    (125/8)(2/3)^3/(1-(2/3)^8)<5,
    (625/16)(2/3)^7/(1-(2/3)^16)<3.

Each inequality follows by multiplying its positive integer denominators.
For the tail, (2/3)^15<1/400 and (2/3)^16<1/600 show t_5<1/3. For s>=5,

    t_(s+1)/t_s
      =c rho^(2^s)/(1+rho^(2^(s+1)))<1/240.

Thus the tail starting at s=5 is less than (1/3)/(1-1/240)<1. Summing the
six bounds gives(20). This is a scalar geometric-series proof, not a
trajectory evaluation or numerical search.

## 5. First-turn structure and the actual crossing times

If a first turn occurs at step i, every earlier step preserved its sign and
satisfied d_level(t)<u_t. If the current step were no larger than some
earlier step, monotonicity u_i>=u_t would forbid the turn. Thus the first
turn is a NEW RECORD level j. Its preceding word is exactly the first H_j.

For j>=1, the preceding first occurrence of level j-1 did not turn or
annihilate, so the first-turn input has

    L=d_(j-1)<=u<D=d_j.                                   (21)

Let q=r^2 at this input. The one-sign H_j prefix and(10) give
v>=S_j q, and therefore

    q<=u/M_j.                                            (22)

Let R_1 be the actual horizontal magnitude immediately after that turn,
the entry to the next H_j block. From the exact two-coordinate update,

    v_after=u+Dq,
    R_1^2=q(D-u)^2.                                      (23)

These formulas keep the initial vertical state: v_after is its actual
accumulated value, not an increment from a newly chosen origin.

Define the first crossing of a normal threshold D after the first turn by

    tau(D)=min{t in{2^j,...,n}: u_t>=D},

with tau(D)=infinity when the set is empty. Define a putative escape from
the larger band by

    sigma(2D)=min{t in{2^j,...,n}: u_t>2D}.

The first turning input is sample2^j-1 and its output is sample2^j;
the minimum of an empty set is infinity in both definitions.

All block entries and crossing states below are samples of the SAME
trajectory. A first escape may be inside a block or the output of a bridge;
neither location is rounded into a fresh independent H_j instance.

## 6. Amortized crossing budget when j>=1

After the first turn u>=L. Hence every H_j block thereafter has one sign:
its steps have excess at most L, and equality would cause absorption,
already excluded. Assume for contradiction that sigma(2D) is finite.
Until its input all bridge inputs have u<=2D.

Write R_ell for the actual horizontal magnitude entering block ell.
For a completed block ell>=1 and its next bridge, let w be the normal
state at that bridge input and s=nu_2(ell+1). Formula(11) and actual GD give

    R_(ell+1)/R_ell<=|D c^s-w|/(M+w)<=C c^s.              (24)

If D c^s>=w, use w>=L and drop the subtraction in the numerator. If
D c^s<w<=2D, then 0<w-D c^s<=D, so the ratio is at most C<=C c^s.
Thus(24) continues to hold after the FIRST threshold D has been crossed.
It also bounds the OUTPUT of the putative escape step when that step is
a bridge, because only its input normal state was used.

For each block entry reached by that time, (18) gives

    R_ell<=R_1 C^(ell-1)c^[ell-p_2(ell)]
           =R_1 beta^(ell-1)c^[1-p_2(ell)]
           <=R_1 beta^(ell-1), ell>=1.                   (25)

Within a one-sign block the horizontal magnitude only decreases. The same
bound therefore controls a partial final block if the first escape occurs
there. In particular the squared gradient at the escape output is at most

    q_escape<=R_1^2/(1+L)^2.                             (26)

By(12), all complete or partial H_j blocks after the first turn contribute
at most R_1^2/[(1+L)(1-rho)] to the vertical increment. At a bridge after
block ell, (11) bounds its squared input gradient by
R_ell^2/(M+L)^2; its actual vertical increment is exactly
(1+D c^s) times that quantity. Equations(20),(25) therefore show that,
up to and INCLUDING the putative first escape output,

    u_escape<=u+Dq+(K/D)R_1^2,                           (27)

where one may use

    K = D/[(1+L)(1-rho)]
        +C^2[(1/D)/(1-rho)+23]
        +D/(1+L)^2
      <18.                                               (28)

There is no uncharged last fragment: (12) covers a partial block, the
bridge sum covers an escape bridge, and(26) supplies the current q in
u=v+q. If the first escape were the first turn's own output, the unused
nonnegative future-charge allowances in(27) still bound it.

Here are explicit constants for(28). Since L=D/c,
D/(1+L)<c<5/2 and D/(1+L)^2<=c/4<5/8. Also
(1/D)/(1-rho)<=12800/2413<11/2, and C<3/8. Therefore

    K<250/19+(9/64)(11/2+23)+5/8
      <53/4+513/128+5/8
      =2289/128<18.

Put z=u/D in[0,1] and delta=D/M. From(22),(23),(27),

    u_escape/D<=z+q+Kq(1-z)^2
                 <=(1+delta)z+K delta z(1-z)^2.

Since z(1-z)<=1/4,

    u_escape/D
      <=(1+delta)z+(K delta/4)(1-z)
      <=max{1+delta,K delta/4}<39/20<2.                  (29)

We used delta<13/30, K<18, and 1+13/30<39/20. This contradicts the definition
of sigma(2D). Thus no escape exists. Applying the same finite charges at
any actual sample proves(2), not just the absence of escape.

Now(24) holds through the entire word. It also holds at the FIRST bridge:
block0 was one-sign by the definition of first turn, and its bridge input
has u>=L. Multiplying from block0 instead of block1 gives

    R_(N-1)/R_0<=C^(N-1)c^[N-1-k]
                 =beta^(N-1)c^(-k), k=m-j.               (30)

The final H_j is one-sign, has its inherited vertical state, and has true
entry distance R_(N-1). The function's global final value is the same
F_par(X_n). Apply Section3 to that final block and then(30), obtaining the
j>=1 line of(4) with the ORIGINAL denominator R_0^2.

## 7. First turn at level0: small post-turn amplitude and exact alignment

Here the first turn is the very first step, with 0<=u_0<a. Put

    A=x_1^2=q_0(a-u_0)^2,
    b=ac=1-1/m, D=d_1=b.

Since q_0<=u_0, maximizing t(a-t)^2 on[0,a] gives

    A<=4a^3/27<1/90,
    a+a^2<85/144<3/5,
    D>=127/128.                                         (31)

The maximum is at t=a/3 (the endpoints give0); its derivative is
(a-t)(a-3t). The strict bound1/90 follows from a<5/12 and
4(5/12)^3/27=125/11664<1/90.

If u never reaches a, every step turns. Whenever all inputs through time t-1
have u<a, the exact horizontal update and(18) give

    |x_t|<=R_0 b^t c^[-p_2(t)],
    |x_t|<=sqrt(A) b^(t-1)c^[1-p_2(t)]   for t>=1.        (32)

The same inequalities hold at the OUTPUT of the first crossing, since its
input still had u<a. If there is no crossing, (9),(32) at t=n already give
P_par<=b^(2n)c^(-2m), which is stronger than(4).

Otherwise let tau=min{t>=1:u_t>=a}. We next bound the actual crossing state.
If tau=1, v_tau=u_0+a q_0<=a+a^2. If tau>1, its input index i=tau-1 is
positive. If its level ell is0, (32) gives q_i<=A and
h_i q_i<2A. If ell>=1, the integer i has at least ell trailing binary1s,
so p_2(i)>=ell. Consequently

    h_i q_i<=A[c^(2-2ell)+a c^(2-ell)]<=A(1+ac)<2A.

Since v_i<=u_i<a, in this case v_tau<a+2A<=a+a^2; the latter uses
2A<=8a^3/27<a^2. In every case(32) also gives |x_tau|^2<=A. Therefore

    v_tau<=a+a^2,
    u_tau<=a+a^2+A<3/5+1/90<D.                            (33)

If tau=n, all inputs in the word were still below a, and the first line
of(32) again proves the stronger all-turn product bound. Suppose tau<n.

If tau is even, it is already the entry to an actual H_1 block. If tau is
odd, retain the NEXT ACTUAL step, at index tau. It has level
ell=nu_2(tau+1)>=1. Its input satisfies u_tau<D<=d_ell by(33), so it turns
and its horizontal factor is at most d_ell. Both estimates in(32) therefore
continue to hold at time tau+1. The same trailing-ones calculation bounds
this one alignment bridge's vertical increment by2A.

We have now reached an even time2K, with K>=1, which is an actual entry to
H_1; no state was reset. Its inherited state satisfies

    u_(2K)>=a,
    v_(2K)<=a+a^2+2A,
    |x_(2K)|<=sqrt(A)b^(2K-1)c^[1-p_2(K)],
    |x_(2K)|<=R_0 b^(2K)c^[-p_2(K)],
    u_(2K)<=a+a^2+3A<D.                                  (34)

The identity p_2(2K)=p_2(K) explains the two retained binary weights.

From here all H_1 low steps are one-sign, because u>=a. Bootstrap up to a
putative first output with u>D. At a coarse bridge its input u<=D, so all
such bridges turn and(24) applies with j=1, L=a, M_1=2+a and

    C=D/(2+2a), beta=cC<9/10.

Let R_ell=|x_(2ell)| for actual H_1 block entries ell>=K. The exact product
over the inherited suffix, not a restarted word, gives

    R_ell<=R_K beta^(ell-K)c^[p_2(K)-p_2(ell)]
           <=sqrt(A) beta^(ell-K)c^[1-p_2(ell)].           (35)

For ell>=1 and s=nu_2(ell+1) one has

    c^s c^[2-2p_2(ell)]<=c.                              (36)

If s=0, p_2(ell)>=1 gives a bound1. If s>=1, the last s binary digits of
ell are1, so p_2(ell)>=s and the expression is at most c^(2-s)<=c.
This identity is the missing chronological charge for a crossing close
to a high-level bridge. Dropping the binary weight in(34) would lose it.

By(12),(35), the vertical cost of all remaining complete or partial H_1
blocks is at most A/(1-rho). By(11),(35),(36), their bridges contribute at
most

    A(1+D c)/[(2+2a)^2(1-rho)]< (7/8)A/(1-rho),

because D<1, c<5/2 and 2+2a>=2. The squared gradient at any current sample
is at most A, including the output of the proposed first escape; (35)
applies to an escape bridge output using only its input normal state.
Thus the remaining cost to v+q is less than

    [1+(1+7/8)/(1-rho)]A=(413/38)A<11A.

Together with(34), this yields

    u_escape<a+a^2+13A<3/5+13/90=67/90<3/4<D.             (37)

This contradicts the proposed first crossing of D. The same bound applies
at every subsequent sample; (33),(34) and u<a before tau cover all earlier
ones. This proves(3).

There are 2^(m-1) actual H_1 blocks, and the last has index
J=2^(m-1)-1 with p_2(J)=m-1. Combining the first inequality in(35) with
the second original-radius bound in(34) gives

    R_J/R_0<=b^(2K) beta^(J-K)c^[-(m-1)]
             <=c^[-(m-1)].                              (38)

The final H_1 step is one-sign, so |x_n|<=R_J. Equations(9),(38) give the
j=0 payoff in(4). The previously separated cases of no crossing and a
crossing at the final sample have even smaller bounds. This accounts for
every possible location of the first threshold crossing, including inside
a partial block.

## 8. What the threshold result says about the turns

This paragraph is a consequence of the budget, not an assumption used to
obtain it. For a first turn of level j, all lower levels have stopped
turning already: for j>=1 use u>=d_(j-1), and for j=0 there are no lower
levels. By(2),(3), u never reaches d_(j+1). Thus every level strictly
greater than j turns at each of its actual occurrences. Level j turns
exactly at the occurrences whose INPUT index is less than tau(d_j), and
never again thereafter, apart from the separately excluded equality
absorption case. Monotonicity proves this chronological-prefix assertion.

In the N=2^(m-j) block decomposition there are N/2 occurrences of level j
and N/2-1 bridges at higher levels. If ell_j is the number of level-j turns,
then the exact total number of turns is

    N/2-1+ell_j, with 1<=ell_j<=N/2.                       (39)

For no threshold crossing ell_j=N/2. With a crossing it is the number of
actual level-j occurrences before that crossing, not a separately chosen
restart count. The normal thresholds crossed after the first turn consist
of at most the single level d_j. All earlier displacement and vertical
history was charged in(23),(27) or(32)--(37).

## 9. Exact benchmark comparison, with no asymptotic B_n assumption

From accepted b98bb807d514e80d, the exact recursions can be written with
C_n=S_circle(n)+1 and B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 as

    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(k+l=n-1) Omega(C_k,C_l),
    B_n=max_(k+l=n-1) G(C_k,B_l),
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2.

Here C_n is a benchmark sequence, different from the block constant C in
Sections4--7. We prove directly the needed finite comparator

    B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^(m+1).                              (40)

Set alpha=2lambda-1=lambda(4-lambda) and
Llin=(4x+lambda^2 y)/alpha. Both coefficients in Llin exceed1, so Llin>=x+y.
Direct expansion using lambda^2=2lambda+1 gives

    alpha^2[Llin^2-(x+y)Llin-xy]
      =(2x/lambda-sqrt(2)lambda y)^2>=0.

Thus Llin>=Omega(x,y), the positive root of z^2-(x+y)z-xy. At
z=lambda Omega(x,y), the polynomial having larger root G(x,lambda y) is

    z^2-(4x+lambda y)z+4x^2
      =x[4x+lambda^2 y-alpha Omega(x,y)]>=0.

Also z>=lambda(x+y)>=(4x+lambda y)/2, so it lies to the right of that
quadratic's vertex. Therefore G(x,lambda y)<=lambda Omega(x,y). Induction
in the exact finite recurrences, using monotonicity of G in its second
argument, proves B_n<=lambda C_n.

Put eta=log_2(lambda)>1, Dpow(t)=(1+t)^eta-1 and ell(z)=log Dpow(exp z).
For t=exp z, differentiation yields

    ell''(z)=eta*t*(1+t)^(eta-2)
      *[(1+t)^eta-1-eta*t]/Dpow(t)^2>0.

The bracket vanishes at0 and has positive derivative for positive t.
Convexity therefore gives Dpow(t)Dpow(1/t)>=Dpow(1)^2=2. For x,y>0 put
Z=(x^(1/eta)+y^(1/eta))^eta. Substituting t=(y/x)^(1/eta) gives
(Z-x)(Z-y)>=2xy, hence Z^2-(x+y)Z-xy>=0. Also Z>=x+y by the increasing
derivative of the positive power. It follows that Omega(x,y)<=Z; zero
arguments follow directly. Induction gives C_n<=(n+1)^eta. Together with
B_n<=lambda C_n this proves(40).

It remains to compare(4) with(40). Equations(14),(16) imply
A_mass>4/5 and hence, for j>=1,

    S_j>(4/5)c^j-1>(23/60)c^j>c^j/3.                     (41)

The middle step uses c^j>12/5. For a first turn j>=1, k=m-j>=1,
(13),(17),(40),(41) give

    B_n P_par
      <(9/8)(lambda/c)^m [lambda*c^(-k)]
           beta^[2(2^k-1)]
      <(9/8)(1/2)(81/100)=729/1600.                       (42)

Here (lambda/c)^m=(1+1/m)^(-m)<=1/2 by the binomial theorem,
lambda c^(-k)<1, and beta<9/10.

For j=0, (4),(40) give

    B_n P_par<=lambda^(m+1)c^[-2(m-1)]
                <=lambda^(3-m)<1/8                      (43)

for m>=128. For no turns, c^m>20 gives S_m>(3/4)c^m and S_m>8, so(13)
and(40) yield

    B_n P_par<(3/8)lambda(lambda/c)^m<=3lambda/16
                <729/1600.                             (44)

For the last strict comparison, lambda<17/7<243/100, since sqrt(2)<10/7;
then 3lambda/16<729/1600. Absorbing trajectories have payoff0. These cases
exhaust all starts and establish(1) as a complete proof draft.

## 10. Audit and unresolved original task

Every threshold argument used the exact h_i>1 recursion. The physical c,a
were kept fixed through all embedded H_j. Every local closest-distance
estimate was multiplied by an explicit ratio to R_0, either(30) or(38).
The j=0 crossing was aligned by retaining its next physical bridge and a
binary-popcount weight; no right child was reset or independently optimized.
The finite benchmark comparison came from its recurrence, not a conjectured
limit for B_n. Equations(6),(7) supply global all-pair legality independently
of the estimates.

The proof is UNVERIFIED and has not entered the fact graph. It is a concrete
candidate for separate selection if the main agent allocates a verifier gate.
Even acceptance would close only this fixed parabolic mechanism on H_m for
m>=128. The original unrestricted exact-profile target remains unresolved.

# Dense full-model discovery and a common-offset mass obstruction

Status: joint **unverified proof draft**, cumulative round 16. The experiment
is closed. No fact_submit is allocated or has been made. This is a named-family
obstruction and a finite discovery report, not the original minimax theorem.

Accepted inputs: b98bb807d514e80d defines the exact benchmark and supplies the
Huber lower bound; 1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the complete interpolation/Gram
model. The new argument below is proved in full, not imported from an earlier
unverified finding. No numerical output is a premise of the proof.

## 1. The actual experiment

The public runner `max_dense_full_pep.py` adapts only the tested public source
`max3_c58_full_pep_batch_used.py`, SHA256
e8e1d0ed399b924eff7be7414fa61fd5c5d94dd7966294f6f4dbd84ce8cc5bc5.
The original runner was not executed. The separate public ledger is
`max_exact_benchmark_discovery_budget.json`; it is CLOSED at 16 evaluations
and 98.02878378597961 measured import/build/solve seconds. Its unused time
does not authorize another solve. The closed prior conic and direct ledgers
are unchanged. Totals: 672 conic evaluations, 171.40263413495765 measured
conic seconds; including the separate closed direct batch gives
172.22190110096332 measured seconds.

Every solve uses the full Gram of (x0,g0,...,gn), every distinct ordered pair
on {star,0,...,n}, common function values, optimum zero, and ||x0||^2<=1.
There is no imposed rank, ray, mode, jump support, recursive dual support,
or incoming-terminal deletion. The complete multipliers are reselected.
For M=1+sum h, the computational variables are
Ghat=Gram(x0,M*g0,...,M*gn), fhat=M*f. Diagnostics, flow, full remainders,
and pair residuals are also evaluated in the original model.

Raw files `max_dense_01_*_raw.json` through `max_dense_16_*_raw.json` retain
the evaluated steps and exact recipes, primal values and both Grams, every
ordered-pair label and raw multiplier, both optimum incidences, full raw
remainders, objective gap, original/scaled signs/flow/PSD diagnostics, and
measured cost. `max_dense_discovery_summary.json` indexes paths and hashes.
No eigenvalue or multiplier was repaired or truncated in those raw files.

The one-step exact calibration is h=(3/2), q=1/4, with

 q||x0||^2-2f1+Q10+Q0star+Q1star=||x0-2g0-2g1||^2/4.

The quadratic f(x)=x^2/2, x0=1, attains q. The numerical solve matched this.
The second calibration is the deterministic exact-recurrence 15-step word,
evaluated at 80 decimal digits, with root split 9. The full recursively
constructed source array has evaluated flow residual <4.5e-16 and full
matrix coefficient residual <1.8e-15. The solver matched 1/B15 to about
6e-9 relative. Radical evaluation and tie selection are NOT interval
certificates; all candidate split values and the complete tree are retained.

The three dense directions use chronological tilt 0,-1/2,+1/2 in section 2.
Every step changes at n=15 and n=31. A five-step instance changes four steps
and exposes a small geometric subproblem. All 14 concrete proposals were
entered before filtering, and all passed the retained necessary screens.

Selected numerical full-model ratios q*B_n (primal and dual agree at the
shown precision; neither is asserted to be an exact certificate):

| n | tilt | parameter | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 5 | 0 | .02 | 1.02146826 |
| 15 | 0 | .002 | 1.01213546 |
| 15 | -1/2 | .002 | 1.01208733 |

The three n15 parameter .1 cases and the n31 back-tilted case returned
`optimal_inaccurate`. The largest displayed original full-dual negative
eigenvalue magnitude is about6.3e-6; all such diagnostics are retained.
These data do not assert exact feasibility, local or global optimality,
or nonexistence of other dense improving schedules. No apparent small gain
is inferred from the baseline's floating discrepancy.

What the complete model changed: it defeated directions that passed the
global Huber, all single-cut, four fixed-curvature quadratic, and symmetric
plateau-to-quadratic screens. The primal Grams have several substantial
directions, and the reselected arrays have nonzero optimum-source mass.
Raw rank counts are tolerance dependent, particularly as the parameter
shrinks; they are not exact rank theorems.

## 2. The named dense family, enlarged beyond the experiment

Let h^0 be any exact dominant word attaining S_bullet(n), and let k be its
root bridge index. Its root children are exact primitive and dominant source
words, possibly empty. On each nonempty child I of length m_I put

 d_i=h_i^0-1>0,        1/2<=w_i<=3/2,
 W_I=sum_(i in I)w_i,
 A_I=sum w_i*d_i/W_I,  H_I=W_I/(sum w_i/d_i),
 c_I=(A_I+H_I)/2,     v_i=w_i(d_i-c_I),
 V_I=sum_(i in I)v_i.

Choose independent REAL amplitudes t_I for the children, and define

 h_i=h_i^0+t_I*v_i                    (i in child I),
 h_k=h_k^0-(1/4)sum_I t_I*V_I.        (root)

Require every actual h_i>=0. The amplitudes, weights, chosen maximizing
tree, and horizon may all vary. The experiment used one common positive
amplitude and w_i=1+tilt*(2j/(m_I-1)-1), with singleton weight1.
No certificate restriction is made in this definition.

**Claim.** Every such schedule satisfies, for n>=1,

 sum h_i <= S_bullet(n)+(27/8)(n-1),
 W_n(h) >= 1/[B_n+(27/4)(n-1)].                    (1)

In particular, uniformly over this entire enlarged family,

 W_n(h)/U_n^ZJ >= [1+27(n-1)/(4B_n)]^(-1) ->1.    (2)

This is a lower bound for unrestricted worst-case performance on the named
physical schedules. Full dual reselection, higher-rank remainders, both
optimum incidences and arbitrarily many new edges cannot evade it.

## 3. A block inequality from nonnegativity

Consider any nonempty base block h_i^0=1+d_i>1 of length m. Let its minimum
step be h_min, attained at j, and assume weights in [w_min,w_max] with
w_min>0. Define A,H,c,v,V as above. Write d_min=h_min-1.

The elementary weighted arithmetic/harmonic inequality H<=A follows from

 (sum w_i*d_i)(sum w_i/d_i) >= (sum w_i)^2:

expand the difference as sum_(i<j)w_i*w_j*(d_i/d_j+d_j/d_i-2), whose terms
are nonnegative because (d_i-d_j)^2/(d_i*d_j)>=0. Also H>=d_min, since
sum w_i/d_i <= (sum w_i)/d_min. Therefore, with W=sum w_i,

 V=W(A-H)/2=W(c-H)>=0,
 V<=W(c-d_min).                                    (3)

Put delta=c-d_min>=0. If delta=0, (3) forces V=0. If delta>0 and t>=0
keeps the jth step nonnegative, then

 0<=h_min-t*w_j*delta,
 t*delta<=h_min/w_j,
 t*V<=W*h_min/w_j <=m*(w_max/w_min)*h_min.          (4)

If t<0, t*V<=0, so the same upper bound holds. This is valid for each block
separately and permits independent amplitudes. It uses one actual small
step in that block; it is not a bound on a compressed recursion.

More generally the same argument works for any center c satisfying
H<=c<=A and A-c<=c-d_min. The midpoint rule meets these conditions.

## 4. Source words have a bounded small step in every nonempty child

Every source step is strictly greater than1. For a primitive bridge, writing
A=1+sum(left), C=1+sum(right), the positive number b-1 solves
(b-1)^2+(A+C)(b-1)-AC=0. For a dominant bridge it has the form
b=1+A/r with r=(1+sqrt(1+8A/D))/2>1 and D>0.

Every nonempty primitive source word contains a step sqrt(2): descend its
finite binary tree to a node with two empty children, where phi(0,0)=sqrt(2).
For a nonempty dominant word, if any primitive child on its dominant spine
is nonempty it contains such a step. Otherwise the last node on that spine
has two empty children, giving psi(0,0)=3/2. Thus every nonempty source word
has h_min<=3/2, without any assumption about maximizing split patterns.

Apply (4) to each root child, with w_max/w_min<=3 and h_min<=3/2. Then

 sum_I t_I V_I <= (9/2)sum_I m_I=(9/2)(n-1).

The root compensation makes the change of the TOTAL physical step sum
exactly (3/4)sum_I t_I V_I. This proves the first inequality of (1), even
when one child is empty or both children are singletons.

For any nonnegative schedule of total sum S, the legal scalar Huber
function of threshold a=1/(1+2S), started at1, has all iterates >=a,
x_n=1-aS and2f(x_n)=a. It has smoothness1 and unique minimizer0.
Consequently W_n(h)>=1/(1+2S), as also proved in b98bb807d514e80d.
Substitute the sum bound to get the second inequality of (1).

## 5. Uniform asymptotics from the exact recurrence

No unverified decimal asymptotic constant is needed. Put lambda=1+sqrt(2)
and P_j=1+S_circle(j). The legal balanced primitive construction gives

 P_(2^m-1)>=lambda^m,

by induction from P_0=1 and the primitive mass join
Omega(A,A)=lambda*A. The dominant mass join is
G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2. Taking a primitive prefix of length2^m-1
and an empty dominant suffix gives B_(2^m)>=2lambda^m.
Moreover B_(j+1)>=G(1,B_j)>B_j, by the allowed empty-prefix split.
For2^m<=n<2^(m+1),

 B_n/n >= (lambda/2)^m ->infinity.

Together with (1), this proves the uniform lower-bound ratio (2).
No conclusion is asserted about W_n(h) having a matching upper bound.

## 6. Scope, stress tests, and what remains

The calculation covers changes at every index, nonsymmetry, arbitrary
amplitudes for both children, and arbitrary bounded positive weights. Its
obstruction is the common subtractive center and the small source step,
not a fixed terminal library, sparse exception set, fixed support, or Huber
tightness of an upper certificate.

The proof identifies its load-bearing assumptions. An unbounded ratio
w_max/w_min only gives O((w_max/w_min)*n) added mass. Groups without a
bounded small step, a different center failing (3), or index-dependent
amplitudes inside one group leave this argument. Repeated separate
nonnegative mutations also accumulate their own cost and are not silently
covered by the single-round estimate. Removing those assumptions requires
a new construction and a new full-model/certificate argument; the generic
unknown SDP remains blocked as an asymptotic proof route.

This finding does not claim that all dense perturbations fail, or that the
exact benchmark is a local/global minimum over unrestricted schedules.
The original all-horizon/all-schedule target remains open.

evidence:
# C65: an amortized threshold budget for the entire parabolic family

Status: COMPLETE PROOF DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. No fact_submit, trajectory experiment,
optimization, installation, or external theorem is used. This is a proposed
closure of the specified parabolic mechanism, NOT of the unrestricted
worst-case functional or the original all-schedule target. The accepted fact
b98bb807d514e80d supplies the definition of the exact benchmark. Every other
argument, including the earlier C60/C63/C64 derivations needed here, is proved
inside this document; those drafts are not assumed as predecessor facts.

## 1. Statement and scope

Fix an integer m>=128. Throughout the WHOLE word, including embedded words,
keep the following enclosing-horizon parameters fixed:

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    n=2^m-1, d_j=a*c^j, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

For this document only, H_j denotes these physical words, not the conjugate
quadratics with the same letter in accepted1252b8823bb5a290. All displayed
scalar r,u,v,x,q and block quantities below are local parabolic variables.

Define one function on the Euclidean plane by

    K_par={(t,s):s>=t^2/sqrt(2)},
    F_par(X)=max_(g in K_par)(<X,g>-||g||^2/2).

For arbitrary r_0!=0 and v_0>=0 start GD at

    X_0=(r_0(1+v_0+r_0^2),-v_0/sqrt(2))

and use the ACTUAL physical word H_m. Write the iterates as

    X_i=(x_i,-v_i/sqrt(2)),
    x_i=r_i(1+u_i), u_i=v_i+r_i^2, q_i=r_i^2.

The true initial squared distance to the minimizer set is

    R_0^2=r_0^2(1+v_0+r_0^2)^2=x_0^2.

The normalized payoff is

    P_par=2F_par(X_n)/R_0^2.

Let B_n=2 S_bullet(n)+1 be the exact Zhang--Jiang denominator defined by
accepted b98bb807d514e80d, with its full finite recurrence reproduced below.
The proposed conclusion is the UNIFORM proper-family bound

    sup_(r_0!=0,v_0>=0) B_(2^m-1) P_par <=729/1600<1/2.       (1)

The same joint proof, with the uniform comparison in Section9.1, gives
the stronger asymptotic candidate conclusion

    limsup_(m->infinity) sup_(r_0!=0,v_0>=0)
          B_(2^m-1) P_par <=lambda/(4e)<1/4.              (1a)

Here e is the base of the natural logarithm. On the subdomain whose first
turn has level at least1, the right side improves to
(3+2sqrt(2))/(32e). The first-turn-level0 subdomain has limit superior0.
All suprema allow initial states depending arbitrarily on the horizon.

In particular the previously open domain of two or more horizontal sign
changes WITH a crossing of the first turning threshold is included.

The proof gives the following stronger chronological assertions. Discard an
absorbing trajectory r_i=0, whose payoff is zero. If the first sign change
has level j>=1, put D=d_j. Then

    u_i<(39/20)D<d_(j+1)                                   (2)

at every sample after that turn, whenever j+1 is used as a comparison level.
Here d_(j+1)=cD is a defined number even at the last physical level. If the
first sign change has level0, then

    u_i<3/4<d_1                                            (3)

throughout the trajectory. Thus a first turning threshold may be crossed,
but the NEXT turning threshold cannot be crossed. This assertion is proved
by an inherited-state budget, not assumed as an ordering of turn levels.

For j>=1, set k=m-j, N=2^k,

    L=D/c, C=D/(M_j+L), beta=c*C,
    E(T)=(2T+3)^2/[8(T+1)^2(2T+1)].

The more detailed payoff bounds are

    P_par<=E(S_m)                              if there is no turn;
    P_par<=c^[-2(m-1)]                         if first-turn level j=0;
    P_par<=E(S_j) beta^[2(N-1)] c^(-2k)         if j>=1.       (4)

These conclusions concern exactly F_par and the specified starts and words.
They do not upper-bound W_n(H_m), do not weaken the accepted finite C59
adversary, and do not decide the original all-horizon/all-schedule problem.

## 2. One global function, every pair, the true distance, and actual GD

The set K_par is nonempty, closed and convex. Completing the square shows
that the maximum defining F_par is attained uniquely at the Euclidean
projection p(X) onto K_par: the equivalent minimization is coercive and
strictly convex. The projection normal inequalities at X and Y imply

    ||p(X)-p(Y)||^2<=<p(X)-p(Y),X-Y>.

Hence p is 1-Lipschitz. Comparing the two defining maxima gives

    0<=F_par(Y)-F_par(X)-<p(X),Y-X>
      <=<p(Y)-p(X),Y-X><=||Y-X||^2.

The remainder divided by ||Y-X|| tends to zero, so F_par is differentiable
with gradient p. It is convex as a supremum of affine functions, and its
gradient is 1-Lipschitz on the whole plane.

For r real and v>=0 define

    u=v+r^2,
    X(r,v)=(r(1+u),-v/sqrt(2)),
    G(r)=(r,r^2/sqrt(2)).

One has X-G=u(r,-1/sqrt(2)). For any (t,s) in K_par,

    <X-G,(t,s)-G><=-(u/2)(t-r)^2<=0.

Thus G(r) is the actual projection and gradient, and substitution yields

    F_par(X(r,v))=r^2(1+v)/2+3r^4/4.                       (5)

For EVERY ordered pair of such states, with f_i=F_par(X_i), expansion gives

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2
        =<X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j>
        =-(u_j/2)(r_i-r_j)^2<=0.                           (6)

The construction therefore retains every interpolation pair, not only the
consecutive pairs used in the estimates below.

The minimizer set is exactly {(0,y):y<=0}. At such points all feasible
inner products are nonpositive and the feasible gradient0 gives value0.
A point of positive vertical coordinate has positive value by testing a
small positive vertical gradient. A point of nonzero horizontal coordinate
has positive value by testing (t,t^2/sqrt(2)) with small t of the same
horizontal sign: the linear term dominates the higher powers of t. The
closest minimizer to X_0 is consequently (0,-v_0/sqrt(2)), which proves the
stated true denominator R_0^2. At a later block entry the corresponding
closest distance is its actual horizontal magnitude; the global minimum
value is still0 for this SAME function.

For a physical step h>=0, actual GD is exactly

    v_plus=v+h*r^2,
    r_plus^3+(1+v_plus)r_plus=r(1+v+r^2-h).                 (7)

The cubic's derivative is1+v_plus+3r_plus^2>=1, so it has one real root.
Equation(7) produces exactly the coordinates of X-hG. In particular

    x_plus=x-h*r,
    u_plus-u=(h-1)q+q_plus.                                (8)

Every step of H_m is greater than1, so u is nondecreasing on the actual
trajectory. This monotonicity is NOT asserted for arbitrary smaller steps.
A sign change occurs precisely when u<d_level; equality makes r_plus=0.
Once r is zero, all remaining r-values and objective values are zero.

Another useful pointwise bound, valid at every state, is

    2F_par(X)<=x^2.                                        (9)

Indeed, after substituting q=r^2 and u=v+q, the difference is
q[u+u^2-q/2]>=0 since u>=q.

## 3. One-sign blocks retain both coordinates

Suppose a consecutive actual block has a fixed nonzero sign. By horizontal
reflection it is enough to consider positive r. At a sign-preserving step,
the cubic in(7) evaluated at the OLD r exceeds its right side by h*r(1+r^2).
Since that cubic is increasing, 0<r_plus<=r. Thus for a whole block of mass T,
entry (r_A,v_A), and exit (r_B,v_B),

    Delta_x=x_A-x_B=sum h_i r_i,
    Delta_v=v_B-v_A=sum h_i r_i^2,
    T r_B<=Delta_x<=T r_A,
    r_B Delta_x<=Delta_v<=r_A Delta_x,
    T r_B^2<=Delta_v<=T r_A^2.                              (10)

For either sign, if R_A=|x_A| and u_B=v_B+r_B^2, this proves

    |r_B|(1+T+u_B)<=R_A.                                   (11)

If u_A>=L>=0, it also proves the following vertical charge, including for
any initial part of that block:

    Delta_v<=|r_A| R_A=R_A^2/(1+u_A)<=R_A^2/(1+L).          (12)

No old vertical state is discarded in (10)--(12).

For a complete one-sign trajectory of mass T>=1/2, put w=1+v_B and q=r_B^2.
Then R_A>=sqrt(q)(T+w+q), and w>=1+Tq, using v_A>=0. Thus its payoff with
the true entry distance is at most

    (w+(3/2)q)/(T+w+q)^2.

With t=w+q>=1, one has q<=(t-1)/(T+1), so this is at most

    [(2T+3)t-1]/[2(T+1)(T+t)^2].

The derivative has the sign of (2T+3)(T-t)+2. Its maximum on t>=1 is at
t=T+2/(2T+3), which belongs to that interval for T>=1/2. Substitution gives
E(T) as in(4). Two useful consequences are

    E(T)<=3/(8T)                  for T>=1/2;
    E(T)<9/(32T)                  for T>=8.                 (13)

For the first, bound w+(3/2)q by (3/2)(w+q) and use
t/(T+t)^2<=1/(4T); the displayed E(T) inherits this bound where it applies.
For the second,
T E(T)<[2+1/(T+1)]^2/16<=361/1296<9/32.

## 4. Physical masses, binary accounting, and fixed constants

The recursive mass identity is

    M_(j+1)=2M_j+d_j,
    M_j=A_mass*c^j+(1-A_mass)*2^j,
    A_mass=a/(c-2).                                        (14)

Here 0<a<c-2 and hence 0<A_mass<1. To check the nontrivial strict inequality,
write epsilon=1/m and use lambda^2=2lambda+1:

    c(c-2)-(1-epsilon)
      =epsilon(2lambda+3)+lambda^2 epsilon^2>0.

Consequently

    d_j/M_j<c-2.                                          (15)

For m>=128 the following convenient rational bounds hold:

    12/5<c<73/30<5/2,
    2/5<a<5/12,
    c-2<13/30,
    d_j>=d_1=1-1/m>=127/128                for j>=1.        (16)

For the upper bound on c, sqrt(2)<99/70 gives
c<(169/70)(129/128)=21801/8960<73/30. The lower bound c>12/5 follows from
sqrt(2)>7/5. Also a<(sqrt(2)-1)<5/12, and
a>(127/128)(30/73)=3810/9344>2/5.

Fix j>=1, D=d_j, L=D/c, M=M_j, delta=D/M, C=D/(M+L), beta=cC. Then

    beta=c*delta/(1+delta/c)
         <c^2(c-2)/(2c-2)
         <69277/77400<9/10,
    C<3/8.                                                (17)

The function c^2(c-2)/(2c-2) is increasing for c>2, because both c^2 and
(c-2)/(2(c-1)) are positive and increasing. Substitute c=73/30 for the
second inequality. The last bound uses c>12/5 and beta<9/10.

Let p_2(t) be the number of1s in the binary expansion of a nonnegative
integer t, and let nu_2(t) be the exponent of2 in a positive integer t.
Counting multiples of powers of2 gives

    sum_(k=1)^t nu_2(k)=t-p_2(t).                           (18)

For completeness, write t=sum_s e_s 2^s with e_s in{0,1}. Then
sum_(b>=1)floor(t/2^b)=sum_s e_s(2^s-1)=t-p_2(t).

H_m consists of N=2^(m-j) chronological H_j blocks, indexed
ell=0,...,N-1. Block ell starts at sample ell*2^j, with inherited state
(r_(ell*2^j),v_(ell*2^j)); its bridge input is sample (ell+1)*2^j-1 and
its bridge output is sample (ell+1)*2^j. In particular
R_ell=|x_(ell*2^j)|. The bridge after block ell has excess

    D*c^[nu_2(ell+1)].                                    (19)

This follows by induction from H_(j+k+1)=(H_(j+k),1+d_(j+k),H_(j+k)).
The midpoint bridge has valuation k; the two child bridge lists have
their earlier valuations unchanged. No physical step is aggregated in
the actual dynamics by writing this partition.

We shall need one explicit convergent series. Put rho=81/100. Then for c<5/2,

    sum_(ell>=1) rho^(ell-1)c^[nu_2(ell+1)]<23.             (20)

Separate k=ell+1 by its binary valuation. The s=0 contribution is
rho/(1-rho^2). For s>=1 the contribution is

    t_s=c^s rho^(2^s-2)/(1-rho^(2^(s+1))).

Use rho<5/6 and rho^2<2/3. The contributions for s=0,1,2,3,4 are respectively
strictly less than 3,5,6,5,3. Here the latter four can be bounded by

    (5/2)/(1-(2/3)^2)<5,
    (25/4)(2/3)/(1-(2/3)^4)<6,
    (125/8)(2/3)^3/(1-(2/3)^8)<5,
    (625/16)(2/3)^7/(1-(2/3)^16)<3.

Each inequality follows by multiplying its positive integer denominators.
For the tail, (2/3)^15<1/400 and (2/3)^16<1/600 show t_5<1/3. For s>=5,

    t_(s+1)/t_s
      =c rho^(2^s)/(1+rho^(2^(s+1)))<1/240.

Thus the tail starting at s=5 is less than (1/3)/(1-1/240)<1. Summing the
six bounds gives(20). This is a scalar geometric-series proof, not a
trajectory evaluation or numerical search.

## 5. First-turn structure and the actual crossing times

If a first turn occurs at step i, every earlier step preserved its sign and
satisfied d_level(t)<u_t. If the current step were no larger than some
earlier step, monotonicity u_i>=u_t would forbid the turn. Thus the first
turn is a NEW RECORD level j. Its preceding word is exactly the first H_j.

For j>=1, the preceding first occurrence of level j-1 did not turn or
annihilate, so the first-turn input has

    L=d_(j-1)<=u<D=d_j.                                   (21)

Let q=r^2 at this input. The one-sign H_j prefix and(10) give
v>=S_j q, and therefore

    q<=u/M_j.                                            (22)

Let R_1 be the actual horizontal magnitude immediately after that turn,
the entry to the next H_j block. From the exact two-coordinate update,

    v_after=u+Dq,
    R_1^2=q(D-u)^2.                                      (23)

These formulas keep the initial vertical state: v_after is its actual
accumulated value, not an increment from a newly chosen origin.

Define the first crossing of a normal threshold D after the first turn by

    tau(D)=min{t in{2^j,...,n}: u_t>=D},

with tau(D)=infinity when the set is empty. Define a putative escape from
the larger band by

    sigma(2D)=min{t in{2^j,...,n}: u_t>2D}.

The first turning input is sample2^j-1 and its output is sample2^j;
the minimum of an empty set is infinity in both definitions.

All block entries and crossing states below are samples of the SAME
trajectory. A first escape may be inside a block or the output of a bridge;
neither location is rounded into a fresh independent H_j instance.

## 6. Amortized crossing budget when j>=1

After the first turn u>=L. Hence every H_j block thereafter has one sign:
its steps have excess at most L, and equality would cause absorption,
already excluded. Assume for contradiction that sigma(2D) is finite.
Until its input all bridge inputs have u<=2D.

Write R_ell for the actual horizontal magnitude entering block ell.
For a completed block ell>=1 and its next bridge, let w be the normal
state at that bridge input and s=nu_2(ell+1). Formula(11) and actual GD give

    R_(ell+1)/R_ell<=|D c^s-w|/(M+w)<=C c^s.              (24)

If D c^s>=w, use w>=L and drop the subtraction in the numerator. If
D c^s<w<=2D, then 0<w-D c^s<=D, so the ratio is at most C<=C c^s.
Thus(24) continues to hold after the FIRST threshold D has been crossed.
It also bounds the OUTPUT of the putative escape step when that step is
a bridge, because only its input normal state was used.

For each block entry reached by that time, (18) gives

    R_ell<=R_1 C^(ell-1)c^[ell-p_2(ell)]
           =R_1 beta^(ell-1)c^[1-p_2(ell)]
           <=R_1 beta^(ell-1), ell>=1.                   (25)

Within a one-sign block the horizontal magnitude only decreases. The same
bound therefore controls a partial final block if the first escape occurs
there. In particular the squared gradient at the escape output is at most

    q_escape<=R_1^2/(1+L)^2.                             (26)

By(12), all complete or partial H_j blocks after the first turn contribute
at most R_1^2/[(1+L)(1-rho)] to the vertical increment. At a bridge after
block ell, (11) bounds its squared input gradient by
R_ell^2/(M+L)^2; its actual vertical increment is exactly
(1+D c^s) times that quantity. Equations(20),(25) therefore show that,
up to and INCLUDING the putative first escape output,

    u_escape<=u+Dq+(K/D)R_1^2,                           (27)

where one may use

    K = D/[(1+L)(1-rho)]
        +C^2[(1/D)/(1-rho)+23]
        +D/(1+L)^2
      <18.                                               (28)

There is no uncharged last fragment: (12) covers a partial block, the
bridge sum covers an escape bridge, and(26) supplies the current q in
u=v+q. If the first escape were the first turn's own output, the unused
nonnegative future-charge allowances in(27) still bound it.

Here are explicit constants for(28). Since L=D/c,
D/(1+L)<c<5/2 and D/(1+L)^2<=c/4<5/8. Also
(1/D)/(1-rho)<=12800/2413<11/2, and C<3/8. Therefore

    K<250/19+(9/64)(11/2+23)+5/8
      <53/4+513/128+5/8
      =2289/128<18.

Put z=u/D in[0,1] and delta=D/M. From(22),(23),(27),

    u_escape/D<=z+q+Kq(1-z)^2
                 <=(1+delta)z+K delta z(1-z)^2.

Since z(1-z)<=1/4,

    u_escape/D
      <=(1+delta)z+(K delta/4)(1-z)
      <=max{1+delta,K delta/4}<39/20<2.                  (29)

We used delta<13/30, K<18, and 1+13/30<39/20. This contradicts the definition
of sigma(2D). Thus no escape exists. Applying the same finite charges at
any actual sample proves(2), not just the absence of escape.

Now(24) holds through the entire word. It also holds at the FIRST bridge:
block0 was one-sign by the definition of first turn, and its bridge input
has u>=L. Multiplying from block0 instead of block1 gives

    R_(N-1)/R_0<=C^(N-1)c^[N-1-k]
                 =beta^(N-1)c^(-k), k=m-j.               (30)

The final H_j is one-sign, has its inherited vertical state, and has true
entry distance R_(N-1). The function's global final value is the same
F_par(X_n). Apply Section3 to that final block and then(30), obtaining the
j>=1 line of(4) with the ORIGINAL denominator R_0^2.

## 7. First turn at level0: small post-turn amplitude and exact alignment

Here the first turn is the very first step, with 0<=u_0<a. Put

    A=x_1^2=q_0(a-u_0)^2,
    b=ac=1-1/m, D=d_1=b.

Since q_0<=u_0, maximizing t(a-t)^2 on[0,a] gives

    A<=4a^3/27<1/90,
    a+a^2<85/144<3/5,
    D>=127/128.                                         (31)

The maximum is at t=a/3 (the endpoints give0); its derivative is
(a-t)(a-3t). The strict bound1/90 follows from a<5/12 and
4(5/12)^3/27=125/11664<1/90.

If u never reaches a, every step turns. Whenever all inputs through time t-1
have u<a, the exact horizontal update and(18) give

    |x_t|<=R_0 b^t c^[-p_2(t)],
    |x_t|<=sqrt(A) b^(t-1)c^[1-p_2(t)]   for t>=1.        (32)

The same inequalities hold at the OUTPUT of the first crossing, since its
input still had u<a. If there is no crossing, (9),(32) at t=n already give
P_par<=b^(2n)c^(-2m), which is stronger than(4).

Otherwise let tau=min{t>=1:u_t>=a}. We next bound the actual crossing state.
If tau=1, v_tau=u_0+a q_0<=a+a^2. If tau>1, its input index i=tau-1 is
positive. If its level ell is0, (32) gives q_i<=A and
h_i q_i<2A. If ell>=1, the integer i has at least ell trailing binary1s,
so p_2(i)>=ell. Consequently

    h_i q_i<=A[c^(2-2ell)+a c^(2-ell)]<=A(1+ac)<2A.

Since v_i<=u_i<a, in this case v_tau<a+2A<=a+a^2; the latter uses
2A<=8a^3/27<a^2. In every case(32) also gives |x_tau|^2<=A. Therefore

    v_tau<=a+a^2,
    u_tau<=a+a^2+A<3/5+1/90<D.                            (33)

If tau=n, all inputs in the word were still below a, and the first line
of(32) again proves the stronger all-turn product bound. Suppose tau<n.

If tau is even, it is already the entry to an actual H_1 block. If tau is
odd, retain the NEXT ACTUAL step, at index tau. It has level
ell=nu_2(tau+1)>=1. Its input satisfies u_tau<D<=d_ell by(33), so it turns
and its horizontal factor is at most d_ell. Both estimates in(32) therefore
continue to hold at time tau+1. The same trailing-ones calculation bounds
this one alignment bridge's vertical increment by2A.

We have now reached an even time2K, with K>=1, which is an actual entry to
H_1; no state was reset. Its inherited state satisfies

    u_(2K)>=a,
    v_(2K)<=a+a^2+2A,
    |x_(2K)|<=sqrt(A)b^(2K-1)c^[1-p_2(K)],
    |x_(2K)|<=R_0 b^(2K)c^[-p_2(K)],
    u_(2K)<=a+a^2+3A<D.                                  (34)

The identity p_2(2K)=p_2(K) explains the two retained binary weights.

From here all H_1 low steps are one-sign, because u>=a. Bootstrap up to a
putative first output with u>D. At a coarse bridge its input u<=D, so all
such bridges turn and(24) applies with j=1, L=a, M_1=2+a and

    C=D/(2+2a), beta=cC<9/10.

Let R_ell=|x_(2ell)| for actual H_1 block entries ell>=K. The exact product
over the inherited suffix, not a restarted word, gives

    R_ell<=R_K beta^(ell-K)c^[p_2(K)-p_2(ell)]
           <=sqrt(A) beta^(ell-K)c^[1-p_2(ell)].           (35)

For ell>=1 and s=nu_2(ell+1) one has

    c^s c^[2-2p_2(ell)]<=c.                              (36)

If s=0, p_2(ell)>=1 gives a bound1. If s>=1, the last s binary digits of
ell are1, so p_2(ell)>=s and the expression is at most c^(2-s)<=c.
This identity is the missing chronological charge for a crossing close
to a high-level bridge. Dropping the binary weight in(34) would lose it.

By(12),(35), the vertical cost of all remaining complete or partial H_1
blocks is at most A/(1-rho). By(11),(35),(36), their bridges contribute at
most

    A(1+D c)/[(2+2a)^2(1-rho)]< (7/8)A/(1-rho),

because D<1, c<5/2 and 2+2a>=2. The squared gradient at any current sample
is at most A, including the output of the proposed first escape; (35)
applies to an escape bridge output using only its input normal state.
Thus the remaining cost to v+q is less than

    [1+(1+7/8)/(1-rho)]A=(413/38)A<11A.

Together with(34), this yields

    u_escape<a+a^2+13A<3/5+13/90=67/90<3/4<D.             (37)

This contradicts the proposed first crossing of D. The same bound applies
at every subsequent sample; (33),(34) and u<a before tau cover all earlier
ones. This proves(3).

There are 2^(m-1) actual H_1 blocks, and the last has index
J=2^(m-1)-1 with p_2(J)=m-1. Combining the first inequality in(35) with
the second original-radius bound in(34) gives

    R_J/R_0<=b^(2K) beta^(J-K)c^[-(m-1)]
             <=c^[-(m-1)].                              (38)

The final H_1 step is one-sign, so |x_n|<=R_J. Equations(9),(38) give the
j=0 payoff in(4). The previously separated cases of no crossing and a
crossing at the final sample have even smaller bounds. This accounts for
every possible location of the first threshold crossing, including inside
a partial block.

## 8. What the threshold result says about the turns

This paragraph is a consequence of the budget, not an assumption used to
obtain it. For a first turn of level j, all lower levels have stopped
turning already: for j>=1 use u>=d_(j-1), and for j=0 there are no lower
levels. By(2),(3), u never reaches d_(j+1). Thus every level strictly
greater than j turns at each of its actual occurrences. Level j turns
exactly at the occurrences whose INPUT index is less than tau(d_j), and
never again thereafter, apart from the separately excluded equality
absorption case. Monotonicity proves this chronological-prefix assertion.

In the N=2^(m-j) block decomposition there are N/2 occurrences of level j
and N/2-1 bridges at higher levels. If ell_j is the number of level-j turns,
then the exact total number of turns is

    N/2-1+ell_j, with 1<=ell_j<=N/2.                       (39)

For no threshold crossing ell_j=N/2. With a crossing it is the number of
actual level-j occurrences before that crossing, not a separately chosen
restart count. The normal thresholds crossed after the first turn consist
of at most the single level d_j. All earlier displacement and vertical
history was charged in(23),(27) or(32)--(37).

## 9. Exact benchmark comparison, with no asymptotic B_n assumption

From accepted b98bb807d514e80d, the exact recursions can be written with
C_n=S_circle(n)+1 and B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 as

    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(k+l=n-1) Omega(C_k,C_l),
    B_n=max_(k+l=n-1) G(C_k,B_l),
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2.

Here C_n is a benchmark sequence, different from the block constant C in
Sections4--7. We prove directly the needed finite comparator

    B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^(m+1).                              (40)

Set alpha=2lambda-1=lambda(4-lambda) and
Llin=(4x+lambda^2 y)/alpha. Both coefficients in Llin exceed1, so Llin>=x+y.
Direct expansion using lambda^2=2lambda+1 gives

    alpha^2[Llin^2-(x+y)Llin-xy]
      =(2x/lambda-sqrt(2)lambda y)^2>=0.

Thus Llin>=Omega(x,y), the positive root of z^2-(x+y)z-xy. At
z=lambda Omega(x,y), the polynomial having larger root G(x,lambda y) is

    z^2-(4x+lambda y)z+4x^2
      =x[4x+lambda^2 y-alpha Omega(x,y)]>=0.

Also z>=lambda(x+y)>=(4x+lambda y)/2, so it lies to the right of that
quadratic's vertex. Therefore G(x,lambda y)<=lambda Omega(x,y). Induction
in the exact finite recurrences, using monotonicity of G in its second
argument, proves B_n<=lambda C_n.

Put eta=log_2(lambda)>1, Dpow(t)=(1+t)^eta-1 and ell(z)=log Dpow(exp z).
For t=exp z, differentiation yields

    ell''(z)=eta*t*(1+t)^(eta-2)
      *[(1+t)^eta-1-eta*t]/Dpow(t)^2>0.

The bracket vanishes at0 and has positive derivative for positive t.
Convexity therefore gives Dpow(t)Dpow(1/t)>=Dpow(1)^2=2. For x,y>0 put
Z=(x^(1/eta)+y^(1/eta))^eta. Substituting t=(y/x)^(1/eta) gives
(Z-x)(Z-y)>=2xy, hence Z^2-(x+y)Z-xy>=0. Also Z>=x+y by the increasing
derivative of the positive power. It follows that Omega(x,y)<=Z; zero
arguments follow directly. Induction gives C_n<=(n+1)^eta. Together with
B_n<=lambda C_n this proves(40).

It remains to compare(4) with(40). Equations(14),(16) imply
A_mass>4/5 and hence, for j>=1,

    S_j>(4/5)c^j-1>(23/60)c^j>c^j/3.                     (41)

The middle step uses c^j>12/5. For a first turn j>=1, k=m-j>=1,
(13),(17),(40),(41) give

    B_n P_par
      <(9/8)(lambda/c)^m [lambda*c^(-k)]
           beta^[2(2^k-1)]
      <(9/8)(1/2)(81/100)=729/1600.                       (42)

Here (lambda/c)^m=(1+1/m)^(-m)<=1/2 by the binomial theorem,
lambda c^(-k)<1, and beta<9/10.

For j=0, (4),(40) give

    B_n P_par<=lambda^(m+1)c^[-2(m-1)]
                <=lambda^(3-m)<1/8                      (43)

for m>=128. For no turns, c^m>20 gives S_m>(3/4)c^m and S_m>8, so(13)
and(40) yield

    B_n P_par<(3/8)lambda(lambda/c)^m<=3lambda/16
                <729/1600.                             (44)

For the last strict comparison, lambda<17/7<243/100, since sqrt(2)<10/7;
then 3lambda/16<729/1600. Absorbing trajectories have payoff0. These cases
exhaust all starts and establish(1) as a complete proof draft.

### 9.1. Uniform asymptotic sharpening, including varying first-turn levels

No limit for the EXACT benchmark B_n is assumed. We continue to use only
the finite comparator (40). Write A_m=a_m/(c_m-2), explicitly showing
the enclosing-horizon dependence already fixed earlier. The physical
definitions and (14) give

    c_m->lambda, a_m->1/lambda=lambda-2, A_m->1,
    (lambda/c_m)^m=(1+1/m)^(-m)->1/e,
    S_j/c_m^j=A_m+(1-A_m)(2/c_m)^j-c_m^(-j).              (45)

For all j>=m/2, the final expression tends to1 UNIFORMLY: the last two
terms have absolute values bounded by
|1-A_m|(5/6)^(m/2)+(5/12)^(m/2), since c_m>12/5.
Also S_j tends to infinity uniformly on that range. The explicit rational
formula E(T) has T E(T)->1/4, so

    sup_(m/2<=j<=m) |c_m^j E(S_j)-1/4| ->0.              (46)

For no turns, (4),(40),(45),(46) yield

    limsup B_n P_par <=lambda/(4e).                      (47)

For first turn j=0, (43) gives a uniformly vanishing bound. For j>=1,
put k=m-j as before. The detailed bound (4) and comparator (40) give

    B_n P_par
      <= (lambda/c_m)^m [c_m^j E(S_j)]
                         lambda c_m^(-k) beta_j^[2(2^k-1)]. (48)

Uniformly in j, (17) gives

    beta_j<bar_beta_m=c_m^2(c_m-2)/(2c_m-2)<9/10,
    bar_beta_m ->beta_star=lambda/(2sqrt(2)).              (49)

The limit in (49) uses lambda^2(lambda-2)=lambda. First consider
j>=m/2. Then k>=1; because c_m>1 and bar_beta_m<1, the last two factors
in (48) are at most (lambda/c_m)*bar_beta_m^2. Equation (46) therefore
proves a uniform limit-superior bound beta_star^2/(4e) on this range.

For 1<=j<m/2, k>m/2. Equations (13),(41) give
c_m^j E(S_j)<9/8. In (48), the other non-dyadic factors are bounded by
lambda, whereas

    beta_j^[2(2^k-1)]
       <=(9/10)^[2(2^(m/2)-1)] ->0.

Thus the smaller-j range is uniformly negligible as well. This explicit
split justifies the supremum over ALL horizon-dependent first-turn
levels; a fixed-j calculation alone would not suffice. We have proved
the sharper turned-domain candidate bound

    limsup_(m->infinity) sup_(first-turn level j>=1)
            B_n P_par <=beta_star^2/(4e)
                       =(3+2sqrt(2))/(32e).              (50)

Taking the maximum of (47),(50), the vanishing j=0 bound, and the zero
absorbing payoff proves (1a). Indeed beta_star^2=lambda^2/8<lambda,
and e>1+1+1/2=5/2>lambda, so lambda/(4e)<1/4. The no-turn and
turning estimates all use the ORIGINAL initial distance.

## 10. Audit and unresolved original task

Every threshold argument used the exact h_i>1 recursion. The physical c,a
were kept fixed through all embedded H_j. Every local closest-distance
estimate was multiplied by an explicit ratio to R_0, either(30) or(38).
The j=0 crossing was aligned by retaining its next physical bridge and a
binary-popcount weight; no right child was reset or independently optimized.
The finite benchmark comparison came from its recurrence, not a conjectured
limit for B_n. Equations(6),(7) supply global all-pair legality independently
of the estimates.

The proof is UNVERIFIED and has not entered the fact graph. It is a concrete
candidate for separate selection if the main agent allocates a verifier gate.
Even acceptance would close only this fixed parabolic mechanism on H_m for
m>=128. The original unrestricted exact-profile target remains unresolved.
