The performance W_n and exact benchmark B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 are those in accepted
facts b98bb807d514e80d and 1252b8823bb5a290. All additional constructions and
estimates are proved below. The initial norm used here is proved to equal the
distance to the ENTIRE minimizer set, not just to an arbitrarily chosen optimum.

The new conclusion has two parts. A fixed core-ended projection defect can
survive an arbitrarily long objective tail with a fixed relative surplus. But
iterating the specified constant-coordinate transfer across balanced primitive
joins necessarily dilutes that surplus. Neither conclusion settles the original
all-schedule minimax problem.

## 1. Projection functions and the meaning of a core endpoint

For a compact convex set K containing 0, put

    F_K(x)=max_(g in K) {<x,g>-||g||^2/2}.

Completing the square shows that the unique maximizer is P_K(x), the Euclidean
projection of x onto K. A vector g in K is this projection exactly when

    <v-g,x-g> <= 0                    for every v in K.             (1)

For polytopes it suffices to check every listed vertex. The two projection
inequalities for x,x' imply

    ||P_K(x')-P_K(x)||^2 <= <x'-x,P_K(x')-P_K(x)>.

Thus the projection is 1-Lipschitz. Evaluating the two maxima at each other's
maximizers gives

    0 <= F_K(x')-F_K(x)-<P_K(x),x'-x>
      <= <P_K(x')-P_K(x),x'-x> <= ||x'-x||^2.

Consequently F_K is finite, convex, differentiable, and has 1-Lipschitz gradient
P_K. Furthermore

    argmin F_K = K^polar := {z : <z,g><=0 for every g in K}.          (2)

Indeed the displayed polar inequalities imply F_K(z)=0. Conversely, if
F_K(z)=0, apply its defining inequality to epsilon*g in K and let epsilon
decrease to zero to obtain <z,g><=0.

Fix a finite nonnegative prefix p=(p_0,...,p_(ell-1)) and actual projection
data x_i,g_i for i=0,...,ell, including 0 as an optimum sample. Thus
x_(i+1)=x_i-p_i*g_i, and (1) holds against 0 and every g_j. It suffices to
use K_0=conv(0,g_0,...,g_ell). Assume

    x_ell = g_ell = w != 0.                                       (3)

This is the *core endpoint* condition. Define

    A=1+sum p_i,  R_i=sum_(j=i)^(ell-1) p_j,
    y_i=x_i-g_i,  r_init^2=||x_0||^2,
    Delta=A^2||w||^2-r_init^2.

The last quantity is the particular squared-distance defect studied here.
It is not asserted to represent every possible failure of primitive validity.

## 2. One finite buffer works for EVERY negative terminal direction

Choose a nonnegative number beta satisfying

    beta >= max_i (-<g_i,w>)_+,
    beta >= max_(i:R_i>0) (-<w,y_i>)_+/R_i.                        (4)

An empty maximum is zero and (u)_+=max(u,0). These are maxima of finitely many
explicit numbers, so beta is finite. For R_i=0, nonnegativity of all remaining
steps gives x_i=x_ell=w. Uniqueness of projection gives g_i=w and y_i=0; those
indices require no division by zero.

For any tau>0 lift the old gradients and positions into one extra coordinate:

    G_i=(g_i,sqrt(beta)),
    X_i=(x_i,(1+R_i)*sqrt(beta)),
    k=-tau*G_ell,
    K=conv(0,G_0,...,G_ell,k).                                    (5)

Every old sample is still a projection sample for this single K. Against an
old vertex G_j the extra-coordinate difference vanishes, so its normal is
exactly the original normal in (1). Against 0 the new normal is

    -<g_i,y_i>-beta*R_i <= 0.

Here <g_i,y_i>>=0 follows by using the old zero vertex. Against k the normal is

    <-tau*w-g_i,y_i>-(1+tau)*beta*R_i <= 0,                        (6)

because -<g_i,y_i><=0 and -<w,y_i><=beta*R_i. The R_i=0 case is zero.

At every point u*k with u>=1, the projection is k. The zero vertex has
nonpositive normal. An old vertex has

    <G_i-k,k>
      =-tau*(<g_i,w>+beta)-tau^2*(||w||^2+beta) <= 0               (7)

by (4); multiply this by u-1. The k vertex has zero normal. Equations
(6)-(7) check every old/new ordered pair through one common projection body.

The lifted initial point has the exact positive-cone representation

    X_0=G_ell+sum_(i<ell) p_i*G_i.                               (8)

For every z in K^polar, (8) gives <X_0,z><=0. Hence
||X_0-z||^2>=||X_0||^2, with equality at z=0. The true initial distance is

    dist(X_0,argmin F_K)^2 = r_init^2+A^2*beta.                    (9)

This includes duplicated gradients and zero physical steps. The construction
does not impose any restriction on upper-certificate support or PSD rank.

## 3. Arbitrary objective tails and a surplus independent of their length

Let z=(z_0,...,z_(m-1)) be ANY finite nonnegative tail, with total T and
D=1+2T. Choose any bridge 1+d with d>0, and use (5) with tau=d/D. After
the prefix, X_ell=G_ell. The bridge sends this point to -d*G_ell=D*k.
At a tail partial sum t, the iterate is (D-t)*k. Since 0<=t<=T,
D-t>=T+1>=1. Section 2 proves that its gradient is always k. In particular
the final point is (T+1)*k, and

    2F_K(X_final)=D*||k||^2=(d^2/D)*(||w||^2+beta).

Combining with (9) proves the exact attained normalized payoff

    E(p,d,z;beta)
       = (d^2/D)*(||w||^2+beta)/(r_init^2+A^2*beta).               (10)

This is an actual lower witness for W_(ell+1+m)(p,1+d,z). It uses the exact
chronological tail; no optimization over its ordering or gradients was made.

In particular choose the source ConPD bridge

    d=(sqrt(D^2+8*A*D)-D)/4,
    2d^2+Dd=AD.                                                  (11)

This equals psi(sum p_i,T)-1 from the problem's exact recurrence. Its total
physical mass is

    B_concat=2A+2d+D=(D+2d)^2/D,
    d^2/(D*A^2)=1/B_concat.                                     (12)

Therefore (10) becomes

    E=(1+delta)/B_concat,
    delta=Delta/(r_init^2+A^2*beta).                             (13)

If Delta>0, this is a strict positive relative surplus INDEPENDENT of the
tail length, total T, ordering, and values. A single beta from (4) works for
all of them. This strengthens a finite strict-defect implication only for
the explicitly stated projection/core class; it does not normalize an
arbitrary smooth-convex defect into that class.

For any L>0 multiply F_K by L. The physical updates h_i/L then produce the
same normalized payoff. Scaling the argument and objective simultaneously
can normalize the true distance in (9) to one.

## 4. The detected dense direction has an explicit core defect

This section rederives the needed geometry; the round16 planar draft is not
used as a correctness premise. Put

    s=sqrt(2), p0=(16-11s)/3, q0=(8s-10)/3, m0=10s-14=q0-2p0.

For 0<=t<=1/50 set

    a=s-p0*t, b=2+q0*t, zeta=b-1,
    prefix p(t)=(a,b,a), A=1+2a+b.

This is exactly the three-step primitive-child part of the balanced dense
redistribution tested in the closed batch. Define

    U=1/(a+1)^2,
    kappa=-[zeta^2+(a+1)/2]/[zeta*(a+2)],
    u=(1/(a+1),0),
    v=(kappa,sqrt(1/2-kappa^2))/(a+1),
    w=-zeta*u-a*v,
    N=zeta^2*(2-a)+a*(a^2-2)/2, J=N/(a+2).

Expansion gives

    ||u||^2=U, ||v||^2=U/2, <u,v>=kappa*U, ||w||^2=J*U,
    r_u:=<u,w>/U=[a(a+1)/2-2zeta^2]/[zeta(a+2)],
    r_v:=<v,w>/U=[zeta^2+(1-a-a^2)/2]/(a+2),
    <w-v,-zeta*u-v>=0.                                         (14)

All following terminating decimals denote exact rationals. Squaring endpoints
gives 1.4142<s<1.4143 and consequently

    .147<p0<.149, .437<q0<.439, .140<m0<.145,
    1.411<=a<=1.415, 1<=zeta<=1.01,
    -.654<kappa<-.639, .578<N<.603,
    .169<J<.177, -.1<r_u<0, -.062<r_v<0.                         (15)

Here -kappa has numerator between 2.2055 and 2.2276 and denominator between
3.411 and 3.44915. The polynomial a(a^2-2)/2 is increasing on this interval,
so bounding it and zeta^2(2-a) separately proves the N bounds. For r_u the
numerator is at least 1.411*2.411/2-2*1.01^2=-.3392395 and is negative;
its denominator is at least 3.411. For r_v the numerator is at least
1+(1-1.415-1.415^2)/2=-.2086125 and is negative; its denominator is at
least 3.411. These prove the last two bounds. Also .654^2<1/2, so v is real
and u,v are independent.

Use K_0=conv(0,u,v,w) and the prefix data

    x_0=(a+1)u=(1,0), g_0=u;
    x_1=u,             g_1=u;
    x_2=-zeta*u,       g_2=v;
    x_3=w,             g_3=w.                                  (16)

The recursion for (a,b,a) holds exactly. At samples 1 and 3 the residual is
zero. At sample 0 it is a*u; (15) checks its normal against all four vertices.
At sample 2, put y=-zeta*u-v. The normals against 0 and u, in units of U,
are zeta*kappa+1/2<0 and

    -zeta+(zeta-1)*kappa+1/2 <= -1/2.

The w normal is zero by (14), and the v normal is zero by definition. Thus
(16) is an actual prefix trajectory with a core endpoint.

The buffer beta=U/8 satisfies (4). Indeed the only negative endpoint
correlations in (14) have magnitude less than U/10. For the residual test,
sample 0 contributes a*(-r_u)*U/(2a+b)<U/10, sample 1 contributes zero,
and <w,y_2>=<v,y_2>=(-zeta*kappa-1/2)U>0. Sample 3 has no remaining
steps and zero residual.

To bound its defect, set

    R_prim(t)=A^2*J/(a+1)^2.

At t=0, A=3+2s=(s+1)^2 and J=(s-1)^2=1/A, so R_prim(0)=1.
Differentiation, with A'=m0>0, gives

    (log R_prim)'=2m0/A+2p0/(a+1)+N'/N+p0/(a+2),
    N'=2zeta*(2-a)*q0-p0[-zeta^2+(3a^2-2)/2].                   (17)

The first product in N' is greater than 1.17*.437; the square bracket is
less than 1.004. Hence N'>1.17*.437-1.004*.149>.361. From (15),

    (log R_prim)' > 294/2415+361/603+147/3415 > 3/4.

The last inequality follows by multiplication by positive integer
denominators. Integrating and using exp(u)>=1+u gives

    R_prim(t)>=1+3t/4.

Also A<=5.84 and a+1>=2.411, so

    1+A^2*U/8 <= 1+5.84^2/(8*2.411^2) < 7/4.

Consequently the surplus in (13) obeys

    delta(t)=[R_prim(t)-1]/[1+A^2*U/8] >= 3t/7.                 (18)

For t>0 the inequalities are strict where indicated. Every bound is uniform
over the full stated parameter interval and has no numerical solver premise.

## 5. A named unbounded-horizon family is strictly worse than the benchmark

Fix any t in (0,1/50]. For each m>=0 take ANY nonnegative m-step suffix z
whose sum T is at most S_bullet(m). Use prefix p(t) from section 4 and bridge
(11). This is a specified family of physical schedules of length n=m+4.
It allows arbitrary tail order, zero steps, and complete dual re-selection.

Since d<A<6, (12) gives

    B_concat < D+4A < B_m+24 <= B_n+24.

The final comparison follows directly from monotonicity of the exact dominant
recurrence: the empty-prefix split gives
G(1,B_j)=2+B_j/2+sqrt(B_j^2+8B_j)/2>B_j. Also B_n>=2n+1 by the same
recurrence, since G(1,D)>=D+2 and B_0=1.

Equations (13) and (18) prove

    B_n*W_n(p(t),1+d,z)
      >= (1+3t/7)*B_n/(B_n+24).                                (19)

In particular the limit inferior, uniformly over this entire suffix class,
is at least 1+3t/7. Explicitly, for n>=ceil(56/t+12), the right side is at
least 1+3t/14. Thus the fixed prefix defect need not disappear when the
objective tail grows without bound.

This is a LOWER bound showing a particular family is too poor. It is not
an improved upper schedule, not an all-horizon minimax converse, and not
an inference from a finite objective value. It does not assume equality
between a Silver subsequence and the exact B_n benchmark.

## 6. What happens when this transfer is repeated at primitive joins

The same projection calculation has a core-ending version. Append any
nonnegative block of capacity C=1+sum(block)>1 to a core prefix of capacity
A, with bridge 1+r satisfying

    r*(A+C+r)=A*C.

Write A_next=A+C+r and tau=r/C=A/A_next in (5). The bridge reaches C*k;
the block's constant gradient k leaves final point k. The complete normal
audit in section 2 applies because every point in this block is u*k with
u>=1. The capacity and initial norm identities give

    A_next^2||k||^2=A^2(||w||^2+beta),
    r_init,next^2=r_init^2+A^2*beta,
    Delta_next=Delta.                                           (20)

Now iterate this SPECIFIC construction. At level j let the capacity be A_j,
the core endpoint w_j, and initial squared distance R_j^2. The jth join has
tau_j=A_j/A_(j+1) in (0,1). It adds one constant coordinate sqrt(beta_j)
to every old gradient, retains all old vertices, and has

    w_(j+1)=-tau_j*(w_j,sqrt(beta_j)).

Allow ANY beta_j>=0 for which the actual construction is legal. It need not
satisfy the sufficient all-tau bound (4). Let N_j=A_j^2||w_j||^2=R_j^2+Delta,
where (20) makes Delta>0 independent of j.

For j>=1, the old prefix contains the previously queried vertex

    v_old=-w_j/tau_(j-1).

At the first point of the new appended block, the residual is
(C_j-1)*w_(j+1). Since C_j>1, its normal against the lifted v_old forces

    beta_j >= [(1/tau_(j-1)-tau_j)/(1+tau_j)]*||w_j||^2.          (21)

This is an ORIGINAL normal inequality, not a condition imposed for
convenience. To see it, expand
<(v_old,sqrt(beta_j))-w_(j+1),w_(j+1)><=0 and divide by tau_j>0.

It follows from (20)-(21) that

    N_(j+1) >= [(1+1/tau_(j-1))/(1+tau_j)]*N_j.

For r>=1 the factors telescope exactly:

    N_r >= N_1 * (1+tau_0)/(1+tau_(r-1)) * A_(r-1)/A_0.         (22)

Thus Delta/R_r^2 tends to zero whenever A_(r-1) tends to infinity. This
permits arbitrary nonempty appended blocks and arbitrarily retuned legal
buffers in the specified construction. The C_j>1 assumption is essential
to this particular normal argument: if the appended block has zero mass,
its first point is already core and that normal provides no restriction.

For balanced joins C_j=A_j, put lambda=1+sqrt(2). Then
A_(j+1)=lambda*A_j, tau_j=1/lambda, and (21) reads
beta_j>=sqrt(2)*||w_j||^2. Consequently

    N_r >= lambda^(r-1)*N_1,
    Delta/R_r^2 <= Delta/[lambda^(r-1)*N_1-Delta].                (23)

If the appended physical block is an identical copy of the current prefix,
its length obeys ell_r+1=2^r*(ell_0+1). Hence the relative defect carried
by this single-branch construction is O((ell_r+1)^(-log_2(lambda))). This
remains true if a fixed modified three-step seed occurs in a positive
fraction of the physical word: the constructed trajectory uses a constant
gradient on each appended copy and does not exploit that copy's own defect.

An eventual objective-tail transfer can only reduce this relative surplus,
since (13) divides Delta by R_r^2+A_r^2*beta_final>=R_r^2. Therefore serial
constant-coordinate transfers do not automatically turn a fixed finite
defect into a fixed relative obstruction on repeated-copy dense variations.

This is a limit of the specified witness construction. It is NOT an upper
bound on W, a restriction on full PEP ranks or multipliers, or an assertion
that no different joint multi-block construction can retain a fixed gap.

There is an explicit counterexample to deleting C_j>1 from the claim about
arbitrarily selected legal buffers. Start with the one-step prefix (2),
K_0=[-1,1], x_0=g_0=1 and x_1=g_1=-1. Its capacity is A_0=3 and
Delta=8. Append only EMPTY right blocks, C_j=1, and the exact primitive
bridges 1+r_j, where r_j*(A_j+1+r_j)=A_j. Choose every beta_j=0.
Then 0<r_j<1, all sampled points stay in [-1,1], and the same function
F_( [-1,1] ) has gradient equal to the point throughout the trajectory.
Every endpoint is core. The identities A_(j+1)*r_j=A_j and
w_(j+1)=-r_j*w_j imply A_j^2*w_j^2=9, while R_j^2=1.
Also A_(j+1)>A_j+1, so A_j tends to infinity. Thus Delta/R_j^2=8
does NOT decay in this zero-mass-right-block case. Every original normal
is valid because its residual is zero. This example pinpoints exactly why
the nonzero appended mass is needed in (21).

## 7. Scope of the advance

The finite full-model data suggested retaining a nontrivial core-ended
prefix, instead of testing only the global Huber and quadratic trajectories.
The new formula (13) gives a tail-uniform quantitative use of such a prefix.
Equation (19) makes it an actual unbounded-horizon obstruction for a named
class. The separate original-pair inequality (21) identifies precisely why
the obvious recursive extension loses its fixed relative strength.

The remaining bridge is a construction coupling defects in a growing set
of modified child blocks, with all original normals and the total initial
distance retained. No such bridge or improving full upper certificate has
been established here. The original target remains unresolved.

evidence:
# Both child defects, an actual common function, and the cost of resetting boundaries

Status: **UNVERIFIED joint proof candidate**, eighth launch, cumulative round19.
No fact_submit, optimization, parameter search, installation or subagent.
This is a construction and a limitation of its specified iteration class,
not a resolution of the original minimax problem. Definitions of W_n, Q_ij
and the exact B_n comparison are from accepted1252b8823bb5a290 and
b98bb807d514e80d. All additional mathematics used below is rederived here;
the previous round's unverified construction is not used as a truth premise.

## 1. Actual core data and the common projection function

The input is a nonnegative finite word p=(p_0,...,p_(ell-1)) and ALL vectors
x_i,g_i,0<=i<=ell, including the endpoint and every repeated/zero-step sample.
The optimum sample is0. Require

    x_(i+1)=x_i-p_i g_i, y_i=x_i-g_i,
    <g_j-g_i,y_i><=0 for every i,j, <g_i,y_i>>=0,
    x_ell=g_ell=w !=0.                                    (1)

Set K=conv(0,g_0,...,g_ell) and

    F_K(x)=max_(g in K)(<x,g>-||g||^2/2),
    f_i=<x_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2, f_*=0,
    A=1+sum p_i, R_i=sum_(t=i)^(ell-1) p_t, R^2=||x_0||^2,
    Delta=A^2||w||^2-R^2, kappa=A^2||w||^2/R^2.            (2)

Completing the square identifies the maximizer with the projection onto K;
(1) is exactly its normal condition. Adding the projection conditions for
two points gives ||P_K(x)-P_K(x')||^2<=<x-x',P_K(x)-P_K(x')>.
It follows that P_K is 1-Lipschitz. Evaluation of the two maxima at their
opposite maximizers bounds the differentiability remainder by ||x-x'||^2,
so F_K is convex differentiable and 1-smooth with gradient P_K and values (2).

Its minimizers are K^polar={z:<z,g><=0 for every g in K}. To prove the
nontrivial implication F_K(z)=0 => z in K^polar, test epsilon*g in the
definition and let epsilon decrease to0. The GD identity gives

    x_0=w+sum_(i<ell) p_i g_i.                             (3)

Thus <x_0,z><=0 for every minimizer z and
||x_0-z||^2>=||x_0||^2, with equality at0. R is the TRUE closest-minimizer
distance. Also direct expansion of the original interpolation residual gives

    Q_ij=<g_i-g_j,y_j>, Q_i*=0, Q_*i=-<g_i,y_i><=0.        (4)

Every subsequent normal check therefore covers all original ordered-pair,
bridge, old-sample and optimum interpolation inequalities, with the indicated
values. No child translation or common value shift is a free operation.

## 2. A finite explicit lift of every actual child

Call a child admissible for the joint operation if, in addition to (1),

    <g_i,w>>=0, <y_i,w>>=0,
    <g_i,x_0>>=0, <y_i,x_0>>=0 for every i.                 (5)

These are four lists of ACTUAL boundary pairings, not a condition on Delta
alone. Any input satisfying (1) can be converted into such a child. Define

    beta_min = max(0,
       max_i (-<g_i,w>),
       max_(i:R_i>0) (-<w,y_i>/R_i),
       max_i (-<x_0,g_i>/A),
       max_(i:R_i>0) (-<x_0,y_i>/(A R_i))).                (6)

An empty maximum is omitted. Choose any finite beta>=beta_min and set

    ghat_i=(g_i,sqrt(beta)),
    xhat_i=(x_i,(1+R_i)sqrt(beta)),
    what=(w,sqrt(beta)), Khat=conv(0,ghat_0,...,ghat_ell). (7)

The physical GD updates hold. For old vertices, the added gradient
coordinates cancel, so every old/old normal is exactly the original one.
The zero-vertex normal is -<g_i,y_i>-beta R_i<=0. The four pairings in
(5) become, respectively,

    <g_i,w>+beta,             <w,y_i>+beta R_i,
    <x_0,g_i>+A beta,         <x_0,y_i>+A beta R_i.         (8)

They are nonnegative by (6). If R_i=0, all remaining physical steps vanish,
so x_i=x_ell=w; uniqueness of projection gives g_i=w and y_i=0. Thus no
uncontrolled numerator was omitted in (6). Formula (6) is the exact minimum
beta within THIS constant-coordinate lift for all four signs (5).

The new values, minimizers and true distance are explicit:

two identical copies of the current complete child and the balanced source
bridge, then ANY finite reset beta satisfying (5). This includes every

    A_(j+1)=lambda A_j, r_j=theta A_j,
    u_j=1/kappa_j=R_j^2/(A_j^2||w_j||^2),
    sigma_j=<x_j,0,w_j>/(A_j||w_j||^2),
    b_j=beta_j/||W_j||^2,

    F(s)=(lambda s-s^2)/(1+lambda s),

For a concrete continuation of the detected small word, put

## 6. Matched objective-tail conversion, without another hidden buffer

Take ANY final child satisfying (1),(5), of capacity A, endpoint w and
true distance R. Let the actual finite tail z have nonnegative entries,

    d=(sqrt(D^2+8AD)-D)/4,
    2d^2+Dd=AD,

normalized objective for the ACTUAL schedule is exactly

    E_tail=kappa/B_concat.                              (29)

This is the full conversion used here; it needs no C61/C62 premise and no
unrecorded final lift. It allows arbitrary ordering, arbitrary finite
nonnegative tail entries, zero mass, and the empty tail. Both L-scaling and
normalizing the true initial distance follow directly from (2).

For every resulting horizon n=ell+1+length(z), its exact comparison is

    B_n W_n(p,1+d,z)>=kappa B_n/B_concat.                (30)

Nothing replaces B_n by B_concat or by a dyadic asymptotic proxy. For the
iteration in section4, the EXTRA factor kappa tends to1 by (21).
The construction therefore supplies no persistent relative surplus over
its own actual reciprocal-mass witness. The right side of (30) must still
be compared with the exact B_n before drawing any schedule-level conclusion.

For example, with an empty objective tail, B_concat(A)=2A+1/2+sqrt(1+8A)/2.

ratio (26). This identifies the leading mass increase; it does NOT assert

## 7. Full-model calibration and the empty-child boundary

If both child ratios are1, (15) gives kappa_new=1 for EVERY buffer. The
orthogonal seed at t=0 has kappa_0=1 by (24); all its reset joins preserve1,
and (29) gives exactly1/B_concat, without a fictitious positive surplus.

There is also a complete exact benchmark calibration. With an empty core
x_0=w=1, A=1, an empty tail D=1 gives d=1/2, schedule(3/2), B_1=4,
K=[-1/2,1], and attained error1/4. On the ORIGINAL formal vectors
(x_0,g_0,g_1), using x_1=x_0-(3/2)g_0, direct expansion gives

    ||x_0||^2/4-2f_1+Q_(1,0)+Q_(0,*)+Q_(1,*)
       =||x_0-2g_0-2g_1||^2/4.                          (31)

Every multiplier is1 and the full remainder is PSD, with exact value flow.
The recurrence in accepted b98bb807d514e80d gives B_1=4, so (31) and the
constructed function match the exact known benchmark. At horizon0,
||x_0||^2-2f_0+2Q_(0,*)=||x_0-g_0||^2 gives B_0=1 as well.

Empty and zero-mass children are allowed in the general construction:
A=1, x_i=g_i=w, y_i=0 and kappa=1. Formula (6) has no division by zero,
and sections2-3 still check all actual samples. A positive-defect seed in
section4 is necessarily nonempty and has positive mass. Its loss statement
concerns repeated IDENTICAL full children and resetting (5) at each level.
It does not apply to serial addition of empty right blocks without those
resets. Indeed, starting at1 on the function with projection body[-1,1]
and word(2), the endpoint is-1, A=3, Delta=8. Serial empty-right joins with
r_j(A_j+1+r_j)=A_j and no buffer keep all residuals zero and A_j^2 w_j^2=9
while the true initial distance stays1. Their constant relative defect8
does not contradict (21): they are not the balanced identical-child reset
operation and do not satisfy its retained sign condition (5).

## 8. What this closes and what is still missing

This package gives a full legal, real, arbitrary-depth two-child construction,
an exact interaction/normalization law, and a necessary old-vertex cost
that makes its relative surplus O(1/depth). It retains a growing collection
of modified blocks, nonzero post-step residuals, values and the global
closest-minimizer distance. It is a substantive improvement over a serial
lift's geometric dilution, but it still has no fixed asymptotic gap.

Leaving this obstruction requires retaining signed boundary data rather than
forcing all four lists (5), changing the cross-correlation operation, using
nonidentical/unequal children outside the class of section4, or changing the
core interface itself. A transverse correlation change alone cannot repair
the particular planar bridge normal recorded in the separate round18 draft.
None of these remaining mechanisms is proved here. A failed lower gluing
rule gives neither an all-h lower theorem nor an improving full upper
certificate. The original target, with every horizon and every nonnegative
schedule compared to the exact B_n, remains open.

# Full transverse coupling: exact separation of the actual 63-step parent

Status: **UNVERIFIED self-contained joint proof candidate**, worker max,
ninth launch, cumulative round 20. The verifier has not accepted this result.
The current TASK and public ledger allow zero verification calls. The only
accepted fact used is 1252b8823bb5a290, for the definition and necessity of the

## 1. Statement and scope

Put s=sqrt(2), lambda=1+s, theta=s-1=1/lambda. Choose a>0 and xi>=theta,
and define H=a+1, b=1+H*xi, D=1+3xi+xi^2. The seed word is (a,b,a).
Its actual orthogonal-core transcript is given in section 3. Recursively
form the words h[0]=(a,b,a) and

    A_j=1+sum h[j]=lambda^j A_0,  A_0=H(2+xi),
    r_j=theta A_j,  h[j+1]=(h[j],1+r_j,h[j]).              (1)

Thus h[j] has 4*2^j-1 steps. At every join use isometric copies of the
complete child transcripts, leave the left copy unscaled, scale the right
copy by alpha=r_j ||w||/||x_0||, and align its initial point with -r_j w.
Keep the projection values f_i=<x_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2 and the optimum jet 0.
No extra gradient coordinate, translation, or function-value change is made.

The following are the claims of this joint candidate.

1. The most general real cross Gram for this operation is parameterized
   by a completely unrestricted real contraction between the two fixed
   transverse spaces. Section 2 gives its exact PSD condition, both sets of
   cross normals, all bridge/optimum constraints, explicit realization,
   common projection function when feasible, and true distance.
2. For zero transverse cross map at the first three joins, the complete
   7-, 15-, and 31-step children are legal. If xi>theta they have strictly
   positive core defect. Nevertheless, for the two actual 31-step children,
   **every** real transverse map at the 63-step join violates

       Q_(36,30)=e_30 [lambda T(xi)-1]>0,
       T(xi)=xi(2+xi)^2(1+xi)/D^2,  e_30=a||w_3||^2>0.   (2)

   This includes all maps satisfying the full PSD condition, without a rank,
   sign, symmetry, or boundary-positivity restriction.
3. The previously observed failed row Q_(32,25) is NOT invariant. Its
   transverse coefficient is nonzero. The different row (2) is the exact

4. If xi>theta, infeasibility persists even when arbitrary transverse maps
   are chosen at every earlier join, and even if different choices are made

       [(1+xi) Q_(36,30)+Q_(38,30)]/[(2+xi)e_30]
          = lambda q-1
          = (xi-theta)(s*xi+lambda)/D >0,
       q=xi(2+xi)/D.                                    (3)

   The two weights are strictly positive. Thus the claimed parent cannot
   satisfy all original Q inequalities. This broader claim needs xi>theta;
   (2), for the fixed rank-one-built children, also covers xi=theta.
5. Re-selecting arbitrary real function values cannot repair either
   obstruction while the displayed positions, gradients, and optimum at
   zero are retained. The projection values are forced separately on every
   embedded seed copy, as proved at the end of section 5.

For the particular modified-word interval requested by TASK, let

    p0=(16-11s)/3, q0=(8s-10)/3,
    a=s-p0*t, b=2+q0*t, 0<=t<=1/50,
    xi=(b-1)/(a+1).                                     (4)

Then a>0 and xi>=theta, with strict inequality for t>0. The SAME algebraic
seed t=1/100 was used for every discovery comparison. Explicitly it is

    a=(311s-16)/300, b=(590+8s)/300,
    H=(284+311s)/300, xi=(290+8s)/(284+311s),
    A_0=(143+105s)/50.                                  (5)

The words, physical child transcripts, and normalization are unchanged
between the zero-map and full-map 63-step tests. These claims exclude this
specified recursive projection construction. They do not exclude different
seed transcripts, lifts, translations, different optimum alignment, or operations, and
do not resolve the original all-schedule, all-horizon exact-profile goal.

## 2. All real transverse freedom and every original constraint

A child input consists of a finite nonnegative word p of length ell and
vectors x_i,g_i for 0<=i<=ell, including all duplicates and the endpoint.
Define y_i=x_i-g_i, e_i=<g_i,y_i>, w=x_ell=g_ell!=0, and require

    x_(i+1)=x_i-p_i g_i,
    <g_j-g_i,y_i><=0 for every i,j, e_i>=0.              (6)

Set K=conv(0,g_0,...,g_ell) and

    F_K(x)=max_(v in K)(<x,v>-||v||^2/2),
    f_i=<x_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2, f_star=0.                (7)

Completing the square proves that the maximizer is P_K(x), the Euclidean
projection. Its unique minimizer condition is
<v-P_K(x),x-P_K(x)><=0 for every v in K. Thus (6) makes g_i=P_K(x_i).
Adding this condition at two points gives
||P_K(x)-P_K(z)||^2<=<x-z,P_K(x)-P_K(z)>, hence P_K is 1-Lipschitz.
Evaluation of the two maxima at the opposite maximizers gives
0<=F_K(x+d)-F_K(x)-<P_K(x),d><=||d||^2. Consequently F_K is differentiable,
convex and 1-smooth, with gradient P_K, and it interpolates (7).

The original residual from fact 1252b8823bb5a290 is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
        =<g_i-g_j,y_j>.                                 (8)

Expansion of the inner products proves this identity. In particular,
Q_i,star=0 and Q_star,i=-e_i. These include both optimum incidences.

The minimizer set of F_K is K^polar={z:<z,v><=0 for every v in K}.
For necessity, test epsilon*v in (7), divide by epsilon, and let epsilon
decrease to zero. Sufficiency follows directly from (7), including v=0.
The update equations imply x_0=w+sum_(i<ell)p_i g_i. For every minimizer z,
<x_0,z><=0, and ||x_0-z||^2>=||x_0||^2. Zero is therefore a closest
minimizer: the TRUE distance is R=||x_0||>0.

For two children L,R, set R_R=||x_R,0||, e=w_L/||w_L||, d=x_R,0/R_R,
alpha=r||w_L||/R_R for the bridge 1+r, where r>0. Let E=e^perp in the
left child span and Dspace=d^perp in the right child span. Write
u_perp=u-<u,e>e and v_perp=v-<v,d>d.

Every allowed pair of real isometries J_L,J_R satisfies J_R d=-J_L e.
It therefore has cross form

    B_C(u,v)=<J_L u,J_R v>
       =-<u,e><v,d>+<u_perp,C v_perp>,                    (9)

where C:Dspace->E is linear and ||C||<=1. To prove necessity, project
J_R v_perp orthogonally onto J_L E; its norm is at most ||v_perp||.
All axial/transverse cross terms vanish because the transverse images are
orthogonal to the common axis. No other restriction on C follows.

Conversely, for any real C with ||C||<=1, put S_C=(I-C^T C)^(1/2), the
positive semidefinite real square root. In R direct-sum E direct-sum Dspace,
define

    J_L u=(<u,e>,u_perp,0),
    J_R v=(-<v,d>,C v_perp,S_C v_perp).                   (10)

The equality C^T C+S_C^2=I proves both isometries, their alignment, and (9).
Zero eigenvalues are retained; nothing is clipped or discarded. In chosen
orthonormal transverse bases, the exact PSD condition is

    [[I,C],[C^T,I]] >=0.                                (11)

Indeed its quadratic form at (z,v) is
||z+C v||^2+<v,(I-C^T C)v>. Setting z=-Cv proves necessity, and the same
identity proves sufficiency. Thus (11) is equivalent to realizability,

## 2. All real transverse freedom and every original constraint

A child input consists of a finite nonnegative word p of length ell and
vectors x_i,g_i for 0<=i<=ell, including all duplicates and the endpoint.
Define y_i=x_i-g_i, e_i=<g_i,y_i>, w=x_ell=g_ell!=0, and require

# Full four-step seed: a compact domain from legal cut functions

Status: complete joint proof DRAFT, not verifier-accepted. This round has no
numerical or fact_submit allowance. No unverified finding is used as a premise.
The accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the interpolation convention Q<=0;
the particular functions and all algebra below are derived explicitly.

## 1. Interface and energy

Let h=(h_0,h_1,h_2,h_3)>=0, s=sum h_i, C=1+s>=193/25.
Indices i,j range over0,...,4. Set p_i=1+sum_(t<i)h_t, so p_0=1,p_4=C.
Let e=(1,1,1,1,1)^T. Define T_ii=1,T_it=h_t for t<i,T_it=0 for t>i,
Lambda_ii=0,Lambda_ij>=0,L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda,
omega=(-2h_0,-2h_1,-2h_2,-2h_3,2s)^T, and
D=diag(h_0(2-h_0),...,h_3(2-h_3),-s(s+2)).
The full interface is

    L^T e=omega, M=D+(LT+T^T L^T)/2 >=0.                 (1)

No multiplier support, rank, remainder, symmetry, or step order is fixed.
For arbitrary formal GD data x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i, define

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V=2sum_(i<4)h_i(f_i-f_4)+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
      -s(s+1)||g_4||^2.

Put delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2 and y_i=x_i-g_i=x_0-(Tg)_i.
Then Q_ij=delta_i-delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>, while
V=-omega^T delta+sum_i D_ii||g_i||^2. Value flow in(1) therefore gives

    V+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij = sum_(i,j)M_ij<g_i,g_j>. (2)

In particular every feasible full certificate implies V>=0 on every legal
convex differentiable1-smooth trajectory with a minimizer. This direction
requires neither certificate necessity nor any duality assertion.

## 2. Legal cut witnesses at every position

Fix j<4, put b=h_j,P=sum_(i<j)h_i,R=sum_(i>j)h_i, and first assume b>1.
Set a=(b-1)/(R+1)>0. Define the scalar function

    f(x)=x-1/2                     if x>=1,
         x^2/2                     if -a<=x<=1,
         -a*x-a^2/2                if x<=-a.

Its derivative is clamp(x,[-a,1]), which is continuous, nondecreasing,
and1-Lipschitz. The function is convex1-smooth and has a minimizer at0.
Start at x_0=P+1. Before and at j all gradients are1, and x_j=1.
After step j, x_(j+1)=1-b=-a(R+1). All subsequent gradients equal-a,
since the remaining nonnegative steps move monotonically to x_4=-a.
Every sampled value obeys f_i=x_i g_i-g_i^2/2, and x_4=g_4.

For any vector-valued data obeying these two identities, GD telescoping gives

    2sum_(i<4)h_i f_i+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
      =||x_0||^2-||x_4||^2,
    V=||x_0||^2-C^2||g_4||^2.                         (3)

Applied to this scalar function, nonnegative V implies

    C(h_j-1)_+ <= (1+P)(1+R), for every j=0,...,3.      (4)

If h_j<=1 the same inequality is automatic. Thus(4) holds on every
zero-step boundary too. Failure of any inequality is a specific legal
negative-V function, hence rules out the full interface(1).

## 3. Prefix bounds and compact capacity

For fixed C>1 define the increasing rational map

    R_C(z)=1+2Cz/(C+z), z>=0,
    r_k=R_C iterated k times at1, k=0,1,2,3.

Rearrangement of(4) gives p_(i+1)<=R_C(p_i). Conversely this inequality
is equivalent to(4) on the nonnegative schedule domain. Induction yields
p_i<=r_i. The cut constraints are invariant under reversing the four
steps, regardless of whether the original certificate admits reversal.
Applying the same induction to the reversed cut inequalities gives

    p_i >= C+1-r_(4-i).                               (5)

Only the cases i=1,2,3 are needed; r_0=1. Explicitly,

    r_1=(3C+1)/(C+1),
    r_2=(7C^2+6C+1)/(C^2+4C+1),
    r_3=(15C^3+23C^2+9C+1)/(C^3+11C^2+7C+1).          (6)

Taking i=2 in(5) and p_2<=r_2 gives C+1<=2r_2, hence

    C^3-9C^2-7C-1<=0.                                (7)

This polynomial is strictly increasing for C>=7: its derivative
3C^2-18C-7 is positive there and increasing. At C=39/4 its value is
131/64>0. Since C>=193/25>7, we conclude

    193/25 <= C < 39/4.                               (8)

In particular this argument covers all larger candidate sums; it did not
replace the target by the slice sum h=168/25.

## 4. All four steps are uniformly positive and bounded

The first and last cut inequalities give

    h_0,h_3 <= 2C/(C+1) < 78/43.                      (9)

For the lower bounds, subtract the upper prefix bound from the lower
bound for the next prefix in(5). This gives

    h_0,h_3 >= C-r_3 = N(C)/(C^3+11C^2+7C+1),
    h_1,h_2 >= C+1-r_1-r_2 = N(C)/((C+1)(C^2+4C+1)), (10)
    N(C)=C^4-4C^3-16C^2-8C-1.

The endpoint lower bound exceeds1/2 exactly when

    A(C)=2C^4-9C^3-43C^2-23C-3>0.

The middle lower bound exceeds4/5 exactly when

    B(C)=5C^4-24C^3-100C^2-60C-9>0.

At C=77/10 these polynomials respectively equal1922412/10000 and
2197285/10000. They are strictly increasing for C>=7: their derivatives
are bounded below respectively by29C^2-86C-23 and68C^2-200C-60,
both positive and increasing on that interval. Since193/25>77/10,

    h_0,h_3>1/2, h_1,h_2>4/5.                         (11)

For completeness, the middle upper bound uses the same cuts, without
assuming either middle step exceeds1. Write

    G_C(z)=R_C(z)-z=1+z(C-z)/(C+z).

For1<=z<=r_1<3 its derivative is
(C^2-2Cz-z^2)/(C+z)^2>0: its numerator is at least C^2-6C-9,
which is positive for C>=15/2. Thus h_1<=G_C(p_1)<=G_C(r_1), and
the reversed cut constraints give the same bound for h_2. Calculation yields

    G_C(r_1)=4C^3/((C+1)(C^2+4C+1)).                  (12)

The right side is strictly increasing in C>0: its logarithmic derivative
has positive numerator5C^2+10C+3 after multiplication by positive
denominators. At39/4 its value is237276/92923<13/5, with the difference
21619/464615. Consequently

    1/2<h_0,h_3<78/43, 4/5<h_1,h_2<13/5.             (13)

This excludes every zero-step boundary for this threshold by actual
witnesses. It does not assert h_i>1, ordering, or reversal of certificates.

## 5. Full multiplier compactness from the common-gradient kernel

This step bounds all20 original multipliers, including every cycle.
The vector p=Te has entries p_i. Since

    sum_i D_ii=-s^2-sum_(i<4)h_i^2,
    omega^T p=s^2+sum_(i<4)h_i^2,

equations(1) give e^T M e=0. Positive semidefiniteness implies Me=0.
For clarity this implication follows by inserting e+t v into the quadratic
form: a nonzero linear coefficient would violate nonnegativity for one
sign of sufficiently small t. Calculation of each component gives

    2De+T^T omega=-diag(p)omega,
    Lp=diag(p)omega.                                  (14)

Define A_ij=Lambda_ij p_j for i!=j and A_ii=0. Since omega_i=out_i-in_i,
equation(14) says sum_j Lambda_ij p_j=p_i in_i. Therefore

    sum_j A_ij=sum_j A_ji for every i.                 (15)

Thus A is a nonnegative circulation. Write c_i=1/p_i. Substituting
Lambda_ij=A_ij c_j into the original value flow and using(15) gives

    sum_i c_i omega_i
      =sum_(i,j) A_ij(c_i c_j-c_i^2)
      =-1/2 sum_(i,j)A_ij(c_i-c_j)^2.

Equivalently, the entire circulation has the fixed Dirichlet energy

    sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij (p_i-p_j)^2/(p_i^2 p_j)
       =4[sum_(i<4)h_i/p_i-s/C] <4s<35.              (16)

All steps exceed1/2 by(13). Consequently |p_i-p_j|>1/2 for i!=j.
Also every p_i<10 by(8), so p_i^2 p_j<1000. Every coefficient of
Lambda_ij on the left of(16) exceeds1/4000. Hence

    sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij < 140000.                      (17)

This is a bound on the complete multiplier vector, not a choice of sparse
support. No skew freedom or PSD remainder is fixed. In particular all
possible solutions of(1) at the requested threshold belong to the closed
bounded box obtained by replacing the strict inequalities in(8),(13),(17)
by non-strict ones. The equations and PSD conditions are continuous, so
their solution set in this box is compact (possibly empty).

## 6. Remaining problem

The necessary cut domain is not asserted sufficient. The full original
feasibility problem is still open inside the compact region above.
Neither a feasible seed nor a global separator has been produced.
All20 multipliers, all five formal gradients, and every remaining step
degree of freedom are retained. C78 is a conditional research bridge,
not a premise or an original-target solution.

The minimizer set of(6) is K_body^polar. If x is in this polar, the
maximum equals0. Conversely, if F(x)=0, insert tv for each v in K_body
and0<t<=1, divide by t, and let t decrease to0; then <x,v><=0.

Consequently <p,v><=0 for v in K_body^polar, and

For a leaf, direct inner products give

 R^2=m^2+Klen z+E,
 N_leaf=||W||^2=rho^2 eta+E,
 D_leaf=<p,W>=rho z+E.                                (8)

## 3. Exact coordinates for the energy-angle tradeoff

Define two dimensionless coordinates of a leaf:

 sigma=rho+E/e,
 u=c sqrt((sigma-rho)/(c+rho)).                        (9)

By(1), 0<=rho<=sigma<=1. The value u is also exactly
c epsilon sqrt(eta)/e. These definitions permit zero E and zero rho.

 C0=a(m^2+az), C1=m^2+2az,

 M-kappa = M * [(1-sigma){C0+(C0+C1)sigma}
                      +(T-D1)u^2]/[D(sigma)+T u^2].   (11)

 233/40<A<583/100,

 34.04<A^2 z<34.14,
 1<M<M_bar=251/250.                                   (12)

All terminating decimals in this manuscript denote exact rationals.

 3.417<m<3.4172, .4127<c<.4128,
 1.0043<z<1.0044, 5.8297<A<5.83;

 2.4127[3.417^2+2.4127(1.0043)]>34.01,

 (5.8297)^2(1.0043)>34.04,

The positive coefficients make endpoint substitution legitimate in

EVERY legal leaf has0<=kappa<=M<M_bar. This is an exact global envelope

## 4. Quantitative cost when a leaf has high energy

For the rest of this section suppose

 kappa>47/50=.94,
 delta=M_bar-kappa<8/125=.064.                        (13)

Then

 delta >= (5/4)(1-sigma)+u^2.                         (14)

                      d>.071-delta/5.                (15)

## 5. An original-row condition at every large bridge

Consider a node whose two children have at least two atomic leaves.
Let the LAST leaf of the left child have parameters with subscript L,
and let the FIRST leaf of the right child have subscript R. Write the
last leaf's overall scale inside the left child as b_scale>0. Its
endpoint and penultimate residual are isometric copies of

 b_scale W_L, b_scale y2_L,
 y2_L=c_L V_L+W_L.

The receiving energy is e_rec=b_scale^2 e_L>0. Direct projection onto
the W_L axis gives

 <W_L,y2_L>/e_L=sigma_L,
 ||(y2_L)_perp W_L||=c_L epsilon_L sqrt(eta_L/N_L).

Within the right child, the FIRST bridge joins its first two leaves.
If its excess is r_first and the second leaf's mass is A_second, the
source identity p_second=m_second U_second+a_second V_second+W_second
and the bridge alignment give

 m_second G4+a_second G6+G7=-r_first W_R.

Here W_R is embedded from the right child's first leaf, and G4,G6,G7
are its actual retained gradients, including all intervening scales.
Dividing by A_second produces a convex combination v_R of these three
gradients, because m_second+a_second+1=A_second. Thus

                 v_R=-tau W_R,
                 tau=r_first/A_second>0.             (17)

This vector identity is retained by EVERY subsequent left embedding,
regardless of earlier transverse choices. The initial vector of the
whole right child is the same isometric copy of p_R from its first leaf.

Apply the proposed parent alignment(3). The component of the weighted
new right gradient along the left endpoint gives exactly

        >= r tau [sigma_L d_R-u_L t_perp,R]-1.         (18)

dimension and all earlier maps. It has not optimized a reduced Gram

For a node containing N_node leaves, the three rows in(18) have actual

Q_(2N_node+7,2N_node-2), with the positive weights in(17).

At a balanced parent of depth at least5, the factor r tau has the
uniform bound

                            r tau>169/5.              (19)

First, the mass ratio q=A_first/A_second of any two leaves is greater
than999/1000, using5.8297<A<5.83. Substitution of r_first=tau A_second

Next, the positive root r in(2) is increasing in either mass: it lies

        =13552911/400000>169/5,

## 6. Each middle pair costs at least a fixed product factor

We claim that every legal node of depth at least5 must satisfy

                       kappa_L kappa_R<P_pair=189/200, (20)

where these are the two LEAF ratios in Section5, not the child ratios.

Suppose instead kappa_L kappa_R>=189/200. Since each ratio is below
M_bar, each exceeds(189/200)/M_bar=945/1004>47/50. Put
delta_L=M_bar-kappa_L and delta_R=M_bar-kappa_R. The arithmetic-geometric
mean inequality gives

 delta_L+delta_R<=2M_bar-2sqrt(189/200)<8/125,

because(243/250)^2<189/200. Thus(14)-(16) apply to both leaves.
Set D_bound=.071-delta_R/5>0. Equations(14)-(16) imply

 sigma_L d_R-u_L t_perp,R
 >=D_bound[1-(4/5)delta_L+(4/5)u_L^2]-(81/500)u_L.

For0<=u_L<=sqrt(delta_L), the right side is decreasing in u_L.

D_bound<=.071 and u_L<sqrt(.064)<.255. Therefore

 sigma_L d_R-u_L t_perp,R
             >=.071-delta_R/5-(81/500)sqrt(delta_L).

For delta_L+delta_R<=8/125, the largest possible subtracted expression
is(81/500)sqrt(8/125). Indeed the derivative of
(8/125-delta_L)/5+(81/500)sqrt(delta_L) is positive throughout
0<delta_L<=8/125. Since sqrt(8/125)<51/200, it follows that

 sigma_L d_R-u_L t_perp,R
         >71/1000-(81/500)(51/200)=2969/100000.         (21)

 sum weights Q/e_rec
        >(169/5)(2969/100000)-1=1761/500000>0.

This contradicts legality and proves(20). No numerical infeasibility
flag or assumption about an optimal transverse map enters this argument.

## 7. Disjoint pairs and the exact normalization product

At each internal node, the endpoint norm is
||w_parent||^2=r^2||w_L||^2||w_R||^2/R_R^2, by(3). Its true initial
distance is R_L, by Section2. Since A_parent r=A_L A_R, one obtains
directly

                kappa_parent=kappa_child,L kappa_child,R.

Inducting gives kappa_root=product_(all leaves)kappa_leaf. If an
endpoint vanishes, this product and all subsequent endpoint energies
are zero and(4) is immediate. Thus the positive-scale argument above
loses no zero case relevant to the bound.

Number the N=2^J leaves from1 toN in chronological order. A midpoint
pair belonging to a node of depth at least5 is exactly a pair

                 (16k,16k+1), 1<=k<N/16.

To check this bijection, write a split position as2^(d-1)(2s+1): its
2-adic valuation is d-1. Thus d>=5 is equivalent to divisibility by16.
All these pairs are disjoint. Their number is M_pairs=N/16-1.
Each pair has product below P_pair by(20), and each remaining leaf has
kappa<M_bar. Hence

 kappa_root<=P_pair^M_pairs M_bar^(N-2M_pairs)
            =M_bar^16(P_pair M_bar^14)^M_pairs.        (22)

For completeness, M_bar^14<529/500 follows by setting x=1/250 and
bounding the binomial coefficients from their quadratic term onwards.
The ratio of each next term to its predecessor is at most4x for these
terms, so

 (1+x)^14<=1+14x+91x^2/(1-4x)
          =1+7/125+91/61500<529/500.

Therefore P_pair M_bar^14<(189/200)(529/500)=99981/100000.
Equation(22) proves(4). This is stronger than merely locating one
low-energy leaf inside each disjoint subtree: the actual pair costs
at ALL large split positions are charged without double counting.

## 8. The original final objective and exact B comparison

The final residual is0, so F(x_n)=||w_root||^2/2. The positive-cone
argument proves the true distance R_root, yielding(5) without a tail,
extra coordinate or boundary reset. There are exactly3N+(N-1)=4N-1
steps. By the mass monotonicity already proved,

 A_root>lambda^J(233/40).

Let p_exp=log_2(3). Accepted factb98bb807d514e80d gives the bound for
the EXACT original dominant recurrence B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1:

                  B_n<=1+4n^p_exp<1+36N^p_exp.

Consequently the actual full-word witness ratio obeys

 B_(4N-1) * 2F(x_(4N-1))/R_root^2
 <= [(1+36N^p_exp) M_bar^16 eta_tree^(N/16-1)]
       /[(233/40)^2 lambda^(2J)] ->0.                 (23)

The bound is uniform over all choices made at this horizon, including
nonidentical leaves and every transverse map. It does not require a
single atom or a single function to serve multiple horizons. For each
chosen run, however, all samples are realized by the ONE function(6).

No objective-tail lemma is used. Appending a different final tail or
altering inherited values is a different construction whose original
rows and distance require separate analysis. Equation(23) bounds the
payoff of these specified witnesses, never the supremum W_n(h).

## 9. Scope test: a different atom iterates with growing energy

It is false that every isometrically retained source-matched projection
tree must have vanishing core energy. Take the single global quadratic
F(x)=x^2/2 on R, x_0=1, and the atom h0=(2,0,0). Every sample has
g_i=x_i, y_i=0, f_i=x_i^2/2. Its endpoint is-1 and its mass is A0=3.
All original Q rows equal0, including the optimum. If desired, it is
also realized by(6), taking the finite convex hull of the gradients of
the final chosen trajectory; all sample points belong to this interval.

Define h_(j+1)=(h_j,1+r_j,h_j), A_j=3lambda^j,
r_j=theta A_j. The gradient-descent endpoint w_j from initial1 obeys

 w_0=-1, w_(j+1)=-r_j w_j^2.

The first equality is the literal atom. The second follows because the
left copy multiplies the initial point by w_j, the bridge by-r_j, and
the right copy again by w_j. Thus every child is an actual scaled
isometric copy on the SAME quadratic and the bridge obeys(2)-(3).
The true initial distance remains1. Its energy satisfies

 kappa_0=9, kappa_(j+1)=kappa_j^2,
                       kappa_j=9^(2^j).

This example violates any proposed extension of(4) to unrestricted
atomic projection trajectories. It does not violate the stated result:
its word, mass, and zero receiving residuals fall outside Section1.
It also supplies no improved schedule or uniform minimax converse.

## 10. A general boundary condition for a changed atom

For any proposed join of projection jets with the value structure(7),
let p_R be the right initial vector, R_R its
norm, and w_L the nonzero left endpoint. For any left receiving residual
y with positive energy e_rec=<g,y>, decompose y along w_L:

 a_axis=<y,w_L>/||w_L||,
 b_perp=||y-a_axis w_L/||w_L||||.

For EVERY convex combination v of retained right gradients, write
v_perp=v-(<v,p_R>/R_R^2)p_R. Alignment(3) and Cauchy--Schwarz give the
necessary original-row condition

 alpha[-a_axis <p_R,v>/R_R-b_perp||v_perp||]<=e_rec,
                  alpha=r||w_L||/R_R.                (24)

Taking the supremum of the left side over the actual retained convex
hull gives the strongest bound furnished by this single-row Cauchy
argument. This is still a necessary condition, not simultaneous
sufficiency for all receiving rows and the full transverse contraction.

The present proof uses the retained source combination(17) in(24),
then prices the leaf's transverse allowance by(11). A successful new
atom must change this quantitative relationship, the retained source
geometry, the source-matched join rule, or the value/residual structure.
The quadratic example avoids the receiving obstruction because every
y is zero. It illustrates an escape in geometry, while leaving the
original all-schedule objective-profile problem unresolved.

## Provenance and glossary

The fact ids1252b8823bb5a290 andb98bb807d514e80d are the only verified
predecessors used. The motivating shared drafts3a81e23df4b047fe and
c21e4e49db154b0c were NOT assumed to be facts. Equations(1)-(24) form one
self-contained unverified candidate argument and may not be cited as
accepted downstream until selected verification accepts it.

All atomic symbols are defined in Sections1-4. J is balanced tree depth,
N=2^J is the leaf count, and n=4N-1 is the actual number of gradient
steps. M_pairs is the number of disjoint large-split midpoint pairs.
The projection body K_body differs from the scalar Klen=a+rho. The
letter M is a leaf-dependent exact envelope; M_bar is its fixed rational
upper bound. The letter d is an atomic normalized inner product, not
ambient dimension. The coordinate u in(9) is a scalar, not a gradient.
The symbol beta in Section4 is an affine-support coefficient, not a
geometric scale; b_scale denotes the geometric scale in Section5.

evidence:
# Full four-step seed: a compact domain from legal cut functions

Status: complete joint proof DRAFT, not verifier-accepted. This round has no
numerical or fact_submit allowance. No unverified finding is used as a premise.
The accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the interpolation convention Q<=0;
the particular functions and all algebra below are derived explicitly.

## 1. Interface and energy

Let h=(h_0,h_1,h_2,h_3)>=0, s=sum h_i, C=1+s>=193/25.
Indices i,j range over0,...,4. Set p_i=1+sum_(t<i)h_t, so p_0=1,p_4=C.
Let e=(1,1,1,1,1)^T. Define T_ii=1,T_it=h_t for t<i,T_it=0 for t>i,
Lambda_ii=0,Lambda_ij>=0,L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda,
omega=(-2h_0,-2h_1,-2h_2,-2h_3,2s)^T, and
D=diag(h_0(2-h_0),...,h_3(2-h_3),-s(s+2)).
The full interface is

    L^T e=omega, M=D+(LT+T^T L^T)/2 >=0.                 (1)

No multiplier support, rank, remainder, symmetry, or step order is fixed.
For arbitrary formal GD data x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i, define

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V=2sum_(i<4)h_i(f_i-f_4)+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
      -s(s+1)||g_4||^2.

Put delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2 and y_i=x_i-g_i=x_0-(Tg)_i.
Then Q_ij=delta_i-delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>, while
V=-omega^T delta+sum_i D_ii||g_i||^2. Value flow in(1) therefore gives

    V+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij = sum_(i,j)M_ij<g_i,g_j>. (2)

In particular every feasible full certificate implies V>=0 on every legal
convex differentiable1-smooth trajectory with a minimizer. This direction
requires neither certificate necessity nor any duality assertion.

## 2. Legal cut witnesses at every position

Fix j<4, put b=h_j,P=sum_(i<j)h_i,R=sum_(i>j)h_i, and first assume b>1.
Set a=(b-1)/(R+1)>0. Define the scalar function

    f(x)=x-1/2                     if x>=1,
         x^2/2                     if -a<=x<=1,
         -a*x-a^2/2                if x<=-a.

Its derivative is clamp(x,[-a,1]), which is continuous, nondecreasing,
and1-Lipschitz. The function is convex1-smooth and has a minimizer at0.
Start at x_0=P+1. Before and at j all gradients are1, and x_j=1.
After step j, x_(j+1)=1-b=-a(R+1). All subsequent gradients equal-a,
since the remaining nonnegative steps move monotonically to x_4=-a.
Every sampled value obeys f_i=x_i g_i-g_i^2/2, and x_4=g_4.

For any vector-valued data obeying these two identities, GD telescoping gives

    2sum_(i<4)h_i f_i+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
      =||x_0||^2-||x_4||^2,
    V=||x_0||^2-C^2||g_4||^2.                         (3)

Applied to this scalar function, nonnegative V implies

    C(h_j-1)_+ <= (1+P)(1+R), for every j=0,...,3.      (4)

If h_j<=1 the same inequality is automatic. Thus(4) holds on every
zero-step boundary too. Failure of any inequality is a specific legal
negative-V function, hence rules out the full interface(1).

## 3. Prefix bounds and compact capacity

For fixed C>1 define the increasing rational map

    R_C(z)=1+2Cz/(C+z), z>=0,
    r_k=R_C iterated k times at1, k=0,1,2,3.

Rearrangement of(4) gives p_(i+1)<=R_C(p_i). Conversely this inequality
is equivalent to(4) on the nonnegative schedule domain. Induction yields
p_i<=r_i. The cut constraints are invariant under reversing the four
steps, regardless of whether the original certificate admits reversal.
Applying the same induction to the reversed cut inequalities gives

    p_i >= C+1-r_(4-i).                               (5)

Only the cases i=1,2,3 are needed; r_0=1. Explicitly,

    r_1=(3C+1)/(C+1),
    r_2=(7C^2+6C+1)/(C^2+4C+1),
    r_3=(15C^3+23C^2+9C+1)/(C^3+11C^2+7C+1).          (6)

Taking i=2 in(5) and p_2<=r_2 gives C+1<=2r_2, hence

    C^3-9C^2-7C-1<=0.                                (7)

This polynomial is strictly increasing for C>=7: its derivative
3C^2-18C-7 is positive there and increasing. At C=39/4 its value is
131/64>0. Since C>=193/25>7, we conclude

    193/25 <= C < 39/4.                               (8)

In particular this argument covers all larger candidate sums; it did not
replace the target by the slice sum h=168/25.

## 4. All four steps are uniformly positive and bounded

The first and last cut inequalities give

    h_0,h_3 <= 2C/(C+1) < 78/43.                      (9)

For the lower bounds, subtract the upper prefix bound from the lower
bound for the next prefix in(5). This gives

    h_0,h_3 >= C-r_3 = N(C)/(C^3+11C^2+7C+1),
    h_1,h_2 >= C+1-r_1-r_2 = N(C)/((C+1)(C^2+4C+1)), (10)
    N(C)=C^4-4C^3-16C^2-8C-1.

## 1. Interface and energy

D=diag(h_0(2-h_0),...,h_3(2-h_3),-s(s+2)).
The full interface is

    L^T e=omega, M=D+(LT+T^T L^T)/2 >=0.                 (1)

No multiplier support, rank, remainder, symmetry, or step order is fixed.
For arbitrary formal GD data x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i, define

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V=2sum_(i<4)h_i(f_i-f_4)+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
      -s(s+1)||g_4||^2.

Put delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2 and y_i=x_i-g_i=x_0-(Tg)_i.
Then Q_ij=delta_i-delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>, while

    V+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij = sum_(i,j)M_ij<g_i,g_j>. (2)

In particular every feasible full certificate implies V>=0 on every legal
convex differentiable1-smooth trajectory with a minimizer. This direction
requires neither certificate necessity nor any duality assertion.

## 2. Legal cut witnesses at every position

Fix j<4, put b=h_j,P=sum_(i<j)h_i,R=sum_(i>j)h_i, and first assume b>1.
Set a=(b-1)/(R+1)>0. Define the scalar function

    f(x)=x-1/2                     if x>=1,
         x^2/2                     if -a<=x<=1,
         -a*x-a^2/2                if x<=-a.

Its derivative is clamp(x,[-a,1]), which is continuous, nondecreasing,
and1-Lipschitz. The function is convex1-smooth and has a minimizer at0.
Start at x_0=P+1. Before and at j all gradients are1, and x_j=1.
After step j, x_(j+1)=1-b=-a(R+1). All subsequent gradients equal-a,
since the remaining nonnegative steps move monotonically to x_4=-a.
Every sampled value obeys f_i=x_i g_i-g_i^2/2, and x_4=g_4.

For any vector-valued data obeying these two identities, GD telescoping gives

    2sum_(i<4)h_i f_i+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
      =||x_0||^2-||x_4||^2,

Applied to this scalar function, nonnegative V implies

    C(h_j-1)_+ <= (1+P)(1+R), for every j=0,...,3.      (4)

If h_j<=1 the same inequality is automatic. Thus(4) holds on every
zero-step boundary too. Failure of any inequality is a specific legal

For fixed C>1 define the increasing rational map

    R_C(z)=1+2Cz/(C+z), z>=0,

Rearrangement of(4) gives p_(i+1)<=R_C(p_i). Conversely this inequality

Applying the same induction to the reversed cut inequalities gives

    p_i >= C+1-r_(4-i).                               (5)

    r_1=(3C+1)/(C+1),

## 9. A sharper capacity cap from cut products and the actual quadratic

# Full four-step seed: a compact domain from legal cut functions

Status: complete joint proof DRAFT, not verifier-accepted. This round has no

The accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the interpolation convention Q<=0;

## 1. Interface and energy

Let h=(h_0,h_1,h_2,h_3)>=0, s=sum h_i, C=1+s>=193/25.
Indices i,j range over0,...,4. Set p_i=1+sum_(t<i)h_t, so p_0=1,p_4=C.
Let e=(1,1,1,1,1)^T. Define T_ii=1,T_it=h_t for t<i,T_it=0 for t>i,
Lambda_ii=0,Lambda_ij>=0,L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda,
omega=(-2h_0,-2h_1,-2h_2,-2h_3,2s)^T, and
D=diag(h_0(2-h_0),...,h_3(2-h_3),-s(s+2)).
The full interface is

    L^T e=omega, M=D+(LT+T^T L^T)/2 >=0.                 (1)

No multiplier support, rank, remainder, symmetry, or step order is fixed.
For arbitrary formal GD data x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i, define

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V=2sum_(i<4)h_i(f_i-f_4)+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
      -s(s+1)||g_4||^2.

Put delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2 and y_i=x_i-g_i=x_0-(Tg)_i.
Then Q_ij=delta_i-delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>, while
V=-omega^T delta+sum_i D_ii||g_i||^2. Value flow in(1) therefore gives

    V+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij = sum_(i,j)M_ij<g_i,g_j>. (2)

In particular every feasible full certificate implies V>=0 on every legal
convex differentiable1-smooth trajectory with a minimizer. This direction
requires neither certificate necessity nor any duality assertion.

## 2. Legal cut witnesses at every position

Fix j<4, put b=h_j,P=sum_(i<j)h_i,R=sum_(i>j)h_i, and first assume b>1.
Set a=(b-1)/(R+1)>0. Define the scalar function

    f(x)=x-1/2                     if x>=1,
         x^2/2                     if -a<=x<=1,
         -a*x-a^2/2                if x<=-a.

Its derivative is clamp(x,[-a,1]), which is continuous, nondecreasing,
and1-Lipschitz. The function is convex1-smooth and has a minimizer at0.
Start at x_0=P+1. Before and at j all gradients are1, and x_j=1.
After step j, x_(j+1)=1-b=-a(R+1). All subsequent gradients equal-a,
since the remaining nonnegative steps move monotonically to x_4=-a.
Every sampled value obeys f_i=x_i g_i-g_i^2/2, and x_4=g_4.

For any vector-valued data obeying these two identities, GD telescoping gives

    2sum_(i<4)h_i f_i+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
      =||x_0||^2-||x_4||^2,
    V=||x_0||^2-C^2||g_4||^2.                         (3)

Applied to this scalar function, nonnegative V implies

    C(h_j-1)_+ <= (1+P)(1+R), for every j=0,...,3.      (4)

If h_j<=1 the same inequality is automatic. Thus(4) holds on every
zero-step boundary too. Failure of any inequality is a specific legal
negative-V function, hence rules out the full interface(1).

## 3. Prefix bounds and compact capacity

For fixed C>1 define the increasing rational map

    R_C(z)=1+2Cz/(C+z), z>=0,
    r_k=R_C iterated k times at1, k=0,1,2,3.

Rearrangement of(4) gives p_(i+1)<=R_C(p_i). Conversely this inequality
is equivalent to(4) on the nonnegative schedule domain. Induction yields
p_i<=r_i. The cut constraints are invariant under reversing the four
steps, regardless of whether the original certificate admits reversal.
Applying the same induction to the reversed cut inequalities gives

    p_i >= C+1-r_(4-i).                               (5)

Only the cases i=1,2,3 are needed; r_0=1. Explicitly,

    r_1=(3C+1)/(C+1),
    r_2=(7C^2+6C+1)/(C^2+4C+1),
    r_3=(15C^3+23C^2+9C+1)/(C^3+11C^2+7C+1).          (6)

Taking i=2 in(5) and p_2<=r_2 gives C+1<=2r_2, hence

    C^3-9C^2-7C-1<=0.                                (7)

This polynomial is strictly increasing for C>=7: its derivative

131/64>0. Since C>=193/25>7, we conclude

replace the target by the slice sum h=168/25.

## 5. Full multiplier compactness from the common-gradient kernel

The vector p=Te has entries p_i. Since

    sum_i D_ii=-s^2-sum_(i<4)h_i^2,

# C82: exact elimination of the C81 witness parameters

Status: UNVERIFIED joint extension. For the complete construction and
proof, concatenate the C81 proof with this file. C81 is not an accepted
fact; its geometry is part of the joint proof, not an imported premise.
There are no new word proposals, optimizer calls or numerical replays.

Let h=(a,b,c,d), a,b,c>1,d>=0, and put

 alpha=a-1, B=b-1, C=c-1, D=d+1, A=1+a+b+c+d,
 H(u)=(u+1)(alpha u-1),
 ell=max{0,C d(D-BC)/D^2},
 R=[2-a+sqrt(a^2+4alpha ell)]/(2alpha),
 U=max{B,R}, K0=A^2(BC/D)^2.

Define three scalar coefficients

 q2=a^2+(1-B^2)alpha,
 q1=-2a+(1-B^2)(a-2),
 q0=B^2-K0,

and q(u)=q2 u^2+q1 u+q0.

## 1. Feasible parameter domain

The C81 triangle has parameters u>=B,z>0 with

 ell<=z^2<=H(u).

Since alpha>0, H has its only nonnegative root at1/alpha;
H'(u)=2alpha u+a-2>=a>0 for u>=1/alpha.
Solving H(u)=ell therefore gives R>=1/alpha exactly as above.
The closure of the admissible parameter domain is

 u>=U, ell<=z^2<=H(u).                                  (1)

Every boundary point in(1) with z=0 is a limit of points with
u>U,z>0 obeying the original normal inequalities. In particular
H(u)>ell for u>U. Taking such a limit in the explicit polynomial
energy is justified by continuity; no assertion about strict normals
at the limiting point is needed.

## 2. Closed formula for the infimum over this entire witness family

The energy is

 E(u,z)=(a u-1)^2+(1-B^2)z^2-K0.

If0<B<=1, its smallest value at fixed u uses z^2=ell.
Moreover a u-1>0 throughout u>=U>=1/alpha, so that value is
strictly increasing in u. Its infimum over the family is

 E_min=(a U-1)^2+(1-B^2)ell-K0.                         (2)

If B>1, its smallest value at fixed u uses z^2=H(u).
Expanding the resulting expression gives exactly q(u). Hence:

 * If q2<0, or q2=0 and q1<0, then E_min=-infinity.
 * If q2=0 and q1>=0, then E_min=q(U).
 * If q2>0, set u_opt=max{U,-q1/(2q2)}. Then
   E_min=q(u_opt).                                      (3)

These statements follow respectively from the leading term, from
linearity on the half-line, and from completing the square
q(u)=q2(u+q1/(2q2))^2+q0-q1^2/(4q2).

Every original full primitive certificate with a,b,c>1,d>=0
therefore must satisfy E_min>=0, with E_min defined by(2)--(3).
If E_min<0, an actual finite u and z>0 give a negative energy:
for an attained strict negative value this follows directly or by
continuity from a zero-z boundary; for E_min=-infinity take a
sufficiently large finite u. The C81 normals then give an actual
convex1-smooth function with a minimizer. This is a completely
parameter-eliminated necessary test for this particular family.

## 3. A broad monotone regime

Suppose1<a<=2 and1<b<=1+sqrt(3). If B<=1, formula(2)
already applies. If1<B<=sqrt(3), then

 q2>=a^2-2(a-1)=(a-1)^2+1>0,
 q'(1/alpha)=a[2/alpha+1-B^2]>=0,

because alpha<=1 and B^2<=3. Since q2>0, q' increases;
thus q is nondecreasing throughout u>=U>=1/alpha.
Consequently no stationary-point alternative is needed in this
regime: E_min=q(U) if B>1. If additionally R>=B, then H(U)=ell
and BOTH cases reduce to the same explicit radical inequality

 (a R-1)^2+(1-B^2)ell >= A^2(BC/D)^2.                    (4)

At B=1 it specializes to Section4 of C81. These are conditional
parameter statements. No unverified global-domain reduction is used
to claim that an arbitrary four-step seed lies in this regime.

## 4. Exact scope of the remaining gap

Eliminating the witnesses is not eliminating the original twenty
nonnegative multipliers. The displayed tests are necessary because
each negative case yields an actual trajectory; their nonnegative
cases certify only that this particular triangle family cannot reject
the schedule. No converse to the full flow/PSD interface is proved.
In particular failure to derive a contradiction from(2)--(4) does not
give a seed, and a negative saved optimization score does not give a
global impossibility theorem.

# C83: exact all-curvature repair at a cut

Status: complete joint UNVERIFIED analytical candidate. No new schedule,
optimizer/model evaluation, numerical replay, installation or verifier
call. This strengthens the shared unit-curvature cut/quad idea by using
every curvature kappa in(0,1], retaining its strictly negative original
interpolation residuals, and deriving the exact maximal repair weight.
The unit-curvature shared draft is motivation only; everything needed
is rederived here. Accepted facts used:1252b8823bb5a290 (interpolation)
and04219554e41d9750 Section10 (full primitive certificate identity).

## 1. Data and statement of the necessary condition

Let h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) be any finite nonnegative word, let
s=sum h_i,A=1+s, and select an index j with h_j>1. Define

 P=sum_(i<j)h_i, R=sum_(i>j)h_i, H=P+h_j=s-R,
 eta=(h_j-1)/(1+R)>0, C0=eta(1+eta),
 V0=(1+P)^2-A^2 eta^2.

For kappa in(0,1] let

 p_0=1, p_i=product_(t<i)(1-kappa h_t) for0<=i<=j+1,
 E=1+kappa R, q=kappa p_(j+1)/E,
 t_kappa=(1-kappa)/(2kappa).

If R>0 put

 beta=max{0, max_(0<=i<=j)
       [q(kappa p_i-q)-t_kappa(kappa p_i-q)^2/R]}.

If R=0 put beta=0. Finally define

 V_kappa=
   kappa sum_(i=0)^j h_i[1+kappa(1-h_i)]p_i^2
   -H[s+R+1+1/kappa]q^2.                               (1)

Every full primitive certificate for the ORIGINAL word necessarily
satisfies, for every such j and every0<kappa<=1,

             beta V0+C0 V_kappa >=0.                    (2)

For beta=0 the stronger explicit interpretation is V_kappa>=0,
which is equivalent to(2) because C0>0. No other step is assumed
positive, above1, symmetric, ordered or part of a primitive prefix.

## 2. The legal scalar cut coordinate

Use the scalar convex function with derivative clip(x,-eta,1),
minimum0 at0, and initial point1+P. Put
P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t and R_i=sum_(t>=i)h_t. Its actual data are

 x_i^0=1+P-P_i,    g_i^0=1,             i<=j,
 x_i^0=-eta(1+R_i), g_i^0=-eta,         i>j,
 f_i^0=x_i^0 g_i^0-(g_i^0)^2/2.

The selected step sends1 to1-h_j=-eta(1+R), and the remaining
updates keep the points on the negative constant-gradient segment,
ending at-eta. All zero steps retain their original sample indices.
This verifies the full GD chronology on one actual function.

For this coordinate the ordered residual is

 Q_ik^0=(g_i^0-g_k^0)(x_k^0-g_k^0).

It is0 inside either block. From the prefix to a suffix target k>j,
it is exactly-C0 R_k. In the opposite direction it is
-(1+eta)(P-P_k)<=0. All optimum comparisons are nonpositive.
The norm-telescoping identity, or direct substitution, gives its
primitive energy V0 exactly as defined above.

## 3. A quadratic prefix and constant-gradient suffix

Define a second set of scalar data, not yet claimed to be legal:

 x_i^1=p_i, g_i^1=kappa p_i, f_i^1=kappa p_i^2/2,       i<=j;
 x_i^1=q(1/kappa+R_i), g_i^1=q,
 f_i^1=q x_i^1-q^2/(2kappa),                           i>j.

The point after the selected step is p_(j+1)=q(1/kappa+R),
so these data follow every original GD update and end at q/kappa.
Include the optimum sample (x_star^1,g_star^1,f_star^1)=(0,0,0).

Write Q_ik^1=f_i^1-f_k^1+g_i^1(x_k^1-x_i^1)
                  +(g_i^1-g_k^1)^2/2.
Direct substitution gives the COMPLETE list of residual types:

 * i,k<=j:
   Q_ik^1=-t_kappa(g_i^1-g_k^1)^2<=0.
 * i,k>j: Q_ik^1=0.
 * i>j,k<=j:
   Q_ik^1=-t_kappa(q-kappa p_k)^2<=0.
 * i<=j,k>j:
   Q_ik^1=R_k q(kappa p_i-q)
                    -t_kappa(kappa p_i-q)^2.
 * Q_(i,star)^1=-t_kappa(g_i^1)^2<=0 for all i.
 * Q_(star,i)^1=-t_kappa(g_i^1)^2 for i<=j, and
   Q_(star,i)^1=-(R_i+t_kappa)q^2 for i>j.

Thus only the fourth type can be positive. If R_k=0 it is
nonpositive. For R_k>0, its quotient by R_k is

 q(kappa p_i-q)-t_kappa(kappa p_i-q)^2/R_k,

which is nondecreasing as R_k increases. Since0<R_k<=R,
its largest possible value is at k=j+1, whose R_k equals R.
This proves that beta is the exact largest nonnegative ratio of
a possibly bad residual to its corresponding suffix mass.

In particular beta=0 makes ALL auxiliary data, including optimum
comparisons, legal. If R=0 there are no positive suffix masses,
so the convention beta=0 has exactly this same meaning.

## 4. Orthogonal repair gives an actual globally legal function

If beta>0 choose epsilon=C0/beta and set

 X_i=(x_i^0,sqrt(epsilon)x_i^1),
 G_i=(g_i^0,sqrt(epsilon)g_i^1),
 F_i=f_i^0+epsilon f_i^1,

with the zero optimum sample. GD still uses the same full word.
Every original residual is Q_ik^0+epsilon Q_ik^1. All types except
prefix-to-suffix are sums of nonpositive numbers. For that type
with R_k>0 the sum is at most

       -C0 R_k+epsilon beta R_k=0;

when R_k=0 the auxiliary residual itself is nonpositive. Therefore
all directed comparisons, including the optimum and original terminal
sample, hold. A maximizing i in beta and k=j+1 show that epsilon
is also the largest permitted weight of this fixed auxiliary data
against this fixed base coordinate. No residual was discarded.

By accepted1252b8823bb5a290, proof paragraph2, these planar jets have
an everywhere finite convex differentiable1-smooth interpolant with
minimum value0 at0. Concretely, with I={star,0,...,n}, define

 c_i=<G_i,X_i>-F_i,
 J_i(v)=c_i+<X_i,v-G_i>+||v-G_i||^2/2,
 J(v)=max_(i in I) J_i(v),
 F(x)=sup_v{<x,v>-J(v)}.

The cited fact proves F(X_i)=F_i and grad F(X_i)=G_i from exactly
the residual convention just verified. Thus these are actual GD data
of one function, not a sum of separately illegal functions.

If beta=0, apply the same accepted interpolation construction directly
to the auxiliary scalar jets, since their full residual list is legal.
No division by beta occurs in this case.

## 5. Exact energy calculation

For the auxiliary suffix, f_i^1-f_n^1=q^2 R_i and
f_n^1=q^2/(2kappa). The elementary finite identity

 2sum_(i>j) h_i R_i = R^2+sum_(i>j)h_i^2

follows by expanding R^2. Thus the combined suffix contribution of
the weighted value differences and gradient diagonals is R(R+1)q^2.
The prefix contribution is

 kappa sum_(i<=j)h_i[1+kappa(1-h_i)]p_i^2-H q^2/kappa.

Subtracting the terminal s(s+1)q^2 gives(1), because
s(s+1)-R(R+1)=H(s+R+1).

The primitive energy is linear in all values and Gram entries.
The repaired planar trajectory therefore has energy

          V0+(C0/beta)V_kappa

when beta>0, and the legal auxiliary trajectory has energy V_kappa
when beta=0. Accepted04219554e41d9750, Section10, says an original
full nonnegative flow/PSD certificate forces nonnegative energy on
every actual trajectory. This proves(2), including beta=0.

## 6. The unit-curvature slice and exact low-degree polynomial interface

At kappa=1, q=p_(j+1)/(1+R)=-eta p_j, t_kappa=0, and

 beta=max{0,max_(i<=j)q(p_i-q)}, V_1=1-A^2 q^2.

For the last identity, the prefix sum in(1) telescopes to
1-p_(j+1)^2, using p_(i+1)^2=(1-h_i)^2 p_i^2. Then
(1+R)^2+H(s+R+2)=A^2. This rederives the unit-curvature
repair without treating the shared max2 draft as a correctness premise.

For R>0 the entire curvature interval can be expressed through
finitely many POLYNOMIAL branches. Define

 d_i(kappa)=[E p_i-p_(j+1)]/kappa,                     0<=i<=j,
 T_i(kappa)=2R p_(j+1)d_i-(1-kappa)d_i^2,
 T_max(kappa)=max{0,T_0(kappa),...,T_j(kappa)},

 P_cut(kappa)=E^2 sum_(i<=j)h_i[1+kappa(1-h_i)]p_i^2
              -H[1+kappa(s+R+1)]p_(j+1)^2.

The numerator defining d_i vanishes at kappa=0, so d_i is a
polynomial, including at0. It has degree at most j. Consequently
T_i has degree at most2j+1, and P_cut degree at most2j+3.
The exact identities are

 beta=kappa^3 T_max/(2R E^2),
 V_kappa=kappa P_cut/E^2.

Since kappa,R,E are positive, (2) is equivalent to

 kappa^2 V0 T_max(kappa)+2R C0 P_cut(kappa)>=0,
                                             0<kappa<=1. (3)

At each branch where0 or a specific T_i is the maximum, (3) is
a polynomial inequality of degree at most2j+3. For a four-step word,
the two middle cuts j=1,2 therefore require degrees at most5,7.
Their branch selection inequalities are the explicit comparisons
T_i>=0 and T_i>=T_k, with the zero branch selected when all T_i<=0.
This gives a precise exact real-algebraic interface for further work;
no polynomial-root search or numerical interval scan is performed.

## 7. Scope and remaining task

The construction gives legal adversaries whenever(2) fails. Passing
all these tests gives no full certificate; no sufficiency is claimed.
The convex combination mechanism retains every original interpolation
pair and all function-value offsets. A favorable or unfavorable outcome
on any finite list of curvatures would not settle the universal interval.

No new word was selected, tested, rounded, or evaluated in deriving this
family. It neither constructs the missing four-step seed nor excludes
every h with sum>=168/25. The accepted conditional lift remains available
as fact04219554e41d9750; the seed existence problem is still OPEN.

# C88: complete elimination of the curved partial-tail chronology

Status: a complete, self-contained analytical proof DRAFT, NOT a verified fact.
