The result below resolves the new family proposed in 657b4a00036ec84f. In
fact, it allows every lower clipping parameter that preserves its chronology,
not just the parameter that puts the third query at the lower ramp boundary.
The entire family adds NO constraint to the enlarged unit-curvature system.
This is a redundancy result for an explicitly specified family, not a
statement about all one-dimensional functions or the original seed cone.

## 1. Statement, canonical variables, and scope

Write the actual four steps as

    h=(u,v,w,z)=(1+a,1+b,1+c,1+d),
    H=u+v, R=w+z, s=H+R, C=1+s, P=u+1.

For this proof assume the following deliberately coarse open box:

    1<u,z<9/5, 1<v,w<5/2, C<9.                       (1)

This contains the canonical box specified in the complete evidence of
81720922d2d132d7 and used in 7cd0bb4a795ee1df:

    193/25<=C<87/10,
    0<a,d<77/97,
    0<b,c<1552559/1081453,
    C=5+a+b+c+d.                                     (2)

Indeed 77/97<4/5 and 1552559/1081453<3/2, by direct cross multiplication.
The proof here takes (1) as an explicit hypothesis; it does not promote the
unverified compact-domain derivation to a fact. Thus it applies, without
any dependency on that derivation, to every actual parameter in the joint
canonical region (2), whatever further constraints are imposed there.
In particular C is variable; it is never fixed to 193/25.

For reciprocal curvature t and lower clipping magnitude alpha, let

    1<=t<v, B=v-t>0,
    0<=alpha<=alpha_B(t):=B/(w+t),
    f_(t,alpha)(x)=x-t/2                   if x>=t,
                  x^2/(2t)               if -t*alpha<=x<=t,
                  -alpha*x-t*alpha^2/2   if x<=-t*alpha.
                                                               (3)

The formulas agree at both boundaries. Start actual gradient descent at
x0=u+t and use the original four steps h. The curvature on the middle
segment is k=1/t, strictly between 1/v and 1 inclusive. This is the whole
partial-tail chronology: the first two gradients are the upper cap, and
the next two are the lower cap. The terminal gradient may leave that cap.
At the endpoint alpha=alpha_B, its expression in curvature k is
(k*v-1)/(1+k*w), exactly the parameter in plan 657b4a00036ec84f.

Let V be the ORIGINAL primitive energy of this actual trajectory:
write f_i=f_(t,alpha)(x_i) and g_i=f'_(t,alpha)(x_i), for 0<=i<=4.

    V=2 sum_(i=0)^3 h_i(f_i-f4)
       +sum_(i=0)^3 h_i(1-h_i)g_i^2-s(s+1)g4^2.       (4)

Then the following are equivalent on (1):

    (i) V>=0 for every t and alpha in (3);

    (ii) C(v-1) <= (u+1)(1+w+z),
         C(v-1)(z-1) <= (u+1)(1+w).                  (5)

In canonical variables these are exactly

    C b <= (2+a)(3+c+d),
    C b d <= (2+a)(2+c).                             (6)

Both are already in the enlarged unit-curvature system. Thus adding ALL
the genuine curvatures and ALL the lower clips in this chronology leaves
that entire joint region unchanged. This statement is not just an
equivalent quantified reformulation: the two continuous parameters have
been removed, and (6) is an already present finite list.

No order between u,v,w,z is assumed. There is no cut saturation,
quadratic saturation, primitive-prefix assumption, symmetry, or fixed
capacity. In particular no claim of nonemptiness of the enlarged joint
region is made.

## 2. One static legal function and every interpolation pair

The derivative of (3) is clamp(x/t,[-alpha,1]). It is continuous,
nondecreasing, and 1/t-Lipschitz, hence f is convex, differentiable, and
1-smooth. For alpha>0 its unique minimizer is 0, with value 0. At alpha=0
its minimizer set is the negative half-line including 0, which is allowed.
The starting point x0=u+t is positive in either case. No jets from
different functions are combined.

The actual queries, gradients, and terminal coordinate are

    x0=u+t,       g0=1,
    x1=t,         g1=1,
    x2=-B,        g2=-alpha,
    x3=-B+w*alpha,g3=-alpha,
    x4=-B+R*alpha,
    g4=clamp(x4/t,[-alpha,1]).                        (7)

To justify both lower-cap claims, alpha<=B/(w+t) gives
B>=(w+t)alpha>=t alpha, so x2<=-t alpha. It also gives
x3=-B+w alpha<=-t alpha. Every displayed update is therefore exactly
x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_i for the single function (3).

At every sample, including a clipping boundary,

    f_i=x_i*g_i-t*g_i^2/2.                           (8)

For a direct audit of ALL interpolation pairs, put n_i=x_i-t*g_i.
If g_i is the upper endpoint 1, then n_i>=0; if it is the lower
endpoint -alpha, then n_i<=0; otherwise n_i=0. Thus, for any two
sample indices i,j,

    n_j*(g_i-g_j)<=0.

The original signed residual consequently satisfies

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+g_i*(x_j-x_i)+(g_i-g_j)^2/2
        =n_j*(g_i-g_j)-(t-1)*(g_i-g_j)^2/2<=0.        (9)

When alpha=0 the normal assertion still holds: the lower endpoint is 0

    omega=(-2u,-2v,-2w,-2z,2s)^T,
    D_prim=diag(u(2-u),v(2-v),w(2-w),z(2-z),-s(s+2)),

## 3. Exact energy, retaining the curvature deficit

Telescoping x_i^2-x_(i+1)^2=2h_i*x_i*g_i-h_i^2*g_i^2,
using (8), gives

    2sum_(i<4)h_i f_i+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)g_i^2
       =x0^2-x4^2-(t-1)sum_(i<4)h_i*g_i^2.

Substitute the actual f4 from (8) into (4), and complete the square:

    V=x0^2-(x4+s*g4)^2
       -(t-1)[sum_(i<4)h_i*g_i^2-s*g4^2].            (11)

The bracketed term cannot be discarded by pretending the values have
unit-curvature saturation. In (7), sum_(i<4)h_i*g_i^2=H+R*alpha^2.
Define

    E0(t)=(u+t)^2-(t-1)H,
    q(t)=1+s/t+s*C/t^2,
    D(t)=t^2+s*t+s*C=t^2*q(t).

Useful elementary identities are

    E0(1)=P^2,
    E0(t)=P^2+(t-1)(t+1+u-v),
    E0'(t)=2t+u-v>1/2 for 1<=t<=v,
    q(1)=C^2, q'(t)=-s/t^2-2s*C/t^3<0.             (12)

Thus E0(t)>=P^2>4, with strict increase for t>1.

## 4. Eliminate every terminal clipping branch and alpha

First the terminal upper cap is IMPOSSIBLE on the stated domain; it is
not suppressed as an assumption. As alpha increases, x4=-B+R alpha
increases. Its maximum is reached at alpha_B, where

    x4=alpha_B*(z-t).

If z<=t it is nonpositive. If z>t, then

    x4/t <= alpha_B*(z-1)
          <=[(v-1)/(w+1)]*(z-1)
          <(3/4)*(4/5)=3/5<1.                       (13)

Consequently no value of alpha in (3), at any curvature, can reach the
upper terminal cap or its boundary. For completeness, without this box

    V=E0(t)-(x4+s)^2-(t-1)R alpha^2+(t-1)s,

but its domain x4>=t has empty intersection with (3) under (1).

The lower/core terminal boundary is the positive number

    alpha_A(t)=B/(R+t),
    0<alpha_A<alpha_B,                               (14)

because R=w+z>w. On 0<=alpha<=alpha_A, x4<=-t alpha and
g4=-alpha. Formula (11) becomes

    V=E0(t)-(B+H alpha)^2+(t-1)H alpha^2
      =E0(t)-B^2-2BH alpha-H(H+1-t)alpha^2.          (15)

Since H+1-t=u+1+B>0 and B,H>0, (15) strictly decreases with alpha.
Its minimum on this whole branch is at alpha_A. At alpha=0 it is

    V=H*(u+1+t-v)>0,

because u+1+t-v>=u+2-v>1/2.

On alpha_A<=alpha<=alpha_B, the terminal gradient is x4/t and

    V=E0(t)-(t-1)R alpha^2-q(t)(R alpha-B)^2.         (16)

This is a concave quadratic in alpha, since q(t)>0 and R>0.
For any point of the interval the defining concavity inequality bounds
its value below by the linear interpolation of its endpoint values;
therefore its minimum is at one of the two endpoints. Formulas (15)
and (16) agree at alpha_A because g4=-alpha_A there. They also remain
valid at alpha_B, where x3=-t alpha_B is exactly the boundary between
the lower flat segment and the middle ramp.

We have now proved, without any division by an energy or a residual,
that at each fixed t the WHOLE clipping interval is nonnegative if
and only if both endpoint energies V_A(t), V_B(t) are nonnegative.

## 5. Eliminate curvature at the full-tail endpoint

At alpha=alpha_A, x4=-t alpha_A and g4=-alpha_A. Formula (11) gives

    V_A(t)=E0(t)-[(t+s)alpha_A]^2
                     +(t-1)H alpha_A^2.            (17)

The nonnegative quantity in square brackets is

    J(t)=(v-t)(t+s)/(R+t)
        =(v-t)*(1+H/(R+t)).

It decreases on [1,v], because

    J'(t)=-(1+H/(R+t))-H(v-t)/(R+t)^2<0.

Using (12) and the nonnegative last term in (17) yields

    V_A(t)>=V_A(1)
          =P^2-[C(v-1)/(R+1)]^2.                   (18)

The first inequality in (5) is therefore necessary and sufficient for
every full-tail endpoint curvature. For t>1, E0(t)>E0(1) shows strict
positivity whenever V_A(1)>=0. No small-curvature approximation is used.

## 6. Eliminate curvature at the partial-tail return endpoint

    x3=-t alpha(t), x4=(z-t)alpha(t),
    g4=(z-t)alpha(t)/t,
    V_B(t)=E0(t)-(t-1)R alpha(t)^2
                    -q(t)alpha(t)^2(z-t)^2.         (19)

Thus necessity of the second inequality in (5) follows by an actual
unit-curvature member, not by a limiting construction.

For sufficiency suppose V_B(1)>=0. We must keep BOTH signs of z-t.

### 6a. Return to the positive ray: 1<=t<=z

Put d=z-1 in (0,4/5) and r=t-1 in [0,d], also retaining t<v.
The ratio alpha(t) decreases with t and q(t)<=q(1)=C^2. Therefore

    q(t)alpha(t)^2(z-t)^2
       <=[P^2-V_B(1)]*(d-r)^2/d^2.

Using the exact E0 in (12), (19) consequently gives

    V_B(t)>=V_B(1)*(d-r)^2/d^2
       +r*[2+u-v+r+P^2*(2/d-r/d^2)-R alpha(t)^2].   (21)

The bracket is uniformly positive over the entire box (1). Explicitly,

    2+u-v+r>1/2,
    P^2*(2/d-r/d^2)>=P^2/d>5,
    R alpha(t)^2<(9/2)*(3/4)^2=81/32.

The first estimate uses u>1,v<5/2. The second uses r<=d,
P>2,d<4/5. The third uses R=w+z<9/2 and
alpha(t)<=alpha(1)<3/4. Hence the bracket exceeds 95/32. In particular,

    V_B(t)>=V_B(1)*((z-t)/(z-1))^2
                        +(95/32)*(t-1),            (22)

with strict inequality in the added estimate when t>1. It follows
that every t in this branch has nonnegative energy, strictly positive
when t>1. This includes t=z if that endpoint lies below v.

### 6b. Terminal point on the negative ray: z<=t<v

This branch has a direct positive margin, independent of (20).
Put r=t-1. Then 0<=r<v-1<3/2, and

         <=r*(3/2-r)/[(1+r)(2+r)]<1/6.             (23)

cross multiplication:

       =7r^2-6r+2=7(r-3/7)^2+5/7>0.

Every schedule in the enlarged canonical necessary system already

evidence:
# C90: signed correlations in orthogonal components

Status: **complete joint draft, UNVERIFIED**. This is completed round22,
after baseline21, within ceiling23 (the historical interruption is counted
separately). No numerical evaluation, scan, replay, solver, installation,
subagent, or verifier call was used. Correctness predecessors are accepted
`1252b8823bb5a290`, `0e7e78056dc6258c`, and `b98bb807d514e80d`.
Earlier unverified character manuscripts are motivation only. All new
arguments used here are proved together below.

The original arbitrary-schedule exact-profile question remains open.

## 1. The general signed statement

Let F be a convex differentiable function on a finite-dimensional Euclidean
space, with 1-Lipschitz gradient and a minimizer. Run actual GD with a
finite nonnegative schedule h of length n>=1. Write X_i for its positions,
g_i=grad F(X_i), f_i=F(X_i)-min F, and

    X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i g_i, R=dist(X_0,argmin F).

Suppose the nonzero QUERIED gradients g_0,...,g_(n-1) belong to M mutually
orthogonal subspaces V_1,...,V_M, each of which is used at least once.
The gradients within a subspace can have arbitrary signed correlations,
arbitrary norms, and arbitrary linear dependencies. No condition is imposed
on the unqueried terminal gradient. A run is a maximal consecutive interval
of queried indices having the same subspace label. Let r be the first index
of the final run, and set

    A_tail=product_(t=r)^(n-1) max{1,(h_t-1)^2}.

The candidate conclusion is

    2 f_n/R^2 <= A_tail beta_(M-1),                     (1)
    c_0=0, c_(j+1)=c_j+2+2sqrt(c_j+1),
    beta_j=4/(1+sqrt(1+2c_j))^2.

If any queried gradient is zero, the trajectory remains at that minimizer
and the terminal gap is zero. Thus excluding zero gradients loses no
positive payoff. In the nonzero case R>0.

The important difference from C89 is that (1) does NOT assume nonnegative
correlations with earlier gradients. Those terms remain signed; the proof
chooses intervals on which they vanish by orthogonality of whole subspaces.

## 2. First occurrences: every skipped term is retained

Translate a closest minimizer to zero. Such a minimizer exists because its
set is nonempty and closed, and a bounded distance-minimizing sequence has
a convergent subsequence. Accepted `1252b8823bb5a290` gives every original
ordered inequality

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0.       (2)

List the first occurrence of each subspace, in chronological order, as
j_0<...<j_(M-1). Put v_a=g_(j_a), q_a=||v_a||^2, and p_a=f_(j_a).
The vectors v_a are pairwise orthogonal. Moreover

    <v_a,g_t>=0 for EVERY t<j_a,                       (3)

because none of those earlier gradients belongs to its subspace.
There are no compressed GD steps in this argument. Applying the original
Q_(j_(a+1),j_a) gives exactly

    p_a >= p_(a+1)+(q_a+q_(a+1))/2
              +sum_(t=j_a)^(j_(a+1)-1)h_t<v_(a+1),g_t>
        = p_(a+1)+(q_a+q_(a+1))/2.                    (4)

The original optimum row, retaining its past displacement, gives

    <X_0,v_a> >= p_a+q_a/2
                       +sum_(t<j_a)h_t<v_a,g_t>
                 =p_a+q_a/2.                         (5)

Also p_(M-1)>=q_(M-1)/2. Define
b=p_(M-1)-q_(M-1)/2>=0 and T_a=b+sum_(s=a)^(M-1)q_s.
Equations (4)-(5) imply <X_0,v_a>>=T_a>0. Expanding the squared norm
after subtracting the orthogonal projections onto v_a yields

    R^2>=sum_a T_a^2/q_a.                              (6)

For completeness, the scalar elimination in accepted
`0e7e78056dc6258c` applies as follows. Inductively
sum_(a<k)T_a^2/q_a>=c_k T_k. Adding the next term and using
T_k=q_k+T_(k+1) reduces this to

    (c_k+1)q_k+(c_k+2)T_(k+1)+T_(k+1)^2/q_k
       >=[c_k+2+2sqrt(c_k+1)]T_(k+1),

which is the nonnegativity of a square. With c=c_(M-1),
z=T_(M-1)/q_(M-1)>=1 and u=(1+sqrt(1+2c))/2, we get
R^2>=q_(M-1)z(z+c), 2p_(M-1)=q_(M-1)(2z-1), and

    z(z+c)-u^2(2z-1)=(z-u)^2>=0.

Therefore 2p_(M-1)/R^2<=beta_(M-1). The same proof includes M=1.
Induction gives c_k>=k^2 and hence beta_k<=2/k^2 for k>=1.

## 3. Run starts cannot transmit an increase to another subspace

Consider consecutive run starts u<v. All gradients g_t for u<=t<v
belong to the old subspace; g_v belongs to a different, orthogonal one.
The actual original pair Q_(v,u) therefore says

    f_u>=f_v+||g_u-g_v||^2/2
                         +sum_(t=u)^(v-1)h_t<g_v,g_t>
        =f_v+(||g_u||^2+||g_v||^2)/2.                  (7)

This identity keeps every physical step of the old run. In particular,
even a large increase INSIDE that run cannot be passed to the next run
start. A first occurrence is a run start. Applying (7) successively after
the last first occurrence proves f_r<=p_(M-1).

For any actual step of a 1-smooth convex function, the segment smoothness
bound and ||g||^2<=2f give

    f(X-hg)<=max{1,(h-1)^2}f(X), h>=0.                 (8)

For h<=2 this is descent. For h>2, use
f(X-hg)<=f(X)+h(h-2)||g||^2/2<=(h-1)^2f(X).
Apply (8) to the complete physical suffix beginning at r. This proves (1).
No sign assumption has been made within any V_a.

## 4. Consequence for arbitrary signed finite-support character kernels

Fix m>=4, N=2^m, n=N-1, and retain the original enclosing parameters

    sigma=1+sqrt(2), delta=1-1/m,
    c_chr=sigma(1+1/m), a_chr=delta/c_chr,
    h_i=1+a_chr*c_chr^(nu_2(i+1)), 0<=i<n.             (9)

Here nu_2 is the exponent of 2 dividing a positive integer. These are
exactly H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_chr*c_chr^j,H_j), with the SAME enclosing
m in every child. The last physical step is 1+a_chr<2.

Let w_s be any nonnegative probability law on s in {0,1}^m, and define
chi_s(i)=(-1)^(sum_l s_l i_l), k(d)=sum_s w_s chi_s(d). Suppose k(d)=0
outside a binary subgroup H of cardinality K. Prescribe queried gradients

    g_i=(Gamma_i sqrt(w_s)chi_s(i))_s, Gamma_i>0.

Then <g_i,g_j>=Gamma_i Gamma_j k(i XOR j). Different H-cosets span
orthogonal subspaces; all within-coset correlations may be negative.
If K>=2, deleting the one unqueried label N-1 leaves all M=N/K cosets
represented. Each coset has at most K queried labels, so the final run
contains at most K physical steps.

For that final suffix, write its indices as N-1-j with 1<=j<=q<=K.
Then nu_2(N-j)=nu_2(j). Levels zero and one have offsets a_chr<1 and
delta<1. For a level k>=2 the offset delta*c_chr^(k-1) is at most
c_chr^(k-1). Consequently

    A_tail <= c_chr^(2 sum_(j=1)^K (nu_2(j)-1)_+)
           = c_chr^(2 sum_(k>=2) floor(K/2^k))
           <= c_chr^K <= [5sigma/4]^K.                (10)

The displayed sum is finite and the middle identity just counts, for each
j, how many powers 2^k with k>=2 divide it. It is NOT an enumeration or a
numerical computation. If M>=2, (1) yields

    2f_n/R^2 <= [5sigma/4]^K beta_(N/K-1)
              <=8[5sigma/4]^K K^2/N^2.               (11)

For K=1 every queried gradient is orthogonal to every other, so M=n,
the final run is one step, and (1) applies directly with beta_(n-1).

Thus every fixed-size correlation subgroup fails to supply a nonvanishing
original-B payoff on (9), regardless of where its binary generators lie,
of any signs in its kernel, of its amplitudes, or of its terminal extension.
Indeed accepted `b98bb807d514e80d` gives
B_n<=1+4n^p, p=log_2(3)<2, so multiplying (11) by B_n tends to zero.
This also covers high-bit subgroups: moving a fixed support to a high
bridge is not an escape. The proof prices the actual FINAL run, rather
than bounding the entire interval after the last first occurrence.

More generally (1) holds without characters whenever the queried
gradients split into orthogonal subspaces with a controlled final run.
It does not exclude a dense correlation graph, growing components whose
actual suffix cost defeats (11), or geometries with correlations between
the proposed components.

## 5. A different full-support law with genuine negative history

For m>=4 define the real signs B=(-1)^s_0, C=(-1)^s_1, D=(-1)^s_2 and

    w_s=N^-1[1-B/2-CD/3+BCD/4].                        (12)

For (B,CD)=(+,+),(+,-),(-,+),(-,-), the density factors in brackets are
5/12,7/12,11/12,25/12. Each occurs equally often, their average is one,
and every atom is positive. The only nonzero nonconstant moments are

    k(1)=-1/2, k(6)=-1/3, k(7)=1/4.                   (13)

All other moments vanish by pairing a free character bit. Thus H={0,1,6,7}.
The moments do not form a product law in any linear sign basis on H:
none of -1/2,-1/3,1/4 equals the product of the other two. For example
1/4-(-1/2)(-1/3)=1/12. This is a different law from C89.

Its negative history is explicit. Every original leaf has correlation
-1/2; at the first level-two bridge the triple at indices 2,3,4 has
correlations -1/2,-1/3,+1/4 for pairs 23,24,34. A largest-representative
selection of the kind used in C89 has negative correlations with skipped
earlier members of its own coset. In particular the last queried gradient
g_(N-2) has correlation -1/3 with g_(N-8). C89's nonnegative-history
hypothesis fails; those negative terms cannot be discarded.

In every eight-label slab the coset labels occur as A,A,B,B,B,B,A,A.
The missing terminal label removes the last A of the last slab. Hence the
final queried run contains only index N-2. Its last physical step is less
than two, so A_tail=1. Applying the complete argument above gives

    V_sig=2f_n/R^2<=beta_(N/4-1)<=128/N^2,
    0<=B_n V_sig<=128(1+4n^p)/(n+1)^2 ->0.             (14)

This is uniform over all positive queried amplitudes, anchors, values,
functions, and free terminal gradients realizing this law.

## 6. Actual nonemptiness, all original pairs, and the true radius

The following explicit construction applies to (12), including a
prescribed terminal gradient, on the complete physical word (9).
In fact its pair checks work for any finite schedule with every h_i>1.
Define

    H_max=max_(i<n)h_i,
    kappa=min{1, min_(i<n)(h_i-1)/4},
    eta=kappa/[16(H_max+kappa+1)],
    Gamma_i=eta^i, f_i=(kappa+1/2)Gamma_i^2, 0<=i<=n,
    K_ij=<g_i,g_j>.

Use (12) and the character gradients for ALL labels 0,...,n. Set

    b_i=(2kappa+1)Gamma_i^2+sum_(t<i)h_t K_ti,
    (X_0)_s=[1/(N sqrt(w_s))]
                    sum_(i=0)^n(b_i/Gamma_i)chi_s(i),
    X_i=X_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t.                          (15)

The elementary character identity sum_s chi_s(i)chi_s(j)=N 1_(i=j)
follows by pairing a differing bit. Thus
<X_0,g_i>=b_i and <X_i,g_i>=(2kappa+1)Gamma_i^2.

For EVERY original pair i<j, direct substitution gives

    Q_ij=(kappa+1-h_i)Gamma_i^2-kappa Gamma_j^2
                        -sum_(i<t<j)h_t K_it-K_ij,
    Q_ji=(kappa+1)Gamma_j^2-kappa Gamma_i^2
                        +(h_i-1)K_ij+sum_(i<t<j)h_t K_jt. (16)

No signed term has been removed from these identities. For estimates use
|K_it|<=Gamma_i Gamma_t, which follows from the explicit unit character
directions and the nonnegative probability weights. Since eta<1/2 and
h_i>=1+4kappa, the first line divided by Gamma_i^2 is at most

    -3kappa+H_max eta/(1-eta)+eta
       <=-3kappa+2(H_max+1)eta <=-23kappa/8<0.

Writing d=j-i>=1, the second line divided by Gamma_i^2 is at most

    -kappa+(kappa+1)eta^2+H_max eta/(1-eta)
       <=-kappa+2(H_max+kappa+1)eta=-7kappa/8<0.

The original optimum rows are exactly

    Q_(i,star)=Q_(star,i)=-kappa Gamma_i^2<0.           (17)

In particular the smallest actual nonempty block, the first leaf
h_0=1+a_chr, has

    Q_01=kappa-a_chr-kappa eta^2+eta/2<0,
    Q_10=(kappa+1)eta^2-kappa-a_chr eta/2<0.            (18)

These are its genuine negative correlation terms, not a positive-history
surrogate. Equations (16)-(17) simultaneously check every later block,
both orientations of every remote pair, and all terminal pairs.

Here is ONE function fixed for the entire run. Put

    y_i=X_i-g_i, delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2=kappa Gamma_i^2,
    H(v)=||v||^2/2+max{0,max_(0<=i<=n)(<y_i,v>-delta_i)},
    F_sig(X)=sup_v(<X,v>-H(v)).                        (19)

The constructive interpolation proof in accepted `1252b8823bb5a290`,
applied to this whole finite jet set, proves that F_sig is everywhere
finite, convex, differentiable, and 1-smooth, and has exactly all the
positions, gradients, and values (15)-(17). Its maximizer is unique
because H is 1-strongly convex. Thus the same F_sig realizes the original
GD recurrence for every physical step, without resets or padding.

Every delta_i is strictly positive. Consequently H(v)=||v||^2/2 in a
neighborhood of zero. Also H>=||v||^2/2, so F_sig(0)=0. For X!=0, choose
v=tX in that neighborhood with 0<t<1; then
F_sig(X)>=(t-t^2/2)||X||^2>0. Hence argmin F_sig={0}.
The TRUE radius is therefore exactly

    R^2=||X_0||^2
       =N^-2 sum_s w_s^-1
                       [sum_i(b_i/Gamma_i)chi_s(i)]^2. (20)

It is finite and at least one, since ||g_0||=1 and the gradient is
1-Lipschitz relative to its unique minimizer. The positive actual payoff is

    2F_sig(X_n)/R^2=(2kappa+1)eta^(2n)/R^2.            (21)

This construction proves nonemptiness and makes its radius cost explicit;
it is not claimed to be a competitive amplitude choice. Bound (14) applies
to every other legal amplitude choice as well.

## 7. Scope, literature, and remaining direction

The selected route was screened by direct proving. Equations (3)-(7) close
the signed component obstruction; (15)-(21) close full interpolation and
normalization of an actual signed law. The attempted positive normalized
payoff for a fixed-size component law is therefore excluded at joint-draft
level. This is not a verifier verdict.

Matlas was queried for negatively correlated GD block constructions and
strict finite interpolation; its hits did not supply the missing result.
An early web search recovered the finite interpolation literature. The
exact local text of Taylor--Hendrickx--Glineur, arXiv:1502.05666,
Section2.5, Theorem4, its proof, construction, Corollary1 and Remark3 was
read. The needed interpolation result is already proved in accepted
1252b8823bb5a290, so no external theorem is imported as a premise.

An actual uncovered freedom is a DENSE signed correlation geometry whose
query graph has one large component. Neither a different fixed-size
subgroup, higher-order dependence within it, nor moving it to high bits
escapes (11). A promising concrete next test is to strictify a known scalar
signed trajectory and add a small full-support orthogonal perturbation.
Its common function and radius must be built jointly: a covariance matrix
alone does not provide either. Such a lift would calibrate the dense law;
it would not automatically improve the known scalar payoff or supply the
uniform arbitrary-h target.

evidence:
# Full primitive reversal for short blocks and saturated middle cuts

Status: complete joint proof DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. This is max2's first new
analytical round under TASK.md and master_guidance 8211d6128deabdf3
(completed baseline20, ceiling22). No numerical evaluation, solver, fixed
replay, verifier, installation, or subordinate agent is used.

Accepted input: fact04219554e41d9750, Sections10--11, supplies the exact
full primitive interface and the full saturated primitive join identity.
Fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the smooth-convex interpolation convention.
All additional algebra used below is proved here. Earlier shared drafts
4a064f93111ac5a2, f3d96c901566e96b, and f7cee3034df8cb7f motivated the
inversion, repair, and cut arguments; none is used as a verified lemma.

## 1. Statements and scope

For a finite nonnegative word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), put s=sum h_i and
C=1+s. On formal GD data x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i define

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                              -sC||g_n||^2.

A full ordinary primitive certificate is an array lambda_ij>=0 on ALL
ordered distinct finite query pairs such that V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij
cancels every independent f_i and is PSD on ALL n+1 independent gradients.
Entries are allowed to be zero; no support is imposed on the input.
This is exactly the interface in fact04219554e41d9750. A signed-terminal
certificate permits arbitrary signs only on lambda_(i,n), i<n.

The joint claims below are:

(A) For every nonnegative word with at most two positive steps, existence
of a full ordinary primitive certificate is equivalent to existence for
its reversal. The proof gives an explicit certificate transformation,
including a possible change of the PSD remainder and full zero-step lift.

(B) Suppose h=(a,1+r,b), A=1+sum a, D=1+sum b,
T=A+D+r, r>0, and rT=AD. Suppose each child a,b has at most two positive
steps. A full ordinary certificate for h yields full ordinary certificates
for BOTH children after re-selection. Consequently h and rev(h) have
ordinary certificates simultaneously, by an explicit construction.

(C) In particular, for four physical steps and a saturated middle cut
(at index1 or2), ordinary full-certificate feasibility is reversal
invariant. Any such feasible word has capacity T<77/10<193/25.
Thus a four-step threshold seed from fact04219554e41d9750 cannot have
either middle cut saturated.

These assertions do NOT prove arbitrary four-step reversal. They cannot
transport the threshold C82/C83 prism exclusions: the class in(C) does
not meet the threshold region. Endpoint saturated cuts can leave a
three-positive-step child, which is outside(A)--(B). Fully unsaturated
four-step words are also outside(B). The original exact-profile goal
remains open. No new fact is asserted.

## 2. Zero-step compression and full-space restoration

This preliminary statement applies to ordinary certificates. It also
applies to signed-terminal certificates when all nonterminal-targeting
coefficients are nonnegative.

Given a nonnegative word, partition its original query indices into
classes that represent the same point after deleting zero updates.
Restrict a supplied certificate to formal data where the values and
gradients in each class are equal. Every original position becomes the
corresponding compressed formal position. A Q between two different
classes is the corresponding compressed Q; a Q within a class vanishes.
Aggregate multipliers over each ordered pair of different classes.
Value cancellation is preserved. The matrix restriction is a congruence,
so it preserves PSD. Nonnegative signs are preserved. In the signed
case only edges entering the final compressed class can be signed.
The original energy restricts to the compressed energy because zero
steps have coefficient zero, and the original terminal becomes the
compressed terminal.

Conversely, for an ORDINARY compressed certificate, choose the original
index of each positive step as its query representative, and the original
index n as the terminal representative. Put its multiplier on that
representative ordered pair and set every other original multiplier to
zero. The represented positions are exactly the compressed GD positions,
as formal identities, since every omitted update has zero coefficient.
The original energy equals the compressed one on those selected formal
gradients; its unused gradients have coefficient zero. Therefore the
lifted identity is PSD on the entire original space, with zero rows and
columns at unused gradients. No equality of duplicated formal gradients
is imposed in the FINAL certificate.

All-zero and empty words have V_h=0 and the zero certificate. Reversal
commutes with positive-step compression up to this representative choice.
It therefore suffices to prove(A) for one or two strictly positive steps.

## 3. Complete two-step signed-terminal repair

This section proves the repair used after inversion and after a cut.
For one positive step u, flow gives lambda_10=lambda_01+2u. Evaluation
at equal gradients gives zero energy and zero Q, so PSD implies that the
all-one vector is in the matrix kernel. Direct expansion then gives
lambda_01=2 and the full identity

 V_(u)+2Q_01+(2+2u)Q_10=(2-u^2)||g_0-g_1||^2.          (1)

Thus u<=sqrt(2), and the coefficients are already ordinary.

For two positive steps (u,v), s=u+v, introduce coefficient names

 a=lambda_01, b=lambda_12, c=lambda_02, d=lambda_20.

Only b,c are allowed to be signed. The other four entries are
nonnegative. Value cancellation gives

 lambda_10=a+c-d+2u,
 lambda_21=b+c-d+2s.

Equal gradients, with values following an affine trajectory, again give
V=Q=0; PSD implies the all-one vector is in the kernel. Expanding its
first and last rows gives

 u*a+s*c=2u,
 v*(b+c)+u*d=2s(u+1).

Consequently

 a=2-(s/u)c,
 b=2s(u+1)/v-c-(u/v)d,
 lambda_10=2(u+1)-(v/u)c-d,
 b=2(u+1)+(u/v)lambda_10>0.                           (2)

To audit both the kernel equations and the entire matrix, use U=g_0-g_1,
W=g_1-g_2. Substitution of the six Q terms gives

 M=[2-u^2+v(u-1)c/u]||U||^2
       +[c-(u-1)d]<U,W>+[Cpair-(u/v)d]||W||^2,
 Cpair=s[2(u+1)/v-s].                                (3)

For example, the forward adjacent Q_01 has quadratic part
(1/2-u)||g_0||^2-<g_0,g_1>+||g_1||^2/2; its reverse has
(||g_0||^2+||g_1||^2)/2+(u-1)<g_0,g_1>.
For Q_02 use x_2-x_0=-u g_0-v g_1; for Q_20 use its negative.
These expansions, the value equations, and(2) give(3) without a
restriction on the independent gradients.

If c>=0, every supplied coefficient is ordinary already, by(2).
If c<0, nonnegativity of the W diagonal in(3), with d>=0, gives
Cpair>=0. If u>=1, nonnegativity of the U diagonal and its nonpositive
c term give u<=sqrt(2). If u<1 that bound holds directly.
Replace the array by

 lambda'_01=2, lambda'_10=2+2u,
 lambda'_12=2s(u+1)/v, lambda'_21=2s(u+1)/v+2s,
 lambda'_02=lambda'_20=0.

These are nonnegative and satisfy exact flow. Formula(3) now gives

 M'=(2-u^2)||U||^2+Cpair||W||^2>=0.                    (4)

This is a change of the full PSD matrix, not a claim about preserving
its rank, its range, or its difference in PSD order. Section2 extends
this repair to words with at most two positive steps and any zero steps.

## 4. Unsigned reversal identity, rederived on the full space

Let the two positive steps be h=(u,v), C=1+u+v. Let e=(1,1,1)^T,
e_2=(0,0,1)^T, hbar=(u,v,0)^T, w=(u,v,1)^T, and

 T_h=[[1,0,0],[u,1,0],[u,v,1]], p=T_h e=(1,1+u,C)^T.

Let L be the row Laplacian of the supplied ordinary multipliers:
L_ij=-lambda_ij for i!=j, L_ii=sum_(j!=i)lambda_ij. Its flow is
L^T e=(-2u,-2v,2(u+v))^T. Define

 K=L+diag(hbar)-hbar e_2^T+diag(w).

Direct expansion of the full interface in fact04219554e41d9750 gives

 M=sym(K T_h)-C^2 e_2 e_2^T,                         (5)
 K e=w, K^T e=C e_2.

For an explicit check of(5), sym((K-L)T_h)=diag(u(2-u),v(2-v),1).
Moreover e^T M e=0, hence M e=0, and therefore

 K p=-C w+2C^2 e_2.

All off-diagonal entries of K are nonpositive. Its row-sum surplus is
w_i>0 at every row. If Kz=0, a coordinate attaining max_i|z_i| and
strict row diagonal dominance force this maximum to be zero. Thus K
is invertible. Put G=K^(-1). The displayed equations imply

 G w=e, G e_2=(p+C e)/(2C^2), e_2^T G=e^T/C.           (6)

Define

 Delta=[[0,-1,1],[-1,1,0],[1,0,0]].

For hrev=(v,u), write wrev=(v,u,1)^T and T_rev=T_(v,u).
Direct multiplication gives

 Delta e=e_2, Delta p=wrev, Delta T_rev=T_h^T Delta.

Set F=Delta G Delta and

 K_rev=4C^2 F-(wrev+2C e_2)e_2^T,
 lambda_rev,ij=-4C^2 F_ij  (i!=j).                    (7)

For now these coefficients are allowed to be signed. Equations(6) give
K_rev e=wrev and K_rev^T e=C e_2. The off-diagonals in(7), including
its last-column correction, are exactly the grounding of lambda_rev;
the row sums fix its diagonals. Thus every reversed function-value
coefficient cancels with the required flow (-2v,-2u,2(u+v)).

The entire reversed quadratic remainder obeys

 M_rev=4C^2 Delta G M G^T Delta.                       (8)

Here is a full algebra check. Inserting K_rev into sym(K_rev T_rev)
produces the non-boundary term 4C^2 sym(Delta G T_h^T Delta).
After subtracting C^2 e_2 e_2^T, its boundary term is

 -(wrev+C e_2)(wrev+C e_2)^T.

Inserting(5) in the right side of(8) produces the same non-boundary
term and the same boundary term, since Delta G e_2=(wrev+C e_2)/(2C^2).
This proves(8) on all three independent reversed gradients. No
positivity of the output multipliers has yet been inferred.

## 5. The four nonterminal-directed signs are automatic in dimension three

This is the additional sign argument specific to two physical steps.
Write k00=K_00 and k11=K_11, and put

 det2=k00*k11-lambda_01*lambda_10>0.

Strict row diagonal dominance gives k00>lambda_01 and
k11>lambda_10, so det2>0. The original value flows also give

 k00=lambda_01+lambda_02+2u=lambda_10+lambda_20,
 k11=lambda_10+lambda_12+2v=lambda_01+lambda_21.         (9)

Every column difference G(e_i-e_j) has last coordinate zero by(6).
Its first two coordinates are obtained by inverting

 [[k00,-lambda_01],[-lambda_10,k11]].

In particular, for columns0-1 the first two coordinates are
((k11-lambda_01)/det2,(lambda_10-k00)/det2), and for
columns1-2 they are(lambda_01/det2,k00/det2).
Using the displayed Delta and(9) gives ALL FOUR signs

 F_01=-lambda_20/det2,
 F_10=-(lambda_02+2u)/det2,
 F_20=-lambda_01/det2,
 F_21=-lambda_21/det2.                                (10)

Therefore the output lambda_rev is nonnegative on every pair whose
target is not the terminal2. Only lambda_rev,02 and lambda_rev,12
could have failed signs. It is precisely a signed-terminal certificate,
with full PSD by(8). Apply Section3, with reversed steps(v,u), to turn
it into an ordinary certificate. In fact Section3 automatically makes
lambda_rev,12 positive, so only the single entry02 can require repair.
If it does, (4) gives the replacement explicitly.

This proves the forward implication in(A). Applying the same result
to the reversed word proves the backward implication. This does not
claim that the unmodified inverse map preserves every ordinary array:
a negative incoming-terminal output can occur and is repaired here.

## 6. Exact extraction at a saturated cut

First compress zero steps as in Section2. Retain a strictly positive
bridge1+r, positive entries in the two children, and allow either child
to be empty. Let their capacities be A,D, with r(A+D+r)=AD,
T=A+D+r, kappa=(T/D)^2. The prefix query set P ends at the bridge query
L; the tail query set B begins just after it and ends at z.

Suppose a full ordinary parent certificate is supplied. An affine Huber
trajectory with constant gradients1 has V=Q=0. A second legal scalar
function has derivative clip(x,[-eta,1]), eta=r/D=A/T, and starts at A.
The prefix gradients are1; the bridge takes x_L=1 to-r; the tail
gradients are-eta and end at x_z=-eta. Integration from0 defines a
convex differentiable1-smooth function with minimizer0. At every query
f_i=x_i g_i-g_i^2/2. Telescoping gives V=A^2-T^2 eta^2=0.

For i in P and j in B, let R_i^a and R_j^b be their remaining child-step
sums, so R_L^a=R_z^b=0. Direct substitution gives every cross residual:

 Q_ij=-(1+eta)eta R_j^b,
 Q_ji=-(1+eta)R_i^a.                                 (11)

Same-block residuals are zero. Since lambda>=0 and M>=0, equality of V
forces complementarity. Thus the only possible cross edges are i->z
for i in P and j->L for j in B. The two equality gradient vectors span
the block indicators; hence both indicators are in the full PSD kernel.
Writing nu_i=lambda_i,z and mu_j=lambda_j,L, the row i<L of M e_B is
-D nu_i/2, so nu_i=0. The row j<z of M e_P is
(r mu_j-nu_L b_j)/2; its row z is(r mu_z-nu_L)/2.
Therefore mu_j=(nu_L/r)b_j and mu_z=nu_L/r. Summing the prefix flow
now yields D nu_L/r-nu_L=2(A+r). Since r<D, this gives

 lambda_L,z=r(kappa-1),
 lambda_j,L=(kappa-1)b_j (j<z in B),
 lambda_z,L=kappa-1,                                  (12)

with all other cross entries zero. The identity
(kappa-1)(D-r)=2(A+r) follows by rT=AD and verifies(12).

The accepted full join identity can now be applied as an algebraic
identity, without assuming that the children are primitive. Subtracting
the forced cross terms(12) gives the block-diagonal remainder

 M_parent=M_a+kappa M_b,
 M_a=V_a+sum_(i,j in P)lambda_ij Q_ij,
 M_b=V_b+sum_(i,j in B)lambda_hat_ij Q_ij,
 lambda_hat_ij=lambda_ij/kappa
                 -(1-1/kappa)b_i*1_(i<z,j=z).         (13)

Each block cancels its own function values. The formal gradient sets
are disjoint, so each block is PSD. The prefix coefficients are ordinary.
The tail coefficients are nonnegative except possibly those entering z.
One cannot discard that possible sign defect in the supplied array.
When each child has at most two positive steps, Section3 repairs the
right child and leaves ordinary full certificates for both children.
Section5 reverses them. The full saturated join from the accepted fact,
with capacities interchanged, constructs a nonnegative full certificate
for (rev(b),1+r,rev(a)). Section2 restores every original zero-step
gradient. This proves(B), and hence the reversal part of(C).

## 7. The saturated-middle class cannot reach the threshold

A singleton full primitive certificate has step<=sqrt(2), by(1), and
capacity<=1+sqrt(2)<483/200. We give a short independent two-step
capacity bound, sufficient for the four-step corollary.

For any full primitive word of total capacity C, the legal clipped
quadratic at a selected step h_j>1, with prefix sum P and suffix sum R,
is obtained from derivative clip(x,[-(h_j-1)/(R+1),1]) starting at P+1.
Its prefix gradient is1, its tail gradient is the negative threshold,
and its terminal point equals that gradient. Since all its values
satisfy f_i=x_i g_i-g_i^2/2, its energy is

 (P+1)^2-C^2 (h_j-1)^2/(R+1)^2.

Nonnegativity gives C(h_j-1)_+<=(P+1)(R+1). For a two-step word, both
endpoint steps are therefore bounded by2C/(C+1), including the case
h_j<=1. The actual unit quadratic, started at1, also gives

 C |(h_0-1)(h_1-1)|<=1.                               (14)

Assume a two-step certificate had C>=201/50. Set alpha=h_0-1,
beta=h_1-1 and rC=(C-1)/(C+1). Then
alpha+beta=C-3 and alpha,beta<=rC. Their lower bound
lC=C-3-rC=C-4+2/(C+1) is positive. If lC>rC the endpoint bounds are
already inconsistent. Otherwise alpha beta>=rC*lC, since both factors
lie in[lC,rC] with fixed sum. The functions C,rC,lC are positive and
strictly increasing for C>=201/50. At that endpoint,

 C*rC*lC=159373101/157502500>1,

contradicting(14). Thus every two-step primitive certificate has
capacity strictly below201/50. This also covers its zero-step limits
by compression or the same witnesses.

At either middle cut in a four-step word, one child has at most one
physical step and the other at most two. Section6 extracts ordinary
certificates for those children. Saturation gives

 T=Omega(A,D),
 Omega(A,D)=(A+D+sqrt((A+D)^2+4AD))/2.

This function is increasing in both positive arguments, directly from
the displayed expression. Consequently

 T<Omega(483/200,201/50)<77/10<193/25.

For the strict penultimate inequality, at t=77/10 the increasing-root
polynomial t^2-(483/200+201/50)t-(483/200)(201/50) equals161/5000>0,
and t is above the nonnegative root's vertex. This proves(C).

## 8. Direct-proving screen and remaining route

The named literature was checked at its exact class and performance:

* Grimmer--Shu--Wang, Composing Optimized Stepsize Schedules for Gradient
  Descent, arXiv2410.16249v2, Definition3 and Proposition2. Definition3
  imposes eta=1/(1+sum h)=product(h_i-1), while Proposition2 proves
  reversal of BASIC s-composable words by recursive child exchange.
  Proposition6 translates its energy under that same rate hypothesis.
  It does not assert reversal of our arbitrary full cone.
* Shu--Wang, A Unified Theory of H-Duality in First-Order Methods,
  arXiv2609.03281v1, Theorem3/Corollary3 and Section4.7 Proposition2.
  The general statement transports unsigned certificates and retains a
  separate coefficient-sign test. Its automatic sign theorem assumes a
  tridiagonal REDUCED certificate, which is not a hypothesis here.
  No external result is used as a black-box proof premise above.

The exact source HTML and readable extracted text are saved in
local downloads/reversal/. Named Matlas searches were attempted and
returned unrelated statements; none was cited as a theorem. A PDF was
downloaded for2410.16249; pdftotext was unavailable, so source HTML was
used without installing anything.

Two routes have been screened rather than silently promoted:

1. The general unsigned map is already shared in4a064f93111ac5a2 and
   fails signs on some ordinary arrays by37622e6cdcb606e6. Section5
   resolves the sign selection ONLY in the two-step case by showing
   that all remaining bad signs target the terminal and are repairable.
   At four steps, negative nonterminal outputs can occur, so this
   repair proof does not extend unchanged.
2. A subcritical tree construction was independently recovered but
   is already fully present in0b2dfaee171c78eb. It is not new progress
   and remains bounded by the exact primitive DP. It cannot transport
   threshold exclusions or supply an improving seed.

A proposed below-threshold counterexample shape was also rejected
analytically, before claiming a certificate. Let
h=(1+u,1+u,1+v,1+v), 0<u<1/2, 0<v<=1, C=5+2u+2v,
and impose C*u^2*v^2=1. An actual capped quadratic with derivative
min(x,1), started at3+2u, has its first two gradients1 and then tail
quadratic gradients1,-v,v^2. All sampled x_i<=1 after the first pair,
so these are legal for this fixed convex1-smooth function, with
minimizer0. Every sample satisfies f_i=x_i g_i-g_i^2/2 and the final
point equals its gradient. Its exact energy is

 (3+2u)^2-C^2 v^4=(3+2u)^2-u^(-4)<0,

because (3+2u)u^2<1 for0<u<1/2. Thus this entire family cannot be the
feasible side of a reversal counterexample. This is a failed candidate
family, not a counterexample to reversal itself.

The outstanding problem remains an ordinary full certificate for an
arbitrary four-step word versus rev(h). In particular, neither the
remaining strict-cut threshold region nor a four-step counterexample
has been decided. The next round must address genuinely nonterminal
inverse signs or construct an actual asymmetric feasible word; it must
not repeat the basic/subcritical theorem or bad-supplied-array examples.

Status: **UNVERIFIED joint proof draft**. This is actual runtime launch
round 2, cumulative round 23 after baseline 21, under the unchanged cap 23.
The previous runtime round contained both C90 and C91; its internal-stage
round count was corrected in finding `92d17fda8c9a843f`. No numerical
evaluation, scan, replay, solver, installation, subordinate agent, or

convex interpolation and its explicit conjugate), `0e7e78056dc6258c`
(the scalar moment elimination), `b98bb807d514e80d` (the original benchmark
and exact single-cut example), and `04219554e41d9750` (the original dyadic
benchmark limit). No unverified C90 or C91 assertion is a proof premise.
All new assertions used below are proved together in this document.

The original arbitrary-schedule problem remains open. The result below
settles the strength of one dense signed geometry, not the original problem.

## 1. Original schedule, class, and claims

For each integer m>=4 set

    N=2^m, n=N-1, sigma=1+sqrt(2), delta=1-1/m,
    c=sigma(1+1/m), a=delta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m.

Use exactly h=H_m, so h_t=1+a*c^(nu_2(t+1)) for 0<=t<n.
All occurrences of a and c retain the enclosing m. Put

    ell=1+a=h_0=h_(n-1), S=sum_(t<n)h_t,
    T=sum_(t=1)^(n-1)h_t=S-ell,
    K_first_m=a^2/(1+2T).

Here K_first_m is the actual first-cut scalar payoff from accepted
`b98bb807d514e80d`. It is not a new benchmark. B_n is the ORIGINAL
Zhang--Jiang denominator, so the benchmark objective is 1/B_n.
The elementary bounds 6/25<a<1/2 give 1<ell<3/2.

Define the following restricted class of legal instances on this schedule.
Normalize smoothness to 1, choose a closest minimizer as 0, and normalize
the true initial distance to ||X_0||=1. Write g_i=grad F(X_i),
f_i=F(X_i)-F(0), with the actual GD displacement

    X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i*g_i.

If a queried gradient is zero, the terminal gap is zero. Otherwise write
g_i=A_i*u_i, A_i>0, ||u_i||=1, for 0<=i<n. The sole queried-Gram
restriction is that there is a number tau in (0,1) with

    <u_0,u_i>=-tau                  (1<=i<n),
    <u_i,u_j>=tau                   (1<=i<j<n).          (1)

Every amplitude, initial anchor, sampled value, and actual function is
otherwise free. Tau may depend arbitrarily on m. In particular the
unqueried terminal gradient g_n is unrestricted. The Gram in (1) is
(1-tau)I+tau*eta*eta^T, where eta_0=1 and eta_i=-1 for i>=1.
It has no orthogonal queried pair and has a negative initial correlation
with every later query. Thus C89's positive-history premise fails and its
large orthogonal selection is absent.

Let V_best_m be the supremum of 2f_n over this class, including all dimensions.
The proposed joint conclusions are:

1. A fully explicit dense character construction, all original pair
   constraints, one static function, unique minimizer, and radius 1 are
   given below. It has an associative physical-tail boundary rule with
   all history and value costs retained.
2. For every m>=4, one specified construction has B_n*2f_n>1/150 and
   minimum character atom exactly 1/[8n(n+1)]. No scalar strictification
   or unpriced anchor component is required.
3. More strongly, the ENTIRE class (1) has the exact asymptotic strength

       lim_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1)*V_best_m
          = Z_1/[2e*sigma^2] < 1/5,                    (2)

   where Z_1=lim sigma^(-m)B_(2^m-1) is the accepted ray constant and
   e=lim (1+1/m)^m. This includes arbitrary horizon-dependent tau and
   free terminal gradients, not merely the displayed construction.

The upper bound in (2) is about this family of lower witnesses. It is
NOT an upper bound on unrestricted W_n(h).

## 2. A direct construction on an arbitrary eligible physical word

First let n>=2, h_0=1+a with a>0, and choose 0<tau<1 such that

    h_i>=1/tau, 1<=i<n.                                (3)

Choose unit vectors u_0,...,u_n with exactly the signed Gram (1), now
including i=n with negative sign. Such vectors are realized explicitly
in Section 6. Choose q>0 and define

    A_0=1, A_i=q*tau^(i-1) for 1<=i<=n,
    g_i=A_i*u_i, X_0=g_0,
    X_i=X_0-sum_(t<i)h_t*g_t.

Define the actual tail moments

    P_i=sum_(t=1)^(i-1)h_t*A_t,
    E_i=sum_(t=i)^(n-1)h_t*A_t^2,  1<=i<=n.

Empty sums are zero. Let b>0 satisfy

    A_n+b/A_n+tau*P_n <= tau*a.                        (4)

Set f_0=1/2 and

    f_i=A_i^2/2+b+tau^2*E_i, 1<=i<=n,                 (5)

and include the optimum jet (0,0,0). These are values on original indices;
no trajectory is compressed or reset. The following sections verify EVERY
ordered interpolation residual

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.         (6)

The necessity and sufficiency of Q_ij<=0, with the explicit construction
of one function, are accepted in `1252b8823bb5a290`.

## 3. Every finite tail pair, with the original displacement

For 1<=i<j<=n put

    W_ij=sum_(t=i)^(j-1)h_t*A_t,
    D_ij=f_i-f_j=(A_i^2-A_j^2)/2
                           +tau^2*sum_(t=i)^(j-1)h_t*A_t^2.

The identity for D_ij follows from (5), not from a compressed update.
The actual signed inner products give the following exact allowed interval:

    L_ij <= D_ij <= U_ij,
    L_ij=tau*A_j*W_ij+(A_i^2+A_j^2-2tau*A_i*A_j)/2,
    U_ij=h_i*A_i^2+tau*A_i*sum_(t=i+1)^(j-1)h_t*A_t
                         -(A_i^2+A_j^2-2tau*A_i*A_j)/2. (7)

Here Q_ji=L_ij-D_ij and Q_ij=D_ij-U_ij. In particular every skipped
history term h_t*<g_i,g_t> is present in (7).

The lower inequality follows from the identity

    D_ij-L_ij
      =sum_(t=i)^(j-1)tau*h_t*A_t*(tau*A_t-A_j)
                          +A_j*(tau*A_i-A_j) >=0.      (8)

For each summand t<=j-1, tau*A_t>=A_j, because A_(t+1)=tau*A_t.
The last term is also nonnegative. For j=i+1 both terms vanish, giving
the exact reverse-row equality Q_(i+1,i)=0.

For the upper inequality put d=j-i. Direct expansion gives

    (U_ij-D_ij)/A_i^2
      =(h_i-1)(1-tau^2)
       +sum_(k=1)^(d-1)(h_(i+k)-1)*tau^(k+1)*(1-tau^(k+1))
       +J_d,

    J_d=-tau^2+tau^(d+1)
                   +sum_(k=1)^(d-1)(tau^(k+1)-tau^(2k+2)). (9)

One has J_1=0 and

    J_(d+1)-J_d=tau^(d+2)*(1-tau^d)>=0.

All coefficients in the first two terms of (9) are nonnegative because
h_i>=1. Thus U_ij-D_ij>=0. This proves both orientations for every
tail pair, not just adjacent samples.

## 4. Every optimum and initial pair; the exact scalar boundary

The negative initial history is retained exactly:

    <g_i,X_i>=tau*A_i*(a-P_i), 1<=i<=n.               (10)

The contribution of the first displacement is +h_0*tau*A_i, while
<g_i,X_0>=-tau*A_i. Deleting that signed initial term would change (10).

The optimum residual Q_(i,star) is nonpositive precisely when

    R_i:=A_i+b/A_i+tau*P_i+tau^2*E_i/A_i <= tau*a.

For 1<=i<n, expansion using A_(i+1)=tau*A_i gives

    R_(i+1)-R_i
      =(1-tau)[(tau*h_i-1)A_i
                    +tau*E_(i+1)/A_i+b/(tau*A_i)] >=0. (11)

Condition (3) is used here. Consequently every optimum upper row follows
from the SINGLE final boundary (4). Conversely the final row requires
(4), so this is an exact elimination for this chosen construction.
The other optimum orientation is

    Q_(star,i)=-b-tau^2*E_i<0.

At i=0, X_0=g_0 and f_0=1/2 give both optimum residuals zero.

For i>=1, direct calculation gives

    Q_(i,0)=Q_(i,star),
    Q_(0,i)=-a-b-tau^2*E_i+tau*(P_i+A_i).             (12)

If i<n, then P_n-P_i>=h_i*A_i>=A_i. Hence
tau*(P_i+A_i)<=tau*P_n<=tau*a by (4).
If i=n, (4) gives tau*P_n+A_n<=tau*a, so
tau*(P_n+A_n)<=tau*a-(1-tau)A_n<=tau*a.
In either case Q_(0,i)<=-(1-tau)a-b-tau^2*E_i<0.

Equations (7)--(12), together with the two zero rows at i=0, check ALL
original directed pairs including the terminal. For the smallest physical
block, indices 0,1 and star, they give Q_(1,0)=Q_(1,star)<=0 and
Q_(0,1)<0 with <g_0,g_1>=-tau*q<0. This block is part of the original
word with its actual h_0, and already has genuinely signed history.

## 5. One static function, values, and exact closest distance

Put y_i=X_i-g_i and d_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2. Then y_0=0,d_0=0 and
d_i=b+tau^2*E_i>0 for i>=1. Define on the same Euclidean space

    H(v)=||v||^2/2+max{0,max_(1<=i<=n)(<y_i,v>-d_i)},
    F(X)=sup_v(<X,v>-H(v)).                            (13)

By the explicit all-pair interpolation construction in accepted
`1252b8823bb5a290`, F is everywhere finite, convex, differentiable and
1-smooth, and F(X_i)=f_i, grad F(X_i)=g_i for every i, including 0 and n.
Thus its actual GD is exactly the prescribed original trajectory.

All d_i with i>=1 are strictly positive, so H(v)=||v||^2/2 in a
neighborhood of zero. Also H(v)>=||v||^2/2 everywhere. It follows that
F(0)=0. For any X!=0, take a sufficiently small t in (0,1) with tX in
that neighborhood. Then

    F(X)>=(t-t^2/2)||X||^2>0.

Therefore argmin F={0}. Its true initial squared distance is exactly
||X_0||^2=||g_0||^2=1. No inverse-Gram or orthogonal-anchor radius cost is
hidden. Multiplication of F by L and use of physical steps h_i/L give
the same normalized payoff for arbitrary L>0.

## 6. A positive finite character law

Let d be any integer with 2^d>=n+1. In the (d+1)-bit label space use

    lambda_0=(0,binary(0)),
    lambda_i=(1,binary(i)), 1<=i<=n.

These labels do not permute the physical indices. Let s range over this
binary space, let e_sig have only its first bit equal to 1, and put

    D=2^(d+1),
    w_s=tau*1_(s=e_sig)+(1-tau)/D,
    (u_i)_s=sqrt(w_s)*(-1)^(s dot lambda_i).            (14)

All weights are positive and sum to one. Summing the binary characters
by pairing a differing bit gives

    <u_i,u_j>=tau*eta_i*eta_j+(1-tau)*1_(i=j).

This is the required full signed Gram, not a PSD-only existence claim:
positions, all values, all original residuals and F were supplied above.
The explicit anchor is simply X_0=u_0. On H_m one may take d=m,D=2N.
The least atom is (1-tau)/(2N).

## 7. Exact payoff and an associative physical block rule

Put

    r=tau^(n-1), H_tail=sum_(t=1)^(n-1)h_t*tau^(t-1).

Then A_n=q*r and P_n=q*H_tail. For fixed q, the largest permitted b in
(4) is

    b=q*r*(tau*a-q*(tau*H_tail+r)).                   (15)

When b>0, (13) has the unique minimizer just proved. Its normalized
terminal payoff is

    V=2f_n=2q*r*tau*a-q^2*r*(2tau*H_tail+r).

Completing the square in q gives the maximum, at

    q=tau*a/(2tau*H_tail+r),
    b=q^2*r*tau*H_tail>0,
    V_tau=tau^2*a^2*r/(2tau*H_tail+r).                 (16)

This is an algebraic formula, not a numerical parameter evaluation.

For a consecutive tail block p=(p_0,...,p_(k-1)), define

    alpha_p=tau^k,
    H_p=sum_(j=0)^(k-1)p_j*tau^j,
    J_p=sum_(j=0)^(k-1)p_j*tau^(2j).

If it starts at tail amplitude A, cumulative moment P, and value f, its
actual end state is

    A_out=alpha_p*A,
    P_out=P+A*H_p,
    f_out=f-A^2*(1-alpha_p^2)/2-tau^2*A^2*J_p.         (17)

For the physical concatenation p followed by qword,

    alpha_(p qword)=alpha_p*alpha_qword,
    H_(p qword)=H_p+alpha_p*H_qword,
    J_(p qword)=J_p+alpha_p^2*J_qword.                 (18)

These identities follow by splitting the defining sums at the actual
index k. They prove associativity without resetting P, A, or the enclosing
schedule parameters. All cross-block Q rows are already covered by
(7)--(12). The final boundary (4) prices the complete history. This is a
legal iterable rule for this restricted tail geometry, not an improving
primitive-capacity composition theorem.

Since tau*H_tail>=r*T, (16) also gives

    V_tau<=tau^2*a^2/(2T+1)<K_first_m.                       (19)

Thus even before the wider obstruction below, the exact block rule does
not improve the scalar first-cut lower bound.

## 8. Quantitative calibration on every original H_m

Choose tau=1-1/(4n). For n>=15,
1/tau<=60/59<31/25<ell, so (3) holds at every original tail step.
The character law's minimum atom is exactly 1/[8nN]. Since H_tail<=T
and r<=1, (16) and Bernoulli's inequality yield

    V_tau >= tau^(n+1)*K_first_m
           >=[1-(n+1)/(4n)]*K_first_m >=(11/15)*K_first_m.        (20)

For completeness the original benchmark comparison uses its exact mass
recurrences, not the physical mass as a substitute. The accepted joins are

    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt((u+v)^2+4uv))/2,
    G(u,v)=2u+v/2+sqrt(v^2+8uv)/2,
    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(k+l=n-1)Omega(C_k,C_l),
    B_n=max_(k+l=n-1)G(C_k,B_l).

Both joins are increasing and G>=Omega: after squaring the nonnegative
quantities 3u+sqrt(v^2+8uv) and sqrt(u^2+6uv+v^2), their squared difference
is 8u^2+2uv+6u*sqrt(v^2+8uv)>=0. Induction gives B_n>=C_n, and the
balanced primitive split gives B_(2^m-1)>=sigma^m.

Counting 2^(m-k-1) occurrences of level k in the actual word gives

    S=N-1+r_sum*(c^m-N),
    r_sum=delta/[c(c-2)], 0<r_sum<1.                  (21)

Here c>sigma>2, and c(c-2)>sigma(sigma-2)=1>delta. Hence
S<c^m-1 and 2T+1<2c^m<6sigma^m. The last inequality uses
(1+1/m)^m<3, obtained by the binomial expansion and sum 1/k!<3.
Finally a=(sqrt(2)-1)(m-1)/(m+1)>6/25 for m>=4. Therefore

    B_n*V_tau >(11/15)*a^2/6
              >396/56250 >1/150.                    (22)

This proves a fully realized, quantitatively priced signed construction
on every original enclosing horizon, while (19) records its limitation.

## 9. Arbitrary amplitudes: an original tail-pair restriction

We now return to the ENTIRE class (1), with arbitrary amplitudes, values,
anchor, and free terminal. Set k=n-1, so the last queried sample is k.
Normalize using the true closest-minimizer distance as in Section 1.

For 1<=i<j<=k, add Q_ij and Q_ji. The accepted necessary inequality is

    <g_i-g_j,X_i-X_j> >= ||g_i-g_j||^2.

Its LEFT side is exactly

    h_i*A_i*(A_i-tau*A_j)
      +tau*(A_i-A_j)*sum_(t=i+1)^(j-1)h_t*A_t.        (23)

If A_j>=A_i/tau, both terms in (23) are nonpositive. The right side is
A_i^2+A_j^2-2tau*A_i*A_j>0 because 0<tau<1 and both amplitudes are
positive. This contradiction proves

    A_i>tau*A_j, 1<=i<j<=k.                           (24)

No nonnegative-history simplification was made across the initial sample.
The assertion is only within the tail where its pair correlations are
actually positive.

## 10. The true anchor and a free terminal: a sharp limiting upper bound

Write A_0=||g_0||. Optimum cocoercivity gives
<X_0,g_0>>=A_0^2, and A_0<=||X_0||=1. Set z=<X_0,u_0>, so z>=A_0.
Resolve the unit vector u_k=-tau*u_0+sqrt(1-tau^2)*v with v perpendicular
to u_0 and ||v||=1. Then

    <X_0,u_k> <= -tau*z+sqrt(1-tau^2)*sqrt(1-z^2).

The right side is decreasing for 0<=z<=1, so it is at most its value at
z=A_0. Put T_pre=sum_(t=1)^(k-1)h_t=T-ell. The original optimum row at k,
including the negative contribution of g_0 and every positive tail term,
therefore gives, using (24),

    f_k <= A_k[tau*a*A_0+sqrt(1-tau^2)*sqrt(1-A_0^2)]
                               -(tau^2*T_pre+1/2)A_k^2.

Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the bracket by

    M_tau=sqrt(tau^2*a^2+1-tau^2).

The actual final step has length ell<2. Smoothness at X_k gives

    f_n<=f_k-ell*(1-ell/2)*A_k^2.

Maximizing the resulting quadratic in A_k proves the uniform class bound

    2f_n <= U_angle(tau)
      :=[tau^2*a^2+1-tau^2]
                    /[1+2tau^2*T_pre+ell*(2-ell)].    (25)

This does not impose any law on g_n. Its initial norm was the TRUE radius,
and neither a translated reset nor an unrecorded anchor adjustment occurs.
Relative to the first-cut payoff, (25) implies

    U_angle(tau)/K_first_m
      <=[1+(tau^(-2)-1)/a^2]
                     *(1+2T)/(1+2T-ell^2).           (26)

In particular, as tau tends to 1 this ratio tends to 1 uniformly over m
because a>6/25, ell<3/2 and T>=n-1.

## 11. Small correlations: a priced moment bound on the actual tail

There are M=n-1 tail queries 1,...,k. For consecutive tail samples, the
original reverse interpolation inequality reads

    f_i-f_(i+1) >= (A_i^2+A_(i+1)^2)/2
                          +tau*(h_i-1)*A_i*A_(i+1)
                    >= (A_i^2+A_(i+1)^2)/2.           (27)

At each tail sample, the optimum row and the actual displacement from X_1
give

    <X_1,g_i> >= f_i+A_i^2/2.

All added terms in this last relation are tau*h_t*A_i*A_t>=0 for
1<=t<i. Write b_tail=f_k-A_k^2/2>=0. Summing (27) gives

    <X_1,u_i> >= [b_tail+sum_(j=i)^k A_j^2]/A_i >0.   (28)

For real coefficients t_i, (1) gives the elementary Gram estimate

    ||sum_(i=1)^k t_i*u_i||^2
       =(1-tau)sum_i t_i^2+tau*(sum_i t_i)^2
       <=[1+(M-1)tau]*sum_i t_i^2.

Apply Cauchy--Schwarz with t_i=<X_1,u_i>. It follows that

    sum_i <X_1,u_i>^2 <=[1+(M-1)tau]||X_1||^2.        (29)

The original first step costs no hidden radius: since ell<2 and
<X_0,g_0>>=A_0^2,

    ||X_1||^2<=1-ell*(2-ell)*A_0^2<=1.

The scalar elimination proved in accepted `0e7e78056dc6258c`, proof
Section 5, applies to (28)--(29): if q_i=A_i^2 and T_i=b_tail+sum_(j>=i)q_j,
it bounds 2f_k by beta_(M-1) times the upper budget for sum T_i^2/q_i.
Here beta_j=4/[1+sqrt(1+2c_j)]^2, c_0=0,
c_(j+1)=c_j+2+2sqrt(c_j+1), with beta_j<=2/j^2 for j>=1.
The actual last step cannot increase f. Hence

    2f_n <= [1+(n-2)tau]*beta_(n-2)
           <= 2[1+(n-2)tau]/(n-2)^2.                 (30)

This is an elementary extension with its full Gram cost written out.
No orthogonality of these actual tail gradients is asserted.

## 12. Intermediate correlations: exact adjacent ratios

For two consecutive tail queries the same cocoercivity inequality gives

    (h_i-1)A_i^2-A_(i+1)^2
                    +(2-h_i)tau*A_i*A_(i+1)>=0.

For z>0 define the positive root

    r_tau(z)=[-tau*(z-1)+sqrt(tau^2*(z-1)^2+4z)]/2.

Then A_(i+1)/A_i<=r_tau(h_i-1). The root obeys r_tau(z)>tau and is
strictly increasing in z. A convenient exact formula, with natural log,
is

    phi_tau(x):=log r_tau(exp x)
       =x/2-asinh(tau*sinh(x/2)).                     (31)

Indeed divide r^2+tau(z-1)r-z=0 by r*sqrt(z) and solve the resulting
hyperbolic-sine identity. Thus phi is odd, phi(0)=0, and

    phi'(x)=1/2-tau*cosh(x/2)
                              /[2sqrt(1+tau^2*sinh^2(x/2))]>0,
    phi''(x)=-tau*(1-tau^2)*sinh(x/2)
                              /[4(1+tau^2*sinh^2(x/2))^(3/2)]. (32)

The derivative positivity follows by squaring: the denominator under its
square root exceeds tau^2*cosh^2(x/2) by 1-tau^2. On x>0, phi is
strictly concave. These formulas also prove r_tau(z)>tau by its limit
as z decreases to zero and strict monotonicity.

The first queried norm is bounded without assuming it shares a positive
correlation. Write d=g_1-g_0. Cocoercivity and X_1-X_0=-ell*g_0 give
-ell*<g_0,d>>=||d||^2, whence

    ||g_1||^2<=||g_0||^2+(1-2/ell)||d||^2<=||g_0||^2<=1.

Define the product over ALL original steps

    P_all=product_(t=0)^(n-1) r_tau(h_t-1).

The first and last physical steps both have excess a. Multiplying only
the legitimate tail inequalities i=1,...,n-2 therefore gives

    A_k <= P_all/r_tau(a)^2 <= tau^(-2)*P_all.         (33)

This product does not assume any condition on the free terminal gradient.

## 13. Ruler counts create a uniform strict product loss

Put Lc=log c. Since the physical excess at level j is delta*c^(j-1)
with delta<1, monotonicity in (31) and the original counts give

    log P_all
      <=(N/2)[-phi(Lc)+sum_(j=2)^(m-1)2^(-j)*phi((j-1)Lc)].

Concavity and phi(0)=0 imply phi(r*Lc)<=r*phi(Lc) for integer r>=1.
Keep the strict deficit at j=3 separately and write

    Delta_tau(c)=2phi(Lc)-phi(2Lc)>0.

The finite identity sum_(j=2)^(m-1)(j-1)/2^j=1-m/2^(m-1) yields

    log P_all <= -m*phi(Lc)-(N/16)*Delta_tau(c).        (34)

This retains all original levels and their actual multiplicities.

For an explicit bound, c>=sigma>2 and c<4 for m>=4. Hence
Lc>1/2 and cosh(Lc)<5/2. The identity

    Delta_tau(c)=integral_(t=0)^Lc integral_(s=t)^(t+Lc)
                                           [-phi''(s)] ds dt

contains the rectangle Lc/2<=t<=Lc, Lc<=s<=3Lc/2. On this rectangle,
sinh(s/2)>1/4, and
(1+tau^2*sinh^2(s/2))^(3/2)<=cosh(Lc)^3<125/8.
Its area is Lc^2/4>1/16. Substitution into (32) proves

    Delta_tau(c)>=tau*(1-tau^2)/4000
                         >=tau*(1-tau)/4000.          (35)

For clarity Lc>1/2 follows from log 2=integral_1^2 dt/t>1/2;
the other bounds are direct inequalities, not numerical evaluation.
Combining (33)--(35), and dropping the nonpositive -m*phi(Lc), gives

    A_k <=tau^(-2)*exp[-N*tau*(1-tau)/64000].

Finally retain the signed original displacement in the optimum row:

    f_k<=<g_k,X_k>
       =<g_k,X_0>+ell*tau*A_0*A_k
                    -tau*A_k*sum_(t=1)^(k-1)h_t*A_t
       <=(1+ell*tau)*A_k <=(5/2)*A_k.

The final physical step is again nonincreasing for f. Thus the entire
class with free terminal satisfies

    2f_n <=5tau^(-2)*exp[-N*tau*(1-tau)/64000].         (36)

This closes fixed correlations bounded away from 0 and 1 exponentially.
It does not discard the regime tau tending to either endpoint.

## 14. Uniform control of every horizon-dependent correlation

Accepted `04219554e41d9750` gives

    sigma^(-m)*B_(2^m-1) -> Z_1 in (0,infinity).

Hence B_(2^m-1)=O(N^rho), rho=log_2(sigma)<3/2.
Split ALL tau in (0,1) into three exhaustive ranges.

* If tau<=N^(-1/2), (30) is at most
  2(1+sqrt(N))/(N-3)^2. Multiplied by B_n, this tends to zero.
* If N^(-1/2)<=tau<=1-N^(-1/2), then
  tau*(1-tau)>=(1/2)N^(-1/2), and tau^(-2)<=N.
  Equation (36) is at most 5N*exp[-sqrt(N)/128000].
  Its product with B_n also tends to zero.
* If tau>=1-N^(-1/2), (26), a>6/25, ell<3/2 and T>=n-1 give

       2f_n <=[1+o(1)]*K_first_m,                           (37)

  where the o(1) is uniform over this full range. Explicitly its
  multiplicative factor is bounded by

       [1+((1-N^(-1/2))^(-2)-1)/(6/25)^2]
                       *(1+2T)/(1+2T-9/4),

  which tends to 1.

Consequently the supremum over the entire class has

    limsup B_n*V_best_m <= lim B_n*K_first_m,                     (38)

once the limit on the right is evaluated below. No interchange of a
nonuniform pointwise limit with the supremum was made; the three estimates
are uniform over their respective ranges.

## 15. Attainment of the limiting class strength and its original-B value

For the explicit construction choose instead tau_m=1-1/n^2. Condition
(3) holds on every H_m, since 1/tau_m<=225/224<31/25<ell. Moreover
tau_m^(n+1)->1, r=tau_m^(n-1)->1, and (16),(19),(20)'s first inequality
give the squeeze

    tau_m^(n+1)*K_first_m <= V_(tau_m) <= K_first_m.

Thus V_(tau_m)/K_first_m tends to 1. This construction is in the queried class
(1) and supplies a legal terminal, so V_best_m>=V_(tau_m).

In (21), r_sum tends to 1, (2/sigma)^m tends to zero, and
c^m/sigma^m=(1+1/m)^m tends to e. Therefore

    T/sigma^m -> e,  a -> 1/sigma,
    B_n*K_first_m -> Z_1/[2e*sigma^2].                      (39)

Equations (38)--(39) and the construction squeeze prove (2).

The strict numerical comparison in (2) needs no computation. In the
accepted ray enclosure, use b=1,j=0. Its UPPER endpoint involves B_1
(not B_0), so B_1=G(1,1)=4 gives

    Z_1 <= (sqrt(B_1)+3/100)^2 = 41209/10000.

Since e>2 and sigma^2=3+2sqrt(2)>29/5,

    Z_1/[2e*sigma^2]
       < (41209/10000)/(116/5)
       =206045/1160000 <1/5.

The ray theorem is used only in its unconditional scalar part. No
four-step seed existence is assumed anywhere in this argument.

## 16. Scope, an actual uncovered freedom, and failed extrapolations

This result closes the one-initial-sign CONSTANT-CORRELATION class (1),
including arbitrary amplitudes, values, initial anchors, horizon-dependent
tau, and a free terminal. It includes the queried geometry of the C91
dense lift but does not use C91 as a proof premise. It does not close
general signed character laws, nonconstant magnitudes of correlations,
more than one chronological sign reversal, or the changed affine-child
geometry pursued by max.

Multiple sign reversals are an actual legal freedom on the SAME original
schedule. For example put

    kappa=(1+1/ell)/2, F_quad(x)=kappa*x^2/2, x_0=1.

Then 0<kappa<1, kappa*h_0=(ell+1)/2>1, and h_1>ell gives kappa*h_1>1.
Thus the first three nonzero gradients have signs +,-,+, outside (1).
For the complete original word its exact data are

    x_i=product_(t<i)(1-kappa*h_t),
    g_i=kappa*x_i, f_i=kappa*x_i^2/2,
    Q_ij=-kappa*(1-kappa)*(x_i-x_j)^2/2<=0

including the optimum. Its single static function has unique minimizer 0,
true radius 1, and actual payoff
kappa*product_(t<n)(1-kappa*h_t)^2. This is an explicit scope check only;
no favorable asymptotic payoff is claimed. In (23), its intervening
signed contributions would not have the two nonpositive signs used there.

The next missing object is a quantitative multiple-sign or nonconstant-
correlation boundary rule, or another legal geometry improving the
underlying trajectory, with every original cross pair and true radius.
A covariance matrix, a relabeling without value constraints, or optimizing
tau inside (1) cannot provide that improvement. The current exact block
rule is iterable but has the completely priced ceiling (2).

For coordination, the construction's full interface is: the signed Gram
(14), anchor X_0=g_0, values (5), actual positions in Section 2, boundary
(4), state update (17), and all cross-pair identities (7)--(12). It has
active reverse tail pairs and both optimum rows active at sample 0; it
does not have C91's strict margin on every distinct pair. No insertion
into a different child word is licensed without matching these data.

All statements in this manuscript remain a joint author proof draft.
No verifier acceptance, original-target answer, resource renewal, or extra
runtime round is inferred.
