# C92: an exact signed tail rule and its complete asymptotic class limit

Status: **UNVERIFIED joint proof draft**. This is actual runtime launch
round 2, cumulative round 23 after baseline 21, under the unchanged cap 23.
The previous runtime round contained both C90 and C91; its internal-stage
round count was corrected in finding `92d17fda8c9a843f`. No numerical
evaluation, scan, replay, solver, installation, subordinate agent, or
verifier call is used here.

Accepted mathematical predecessors are `1252b8823bb5a290` (all-pair smooth
convex interpolation and its explicit conjugate), `0e7e78056dc6258c`
(the scalar moment elimination), `b98bb807d514e80d` (the original benchmark
and exact single-cut example), and `04219554e41d9750` (the original dyadic
benchmark limit). No unverified C90 or C91 assertion is a proof premise.
All new assertions used below are proved together in this document.

The original arbitrary-schedule problem remains open. The result below
settles the strength of one dense signed geometry, not the original problem.

## 1. Original schedule, class, and claims

For each integer m>=4 set

    N=2^m, n=N-1, sigma=1+sqrt(2), delta=1-1/m,
    c=sigma(1+1/m), a=delta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m.

Use exactly h=H_m, so h_t=1+a*c^(nu_2(t+1)) for 0<=t<n.
All occurrences of a and c retain the enclosing m. Put

    ell=1+a=h_0=h_(n-1), S=sum_(t<n)h_t,
    T=sum_(t=1)^(n-1)h_t=S-ell,
    K_first_m=a^2/(1+2T).

Here K_first_m is the actual first-cut scalar payoff from accepted
`b98bb807d514e80d`. It is not a new benchmark. B_n is the ORIGINAL
Zhang--Jiang denominator, so the benchmark objective is 1/B_n.
The elementary bounds 6/25<a<1/2 give 1<ell<3/2.

Define the following restricted class of legal instances on this schedule.
Normalize smoothness to 1, choose a closest minimizer as 0, and normalize
the true initial distance to ||X_0||=1. Write g_i=grad F(X_i),
f_i=F(X_i)-F(0), with the actual GD displacement

    X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i*g_i.

If a queried gradient is zero, the terminal gap is zero. Otherwise write
g_i=A_i*u_i, A_i>0, ||u_i||=1, for 0<=i<n. The sole queried-Gram
restriction is that there is a number tau in (0,1) with

    <u_0,u_i>=-tau                  (1<=i<n),
    <u_i,u_j>=tau                   (1<=i<j<n).          (1)

Every amplitude, initial anchor, sampled value, and actual function is
otherwise free. Tau may depend arbitrarily on m. In particular the
unqueried terminal gradient g_n is unrestricted. The Gram in (1) is
(1-tau)I+tau*eta*eta^T, where eta_0=1 and eta_i=-1 for i>=1.
It has no orthogonal queried pair and has a negative initial correlation
with every later query. Thus C89's positive-history premise fails and its
large orthogonal selection is absent.

Let V_best_m be the supremum of 2f_n over this class, including all dimensions.
The proposed joint conclusions are:

1. A fully explicit dense character construction, all original pair
   constraints, one static function, unique minimizer, and radius 1 are
   given below. It has an associative physical-tail boundary rule with
   all history and value costs retained.
2. For every m>=4, one specified construction has B_n*2f_n>1/150 and
   minimum character atom exactly 1/[8n(n+1)]. No scalar strictification
   or unpriced anchor component is required.
3. More strongly, the ENTIRE class (1) has the exact asymptotic strength

       lim_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1)*V_best_m
          = Z_1/[2e*sigma^2] < 1/5,                    (2)

   where Z_1=lim sigma^(-m)B_(2^m-1) is the accepted ray constant and
   e=lim (1+1/m)^m. This includes arbitrary horizon-dependent tau and
   free terminal gradients, not merely the displayed construction.

The upper bound in (2) is about this family of lower witnesses. It is
NOT an upper bound on unrestricted W_n(h).

## 2. A direct construction on an arbitrary eligible physical word

First let n>=2, h_0=1+a with a>0, and choose 0<tau<1 such that

    h_i>=1/tau, 1<=i<n.                                (3)

Choose unit vectors u_0,...,u_n with exactly the signed Gram (1), now
including i=n with negative sign. Such vectors are realized explicitly
in Section 6. Choose q>0 and define

    A_0=1, A_i=q*tau^(i-1) for 1<=i<=n,
    g_i=A_i*u_i, X_0=g_0,
    X_i=X_0-sum_(t<i)h_t*g_t.

Define the actual tail moments

    P_i=sum_(t=1)^(i-1)h_t*A_t,
    E_i=sum_(t=i)^(n-1)h_t*A_t^2,  1<=i<=n.

Empty sums are zero. Let b>0 satisfy

    A_n+b/A_n+tau*P_n <= tau*a.                        (4)

Set f_0=1/2 and

    f_i=A_i^2/2+b+tau^2*E_i, 1<=i<=n,                 (5)

and include the optimum jet (0,0,0). These are values on original indices;
no trajectory is compressed or reset. The following sections verify EVERY
ordered interpolation residual

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.         (6)

The necessity and sufficiency of Q_ij<=0, with the explicit construction
of one function, are accepted in `1252b8823bb5a290`.

## 3. Every finite tail pair, with the original displacement

For 1<=i<j<=n put

    W_ij=sum_(t=i)^(j-1)h_t*A_t,
    D_ij=f_i-f_j=(A_i^2-A_j^2)/2
                           +tau^2*sum_(t=i)^(j-1)h_t*A_t^2.

The identity for D_ij follows from (5), not from a compressed update.
The actual signed inner products give the following exact allowed interval:

    L_ij <= D_ij <= U_ij,
    L_ij=tau*A_j*W_ij+(A_i^2+A_j^2-2tau*A_i*A_j)/2,
    U_ij=h_i*A_i^2+tau*A_i*sum_(t=i+1)^(j-1)h_t*A_t
                         -(A_i^2+A_j^2-2tau*A_i*A_j)/2. (7)

Here Q_ji=L_ij-D_ij and Q_ij=D_ij-U_ij. In particular every skipped
history term h_t*<g_i,g_t> is present in (7).

The lower inequality follows from the identity

    D_ij-L_ij
      =sum_(t=i)^(j-1)tau*h_t*A_t*(tau*A_t-A_j)
                          +A_j*(tau*A_i-A_j) >=0.      (8)

For each summand t<=j-1, tau*A_t>=A_j, because A_(t+1)=tau*A_t.
The last term is also nonnegative. For j=i+1 both terms vanish, giving
the exact reverse-row equality Q_(i+1,i)=0.

For the upper inequality put d=j-i. Direct expansion gives

    (U_ij-D_ij)/A_i^2
      =(h_i-1)(1-tau^2)
       +sum_(k=1)^(d-1)(h_(i+k)-1)*tau^(k+1)*(1-tau^(k+1))
       +J_d,

    J_d=-tau^2+tau^(d+1)
                   +sum_(k=1)^(d-1)(tau^(k+1)-tau^(2k+2)). (9)

One has J_1=0 and

    J_(d+1)-J_d=tau^(d+2)*(1-tau^d)>=0.

All coefficients in the first two terms of (9) are nonnegative because
h_i>=1. Thus U_ij-D_ij>=0. This proves both orientations for every
tail pair, not just adjacent samples.

## 4. Every optimum and initial pair; the exact scalar boundary

The negative initial history is retained exactly:

    <g_i,X_i>=tau*A_i*(a-P_i), 1<=i<=n.               (10)

The contribution of the first displacement is +h_0*tau*A_i, while
<g_i,X_0>=-tau*A_i. Deleting that signed initial term would change (10).

The optimum residual Q_(i,star) is nonpositive precisely when

    R_i:=A_i+b/A_i+tau*P_i+tau^2*E_i/A_i <= tau*a.

For 1<=i<n, expansion using A_(i+1)=tau*A_i gives

    R_(i+1)-R_i
      =(1-tau)[(tau*h_i-1)A_i
                    +tau*E_(i+1)/A_i+b/(tau*A_i)] >=0. (11)

Condition (3) is used here. Consequently every optimum upper row follows
from the SINGLE final boundary (4). Conversely the final row requires
(4), so this is an exact elimination for this chosen construction.
The other optimum orientation is

    Q_(star,i)=-b-tau^2*E_i<0.

At i=0, X_0=g_0 and f_0=1/2 give both optimum residuals zero.

For i>=1, direct calculation gives

    Q_(i,0)=Q_(i,star),
    Q_(0,i)=-a-b-tau^2*E_i+tau*(P_i+A_i).             (12)

If i<n, then P_n-P_i>=h_i*A_i>=A_i. Hence
tau*(P_i+A_i)<=tau*P_n<=tau*a by (4).
If i=n, (4) gives tau*P_n+A_n<=tau*a, so
tau*(P_n+A_n)<=tau*a-(1-tau)A_n<=tau*a.
In either case Q_(0,i)<=-(1-tau)a-b-tau^2*E_i<0.

Equations (7)--(12), together with the two zero rows at i=0, check ALL
original directed pairs including the terminal. For the smallest physical
block, indices 0,1 and star, they give Q_(1,0)=Q_(1,star)<=0 and
Q_(0,1)<0 with <g_0,g_1>=-tau*q<0. This block is part of the original
word with its actual h_0, and already has genuinely signed history.

## 5. One static function, values, and exact closest distance

Put y_i=X_i-g_i and d_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2. Then y_0=0,d_0=0 and
d_i=b+tau^2*E_i>0 for i>=1. Define on the same Euclidean space

    H(v)=||v||^2/2+max{0,max_(1<=i<=n)(<y_i,v>-d_i)},
    F(X)=sup_v(<X,v>-H(v)).                            (13)

By the explicit all-pair interpolation construction in accepted
`1252b8823bb5a290`, F is everywhere finite, convex, differentiable and
1-smooth, and F(X_i)=f_i, grad F(X_i)=g_i for every i, including 0 and n.
Thus its actual GD is exactly the prescribed original trajectory.

All d_i with i>=1 are strictly positive, so H(v)=||v||^2/2 in a
neighborhood of zero. Also H(v)>=||v||^2/2 everywhere. It follows that
F(0)=0. For any X!=0, take a sufficiently small t in (0,1) with tX in
that neighborhood. Then

    F(X)>=(t-t^2/2)||X||^2>0.

Therefore argmin F={0}. Its true initial squared distance is exactly
||X_0||^2=||g_0||^2=1. No inverse-Gram or orthogonal-anchor radius cost is
hidden. Multiplication of F by L and use of physical steps h_i/L give
the same normalized payoff for arbitrary L>0.

## 6. A positive finite character law

Let d be any integer with 2^d>=n+1. In the (d+1)-bit label space use

    lambda_0=(0,binary(0)),
    lambda_i=(1,binary(i)), 1<=i<=n.

These labels do not permute the physical indices. Let s range over this
binary space, let e_sig have only its first bit equal to 1, and put

    D=2^(d+1),
    w_s=tau*1_(s=e_sig)+(1-tau)/D,
    (u_i)_s=sqrt(w_s)*(-1)^(s dot lambda_i).            (14)

All weights are positive and sum to one. Summing the binary characters
by pairing a differing bit gives

    <u_i,u_j>=tau*eta_i*eta_j+(1-tau)*1_(i=j).

This is the required full signed Gram, not a PSD-only existence claim:
positions, all values, all original residuals and F were supplied above.
The explicit anchor is simply X_0=u_0. On H_m one may take d=m,D=2N.
The least atom is (1-tau)/(2N).

## 7. Exact payoff and an associative physical block rule

Put

    r=tau^(n-1), H_tail=sum_(t=1)^(n-1)h_t*tau^(t-1).

Then A_n=q*r and P_n=q*H_tail. For fixed q, the largest permitted b in
(4) is

    b=q*r*(tau*a-q*(tau*H_tail+r)).                   (15)

When b>0, (13) has the unique minimizer just proved. Its normalized
terminal payoff is

    V=2f_n=2q*r*tau*a-q^2*r*(2tau*H_tail+r).

Completing the square in q gives the maximum, at

    q=tau*a/(2tau*H_tail+r),
    b=q^2*r*tau*H_tail>0,
    V_tau=tau^2*a^2*r/(2tau*H_tail+r).                 (16)

This is an algebraic formula, not a numerical parameter evaluation.

For a consecutive tail block p=(p_0,...,p_(k-1)), define

    alpha_p=tau^k,
    H_p=sum_(j=0)^(k-1)p_j*tau^j,
    J_p=sum_(j=0)^(k-1)p_j*tau^(2j).

If it starts at tail amplitude A, cumulative moment P, and value f, its
actual end state is

    A_out=alpha_p*A,
    P_out=P+A*H_p,
    f_out=f-A^2*(1-alpha_p^2)/2-tau^2*A^2*J_p.         (17)

For the physical concatenation p followed by qword,

    alpha_(p qword)=alpha_p*alpha_qword,
    H_(p qword)=H_p+alpha_p*H_qword,
    J_(p qword)=J_p+alpha_p^2*J_qword.                 (18)

These identities follow by splitting the defining sums at the actual
index k. They prove associativity without resetting P, A, or the enclosing
schedule parameters. All cross-block Q rows are already covered by
(7)--(12). The final boundary (4) prices the complete history. This is a
legal iterable rule for this restricted tail geometry, not an improving
primitive-capacity composition theorem.

There is an explicit reserve test when appending to a fixed existing
prefix. Write d_in=f-A^2/2. The inherited values remain unchanged, while

    d_out=d_in-tau^2*A^2*J_p.

A permitted append must have d_out>0 and

    A_out+d_out/A_out+tau*P_out<=tau*a.

With these tests, the enlarged transcript has the same form (5), with
b=d_out: splitting its future sum shows that every old value is exactly
its previous value. Thus the all-pair proof applies to the old and new
samples together. If d_out<0 the original optimum lower row fails; if
the displayed boundary fails, the original optimum upper row fails.
No claim is made that an arbitrary further block passes these paid tests.

Since tau*H_tail>=r*T, (16) also gives

    V_tau<=tau^2*a^2/(2T+1)<K_first_m.                       (19)

Thus even before the wider obstruction below, the exact block rule does
not improve the scalar first-cut lower bound.

## 8. Quantitative calibration on every original H_m

Choose tau=1-1/(4n). For n>=15,
1/tau<=60/59<31/25<ell, so (3) holds at every original tail step.
The character law's minimum atom is exactly 1/[8nN]. Since H_tail<=T
and r<=1, (16) and Bernoulli's inequality yield

    V_tau >= tau^(n+1)*K_first_m
           >=[1-(n+1)/(4n)]*K_first_m >=(11/15)*K_first_m.        (20)

For completeness the original benchmark comparison uses its exact mass
recurrences, not the physical mass as a substitute. The accepted joins are

    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt((u+v)^2+4uv))/2,
    G(u,v)=2u+v/2+sqrt(v^2+8uv)/2,
    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(k+l=n-1)Omega(C_k,C_l),
    B_n=max_(k+l=n-1)G(C_k,B_l).

Both joins are increasing and G>=Omega: after squaring the nonnegative
quantities 3u+sqrt(v^2+8uv) and sqrt(u^2+6uv+v^2), their squared difference
is 8u^2+2uv+6u*sqrt(v^2+8uv)>=0. Induction gives B_n>=C_n, and the
balanced primitive split gives B_(2^m-1)>=sigma^m.

Counting 2^(m-k-1) occurrences of level k in the actual word gives

    S=N-1+r_sum*(c^m-N),
    r_sum=delta/[c(c-2)], 0<r_sum<1.                  (21)

Here c>sigma>2, and c(c-2)>sigma(sigma-2)=1>delta. Hence
S<c^m-1 and 2T+1<2c^m<6sigma^m. The last inequality uses
(1+1/m)^m<3, obtained by the binomial expansion and sum 1/k!<3.
Finally a=(sqrt(2)-1)(m-1)/(m+1)>6/25 for m>=4. Therefore

    B_n*V_tau >(11/15)*a^2/6
              >396/56250 >1/150.                    (22)

This proves a fully realized, quantitatively priced signed construction
on every original enclosing horizon, while (19) records its limitation.

## 9. Arbitrary amplitudes: an original tail-pair restriction

We now return to the ENTIRE class (1), with arbitrary amplitudes, values,
anchor, and free terminal. Set k=n-1, so the last queried sample is k.
Normalize using the true closest-minimizer distance as in Section 1.

For 1<=i<j<=k, add Q_ij and Q_ji. The accepted necessary inequality is

    <g_i-g_j,X_i-X_j> >= ||g_i-g_j||^2.

Its LEFT side is exactly

    h_i*A_i*(A_i-tau*A_j)
      +tau*(A_i-A_j)*sum_(t=i+1)^(j-1)h_t*A_t.        (23)

If A_j>=A_i/tau, both terms in (23) are nonpositive. The right side is
A_i^2+A_j^2-2tau*A_i*A_j>0 because 0<tau<1 and both amplitudes are
positive. This contradiction proves

    A_i>tau*A_j, 1<=i<j<=k.                           (24)

No nonnegative-history simplification was made across the initial sample.
The assertion is only within the tail where its pair correlations are
actually positive.

## 10. The true anchor and a free terminal: a sharp limiting upper bound

Write A_0=||g_0||. Optimum cocoercivity gives
<X_0,g_0>>=A_0^2, and A_0<=||X_0||=1. Set z=<X_0,u_0>, so z>=A_0.
Resolve the unit vector u_k=-tau*u_0+sqrt(1-tau^2)*v with v perpendicular
to u_0 and ||v||=1. Then

    <X_0,u_k> <= -tau*z+sqrt(1-tau^2)*sqrt(1-z^2).

The right side is decreasing for 0<=z<=1, so it is at most its value at
z=A_0. Put T_pre=sum_(t=1)^(k-1)h_t=T-ell. The original optimum row at k,
including the negative contribution of g_0 and every positive tail term,
therefore gives, using (24),

    f_k <= A_k[tau*a*A_0+sqrt(1-tau^2)*sqrt(1-A_0^2)]
                               -(tau^2*T_pre+1/2)A_k^2.

Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the bracket by

    M_tau=sqrt(tau^2*a^2+1-tau^2).

The actual final step has length ell<2. Smoothness at X_k gives

    f_n<=f_k-ell*(1-ell/2)*A_k^2.

Maximizing the resulting quadratic in A_k proves the uniform class bound

    2f_n <= U_angle(tau)
      :=[tau^2*a^2+1-tau^2]
                    /[1+2tau^2*T_pre+ell*(2-ell)].    (25)

This does not impose any law on g_n. Its initial norm was the TRUE radius,
and neither a translated reset nor an unrecorded anchor adjustment occurs.
Relative to the first-cut payoff, (25) implies

    U_angle(tau)/K_first_m
      <=[1+(tau^(-2)-1)/a^2]
                     *(1+2T)/(1+2T-ell^2).           (26)

In particular, as tau tends to 1 this ratio tends to 1 uniformly over m
because a>6/25, ell<3/2 and T>=n-1.

## 11. Small correlations: a priced moment bound on the actual tail

There are M=n-1 tail queries 1,...,k. For consecutive tail samples, the
original reverse interpolation inequality reads

    f_i-f_(i+1) >= (A_i^2+A_(i+1)^2)/2
                          +tau*(h_i-1)*A_i*A_(i+1)
                    >= (A_i^2+A_(i+1)^2)/2.           (27)

At each tail sample, the optimum row and the actual displacement from X_1
give

    <X_1,g_i> >= f_i+A_i^2/2.

All added terms in this last relation are tau*h_t*A_i*A_t>=0 for
1<=t<i. Write b_tail=f_k-A_k^2/2>=0. Summing (27) gives

    <X_1,u_i> >= [b_tail+sum_(j=i)^k A_j^2]/A_i >0.   (28)

For real coefficients t_i, (1) gives the elementary Gram estimate

    ||sum_(i=1)^k t_i*u_i||^2
       =(1-tau)sum_i t_i^2+tau*(sum_i t_i)^2
       <=[1+(M-1)tau]*sum_i t_i^2.

Apply Cauchy--Schwarz with t_i=<X_1,u_i>. It follows that

    sum_i <X_1,u_i>^2 <=[1+(M-1)tau]||X_1||^2.        (29)

The original first step costs no hidden radius: since ell<2 and
<X_0,g_0>>=A_0^2,

    ||X_1||^2<=1-ell*(2-ell)*A_0^2<=1.

The scalar elimination proved in accepted `0e7e78056dc6258c`, proof
Section 5, applies to (28)--(29): if q_i=A_i^2 and T_i=b_tail+sum_(j>=i)q_j,
it bounds 2f_k by beta_(M-1) times the upper budget for sum T_i^2/q_i.
Here beta_j=4/[1+sqrt(1+2c_j)]^2, c_0=0,
c_(j+1)=c_j+2+2sqrt(c_j+1), with beta_j<=2/j^2 for j>=1.
The actual last step cannot increase f. Hence

    2f_n <= [1+(n-2)tau]*beta_(n-2)
           <= 2[1+(n-2)tau]/(n-2)^2.                 (30)

This is an elementary extension with its full Gram cost written out.
No orthogonality of these actual tail gradients is asserted.

## 12. Intermediate correlations: exact adjacent ratios

For two consecutive tail queries the same cocoercivity inequality gives

    (h_i-1)A_i^2-A_(i+1)^2
                    +(2-h_i)tau*A_i*A_(i+1)>=0.

For z>0 define the positive root

    r_tau(z)=[-tau*(z-1)+sqrt(tau^2*(z-1)^2+4z)]/2.

Then A_(i+1)/A_i<=r_tau(h_i-1). The root obeys r_tau(z)>tau and is
strictly increasing in z. A convenient exact formula, with natural log,
is

    phi_tau(x):=log r_tau(exp x)
       =x/2-asinh(tau*sinh(x/2)).                     (31)

Indeed divide r^2+tau(z-1)r-z=0 by r*sqrt(z) and solve the resulting
hyperbolic-sine identity. Thus phi is odd, phi(0)=0, and

    phi'(x)=1/2-tau*cosh(x/2)
                              /[2sqrt(1+tau^2*sinh^2(x/2))]>0,
    phi''(x)=-tau*(1-tau^2)*sinh(x/2)
                              /[4(1+tau^2*sinh^2(x/2))^(3/2)]. (32)

The derivative positivity follows by squaring: the denominator under its
square root exceeds tau^2*cosh^2(x/2) by 1-tau^2. On x>0, phi is
strictly concave. These formulas also prove r_tau(z)>tau by its limit
as z decreases to zero and strict monotonicity.

The first queried norm is bounded without assuming it shares a positive
correlation. Write d=g_1-g_0. Cocoercivity and X_1-X_0=-ell*g_0 give
-ell*<g_0,d>>=||d||^2, whence

    ||g_1||^2<=||g_0||^2+(1-2/ell)||d||^2<=||g_0||^2<=1.

Define the product over ALL original steps

    P_all=product_(t=0)^(n-1) r_tau(h_t-1).

The first and last physical steps both have excess a. Multiplying only
the legitimate tail inequalities i=1,...,n-2 therefore gives

    A_k <= P_all/r_tau(a)^2 <= tau^(-2)*P_all.         (33)

This product does not assume any condition on the free terminal gradient.

## 13. Ruler counts create a uniform strict product loss

Put Lc=log c. Since the physical excess at level j is delta*c^(j-1)
with delta<1, monotonicity in (31) and the original counts give

    log P_all
      <=(N/2)[-phi(Lc)+sum_(j=2)^(m-1)2^(-j)*phi((j-1)Lc)].

Concavity and phi(0)=0 imply phi(r*Lc)<=r*phi(Lc) for integer r>=1.
Keep the strict deficit at j=3 separately and write

    Delta_tau(c)=2phi(Lc)-phi(2Lc)>0.

The finite identity sum_(j=2)^(m-1)(j-1)/2^j=1-m/2^(m-1) yields

    log P_all <= -m*phi(Lc)-(N/16)*Delta_tau(c).        (34)

This retains all original levels and their actual multiplicities.

For an explicit bound, c>=sigma>2 and c<4 for m>=4. Hence
Lc>1/2 and cosh(Lc)<5/2. The identity

    Delta_tau(c)=integral_(t=0)^Lc integral_(s=t)^(t+Lc)
                                           [-phi''(s)] ds dt

contains the rectangle Lc/2<=t<=Lc, Lc<=s<=3Lc/2. On this rectangle,
sinh(s/2)>1/4, and
(1+tau^2*sinh^2(s/2))^(3/2)<=cosh(Lc)^3<125/8.
Its area is Lc^2/4>1/16. Substitution into (32) proves

    Delta_tau(c)>=tau*(1-tau^2)/4000
                         >=tau*(1-tau)/4000.          (35)

For clarity Lc>1/2 follows from log 2=integral_1^2 dt/t>1/2;
the other bounds are direct inequalities, not numerical evaluation.
Combining (33)--(35), and dropping the nonpositive -m*phi(Lc), gives

    A_k <=tau^(-2)*exp[-N*tau*(1-tau)/64000].

Finally retain the signed original displacement in the optimum row:

    f_k<=<g_k,X_k>
       =<g_k,X_0>+ell*tau*A_0*A_k
                    -tau*A_k*sum_(t=1)^(k-1)h_t*A_t
       <=(1+ell*tau)*A_k <=(5/2)*A_k.

The final physical step is again nonincreasing for f. Thus the entire
class with free terminal satisfies

    2f_n <=5tau^(-2)*exp[-N*tau*(1-tau)/64000].         (36)

This closes fixed correlations bounded away from 0 and 1 exponentially.
It does not discard the regime tau tending to either endpoint.

## 14. Uniform control of every horizon-dependent correlation

Accepted `04219554e41d9750` gives

    sigma^(-m)*B_(2^m-1) -> Z_1 in (0,infinity).

Hence B_(2^m-1)=O(N^rho), rho=log_2(sigma)<3/2.
Split ALL tau in (0,1) into three exhaustive ranges.

* If tau<=N^(-1/2), (30) is at most
  2(1+sqrt(N))/(N-3)^2. Multiplied by B_n, this tends to zero.
* If N^(-1/2)<=tau<=1-N^(-1/2), then
  tau*(1-tau)>=(1/2)N^(-1/2), and tau^(-2)<=N.
  Equation (36) is at most 5N*exp[-sqrt(N)/128000].
  Its product with B_n also tends to zero.
* If tau>=1-N^(-1/2), (26), a>6/25, ell<3/2 and T>=n-1 give

       2f_n <=[1+o(1)]*K_first_m,                           (37)

  where the o(1) is uniform over this full range. Explicitly its
  multiplicative factor is bounded by

       [1+((1-N^(-1/2))^(-2)-1)/(6/25)^2]
                       *(1+2T)/(1+2T-9/4),

  which tends to 1.

Consequently the supremum over the entire class has

    limsup B_n*V_best_m <= lim B_n*K_first_m,                     (38)

once the limit on the right is evaluated below. No interchange of a
nonuniform pointwise limit with the supremum was made; the three estimates
are uniform over their respective ranges.

## 15. Attainment of the limiting class strength and its original-B value

For the explicit construction choose instead tau_m=1-1/n^2. Condition
(3) holds on every H_m, since 1/tau_m<=225/224<31/25<ell. Moreover
tau_m^(n+1)->1, r=tau_m^(n-1)->1, and (16),(19),(20)'s first inequality
give the squeeze

    tau_m^(n+1)*K_first_m <= V_(tau_m) <= K_first_m.

Thus V_(tau_m)/K_first_m tends to 1. This construction is in the queried class
(1) and supplies a legal terminal, so V_best_m>=V_(tau_m).

In (21), r_sum tends to 1, (2/sigma)^m tends to zero, and
c^m/sigma^m=(1+1/m)^m tends to e. Therefore

    T/sigma^m -> e,  a -> 1/sigma,
    B_n*K_first_m -> Z_1/[2e*sigma^2].                      (39)

Equations (38)--(39) and the construction squeeze prove (2).

The strict numerical comparison in (2) needs no computation. In the
accepted ray enclosure, use b=1,j=0. Its UPPER endpoint involves B_1
(not B_0), so B_1=G(1,1)=4 gives

    Z_1 <= (sqrt(B_1)+3/100)^2 = 41209/10000.

Since e>2 and sigma^2=3+2sqrt(2)>29/5,

    Z_1/[2e*sigma^2]
       < (41209/10000)/(116/5)
       =206045/1160000 <1/5.

The ray theorem is used only in its unconditional scalar part. No
four-step seed existence is assumed anywhere in this argument.

## 16. Scope, an actual uncovered freedom, and failed extrapolations

This result closes the one-initial-sign CONSTANT-CORRELATION class (1),
including arbitrary amplitudes, values, initial anchors, horizon-dependent
tau, and a free terminal. It includes the queried geometry of the C91
dense lift but does not use C91 as a proof premise. It does not close
general signed character laws, nonconstant magnitudes of correlations,
more than one chronological sign reversal, or the changed affine-child
geometry pursued by max.

Multiple sign reversals are an actual legal freedom on the SAME original
schedule. For example put

    kappa=(1+1/ell)/2, F_quad(x)=kappa*x^2/2, x_0=1.

Then 0<kappa<1, kappa*h_0=(ell+1)/2>1, and h_1>ell gives kappa*h_1>1.
Thus the first three nonzero gradients have signs +,-,+, outside (1).
For the complete original word its exact data are

    x_i=product_(t<i)(1-kappa*h_t),
    g_i=kappa*x_i, f_i=kappa*x_i^2/2,
    Q_ij=-kappa*(1-kappa)*(x_i-x_j)^2/2<=0

including the optimum. Its single static function has unique minimizer 0,
true radius 1, and actual payoff
kappa*product_(t<n)(1-kappa*h_t)^2. This is an explicit scope check only;
no favorable asymptotic payoff is claimed. In (23), its intervening
signed contributions would not have the two nonpositive signs used there.

The next missing object is a quantitative multiple-sign or nonconstant-
correlation boundary rule, or another legal geometry improving the
underlying trajectory, with every original cross pair and true radius.
A covariance matrix, a relabeling without value constraints, or optimizing
tau inside (1) cannot provide that improvement. The current exact block
rule is iterable but has the completely priced ceiling (2).

For coordination, the construction's full interface is: the signed Gram
(14), anchor X_0=g_0, values (5), actual positions in Section 2, boundary
(4), state update (17), and all cross-pair identities (7)--(12). It has
active reverse tail pairs and both optimum rows active at sample 0; it
does not have C91's strict margin on every distinct pair. No insertion
into a different child word is licensed without matching these data.

All statements in this manuscript remain a joint author proof draft.
No verifier acceptance, original-target answer, resource renewal, or extra
runtime round is inferred.

evidence:
# Every finite delay: exact value pricing and complete redundancy

Status: UNVERIFIED complete joint proof draft, max2 round26.
TASK.md and master_guidance6e0a18d700dcd62f prohibit fact_submit.
Nothing in this document is an accepted fact. No numerical/model scan,
solver, machine algebra, replay, installation or subordinate agent was used.

Accepted inputs: fact04219554e41d9750 Section10 for the ORIGINAL
primitive identity and its full formal-gradient certificate interface;
fact1252b8823bb5a290 proof paragraphs1--2 for the interpolation convention
and constructive sufficiency. Every other calculation is proved jointly
below. The earlier immediate-annihilation draft cc0fc35f2fb5d6bb is
awareness, not a predecessor or an assumed lemma.

Sections1--7 first prove a family with TWO negative fast samples before
annihilation, including its exact three-path price and a polynomial
budget. Section9 then proves the stronger final result: ANY finite
negative excursion after a reversal at ANY index, followed by
annihilation, is redundant under the stated global and local prefix
bounds. For killing step b<=2 the local bounds are automatic. Thus this
final scope is not limited to an initial reversal, two negative samples,
or the previous immediately annihilated family. Its entire
parameter-and-value minimum is decided, not merely its price formula.

The proof supplies one static attaining smooth convex function, every
directed finite and optimum inequality, the complete minimizer set and
true distance, all coincident-point boundaries, and all zero-step indices.
It does not decide the general full cone or the original exact-profile
target. The verifier gate stays closed.

## 1. Family, exact minimum and complete comparison

Fix an integer n>=3 and a nonnegative finite word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)).
Write P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, s=P_n and C=1+s. Assume

    h_0=r, h_1=c, h_2=b,
    1<=b<=r<=2, 0<=c<=b,
    h_i<=P_i+2 for every i<n.                       (1)

No bound on n or on the total tail mass is imposed. In particular the
case n=4 retains the original five formal gradients at arbitrary
capacity allowed by(1); capacity C is not frozen to a sample value.

Choose d>=1, amplitudes u_1,...,u_d,v>=0 and curvatures satisfying

    beta=1/b, 0<alpha_q<beta,
    alpha_q*h_i<=1 for every i<n and 1<=q<=d.

Set

    p_(0,q)=1, p_(i,q)=product_(t<i)(1-alpha_q*h_t),
    m=r/b-1, theta=1-c/b,
    z_0=1, z_1=-m, z_2=-m*theta, z_i=0 for i>=3,
    x_i=(u_q*p_(i,q) for1<=q<=d, v*z_i),
    g_i=(alpha_q*u_q*p_(i,q) for1<=q<=d, beta*v*z_i). (2)

These samples obey every GD update x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_i. Before values
are varied they are samples of the SINGLE fixed diagonal quadratic

    F_base(x)=sum_q alpha_q*x_q^2/2+beta*x_(d+1)^2/2.

Thus no Hessian switching or gluing of independently chosen jets is
assumed. Every slow coordinate is nonnegative and nonincreasing. If
r>b, v>0 and 0<c<b, the fast mode is positive at0, negative and nonzero
at1 and2, and first zero at3. This is genuine delayed annihilation.

Define the nonnegative slack weights and the first three slow gaps by

    U_q=alpha_q*(1-alpha_q)*u_q^2/2,
    B=beta*(1-beta)*v^2/2,
    Delta_(i,q)=p_(i,q)-p_(i+1,q) for0<=i<n.

The three energy price increments are

    X26=4r*sum_q U_q*(Delta_(0,q)*Delta_(1,q)
                     +Delta_(0,q)*Delta_(2,q)
                     +Delta_(1,q)*Delta_(2,q)),
    Z26=4r*[sum_q U_q*Delta_(0,q)*Delta_(1,q)
                         +B*m*theta*(1+m*theta)],
    Y26=4r*B*[m+m^2*(1-theta+theta^2)].             (3)

Here X26 bypasses BOTH negative samples; Z26 visits the second negative
sample and bypasses the first; Y26 visits both chronologically in reverse.
They are increments above the sum of separate-mode optimal prices.

For a_(i,q)=alpha_q*u_q*p_(i,q) and
t_(i,q)=a_(i,q)-a_(i+1,q), put

    L_slow=sum_(q,i<n) P_(i+1)*t_(i,q)
               *[2(1+P_i)*a_(i,q)-P_(i+1)*t_(i,q)],
    K_neg=c^2*beta*(2-c^2*beta)
                   +(c+b)*(c+2-b)*theta^2,
    H_fast=beta^2*v^2*[r*(2-r)+m^2*K_neg].          (4)

For any scalar values f_i on(2), define the primitive energy

    V_h(f)=2sum_(i<n)h_i*(f_i-f_n)
       +sum_(i<n)h_i*(1-h_i)*||g_i||^2-s*(s+1)*||g_n||^2.

Among ALL values satisfying ALL ordered finite interpolation constraints,
the exact minimum is

    V_min=L_slow+H_fast-min(X26,Y26,Z26).           (5)

The same minimum holds when the fixed actual optimum jet(0,0,0) is
required. It is attained by the static function in Section6.

The full parameter comparison is

    L_slow>=X26+r^2*(2-r)*sum_q alpha_q^3*u_q^2,
    H_fast>=beta^2*v^2*r*(2-r),
    V_min>=r*(2-r)*[beta^2*v^2
                           +r*sum_q alpha_q^3*u_q^2]>=0. (6)

The first THREE terms of each slow-mode energy already cover its share
of X26. All subsequent terms are nonnegative. The comparison is uniform
over every permitted curvature, amplitude, tail and choice of legal
joint values, including values from nonseparable functions. Consequently
the ENTIRE displayed delayed-annihilation family imposes no additional
primitive condition beyond(1).

For r<2 and a nonzero initial vector, the final bound in(6) is strict.
For 1<b<r, 0<c<b, v>0 and at least one active slow mode with
alpha_q*r<1, all three quantities in(3) are positive. Thus incompatible
orderings really do create a strict positive joint price. Inequality(6)
decides its information content after full optimization.

## 2. Original orientation and the all-value problem

Keep every original index I={0,...,n}, including zero-step samples.
For distinct i,j set

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 gives both the necessity of Q_ij<=0 and its
constructive sufficiency with an optimum sample. Let Lambda_ij>=0,
Lambda_ii=0, e=(1,...,1)^T, and define

    L_flow=diag(Lambda*e)-Lambda,
    omega=(-2h_0,...,-2h_(n-1),2s)^T,
    T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, T_it=0 for t>i,
    D_prim=diag(h_i*(2-h_i) for i<n, -s*(s+2)).

The ORIGINAL sufficient primitive certificate is

    L_flow^T*e=omega,
    M_prim=D_prim+(L_flow*T+T^T*L_flow^T)/2 PSD on R^(n+1). (7)

Its full identity from accepted04219554e41d9750 is

    V_h(f)+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij*Q_ij
                        =<M_prim,Gram(g_0,...,g_n)>. (8)

The flow here is OUTGOING minus incoming. The terminal n is the source
of mass2s, and each i<n is a sink of mass2h_i. An auxiliary minimum-cost
flow below is not presumed to satisfy the PSD condition in(7).

For the base values f_i^0=F_base(x_i), direct expansion gives the
symmetric nonnegative slack costs

    w_ij=-Q_ij(f^0)
        =sum_q U_q*(p_(i,q)-p_(j,q))^2+B*(z_i-z_j)^2. (9)

Let d_i be the shortest path cost n->i in the complete finite graph
with these costs. The minimum exists over simple paths; nonnegative
costs allow the removal of every cycle even when some edges cost zero.
New values f_i^0+delta_i satisfy every directed inequality exactly when

    delta_i-delta_j<=w_ij for every distinct i,j.

Every path n->i implies delta_i-delta_n>=-d_i. Since h_i>=0,

    min_f V_h(f)=V_h(f^0)-2sum_(i<n)h_i*d_i.       (10)

All lower bounds are attained simultaneously by delta_i=-d_i: the
distance inequalities d_j<=d_i+w_ij verify EVERY directed constraint.

For any original prescribed flow, w_ij>=d_j-d_i and the flow equation
give

    sum Lambda_ij*w_ij>=-sum omega_i*d_i
                                =2sum_(i<n)h_i*d_i.

Send2h_i units along a shortest n->i path for each i with h_i>0.
This is a nonnegative original prescribed flow attaining equality.
Zero-weight vertices remain in the complete graph. This proves that
(10) is the exact ORIGINAL terminal-source price, not the reverse-flow
quantity. It also proves why this optimizing flow need not be PSD.

## 3. All shortest paths and the three competing increments

For ordered scalar positions p_0>=...>=p_n and squared-distance edge
costs U*(p_i-p_j)^2, the distance from n to i is

    U*sum_(k=i)^(n-1)(p_k-p_(k+1))^2.              (11)

Indeed an edge spanning several ordered gaps has cost at least the sum
of the squared gaps it spans. Every path between two ordered positions
crosses every intervening gap at least once. Summing these lower bounds
proves(11); the path through the consecutive ordered points attains it.
Zero gaps and tied positions satisfy the same proof.

In the separate fast scalar coordinate, the finite sampled positions
are1,-m,-m*theta,0 with possible repetitions. The shortest costs from
the zero terminal are

    d_0^fast=B,
    d_1^fast=B*m^2*[theta^2+(1-theta)^2],
    d_2^fast=B*m^2*theta^2,
    d_i^fast=0 for i>=3.                           (12)

Apply the same ordered-gap proof on each side of0. For the positive
target1, detouring through any negative position only increases cost.
For each negative target, detouring through the positive position only
increases cost. This also proves every equality in degenerate cases.

Let d_i^sep be the sum of(12) and all slow distances(11). Every joint
path costs at least the sum of the separate minima. For every i>=1,
the chronological path n,n-1,...,i simultaneously attains all those
separate minima, so

    d_i=d_i^sep for every i>=1.                    (13)

There is no assumption that the best paths to0 coincide across modes.
For a path whose last edge is k->0, the preceding cost is at least
d_k^sep, and this lower bound is attained by a path avoiding0.
Thus d_0=min_(k>=1)(d_k^sep+w_(k,0)).

Among k>=3 the best choice is k=3. The fast position is zero at every
such k. In each slow coordinate insert the intermediate points
k-1,...,3 into the last edge k->0. Splitting a nonnegative gap reduces
the sum of squared gaps, so

    d_k^sep+w_(k,0)>=d_3^sep+w_(3,0).

Therefore exactly three paths suffice: n,...,3,0; n,...,2,0; and
n,...,1,0. Their costs minus d_0^sep are respectively

    2sum_q U_q*(Delta_(0,q)*Delta_(1,q)
                +Delta_(0,q)*Delta_(2,q)
                +Delta_(1,q)*Delta_(2,q)),
    2sum_q U_q*Delta_(0,q)*Delta_(1,q)
                         +2B*m*theta*(1+m*theta),
    2B*[m+m^2*(1-theta+theta^2)].                  (14)

For the first line expand the square of the sum of three slow gaps.
For the second line the slow excess is the cross product of the first
two gaps; the fast excess is

## 4. Exact separate energies

For a slow scalar coordinate write a_i=alpha*u*p_i and

## 5. Three slow terms pay for the full delayed bypass

It suffices to consider one slow mode alpha,u. Write

    ell=1-r*alpha, tau=c/r, zeta=b/r,

All ell,tau,zeta belong to[0,1], and p_1=ell, p_2=ell*k.

Here ell,tau,zeta are held fixed when viewing D(r) as an affine

                                              +2(1-ell)*S>=2. (19)

At r=2, put A=6-2tau-2tau^2 and B_aux=6+4tau-2zeta*R. Since
zeta<=1, zeta*R<=2+tau and B_aux>=2+2tau. Expanding(18) gives

    D(2)=C_1*ell+C_2*ell^2+C_3*ell^3+C_4*ell^4+C_5*ell^5,

    C_2=tau*(1+tau)*A+zeta*R*a^2*B_aux

    C_3=2tau^2*(1+tau)^2+2zeta*R*a*tau*B_aux

    C_4=tau^2*zeta*(R*B_aux-2)+4zeta^2*R^2*a*tau,

    f_j'-f_K=alpha*u^2*(p_j^2-p_K^2)/2
                          -U*(p_j-p_K)^2,

or equivalently

    2(f_j'-f_K)/a_j^2
           =1+2(1/alpha-1)*q-(2/alpha-1)*q^2.

These temporary comparison values need not be interpolable; this step
is ONLY an algebraic bound on the cost of the explicit bypass path.
Actual attaining values have already been proved legal in9.1.

Split the energy of these comparison values at j and j+1. Restoring
the prefix terminal term contributes P(P+1)*a_j^2, the step r
contributes r*(1-r)*a_j^2, and the shift in value references contributes
2H_cut*(f_j'-f_K). The final gradient coefficient differs from that
of E_tail,alpha by-H_cut*(H_cut+2T_neg+1)*a_j^2*q^2. Combining them gives

    first_K_slow_terms-2H_cut*A_K,alpha
      =E_pre,alpha+E_tail,alpha+H_cut*a_j^2*J(q),
    J(q)=P+2-r+2q*[(1/alpha-1)
                              -(1/alpha+H_cut/2+T_neg)*q]. (39)

This also checks the prefix weights explicitly, instead of treating
the reversal as a new initial point without paying its earlier mass.

The function J is concave on the interval[0,q_bar], so it is at least
the smaller of its two endpoint values. The first is

    J(0)=P+2-r>=0.

For the second, use q_bar=(1-r*alpha)/(1+alpha*T_neg) to obtain

    J(q_bar)=P+2-r+2(r-1)*q_bar-H_cut*q_bar^2
            =(1-q_bar)*[P+2-r+H_cut*q_bar]>=0.     (40)

The equality uses H_cut-(P+2-r)=2(r-1). All its factors have the
required signs by the GLOBAL old prefix bound at the reversal.
There is a useful quantitative margin. Since q_bar<=1-r*alpha and
0<=r*alpha<=1, BOTH endpoints in(40) and J(0) are at least
r*alpha*(P+2-r). Concavity therefore gives

    J(q)>=r*alpha*(P+2-r).

Equations(38)--(40) prove

    L_alpha>=2H_cut*A_K,alpha
                   +H_cut*r*(P+2-r)*alpha^3*u^2*p_j^2.

This holds for EVERY permitted slow curvature. Summing over modes
proves the quantitative first inequality in(34). Since B_K=0, the
k=K path in(31) gives2H_cut*delta_cut<=X_all, proving ALL of(34).
Combining the same margin with(32) also gives the explicit bound

    V_min>=E_pos+E_neg+H_cut*(P+2-r)*
                 [(beta*v*z_j)^2+r*sum_q alpha_q^3*u_q^2*p_(j,q)^2]. (41)

For j=0 this recovers the strict initial bound(6) for EVERY finite
delay, without extending the degree-five polynomial calculation.

No number of intervening negative steps, amplitude optimization,
nonseparable choice of values, or choice among the competing crossing
paths can defeat this bound within(28)--(29). It is a complete
redundancy theorem for the entire newly stated family.

### 9.4 Final scope and the original four-step interface

The result includes every initial single reversal followed by an
arbitrarily delayed annihilation: then r<=2 by the global bound, so
b<=r<=2 and(29) is automatic. It also includes a reversal at ANY later
index with killing step b<=2, regardless of the size of r permitted
by r<=P_j+2. It includes further b>2 cases whenever the explicit
standalone negative-block bounds(29) hold.

For n=4, all possible reversal/killing locations satisfy0<=j<K-1<4.
In particular the previously open delayed middle pattern
h=(a,r,c,b), j=1, K=4 is covered whenever a<=b<=2, b<=r<=a+2,
0<=c<=b, together with the already stated global bounds. The genuinely
delayed interior has a<b, r>b and0<c<b. No capacity is held fixed:
C=1+a+r+c+b can lie in the high-capacity range C>=193/25.

Zero steps at any position, repeated fast or full points, earlier
annihilation on a boundary, vanished amplitudes, zero products and
unit curvature remain in the proof. Every ordered pair and all original
formal gradient coordinates are retained; no quotient of the ambient
R^5 certificate space has been taken. The original h/Lambda/exact-flow/
full-PSD problem of04219554e41d9750 is preserved.

The exact gain2H_cut*delta_cut can be positive, as the explicit
three-path interior of Section1 demonstrates. The budget(39)--(40)
shows why it supplies no new exclusion here. Modes nonzero at the
terminal, multiple reversals or multiple changing modes, and suffixes
failing(29) remain outside the final theorem. General full-cone seed
feasibility and the original asymptotic exact-profile target stay open.

All statements in this extension remain UNVERIFIED joint drafts.
No fact has been submitted or represented as verifier-accepted.

evidence:
# Two retained signed modes and a long step: complete scalar dominance

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof draft, max2 round29, first of the TWO
analytical rounds allocated after completed baseline28 by TASK.md and
master_guidance4226374d0649bf55. No formal-verifier allocation is open.
No numerical evaluation, scan, solver, machine algebra, replay,
installation, consult, or subagent was used. Nothing below is a new fact.

Accepted inputs:1252b8823bb5a290, proof paragraphs1--2, for the ordered
smooth interpolation convention;04219554e41d9750, Sections10--11, for
the original primitive identity and primitive composition identity.
Every additional ingredient is proved jointly below. No earlier
annihilation or retained-terminal draft is used as an accepted premise.

This is a complete dominance result for the explicit domain below,
including all joint values, amplitudes, and curvatures. Both modes are
retained and signed on an open domain and the second physical step is
strictly greater than2. There is a genuine positive joint value price.
That price adds no negative primitive-energy test beyond the COMPLETE
value-optimized scalar channel. A full original certificate is also
given for one below-threshold member, to prove the domain is not
already excluded by the older necessary conditions.

This does not give a threshold seed, prove a global no-seed theorem, or
decide the original exact-profile Goal. The goal's convention stays
W_n(h)=sup 2(f(x_n)-min f)/(L||x_0-x_star||^2), hence W=2R.

Notation: all new local letters a,b,c,d,alpha,beta,u,v,p_i,z_i,ell,m,
t,U_alpha,U_beta,e_i^theta,d_i^theta,r_i^theta,J_theta,X_i,Y_i,
E_tail,E_mix,j_min,Conj,A_i,MinHull,R_true,kappa,delta in this draft
mean their versions with suffix29. They do not redefine project
symbols with the same printed names. The schedule h, mass s, original
Q_ij, Lambda_ij, L_flow, T, D_prim and M_prim retain their stated roles.

## 1. Actual word, curvatures, amplitudes, and all signs

Fix a word in the domain

    h=(a,b,c,d),
    7/5<=a<=7/4,   2<b<=9/4,   0<=c,d<=a.                 (1)

Set s=a+b+c+d and C=1+s. These are variable, not a fixed-capacity
slice. Define

    beta_max=min({1} union {1/c:c>0} union {1/d:d>0}),
    1/b<=alpha<=1/a,      1/a<=beta<=beta_max,
    u,v>=0.                                               (2)

The beta interval is nonempty because c,d<=a and a>1. Negative initial
amplitudes give equivalent geometries by coordinate reflection, so
nonnegative u,v loses nothing. Both pure-amplitude endpoints are retained.

For i=0,...,4 define

    p_i=product_(0<=j<i)(1-alpha*h_j),
    z_i=product_(0<=j<i)(1-beta*h_j),
    x_i=(u*p_i,v*z_i),
    g_i=(alpha*u*p_i,beta*v*z_i).                          (3)

The empty products are1. These are the exact samples of ONE static,
convex, 1-smooth base function

    F_base(x,y)=alpha*x^2/2+beta*y^2/2.

The gradient-descent recursion is x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_i. All original
indices, including the terminal index4, are present.

Put ell=1-a*alpha and m=ell*(b*alpha-1). Then

    p=(1,ell,-m,-m*(1-c*alpha),
                         -m*(1-c*alpha)*(1-d*alpha)).      (4)

Thus ell,m>=0. Both tail factors lie in[0,1]. The fast samples obey

    z_1<=0,  z_2=(a*beta-1)*(b*beta-1)>=0,
    0<=z_4<=z_3<=z_2<=15/16<1.                            (5)

For the last bound, (a*beta-1)*(b*beta-1) increases for beta>=1/a:
its derivative is2ab*beta-a-b>=b-a>0. Hence it is at most
(a-1)*(b-1)<=(3/4)*(5/4)=15/16. The two beta-tail factors are
nonnegative by(2).

On the open domain with strict curvature endpoints, 0<c,d<1/beta,
and u,v>0, the slow signs are +,+,-,-,- and the fast signs are
+,-,+,+,+. Both modes survive to index4; neither is an early-killed
mode. This open set is nonempty even for the full-certificate word in
Section9. Curvature endpoints, c=0, d=0, and all product-zero cases
are included in(1)--(5). The limiting face b=2 obeys the same formulas,
although the selected family itself has b>2.

## 2. The original primitive interface and exact terminal-source price

For distinct i,j in{0,1,2,3,4}, use

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

All TWENTY ordered constraints Q_ij<=0 are imposed. The primitive
energy is exactly

    V=2sum_(i<4)h_i(f_i-f_4)
             +sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-sC||g_4||^2.   (6)

For the original full certificate retain all twenty Lambda_ij>=0,
zero diagonal, and define

    e=(1,1,1,1,1)^T,  L_flow=diag(Lambda*e)-Lambda,
    omega=(-2a,-2b,-2c,-2d,2s)^T,
    T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, T_it=0 for t>i,
    D_prim=diag(a(2-a),b(2-b),c(2-c),d(2-d),-s(s+2)).

Accepted04219554e41d9750 gives the exact identity

    L_flow^T e=omega,
    M_prim=D_prim+(L_flow*T+T^T*L_flow^T)/2,
    V+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij
                          =<M_prim,Gram(g_0,...,g_4)>.    (7)

A seed still requires M_prim positive semidefinite on ALL of R^5.
No coordinate, sign, pair, or zero-step formal gradient is deleted.

Write U_theta=theta*(1-theta)/2 for theta=alpha,beta. Substitution in
Q_ij at the base values gives the symmetric nonnegative slack

    w_ij=-Q_ij(F_base)
         =u^2 U_alpha(p_i-p_j)^2+v^2 U_beta(z_i-z_j)^2.    (8)

For arbitrary new values f_i=F_base(x_i)+epsilon_i the complete
constraint system is epsilon_i-epsilon_j<=w_ij. Let D_i be the
shortest w-cost from the ORIGINAL terminal source4 to node i in the
complete five-node graph, with D_4=0. A shortest simple path exists:
weights are nonnegative and cycles can be removed, including zero-cost
cycles. Following a path from4 to i gives epsilon_i-epsilon_4>=-D_i.
All h_i are nonnegative, so the simultaneous all-value minimum is

    V_min=V_base-2sum_(i<4)h_i D_i.                       (9)

It is attained by epsilon_i=-D_i. Indeed the distance triangle
inequality D_j<=D_i+w_ij proves every ordered residual is nonpositive.

The matching auxiliary flow sends2h_i units from4 to each i<4 along
an attaining path. Conversely w_ij>=D_j-D_i and(7)'s flow give
sum Lambda_ij w_ij>=2sum h_i D_i. This proves the exact price and its
terminal-source orientation. An optimal auxiliary price flow is not
asserted to be a full PSD certificate.

## 3. Scalar distances and energies: explicit formulas

For real points t_i on a line, the shortest path with squared-distance
edge weights from one sampled value to another consists of all sampled
values between them in monotone order, with ties allowed. Here is a
proof that also covers endpoints and equal values. List the distinct
ordered sampled values and their nonnegative adjacent gaps. The square
of any edge spanning several gaps is at least the sum of the squared
gaps it spans. Every path between the selected endpoints crosses every
gap between them at least once. Its cost is therefore at least the
sum of those squared gaps; the monotone path attains that sum. Excursions
outside the interval cannot improve it. Tied nodes add zero gaps and
remain valid original nodes.

For q_i=p_i or z_i define

    e_1(q)=(q_1-q_4)^2,
    e_2(q)=(q_2-q_3)^2+(q_3-q_4)^2,
    e_3(q)=(q_3-q_4)^2,
    e_4(q)=0.                                           (10)

For the slow coordinate, the complete order is

    p_2<=p_3<=p_4<=p_1<=p_0=1.

For the fast coordinate, it is

    z_1<=z_4<=z_3<=z_2<z_0=1.

Consequently the unweighted scalar distances from terminal4 are

    d_0^alpha=(1-p_1)^2+(p_1-p_4)^2,
    d_0^beta =(1-z_2)^2+(z_2-z_3)^2+(z_3-z_4)^2,
    d_i^alpha=e_i(p), d_i^beta=e_i(z),  i=1,2,3,4.         (11)

Define the base scalar energy for any q_i=product_(j<i)(1-theta*h_j)
by direct substitution into(6):

    B_theta=theta sum_(i<4)h_i[1+theta(1-h_i)]q_i^2
                      -s*theta[1+C*theta]q_4^2.          (12)

The exact all-value scalar minimum at that curvature and unit initial
amplitude is

    J_theta=B_theta-theta(1-theta)sum_(i<4)h_i d_i^theta,
                         theta=alpha or beta.            (13)

Equations(9)--(11), or the one-dimensional conjugate in Section8,
prove that this is attained by an actual scalar smooth convex function
with a minimizer. It is not just the energy of the original quadratic:
ALL scalar values have been optimized using ALL original pairs.

## 4. Exact joint distances and the four competing prices

For the four nodes1,4,3,2, both coordinates have the same monotone
node order, with opposite coordinate directions. The path along this
chain between any pair simultaneously attains both scalar shortest
distances. Node0 is outside the coordinate range of this chain in each
coordinate, so it cannot lower either scalar distance. Thus the joint
distances to i=1,2,3 are exactly

    D_i=u^2 U_alpha e_i(p)+v^2 U_beta e_i(z).              (14)

A shortest simple path to0 has a last chain node k in{1,4,3,2}.
Its prefix can be replaced by a shortest chain path, so exactly

    D_0=min_(k in{1,4,3,2})
       [u^2 U_alpha r_k(p)+v^2 U_beta r_k(z)],
    r_k(q)=e_k(q)+(1-q_k)^2.                             (15)

This argument examines every possible path; it does not assume that a
chronological path must remain shortest after a sign change.

Define the ENERGY price increments

    X_k=2a U_alpha[r_k(p)-d_0^alpha],
    Y_k=2a U_beta [r_k(z)-d_0^beta].                      (16)

They already include the original sink0 demand2a. All are nonnegative,
X_1=0, Y_2=0. Expanding differences of squares gives

    X_4=4a U_alpha(1-p_1)(p_1-p_4),
    X_3=X_4+4a U_alpha(p_4-p_3)(1-p_3),
    X_2=X_3+4a U_alpha(p_3-p_2)(1-p_2),

    Y_3=4a U_beta(z_2-z_3)(1-z_2),
    Y_4=Y_3+4a U_beta(z_3-z_4)(1-z_3),
    Y_1=Y_4+4a U_beta(z_4-z_1)(1-z_1).                   (17)

Hence0=X_1<=X_4<=X_3<=X_2 and0=Y_2<=Y_3<=Y_4<=Y_1.
The EXACT full all-value answer at all amplitudes and curvatures is

    V_min=u^2 J_alpha+v^2 J_beta
                  -min_(k in{1,4,3,2})(u^2 X_k+v^2 Y_k). (18)

On the strict open domain from Section1 with beta<1 and c,d>0, all
four candidates in the final minimum are positive for u,v>0. Thus the
joint price is strictly larger than the sum of the separate scalar
prices. The theorem below pays this actual positive price; it does not
pretend the coordinatewise minimizations are additive.

There is also an exact finite amplitude elimination. Normalize
u^2+v^2=1 and put lambda=u^2. For fixed alpha,beta the right side is
the maximum of the four affine lines

    L_k(lambda)=A_k+B_k lambda,
    A_k=J_beta-Y_k,
    B_k=(J_alpha-X_k)-(J_beta-Y_k).                       (19)

Its minimum on[0,1] is attained at0,1, or a pairwise intersection
lambda=(A_l-A_k)/(B_k-B_l) lying in[0,1], for B_k!=B_l. Evaluate
the maximum of ALL four lines at each candidate. Parallel or identical
lines create no missing candidate: a flat minimum interval has an
endpoint at an intersection or at0 or1. At most six intersections
and the two endpoints suffice. This covers amplitude-zero boundaries,
ties, and collapsed branches without a numerical optimization.

## 5. The retained slow mode pays the full price through node2

The quantitative estimate is

                 J_alpha-X_2>=41 alpha^2/576.             (20)

This is uniform over every word and curvature in(1)--(2), independent
of the other mode. The proof is given completely here.

First observe from(16) that J_alpha-X_2 is the scalar energy obtained
by using the route4->3->2->0 for sink0, the direct route4->1 for
sink1, and the usual monotone routes for sinks2,3. This route choice
is an UPPER bound on the scalar price, rather than its optimum.
Call the corresponding algebraic energy E_tail. Its value is allowed
to be below the scalar minimum; we prove even E_tail is positive.

Use theta=alpha, ell=1-a*theta, m=ell*(b*theta-1). After the first
two steps the scalar point is -m. Append a list of zero, one, or two
tail steps, each between0 and a. Let T_tail be its sum, s_tail=a+b+T_tail,
and let -t be its terminal point. For a tail index k let p_k be its
point just before that update, and T_k the tail sum up to and including
that update. Then direct telescoping gives

 E_tail=1-(1+s_tail*theta)^2 t^2
       -2theta(1-theta)[a(1+m)+b*ell*(ell+t)
                    +theta sum_(tail k)(a+T_k)h_k p_k^2]. (21)

Here is a derivation retaining every term. For any scalar sampled
values write f_i=x_i*g_i-g_i^2/2-A_i. Substitution in(6), followed by
x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_i, gives

    V=x_0^2-(x_end+s_tail*g_end)^2
                                      -2sum h_i(A_i-A_end).

For the specified route prices A_i=U_theta(p_i^2+d_i), A_end=U_theta*t^2.
For a negative monotone tail,

    p_i^2-t^2+d_i=2theta sum_(k>=i in tail)h_k p_k^2.

For index0 the same expression is2(1+m) plus the expression for
index2; for index1 it is2ell(ell+t). Collecting each tail update's
coefficient gives a+T_k. As2U_theta=theta(1-theta), these identities
prove(21), with no restriction on zero tail steps.

Now append one more tail step r in[0,a] at the old terminal point -y,
where y>=0, and write S for the old total mass. The new terminal
magnitude is y(1-r*theta). Subtracting(21) before and after the step
gives the EXACT increment

 E_new-E_old
  =theta^2*r*y^2{
      theta(S+r)[2(S+1)-theta*r*(S+r)]+2b(1-theta)}
       +2b*ell*y*theta^2*r*(1-theta).                    (22)

To check the terminal-square part, use
(1+(S+r)theta)(1-r theta)=1+S theta-r(S+r)theta^2.

## 2. The actual circular body and finite local construction

Fix beta in(0,1/4]. Define

    R_circ=1+beta, C_beta=beta+sqrt(1+2beta),
    p(q)=beta+sqrt(R_circ^2-(q+beta)^2), 0<=q<=1,
    v(q)=(p(q),-q),
    K_ctr=conv({0} union {v(q):0<=q<=1}).           (2.1)

The circular center is(beta,beta); its disk contains0 because
2beta^2<=(1+beta)^2. Thus its radial normals support this convex hull
on the displayed arc. The endpoints are(C_beta,0) and(beta,-1).
For every(p,-q) in K_ctr,

    0<=p<=C_beta, 0<=q<=1, p>=beta*q,
    (p,0) belongs to K_ctr.                         (2.2)

For any compact convex K containing0 put

    E_K(r)=max_(g in K){<g,r>-||g||^2/2}.             (2.3)

Completing the square identifies its unique maximizer as the Euclidean
projection Pi_K(r). Its characterization is

    <r-Pi_K(r),g-Pi_K(r)> <=0 for every g in K.       (2.4)

Adding this inequality at two points shows

The projection is therefore1-Lipschitz. Comparing the two maximizing
expressions in(2.3) gives the derivative Pi_K(r) and a remainder bounded
by ||s-r||^2. Hence E_K is convex, nonnegative, differentiable and1-smooth.
Its zero set is the polar cone of K: positive support in a direction
produces a positive value using a sufficiently small multiple of that
supporting vector, while nonpositive support makes0 the maximizer.
The cone of K_ctr is generated by its two nonzero endpoints, since

    (p,-q)=((p-beta*q)/C_beta)(C_beta,0)+q(beta,-1).

For sigma>0 it follows that

    E_(sigma K_ctr)(U,V)=0 iff U<=0 and beta*U<=V.   (2.5)

Use the one-sided Huber function

    Hub_delta(z)=0 for z<=0;
                 z^2/2 for 0<=z<=delta;
                 delta*z-delta^2/2 for z>=delta.    (2.6)

It is convex and1-smooth, with derivative min(delta,max(z,0)).

Here is a finite construction for the ACTUAL ordinary block H_J, with
its ordered steps h_1,...,h_N, N=2^J-1. Set alpha_i=h_i/2. Construct

       =max{ beta/(C_beta-beta),

and set

## 3. One static global function, every step, and its radius

For our identical ordinary blocks H_J, use the SAME u,y,M in both.
Put

    T_1=b_J/2-1, T_2=b_(J+1)/2-1,
    sigma_1=1/M, D_2=T_1/M,
    sigma_2=D_2/M, D_3=T_1*T_2/M^2,
    ell_2=y/M, ell_3=D_2*y/M,

    Phi_2(Y,Z)=E_(sigma_2 K_ctr)(Y-A_2,Z-ell_3),
    F(X,Y,Z)=(Phi_1(X,Y)+Phi_2(Y,Z)
                                      +Hub_delta(Z-ell_3))/2. (3.2)

The function is convex and1-smooth. To check the constant, the linear map

    Y^+=Y-h(P_2-Q_1)/2,

All components in this formula belong to the SAME static function.
During the first H_J and b_J the first pair follows(2.13)--(2.14);

and final Huber are zero there, so they do not change these updates.
The first checkpoint gives

    X<=A_1, Y>=beta*X,
    Y<=A_2, Z>=beta*(Y-ell_2),

The point x_star=(A_1,ell_2,0) belongs to(3.5). For any point of(3.5),

Every smooth-convex interpolation row follows from this actual function.

## 4. Exact tail dynamics and all terminal terms

Throughout the entire remaining H_L the third-coordinate excess is

where s' is the physical mass already traversed. This statement is an
exact trajectory identity, justified inductively: it keeps Q_2=0 by the
output-isolation property in Section2, so P_3=delta and the displayed
update continues. In particular the old second component has the exact
horizontal expression

    Phi_2(w,Z)=Hub_(C_beta*sigma_2)(w-A_2).          (4.2)

The first coordinate never increases by(3.3), and hence v<=A_1. For any
such v its projection lies on the sloped segment p=beta*q: for fixed q,
reducing p to beta*q increases the expression being maximized, since
v-A_1<=0 and p>=0. The segment is in K_ctr. Maximization along it gives

    Phi_1(v,w)=Hub_((1+beta^2)*sigma_1)(beta*v-w)/(1+beta^2). (4.3)

Put sigma=sigma_1, kappa_tail=1+beta^2, and cap_ratio=C_beta*D_2.
The exact dynamics for EVERY physical tail step h are therefore

    q=min(sigma,max(beta*v-w,0)/kappa_tail),
    r=min(cap_ratio*sigma,max(w-A_2,0)),
    v^+=v-h*beta*q/2,

    g=A_2-beta*v,
    g_in=ell_3/beta+beta^2*D_2>0,
    g^+=g+h*beta^2*q/2>=g.                         (4.5)

Thus q and r cannot be positive together. When the pair enters that
interval both vanish, the pair is stationary, and(4.1) keeps it decoupled
from the still evolving third coordinate. This is exact absorption.

                           +D_3^2/(2(1+S_L))]/R_true^2. (4.6)

term. Until absorption is proved, both old terms in(4.6) are retained.

## 5. A finite last-crossing absorption lemma

This is the comparison used in this round. It treats the true quadratic
caps, the moving interval and all large steps exactly. It is NOT a
continuous-time limit or an approximation by the total word mass.

Consider(4.4) on a finite recursive word H_L with positive step values
b_0,...,b_(L-1), for fixed sigma>0, cap_ratio>0, beta>0 and A_2. Suppose
its incoming state has w_in<A_2 and positive width g_in=A_2-beta*v_in.
Let

    P_j=sum_{h in H_j, h>=2} h,
    z_in=beta*v_in-w_in,
    kappa_tail=1+beta^2.                            (5.1)

Empty sums are0. Suppose the following FINITE inequalities hold:

    max(z_in,0) <= kappa_tail*sigma*P_L/2;          (5.2)
    sigma*(b_j-cap_ratio*P_j)/2 <= g_in,
                                     0<=j<L;       (5.3)
    sigma*(cap_ratio*b_j-kappa_tail*P_j)/2 <= g_in,
                                     0<=j<L.       (5.4)

Then the actual pair has entered its flat interval by the end of H_L.

Proof. If the incoming point is in the interval, absorption already holds.
Otherwise w_in<A_2 forces it to be on the left, with z_in>0. Assume for
contradiction that the terminal pair is active. Since a point in the closed
flat interval is absorbing, EVERY sample, including every post-step sample,
has then been strictly on the left or strictly on the right. There are
finitely many samples, so if a side change occurs it has a last occurrence.

While consecutive samples stay on the left, z=beta*v-w>0 evolves by

    z^+=z-h*kappa_tail*min(sigma,z/kappa_tail)/2.    (5.5)

If h>=2 and z<kappa_tail*sigma, the right side is(1-h/2)z<=0,
contradicting staying on that side. Consequently every such high step
has q=sigma and decreases z by h*kappa_tail*sigma/2. This also covers
the cap boundary; if it would land at0 that would be absorption or a
side change, which is excluded on a constant-side segment. Low steps
h<2 still cause nonnegative decrease. Likewise, on a constant right-side
segment, t=w-A_2>0 evolves by

    t^+=t-h*min(cap_ratio*sigma,t)/2,               (5.6)

so every h>=2 must have r=cap_ratio*sigma and decreases t by precisely
h*cap_ratio*sigma/2. This proves both necessary high-step mass losses
without neglecting any low step or near-boundary query.

If there is no side change, the whole H_L stays left, and(5.5) gives
z_in>kappa_tail*sigma*P_L/2, contrary to(5.2).

Otherwise let the last side change occur at a step of level j. Every
occurrence of b_j in H_L is immediately followed by a full H_j. This
follows by induction from H_(j+1)=(H_j,b_j,H_j): a node's right subtree
is read immediately after the node, before any ancestor or later subtree.
That complete following H_j lies in the original remaining tail.

For a left-to-right change, at the preceding sample write z=beta*v-w>0
and g=A_2-beta*v>=g_in. The new right margin satisfies exactly

    t^+=h*q/2-z-g < b_j*sigma/2-g_in.              (5.7)

By lastness of the crossing the following H_j remains strictly right.
Equation(5.6) therefore requires t^+>cap_ratio*sigma*P_j/2.
Combined with(5.7) this contradicts(5.3).

For a right-to-left change, at the preceding sample put t=w-A_2>0.
The left coordinate v is unchanged on this step, and the new left margin
satisfies

    z^+=h*r/2-t-g < b_j*cap_ratio*sigma/2-g_in.     (5.8)

The following H_j remains strictly left, so(5.5) requires
z^+>kappa_tail*sigma*P_j/2, contradicting(5.4).
All cases contradict terminal activity. The flat interval is reached,
which proves the finite lemma.

This proof is valid even if the gap increases substantially and if many
earlier crossings occurred. It does not compare two different words of
equal mass. The exact following-subtree property is indispensable.

## 6. Uniform control of the local backward data

We now derive the bounds needed to verify ALL inequalities(5.2)--(5.4)
uniformly over growing m. No prefix-to-infinite-composition exchange occurs.
For fixed beta write

    I_beta=sqrt(2)(1+beta)-beta<2,
    Y_beta=beta(exp(I_beta/beta)-1),
    U_beta=beta+(C_beta-beta)(Y_beta+beta)/beta.     (6.1)

For the finite backward trajectory in Section2 put
w_i=(y_i+beta)/(q_i+beta). At each uncapped point the radial equation is
u_i-beta=(p(q_i)-beta)w_i. Taking a cross product of(2.8) with
v(q_(i-1)) cancels the alpha_i term and gives

    w_(i-1)=w_i[1+
       (p(q_(i-1))*q_i-q_(i-1)*p(q_i))
            /{beta*(p(q_(i-1))+q_(i-1))}].         (6.2)

At a transition to q_(i-1)=0 this same formula follows from y_(i-1)=y_i;
if both q values are0 it is equality. Thus all endpoint cases are covered.
The numerator is

    integral_(q_(i-1))^(q_i)
                 [p(q_(i-1))-q_(i-1)*p'(t)] dt.

After dividing by p(q_(i-1))+q_(i-1), the integrand is a weighted mean
of1 and -p'(t), hence is at most max(1,-p'(t)). Multiplying(6.2), using
1+x<=exp(x) and w_N=1, gives

    y+beta <= (q_0+beta)
       exp(beta^(-1) integral_(q_0)^1 max(1,-p'(t))dt)
       <= beta exp(beta^(-1) integral_0^1 max(1,-p'(t))dt). (6.3)

For the second inequality, log(1+q_0/beta)<=q_0/beta and the integrand
is at least1. The derivative is
p'(t)=-(t+beta)/(p(t)-beta). It crosses -1 at
(1+beta)/sqrt(2)-beta. Integrating on the two sides yields exactly I_beta.
In particular

    1<=y<=Y_beta<=beta*exp(2/beta).                 (6.4)

For any q_i>0, the radial relation and y_i<=Y_beta imply u_i<=U_beta.
The steps with q_(i-1)>0 form one contiguous final part of the ordinary

    u=beta+C_beta*S/2-E_gap,
    0<=E_gap<=C_beta*(U_beta-beta)/beta
                       <=4 beta^(-1) exp(2/beta).  (6.5)

All other steps have q_(i-1)=0 and p=C_beta, so they contribute no gap

    K_bound(beta)=6 beta^(-1) exp(2/beta).          (6.6)

Combining M=u+y/beta with(6.4)--(6.5) proves

    |M-C_beta*S/2|<=K_bound(beta),
    |u-C_beta*S/2|<=K_bound(beta),

    K_bound(beta)<=(3m/4)exp(m/4)<=m(4/3)^m.        (6.8)

The last estimate follows from exp(1/4)<sum_(r>=0)(1/4)^r=4/3.

## 9. An elementary all-split scalar envelope and absolute deficit

This section is part of the same JOINT UNVERIFIED argument. Its
scalar bound is proved independently of saved numerical endpoints.
Set rho=log_2(lambda), p=rho/2 and kappa=62/25. One has p>5/8,
because lambda^4=17+12sqrt(2)>32 (use sqrt(2)>5/4).

First the following elementary power inequality holds:

    (25/31)x^(2p)+(1-x)^p<=1,
                0<=x<=1, p>=5/8.                   (9.1)

Increasing p can only decrease the left side, so consider

    psi(x)=(25/31)x^(5/4)+(1-x)^(5/8).

Its endpoint values are 1 and 25/31. An interior critical point obeys

    x^(1/4)(1-x)^(3/8)=31/50,
    x^2(1-x)^3=(31/50)^8.                           (9.2)

The function x^2(1-x)^3 decreases for x>=2/5. For x>=5/8,

    x^2(1-x)^3<=675/32768<21/1000
        <(147/1000)^2<(31/50)^8.                    (9.3)

The fixed rational comparisons use 675000<688128,
21000<21609, and
(31/50)^4=923521/6250000>147/1000 since 923521>918750.
Thus every interior critical point lies below 5/8.

At a critical point, the derivative equation makes

    psi(x)=(1-x/2)/(1-x)^(3/8)=:g(x).

The logarithmic derivative of g has the sign of 5x-2:

    g'(x)/g(x)=(5x-2)/[8(1-x)(2-x)].

Consequently its maximum on [0,5/8] is at an endpoint. Now g(0)=1
and g(5/8)<1, the latter being equivalent to

    11^8=214358881<226492416=27*2^23.

The continuous function psi attains a maximum either at an endpoint
or at such an interior critical point. This proves (9.1).
All these are displayed symbolic rational inequalities, not results
of an executed calculation or a numerical evaluation.

We also give the primitive power inequality rather than assume a
new recurrence fact. For positive a,b let A=a^(1/rho), D=b^(1/rho),
T=(A+D)^rho. Put E(t)=(1+t)^rho-1. The function
z -> log E(exp z) is convex: its second derivative is

    rho*t*(1+t)^(rho-2)
       *[(1+t)^rho-1-rho*t]/E(t)^2 >=0,  t=exp z,

because the bracket vanishes at zero and has positive derivative
for t>0. Convexity at opposite arguments gives

    E(t)E(1/t)>=E(1)^2=(lambda-1)^2=2.

It follows that (T-a)(T-b)>=2ab, or
T^2-(a+b)T-ab>=0. Since T is positive, it lies above the positive
root Omega(a,b). Zero arguments follow by continuity. Induction over
ALL original primitive splits therefore proves

    C_n<=(n+1)^rho.                                 (9.4)

We claim the corresponding dominant bound

    B_n<=kappa(n+1)^rho,              n>=0.          (9.5)

The case n=0 is 1<=kappa. In an arbitrary split at n>=1 put
A=k+1, D=n-k and N=A+D=n+1. By induction and (9.4), the two
arguments of G are at most A^rho and kappa D^rho. The function G
is increasing in both nonnegative arguments, directly from its formula.
Its value G(a,b) is the square of the positive root v of
v^2-sqrt(b)v-2a=0. Therefore it is at most T=kappa N^rho if

    2A^rho+kappa D^(rho/2)N^(rho/2)<=kappa N^rho.

On dividing by kappa N^rho, this is exactly (9.1) with x=A/N
and p=rho/2, since 2/kappa=25/31. It holds for EVERY split, so
taking their original maximum proves (9.5), without balancing or
deleting any split. In particular, (1.1) gives

    Z_1<=62/25.                                    (9.6)

Write C=beta+sqrt(1+2beta), R_circle=1+beta, kap=1+beta^2.
In coordinates (p,-q), the FULL convex body is
K={0<=q<=1, beta*q<=p, (p-beta)^2+(q+beta)^2<=R_circle^2}.
Its boundary consists of the segment from 0 to (C,0), the segment
from 0 to (beta,-1), and the circular arc connecting their far endpoints.
The displayed disk intersects those two half-planes in exactly the
horizontal sections beta*q<=p<=beta+sqrt(R_circle^2-(q+beta)^2).

For any centered normalized input w=(r,s), its projection is w if
w belongs to K. Otherwise a nearest boundary point is among:
(clip(r,0,C),0); (beta*t,-t), t=clip((beta*r-s)/kap,0,1);
and the radial point (beta,beta)+R_circle*(w-(beta,beta))/||w-(beta,beta)||
when that point lies on the stated arc. These are the exact nearest
points on the two segments and on the arc whenever the latter has an
interior stationary minimum; remaining arc minima are endpoints already
included. Choose the candidate maximizing <g,w>-||g||^2/2.
The production implementation can return the radial disk projection
directly when it belongs to the arc, since K is a subset of that disk.

The full support function at d=(d_x,d_y) is the maximum of
0, C*d_x, beta*d_x-d_y, and

                         +h_i[nu_j+sum_(v<=i)K_jv], i<j. (3)

are present: their diagonal contribution is included through (1), while
they create no x_0 mixed term. Half the incident mass at i equals
out_i-1_(i=n). Forward position terms subtract h_i K_iv from the source
diagonal; difference squares and both prefix position terms give (3).

    X=sum_i xiCert_i,
    E=sum_i(1+Ppos_i)xiCert_i,
    Hprice=sum_i(2S-Ppos_i)xiCert_i=D X-E,
    delta=zeta-1>0, q=zeta/D.

Summing (1) gives sum nu_i=2+X. Its position-weighted sum gives
sum K_ij(Ppos_i-Ppos_j)=2S-sum(nu_i-xiCert_i)Ppos_i.
Expanding the common-gradient polynomial consequently yields

    e^T Cgrad e=D+E.                                  (5)

Use the explicit one-sided Huber function Hub_1(z), equal to zero for
z<=0, z^2/2 on [0,1], and z-1/2 for z>=1. It is convex and 1-smooth.
Starting at D gives x_i=D-Ppos_i>=S+1>=1 at every query.
The actual scale-D Huber transcript is x_0=D, g_i=1,
f_i=D-Ppos_i-1/2. Its finite and outgoing optimum rows have residual
zero; its incoming residual is -(2S-Ppos_i). Hence exactly

    M(D,e)=delta D-Hprice.                            (6)

Necessary WHOLE-word Huber expenditure is Hprice<=delta D.
Since Ppos_i<=S, Hprice>=S X and X<=delta D/S when S>0.
This is not a renewable allowance for each child or outgoing row.

The full common-gradient/initial-point restriction is

    M(x_0=r,g=t e)=q r^2-(2+X)r t+(D+E)t^2.            (7)

Its exact PSD condition is

    zeta >= D(2+X)^2/[4(D+E)].                         (8)

It retains the changed outgoing mass2+X and can be stronger than (6).

The complete common-gradient derivative is

    2(csum)_i=2h_i+xiCert_i+h_i sum_(t>i)xiCert_t
       +(1+Ppos_i)nu_i+sum_j K_ij(Ppos_i-Ppos_j).       (9)

For finite rows the source derivative is the last term. Their physical
position derivative is h_i times later finite-node flow. Adding later
outgoing optimum contributions makes that sum 2+sum_(t>i)xiCert_t;
the incoming square contributes xiCert_i. This proves (9), including
the original terminal coordinate h_n=0.

For arbitrary incoming support put

    Acommon=[[q,-(2+X)/2],[-(2+X)/2,D+E]],
    DeltaCommon=q(D+E)-(2+X)^2/4.

If DeltaCommon>0, write the scalar gradient vector uniquely as t e+v,
e^T v=0. Its coupling to (x_0,t) is
l(v)=(-nu^T v/2,csum^T v). Exact expenditure on an arbitrary direction is

    Price(v)=l(v)^T Acommon^(-1)l(v)
      =[(D+E)(nu^T v)^2/4
          -(2+X)(nu^T v)(csum^T v)/2
          +q(csum^T v)^2]/DeltaCommon.                (10)

Under DeltaCommon>0, full original-space PSD is equivalent to the stated
positive definiteness of Acommon
and v^T Cgrad v>=Price(v) for EVERY v in e-perp. This is an invertible
decomposition retaining all coordinates, not a selected quotient theorem.
If DeltaCommon=0, the coupling must annihilate Acommon's kernel and the
semidefinite Schur condition remains necessary; no singular direction is
silently removed.

For zero incoming mass let

    dcontact=csum-D nu/2, e^T dcontact=0.

Then DeltaCommon=delta and (10) is exactly

    Price(v)=(csum^T v)^2/D
                       +(dcontact^T v)^2/[D(zeta-1)]. (11)

Thus relaxed q does NOT force dcontact=0. The contact-defect square spends
1/[D(zeta-1)] on the entire transverse space. At the tight level zeta=1
the coupling would force zero defect; importing that kernel at larger q
would improperly discard allowed constructions. A fixed negative direction
of Cgrad at x_0=0 is nevertheless unaffected by any q.

Equations(1)–(11) are full necessary conditions and exact square-completion
identities, jointly UNVERIFIED here. They are not an accepted intermediate
or an unrestricted W upper.

The screened words require an ORIGINAL full objective certificate, not a
matrix involving only three block endpoints. For one chosen X and every

## 6. General balanced-circulation contact obstruction

This calculation is not limited to the rank-product law. Let J_ij>=0
be ANY zero-diagonal finite-node array with equal row and column sums
at every node. On ANY finite nonnegative word define

    R_J(g)=sum_(i!=j)J_ij[<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2].

Its value terms cancel by balance and its x_0 terms cancel in position
differences. Let C_J be its full symmetric gradient matrix. At common
gradients, R_J(e)=0. Its row-sum vector satisfies

    (C_J e)_i=(1/2)sum_j J_ij(P_i-P_j),
    P^T C_J e=(1/4)sum_(i,j)J_ij(P_i-P_j)^2.         (33)

For the first equality, the derivative of the source gradient gives
sum_j J_ij(P_i-P_j). The derivatives of the positions cancel because
row and column masses agree. The difference-square derivative vanishes
at e. Divide the derivative by2. For the second equality, expand the
sum of squared differences and use balance to equate the P_i^2 and
P_j^2 sums. This proves both equalities directly without invoking a
graph theorem.

It follows that C_J e=0 if and only if every positive J_ij joins
equal P_i and P_j. Necessity follows from the nonnegative sum in(33);
sufficiency follows from its first equality. With nonnegative h,
P_i=P_j means all intervening steps are zero, hence x_i=x_j as a
FORMAL identity even with independent gradients. In this case

    R_J(g)=(1/2)sum J_ij||g_i-g_j||^2 >=0.           (34)

Conversely, if some positive edge has unequal physical prefixes,
C_J e!=0 while e^T C_J e=0. Taking v=C_J e and expanding
R_J(e+t v)=2t||C_J e||^2+t^2 v^T C_J v shows a negative value
for sufficiently small negative t. Thus C_J is not PSD. In particular,
on a strictly positive word EVERY nonzero nonnegative balanced finite
circulation is an indefinite correction, despite exact value balance.

Moreover no collection of such additions can cancel its physical-
prefix contact work: the right side of(33) is additive and nonnegative.
At an exactly contacting base with zero incoming optimum rows and
q=1/D, the common kernel condition forces C_J e=0. Hence no nonzero
nonnegative finite circulation preserves full PSD at that exact level
on a positive word. This is NOT a statement at q>1/D, about signed
changes with paid decrements, about changed optimum profiles, or about
arbitrary full certificates. The explicit paid test in the next
section is needed to exclude our concrete laws at larger q.
