# Tail-weighted full squares and an explicit balanced first-row repair

JOINT UNVERIFIED analytical report, worker max, invocation83.
Original exact-profile minimax problem OPEN. No new fact or verifier verdict.

This is one joint derivation, not a sequence of accepted intermediate facts.
TASK.md and master_guidance a16df0f0aca7349e permit ONE invocation and at
most TWO substantive coefficient laws. They forbid mathematical programs,
numerical evaluations, arithmetic/trajectory/recurrence replays, solvers,
formal calls/fact_submit, installations, consults and subagents. All those
counts remain zero. All scalar inequalities below are textual mathematics.

## 1. Outcome and exact scope

The exact suffix-product scale is retained in BOTH the nonisotropic detail
metric and the actual terminal distribution. Every original queried gradient,
the actual unqueried terminal gradient, and the initial vector remain
independent. The two explicit laws use the same weighted full square and
distributed imbalance, but genuinely different original coefficient arrays.

Law A uses the canonical weighted skew for that imbalance. Throughout its
entire domain, its incoming optimum multiplier at original query1 is
negative. Independently, making its first-to-last queried multiplier
nonnegative forces its exact global square charge above the assigned
qtar=17/(16D). This quantifies why paying through an exponentially tiny
initial tail weight fails in this particular matching.

Law B adds an EXPLICIT BALANCED skew transport, with no sign-feasibility
oracle. It equalizes the entire first row, and can make all its finite
multipliers nonnegative while maintaining the full PSD factor at qtar.
Nevertheless, for EVERY member of Law B, either the original multiplier
from the last queried leaf to the preceding queried leaf is negative, or
the original incoming optimum multiplier at query1 is negative. This is
an exhaustive obstruction for this displayed balanced correction, including
arbitrary positive metric scale and arbitrary nonnegative imbalance scale.

Neither exclusion is an impossibility theorem for all balanced corrections,
all weighted variances, all terminal probabilities, or the full dual cone.
No primal interpolability or lower bound on W is inferred from a formal
negative direction or a negative signed multiplier. No full upper bound on
W, benchmark improvement, or resolution of the original problem is obtained.

## 2. Original problem and accepted inputs

For a predetermined nonnegative word h of length n and L>0, W_n(h) denotes
the supremum of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over every finite
Euclidean dimension, convex differentiable L-smooth function with an
attained minimizer x_star, and x_0!=x_star, under the original recursion
x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Thus W=2R. The original question concerns
whether W_n_star/U_n^ZJ tends to1, where W_n_star=inf_(h>=0)W_n(h) and
U_n^ZJ=1/B_n. The original benchmark retains EVERY integer split:

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt(u^2+6uv+v^2))/2,
    G(u,v)=2u+v/2+sqrt(v^2+8uv)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=j<n) Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=j<n) G(C_j,B_(n-j-1)).

Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the original interpolation
orientation, full independent-vector certificate interpretation, and exact
incoming-terminal-free reduction. It deletes NO queried-prefix row.
Accepted fact931b9653ce0f7201 supplies the same-enclosing-m word below,
its mass identity and the scalar comparison B_n/D<47/50. Its implication
from W_n(H_m)<=17/(16D) to a strict benchmark improvement is CONDITIONAL;
that full-class upper hypothesis is still missing. These are the only
accepted mathematical inputs used here. Historical draft6e66efffac0795f1
is recall only; its coordinate and row identities are rederived below.

Fix ANY integer m>=1536. All children use this SAME enclosing m:

    ell=1+sqrt(2), eps=1/(4m), beta=1-eps,
    c=ell(1+eps), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    h=H_m, n=2^m-1, z=n-1,
    S=sum_(i<n)h_i, Aword=1+S, D=1+2S=2Aword-1,
    p=1/Aword, qtar=17/(16D), b=1+a.

The symbols p and q in this report mean p83 and q83; neither is a benchmark
exponent or a primal derivative. The letter B without a subscript below is
a skew matrix, not the benchmark B_n. All other hierarchy notation is local.
The actual physical step is h_i=1+a*c^v2(i+1), where v2(j) is the exponent
of2 dividing the positive integer j. The final three steps are
(b,1+beta,b). The first and last queried steps equal b; index n is the
ACTUAL terminal, distinct from z.

The elementary bounds needed below are

    12/5<c<5/2, 7/8<beta<1, 1/3<a<1/2, 4/3<b<3/2.       (2.1)

For example sqrt(2)>7/5 and sqrt(2)<17/12; hence ell>12/5 and
ell<29/12, and (29/12)(1+1/6144)<5/2. Also beta>7/8,
a>(7/8)/(5/2)>1/3, and a<1/ell<1/2.
The accepted mass formula is

    Aword=(1-vword)2^m+vword*c^m,
    vword=beta/[c(c-2)] in (0,1).

Indeed c>ell>2 and ell(ell-2)=1 give c(c-2)>1. Consequently

    2^m<Aword<c^m, 0<p<2^(-m)<1/128.                  (2.2)

Every h_i>1, consistently with these strict mass inequalities.

## 3. Exact physical suffix products and the selected terminal law

Write sbit(L) for the binary digit sum of a nonnegative integer L, including
sbit(0)=0. For 0<=L<=n define the product of the FINAL L actual factors:

    r_L=product_(t=n-L)^(n-1)(h_t-1), r_0=1.

The index j counted backward from the final physical step has
h_(n-j)-1=a*c^v2(2^m-j)=a*c^v2(j), for 1<=j<2^m. The valuation equality
follows by factoring the exact power of2 from j: the remaining difference
from2^m is odd. For any L, sum_(j=1)^L v2(j)=sum_(t>=1)floor(L/2^t).
Writing L in binary and summing each digit's contributions gives
sum_(t>=1)floor(L/2^t)=L-sbit(L). Therefore the EXACT suffix identity is

    r_L=beta^L*c^(-sbit(L)), 0<=L<=n.                 (3.1)

No product or recurrence has been numerically evaluated. In particular
s:=r_n=beta^n/c^m, and the signed full-word product is -s since n is odd.
Define the actual terminal coefficient and its absolute scale by

    k_i=h_i product_(i<t<n)(1-h_t),
    u_i=|k_i|, U=sum_(i<n)u_i, rho_i=u_i/U.

If L=n-1-i, adding the next backward factor shows

    u_i=r_L+r_(L+1), k_i=(-1)^L u_i=(-1)^i u_i.       (3.2)

Thus all u_i are strictly positive. The last three are

    u_z=b, u_(z-1)=a(1+beta), u_(z-2)=b*a*beta,
    u_0=(b/a)s.                                      (3.3)

Expanding a product over the m binary digits gives the finite identity

    Z=sum_(L=0)^n r_L=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1+beta^(2^j)/c),
    U=2Z-1-s <2(3/2)^m.                              (3.4)

The last inequality uses beta<1 and c>2. The three distinct last terms
in (3.3), with (2.1), give

    U>4/3+5/8+7/18=169/72>7/3.                       (3.5)

Both laws use these SAME explicit terminal probabilities:

    alpha_star=p, alpha_i=(1-p)rho_i=delta*u_i,
    delta=(1-p)/U, rplus=1-delta, rminus=1+delta,
    v=k-alpha.                                       (3.6)

They sum to1 and are strictly positive on every original queried sample
and the optimum. They are probabilities on real original rows, not on a
selected child interface. Since U>7/3, one has 0<delta<3/7, rplus>1/2,
and 1<rminus<3/2. Precisely

    v_i=rplus*u_i for i even,
    v_i=-rminus*u_i for i odd.                        (3.7)

Several uniform small-initial-weight bounds will be used. The binomial
expansion implies n=2^m-1>m(m-1)/2>128m for m>=1536. Also
(1-eps)^(-n)>(1+eps)^n>=1+n*eps, so beta^n<1/33. From Aword<c^m,
s/p=beta^n*Aword/c^m<beta^n. Because b/a=1+1/a<4,

    s<p/33, u_0<4p/33<p/8,
    alpha_0<p/8, rho_0<3p/56<1/10.                  (3.8)

These are symbolic inequalities uniform in all enclosing m in the task.

## 4. Full original coordinates and the complete signed matching

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Keep arbitrary independent
vectors x_0,g_0,...,g_n, with every original position defined by

    x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t*g_t.

The residual orientation is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Legal actual jets obey Q_ij<=0. For i<n let y_i=x_i-g_i and
Delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2, with the corresponding star quantities zero.
Let e be the all-ones column of length n, e_i its coordinate columns, and
T=T82 the lower triangular matrix T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, zero for t>i.
For vector columns g=(g_0,...,g_(n-1)) and y=(y_0,...,y_(n-1)),

    y=e*x_0-Tg, g=T^(-1)(e*x_0-y).                    (4.1)

This is invertible on the ENTIRE formal space. Explicitly, if
pi_i=product_(t<i)(1-h_t), then

    g_i=pi_i*x_0-y_i
          +sum_(j<i)h_j product_(j<t<i)(1-h_t)*y_j.  (4.2)

Substitution into x_(i+1)=(1-h_i)x_i+h_i*y_i proves

    x_n=-s*x_0+k^T y, e^T k=1+s, T^T k=h.           (4.3)

For the latter identity, h_j=1-(1-h_j) telescopes on each suffix:
k_i+h_i sum_(j>i)k_j=h_i. In particular e^T v=p+s.
The cumulative terminal probabilities, distinct from detail weights below,
are Cprob_i=p+sum_(j<=i)alpha_j. Define

    R_i=h_i*Cprob_i-alpha_i,
    t_i=1+sum_(j<i)h_j, t=Te,
    Uclock=sum_i R_i=t^T v,
    gamma=2p/(p+s), eta=(p-s)/(p+s).

Then T^T v=R and
R_i=h_i(p+sum_(j<i)alpha_j)+(h_i-1)alpha_i>0. Thus Uclock>0,
1<gamma<2, eta>0 and gamma=1+eta. In particular

    R_0=bp+a*alpha_0, H=p+s-v_0=p+alpha_0-s/a,
    bp<R_0<25p/16, 7p/8<H<9p/8.                     (4.4)

The lower bound on H follows from H=p+s-rplus*u_0>p-u_0; its upper
bound follows from the second expression in (4.4).
The actual terminal center is V=-s*x_0+v^T y.

For the moment let w_i>0 be arbitrary DETAIL weights, Ww=sum_i w_i,
and let d be any real column with e^T d=0. Define

    K=diag(w)-w*w^T/Ww,
    A=(d*w^T-w*d^T)/Ww+B, B^T=-B, Be=0,
    P=K+gamma*v*v^T, N=T^T(P+A).                     (4.5)

Thus Ke=0, A^T=-A and Ae=d. The matrices are instantiated explicitly in
Sections6 and7; an arbitrary sign-feasible B is NOT a proposed result.
Every scalar entry is

    N_ij=K_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(u>i)(K_uj+A_uj)
                                      +gamma*R_i*v_j. (4.6)

The entire ORIGINAL SIGNED coefficient array is

    lambda_(n,star)=2p, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
    lambda_(j,n)=0 for j in {star,0,...,n-1},
    lambda_(i,j)=-N_ij for i!=j<n,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i=(Ne)_i=2p*R_i+(T^T d)_i,
    lambda_(star,i)=nu_i=(N^T e)_i-2alpha_i
                      =(Kt)_i+gamma*Uclock*v_i-(At)_i-2alpha_i,
    lambda_(i,i)=0.                                  (4.7)

Signs are not presumed. This lists every original coefficient, including
both optimum orientations and the actual outgoing terminal distribution.
For each prefix index i, the outgoing sum is N_ii, while the incoming
PREFIX sum is N_ii-2alpha_i. The incoming terminal coefficient2alpha_i
therefore gives zero total divergence at i. Terminal divergence is2;
optimum divergence is-2. Consequently all original sampled values cancel
in M(q)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij.

To check the quadratic directly, Q_ij=Delta_i-Delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>
for prefix indices, including star. The prefix value terms cancel the
-2sum alpha_i Delta_i from the outgoing terminal expansion. The remaining
prefix term is -g^T N y. Since N=T^T(P+A), this equals

    -<x_0,e^T(P+A)y>+y^T P y,
    e^T P=2p*v^T, e^T A=-d^T.

The terminal expansion contributes ||g_n-V||^2-||V||^2. Completing the
common square gives the full identity, on arbitrary original vectors,

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2+y^T K y
       +eta||v^T y-(p+s)x_0||^2
       +(q-p^2)||x_0||^2+<x_0,d^T y>.                (4.8)

For an expansion check, the unsquared prefix terms are
(q-s^2)||x_0||^2+2(s-p)<x_0,v^T y>+eta||v^T y||^2
+y^T K y+<x_0,d^T y>. The relation eta(p+s)=p-s proves (4.8).

## 5. Weighted completion, the real common derivative, and a row invariant

Let ybar_w=sum_i w_i*y_i/Ww. Since sum_i d_i=0, expanding the squares gives

    sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(d_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2
    =y^T K y+<x_0,d^T y>+J||x_0||^2,
    J=(1/4)sum_i d_i^2/w_i.                          (5.1)

Thus the COMPLETE factor is

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2
       +sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(d_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2
       +eta||v^T y-(p+s)x_0||^2+(q-p^2-J)||x_0||^2.  (5.2)

The charge J is paid ONCE globally. No child gradient, common mode, leaf,
checkpoint, terminal square or initial cross derivative has been removed.
The detail form has kernel exactly the constant y columns, because every
w_i>0. The common square controls that remaining direction since e^T v>0.

Full PSD in (5.2) is EQUIVALENT to q>=p^2+J. To prove necessity take scalar
x_0=1, set c0=1+[sum_i v_i*d_i/(2w_i)]/(p+s), y_i=c0-d_i/(2w_i),
and g_n=p. The weighted mean of y is c0 because sum d_i=0. All detail,
common and terminal squares vanish. Reconstruct each original g_i by
(4.2). The value of M is exactly q-p^2-J. This is a formal full-space
negative direction if that quantity is negative; it is NOT an actual
interpolable primal trajectory.

Setting every original queried gradient equal to an arbitrary vector G
instead gives y_i=x_0-t_iG. Directly in (4.8),

    R_common=(q-p^2)||x_0||^2-(d^T t)<x_0,G>
                      +(t^T Kt+eta*Uclock^2)||G||^2. (5.3)

The genuine nonzero initial/common derivative is -(d^T t)x_0. A balanced
B changes neither this derivative nor the full square polynomial.

Now derive the original FIRST-ROW off-diagonal sum including d_0.
The first column of T is (1,b,...,b)^T. Since K has column sums zero,
(T^T K)_00=-a*K_00. Skewness gives A_00=0, and e^T A=-d^T gives
(T^T A)_00=-b*d_0. Meanwhile (T^T d)_0=-a*d_0. Subtracting the diagonal
from the row sum in (4.7) yields

    sum_(j>0) N_0j
       =a*K_00+gamma*R_0*(p+s-v_0)+d_0
       =a*K_00+gamma*R_0*H+d_0.                     (5.4)

Every balanced B leaves this sum invariant. Nonnegative finite first-row
multipliers require the right side to be <=0. A balanced correction can
redistribute that sum among entries; it cannot change the sum itself.

There is also an exact inverse-metric price for this invariant. Weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz on i>0 gives
sum_(i>0)d_i^2/w_i >=d_0^2/(Ww-w_0), since sum_(i>0)d_i=-d_0.
Consequently

    J>=d_0^2/(4*K_00), K_00=w_0(1-w_0/Ww).          (5.5)

Equality holds precisely when d_i=-d_0*w_i/(Ww-w_0) for every i>0.
Because H>0, (5.4)--(5.5) imply for any nonnegative first row

    J>=(a*K_00+gamma*R_0*H)^2/(4*K_00)
      >=a*gamma*R_0*H.                               (5.6)

The final inequality expands the nonnegative square
(a*K_00-gamma*R_0*H)^2. This is a necessary first-row screen, NOT a
sufficient certificate condition. The two selected laws now instantiate
all weights and skew matrices rather than leaving the screen unsolved.

## 6. Law A: exact tail metric with minimum-price distributed imbalance

For EVERY kappa>0 and tau>=0 choose

    w_i=kappa*u_i, Ww=kappa*U,
    d=tau*(rho-e_0),
    A_A=tau*(rho*e_0^T-e_0*rho^T), B_A=0.             (6.1)

Here A_A=(d*w^T-w*d^T)/Ww exactly, and A_A e=d. The imbalance is
negative at0 and positive at EVERY other actual queried index, not just
at one endpoint. It attains equality in (5.5). The metric is nonisotropic
because u_0<p/8 whereas u_z=b>4/3. The terminal probabilities remain (3.6).

The exact global charge and common derivative are

    J_A=tau^2*(1-rho_0)/(4*kappa*u_0),
    d^T t=tau*(tbar-1), tbar=sum_i rho_i*t_i.          (6.2)

Thus (5.2) is a fully specified factor iff q>=p^2+J_A.
For a literal scalar description of EVERY finite entry put
F_i=u_i+h_i sum_(j>i)u_j. Then

    N^A_ij=kappa*(u_i*1_(i=j)+h_i*u_j*1_(j>i)-F_i*rho_j)
          +gamma*R_i*v_j
          +tau*((F_i/U)*1_(j=0)-1_(i=0)*rho_j).      (6.3)

can also be written explicitly:

    mu_0=2p*R_0+a*tau*(1-rho_0)>0,
    mu_i=2p*R_i+tau*F_i/U>0 for i>0,
    nu^A_i=kappa*u_i*(t_i-tbar)+gamma*Uclock*v_i
                         -tau*(rho_i-1_(i=0)*tbar)-2alpha_i. (6.4)

All terminal outgoing signs and all outgoing optimum signs pass. No sign
is silently assigned to nu^A or an off-diagonal -N^A.

### 6.1 A first-row charge obstruction at the assigned target

Since v_z=rplus*u_z, the actual first-to-last queried entry is

    N^A_0z=rho_z*(a*kappa*u_0-tau)
                                +gamma*R_0*rplus*u_z. (6.5)

If lambda_(0,z)=-N^A_0z>=0, positivity of rho_z gives

    tau>=a*kappa*u_0+gamma*R_0*(U-1+p).               (6.6)

Apply (a*x+C)^2/(4x)>=a*C for x=kappa*u_0>0 and
C=gamma*R_0*(U-1+p)>0. Equations (6.2) and (6.6) imply

    J_A>=a*gamma*R_0*(U-1+p)*(1-rho_0)
       >(4/9)*p*(4/3)*(9/10)=8p/15.                (6.7)

The strict lower bounds use a*b>4/9, gamma>1, R_0>bp, U>7/3 and
rho_0<1/10. On the other hand Aword>128 gives

    qtar/p=17*Aword/[16*(2Aword-1)]<8/15,             (6.8)

because this inequality is equivalent to Aword>128. Thus no member of
Law A has both full PSD and lambda_(0,z)>=0 at q<=qtar. This argument
uses the exact SINGLE global charge and no local Schur-budget summation.

### 6.2 A stronger literal incoming-optimum failure for every q

The weighted clock is uniformly large. By (3.3)--(3.5), t_z>n and
n>2^(m-1), so

    tbar>=rho_z*t_z> b*n/[2*(3/2)^m]
                     >(1/3)*(4/3)^m>27.             (6.9)

For the last inequality m>=16 and (4/3)^4=256/81>3, so (4/3)^16>81.

In (6.4) its metric term is strictly negative, its rank term is strictly
negative, its skew term is nonpositive, and -2alpha_1 is strictly negative.
Hence

    nu^A_1=lambda_(star,1)<0                         (6.10)

for EVERY m>=1536, kappa>0, tau>=0 and every real q. This excludes
Law A as an original-row certificate even at larger q. It does not exclude
a balanced re-selection, which can change nu_1 and (6.5). Law B performs
one such correction explicitly; it is not dismissed by (6.10).

## 7. Law B: an explicit balanced transport that repairs the entire first row

Keep the SAME w,d,alpha,p and arbitrary kappa>0,tau>=0 as in Law A.
Define the probability column on noninitial queried samples

    r_0^pool=0, r_i^pool=u_i/(U-u_0) for i>0,
    chi=e_0-r^pool,
    xi=gamma*R_0/a,
    bvec_0=0, bvec_i=xi*(v_i-H*r_i^pool) for i>0,
    B_B=chi*bvec^T-bvec*chi^T,
    A_B=A_A+B_B.                                     (7.1)

The r^pool column is distinct from the suffix product r_L. Its denominator
is positive, and its entries sum to1. Since sum_(i>0)v_i=H, both chi and
bvec have sum zero. Therefore B_B is skew AND B_B e=0. In particular
A_B e=d, and the entire factor (5.2), charge (6.2), and real derivative
(5.3) are unchanged. There is no hidden skew unknown in this law.

For complete scalar coefficients define
C_i=chi_i+h_i sum_(j>i)chi_j and
E_i=bvec_i+h_i sum_(j>i)bvec_j. Then

    N^B_ij=N^A_ij+C_i*bvec_j-E_i*chi_j.              (7.2)

Equations (4.7), (6.3), (7.1)--(7.2) specify EVERY original coefficient.
The outgoing optimum coefficients are still the strictly positive mu_i
in (6.4). The incoming optimum coefficients are

    nu^B_i=nu^A_i-chi_i*(bvec^T t)+bvec_i*(chi^T t).  (7.3)

No positivity of these incoming coefficients is assumed.

### 7.1 The entire first row is explicitly equalized

For j>0, B_B,0j=bvec_j. Because B_B has zero column sums,
(T^T B_B)_0j=-a*bvec_j. Substituting (7.1) in (6.3) yields

    N^B_0j=r_j^pool*S0,
    S0=(a*kappa*u_0-tau)*(1-rho_0)+gamma*R_0*H.      (7.4)

In particular ALL original finite first-row multipliers are nonnegative
iff S0<=0, equivalently

    tau>=a*kappa*u_0+gamma*R_0*H/(1-rho_0).           (7.5)

This realizes the invariant (5.4), rather than assuming it can be repaired.
It changes the demanding Law A quantity U-1+p in (6.6) to the much smaller
H/(1-rho_0). Thus the Law A charge obstruction does NOT transfer to Law B.

The simultaneous first-row and full-PSD conditions at qtar are nonvacuous.
Within this same two-parameter law choose the explicit member

    kappa_0=gamma*R_0*H/[a*u_0*(1-rho_0)],
    tau_0=2*gamma*R_0*H/(1-rho_0).                    (7.6)

These are positive. Equation (7.4) gives N^B_0j=0 for every j>0, and
J_A=a*gamma*R_0*H. From (2.1), gamma<2 and (4.4),

    J_A< (25p/16)*(9p/8)=225p^2/128<2p^2.

Consequently p^2+J_A<3p^2<p/2<qtar, because p<1/128 and
qtar/p=17*Aword/[16*(2Aword-1)]>17/32>1/2. This is a strictly positive
full factor at the target with all finite first-row multipliers zero,
positive terminal probabilities, and positive outgoing optimum multipliers.
It remains a FAILED certificate because the complete array still has a
negative original coefficient, as the next subsection proves.

### 7.2 Last-to-previous-leaf versus incoming optimum1: exhaustive sign conflict

Let j=z-2, the genuine preceding queried leaf. Both z and j are even.
For i,j>0 the balanced correction has the explicit entry

    B_B,ij=xi*(v_i*r_j^pool-r_i^pool*v_j).            (7.7)

By (3.7), v_z/u_z=v_j/u_j=rplus. Therefore B_B,zj=0. Also
A_A,zj=0. The last row of T^T is the last coordinate row, so exactly

    N^B_zj=u_z*u_j*(-kappa/U+gamma*rplus^2).          (7.8)

If kappa<gamma*U*rplus^2, this entry is positive and the ORIGINAL
lambda_(z,z-2) is negative. Otherwise its sign passes and necessarily

    kappa>=gamma*U*rplus^2>7/12.                     (7.9)

The strict lower bound follows from gamma>1, U>7/3 and rplus>1/2.
We now prove that throughout this remaining domain nu^B_1 is negative.

Put tpool=sum_i r_i^pool*t_i=(tbar-rho_0)/(1-rho_0). Then
bvec^T t=xi*(Uclock-v_0-H*tpool), chi^T t=1-tpool.
For i>0, using (7.3) gives the exact expression

    nu^B_i=kappa*u_i*(t_i-tbar)
       +[gamma*Uclock-xi*(tpool-1)]*v_i
       +xi*r_i^pool*(Uclock-(p+s))-tau*rho_i-2alpha_i. (7.10)

This includes the actual initial clock t_0=1 in BOTH appearances of
(tpool-1) and (p+s); omitting it would change the optimum row.
At query1, divide by the positive u_1 and use v_1/u_1=-rminus:

    nu^B_1/u_1=kappa*(t_1-tbar)
       +[-gamma*rminus+xi/(U-u_0)]*Uclock
       +xi*rminus*(tpool-1)-xi*(p+s)/(U-u_0)
       -tau/U-2delta.                                (7.11)

All signs in this expression can be bounded uniformly. Since b/a<4,
alpha_0<p/8, and gamma<2,

    xi=gamma*(bp/a+alpha_0)<2*(4p+p/8)<9p.           (7.12)

Also U-u_0>7/3-1/8>2. With p<1/128, (7.12) implies
xi/(U-u_0)<9p/2<1<gamma*rminus. Thus the coefficient of Uclock in
(7.11) is negative; Uclock>0. The terms -xi*(p+s)/(U-u_0), -tau/U and
-2delta are nonpositive, with the first and last strictly negative.
Further,

    tpool < tbar/(1-rho_0),
    xi*rminus*tpool < (9p)*(3/2)*(10/9)*tbar
                                      =15p*tbar.    (7.13)

Since t_1<tbar/2 by (6.9), dropping the negative terms in (7.11) gives

    nu^B_1/u_1<(-kappa/2+15p)*tbar<0.               (7.14)

For the final strict sign, (7.9) gives kappa/2>7/24, whereas
15p<15/128<7/24. All denominators and u_1,tbar are positive.

Combining (7.8) and (7.14) covers EVERY kappa>0,tau>=0, with no assumption
on PSD or the first-row signs: either lambda_(z,z-2)<0, or
lambda_(star,1)=nu^B_1<0. At equality kappa=gamma*U*rplus^2, (7.9) and
(7.14) still apply. This excludes the WHOLE displayed Law B domain at any
q, in particular every full-PSD member at qtar, including (7.6).

This conflict concerns the literal balanced correction (7.1). Another
balanced matrix can change the pair (7.8), the optimum row (7.11), or both.
No universal exclusion of balanced re-selection is asserted.

## 8. Boundary, sign and scope audit

* All enclosing integers m>=1536 are treated with the SAME beta,c,a at
  every child. No finite numerical horizon test or reset is used.
* The probabilities at every original queried target and at the optimum
  are strictly positive. The actual terminal gradient remains free, with
  its exact square retained. No earlier remote row is removed.
* The variance metric controls all n-1 independent detail directions.
  The independent common direction and its real derivative are retained.
* Every finite and optimum coefficient has a literal scalar formula.
  Terminal and outgoing-optimum signs pass for both laws. Incoming-optimum
  and finite signs fail as proved; no signed row is called a certificate.
* tau=0 is allowed and covered; kappa>0 is necessary for the specified
  positive metric. Equality in PSD and in the tail sign has been covered.
* Balanced B_B e=0 is checked explicitly, and the initial clock contribution
  is retained in the exact incoming-optimum formula. This is not the old
  isotropic endpoint correction or the old physical-tree uniform pool.
* The first-row invariant includes d_0. Its inverse-metric charge is paid
  once, with an explicit global square-zero direction proving necessity.
* Formal negative directions are not actual trajectories. Failure of these
  two coefficient laws gives no lower bound on W and no global no-certificate
  theorem. Fact931's missing full-function hypothesis remains unproved.

The row identities and inequalities above have received a textual author
audit only. They are not verifier-accepted facts, and no downstream argument
may treat this report as an accepted building block.

## 9. Retrieval, failure synthesis and handoff

The query-memory, immediate-conclusions, direct-proving,
construct-counterexamples and identify-key-failures procedures guided this
bounded joint attempt. The fact search found no accepted version of the
new weighted first-row identity or these two row laws. Current guidance
was recalled by its targeted query after an empty-string query returned
count0. Oversized initial recall output was truncated; the relevant old
joint report and accepted inputs were reread in bounded portions.

A repair-mode Matlas search for full PSD weighted interpolation certificates
returned unrelated PL, stochastic and constant-step statements; none was
used. Web search located Altschuler--Parrilo, 'Acceleration by Stepsize
Hedging II: Silver Stepsize Schedule for Smooth Convex Optimization',
arXiv:2309.16530, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16530, already read in the prior
round as exact proof-pattern background. No external theorem or proof step
is imported here. The new laws reduce to explicit coefficient identities
in that already-audited interpolation regime; no additional literature
layer or new mathematical machinery is needed for these scoped algebraic
rejections. No notebook or numerical certificate was run.

Law A's failure is not caused by forgetting tail scales: it uses them in
both the metric and terminal distribution, and its imbalance is optimally
distributed for its fixed initial component. Its literal first-to-last row
still overcharges, and the early negative-k incoming optimum row fails.

Law B demonstrates a real escape from Law A's first-row charge argument:
an explicit balanced transport repairs the entire row at affordable full
PSD cost. Its remaining failure is a different, complete-original-array
conflict: a same-sign pair of late queried leaves fixes a nonvanishing
metric scale, while the early odd query sits below the weighted mean clock
and has negative terminal coefficient. The specified transport is too
small to pay that original optimum row at that forced metric scale.

The next missing mechanism would have to alter this second conflict, for
example through a different balanced transport affecting the relevant
late pair and optimum load, a different genuinely nonisotropic metric, or
a different actual terminal law. These are uncovered freedoms, not a third
law attempted in this invocation and not a solution by an unknown matrix.
The first-row invariant (5.4) and its charge (5.5) remain necessary checks
in the stated general architecture; their sufficiency has not been claimed.

## 1. Outcome and scope

The prescribed new terminal mixture has clock V=2 exactly. Its positive

full original-space PSD identity are explicit below. Both complete endpoint

Nevertheless the law is impossible, INCLUDING EVERY skew correction C with

The second mechanism derives a finite transport formulation retaining the

these conditions fails for every skew completion and every nonnegative

All these statements are one jointly derived UNVERIFIED proof draft.
Accepted facts1252b8823bb5a290 and931b9653ce0f7201 are used only at their

## 2. Original problem and accepted interfaces

For a predetermined nonnegative word h of length n, W_n(h) is the supremum
of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over every finite Euclidean
dimension, convex differentiable L-smooth f with an attained minimizer,
and x_0!=x_star, using x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Thus W=2R.
The original question asks whether W_n_star/U_n^ZJ tends to1, where
W_n_star=inf_(h>=0)W_n(h), U_n^ZJ=1/B_n, and the ALL-SPLIT benchmark is

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt(x^2+6xy+y^2))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=j<n)Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=j<n)G(C_j,B_(n-j-1)).

Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the signed interpolation convention and
full terminal-square interpretation. Only incoming edges at the actual
UNQUERIED terminal n may be deleted. No queried gradient or prefix pair

Fix an arbitrary integer m>=1536 and use its SAME parameters in every child:

    eps=1/(4m), beta=1-eps, c=(1+sqrt(2))(1+eps), a=beta/c,

    S=sum_(i<n)h_i, D=1+2S, p=1/(1+S), qtar=17/(16D).

Here l and r are last and penultimate QUERIED indices. The terminal n
remains distinct. All short symbols in this report are local aliases;
public names for newly published quantities carry the suffix86, avoiding
any reassignment of project glossary entries. In particular rho below is
a probability VECTOR, not the benchmark exponent. Ltri is a matrix; T is
a scalar clock; superscript T denotes transpose.

Let e be the all-ones column on n queries and e_i its coordinate columns.
Define the strictly increasing clocks

The last three physical steps are (b,hgap,b). The needed scalar bounds are

    12/5<c<5/2, 7/8<beta<1,

For the lower bound on a, sqrt(2)<10/7 gives

Every elementary small-p comparison below uses this SAME all-m bound;

## 3. Tail probabilities and the exact mixed terminal clock

For integer suffix length Len in[0,n], write sbit(Len) for its binary
digit sum and define

    rtail_Len=product_(j=n-Len)^(n-1)(h_j-1)
             =beta^Len*c^(-sbit(Len)),

    k_i=h_i product_(i<j<n)(1-h_j),
    u_i=|k_i|, U=sum_i u_i, rho_i=u_i/U.

Here v2(j) is the exponent of2 dividing the positive integer j.
The suffix formula follows from h_(n-j)-1=a*c^v2(j) and

The last three terms exceed4/3,5/8,7/18, whose sum169/72>7/3;

    0<s<u_0<p^2/64, rho_0<1/10, s<p.               (3.1)

For completeness, 2^m-1>16m^2 for m>=16 follows by induction (the
base is the integer inequality at16, and doubling dominates the next

## 4. Complete original-space coefficient identity

Normalize smoothness to1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Keep
x_0,g_0,...,g_n independent formal vectors and substitute ONLY the
actual GD updates. From fact1252b8823bb5a290 use the signed residual

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

For every queried index set y_i=x_i-g_i and delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2.
Then

    y=e*x_0-Ltri*g, g=Ltri^(-1)(e*x_0-y),
    x_n=-s*x_0+k^T y.                               (4.1)

The unit-diagonal triangular matrix Ltri is invertible; hence this
coordinate change retains every original queried-gradient direction.
The actual terminal gradient g_n is independent of these coordinates.

For ANY positive weights w_i, let Ww=sum_i w_i and

    K=diag(w)-ww^T/Ww.

For any z with e^T z=E and any zeta with e^T zeta=0 define

    P=K+vv^T+eta zz^T,
    d=zeta+F(v-z),
    A^T=-A, Ae=d, N=Ltri^T(P+A).                    (4.2)

For distinct original indices the literal signed array is

    lambda_(n,star)=2p, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
    lambda_(j,n)=0 for j in {star,0,...,l},
    lambda_(i,j)=-N_ij for distinct i,j<n,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i=(Ne)_i,
    lambda_(star,i)=nu_i=(N^T e)_i-2alpha_i.          (4.3)

Diagonal multipliers vanish. Each matrix entry is explicitly

    N_ij=K_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(u>i)(K_uj+A_uj)
                            +R_i v_j+eta Zout_i z_j,
    Zout=Ltri^T z.                                  (4.4)

Thus no finite pair is omitted or replaced by a feasibility assumption.
The total finite-prefix outgoing mass at i, including its optimum edge,
is N_ii; the incoming prefix mass is N_ii-2alpha_i; the terminal adds
2alpha_i. Finite-node divergence is zero, terminal divergence is2,
and optimum divergence is-2, even before any sign claim.

For prefix indices, including star,
Q_ij=delta_i-delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>. The remaining prefix quadratic
is -g^T N y=-<x_0,(Pe-d)^T y>+y^T P y. The terminal contribution
WITH -2f_n included is

    ||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2-||-s*x_0+v^T y||^2
                                         -2sum_i alpha_i delta_i.

Its value terms cancel the prefix divergence terms. Since
Pe=Ev+Fz and eta E^2=p^2-s^2, the full identity is

    M(q):=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij
      =||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2+y^T K y
        +eta||z^T y-E*x_0||^2
        +(q-p^2)||x_0||^2+<x_0,zeta^T y>.           (4.5)

With ybar_w=sum_i w_i y_i/Ww and e^T zeta=0, this becomes

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2
      +sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(zeta_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2
      +eta||z^T y-E*x_0||^2+(q-p^2-J)||x_0||^2,
    J=(1/4)sum_i zeta_i^2/w_i.                      (4.6)

The initial charge is paid once. Necessity of q>=p^2+J follows by
setting scalar x_0=1, y_i=c0-zeta_i/(2w_i),
c0=1+sum_i z_i zeta_i/(2w_i E), and g_n=-s+v^T y;
then every square vanishes. Equation (4.1) reconstructs all gradients.
Thus full PSD is equivalent to q>=p^2+J, on the entire original formal
space, not just on legal trajectories. On the actual common queried
gradient direction g_i=G, put X=t^T Kt, Z=t^T z and theta=t^T zeta.
The entire prefix remainder is

    (q-p^2)||x_0||^2-theta<x_0,G>+(X+eta Z^2)||G||^2.

The common derivative has not been discarded.

## 8. Second mechanism: transport with diagonal exclusion and the full factor

This section treats an entire family, rather than adding another metric
atom. First give the exact finite transport interface for any fixed
P,mu,nu,alpha in the architecture above. Write

    D_i=N_ii, a_ij=-N_ij for i!=j, a_ii=0,
    r_i=D_i-mu_i,
    c_i=D_i-nu_i-2alpha_i,
    b_i^clock=t_i D_i-(Nt)_i.                       (8.1)

Here a_ij denotes transport mass and is unrelated to the physical scalar
a. If the original finite multipliers are nonnegative, then a_ij>=0 and

    sum_j a_ij=r_i, sum_i a_ij=c_j,
    sum_j t_j a_ij=b_i^clock.                       (8.2)

Thus every r_i,c_j is nonnegative, sum r=sum c, and
sum_i b_i^clock=sum_j t_j c_j. A zero r_i forces b_i^clock=0.
For positive r_i the mean b_i^clock/r_i lies in the interval spanned
by {t_j:j!=i}; retaining the exclusion is essential at either endpoint.
With Kmass=sum r=sum c, the forbidden diagonal further implies

    r_i+c_i<=Kmass.                                 (8.3)

Indeed all mass from row i must land outside column i, whose total
capacity is Kmass-c_i. This is a true cut inequality.

There are elementary clock cuts as well. For any real tau,

    sum_i max(0,b_i^clock-tau*r_i)
                              <=sum_j c_j max(0,t_j-tau).       (8.4)

For each row, max(0,sum_j a_ij(t_j-tau))<=sum_j a_ij max(0,t_j-tau);
summing proves (8.4). More generally for any convex function phi on[1,T],
finite convexity gives

    sum_(i:r_i>0) r_i phi(b_i^clock/r_i)
                                      <=sum_j c_j phi(t_j).    (8.5)

This is merely the finite convex-combination inequality, provable by
induction on the number of nonzero row entries, and imports no transport
existence theorem. It is necessary, not sufficient for the original law.
The following more general elementary cut keeps the missing diagonal
visible: if real Ucut_i,Vcut_i,Zcut_j obey
Ucut_i+Vcut_i*t_j+Zcut_j>=0 for EVERY i!=j, then

    sum_i Ucut_i*r_i+sum_i Vcut_i*b_i^clock+sum_j Zcut_j*c_j>=0. (8.6)

Multiply each allowed coefficient by a_ij>=0 and sum. No condition on
Ucut_i+Vcut_i*t_i+Zcut_i is imposed, because that edge is forbidden.

Crucially, the chronological symmetric-factor constraint remains

    Ltri^(-T)N+N^T Ltri^(-1)=2P.                    (8.7)

A transport coupling satisfying row/column masses and clock conditions

The last row of Ltri^(-T) is e_l^T. The (l,l) entry of (8.7) therefore
pins D_l=P_ll. The nonnegative column mass c_l gives

factor constraint. Allowing D_l to float freely would lose it.

For ANY strictly positive metric weights w, set X=t^T Kt and

    Qgap=sum_(i<l) w_i (T-t_i)^2 / sum_(i<l)w_i.

Retaining only pairs involving l and using
K_ll=w_l(Ww-w_l)/Ww gives the exact necessary estimate

    X>=K_ll*Qgap, so K_ll<=X/Qgap.                  (8.9)

Every denominator is positive since w_i>0 and the clocks are distinct.

 Bneed:=2alpha_l+nu_l-(b-alpha_l)^2-eta*z_l^2>0,

Fix any same-enclosing-m word as in Section2. Consider ALL choices with

       <1/12+1/144-23/144=-5/72<0.                 (8.13)

## 2. Original target, coordinates, and uniform scalar bounds

and exact unqueried-terminal reduction. No queried sample is deleted.

    S=sum_i h_i, D=1+2S, p=1/(1+S), qtar=17/(16D).

a probability vector, not the benchmark exponent; T is a scalar clock,

## 7. Mechanism2: explicit chronological PSD details and their global price

We now enlarge the detail term itself, instead of changing another
weight within one weighted-variance metric. The identified constraint
is the first diagonal's ability to pay a column load under a small
initial charge. Both clock-bearing and clock-annihilating details are
allowed below; the former change the paid column and all load moments.
Their price is recomputed, not assumed to vanish.

On the ORIGINAL queried indices define the literal chronological vectors

    gdetail_i=e_i-e_(i+1), 0<=i<=n-2,
    ddetail_i=h_(i+1)e_i-(h_i+h_(i+1))e_(i+1)+h_i e_(i+2),
                                           0<=i<=n-3.

They obey

    e^T gdetail_i=0, t^T gdetail_i=-h_i,
    e^T ddetail_i=0, t^T ddetail_i=0.              (7.1)

For the latter clock identity substitute
(t_i,t_(i+1),t_(i+2))=(t_i,t_i+h_i,t_i+h_i+h_(i+1));
each term cancels. Thus zero sum alone does NOT imply zero clock energy.

Choose this ONE explicit enlarged coefficient law:

    gamma_i=Xreq/[2(n-1)h_i^2], 0<=i<=n-2,
    tau_i=p/[1+h_i+h_(i+1)]^2, 0<=i<=n-3,
    Hclock=sum_(i=0)^(n-2) gamma_i gdetail_i gdetail_i^T,
    Hnull=sum_(i=0)^(n-3) tau_i ddetail_i ddetail_i^T,
    Qdetail=K/2+Hclock+Hnull.                      (7.2)

Every vector and weight is an original-index formula. No optimizer,
recurrence replay, matrix-existence claim, or selected support is used.
All sums are finite symbolic definitions, not executed computations.
The entries of K/2 correspond to the positive weights w/2. Consequently
Qdetail is PSD and positive definite on e-perp. From (7.1),

    Qdetail e=0,
    t^T Hclock t=sum_i gamma_i h_i^2=Xreq/2,
    Hnull t=0, t^T Qdetail t=Xreq.                (7.3)

Retain the same terminal pool and late common column, and REPLACE

    zeta by zeta_new=(theta/Xreq)Qdetail t,
    P by Pnew=Qdetail+vv^T+eta zz^T,
    d by dnew=zeta_new+F(v-z).

Use (4.6) with Kt replaced by Qdetail t, d replaced by dnew, and
rvec=Qdetail t+2v+eta Zz-2alpha-nu_target. This again is a literal skew
completion and, with (3.3), specifies EVERY original multiplier.

incoming-load compatibility moments remain ellload. The incoming
optimum vector is exactly nu_target; it is not a free unpriced correction.

The complete polynomial is (3.4) with K,zeta replaced by
Qdetail,zeta_new. In particular its paid part equals

    (y+(theta/(2Xreq))*t*x_0)^T Qdetail
                   (y+(theta/(2Xreq))*t*x_0)
        +(q-p^2-theta^2/(4Xreq))||x_0||^2.         (7.4)

This equality follows by expanding the square and using (7.3).
Necessity of this same charge follows with scalar x_0=1,
y=-(theta/(2Xreq))*t+c0 e, choosing c0 to cancel the common square,
and choosing the independent g_n to cancel the terminal square.
Thus the exact global charge remains

    q>=p^2+theta^2/(4Xreq),                       (7.5)

which passes at qtar by (4.4). There is no extra hidden initial cost,
no omitted clock energy, and no uncancelled terminal square.

All optimum signs pass for this second law as well. Hnull t=0, and
Ltri^T Kt has strictly positive entries by the argument following (4.6).
For Hclock t write aedge_i=gamma_i h_i>0, with aedge_(-1)=aedge_l=0.
The i-th coordinate of Hclock t is aedge_(i-1)-aedge_i; its suffix
after i is aedge_i. Therefore

    (Ltri^T Hclock t)_i=aedge_(i-1)+(h_i-1)aedge_i>0

for every i, interpreting endpoints by the zero conventions. This

The source data have changed explicitly:

    Qdetail_00=K_00/2+gamma_0+tau_0*h_1^2,
    zeta_new,0=zeta_0/2-theta/[2(n-1)b].           (7.6)

Thus this mechanism changes the first diagonal and paid source column,

the tau_0 term in (7.6) must be included, even though Hnull t=0.
The full failure of this enlarged law follows from the next global
inequality, which covers considerably more freedom than (7.2).

### 7.1 A source-capacity inequality for the entire PSD-detail class

For this necessary-condition argument allow ANY symmetric PSD Qdetail
with Qdetail e=0; no such matrix is asserted to solve a feasibility
problem. Allow ANY zero-sum paid vector zeta and ANY common vector z
with e^T z=E. Keep v=k-alpha, e^T alpha=1-p, 0<s<p, eta=F/E,
and the original coefficient formulas

    P=Qdetail+vv^T+eta zz^T,
    d=zeta+F(v-z), A^T=-A, Ae=d, N=Ltri^T(P+A).

The incoming vector may now vary as well. Assume only that the full
original polynomial at level q is PSD. That assumption will be used
to derive a necessary inequality, not to posit a feasible completion.
For any scalar x,u choose

    x_0=x,
    y=u e_0+[x-(z_0/E)u]e,
    g_n=-s*x+v^T y.

These are permissible original formal directions by invertibility
of Ltri. The common and terminal squares vanish EXACTLY. Because
Qdetail e=0 and e^T zeta=0, full PSD implies, for every x,u,

    Qdetail_00*u^2+zeta_0*x*u+(q-p^2)*x^2>=0.    (7.7)

In particular the following explicitly evaluated quantity is nonnegative:

    Rsource=Qdetail_00+(b/a)zeta_0
                         +(b^2/a^2)(q-p^2)>=0.   (7.8)

The first diagonal formula (5.2) holds unchanged:

    N_00=b(2s v_0+2Fz_0-zeta_0)
                    -a(Qdetail_00+v_0^2+eta z_0^2).

Now expand these THREE nonnegative terms:

    b^2 q/a-N_00
       =a Rsource
         +a(v_0-bs/a)^2
         +a*eta*(z_0-bE/a)^2 >=0.                (7.9)

To check the constant exactly, eta E=F and
s^2+eta E^2=p^2. The constants on the right are therefore
(b^2/a)[q-p^2+s^2+eta E^2]=b^2 q/a;
the linear terms are b*zeta_0-2bs v_0-2bFz_0,
and the quadratic terms are a(Qdetail_00+v_0^2+eta z_0^2).
This verifies (7.9) term by term without an inverse or external theorem.

If the actual finite incoming multipliers at the first query are
nonnegative, their total is N_00-nu_0-2alpha_0>=0. Hence

    nu_0+2alpha_0 <= N_00 <= b^2 q/a.             (7.10)

This bounds the source load by the ENTIRE paid initial budget.
It cannot be repaired by moving clock energy between details,
using clock-annihilating details, changing their ranks or supports,
changing zeta, changing z (including its clock), or changing skew
corrections while keeping the large source load and small q.
It even allows a different terminal distribution with nonnegative
alpha_0, as long as the displayed architecture and p,s apply.

For the physical parameters, b^2/a<(17/12)^2/(2/5)<6 and qtar<p.
Thus, whenever q<=qtar,

    N_00<6p<1/128,
    N_00-(1/64)-2alpha_0<-1/128                  (7.11)

if alpha_0>=0. This proves a uniform failed ORIGINAL first column
for the explicit enlarged law (7.2), and for the full class in this
subsection retaining nu_0=1/64. It is independent of all compatible
skew corrections. Equivalently that fixed load requires q>1/384,

For clarity, the obstruction includes arbitrary finite nonnegative
weights on the literal vectors gdetail_i,ddetail_i, arbitrary positive
variance metrics, their sums, and any other zero-sum PSD detail
construction. Only necessary inequalities are claimed for this class;
there is no arbitrary unknown PSD object adopted as a certificate.

### 7.2 Moment accounting for the surviving enlargement freedoms

A general sum H=sum gamma_i gdetail_i gdetail_i^T
+sum tau_i ddetail_i ddetail_i^T, with nonnegative scalar weights,
has He=0, t^T Ht=sum gamma_i h_i^2, and its second sum annihilates t.

and the incoming total and clock are again ellload. This describes
the larger parameter class covered by (7.10); (7.2) is its single
fully fixed original-index instance used in this report.

If all details annihilate both e and t and one leaves K,zeta fixed,
then the optimum vectors and load moments remain unchanged, but
N_00 decreases by a H_00, N_ll increases by H_ll, and the last-row
clock defect changes by -hgap H_ll. The latter follows from
H t=0, mu unchanged, and the last row of Ltri^T being e_l^T.
These diagonal and endpoint changes still have to be paid; null
clock energy is not permission to ignore them.

If one changes z, alpha, or the incoming vector beyond the fixed
law, the general compatibility equations are

    e^T nu=2pV+theta-2(1-p),
    t^T nu=X+V^2+eta Z^2-2alpha^T t,
    V=t^T v, Z=t^T z, X=t^T Qdetail t,
    theta=t^T zeta.

Thus changing nu_0 is a real global-moment change. The current
necessary bound requires nu_0+2alpha_0=O(p) at the target scale.
It does not assert that such a smaller load is sufficient, nor
exclude a nonnegative incoming distribution supported elsewhere.
No attempt to choose a third coefficient law is made in this round.
